member of the commission.– mr president, first of all thank you very much for inviting me here today, and very warm thanks to mr langen, both for his introductory remarks but most of all for the substantial work that has been done with the report and in the co-work with the shadow rapporteurs. the very fundamental thing here is that we are together in this, making sure that competition law is enforced and that it is done in a way that supports the everyday life of citizens. one obvious point is that powerful companies who are successful do not misuse their power, that we keep the market open, keep the playing field level, and make sure that every company has a fair chance of making it if they can attract consumers. as you well know, i have opened a public consultation on the work of the national competition agencies. we in the commission, and therefore hopefully also you, are very dependent on their strength and commitment, as well as the decisions they take using european law. i hope very much that together we can strengthen the competences of the national competition agencies and i will do my utmost to make sure that parliament will have full engagement in these efforts. i very much appreciate that you are focusing your attention on the work that we do when it comes to corporate taxation. i think this is very crucial to keeping the playing field level. if one company can pay very little or almost no taxes and another one just pays the taxes by the book, obviously there is a distortion of competition. last week we took a decision on the belgian ‘excess profit’ scheme, declaring that it is illegal under state aid legislation. first of all, because it gives multinationals a selective tax advantage that their domestic competitors cannot get. secondly, because instead of ensuring that profits are attributed to the right group company and taxed there, the system just exempted a proportion of profits from taxation. with this decision we take another step forward in ensuring that we have companies paying their fair share of taxes. but of course we need to do that in cooperation and i very much appreciate the work done here in parliament in the special committee on tax rulings but also in the working group on competition. keeping markets fair and open also relates to mergers. and here it is very important to have lively debates about how we apply our merger regulation. i think the report makes a very valuable contribution to that discussion and, in the end, merger control also relates to the consumer and the individual and making sure that the consumer can have affordable prices, high quality and, of course, choice. as the market has gone global, it is very important that our enforcement is global as well and i think it is very important that we do not give up on our european values but do our best to work with counterparts in the us, in china, in south africa, in south korea and in canada, to make sure that these values of fair and open competition are the values that we work with globally. we work with that in the international competition network, in the oecd and in un entities. i think this is very important, both when negotiating free trade agreements, where we are discovering anti-trust-relevant cartels and mergers, and when entering into state aid. in conclusion, i would say that a lot of things have happened. it is clearly reflected in your report, mr langen. we have worked on making digital markets work better by launching a sector inquiry into e-commerce; we have had cases concerning google and concerning qualcomm; we have acted to protect the internal market for energy with our cases involving gazprom and bulgaria energy holding; we have launched the first ever sector inquiry into state aid, looking into capacity mechanisms; and we continue our actions against cartels affecting products that consumers use every day. we have reviewed major cross-border mergers as general electric’s acquisition of alstom in energy-related businesses. but it all boils down to one thing – that we need very good cooperation with the european parliament; we need strong support for an open, competitive and fair market. in doing that we can both serve the interests of the european consumer and of the european citizens.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are protected. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i would like to draw your attention to a number of specific points which are of particular interest to the committee on the internal market, but not only. the first concerns the digital single market: we need common rules. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. but i would like to insist with you on the tax side: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the tax system is not rigid. until there is an obligation to report in each country on what companies do and what they pay in taxes, we shall have a state of disparity which will end up dealing a very heavy blow to the expectations and potential of small businesses. i think that this limit must be quickly crossed.

member of the commission.– madam president, i would like to thank mr gabriel mato. the commission very strongly appreciates the draft report as prepared by the rapporteur, mr mato. it is obviously the result of a very good understanding of the issues which surround the status of bluefin tuna, a very important species. it provides a very valuable contribution and also some positive suggestions for the modification of the initial proposal. it is also important to remember that this proposal aims, as has already been explained, to transpose into eu law measures which were already adopted by iccat, the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tuna. they were adopted in 2014, and they have been applicable to member states and operators since july 2015. it is important to say that this recovery plan has been very widely acknowledged as a success story, and the stock of bluefin tuna is well on its way towards recovery. having said that, there is and there can be no room for complacency. we still need to continue to give priority to the sustainable management of this important stock. measures adopted in the recovery plan by iccat are therefore crucial. many of the provisions of the recovery plan are directly applicable to all our member states. however, transposition is needed to ensure that the provisions applicable to natural or legal persons are also complied with in the european union. this is necessary to ensure that compliance is there – the compliance of the union with its international obligations – and it is also there to maintain the eu’s credibility in sustainable fisheries management. while this report largely meets our expectations, there are still some divergences. this is the case regarding the interpretation of the competences of the respective institutions when transposing provisions from the regional fisheries management organisations (rfmos). however, we are confident that they can be solved. regarding the provisions for the empowerment of the commission to adopt delegated acts, the commission strongly believes that due to the frequent amendments of the recovery plan in iccat, this is a crucial element within the proposal. why? because such delegated acts are required in order to swiftly incorporate into eu law any future amendments of the recovery plan at iccat level. these amendments are bound to, and do, occur regularly. in these cases, going through the full ordinary legislative procedure very often impedes us from implementing new measures in time to ensure the european union’s compliance with our international obligations. the adoption of delegated acts by the commission provides the possibility to accurately and, most importantly, rapidly transpose iccat measures into eu law by amending only the non-essential elements of the legislative acts. this requires appropriate consultations including consultations at expert level. it also requires the timely and appropriate transmission of relevant documents to the european parliament and to the council. the commission also believes that it should be empowered to adopt implementing acts. this is justified by the frequent need to establish how certain measures of the recovery plan should be implemented at the level of the eu. we need this to achieve a level playing field for the member states and also to ensure the effectiveness of the same measures. this is particularly relevant for control measures introduced in iccat whose interpretation could be different amongst different member states and which are directly linked to the respect of quotas and other international obligations. the commission’s proposal for a regulation on the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna provides a very balanced and effective follow-up to the iccat agreement. the report of mr mato, i will repeat, is a very valuable contribution and i look forward to hearing the views of this chamber.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to make two points. the first concerns the question of so-called delegated acts: the commission proposes to implement the future amendments to the bluefin tuna recovery plan in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean by means of delegated acts, but if this were to happen, parliament would no longer have any say in icat. in my view, and in our view, the implementation of the recommendations of the regional fisheries management organisations must remain a joint responsibility of parliament and the council under the ordinary codecision procedure. the second point concerns the quotas for bluefin tuna: it is not clear why the diversification of quotas for each vessel should be based only on the quantity caught in 2000, nor how such a quota can in fact be exclusively to the advantage of certain fishermen to the detriment of many other operators, especially small-scale operators. the mechanism for fishing quotas for bluefin tuna must be freed from the monopoly of large shipowners, favouring more sustainable fishing systems and small and medium-sized enterprises. as an s&d group we have proposed an amendment to call on the member states and icat to review the current system and i ask my colleagues to support it.

member of the commission.– madam president, the commission wholeheartedly welcomes the report on the role of intercultural dialogue, cultural diversity and education in promoting eu fundamental values. i would like to congratulate the rapporteur ms ward on the excellent result of her work. the terrible terrorist attacks in france and elsewhere in europe remind us yet again of the importance of building cohesive societies, where everyone can feel safe and valued irrespective of one’s conviction or background. the richness of the social, linguistic and cultural diversity that the eu represents is indeed held together, as the report says, by the fundamental values that we share: respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights, including the rights of persons belonging to minorities. continuous efforts to promote multiculturalism, integration and social cohesion are needed to guarantee a union in which pluralism, non-discrimination, tolerance, justice, solidarity and equality prevail. the commission welcomes the strong emphasis of the report on the role of intercultural dialogue and education, which helps learners to show an open mind and be active, responsible citizens equipped with a critical mind and committed to our common fundamental values. this is precisely the point of the paris declaration which the education ministers and myself endorsed in march last year. to follow up on this declaration with concrete actions is a key priority for me. preventing violent radicalisation by promoting an inclusive society and democratic values is firmly embedded in the european security agenda, which recognises the key role of education, youth work and intercultural dialogue in this context. we will also follow up on the european council’s call to address the factors underlying radicalisation. such a complex phenomenon cannot be handled in a simplistic manner. quick fixes and spectacular announcements will not do. we need deeper changes in the social fabric of our societies that can only be achieved through longer—term actions, particularly through formal and non—formal learning. the ward report identifies several very relevant areas for action: the need for civic education to start from an early age, the creation of common education platforms, the development of quality training programmes promoting diversity, the provision of counselling services at schools, the need to provide teachers with multilingual and intercultural skills, and the creation of rights-based and gender-sensitive learning environments. important steps have, in the meantime, already been taken. firstly, the education ministers have agreed to anchor the objectives of the paris declaration firmly in the current priorities for european cooperation in the field of education and training. secondly, we will also use the erasmus+ programme to its full, in order to put the paris declaration into action. projects linked to equity, inclusion and non-discrimination will be substantially reinforced. in 2016, eur 400 million will be spent on transnational projects which will enhance, amongst others, the education of disadvantaged learners and promote the integration of newly arrived migrants. in addition, a specific call will soon be released with a budget of eur 13 million to disseminate good practices in the field of inclusion, anti-radicalisation and integration of migrants. the report also rightly emphasises the importance of intercultural dialogue in promoting fundamental values. the commission work programme for 2016 stresses the importance for the eu to take advantage of opportunities to advance its values, as well as european history and culture. in line with this idea, i, together with high representative/vice-president mogherini, am currently working on measures to further cultural diplomacy, in particular to enhance intercultural understanding through direct people-to-people contacts and civil society relationships. again, this is fully in line with the report in front of us, which calls on the eu to include culture and cultural exchanges and to enhance education in eu external relations. generally speaking, promoting intercultural dialogue, cultural awareness and cultural expression are high up on our working agenda with the member states and they will be discussed at the european culture forum, which will take place in brussels on 19 and 20 april. i greatly appreciate the commitment of parliament to stand behind this important agenda of enhancing fundamental values through culture and education. i am looking forward to working with you on these issues. we have no time to lose and we need to join forces to take concrete action now.

secondly, in the second chapter, i believe that the exchange of good practice, networking and entrepreneurship education are important components, hence the development of a european platform for women entrepreneurs; the third. the real barrier in chapter 3 for women is access to credit and i believe that greater implementation of the equal access to services directive has become indispensable. banks must treat everyone equally and not favour investment projects over male ones; 4. other the penultimate chapter: i believe that an entrepreneurial culture needs to be instilled in vice-president of the commission.– mr president, the european parliament’s own-initiative report on the digital single market is a significant document which covers a wide variety of important themes for europe. we need to ensure european people, consumers, companies and industry can benefit from a truly functioning digital single market. this is a top priority of this commission. it is also an area where europe and the european project have many positive stories to tell. that is why working closely and early enough with the co-legislators is key for success. i would like to thank the rapporteurs and all other members of the european parliament involved in this report. the digital single market strategy identifies 16 key initiatives. in december 2015, we already presented a communication on copyright with a legislative proposal on cross-border portability. this means that we want to ensure that subscribers to online content services can access what they have paid for while temporarily present in another member state. the copyright communication sets out political objectives and areas of action, with concrete measures and a timeline. we have also made legislative proposals for new rules to improve protection for consumers who buy digital content or goods online across the european union and to help businesses to expand their online sales. as you can see, we are already delivering important elements of the digital single market. this will continue through 2016. in addition to a common and comprehensive solution to geo-blocking, we want to simplify vat payments for companies and also promote efficient and affordable parcel delivery. geo-blocking goes against the very idea of a single market, without borders or discrimination based on nationality or place of residence. beyond consumers, start-ups and smes, we also want to support european industry in embracing digital transformation. this is key for growth and jobs. industry is a pillar of the european economy. it is also important to focus on the skills of the workforce. in the next month, we will review the rules which apply to telecoms, audiovisual and e-privacy. we will improve cybersecurity, leverage cloud computing activities, support the development of a european science cloud and enable free flow of data. i am looking forward to hearing your views during the debate and to working with you to make the digital single market a reality, and a success story for europe.

in writing. ‒ the international commission for the conservation of tunas (iccat) is the international organisation responsible for the conservation of this species in the atlantic area. in 2006, iccat adopted a 15-year recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean, which is periodically revised on the basis of stock assessments, control experience and new technologies. in order to make the measures taken for the recovery of bluefin tuna more effective, the commission proposed that the iccat recommendations be incorporated into community law. i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean. this is a mainly technical measure aimed at transposing into community law the measures of the recovery plan developed by iccat between 2012 and 2014. bluefin tuna is an important fishery resource for several eu countries, including italy, and this project, alongside important measures, has a reference to the issue of quotas. the current mechanism, operated at state level, has favoured and continues to favour large shipowners over small-scale operators. europe can and must work to overcome the current situation which, in addition to penalizing small fishermen, risks undermining the sustainability of fisheries. the socialist group has therefore tabled and passed an important amendment, which i support, calling on the member states to adopt fairer criteria for allocating quotas in order to favour small-scale fishermen.
in writing. ‒ while i share the objectives of rebuilding the bluefin tuna stocks, there are still technical steps that i do not share and which leave me sceptical about a positive vote on this report, which is why i decided to abstain.
in writing. - i vote for it. the measure frees the current mechanism from the monopoly of large shipowners and promotes more sustainable fishing systems such as those for small-scale fisheries.
in writing. ‒ today the european parliament approved by a very large majority the amendment i tabled on the redistribution of tuna quotas. this measure is very much appreciated by small-scale artisanal fishermen because it calls on the member states to review quotas on the basis of fairer criteria, without favouring the monopoly of a few shipowners, as is the case today. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fishermen are not caught unintentionally. in 2015, there was an increase of 20% in the overall bluefin tuna fishing quota, an increase due to the progressive replenishment of the stock, as certified by iccat. this increase in the overall quota for bluefin tuna decided by iccat was unfortunately applied according to discretionary distribution criteria by the individual member countries. a 'failure' which has in many cases meant that only a few shipowners benefit from these quotas, to the detriment of small-scale artisanal fishermen. the large shipowners are running out of quotas in a short time and are taking the tuna to the fattening areas, guaranteeing themselves very high profits. the approval of our amendment means that we want bluefin tuna to be on our tables too and not just on those of asia.
in writing. ‒ since 2008, the bluefin tuna biomass has shown a markedly positive trend. in 2014, the regional organisation decided to increase the tac by 20% for the following three years (2015 to 2017), as sound scientific data show that stocks are at optimal levels of abundance. the rapporteur welcomes the commission proposal, which aims to transpose the recommendations of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) into community law. the iccat has the power to take decisions for the conservation and management of fisheries in its area of competence. those acts are binding and must be transposed into union law. i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because, in addition to sharing its content, i was pleased to see that sometimes the policies that this european union imposes work. i hope that the evolution of the bluefin tuna stock is a good anticipation of what will happen to the real economy: after years of deprivation and cuts, i hope to soon enjoy the fruits of renewed growth. we really need it.
in writing. ‒ i support the proposal for a regulation on the multiannual recovery plan for atlantic bluefin tuna as the new measures for increasing maximum fishing levels are sufficiently supported by scientific data on the current optimum level of abundance. for italy in particular, this will mean a 20% increase in the maximum allowable catch limits for the year 2016, significantly increasing the amount of fish caught without compromising the balance of our marine environment. the commission notes that the measure is not intended to provide a guarantee for the recovery of the aid granted to the beneficiary.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' in the definition of the term 'commercial vehicle'. the iccat has the power to adopt decisions ('recommendations') for the conservation and management of fisheries in its area of competence; such acts are binding and must be transposed into union law. bluefin tuna is the most important species. fishermen have made considerable efforts to adjust their catches to a reduced total allowable catch (tac) as a result of the decisions taken in 2006 while respecting the fishing conditions set out in the plan. in the light of the positive evolution of the stock situation, iccat decided to increase the total allocation slightly. the current tac for 2015 is 15 821 tonnes and the eu quota is 9 372,9 tonnes. since 2008, the bluefin tuna biomass has shown a markedly positive trend. in 2014, the regional organisation decided to increase the tac by 20% for the following three years (2015 to 2017), as scientific evidence shows that stocks are at optimal levels of abundance, therefore i vote in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ this is a sensitive issue, especially for our country, because the bluefin tuna issue opens up the debate on the criteria for allocating quotas among fishermen. the tuna quotas are decided by iccat but the internal distribution is managed by individual member countries on a discretionary basis. in our case, the criteria which have forced many small-scale fishermen to abandon their gear because they were not able to access the quotas, despite the increase decreed by iccat, must be revised. that is why i supported the amendment which challenges the current monopoly mechanism of large shipowners, which is intended to promote more sustainable fishing systems, such as those used by small-scale fisheries. the member states must do more to review the quota system, which is detrimental to small-scale fishermen and their future.
in writing. the commission proposal is intended to implement the recommendations of iccat (the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas). the bluefin tuna in particular is certainly the most important species and the fishery is regulated by iccat, which, having established a total allowable catch, has forced fishermen to make considerable logistical efforts to bring the tonnage of catches within the permitted limits. however, a positive evolution of the available stock, supported by scientific data, has allowed an increase in the total allowable catch for the eu, which has increased from 7939 tonnes in 2014 to 9372 tonnes in 2015. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ this proposal aims to transpose into eu law all the measures of the east atlantic and mediterranean bluefin tuna recovery plan adopted by iccat. the project lays the foundations for a greater sensitivity to artisanal fishing and for the implementation of the technical nature of the gear used. however, i think that some crucial points deserve more detailed clarification, such as the measures proposed by the regulation concerning specimens of bluefin tuna caught accidentally and confiscated by the authorities of the member states. in most cases, the focus is on punishing the fisherman who has inadvertently caught the tuna, and not on the possible use of the confiscated fish, for example. such clarifications, even after the introduction of the landing obligation, would ensure better application of the new provisions.
in writing. ‒ with this report we have clearly expressed the european parliament's support for artisanal fishing and more artisanal and sustainable types of gear, such as traditional tuna traps, and we have clearly stated our intention to give european consumers quality european bluefin tuna, avoiding that the best products end up on foreign markets. we shall be watching the council and the member states to ensure that our words do not remain words but are soon transformed into action.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep legislative resolution on the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean because i consider it a very important act in defence of sustainable fisheries, the interests of territories such as the south of italy and of economic operators who are often sacrificed to the needs of big business. i am thinking of the small fishermen who have often felt suffocated by an excess of quota rules and regulations which have so far favoured the big industry at the expense of small local boats. the s&d group has been fighting for new quota systems for bluefin tuna that eliminate the monopoly of large shipowners, promote sustainable fishing, and promote small-scale fishing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the regulation to include the fishing industry, which is the main source of income for the fishermen. this is an important step, born of listening directly to the territories and operators. it is now up to the member states to review their course and find a high point of synthesis between economy, employment protection and respect for the environment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, but above all i voted in favour of my group's amendment against the monopoly of the big shipowners to protect small-scale fishing and traditional techniques, the old tuna nets: all sustainable systems that disappear. it is a heritage that must be protected as much as the precious bluefin tuna.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean and repealing regulation (ec) no 302/2009. bluefin tuna is the most important species regulated by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (icccat), to which the european union is a contracting party and whose decisions on fisheries conservation and management are binding under union law. the proposal aims to consolidate into a regulation a number of measures adopted between 2012 and 2014, such as technical measures on the transfer of live bluefin tuna or provisions on the declaration of catches, in order to ensure uniform application throughout the european union and to guarantee a level playing field for all operators in the tuna fisheries sector.
in writing. ‒ to ensure that our bluefin tuna stocks can be repopulated, it is very important to maintain limits on the quotas of vessels. i voted for this report because i agree with the rapporteur that there is a need for greater supervision of fisheries activities in order to safeguard an important part of the european economy.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposal takes over the recommendations of iccat, the regional fisheries management organisation responsible for the management of bluefin tuna and related species in the atlantic ocean and adjacent seas, which has adopted a multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan, due for completion in 2022. i agree with the rapporteur and support his position that the purpose of the transposition of the iccat recommendations is to ensure uniform application throughout the eu and not to reopen the debate on what has been decided after lengthy negotiations. uniform application should ensure a level playing field for all operators in the tuna fisheries.
in writing. ‒ while the common fisheries policy was originally part of the common agricultural policy, it has gradually acquired a distinct identity in the course of the community's evolution. for this reason, referring to the question put by the rapporteur on the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna and considering that it has shown a markedly positive trend in recent years, i consider it appropriate that the european union should propose to incorporate them into the european system by means of a specific regulation. the european fisheries sector also produces about 3.3% of the world's fisheries, a figure which should not be underestimated for the economies of our countries. the union will certainly continue to work towards this, and i am voting in favour of this.
in writing. ‒ the multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan, adopted in 2006 by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat), to which the european union is a contracting party, is bearing fruit. since 2008, bluefin tuna stocks have been growing again and experts believe that since 2014 they have been at optimal levels of abundance. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a regulation on the establishment of a european union fisheries fund (eff) for the period 2014-2020. i welcome the report's proposal to include in a regulation all the measures of the restructuring plan adopted in order to ensure their uniform and effective implementation throughout the eu. i think it is equally important to ensure a level playing field for all those involved in the tuna fisheries. finally, i welcome the adoption of the amendment calling on the member states to allocate tuna quotas more equitably, not only to the benefit of large shipowners but also to small fishermen who use sustainable fishing techniques.
in writing. ‒ in 2006, iccat adopted a multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan, which is expected to be completed by 2022. the commission has also assessed the impact of the measures on the fishing industry in the union. the commission has also taken into account the fact that the tacs for 2017 have been increased by the tacs for 2017 and 2017 respectively. in addition, the iccat recommendations take into account the specificities of the different tuna fishing gear, in particular traditional, more artisanal and sustainable gear. such gears have a very low impact on marine ecosystems due to their low level of energy consumption and bycatch. i voted in favour of this proposal which aims to include in a regulation all the measures of the restructuring plan adopted between 2012 and 2014 in order to ensure their uniform and effective implementation throughout the eu. this will ensure that the transposition of iccat recommendations is applied uniformly throughout the eu and that there is a level playing field for all tuna fishermen.
in writing. ‒ the new bluefin tuna recovery plan aims to transpose into european law some of the recommendations adopted by iccat for better management of this precious fishery resource in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean. i supported parliament's first reading position that there is a need to pay greater attention to small-scale fishing and to the types of gear that are more sustainable and contribute to the achievement of the plan's objectives, because of their high level of selectivity and their low environmental impact. while i agree with the general approach of the proposal, i would have thought it appropriate to clarify the monitoring measures provided for in the regulation in respect of specimens of bluefin tuna caught accidentally and confiscated by the member states' authorities. unfortunately, this measure is often interpreted as a penalty for the fisherman who has caught tuna, even if it was unintentional. i hope that on this point we will go in a different direction, for example by establishing the possible uses of confiscated fish. i believe that, following the entry into force of the landing obligation, such clarification would ensure better implementation of the new provisions.
in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean, with a view to ensuring a more sustainable development of the stock and introducing measures to support small-scale fishing. the purpose of this regulation is to implement in the union the binding conservation and management measures agreed at international level by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) and contained in the recommendations adopted at the annual meetings in 2012-2014. although the regulation covers purely technical aspects, the issue of bluefin tuna fishing is particularly important for italy from the point of view of the criteria for allocating quotas among fishermen. these quotas are decided within iccat but distributed nationally by the individual member states. that is why i voted in favour of an amendment calling on the member states to review the system for allocating fishing quotas for bluefin tuna in order to favour small-scale fishermen, who can ensure a more sustainable system than large shipowners.
in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean. the resolution contains technical measures such as those on the transfer and caging of live fish, and includes measures on the use of stereoscopic cameras to estimate tuna quantities and catch reporting requirements. i am particularly pleased that the report has been approved, particularly with regard to the new distribution quotas. the system in force until now has particularly penalized small-scale fishermen and has undermined the sustainability of fisheries.

in writing. ‒ the european union is immensely rich in cultural, social and linguistic diversity. in this context, preserving the common values that unite our societies such as freedom, democracy, human rights, tolerance and solidarity becomes crucial for its advancement. the many challenges facing us today, including immigration, the dangers of radicalisation, rising inequalities and the violence of populist policies, require a common commitment to avoid a closed society in which citizens' sense of belonging and collective capacity to react have been eroded. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that strengthening intercultural dialogue can make a significant contribution to building a pluralist and inclusive society. promoting cultural pluralism is important for the improvement of democracy and for laying the foundations for a new culture of citizenship, which shapes a collective european consciousness. intercultural dialogue can thus be the prime venue for the understanding and development of innovative democratic practices and a vehicle for a new level of unity within the union.
in writing. ‒ in defending the eu's core values, common efforts are needed. preventing and addressing exclusion, intolerance, racism and radicalisation, as well as preserving a framework of equal opportunities for all, is key to solving current challenges. this report aims to promote inclusion, participation and active citizenship through the development of new education policies, such as high-quality training programmes for educators in both the statutory and voluntary sectors. the report particularly highlights the positive role played by volunteering, sport and the arts in strengthening socialisation processes. it is also important to ensure that cultural heritage and history are not used as a tool of division but as an opportunity for inclusion. promoting the eu's core values also requires increased cooperation between international institutions, in particular between the union, its member states and international organisations such as the united nations and its agencies, and increased structural and sustainable support to ngos, organisations working with children and young people, training institutions and all organisations concerned. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the resolution on the role of intercultural dialogue, cultural diversity and education, because i believe that this text is an effective response to the increasingly evident multidimensional and multicultural structure of europe, and because i believe that it is essential, in the light of recent events, to promote intercultural and interreligious exchange in an interactive and inclusive dimension. an inclusive society is one that invests in education that is accessible at all levels, that simplifies the bureaucratic procedures for obtaining citizenship, that offers the possibility of acquiring intercultural and social civic skills. creating such a society means providing future generations with the tools to tackle and overcome bold challenges in an innovative way and to combat in a concrete way the social phenomena of discrimination, violence, racism, xenophobia and radicalism. in this resolution, we therefore call on all levels of government to promote more and more initiatives aimed at supporting cultural diversity, intercultural dialogue, education, making full use of existing financial resources and initiatives at european level.
in writing. ‒ at a time like the present, marked by violent and tragic events in europe, i believe it is more necessary than ever to reiterate the need to foster intercultural dialogue through concrete interventions in the daily lives of all citizens. education, education, training and culture must be considered key words in our daily lives. the aim of all our actions is integration and solidarity, especially with regard to the many children who are forced by war and hunger to leave their country of origin. the common foreign and security policy must be given a boost, also through cultural diplomacy, and strong signs of social and economic integration are needed, which can be achieved by extending access to culture and education for immigrants, with educational corridors for students in refugee camps. promoting inclusion through active citizenship programmes and support for new forms of entrepreneurship.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe in the role of intercultural and interreligious dialogue and education as fundamental tools for promoting peace, facilitating conflict management and promoting human rights. this is particularly important in the light of the recent events which have shaken europe. we must work with young people in particular to help them become members of an open society that adheres to the eu's values and fights against phenomena such as racism, radicalism and discrimination.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the adoption of the report on intercultural dialogue, cultural diversity and education in the fundamental values of the european union. i agree with the report almost entirely: it is important to note that intercultural and interreligious dialogue and education are fundamental elements for the creation of a climate of peace and important tools for conflict management. this is particularly true today in the light of the tragic terrorist attacks that have just occurred. i particularly share the report where it recognises that joint efforts are needed to prevent and combat marginalisation, intolerance, racism and radicalisation. i would also like to remind you that we have a duty to work to preserve a framework of equal opportunities for all.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have spoken on several occasions about the quality of financial regulation and governance in this sector. with the report we have approved, we are taking a step towards greater transparency in the legislative process on financial services, in order to avoid a relapse into a severe recession like the one in 2008 with subprime mortgages. this risk is less abstract than one might think, if leading economists are now predicting an "epidemic" in the energy sector due to the possible failure of shale oil companies and if the monetary authorities of the main countries do not take proactive steps. i agree with the report and i share the rapporteur's concern about the inconsistencies and lack of uniformity in the legislation, particularly on the objectives which i hope all the regulators involved will embrace, namely financial stability, consumer protection and the financing of small and mediumsized enterprises. as a result, the overall competitiveness of europe's financial sectors, which is also threatened by china, brexit and the ongoing tensions in the euro area, needs to be stimulated by a cultural change in the financial sector that puts consumers' interests first with a coherent and risk-based approach.
in writing. ‒ the capital markets union aims to tackle the investment gap with determination by expanding and diversifying sources of finance for long-term businesses and projects in europe. to this end, the commission has proposed an action plan to be completed by 2019 to facilitate cross-border investment with the ambition of making the european financial system more stable and competitive. the proposed capital markets union does not meet the particular financing needs of smes, which need local banks with a local basis. that is why i voted against the proposed system, which i consider to be unsuitable for protecting smes, and which would instead create an even more complex and costly channel of financing.
in writing. ‒ the economic crisis since 2008 has highlighted all the risks associated with a lack of regulation in the financial sector. the real economy has been hit by severe shocks to stock markets, the banking system and the whole financial institutions complex. the eu's efforts in recent years to promote a more shock-resistant and more transparent financial system have, however, been linked to a non-exhaustive assessment by the commission of the outcome of the reforms it has promoted. i supported the balz report because i believe that the path towards a capital markets union that is conducive to the real economy should be promoted as much as possible. the new financial system will have to be based on a renewed culture and ensure that savers and investors have access to relevant, accurate, simple and reliable information. initiatives to improve sme financing should be extended to start-ups, micro and medium-caps in order to promote stable and sustainable growth and the creation of new jobs.
in writing. ‒ i do not agree with the balz report which analyses the budget and the challenges of eu regulation of financial services. i believe that the eu's financial services legislation needs to be completely reviewed. a few legislative initiatives are not enough to finally bring stability to the community's financial markets. a radical change is needed, one that restores confidence to businesses and consumers. that is why i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ the review of financial services regulation gives us the opportunity to take stock of the situation and propose improvements in an area which, as the financial crisis has shown, is having an increasingly wide impact on the real economy. this report, which i support, has the merit of striking a good balance between the desire to facilitate access to finance and the need to review a regulation which has often proved unsuitable to meet the problems and challenges of the present time. the revision of the financial services legislation does not mean that we are moving towards gradual deregulation, but towards better regulation. the creation of a capital markets union also requires clearer and more effective, but also more transparent and coherent legislation, which is capable of creating a more favourable investment environment, including the creation of new channels of access to credit, which can benefit in particular small and medium-sized enterprises and start-ups. a clear and consistent regulatory framework is needed to ensure financial stability and competitiveness.
in writing. ‒ the report is a compendium of good intentions, which can be shared in part, but with a 'distinction' such as point 14, which seems inherently contradictory. the problem, however, is that there is complete silence on the only basic prerequisite for good intentions, namely the restoration of a clear separation between those who deal with finance and those who must exercise credit (the glass steagall act). without this there can be neither protection of savings nor adequate credit to the real economy. the report also underestimates the value of non-conflict resolution systems for debt disputes and in fact demonizes shadow banking (point 26), which is designed to compensate for the credit shortfalls even among the wealthy. and above all, it does not provide any practical measures for the analysis of risks in derivative products to protect the widespread interest of investors, and in particular of small european savers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the actions taken by the eu in the field of financial services represent an important step towards the completion of the single market and european integration. in particular, i think it is important that regulation in this area should focus more on the end users of capital markets, namely companies and investors.
in writing. ‒ following the financial and debt (private, but omitted) crisis that erupted in 2007/2008, a number of legislative initiatives in the field of eu financial services were launched with the aim of restoring financial stability, strengthening consumer protection and putting the lessons learned from the crisis into practice. this own-initiative report is a first step in taking stock of this legislative work, in the context of major new commission initiatives such as the investment package and the capital markets union. there is no need for a mere cosmetic operation to a set of economic and financial rules that have made the eu, and in particular the eurozone, immune to external shocks and the global demand black hole. moreover, entrusting the governance of financial markets to the commission (such as the capital markets union) is like putting a fox in a henhouse. the first and only effective action to be taken is the (coordinated, hopefully) dismantling of the economic and monetary union, followed by the consequent dissolution of the banking union. i vote against.
in writing. ‒ the report focuses on the completion of the capital markets union, with the aim of overcoming the fragmentation of financial markets by reducing the dependency of firms on the banking system. the text focuses on alternative financing channels to bank loans through greater financialization of the economy (to be carried out through new instruments, such as peer to peer lending and crowdfunding, as well as others already known as securitization). the solution to fostering more growth and employment was therefore found in the further expansion of finance, forgetting that it is precisely in the dominance of finance over the real economy that the crisis itself has its roots. the proposal, which calls for greater consistency both within eu legislation and within the international framework, also fails to take account of the specificities of european smes and the harm that standardisation of financial products would cause them. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ i have chosen to vote in favour of the own-initiative report because i believe that financial stability and consumer protection are a priority for the legislator's action. the measure aims to address the shortcomings in the regulation of financial services. the rapporteur also believes that the current legislation must be fully implemented and strictly applied in the member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that we must not only not forget the lessons of this crisis, but we must not stop watching because there is still so much to learn. the legislation that followed the 2007-2008 crisis in particular needs to be implemented and we cannot afford to relax, because distraction in this sector can lead to enormous damage, which is spread mainly to the innocent, and this is not politically acceptable.
in writing. ‒ the real competitiveness of european legislation and the financial sectors of the european union is a crucial challenge for financial services regulation. such regulation should be consistent and proportionate, especially in relation to existing initiatives on smes and sme funding. the lack of information on the financial situation of these companies is still one of the main obstacles to investment. in view of this, i felt i had to vote in favour of this own-initiative report and i hope that sound financial stability can be restored soon, particularly by strengthening consumer protection, encouraging investment and putting into practice the lessons learned from the crisis.
in writing. ‒ the own-initiative report welcomes the commission's proposal to establish a capital markets union (cmu) with the aim of overcoming the fragmentation of financial markets by reducing the dependency of firms on the banking system. the focus is on alternative financing channels to bank lending through increased financialization of the economy, both through new instruments such as peer to peer lending and crowdfunding, and through instruments already in use such as securitisation. the latter remains a too complex and expensive financing channel to meet the financing needs of smes, which need local banks that can know directly the territorial context in which the company operates. cmu will make the economic system more fragile, interconnected and exposed to systemic risks and new crises at the expense of growth and the real economy. it will not solve the problem of financing smes, which need stable, sustainable and long-term sources of credit. it is also dangerous and irresponsible to promote market integration in the absence of structural banking reform based on the separation of credit and investment activities and real regulation of the shadow banking system. my vote is therefore against.
in writing. ‒ the dangerous fluctuations caused by the oil price fall, the instability of the financial markets in china and the unresolved knots in the economic and financial structure may once again be explosive for the fragile economic growth in europe and italy. so when we think about financial reform in europe we should act with the possible dangers we might encounter if we were to loosen some of the regulatory framework that the european institutions have painstakingly carried forward over the years. today it is time to read the history of the last few years and strengthen those reforms implemented as emir and still to be implemented as mifid ii and mmf in a key of economic recovery, which does not mean reducing their scope, but making them consistent with an economy not yet ready for new global challenges. it is up to us as legislators to start work on making the capital markets union a winning challenge for all european economies, not just those which have already developed platforms in this sense, by overcoming the credit problems especially for small and medium-sized enterprises. for these reasons i thought it necessary to vote in favour of this proposal.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on eu regulation of financial services. the lack of uniformity in the regulation of these services has often led to the adoption of less stringent rules to attract firms, with negative results for the functioning of the internal market. i believe that the implementation of the legislative process in this particular area is essential in terms of coordination and transparency, in order to ensure the overall competitiveness of the eu's financial sectors. to do so, it is necessary that the esas and the ssm have a decisive role to play in achieving the objectives of better regulation and supervision.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep resolution on the budget and the challenges of the recent financial services legislation: i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware of the fact that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter. the last parliamentary term ended with unprecedented financial legislation, as a result of the financial crisis imported from the united states. a substantial part of it has entered into force, another part is still being implemented. the european legislator therefore faces a major challenge: firstly, to ensure that the existing legislation is properly applied, and secondly, to complete the banking union with the third pillar of the european deposit insurance system, which is more necessary than ever to protect european depositors wherever they have deposits, to ensure that the rules are applied uniformly, and to ensure that they are applied with certainty and that discretion is reduced. equal commitment is required to achieve the objective of creating a capital markets union that will expand credit opportunities for european businesses, diversify the source and increase the competitiveness of the system.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the budget and on the challenges of eu regulation in financial services. the report aims to highlight the importance of a thorough analysis of the impacts of legislation that have not been properly assessed. both financial stability and consumer protection remain priorities, and the report identifies the overall competitiveness of eu legislation and eu financial sectors as a key challenge in regulating financial services.
in writing. ‒ this report confirms that much progress has already been made in overcoming the financial crisis of 2007-08; however, we must continue to work to prevent future financial crises. i agree with the rapporteur that it is important to support the real economy, but we must not forget that the financial sector is the real nerve of this economy. the real economy depends on the financial sector, so we must ensure that both are strong enough to continue on the road to progress. that is why i voted in favour of the report calling for more rules for financial services.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of mr balz's report because i believe it is important that financial stability and consumer protection remain the priorities of the legislators and that more weight is given to the application of a coherent risk-based approach. i also believe that the overall competitiveness of european legislation and the eu's financial sectors is a challenge for financial services regulation, the quality of which also depends on the transparency and timeliness of the legislative process.
in writing. ‒ having taken note of all the actions taken to deal with the crisis that erupted in 2007/2008, i believe that it is appropriate to focus on long-term growth through, for example, diversification of funding channels. i am also concerned that the gaps and inconsistencies in the european financial services legislation may be detrimental to the activities of smes, which are struggling to navigate the regulatory maze. i therefore welcome the presentation of the resolution which complements and harmonises the rules, also on the basis of the comments of the itre committee, and i feel i can firmly express my vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ following the financial and debt crisis of 2007-2008, a number of legislative initiatives have been launched in the field of eu financial services, with the aim of restoring financial stability, strengthening consumer protection and putting the lessons learned from the crisis into practice. many of these legislative acts have already been implemented and applied or will be implemented in the near future. but there are challenges ahead. a thorough impact assessment of the financial services framework, which should be repeated at regular intervals and based on efficient regulation, can undoubtedly yield better results. in addition, mandatory consistency and proportionality checks should ensure that the application of financial services legislation is less complex and is more understandable and better adapted to the needs of small and medium-sized entities. the member states will have to apply the existing legislation strictly. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the european union has made a huge effort in recent years to regulate a banking and financial system that has suddenly plunged into a serious crisis. much has been done, but sometimes, pressed by contingency, in a somewhat hasty manner. it is therefore time to review what has been done, its usefulness, any errors and to propose the necessary changes to further improve the system.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it gives a balanced account of the legislative work carried out by financial institutions following the debt crisis that erupted in 2008. i also believe that the report provides a good opportunity to reflect not only on the shortcomings of the current regulation but also on the overall impact of the legislative measures on financial services, especially with regard to small and mediumsized enterprises. it is time to put the lessons of the crisis into practice and to analyse carefully the initiatives taken so far, with a view to responding effectively and reasonably to future challenges.
in writing. ‒ i welcomed the report on eu regulation of financial services, which provides a comprehensive overview of the impact of recent financial services legislation and its effectiveness in financing the real economy and small and medium-sized enterprises. i believe that all financial sectors are undergoing profound changes, including banking and insurance, and therefore need the creation of a capital markets union as an opportunity to strengthen the eu economy. in fact, considering that the financial crisis of 2007-2008 and its widespread negative repercussions were caused, inter alia, by the failure to implement adequate and quality financial services regulation for increasingly complex markets and products, i believe that it is necessary to actively participate in the construction of a regulatory framework that ensures financial stability, making the system more resilient to shocks, limiting risks and better responding to the needs of investors. all of this is to the benefit of the union's real economy.
in writing. ‒ the economic system is made even more fragile and exposed to systemic crisis risks by the capital markets union envisaged in this report, to the detriment of real economic growth, european businesses and savers. the text adopted emphasises the predominant role of finance in the real economy. the special financing needs of small and medium-sized enterprises, which need stable and long-term sources of credit, are best understood only by local banks and not by volatile capital markets and short-term speculative logic, as is proposed. the report, on the contrary, relaunches instruments such as securitisation, insisting on a financial channel which is too complex and burdensome for smes. i believe that the push for further market integration and regulatory uniformity is dangerous and irresponsible. the european economic system thus remains unstable without the implementation of a separation between credit and investment banking activities. for these reasons, i voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report welcomes the commission's proposal to establish a capital markets union (cmu) with the aim of overcoming the fragmentation of financial markets by reducing the dependency of firms on the banking system. such a union is certainly going in the wrong direction. the solution to fostering more growth and employment has been identified in a further expansion of finance, forgetting that the crisis was generated precisely by the dominance of finance over the economy. the cmu is in fact promoting further financialization of the economy, a revival of non-bank lending and securitisation. the latter remains a too complex and expensive financing channel to meet the financing needs of smes, which need local banks that can understand the territorial context in which the companies operate. cmu will make the economic system more fragile, interconnected and exposed to systemic risks. it will therefore not solve the problem of financing smes which need stable, sustainable and long-term sources of credit. finally, there is the irresponsible promotion of market integration in the absence of structural banking reform based on the separation of credit and investment activities and real regulation of the shadow banking system.
in writing. the own-initiative report welcomes the commission's proposal to create a capital markets union (cmu) which aims to reduce the dependency of businesses on the banking system in favour of financial markets. i voted against this report because i think the cmu is going in the wrong direction in that it is not addressing the causes of the crisis. the solution to foster more growth and employment has been identified in a further expansion of finance through alternative forms of lending such as peer to peer lending, crowdfunding and securitisation, forgetting that the crisis was generated precisely by the dominance of finance over the real economy. the capital markets union thus conceived will make the economic system more exposed to systemic risks at the expense of savers. the report does not address the need for smes to have stable markets and longterm financing. the document focuses on capital markets, which are volatile and driven by short-term speculative logic. i believe that it is dangerous and irresponsible to promote further integration of markets in the absence of structural banking reform based on the separation of credit and investment activities.
in writing. ‒ in 2014, the employment rate for men in the eu was 70.1%, while that for women was only 59.6%. unfortunately, these percentages fall even further when we look at the female entrepreneurship sector in europe. the factors that most influence women to prefer employed employment to freelance work have been identified in the difficult access to finance and the complicated work-life balance, especially with regard to maternity rules. in line with european policies for economic growth and job creation, the eu must support women's entrepreneurial activities, trying to meet the demands and needs of a category still discriminated against by old social legacies. i therefore voted in favour, confident that new measures will be taken to ensure equal opportunities for men and women.
in writing. ‒ women's entrepreneurship represents one of the largest untapped potential in the european union: in 2012, only 31% of entrepreneurs were women, a negative figure especially when considered in light of the existence of realities in which the name of women is used, as a nickname, to obtain tax and legislative benefits. i voted in favour of the report on external factors that constitute obstacles to female entrepreneurship to support the eu's efforts in this area. opening up new spaces for women in the world of self-employment means first of all promoting growth and employment in all member states, and also encouraging positive mechanisms of cultural change. commitment to this means making childcare and eldercare facilities available and affordable; the aim of the programme is to promote the reconciliation of private life and professional activity and to promote an equitable distribution of family responsibilities between women and men. the european union must promote a holistic approach to women's entrepreneurship, combating gender stereotypes, fostering the creation of an environment that develops women's entrepreneurial potential and facilitating access to finance.
in writing. ‒ the report is balanced and shareable, and it does not fall into the usual gender rhetoric we are used to, which is why i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ promoting entrepreneurship is a key driver of employment, economic growth, development and innovation, a top priority of the european union and at the heart of the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. despite this, european numbers are well below the entrepreneurship rates of china or the united states. this issue is linked to another major challenge, that of gender equality. inequalities between women and men are evident in the entrepreneurial professions: in 2012, women accounted for only 31% of the total self-employed in the eu-28. the causes of this situation are many, ranging from difficulties in reconciling family life and professional careers to obstacles in accessing finance. for these reasons, i believe that the only answer must be to promote a holistic approach to female entrepreneurship, aimed at building a framework that enables women to realise their potential, while also encouraging an entrepreneurial culture in education and training, which also makes them more aware of the economic and social opportunities at stake. the solution to this problem is a priority: i therefore supported this report, which calls on the commission to come forward with concrete legislative proposals on this by the end of 2016.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i firmly believe that it is the task of the european union and its institutions to remove all obstacles to the development of women's entrepreneurship. the benefits of developing women's entrepreneurship would be innumerable and would have a positive impact on society as a whole, not just economically.
in writing. ‒ female entrepreneurship and the employment rate of women in europe are still under-represented in relation to the europe 2020 targets. the difficulties in ensuring work-life balance, access to finance and proper procedural information, together with the prejudices they face, still prevent many women from competing on an equal footing with men in the contemporary world of entrepreneurship. the union must work to remove the remaining obstacles, both material and cultural, by ensuring equal opportunities and promoting female entrepreneurship, which, in both the social and more traditional sectors, represents a means of personal emancipation, social advancement and economic development not only for individuals but also for the entire economic community, which will only grow and develop effectively again when its average domestic entrepreneurship and employment rate approaches the europe 2020 targets.
in writing. ‒ the report presents no problems and does not fall into the usual gender rhetoric, privileging or discriminating against women depending on their sexual orientation, immigrant or not, etc. the report encourages member states to recognise the value of female entrepreneurship to their economies and calls on member states to come forward with concrete strategies to exploit the full potential of women as entrepreneurs. welcomes the creation of the various european networks of women entrepreneurs and urges the equal opportunities bodies in the member states to raise awareness among funders of the obligation to ensure equal treatment and to study the possibility of introducing gender equality in investment mandates. encourages the member states to promote an entrepreneurial culture in education and training programmes and stresses the importance of providing courses on finance, entrepreneurship and the development of new businesses in secondary education, especially in the courses more frequented by girls, such as healthcare and other services; it also calls on schools and universities to encourage girls and women to study subjects that open up career opportunities in finance and high-growth sectors such as technology, including green technologies. i vote for it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on external factors that hinder european women's entrepreneurship today because i believe that female entrepreneurship is a key policy issue for the european institutions. unfortunately, the gender gap is still very high in eu countries and not just in the field of entrepreneurship. most women do not consider entrepreneurship as a career option. the current share of women entrepreneurs in the eu is 33%, while only 34.4% of self-employed people in the eu are women. there is still a long way to go, and unfortunately we are still a long way from the full application of european legislation. europe needs to commit to working with national authorities to address those areas, such as access to credit and entrepreneurial networks, where the needs of women entrepreneurs are still not sufficiently addressed. this type of policy is also crucial to stimulating economic growth, prosperity and competitiveness.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which aims to tackle the problems facing women in the field of entrepreneurship today, which unfortunately in europe is still characterised by considerable differences between men and women. there are many obstacles faced by women who want to enter the business world: access to finance (the banking sector often discourages women's participation and finds it more difficult to provide funds for them); the difficult balance between work and private life and, above all, the need to overcome long-standing cultural and social legacies which require a full awareness on the part of society of the equal opportunities which must be guaranteed to men and women. the report is an invitation to the european commission to implement new measures and to make greater efforts to increase female participation.
in writing. ‒ for many women, self-employment and business creation have been the solution to unemployment and often the preferred way of reconciling family and working life. whatever the reasons for their choice of entrepreneurship, only 31% of selfemployed people in the european union today are women. despite european legislation and community guidelines calling on member states to create conditions for equal access to the labour market for men and women, it is still difficult for women entrepreneurs to obtain bank and insurance guarantees or access credit, despite the fact that they are rarely insolvent when it comes to repaying loans compared to men. these difficulties have not only discouraged the start-up of new activities but also limited their development and reduced the potential for job creation. to get europe back on the growth tracks and reach the 75% female employment target by 2020, not only does european legislation need to be implemented, but the credit world needs to overcome mistrust of women. one of the reasons why i voted in favour is the call for the commission to monitor the states to create an environment favourable to the development of women's enterprise.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure because i recognise the value of women's entrepreneurship as a key contribution to the development of local communities and social inclusion. in 2012, women accounted for only 31% of the total self-employed in the eu-28. statistics show that women have less recourse to external financing, have difficulty accessing equity financing and tend to choose more expensive forms of capital raising. although directive 2004/113/ec expressly prohibits financial services from discriminating in the provision of bank loans, i feel it is necessary to stress the issue of differential treatment in access to credit for women entrepreneurs by financial service providers.

in writing. ‒ in its strategies to boost the economy and create new jobs, the european union should not overlook two key factors: to provide access to more entrepreneurs and adopt a strategy for smart and sustainable growth. unfortunately, there are still too many cases of gender discrimination in the area of women entrepreneurship, in access to credit, equal economic independence is not guaranteed and the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy have so far not made significant progress in this direction. i therefore believe that, in order to prevent these critical issues from having a negative impact on the economy, more initiatives to promote employment and respect for gender equality should be encouraged. i therefore support the european parliament's motion for a resolution, and hope that many of the obstacles to female entrepreneurship in europe will be effectively removed.
in writing. ‒ the report aims to address the problems faced by women in entrepreneurship today, which in europe is still characterised by significant differences between men and women. there are a number of factors which hinder women's access to the business world and with this report the femm committee has wanted to address a call to the european commission to implement new measures and greater efforts to increase female participation. one of the obstacles identified is access to finance, as the banking sector often does not favour women's participation and has a harder time allocating funds to them. another obstacle is the difficulty of balancing work and life. the report also refers to the failure to adopt the maternity leave directive and calls for new measures to remedy this situation and to enable women to combine work and family life. the need for specific training in entrepreneurship and the overcoming of old cultural and social legacies is also highlighted. i think it is a good report and therefore i vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament resolution i voted for encourages member states to recognise the value of female entrepreneurship to their economies and the obstacles to be overcome. in order to reduce these obstacles, the european parliament believes that the gender dimension should be fully integrated into future entrepreneurship policy and calls on the member states to come forward with concrete strategies to promote a culture of female entrepreneurship through easier access to finance, the use of information and networks, greater education and training in entrepreneurship, and taking into account the need to focus on the needs, motivations and conditions for eliminating gender stereotypes, as well as different management and leadership methodologies and new organisational and management models of enterprises.
in writing. ‒ the data speak for themselves and the gap between male and female entrepreneurship is huge in terms of both employment and net earned income. the heavy burden of family and parental care and the traditional gender roles of women and men are hampering women's entrepreneurial ambitions and potential. contrary to the claims that women are more risk averse and less self-confident, it should be acknowledged that there is a tendency in society to consider a female entrepreneurial project less likely to succeed, with a consequent greater difficulty for women to access finance. my vote on this report is in favour, as it calls on the european commission and the member states to establish strategic policies and take concrete action to enable a reconciliation between work and personal life, facilitating access to services, guaranteeing access to credit, tax and financial support for women entrepreneurs, including through european microfinance instruments such as progress. through further cultural change to remove stereotypes and all forms of discrimination, it will therefore be possible to remove barriers and allow women entrepreneurs to express their full potential.
