in writing. ‒ youth unemployment is a scourge for our society. fighting it must be our priority. more flexible education systems, multidisciplinary approaches, support for entrepreneurial culture and better links between school and work are needed. i think it is extremely important to involve young people in decision-making processes, to create partnerships between local authorities, employment services and businesses. the local authorities also need to be given appropriate training to use european funds more effectively and strategically. i believe it is essential to ensure entrepreneurship training at all levels of education, to remove administrative and financial obstacles to starting and running businesses by simplifying procedures, and to ensure easier access to microfinance and credit.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which promotes policies to combat youth unemployment by developing new skills required by the labour market. the problem of youth unemployment affects millions of young european citizens, and reducing it remains a priority, otherwise europe will lose an entire generation. governments must commit themselves to the proper implementation of the youth employment initiative and the youth guarantee. it is crucial to increase the long-term benefits of the opportunities we offer to this population.
in writing. reducing the alarming level of youth unemployment is one of the eu's main challenges today. at the same time there are two million unfilled jobs for which there is no adequately trained staff. this situation constitutes a serious threat to the social cohesion and economic development of the eu. the five star movement worked hard on this text, proposing amendments against youth unemployment and working to get them passed. the report, which i voted in favour of, stresses the importance of more flexible education systems which allow for the integration and development of knowledge and skills at all stages of the professional career. the key role played by enterprises, including smes, social and solidarity economy actors and microenterprises in vocational skills training and job creation for young people is also highlighted. the text also highlights the need to provide young people with an education that prepares them for entrepreneurship as widely as possible. the real employment needs for the future and the areas of job development for young people, with a focus on the social and green economy, which are the objective of the coming years, must be clarified.

in writing. ‒ the eu aims to create a digital single market that will enable the digital economy to expand, while ensuring more competitive services for consumers and growth for businesses. the strategy is to facilitate online access to products and services across europe, through a long and gradual legislative path on infrastructure investment, increased citizen participation in digital life and new rules for online commerce. in fact, only 15% of citizens buy online from another country and only 7% of businesses sell in another eu country. i therefore voted in favour, because the creation of a fully functioning digital single market could benefit the european economy and above all its citizens.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because, even beyond its specific merits, it is part of a process that has been affecting us all for some years now and which is strongly re-proposed for the future: a firm producing goods that interest 10% of the population, if it also has to compete with competitors, will probably not find it profitable to remain in a small market and will give up production. but if that market is ten times bigger, the numbers can get a lot more interesting, and if that company can tap into some of the excellence in raw materials, human resources, or whatever, it can take over the market. this is the essence of the digital single market: a ploy to expand the market and make sure that the good guys can play for a much higher stake by dragging the whole industry with them. it's a big bet, that a land of excellence like ours can't miss.

in writing. the european commission is ready to sanction poland for the new media law that has just been passed. the commission is considering initiating the procedure provided for in article 7 of the treaty on european union, which provides for the suspension of the voting rights of a member state in the council in the event of a serious and persistent breach of the values enshrined in article 2 of the treaty. the new polish government has been accused of undermining media freedom and information pluralism, because the new law, among other things, reserves to the ministry of treasury, and no longer to the national broadcasting council (the equivalent of agcom), the power to appoint and dismiss the heads of public broadcasting companies. the situation is similar to the rules approved by the renzi government on the governance of rai, which give unprecedented power to the president of the council, contrary to what was established by the consulta in judgment no 225 of 1974. the european commission is therefore right to try to clarify the situation in poland and to remove any doubts, and it should do the same with regard to italy: the rule of law, freedom of expression and information pluralism are all too important for democracy.

valuable for institutions or people. this is one of those cases. this is the global role of the european union. this is our strength. this is the strength of our contribution, somehow, to peace in the conflict. i could not agree more. that is why it is much more convenient for us to invest in conflict prevention than to try to find a way out of a conflict that has already exploded. but there is a way – i would say a european way – of facilitating dialogue, facilitating cooperation, finding mediation, encouraging compromise also, because this comes from our history too. this will come up in the following debate on the situation in syria and the debate after that on tensions in the middle east. at the end of the day, it is always the same story. european history is a history of conflicts – centuries of conflicts – that we have somehow spread around the world, dragging others into our own conflicts and wars, and which we finally managed to stop at the point when we discovered that regional cooperation and reconciliation within europe was the way out. that brought us peace, stability and prosperity, even if we sometimes tend to forget this today. so it is our european way that can bring hope and in some way good stories around the world. it is also the role of the european union to invest in good stories, making them possible, and, once they do happen, making them be lasting peace. please, we cannot afford another failure on the path to peace and reconciliation. this is the spirit, i think, in which we engage, we continue to engage, with our colombian friends, knowing that the way ahead is still difficult and we should not take it for granted, but knowing that it is possible. i am also convinced that 2016 can be the year when this conflict finally comes to an end and colombia can find its peace.

the agenda includes the statement by the vice-president of the commission / high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy on the situation in syria (2015/2517 ((rsp)).
vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs.– mr president, in syria we are facing the biggest humanitarian tragedy in our region since the second world war. six and a half million syrians are internally displaced, and if the fighting continues these could be the refugees of tomorrow. around 400 000 syrians have no access to humanitarian aid, especially in areas that are besieged. we now have 4.6 million syrian refugees in the neighbouring countries, with chances being high that this number will continue to grow due to intense fighting on the ground. starvation inside syria is used as a means of warfare against the weakest and most vulnerable people on the ground, in particular against women and children. the syrian government has now guaranteed humanitarian access in madaya, but this is far from being enough. in other ongoing sieges, people have been trapped for months, unable to exit, with no access to food, no access to medication and no access to basic services. several local ceasefires reached in recent months are a reason for hope, for example in the waer neighbourhood of homs, but still they stopped far short. the goal of a nationwide ceasefire between the government and the opposition is an urgent one. the bombings and targeting of civilian areas and structures such as hospitals and schools, in particular by the syrian regime and its allies, are unacceptable. this is why it is crucial that, in parallel with the efforts to start a political process, we call for all parties to cease all attacks and bombing of civilian targets, to put an end to the sieges of civilian areas and to fully respect international humanitarian law. it would be a disaster if, as we manage hopefully to start the political process, the situation on the ground does not improve; the credibility of the whole process would suffer enormously. some progress was made in the fight against da’esh in iraq, but less so in syria. let me say very clearly that the terrorist group cannot and will most probably not be fully defeated if the civil war in syria continues. daesh bases its own survival and its propaganda on sectarian strife and chaos in syria and in iraq, and only a united syria – only a syria that puts an end to its own civil war and finds ways to reconciliation – will defeat daesh once and for all. in these weeks and days, this is somehow a real condition to not only fight, but also to defeat, daesh. we have worked hard to build such a united front outside syria and inside syria, with the european union playing a crucial role first and foremost for humanitarian reasons, but also because we know very well that ending the war in syria concerns our own security because it is clearly the condition to better fight against daesh, and it is in our own interests. the consensus we reached in the international syria support group – first in vienna with two rounds of difficult but successful talks, and then in new york in december – led to the unanimous adoption of un security council resolution 2254 last december. finally, we managed to unite the international community around a roadmap, endorsing the talks in vienna, their format and their content, and showing the syrians and the regional actors that there is unity on the international side to indicate the way forward. the resolution calls for intra-syrian talks between the government and the opposition. preparations are underway and the talks are foreseen to start in geneva next week. the resolution sets up a schedule of six months for the establishment of inclusive and credible governance in syria and a target of 18 months for free and fair elections based on a new syrian constitution with the clarification of the fact that wherever the election takes place it will have to see the syrians outside syria taking part in it too. in parallel with the political process, the resolution also calls for the development of confidence-building measures between parties in conflict and for a mechanism of implementation and the monitoring of ceasefire. this is clearly a very ambitious calendar, a very ambitious agenda, but it is clear that we cannot afford to waste time and we have to set high objectives in order to have some hope that the process starts. as peace gets closer – as the possibility of starting this process gets real – we see that the resistance from the enemies of peace is getting even stronger. i believe we should consider the current phase as a window of opportunity that was not there in the past years. let me say that this window might not be open forever if we miss this chance, and let me add that i believe that we finally managed to bring all the different regional actors around the same table on the syrian conflict partly because we managed last july to find an agreement on the iranian deal, opening the way for the possibility – although not yet the reality – of a different kind of cooperation in the region. we will discuss that in the next debate. the conditions are there again, but the way forward will be bumpy, difficult and challenging for all. the un special envoy for syria, staffan de mistura, has our full and united support. we have put this issue on the agenda of all the last foreign affairs council meetings – the last one took place just yesterday – and we discussed at length on how, united, we can support the process and the work of staffan de mistura. i am in constant contact with him; i met him just a few days ago in brussels to discuss exactly the preparation of the talks, the way ahead, and how the european union as such, together with the member states, in a coordinated way, can further contribute to the implementation of the un security council resolution. yesterday, the foreign affairs ministers discussed syria and our further work on the implementation of this resolution. the european union and the member states will provide support to the intra-syrian talks and the entire transition process in terms of mediation, expertise and consensus—building. we will support the ceasefires, and once the ceasefires are in place – whether local ceasefires or a national ceasefire – we are preparing to step up our aid to the syrian people. this also includes local governance needs, rehabilitation and reconstruction of the country, because it is key that, as we are trying to do in iraq, liberated areas or areas in times of ceasefire or peace are immediately supported with humanitarian aid wherever the access of humanitarian aid is possible. as you know, the european union is the biggest donor to the management of the syrian crisis, with almost eur 5 billion that we have mobilised so far. the ministers also agreed yesterday on a european union common approach and preparation towards the upcoming syria-london conference that will be hosted in london by the uk and co-hosted by germany, norway and kuwait on 4 february. we have already prepared substantial support to turkey. we are putting together further additional comprehensive support packages for jordan and lebanon, not only to support them in their remarkable work in protecting and hosting refugees, but also to strengthen the resilience of the two countries, which has been tested in different ways in each country, and it is a top priority for the european union to invest in the resilience of these two countries in order to prevent them from facing major security, social, economic or political problems that could turn the crisis in syria into something even bigger. in addition, we need to be ready for the fast deployment of humanitarian and civilisation aid once the conditions change inside syria to make sure that, if and when we get to the point of something close to peace, the country can be rebuilt in all forms. later in the evening, we will discuss the current tensions between saudi arabia and iran. let me just reiterate that i had lengthy discussions with the foreign ministers of both countries to convey the message that it is vital that the syrian talks are protected and that there is no serious spillover of these bilateral tensions over this multilateral process that has finally, and in a difficult way, started. it is also vital that together as europeans, in a coordinated way, and together with our partners, starting with the united states but also others, we pass on the same message to all the interlocutors in the region. all those with influence over the warring parties inside syria should help them walk the difficult path towards peace. confidence-building measures in particular have to be implemented immediately to create a favourable environment for the talks, and to guarantee that the process is credible and delivers to the syrian people immediately. this is a critical phase for the political process. what we agreed on in vienna and new york with regional and international actors has to become reality on the ground, otherwise it will not fly. only the syrian parties and people can make this happen with the help of the international community, which, as i see, is ready to do that. last week i met with riad hijab, the coordinator of the syrian opposition’s high negotiations committee, and i confirmed the eu’s readiness to support these talks and to provide capacity-building during negotiations and afterwards and during the political transition when it starts. we also support the work of the un envoy for inclusive representation in the talks and accompany him in the difficult task of arranging the way in which the talks can be organised. only a comprehensive representation of syrian groups will help us to reach the much needed consensus for the way ahead. let me also say something that is not normally mentioned: the role of syrian society in managing the way out of this conflict. i believe the civil society inside syria will play a major role in the implementation and monitoring of confidence-building measures, for example local ceasefires, and so the civil society in its different parts and ways needs to be brought into the discussion as early as possible, and all minorities and religious groups should have a say. excluding this or that group on sectarian or ethnic grounds would be a non-starter. inclusiveness is the only way forward towards national reconciliation and will be the most powerful and the most effective way to defeat daesh: we have seen this in the past in iraq. we have to try to avoid the mistakes that were made in previous years. the work to build a democratic, non-sectarian, inclusive syria has only just begun, but we are finally heading in the right direction. peace in syria is possible, and we have shown in the last year that some incredible things and positive things are indeed possible. the transition can start and daesh can be defeated. the international and regional players have finally united after five years, five long years of work to make it possible, and it is now time for the syrians to take this opportunity to start the transition, to stop the war, and to stop daesh, and they will need to know – as we have been telling them all – that we will be at their side, continuing to work for the unity of the international community and the region to make this process possible. i have just member of the commission.– madam president, i would like to congratulate and thank ms griesbeck and all the shadow rapporteurs for their work and dedication on this file, which made a swift agreement on this directive possible. this text is not merely a statement of principle. our objective was to make the presumption of innocence effective in all the member states. this directive will strengthen the right to a fair trial and protect the rights of suspects and accused persons in the european union. today great disparities in the protection of the presumption of innocence exist in europe, as evidenced by the recent and still-too-frequent condemnations of member states by the european court of human rights. the compromise text on which you will vote tomorrow is carefully balanced. it is based on the european convention on human rights and the case law of the european court of human rights. the directive prohibits public references to guilt, and it contains clear rules on the burden of proof. the burden of proof is on the prosecution, and any doubt is to benefit the suspect or accused person. the right to remain silent and the right not to incriminate oneself are protected. the directive will also harmonise the right to be present at the trial, which is an important aspect of the right to a fair trial. the commission would like to add two declarations to this compromise. the first is a clarification of our understanding of the text concerning the right to remain silent and the right not to incriminate oneself. the second is our position on the question of the burden of proof. the commission regrets the deletion of a paragraph on its initial proposal on presumptions of fact or law. our concern was that, as such presumptions already exist in member states, it is important to have them regulated in the text of the directive so that all the safeguards for defendants are precisely set out. this being said, the overall compromise is highly satisfactory. the standards set in this directive will become eu law and will be enforced as such. the commission will closely follow the transposition and the implementation of this directive in member states and will ensure that it is correctly applied in practice. commission’s statements (written text) 1. relating to article 6 on the burden of proof "the commission regrets the deletion of article 5, paragraph 2, of its proposal for a directive on the strengthening of certain aspects of the presumption of innocence and of the right to be present at trial in criminal proceedings. the commission considers that the compromise in relation to article 6 may lead to problems in the implementation of this directive, in terms of legal certainty, monitoring and operability, which may increase the risk of unnecessary litigation, in particular at national level. however, the commission does not stand in the way of the adoption of this directive ". 2. relating to article 7, paragraph 6, on the right to remain silent and the right not to incriminate oneself "the commission considers that article 7, paragraph 6, of the directive on the strengthening of certain aspects of the presumption of innocence and of the right to be present at the trial in criminal proceedings must be interpreted as merely confirming the possibility for member states to decide that, with regard to minor offences, the conduct of the proceedings, or certain stages thereof, may take place in writing or without questioning of the suspect or accused person by the competent authorities. in contrast, this provision does not allow derogating from the rights enshrined in article 7, and it may notably not be interpreted as obliging a suspect to make any statements in relation to the facts at issue or allowing a member state to draw negative consequences from the exercise of the suspects' right to remain silent.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i also want to thank mr griesbeck for the excellent work he has done. the presumption of innocence is indeed a basic principle of the rule of law, but the absence of a common framework of guarantees has allowed for its violation and has hindered trust between states, especially in sensitive but crucial areas. i am thinking, for example, of mutual recognition of certain preventive confiscation measures, which are essential in the fight against organised crime. this directive aims to fill this gap. the libe committee had strengthened the commission's proposal and i am glad that the final text preserves many of the advances to which i myself had tried to contribute through some amendments. even on some particularly sensitive issues, such as the burden of proof, the conditions for the use of coercive powers, the possibility of taking into account the conduct of the accused for the purposes of the judgment, balanced solutions were also reached on these issues. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos is a very important one.
in writing. judicial cooperation in criminal matters needs a common basis for the safeguarding of fundamental rights and it is therefore very important that the measures forming part of the package on european procedural rights are adopted swiftly. they are a sign of the level of agreement reached by the member states on this matter and should aim to increase the guarantees. the presumption of innocence and the right to be present at criminal proceedings are among the cornerstones of a fair trial, as demonstrated by the fact that they are enshrined in the european convention on human rights, the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, the international covenant on civil and political rights and the universal declaration of human rights. the commission has also proposed that the court of justice should be able to give its opinion on the case before it.
in writing. the european union's commitment to procedural guarantees for defendants is particularly important with regard to the presumption of innocence. the commission has sent parliament a proposal which is not very ambitious, and we have undertaken to improve it, first by removing the unacceptable clause which allowed the burden of proof to be reversed, but which must always be on the prosecution, along with the affirmation of the principle of 'in dubio pro reo'. we have also strengthened the wording of the right not to incriminate oneself, to refuse to cooperate and to remain silent, also stipulating that the exercise of this right cannot be used against suspects or accused persons. the presumption of innocence must, moreover, be valid at all stages of the proceedings until their final conclusion. this requires particular caution from the public authorities, who, while leaving the prerogatives of the public prosecution and freedom of information unimpaired, must always avoid presenting the accused as guilty before the final judgment. in the context of the desirable approximation of criminal procedure legislation, this directive, although it does not yet achieve the maximum of the guarantees already guaranteed by some member states, by the charter of fundamental rights and by the echr, which in any case remain unaffected, is certainly a positive and acceptable result. ♪ i'm not a girl ♪

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on personal protective equipment. as stated in the text voted, council directive 89/686/eec needs to be replaced in order to update the entire regulatory framework for this type of goods on the single market and to streamline and simplify the sources of law still in force. the regulation clarifies the role of economic operators, strengthens cooperation between all those concerned, introduces common definitions and clarifies the responsibilities of market surveillance authorities. the directive also introduces an obligation for importers and distributors to inform the manufacturer and the market surveillance authorities of non-compliant devices. the text which has been presented to us fully achieves the objectives which were identified and i have therefore voted in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on personal protective equipment. since 1989, the presence of personal protective equipment (ppe) on the eu market has been fully harmonised by council directive 89/686/eec. however, the current ipr legislation needs to be updated in line with the new regulatory framework, which is a package of measures designed to streamline and simplify the regulations on goods in the single market. the ipr regulation replacing the current directive 89/686/eec responds to the need to improve the protection of the health and safety of users and to ensure the free movement of ipr on the eu market.
in writing. ‒ italian companies are european leaders in the production of personal protective equipment. it is therefore good news that we are further harmonizing technical standards to reduce the possible non-tariff barriers that our products face when they enter other markets. the great strength of the eu, and the greatest reason why it is worth being in europe, is precisely this huge potential market for italian products, and helping businesses to seize this potential is our task as members of parliament. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i support the updating of the existing directive to bring it into line with the new legislative framework and the provision of the regulation instrument which improves harmonisation between the different national systems. improved personal protective equipment undoubtedly increases the safety of those who wear it and reduces health risks.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on personal protective equipment (ppe) simplifies and improves existing legislation, which is an outdated directive. a legislative measure that finally defines a harmonised and clear european regulatory framework, interprets and applies the provisions on products of daily use for european citizens and workers, such as protective clothing and headgear, life jackets and sunglasses. the regulation i voted for also lays down common technical standards, compliance and safety requirements and specific rules for the supervision of the market in personal protective equipment. a series of technical measures to further protect the health of users of these products, safeguard their safety and ensure fair and simplified conditions of competition for european companies producing these products. the updating of european standards is necessary for the completion of the single market and for the proper functioning of a sector of importance to european and italian industry, such as that of personal protective equipment, which has over 4000 companies and an estimated annual average turnover of several billion. italy is the leader and the main producer in this sector.

in writing. ‒ given the need to adapt the current directive, which was launched in 1989, to the new regulatory framework (nrc), we welcome the ford report. in particular, the reform is intended as a means of simplifying and clarifying the current legislation, which has been criticised for its alleged repetitiveness and lack of precision. the proposed text also aims to strengthen cooperation between the various actors, both institutional and non-institutional, by providing definitions and rules common to the european union as regards the treatment of goods placed on the european market whose safety is in question. we also agree with the rapporteur's intention not to upset the current regulatory framework by changing its objectives. the reform is designed to update and improve the instruments provided by the previous directive, while sharing its objectives. the purpose of the legislation is to ensure maximum safety for users of personal protective equipment, workers and consumers, within a common community framework. we also share innovations in market surveillance and corporate responsibility obligations. finally, the text appears to be consistent with the strategy for harmonizing the common market adopted by the european commission.

in writing. ‒ the current legislation on personal protective equipment (ppe), while well-functioning, requires an update in line with the new regulatory framework (nfr), which is a package of measures designed to streamline and simplify regulations on goods in the single market. in particular, this regulation clarifies the role of economic operators and introduces common definitions. in addition, it is proposed to eliminate the maximum five-year validity of the eu certificate of competence as, according to economic operators, this period is too short in relation to the normal life of ppe. i voted in favour of this report, hoping that the negotiations on this dossier can be concluded quickly.

in writing. - i abstained. our delegation has always opposed the current system of generalised tariff preferences in the eu (and its recent reform), not because we do not believe that these types of instruments are useful and appropriate (they should facilitate trade for poor or less developed countries), but because we believe that they should be limited to a much smaller number of beneficiaries. the beneficiaries of the gsp+ system are not only countries with unfavourable economic conditions, but also producers who can create market distortions with their exports to europe (think of pakistan's textiles or the philippines' fisheries, for example). for these reasons, therefore, we find it instrumental to object to kyrgyzstan, a former soviet state in central asia which certainly does not represent a problem in terms of potential competition with our production system and which, incidentally, seems to be getting closer politically to putin's russia.

in writing. ‒ weaning foods play a key role in the transition from a diet based entirely on breast milk to a diet with the introduction of solid foods. each of these products must meet high standards of quality and be formulated in such a way as to enable the infant to receive the nutrients required for his specific stage of development. the who recently published a recommendation that there should be no added salt or sugar in infant formulae. this is a much more restrictive position than that laid down in part 3 of annex i to the delegated regulation submitted by the commission, which provides that 30% of the energy supplied by infant foods may come from sugar. it is precisely in view of this that i decided to vote in favour of the objection, considering that the commission has not paid sufficient attention to the dimension of the protection of children's health.

in writing. the who recommends limiting sugar intake to less than 10% of total energy consumption, making it clear that adhering to the 5% limit would offer greater guarantees to prevent the onset of certain diseases. however, according to the european commission's proposal, sugars could still account for up to 30% of the calorie intake of baby food, which is three times more than the recommended amount. the introduction of such high levels of sugar in foods, especially at such an early age, would have contributed to the increase in childhood obesity and could affect children's food preferences. in particular, as recommended by who, for infants and young children, added sugar levels should be kept to a minimum. given that poor nutrition is still the single biggest cause of illness and death worldwide, even more so than smoking, alcohol and physical inactivity taken together, i find the commission's proposal puzzling. i therefore voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because i believe that the maximum level of sugar allowed in foodstuffs must be brought into line with the requirements laid down by the world health organization.

on behalf of the efdd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, thank you for being here and for the work you have done in paris, which we all appreciated. the agreement is a compromise, because 195 countries were sitting around the table, so it could not have been otherwise. as with any compromise, there are positive aspects, which you and your colleagues have already mentioned, and negative aspects, on which i should like to focus. it is disappointing, for example, that the word decarbonisation disappears: our goal should be to stop emitting, but instead we're left with a definition that's a little ambiguous because it says to strike a balance between anthropogenic emissions and removals through greenhouse gas sources. we are talking about negative emissions technology, which would of course offset the positive emissions that are obviously left over. we've created an alibi, and it's an alibi that involves advanced technology and massive land use. in the agreement scenario these technologies are absolutely crucial, but at the moment they are in a very experimental state, very expensive and we don't know if they work, they don't work everywhere at the moment. now i ask you specifically, we would like to know what is the real capacity to implement these negative emission technologies on a very large scale and what are the measures that governments will be taking to facilitate this process? another point is the market, the ets system. it is a system which we believe is not working, it has failed to stimulate investment in new technologies to reduce emissions and this has led to fraud and financial speculation. the establishment of a global market, as called for in the paris agreement, is even more worrying because of the delay it would cause in the implementation of other policies which have had a more significant impact on the eu than the ets, such as incentive tariffs for renewable sources and energy saving and efficiency measures. finally, we must close the gap between our perception of reality and reality itself, or we will be too slow to make changes. article 12 of the agreement is good and we welcome it, but it must be implemented with determination and precise messages are needed that are proportionate to the problems. we need them now and above all they must be directed at citizens and local authorities, so that they too can work with commitment. we have to make it clear what we're playing at and that there's no more time to play.

member of the commission, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy.– madam president, i am grateful, on behalf of the high representative, for this opportunity to take stock of where we are concerning the association agreement and the implementation, as approved a year ago in this house, with ukraine, georgia, and moldova. for ukraine, the dcfta can bring significant economic benefits. ukrainian businesses will now receive stable and predictable preferential access to the largest market in the world, with 500 million customers, and eu enterprises will be able to benefit from easier access to the ukrainian market, so we must help ukraine develop the right conditions to encourage new business and investment relationships. over 20 meetings were held in trilateral format to address alleged russian concerns about the dcfta implementation. now ukraine faces a number of measures imposed by russia impeding trade and transit and will need our support here too. in 2016 we will be stepping up our efforts to support ukraine with more coordination with eu member states and greater visibility for our work. particularly on the implementation of the dcfta, we will build on current support programmes to improve the business climate, provide support to small and medium-sized enterprises, and help ukraine find new markets. ukraine needs to show it is open for business by aligning with eu standards in key sectors and taking decisive action on the rule of law. the support group for ukraine is playing a key role with the commission in all these areas. despite very challenging circumstances, the ukrainian government has made progress in implementing the association agreement. the national anti-corruption bureau and the new national police force have started to work. the selection process for an anti-corruption prosecutor has been completed. the government has also adopted a law on the natural gas market, which aims at bringing the gas sector of ukraine into line with the eu third energy package. these developments were welcomed at the second association council in brussels which was held on 7 december, but we should not underestimate the challenges ahead. the fight against corruption, reform of the judiciary and the public administration, as well as amendments to the constitution, particularly the second reading on decentralisation, will require courage and political will. shortly before christmas, we published our final report on ukraine’s implementation of the visa liberalisation action plan which concluded that, since the necessary process has been made and the number of additional commitments undertaken by the ukrainian leadership, a positive recommendation for visa-free travel could be made. we aim to present a legislative proposal to pave the way for visa liberalisation with ukraine soon. turning to moldova, the country has made great strides in concluding and implementing the association agreement and dcfta with the european union. since 1 january the region of transnistria also has the possibility to trade preferentially under the dcfta, making an important contribution to our conflict resolutions, but recent moldovan governments have not implemented important reforms. we are currently witnessing a highly unstable political situation, which is also an obstacle to the effective implementation of the association agreement and making full use of opportunities. the country is in great need of stable leadership, with the determination and energy required to address a number of problematic issues, including high-level corruption. this is necessary before moldova can proceed with other key reforms, in particular in the justice, financial and media sectors and the reform of the public administration. i have just received information that there was a positive vote on the new government and i hope this is now a stable one. i think we should support any government that is ready to undertake the necessary reforms, and it is also important to provide the necessary substantial support in terms of staff, human resources, but also, if needed, and this is definitely the case, in terms of money, provided that there is a positive assessment by the imf. finally, as regards georgia, impressive efforts have been made to implement the association agreement and the results are already visible, with strong growth in foreign direct investment. other indicators also show promising signs. the visa liberalisation action plan has proven to be an effective tool for promoting a range of reforms, but georgia has gone beyond the action plan benchmarks and taken further steps to reform the judiciary as well as the prosecutor’s office. in this regard, we also closely monitor the authorities to ensure that there is no unlawful conduct targeting the constitutional court and its personnel. the result was our positive report last december and with georgia, too, we will press ahead now with legislation to achieve full visa liberation as soon as possible. in summary, we can be happy that we have already come so far with our three association agreement partners, but we still have a long way to go and no room at all for complacency. i look forward to hearing the honourable members’ views during this debate today.

member of the commission.– madam president, let me start by thanking you for your support for the continuing development of eu-kosovo relations. i also want to thank the foreign affairs and international trade committees and rapporteurs – ulrike lunacek in particular – for their support. tomorrow’s vote on the stabilisation and association agreement, renegotiated with kosovo, is testament to this focus. the saa is a milestone in eu-kosovo relations and of critical importance for the future of kosovo and the whole western balkans. the agreement is the first formal contractual relationship that ties the european union and kosovo together. it allows kosovo to join the rest of the region, sharing the benefits of deepening political and economic interdependence and sharing in the common european perspectives that make peace, stability and prosperity our joint goal. the agreement will help kosovo with much-needed economic reform underpinned by the rule of law. this should ensure a more predictable business environment, leading to much-needed growth and jobs. the agreement helps establish a stable legal framework and gradual approximation with eu laws and standards. it also promotes the free movement of goods, services and capital and envisages higher standards and increased choice and lower prices for kosovo citizens. it should stimulate kosovo’s progress in the area of transport and energy as it foresees the gradual integration into europe’s energy markets and the development of quality infrastructure. the agreement should also strengthen regional cooperation. under its terms, kosovo commits itself to a visible and sustainable improvement in relations with serbia. this is an essential principle of our agreement. the continuation of the eu-facilitated dialogue with serbia is therefore a legal obligation. kosovo will need to implement the agreements it has reached and continue to work towards further agreements. as we have seen over the last few months, this sometimes involves taking difficult decisions and the need for compromise. finally, i want to underline that the agreement includes provisions that commit kosovo to high international standards in terms of respect for democratic principles. this is of particular relevance to the challenges kosovo is facing at the moment. it means that the institutions set up to ensure democratic government and the rules that allow these institutions to do their work should be respected. it also means there can be no obstruction to free and transparent political discourse. obstruction and violence have no place in a democratic system. allow me to use this opportunity to call on kosovo’s politicians to engage in a free political exchange to solve the differences in a way that is worthy of the country’s european perspective: without obstructions, without violence and without threats and intimidation. allow me to thank you once more for your support, and i look forward to the debate.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as the high representative, federica mogherini, has said, the signing of the stabilisation and association agreement between the european union and kosovo marks the beginning of a new phase in relations between the 28 member states and kosovo. the agreement is an important contribution to stability and prosperity in the region and will help to undertake the necessary reforms that create the conditions for stable and sustainable growth, to implement the necessary reforms and to create trade and investment opportunities. the kosovo government continues to work on the reform process which will enable the country to modernise, grow economically and competitively and, as a result, provide a better future for its citizens. kosovo still faces many challenges, and i hope that the government will commit itself to making the necessary and courageous choices to continue the negotiations with the european union successfully.
in writing. ‒ since 2000, kosovo has enjoyed preferential trade arrangements with the eu, providing duty-free and quota-free access to the european market, except for certain agricultural and fishery products. the eu-kosovo stabilisation and association agreement establishes new contractual relations that can strengthen political dialogue between the institutions and improve integration and trade cooperation. the agreement represents a first step towards the formal and gradual accession process of the republic of kosovo, providing, inter alia, new opportunities for investment, growth and business development. for these reasons i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the balkan region is a key part of european history, culture and civilization. after a terrible season of war and violence, many countries in this part of europe have been welcomed into the great political and economic project of the european union. kosovo, which declared independence in 2008, has embarked on a path of opening up, consolidation of democratic institutions and affirmation of civil rights that has yet to be fully realized. i voted in favour of the eu-kosovo stabilisation and association agreement because i believe it is an important step towards strengthening political dialogue and establishing closer trade relations. the economic and social development of the country can only be achieved through a complete stabilisation of the whole region, which can also be achieved through forms of cooperation with the union in the field of justice and home affairs. europe has already shown great concern for the countries bordering on it, and with this text it is undertaking to continue important work in this direction. for these reasons i have decided to vote in favour of the agreement.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the lunacek report is unbalanced and not acceptable, which is why i did not intend to support it with my vote.

in writing. ‒ the strengthening of relations with kosovo and the privileged trade relationship aimed at the region's inclusion in the european free trade area is instrumental to the region's inclusion in the european system. only a fully european kosovo will be able to develop economically and strengthen culturally, making its democratic institutions and civil rights practices more solid. the european union must take responsibility for protecting and guiding its neighbourhood towards development and democracy, with particular regard to those territories which have experienced a troubled, suffering and complex history such as kosovo over the last thirty years. the eu-kosovo stabilisation and association agreement (saa) is a key point in the process of normalising relations in the area and overcoming the regional isolation of the former yugoslav territories, to which we must all contribute, both in european and in the home countries.

in writing. ‒ this is a single vote to approve the eu-kosovo stabilisation and association agreement. the agreement, which helps improve political dialogue and open trade between the eu and kosovo, was signed in october 2015 by the eu's foreign policy chief, federica mogherini, and ratified by kosovo's national parliament last november. all matters dealt with in this agreement fall within the eu's competence. this makes it an 'eu only' agreement: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial instruments are not used to the detriment of the community's own resources. the european parliament cannot take a position on the text of the agreement but can only express a favourable or unfavourable opinion. my vote was in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the union, of the stabilisation and association agreement between the european union and the european atomic energy community, of the one part, and kosovo, of the other part. the agreement establishes contractual relations involving enhanced political dialogue, closer trade integration and new forms of cooperation in the fields of human rights, education, the environment, energy, justice and home affairs, and aims to create a free trade area. the asa is a very important first step towards the formal eu accession process and the european integration path of the republic of kosovo, and is expected to be strengthened through the introduction of the visa-free regime for kosovo citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this draft decision because i believe that a good neighbourhood policy is essential to prevent many problems, not just a few. it is no coincidence that the migratory flows we are witnessing today are the result of a neighbourhood policy, and a wider foreign policy, which has been flooded on all sides. this agreement with kosovo is a major boost to the modernisation and greater interoperability of the infrastructure, particularly legal infrastructure, which can allow our companies to do business there. moreover, the ultimate aim of these steps is to reduce poverty in kosovo, with the consequence of importing less crime from there and creating an additional outlet market for our products. it's a win-win situation.
in writing. ‒ the creation of a free trade area between the eu and kosovo is important as trade relations with kosovo, thanks to the facilitations provided by the tariff reduction, have already generated a considerable surplus for the union since 2014. i am therefore in favour of the conclusion of the stabilisation agreement with kosovo, as this would only further improve relations between the two trading partners. the results will be positive for cooperation and will provide a solid basis for the definition of reforms in that country with a view to approximating legislation in the interests not only of economic trade but also of social and human rights.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, solidarity, mutual aid and assistance between the member states are among the founding values of the european union. the full and unanimous support which all the member states have expressed to france and their readiness to provide all the necessary aid and assistance following the invoking of the mutual defence clause by france itself after the paris attacks should therefore be welcomed. however, as the report indicates, there are currently no practical arrangements to ensure an effective response in the event that a member state invokes the mutual defence clause. the high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy, federica mogherini, is therefore working to further define the guidelines and practical arrangements for the future activation of the mutual defence clause, in order to ensure a swift decision in the council in support of the member state under attack. i very much hope that the present activation of the clause will act as a catalyst to exploit the potential of all the provisions of the treaty on security and defence and, above all, that it will pave the way for a common foreign policy of the european union in syria and the middle east, where an integrated european approach is currently lacking.
in writing. ‒ the serious terrorist attacks in paris on 13 november 2015 prompted the french government to invoke the defence clause in article 42 (7) teu. for the first time in the history of the union, a member state has asked for this mechanism to be activated, requesting help and assistance from other states following an aggression. the unanimous acceptance of the position expressed by the president of the french republic was a turning point in the union's defence policy. i voted in favour of the resolution on the mutual defence clause because i believe that it is a starting point for urging the council and the member states to start fully implementing the security and defence architecture provided for in the treaties. after the failure of the ecsc in 1954, european countries did not commit themselves sufficiently to developing a defence system capable of achieving ambitious objectives, but the treaty of lisbon opened the way to permanent structured cooperation in defence. the great challenges of our time can only be met by an eu united in its foreign policy and equipped with the tools to intervene in different contexts.
in writing. ‒ it is time for the eu to set out clear and firm guidelines on the 'mutual defence clause' to ensure an effective response should a member state invoke its application, as president hollande did after the terrorist attacks in paris on 13 november. all european countries must make the maximum effort to combat terrorism and a more rigorous approach must be taken at both national and union level. for all these reasons i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this document because i believe that, following the activation of the mutual defence clause under article 42 (7) of the treaty on european union, it is important that the member states provide all the necessary assistance to france and that, at the same time, efforts are made to prepare instruments to make the effective application of the measures provided for in the clause more effective and efficient.
in writing. - i vote for it. the mutual defense clause was invoked by hollande (and for the first time in europe) on 13 november 2015 following the paris attacks. the resolution condemns in the strongest terms the terrorist attacks perpetrated by isis and expresses concern that the management of aid and assistance under the mutual defence clause on a bilateral basis as in this case will not be possible for all member states; the european council therefore calls on the european council to give impetus to the development of this clause and urges it to develop the facilitating role of the relevant eu institutions. it therefore called on all european countries to commit themselves to the fight against terrorism and to adopt a rigorous approach at both national and non-national level. it calls for appropriate measures to control the movement of weapons, explosives and suspicious persons. it urges the member states to set up a structured system for information sharing and operational cooperation for border management, police and other law enforcement agencies, as well as the sharing of national databases.
in writing. ‒ the resolution expresses concern at france's decision to activate the mutual defence clause in article 42 (7) teu following the tragic events in paris on 13 november. despite some positive remarks in the text, i think that there is too much leniency in the approach to the missed opportunity to use a clause that was much more suited to the situation in question. it seemed more appropriate to invoke article 222 tfeu, which governs the case where a member state is the victim of a terrorist attack. the use of article 42 (7) teu, which is applicable where a member state is the victim of an armed attack, not only risks implicitly recognising daesh as a state but also confirms the primacy of the intergovernmental approach over the community approach. for these reasons i have decided to vote against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure because i believe that the fight against international terrorism is one of the union's priorities and that only with an autonomous security and defence capability will the eu be able to address the enormous threats and challenges to internal and external security. following the terrorist attacks in paris on 13 november 2015, the french government officially invoked the mutual defence clause referred to in article 42 (7) teu. the eu member states are obliged to provide aid and assistance to france by all means in their power, in accordance with article 51 of the charter of the united nations. parliament believes that the present case should act as a catalyst for in-depth political discussions on the multidimensional nature of european security and defence; calls on all member states to maintain their unconditional and lasting support and to continue to provide their contributions for as long as necessary. the legislator stresses a holistic approach to deradicalization, including national efforts to address youth, prevent violent extremism and combat terrorism, aimed at strengthening social cohesion and preventing crime.
in writing. ‒ this clause is a very important instrument of international law, and at this specific moment it is quite relevant that france has requested that it be applied. however, there are aspects which should not be underestimated and which have emerged strongly during the negotiations for the preparation of these reports. i am therefore very pleased with the final text, to which i contributed my vote, because it represents a balanced and effective summary of the pros and cons of the decision to rely on this particular institution of international law now, and of the reasons which should guide these choices.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this very important resolution of parliament, which is being adopted on the occasion of the first use of the mutual defence clause. i think it is necessary to promote the development of this clause and to identify practical arrangements and guidelines to ensure an effective response in the event that a member state activates it to defend itself against an attack such as the one that took place in paris on 13 november. i do not think that bilateral management of these situations is the right response, since a european response is needed. this occasion can indeed be an opportunity to lay a new and stronger foundation for a strong and effective european defence union, improving the union's security and self-defence capability against external attacks which so seriously undermine its stability.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the mutual defence clause. according to this clause, contained in article 42 (7) of the treaty on european union (teu), if a country of the union is subject to armed aggression on its territory, the other eu countries are obliged to provide it with aid and assistance by all means at their disposal, in accordance with article 51 of the charter of the united nations. solidarity, mutual aid and assistance between member states, including through the use of union funds, are among the foundations of the european union. a common european strategy is essential if the principle of mutual defence is to be respected and the fight against international terrorism, which is one of the union's priorities, is to be guaranteed, and the principle of solidarity, which requires action both within and outside the union, is to be applied.
in writing. ‒ europe is a possible battleground, and in view of the recent terrorist attacks, we have a duty to show solidarity, help and assistance. mutual defence is a right that i believe should be pursued. i would give you all my full support by voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ terrorism is a reality that undermines the stability of our societies. in recent months we have witnessed a violent escalation in europe, culminating in the bloody attacks in paris on 13 november 2015. the fight against terrorism is certainly a priority for the union, as the mutual defence clause shows, but it should be remembered that efforts to prevent it must be intensified. following the atrocious events in france, the country invoked article 42 (7) for the first time in the history of the union, triggering the aforementioned clause. this is a very important instrument for establishing effective cooperation between member states and a single european defence which would make the union's external action coherent and autonomous. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that it is necessary to bring the subject up in the political debate, particularly in the council and the european parliament, in order to achieve integration between the eu's instruments in the field of security and defence and the resources of the member states, thus enhancing their effectiveness. the priority, given the events, is to ensure greater and more careful information sharing by the intelligence services of each member state.
in writing. ‒ following the terrorist attacks in paris last november, france called for the support of the other eu countries using the 'mutual defence' clause in article 42 (7) teu, which had never been used before. the clause, being used for the first time, has given rise to the need to implement ad hoc measures and to provide for entirely new management and cooperation. for this reason, the establishment of practical arrangements and guidelines for a future activation of the mutual defence clause should be a priority for the union. i welcomed the unanimous support given to france by all the member states and the readiness to provide all the necessary aid and assistance. i hope that the member states will continue to give their unconditional and lasting support for as long as it takes to ensure the maximum security of the citizens of the alps. i consider the activation of the mutual assistance clause a unique opportunity to lay the foundations for a genuine common defence and security policy of the european union.
in writing. ‒ the problems now on the table, from internal terrorism on europe's borders to political instability in many countries bordering the mediterranean and the control of the flow of migrants, make it necessary to accelerate the project, which is increasingly being discussed, of a common european defence policy. the member states must stop 'chattering' about this issue and open themselves to a structured dialogue with well-defined deadlines, starting with improving cooperation between (external) border control officers, police and intelligence services.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution because i consider it a mistake - a serious mistake - to ask for the establishment of permanent headquarters to plan the defence of the eu and to manage it in cooperation with nato. the idea of an eu going toe way of nato will certainly not help to create favourable feelings towards it. the eu cannot be seen as a peaceful mediator who puts himself above the parties. i hope that instead of thinking of developing and coordinating its military defence capabilities, the eu will return to the peaceful vocation that marked its birth, which was born out of a commitment not to repeat the horrors and mistakes of the two world wars.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the 2014 annual report on the activities of the committee on petitions. the right to petition parliament is a cornerstone of european citizenship, enshrined as a fundamental right under article 227 of the treaty of lisbon. any natural or legal person residing in the union may, individually or in association with others, submit a petition to the european parliament on a matter within the union's field of activity. it thus makes it possible to establish a close link between institutions and citizens, and to monitor and study the impact of different eu policies and legislation on people's daily lives. the work of the committee on petitions to enable eu citizens and residents to participate in the defence and promotion of their rights is crucial. however, as the report indicates, in order to address the issues raised by the petitions in a timely manner, it is essential to improve institutional coordination with the institutions at union, national and regional level and with other bodies. this would also make it possible to strengthen the legitimacy and accountability of the european parliament's decision-making process.

in writing. when china joined the world trade organisation in 2001, subject to certain conditions, the eu agreed that after 15 years it would consider whether to grant it market economy status (mes) and thereby remove all anti-dumping restrictions on imports of chinese products, justified precisely by the need to protect the european economy from unfair competition from a fully non-market economy. the 15 years are up in december, and yet we still do not know the real intentions of the commission, which has so far avoided any real public debate and discussion. but the most disturbing fact is that the commission has never ruled out that granting china an esm could happen almost automatically, without adequate political reflection or an effective impact study. for the five star movement, not only is there no obligation to recognise china as a market economy, which it is not, but a decision to do so would be a real suicide for the european economy, which would obviously be exposed to unsustainable competition from chinese products, based on artificially low or sub-cost prices, with enormous distortions in the internal market and dramatic repercussions on employment and even on our already under pressure social and environmental standards.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, we are dealing with an important text which will serve to create a high-level european body with a central objective, namely to combat undeclared work. we know that this problem is not only a burden on public finances, generating tax evasion and unfair competition between companies, but is above all a source of serious risks for workers and society in general. it is a threat to the health and safety of workers who are often employed in hazardous and strenuous sectors such as agriculture, construction and industry. it is a problem of maintaining the social fabric, also in the geographical and gender sense. it also affects the most vulnerable groups, including refugees. it is therefore right that the european union should make efforts to find a solution and that representatives of the member states, the european commission and civil society, including trade unions and employers, should be brought together to identify the european dimension of the problem. in my view, a long-term objective we must set ourselves is precisely the legalisation of undeclared work. i am pleased with the efforts we have made to improve the text, together with our colleagues, starting with the rapporteur, mr pirinski, who has done an excellent job and for whom i would like to thank him. it is important, commissioner thyssen, that the commission quickly, efficiently and concretely implement the choice we are making.
in writing. each state has its own legislation on the fight against undeclared work and an independent scope of application, but the commission has given a common minimum definition. this has been recognised in any lawful activity of any kind, but not declared to the public authorities. this is a particular scourge in italy, where it contributes to tax evasion and avoidance, as well as generally deplorable working conditions. the idea of a common european platform for the exchange of good practice and comparison between member states and between them and the social partners is certainly a useful tool, but the direction must be to identify more effective mechanisms, both in terms of repression and prevention.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would say that the expression 'the mountain gave birth to a mouse' would be very appropriate for this proposal. it is a classic example of the community's approach that the union tries to solve very serious problems by using inadequate remedies. we would expect much more courage from the commission, because we know that we will then have to fight with the council to get satisfactory agreements and we know well what the attitude of some member states is, for which the facts speak louder than a thousand words. i wonder, for example, where the dutch presidency is today. they are probably trying to find some new agreement and new tax advantage measures to attract businesses, to the detriment of their european partners, as they have done all these years, and in good company, together with belgium, ireland or president juncker's luxembourg. the european commission says nothing about these shameful practices, because it knows full well that there is no common will in this respect at european level, but rather it is a race to take advantage of neighbouring countries, facilitating only the large multinationals to the detriment of small and mediumsized enterprises. i would like to understand why the commission does not refer in its proposal to a country by country report which is public, because that is what the european citizens are asking for and it is the only way to make it effective. transparency must be the key to everything, because only in this way will we have an awareness of how multinationals and member states really operate, the same ones who say they are ready to cooperate but then refuse to provide documents or delete all compromising information, as we have all seen in the work of the taxe committee.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i can tell you quite frankly that the lines in the package you have outlined are acceptable, but the contents of the package are not. they're not consistent with those lines. they are far from the requirement which you yourself have put forward and which you want to solve, namely that taxation be conducted in accordance with the rules by citizens and in particular by companies. what is missing is the heart, not just the detailed proposal that will have to come, but the idea that there should be no transparency on some of the most sensitive points, i am thinking mainly of country by country. the oecd guidelines lock and lock this information in the tax administration, they don't make it available to the public, and that's not good. transparency has a tremendous deterrent effect. i understand the commission's concerns and it is right that the work on impact assessment should be completed. but - you know this very well and i remind everyone of it - when the same work was done for banks, the conclusion was reached that transparency did not create problems for competitiveness, but rather made it stronger. the same thing should be done for businesses. we must broaden the scope of the directive and we must have transparency as a basis. finally, as you said - and i agree - that the package is timely, if timeliness is the issue, when you have finished the work on the impact assessment, do not make an ad hoc directive, but put the conclusions of the proposal into the shareholder rights directive, which is already at an advanced stage of discussion, and we will have recovered months and months. and in this case we would have given substance to the idea of early intervention.
member of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would first like to congratulate you on this high-level debate, with almost 50 speeches which have allowed a large number of points to be dealt with in depth, and what i see, of course with respect for the various sensitivities, is a consensus on the need to continue our joint action against tax fraud and tax evasion, which is a major topic. the package adopted by the college last thursday, at the instigation of jean-claude juncker, whom i welcome, provides us with additional tools to shape a fairer and more efficient tax system within the union and at international level. we must continue to work together towards a taxation that is adapted to the realities and challenges of the 21st century and that also facilitates growth and employment. there have been so many speeches that i cannot answer each one, but i just want to make three remarks. the first, for those who are concerned and whom i want to reassure, concerns the impact of this package on the competitiveness of european companies. no, tax justice and tax transparency are not opposed to economic efficiency. today we are witnessing a genuine global movement against tax evasion and i want to tell you that the european union is not alone in this fight against aggressive tax planning. more than 100 states and territories have already committed themselves to implementing the oecd recommendations swiftly at the g20 summit in antalya last october. i am convinced that a coordinated approach to the implementation of these recommendations at european level will, on the contrary, ensure our companies greater legal certainty, less administrative burden and - i would like to stress this again - fairer tax competition. so this package that is good for justice is also good for investment. as many of you have said - and this is my second point - the ball is now in the court of the member states. i am confident in their good will, not out of naivety, but because i think there is a very consensual subject with strong pressure from european and international public opinion. this goodwill was demonstrated by the rapid adoption within seven months of the directive on the automatic exchange of information on tax returns. however, as you know - and i cannot hide it from you - unanimity at 28 is still a huge challenge. as for me, you can count on my full and determined commitment, particularly within the ecofin council, but i will certainly need your support, i would even say your constant political pressure and your reform drive, so that the fine statements made by some national governments will be followed up with effect. i therefore count on your active support to make rapid progress. third reflection: many interventions focused on the publication of country-by-country information and many of them requested publicity. i told you what my wish was, and it's not rhetoric. i told you my personal position, and it's sincere. at the same time, we must be aware that we must respond pragmatically. yes to transparency, including advertising, provided that it does not undermine investment and competitiveness. so again, we must be very realistic about this and the commission will do that. we must move towards an intergovernmental exchange as of tomorrow. that's what the oecd suggests. we shall have occasion to return to the debate later this year, but parliament is of course heard and so will the positions which are expressed elsewhere in all the benches. i want to end by referring to an interesting, important debate which mr lamberts has raised with humour about the way the french approach love. i do not want to be too harsh and stretch this metaphor too far, but it is true that foreplay is often a necessary condition for a successful act and i would add that the french sometimes go on to act, since the fertility rate in france is among the highest in europe, but i do not want to push this metaphor any further, because as i said there are risks. besides, love and politics are not exactly the same thing. so we must move quickly in political matters, and that is what i have spoken about today, the transition to joint action. that's what we want to do together.

in writing. ‒ the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution aims to protect the human environment from air pollution. it has been known since 1972 that air pollutants can be transported thousands of kilometres before they are deposited, which highlighted the need to address the problems caused by air pollution at international level as early as 1979, with the signing of the convention on transboundary air pollution which entered into force in 1983. it establishes a common framework for controlling and reducing the harm caused by transboundary air pollution to human health and the environment. the european parliament is due to vote today on the commission's proposal to update the 1998 protocol to reduce and control anthropogenic emissions of lead (pb), cadmium (cd) and mercury (hg) into the atmosphere: the parties are required to reduce their total annual emissions of these three metals to levels below 1990 levels and emission limit values are defined for certain large fixed sources, as well as requiring states to apply best available techniques (bat). it is important to support all efforts to curb air pollution and protect the health of our citizens.
in writing. ‒ the 1998 aarhus protocol on persistent organic pollutants aims to control, reduce or eliminate discharges, emissions and releases of persistent organic pollutants (dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane (ddt), hexachlorocyclohexane (hch), polychlorinated biphenyls (pcbs), polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (pahs), dioxins/furans (pcdd/pcdf) and hexachlorobenzene (hcb)). in december 2009, the protocol was amended by decisions 2009/1, 2009/2, 2009/3 and 2009/4, the last two of which refer to best available techniques (bat). decisions 2009/1 and 2009/2 include seven new substances, update the implementation obligations for a number of substances, update the limitations on emissions of pcdd/pcdfs from different sources and add pcbs to the list of substances subject to annual emission limitations and reporting obligations. the amendments to the protocol, already largely covered by eu legislation, will be further transposed by the revision of the directive setting national emission ceilings (necs) for certain air pollutants and establishing annual national emission inventories, currently under way. i vote for it.
