in writing. ‒ since 1972, we have known that air pollutants are transported thousands of kilometres before they are deposited, which highlighted the need to address the problems caused by air pollution at international level as early as 1979, with the signing of the convention on transboundary air pollution, which entered into force in 1983. it establishes a common framework for controlling and reducing the harm caused by transboundary air pollution to human health and the environment. the european parliament is today expected to support the commission's proposal to update the 1998 protocol to reduce and control anthropogenic emissions of dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane (ddt), hexachlorocyclodexane (hch) and polychlorinated biphenyls (pcbs) and to reduce the total annual emissions of aromatic polycyclic hydrocarbons (pahs), dioxins/furans (pcdd/pcdf) and hexachlorobenzene (hcb) into the atmosphere: the parties are required to reduce their total annual emissions of these three metals to levels below 1990 levels and emission limit values are defined for certain large fixed sources, as well as requiring states to apply best available techniques (bat). it is important to support all efforts to curb air pollution and protect the health of our citizens.
in writing. ‒ the 1998 aarhus protocol on persistent organic pollutants aims to control, reduce or eliminate discharges, emissions and releases of persistent organic pollutants (dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane (ddt), hexachlorocyclohexane (hch), polychlorinated biphenyls (pcbs), polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (pahs), dioxins/furans (pcdd/pcdf) and hexachlorobenzene (hcb)). in december 2009, the protocol was amended by decisions 2009/1, 2009/2, 2009/3 and 2009/4, the last two of which refer to best available techniques (bat). decisions 2009/1 and 2009/2 include seven new substances, update the implementation obligations for a number of substances, update the limitations on emissions of pcdd/pcdfs from different sources and add pcbs to the list of substances subject to annual emission limitations and reporting obligations. the amendments to the protocol, already largely covered by eu legislation, will be further transposed by the revision of the directive setting national emission ceilings (necs) for certain air pollutants and establishing annual national emission inventories, currently under way. i vote for it.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision on the acceptance of amendments to the 1998 protocol to the 1979 convention on long-range transboundary air pollution on persistent organic pollutants. the problem of long-range transboundary air pollution has been addressed at international level by the convention signed in 1979 and entered into force in 1983. over the years, it has been extended by eight protocols, such as the 1998 protocol on persistent organic pollutants, which was established with the aim of controlling, reducing or eliminating discharges, emissions and spills of persistent organic pollutants, limiting the use of many substances compared to the pre-1990 period. the amendments to the protocol, already largely covered by eu legislation, will be further implemented by a new directive updating national emission limits for certain air pollutants and establishing annual national emission inventories.
in writing. ‒ the amendments to the protocol to the convention on long-range air pollution include the inclusion of as many as seven new persistent pollutants, update the implementation obligations and limitations of total annual emissions of dioxins/furans (pcdd/f) from different sources, and provide for the addition of polychlorinated biphenyls (pcbs) to the list of substances subject to annual emission limitations. this is therefore an important step towards an international approach to the problems caused by air pollution and i voted in favour of ratifying these amendments with great conviction.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the amendments because i believe that the problems caused by air pollution must be tackled at european level. the aarhus protocol on persistent organic pollutants aims to control and reduce discharges and emissions of these substances. this vote marks important steps towards protecting the environment and combating pollution, fundamental objectives which the european union must pursue at supranational and national level.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation because, in addition to confirming principles that i agree with and which are already part of other legislative measures, it goes in the direction of improving air quality and better protecting the health of citizens. given the obvious advantages, i made this voting decision lightly.
in writing. ‒ since the 1970s, studies have been conducted on the environmental and human health hazards of the release of persistent organic pollutants into the atmosphere. since then, the subject has continued to evolve as new issues and problems have arisen. the ratification of the amendments to the protocol on persistent organic pollutants, to which the union acceded in 2004, is important in order not to hinder the progress made towards continuous improvement of regulations on persistent organic pollutants. the amendments will enable eu citizens to live in an increasingly healthy environment, and for these reasons i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament resolution, which i voted for, approves the amendments to the protocol to the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution on persistent organic pollutants. the proposed amendments set stricter limits on transboundary emissions than those set out in the protocol to the convention in order to better prevent air pollution and its effects on human health.
in writing. the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution aims to protect the human environment from air pollution. the convention, which was signed in 1979 and entered into force in 1983, was the first legally binding international instrument in this field. it establishes a framework for controlling and reducing the harm caused by transboundary air pollution to human health and the environment. the convention entrusts the secretariat of the executive secretariat of the united nations economic commission for europe (unece) with the secretariat functions. to date, the convention has been extended by eight protocols. this decision, which entered into force on 23 october 2003, was transposed into eu law by several instruments and was amended by decisions 2009/1, 2009/2, 2009/3 and 2009/4, the latter two of which relate to bat. the amended protocol includes seven new substances, updates the implementation obligations for a number of substances, updates the limitations on emissions of pcdd/pcdfs from different sources and adds pcbs to the list of substances subject to annual emission limitations and reporting obligations, ensuring a higher level of protection of human health and the environment from transboundary air pollution. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the recommendation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal to revise the national emission limits for certain persistent organic pollutants.
in writing. the 1998 aarhus protocol further extends the 1979 convention on long-range transboundary air pollution to include persistent organic pollutants. it therefore aims to control, reduce or eliminate discharges, emissions and spills of persistent organic pollutants. the amended protocol includes seven new substances, updates the limits on emissions of pcdd/pcdfs and adds pcbs to the list of substances subject to annual emission limits and reporting obligations. in this second case too, i asked my colleagues to give their consent to the council's decision, in order to formally adopt the amendments to the protocol, which are already largely covered by european legislation.
in writing. ‒ the 1998 aarhus protocol further extends the 1979 convention on long-range transboundary air pollution to include persistent organic pollutants and aims to control and reduce discharges and emissions of these substances. i voted in favour of this so that we can move forward in the direction of protecting the environment and combating pollution, which are fundamental objectives which the european union must pursue.
in writing. ‒ in 1983, the convention on air pollution came into force, the first legally binding international instrument in this field. the aarhus protocol on persistent organic pollutants was subsequently established in 1998 with the aim of controlling, reducing or eliminating discharges, emissions and spills of these pollutants. the convention has had its results and i therefore express my positive and confident vote on this project.
in writing. ‒ the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution, signed in 1979 and entered into force in 1983, aims to protect the human environment from air pollution and is the first legally binding international instrument adopted in this field. it establishes a framework for controlling and reducing the harm caused by transboundary air pollution to human health and the environment. over the years, the convention has been expanded by eight protocols, which define specific measures that the parties must take to reduce emissions of air pollutants. the 1998 aarhus protocol on persistent organic pollutants aims to control, reduce or eliminate discharges, emissions and spills of persistent organic pollutants. the amended protocol includes seven new substances, updates the implementation obligations for a number of substances, updates the limitations on emissions of dioxins/furans from different sources and adds polychlorinated biphenyls to the list of substances subject to annual emission limitations and reporting obligations. i consider that the amendments to the amendments to the protocol (08648/2015 add 1) are fully consistent with the existing eu legislation and constitute an important step towards a higher level of protection of human health and the environment from transboundary air pollution. i voted in favour of all of this.
in writing. ‒ with today's vote, parliament is transposing into eu law the amendments to the 1998 aarhus protocol to the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution on persistent organic pollutants. the convention, signed in 1979, establishes a framework for controlling and reducing the harm caused by transboundary air pollution to human health and the environment. the amendments to the 1998 protocol include seven new pollutants, update the implementation obligations for a number of substances, update the limitations on emissions of dioxins/furans from different sources and add polychlorinated biphenyls to the list of substances subject to annual emission limitations and reporting obligations. i voted in favour of the recommendation because ratification of these amendments will be an important step towards a higher level of protection of human health and the environment from transboundary air pollution.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the adoption of decisions 2009/1 and 2009/1 amending the 1998 aarhus protocol on persistent organic pollutants. we recognise that this protocol has been an important tool in countering acidification, eutrophication and ground-level ozone, providing for the first time national emission limits for ddt, hch and pcbs and commitments to reduce ipa, pcdd/pcdf and hcp through best available technologies (bat). we believe that updating the protocol and broadening its scope can enhance its effectiveness. in particular, it covers seven new substances, adjusts the implementation obligations and sets emission limits and stricter controls for pcbs and pcdd/pcdfs. this is a necessary and important step forward in protecting the health of citizens and the environment from transboundary air pollution. we will ensure that the flexibility in emission benchmarks and the time-limits for the application of emission limit values and bats given to those economies in transition that are party to the protocol does not undermine its effectiveness. we hope that the parties will ratify decisions 2009/1 and 2009/2 as soon as possible and commit themselves to promoting the technological improvement necessary to protect the health of citizens and the environment.

in writing. ‒ the protection of biological diversity is a key factor in maintaining individual well-being. habitat destruction, changes in consumption patterns and the impact of human activities on the environment pose serious threats to both life and the planet's economy. the european union adopted a biodiversity strategy in 2011 which has so far failed to deliver the expected results. the failure to achieve the targets, with an estimated loss of €50 billion per year, led the commission to propose a revision. the demesmaeker report, which i supported with my vote, has effectively highlighted how full implementation and effective funding are the fundamental prerequisites for the success of the union's biodiversity strategy. the development of a trans-european network for green infrastructure, the adoption of sustainable solutions for agriculture and the commitment to reduce marine pollution are some of the first measures that must be put into practice together with a commitment to halt the loss of biodiversity also outside protected natural areas.

in writing. ‒ after careful reflection and debate in the house, i have voted in favour of the report on the mid-term review of the eu biodiversity strategy, on the basis of the following considerations: biodiversity is a human resource under threat and in a precarious equilibrium, to the point that its compromise is estimated to be among the ten most serious global risks to ecosystems and to the resilience of the earth, a 'system' resource that cannot be eliminated to address the necessary challenges of environmental sustainability; the six-objective strategy is complex and far from being achieved. it is regrettable that only two objectives have visible positive aspects (for fisheries and invasive alien species) and that this step will not, unfortunately, produce satisfactory results by 2020, not even a small one, and in particular for two key sectors, agriculture and forestry. it follows that ultimately, greater political will and a multi-stakeholder approach are needed, with the development of a higher ecological awareness by regional and local actors, which collectively contribute to developing an ecological footprint that is double that of the sustainable one.

in writing. ‒ pollution, overexploitation of natural resources, climate change, land use change and deforestation are among the main factors driving biodiversity loss in europe, with adverse impacts on species survival. already in 2010, europe failed to meet the agreed targets. therefore, new and substantial efforts to restore ecosystems will be required by 2020. today, only 17% of the habitats and species and 11% of the main ecosystems protected by eu legislation in the eu enjoy a satisfactory conservation status. this means that the natura 2000 network and the habitats and birds directives, where implemented, have delivered the expected results but it is still too little compared to the rate at which we are seeing biodiversity loss. a change of pace and a greater commitment by the states, especially to apply existing legislation, are needed. but unless these efforts are accompanied by a more resource-efficient, climate-resilient and low-carbon economy, the eu risks failing to meet its 2020 target. i share the report's content and call on all public and private actors to play an active role in safeguarding our planet.

in writing. ‒ the european commission published (10/2015) a report on 'the mid-term review of the eu biodiversity strategy to 2020', which assesses the results achieved since 2011, the date of adoption of the strategy, in implementing the actions and achieving the targets set. overall, the report finds no significant progress towards the key objective of 'stopping biodiversity loss and ecosystem degradation in the european union (eu) by 2020'. the council agreed last december to want better implementation of the sectoral directives (habitat and birds directives); more effective integration of biodiversity into other sectoral policies, in particular the common agricultural policy (cap), a more targeted use of existing financial instruments; a greater focus on international strategies; the urgency of raising awareness and involving all sectors of society and all levels of government; a greater use, including economic use, of ecosystem services. the rapporteur strongly stressed the need not to amend the habitat and other biodiversity protection directives, as these, when well implemented, give positive results. i consider it a good report, so i vote in favour.

in writing. some in europe are under the illusion that building walls will stop the flow of migrants. but the phenomenon of immigration cannot be stopped, it is an epochal phenomenon that must be governed and managed. and if the borders are closed and schengen is called into question, we are on a very dangerous ridge: schengen is a pillar of europe, and if schengen collapses, europe collapses. i agree with the commission's proposals, but i would stress that we must first change dublin and then evaluate schengen. to do otherwise would be unjust as well as wrong. first we must correct the distorted mechanisms for the reception of migrants, and only then can we assess schengen. it is not by giving ultimatums or setting deadlines that a european migration policy is built. the position of the countries which want to close schengen is very serious. it means turning our backs on the thousands of desperate people who are arriving, but it also means, and above all, turning our backs on the other member states of the european union which are at the forefront of the crisis. the countries that founded this union and built it. it's too easy to close the doors when the going gets tough. without schengen we cannot even call it a union.
in writing. the schengen treaty must be defended for what it is and what it represents: the european union is a common space of freedom and security, an area of fundamental values. the commission's proposal to establish a european coast guard to control the external borders is therefore a welcome expression of the shared responsibility which underlies it. it is obviously important that all guarantees be given to ensure that the fundamental rights which europe stands for are respected. recent data, provided by, inter alia, the eu agency for fundamental rights, indicate that numerous barriers to access to legal aid and insufficient information for asylum seekers in hotspots still persist. our priorities as members of parliament and as european citizens are the establishment of active life-saving rescue services, the need to open safe and legal access routes, the facilitation of family reunification and adequate training of border staff to better identify people in need of protection. respect for fundamental rights must be an integral and indispensable part of our security policies.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the safety and well-being of patients must be safeguarded with all possible care during clinical trials. the recent tragedy in france shows that this is not always the case: the five hospitalizations and one death of volunteers following the ingestion of an experimental molecule foreseen by the programme for the development of a new drug are a very serious matter. fortunately, what has happened in france is a rare occurrence, but it is clear that much more can be done in the field of safety in research. regulation (eu) no 536/2014 on clinical trials will not enter into force in full until 2018. in the meantime, we cannot allow any more tragedies to happen. the regulation requires that thorough studies be carried out to collect as much information as possible before a medicinal product is administered to humans and obliges member states to share all available information, including by sharing the european clinical trial database and making the results of phase 1 trials publicly available. i would expect the commission to provide clarification on the progress of the implementation of the regulation and any measures to speed up its entry into force.

president-in-office of the council.– mr president, i would like to thank the members for this debate and for the many questions that were raised. it is true that the next european council will be crucial for very important aspects of the definition of our union. it will deal with the two elements that determine our collective will to confront common challenges. one is obviously the debate on the united kingdom, and i will come back to that in a second. it is true, as mr weber said, that it requires a certain amount of courage and leadership to deal with these two issues without any cost to discussing the many other challenges in the european union. the position of the united kingdom in the european union, as well as the improved management of the refugee crisis – we talked about that for many hours yesterday – is obviously crucial for the decisions that we will have to make in february. first of all, i think it is important to say that i am encouraged by the level of support that i hear about the type of package that has been proposed by president tusk. of course, the devil is in the detail and everything has to be weighed up, but nevertheless i feel a large majority of parliament here feels that it is in our interest to keep the united kingdom in the european union – not at the highest price. but in a reasonable constructive debate, these are important views. you are partners in this; you will be consulted; you have your ‘sherpas’, and you will be part of the council meetings. of course, it might involve changes to secondary legislation. therefore, your role is also essential and your concerns need to be addressed. this package has to be fair not only to the united kingdom, but also to all citizens in europe. it is vitally important to underline that in all aspects, including the most complex part, which deals with social benefits. we have to talk about a deeper and a fairer internal market and we will have to see what the conclusions are in the council discussions in february. many elements in the package benefit us all – such as more competitiveness and a deeper internal market – but, as i said, fairness is also an important point in this. i would also like to say that it gratifies me to hear mr kamall speak. he qualifies this package as at least being a good starting point, and that gives me hope that the negotiations will be constructive. on the issue of ever-closer union, which was mentioned by mr verhofstadt, it would not be a good idea for there to be an opt-out for the united kingdom. i would like to remind you that, in article 1 of the treaty, it states very clearly ‘an ever closer union between the peoples of the european union’. that is what is written in the treaty. for some it might mean a federal europe and for others there might be another connotation, but what we do in the draft european council decision is to clarify that, in itself, it does not offer a legal basis to transfer competences to the european union. that is a statement of fact, nothing more and nothing less. at the same time, the draft european council decision states that the treaties allow for a deeper degree of integration. i think that is your point. so the treaties do not represent an obstacle to your vision of europe, but neither do they oblige us to transfer competences. therefore i do not think that it would be wise to look at an opt—out. on the refugee crisis, i will not take up your time. we discussed it at length yesterday. regarding article 78(3), i would say that this is a possibility, but do not forget that at the moment we have a borders package which is being discussed every month in detail to make sure that we come to the quickest agreement on this. the eu interior ministers discussed these issues at their informal gathering held in amsterdam on 25—26 january 2016, and this will continue to be done consecutively. so we do not need the article to do it more quickly. what you need is the reality on the ground so that we have the right people from the european asylum support office (easo) and frontex in the hotspots. in conclusion, let me stress the importance of schengen. the continuing flow of migrants over the past months has seen several countries temporarily re-impose border controls. i would like to say here that the presidency is committed to securing the preservation of schengen – a system which is at the heart of the european project and one of the greatest achievements of european integration. we will do all we can to find a solution to the current problems on the basis of the expected commission proposal and in cooperation with the commission, parliament and the member states concerned.
in writing. the european council on 18 and 19 february will have to deal with the delicate issue of the proposed agreement between the european union and the uk government, in preparation for the referendum to be held in june. at this moment of crisis in the union, when national interests seem to prevail over the will to find common and cohesive solutions, the european institutions will have to do everything possible to prevent the united kingdom from leaving, an assumption which would undermine the very foundations of the union itself. at the same time, the european union cannot accept the four conditions demanded by the cameron government. in fact, while i believe that it is necessary to discuss the reform of the european institutions, as proposed by the british government, i am also convinced that this must be done in a shared and coordinated way at european level, and not on the basis of the request of a single member state, however 'special' it may be. that is why the agreement proposal put forward by mr tusk today risks taking us in a direction which is dangerous for the future of european integration. the first response to the british government is that of a minimalist europe, blocked by veils and devoid of any federalist perspective, the exact opposite of the strong and ambitious europe we need today.
president of the federal republic of nigeria.– mr president, i wish to express my utmost appreciation to the president of the european parliament, mr martin schulz, for inviting me to address the plenary session of this legislative arm of the european union. i am honoured and humbled at having been selected to make an address on this occasion. let me also bring to the european leaders, parliamentarians and the good people of europe, a goodwill message from my fellow countrymen and women. the nigerian people acknowledge with deep appreciation the material and financial sacrifices the european union, and individual friendly european nations, made towards the conduct of elections and institutionalisation of democratic norms in nigeria. as it had done before, the european union has supported the independent national electoral commission (inec) in the smooth conduct of the last general elections in nigeria, the outcome of which received worldwide acclamation. nigerians noted the huge contributions that europe has made towards the realisation of acceptable, free and fair elections in our country. today i will tell this august gathering that european investments are beginning to bear fruit. i am one of the returns on the european investments in the democratisation of nigeria. indeed, the present regime is the product of a democratic choice consciously made by the people of nigeria through the ballot box. democracy has come to nigeria to stay – sooner than many of us would have imagined. nigeria will be counted among the most stable, strongest and most virile democracies in africa. there may be strife and stresses, but these can be contained by the safety mechanisms of an electoral democracy. the events leading to the general elections in nigeria in the early part of the year 2015 gave strong indications that the country was in trouble. seeming anger, expressions of vituperation and open animosity, as well as threats and violence unleashed against the electorate, aimed at forcing them to vote for the status quo, were unpalatable developments that brought the stability of nigeria into question. the drama that took place at the national collation centre was a momentarily frightening situation, unleashed by desperate agents of the status quo with the purpose of maintaining their grip on the national resources for their selfish interests. the maturity and patience with which the officials of the independent national electoral commission under professor attahiru jega handled the matter saved the struggle for democracy and the huge european contributions. we must thank god that nigeria survived this drama. as i have stated in other fora, the actions of nigeria’s former president, goodluck ebele jonathan, are commendable. for the first time in the history of nigeria, a presidential candidate and sitting president conceded electoral defeat in defiance of calls by strong forces, including agents and benefactors of the regime, not to do so. i do appreciate the special relationship that exists between nigeria and the european union. the european union is nigeria’s main development partner and the pillar of support for the consolidation of democracy and the economic development of our country. we in africa appreciate that your problems are mainly managing prosperity and competition. however, our problems are poverty, disease and technological backwardness. it is not too difficult to appreciate the kind of challenges these problems pose: internal strife, refugees, boat people, drug and human trafficking, etc. chaos is not a neighbour anybody would wish to have. it is therefore in our collective interest to cooperate and tackle these serious problems in africa. i am pleased that we already have the nigeria-european union annual political dialogue, which has continued to strengthen our cooperation based on shared values and interests, especially in the areas of peace, security, democracy and good governance. through this forum we have been able to continue, on a regular basis, to share perspectives on important regional, continental and global issues, with a view to forging common positions. we are committed to intensifying political dialogue and cooperation in the context of the nigeria-european union joint way forward. both of us believe in peace and security, respect for human rights, democracy and good governance, equality and tolerance, as ways of developing prosperous and strong societies. furthermore, in the context of these european union-nigeria relations, i wish to acknowledge that the european union had, severally, condemned the activities of extremist groups, including boko haram in nigeria and in the entire economic community of west african states (ecowas). the european union had noted and commended nigeria’s development of a national counter-terrorism strategy and the amendment of the country’s counter—terrorism act in demonstration of the government’s commitment to finding a lasting solution to the threats posed by boko haram terror elements. nigeria appreciates the eu’s collaboration, especially in the area of technical support, capacity-building for security services and provision of development assistance. for our part, we have updated our rules of engagement in fighting terrorism, and we pay very close attention during operations to the treatment of captured terrorists, to civilians caught up in the conflict and, in general, to safeguarding property. our aim is to use the minimum force necessary in our fight against terrorists. in light of this, i wish to seize this opportunity to thank individual european member states for their assistance towards the success of the nigerian military onslaught against the boko haram terror elements. many european union member states have pledged to support our efforts in the rescue of the kidnapped chibok schoolgirls. it may interest you to know that in a recent meeting i had with the parents of the chibok girls, i assured them that the government would not rest until all the girls are rescued alive and reunited with their families. i remain fully committed to this pledge. (applause) since my assumption of office in may last year, we have reorganised the nigerian armed forces and repositioned them to deal decisively with the boko haram terrorists. indeed, all the local government areas that were hitherto under the control of the boko haram terrorists in adamawa, borno and yobe states in the north-eastern flank of nigeria, have been recaptured. internally displaced persons (idps) are gradually returning to their communities. the federal government is committed to rebuilding schools, hospitals and other vital infrastructure destroyed by the fleeing terrorists. currently, the activities of boko haram have been reduced to the sambisa forest, and their capacity to launch major offensives has been degraded. boko haram has now resorted to attacking soft targets, such as markets, mosques and churches, using innocent, under-age, hapless children to detonate locally-made improvised explosive devices (ieds). i must express our serious concerns about the alarming situation in southern libya, which is becoming a strategic time bomb for africa and indeed europe. the ungoverned swathe of land of southern libya has become a thriving arms bazaar which threatens the security of the sahel region, as well as the west africa region and beyond. we must therefore intensify our efforts to find a lasting solution to the libyan crisis. nigeria is a peace-loving nation and has played a critical role in conflict management and resolution within and outside africa. peace-keeping and peace-building have been part of nigeria’s foreign policy since independence. nigerian troops have participated in almost all united nations sub-regional and regional peace-keeping and peace-building operations. in spite of our current security challenges, nigeria is among the 10 top troop-contributing countries to the united nations peacekeeping operations around the world, with huge financial and human commitment. nigeria’s first outing on peacekeeping operations was to the congo, as part of the 20 000—strong united nations operations in the congo (onuc) in july 1960, of which i was privileged to be a member of the contingent in 1963 – barely three months before nigeria’s independence. nigeria participated in united nations operations in the congo for only three-and-a-half years. it contributed the third largest national force in the congo, after india and ethiopia. since then, nigeria has maintained a presence in global peacekeeping efforts. nigeria has indeed participated in the maintenance of law and order following a mutiny in tanganyika in 1964. in 1979 and 1982, soldiers of nigeria’s 21st infantry battalion and the 202 reconnaissance regiment were deployed to chad as a peacekeeping force to monitor a ceasefire and inspire confidence in the ongoing peace process. in addition, it contributed to the largest contingent when the economic community of west african states monitoring group (ecomog) was moved to sierra leone on a peacekeeping—cum—peace-enforcement mission. the economic community of west african states monitoring group recovered most parts of the country from the rebels and returned the ousted president, tejan kabbah, to office on 10 march 1998. under the mandate of the african union, nigeria embarked on a peacekeeping mission in são tomé and príncipe, where it succeeded in persuading dissident soldiers to subject themselves to constitutional authorities. besides this, nigeria has also deployed its personnel in rwanda and in the darfur region of sudan in order to maintain the peace in these two countries. nigeria has additionally deployed its contingent to the following african countries: angola (united nations angola verification mission); namibia (united nations transition assistance group); mozambique (united nations operations in mozambique); western sahara (united nations mission for the referendum in western sahara); somalia (united nations operation in somalia); and the auozou strip (united nations aouzou strip observer group). on migration from africa to europe: nigeria wishes to acknowledge and share the concerns expressed by the european union with respect to the influx of migrants from africa through the mediterranean sea, with its attendant loss of lives. in this regard, nigeria will collaborate with the european union to address illegal immigration to europe. the federal government of nigeria is making concerted efforts to address the push factors that propel migration, especially from nigeria, as both a destination and a transit country. in this year’s budget, the government has provided for over 500 000 graduate employment positions in the teaching profession alone. we are also collaborating with the states and local governments to strengthen skills acquisition centres, in order to train the teeming youth in various vocational skills so that they can be self-employed and eventually become employers of labour. we are also making efforts to diversify the economy, giving impetus to agriculture and solid minerals exploitation, to create wealth and employment. nigeria welcomes the outcome of the valletta eu-africa summit on migration, including the launching of the eur 1.8 billion emergency fund to address the root causes of migration from africa to europe. nigeria will work with the countries of the sahel and central africa to submit to the board of the emergency trust fund the projects that we have identified for funding in due course. the common agenda on migration and mobility (camm), which nigeria signed on 12 march 2015 and was indeed the first country to sign from sub-saharan africa, is a demonstration of the positive spirit of our cooperation with the european union in the field of migration and development. it is in the light of this understanding that i wish to propose the reciprocal visa waiver for holders of nigerian diplomatic and official passports attending official meetings and conferences in europe. economic partnership agreements (epas): the economic partnership agreement between the european union and the african, caribbean and pacific group of states, collectively endorsed by the economic community of west african states, is yet to be signed by nigeria and a few others. during economic partnership agreement negotiations, nigeria raised some pertinent technical issues that are yet to be addressed. giving due consideration to the mismatch of the two regions, europe and ecowas, in terms of technology and manufacturing experience, the manufacturers association of nigeria (man) and associated trade unions raised concerns over the negative impact of epas on nigeria’s industrialisation programme. nigeria is working towards addressing its own side of the issues. i am therefore urging our european union partners to also address our own concerns to allow for economic partnership agreements that are mutually beneficial and contribute to the prosperity of our people, in the context of our shared values and interests in promoting cordial bilateral trade relations. on oil theft and illegal bunkering: nigeria is facing the challenges of oil theft and illegal bunkering in the niger delta, as well as the recovery of illicit funds. it is therefore expedient to raise these issues with you, distinguished parliamentarians. in this regard, nigeria solicits the cooperation of the european parliament to support the efforts aimed at stemming these vices. our attempts to restore security, curb corruption and fight crime will result not only in improving social stability in nigeria but will re-open the doors for full economic relations with europe and the outside world. those who wish to invest in our country have vast opportunities, and we intend to guarantee the security of people and investments brought to nigeria. the whole world recently converged in paris, france, for the climate change conference (cop21). a positive approach to the issue resulted in mutually-acceptable decisions. the world leaders have forged a common platform in addressing the devastating effects of climate change, particularly in the underprivileged countries across the entire length and breadth of the globe. during this all-important global event, i declared my country’s position on climate change. i reiterate here that it portends serious threats to nigeria’s security and development. nigeria is watching helplessly as lake chad dries up. this has monumental consequences for the people living in the lake chad basin, whose livelihood has, for generations, been dependent on the resources of the lake. these resources are fast dissipating, throwing communities out of jobs. it is pertinent to mention that all the states contiguous to lake chad are facing the effects of climate change. collectively, we are under an obligation to face these common challenges. our collective efforts may not be enough, as we are constrained by the dearth of funds, technology and manpower to initiate the right solutions. we are therefore calling for quick global action to address the issues. indeed, these will serve in part as panaceas to the issues facing the countries sharing lake chad’s resources. in an effort to find a lasting solution to this problem, nigeria has contributed the sum of usd 5 million, which has already been used in the conduct of a holistic study on the inter-basin water transfer from the congo basin to lake chad. the study has revealed that the project will require the sum of usd 15 billion to reach completion. i wish to state that this study has indicated that the proposed lake chad project would be able to pay back this huge investment if it is private-sector driven. against this background, let me invite parliament to use its good offices by lending its support to the realisation of this laudable project. i wish once again to express, with all sense of humility, my profound appreciation to the president of the european parliament, members of the european parliament, european leaders and the people of this continent for the honour personally extended to me, and by and large the people of nigeria, to address the plenary session of one of the largest groups of democracies in the world. i thank you all for this rare honour. thank you very much. member of thecommission.– madam president, i will read the official statement of the commission, but firstly let me underline that the commission and parliament have a very common interest. we were able, during the last week, to present a very robust and stronger type of approval system in europe. the commission will get supervisory powers, and we will make sure that member states enforce the rules. so there will be no new volkswagen cases in the future. now let me go onto the official commission statement. commission statement the commission is fully committed to putting very robust emission-testing procedures in place, as of september 2017, to measure real driving emissions (rde). the commission counts on the european parliament’s support in this respect. on 28 october 2015, the technical committee for motor vehicles (tcmv) voted on a draft commission regulation introducing rde limits for light duty vehicles. the commission is aware that the final result of the vote at the tcmv raised criticism from the european parliament as to the level of conformity factors. the commission considers the review mechanism of the draft regulations to be a very appropriate tool to address this criticism. the annual review of the second conformity factor is explicitly included in the enacting terms of the draft commission regulation. the objectives of this revision clause are to bring the conformity factor to 1, as soon as possible and at the latest by 2023. the commission is committed to making use of this revision clause to reduce the second conformity factor by 2017 already, and on an annual basis. due to this revision clause and the technical improvements which can be expected, manufacturers will, as of today, have to design vehicles that will comply with a conformity factor of 1. the commission welcomes the report on the reduction of pollutant emissions from road vehicles (dess report) and agrees with the european parliament on the need to ensure that the commission is empowered to adopt measures and requirements on rde test procedures, including conformity factors, through delegated acts following the revision of the euro 5/6 legislation. the commission is committed to working closely with the european parliament and with the council to reach a compromise to this end without delay. the commission will, in any case, ensure that the european parliament is duly and closely involved in the setting-out of the rde conformity factors. the commission believes that the joint work by both co-legislators will allow the establishment of a new, efficient and reliable approval framework for motor vehicle products.
chair of the envi committee.– madam president, i would like to thank commissioner bieńkowska for her presence today in the plenary, and also vice-president šefčovič, for their important work. this statement is proof of positive interinstitutional cooperation and represents a clear commitment for the future. i would like to invite all members of the european parliament to take this commitment into account during the vote – important for our european citizens.
in writing. ‒ on 13 november 2014, parliament approved an eu-moldova association agreement which establishes a comprehensive and deep free trade area. however, the agreement contains a bilateral safeguard clause which temporarily suspends the trade preferences in force if the import arrangements for products from the associated country are likely to cause damage to the european market. the safeguard clause is accompanied by an anti-circumvention mechanism, which allows the original rate of customs duties to be re-established if imported products exceed a certain threshold. i voted in favour of the proposal to implement these clauses because i consider it a priority to protect the european market and its balances.
in writing. ‒ the european union is moldova's main trading partner, accounting for 46.4% of the country's total trade. my vote in favour of the scholz report is motivated by the conviction that the eu-moldova association agreement represents an important step forward in relations with this country, a step which must, however, take due account of the risks for european producers and consumers. i therefore welcome the introduction of safeguard clauses in community legislation to protect the continent's industry and production, which are threatened by the danger of excessive imports. the entry of non-moldovan products onto the european market through a first crossing into the country may represent a problem whose solution can be effectively identified in the introduction of the anti-circumvention mechanisms already provided for in the agreement.

in writing. i voted in favour of this document because i believe that the eu-republic of moldova association agreement represents an opportunity for both parties from both an economic and a geopolitical point of view. i also think it is important that the agreement in question contains appropriate safeguard clauses and anti-circumvention mechanisms and that they are applied effectively.
in writing. ‒ the safeguard clauses contained in the anti-circumvention mechanism of the trade association agreement between the european union and the republic of moldova should not be understood as an anachronistic protectionist measure which does not belong to the political will of either the commission or the parliament, but rather as a form of protection for producers and consumers through the possibility of restoring the rate of the npf customs duty if imports of certain agricultural products from moldova (listed in annex xv-c) exceed a certain threshold in the absence of a valid justification as to their exact origin. the anti-circumvention clauses are important to avoid the importation into the union of non-moldovan products via moldova, using the advantages of the agreement to circumvent the 'rules of origin' requirements. chapter ii of the proposal (article 13) lays down the procedures for the application of this mechanism, which is without prejudice to the application of the measures defined in chapter i (safeguard measures). it is important to promote trade association agreements and international free trade, but this must be done on the basis of transparency and mutual respect for the rules.
in writing. - i abstained. the eu-moldova association agreement was signed in june 2014 and has been provisionally applied since september 2014. this regulation is nothing more than an ancillary measure providing for the possibility of suspending the preferential duties granted to moldova for a period of up to six months in the event of excessive entry of products into the eu. the measure itself is not at all problematic. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. i shall abstain for several reasons: our delegation did not support and opposed the association agreement with a country traditionally influenced by russia, moldova. this undue interference in a geopolitical area which is not very close to ours is not, however, of commercial interest to our companies. there is no concrete risk for the italian and paduan production and agricultural system from moldova; if the problem exists, our delegation does not believe in the operation of safeguard procedures which, when the facts are tested, almost always prove to be slow and not very effective for the purposes for which they are intended.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation implementing the safeguard clauses and the anti-circumvention mechanism, which provides for the temporary suspension of the tariff preferences contained in the association agreement between the european union and the republic of moldova. the bilateral safeguard clause allows for the temporary suspension of the preferences granted to the republic of moldova in the event of an unexpected and significant increase in imports causing substantial economic injury to the domestic industry of the european union. this shall only be done subject to an obligation on the part of the union to consult the moldovan authorities prior to the imposition of a definitive safeguard measure. in line with the report, i also think that the commission's proposal should be welcomed, as it is necessary to incorporate into union law the instruments necessary for the application of temporary safeguard measures in the event of an increase in imports causing economic damage to the union market and its producers.
in writing. ‒ the association agreement with moldova, like most eu trade agreements, contains a bilateral safeguard clause. in other words, this instrument allows preferences to be temporarily suspended in the event that their application would result in an unexpected and significant increase in imports causing economic injury to the domestic industry of the importing party. i voted in favour of the report also in the light of some positive elements in the text, such as the obligation for the commission to submit an annual report on the application, implementation and compliance with the regulation and the obligation for the union to hold consultations with the moldovan authorities before a definitive safeguard measure is imposed.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council implementing the safeguard clauses and the anti-circumvention mechanism providing for the temporary suspension of the tariff preferences contained in the association agreement between the european union and the european atomic energy community and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of moldova, of the other part. these trade protection instruments are indispensable to prevent infringements of the agreement. in particular, the bilateral safeguard clause allows for the temporary suspension of tariff preferences in the event that their application would result in an unexpected and significant increase in imports causing economic injury to the domestic industry of the importing party. in addition, the agreement also includes an 'anti-circumvention' mechanism, which allows the customs duty rate to be reinstated if imports of certain agricultural products from moldova exceed a certain threshold in the absence of a valid justification as to their exact origin.

in writing. ‒ i decided to vote in favour of the proposal for a regulation because it provides the necessary instruments to protect european producers in the event of circumvention attempts and will also make it possible to apply the bilateral safeguard clause. these elements are necessary because when creating deep free trade areas such as the eu-moldova case in question, account must be taken of possible issues that could arise to the disadvantage of european producers, which can be addressed by ensuring the use of well-established trade instruments such as the aforementioned safeguard clauses and the anti-circumvention mechanism.
in writing. ‒ as with most of our trade agreements, the association agreement with moldova contains a bilateral safeguard clause. this instrument allows preferences to be temporarily suspended in the event that their application would result in an unexpected and significant increase in imports causing economic injury to the domestic industry of the importing party. in addition, the agreement also includes an 'anti-circumvention' mechanism, which allows the re-establishment of the rate of the customs duty of the npf if imports of certain agricultural products from moldova exceed a certain threshold in the absence of a valid justification as to their exact origin. the proposal applies the provisions of the eu-moldova association agreement which parliament approved on 13 november 2014. among the positive elements: the obligation for the commission to submit an annual report on the application, implementation and compliance of the regulation and the obligation for the union to consult the moldovan authorities before the imposition of a definitive safeguard measure. this has been the subject of negotiation and agreement between the eu and moldova and is reflected in article 160 of the association agreement. my vote is in favour.
in writing. ‒ since september 2014, following the conclusion of the association agreement, the european union has become the largest trading partner of the republic of moldova: the substantial increase in trade has seen exports to the european union double or even triple for some products. i am convinced that trade must continue to be an effective instrument to support the process of deep structural reforms in moldova, increasingly contributing to the stabilisation of the country, especially in the light of recent political developments. the proposal is largely based on regulations already adopted for free trade agreements with south korea, central america and colombia/peru and creates a sound safety net for european industry and producers, protecting them in the event of particularly critical conditions for the european market. it also introduces an obligation for the commission to submit an annual report to parliament and the council, ensuring adequate democratic control over the application of this regulation. i therefore voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation implementing the safeguard clauses and the anti-circumvention mechanism providing for the temporary suspension of the tariff preferences contained in the association agreement between the european union and the republic of moldova.
in writing. ‒ the association agreement with moldova contains a bilateral safeguard clause. this instrument allows for the temporary suspension of trade preferences in the event that their application would result in an unexpected and significant increase in imports causing economic injury to the domestic industry of the importing party. the agreement also includes an 'anti-circumvention' mechanism which allows the most-favoured-nation (mfn) rate of customs duty to be reinstated if imports of certain agricultural products from moldova exceed a certain threshold in the absence of a valid justification as to their exact origin. a regulation of the european parliament and of the council is needed to introduce into eu internal law the instrument necessary to enable the application of the bilateral safeguard clause and the anti-circumvention mechanism. that is why i voted in favour of this measure.

in writing. ‒ the association agreement between the european union and the republic of moldova signed in 2014 introduced a preferential trade regime guaranteeing mutual free market access. following the entry into force of the agreement, imports into the union from moldova increased by 20%, while imports of agricultural products increased by as much as 30%. the report we have voted on today therefore calls for the implementation of the safeguard clauses and the anti-circumvention mechanism provided for in the agreement. these measures are imposed where a product originating in moldova is imported into the union in such increased quantities that it causes serious injury to the union industry and provide for the suspension or reintroduction of the customs duty on the product concerned. the anti-circumvention mechanism also prevents the importation into the union of non-moldovan products via moldova by using the advantages of the agreement to circumvent the origin requirements. i voted in favour of the report because it protects european agricultural producers from excessive imports of moldovan products.

in writing. ‒ the agreement with georgia introduced an ambitious preferential trade regime between both parties known as the deep and comprehensive free trade area (dcfta). it is important to promote trade association agreements and international free trade, but this must be done on the basis of transparency and mutual respect for the rules. to this end, safeguard clauses have been inserted into the anti-circumvention mechanism of the trade association agreement between the european union and the republic of georgia: they do not constitute an anachronistic protectionist measure, which does not belong to the political will of either the commission or the parliament, but a form of protection for producers and consumers by the possibility of restoring the rate of customs duty if imports of certain agricultural products from georgia (listed in annex ii-c) exceed a certain threshold in the absence of a valid justification as to their exact origin. the anti-circumvention clauses are important to avoid the importation into the union of non-georgian products through georgia using the advantages of the agreement to circumvent the 'rules of origin' requirements.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation implementing the anti-circumvention mechanism providing for the temporary suspension of the tariff preferences contained in the association agreement between the european union and georgia. the anti-circumvention mechanism allows the suspension of a more favourable customs duty on imports of certain agricultural products from georgia in order to restore the original tariff rate whenever a certain threshold is exceeded without any justification. the draft resolution also provides for the application of another circumvention clause, which makes it possible to prevent imports into the eu of non-georgian products which, through georgia, would be able to enter the european market thanks to the advantages provided for by the abovementioned association agreement. in particular, it is intended to prevent other countries from circumventing the requirements of 'rules of origin' and still being able to bring their goods into europe. the proposed regulation implements the provisions of the eu-georgia association agreement which parliament gave its consent to on 18 december 2014 and i have therefore decided to vote in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ the association agreement between the european union and georgia signed in 2014 introduced a preferential trade regime that guarantees mutual free market access. to protect producers from both sides, the agreement includes an anti-circumvention mechanism providing for the possibility of reintroducing the most-favoured-nation customs duty when imports of certain agricultural products from georgia exceed a certain threshold without due justification of their exact origin. in addition, the 'circumvention clause' is necessary to prevent imports into the eu of non-georgian products through georgia by taking advantage of the agreement and to prevent countries with bilateral free trade agreements with georgia, such as turkey, from using the agreement with the union to circumvent the origin requirements. the anti-circumvention mechanism will therefore temporarily suspend the tariff preferences contained in the agreement, in order to protect european producers and citizens. that is why i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution. i am against gmos and i am if possible even more against gmos which, like fg72 soybean, express resistance to herbicides: in this case the notorious glyphosate and isoxaflutol, whose safety data sheet reads: "highly toxic to aquatic organisms". obviously, if a crop is not affected by the use of isoxaflutol, it will tend to use more of it. rain transfers the weedkillers to watercourses - the very environment in which the weedkiller isoxaflutol is highly toxic - and to groundwater. according to the 12th national report on pesticides and water prepared by ispra (the higher institute for protection and research under the ministry of the environment), italian waters are full of everything, starting with herbicides: up to 60 different substances in the same sample. the substances in this cocktail can produce an additive effect or, worse, a synergistic effect. in any case, the damage is greater than the simple sum of its components. the commission has also proposed that the eu should be able to use its own resources to support the development of the eu's energy sector.
in writing. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution which strongly calls on the european commission not to authorise the placing on the market of genetically modified soybean fg72 (mst-fgø72-2) designed by monsanto to tolerate glyphosate spraying. once again the big biotech companies have tried to sell gm products to 500 million european citizens. glyphosate-resistant soybeans and glyphosate are yet another commercial package designed by monsanto, a multinational corporation that, in order to increase its profits, is ready to override the health of people without any scruples, as shown by the case of argentina. glyphosate, the most widely used weedkiller in the world, has been classified by the international agency for research on cancer (iarc) and the world health organization (who) as "probably carcinogenic" to humans, and we in the five star movement have long campaigned for its ban in europe. we therefore have no intention of allowing the cultivation of organisms specially modified to tolerate this pesticide on european territory. since the beginning of my mandate i have been fighting to make europe a gmo-free area and with this vote i reiterate a firm no to the entry of transgenic products into european territory.
in writing. ‒ the five star movement has always defended the interests of citizens, both in italy and in europe, and has fought against the placing on the market of food and feed containing genetically modified soya. the application for authorization submitted by monsanto requires unanimous agreement by the scientific community, and this agreement has not yet been reached. for these reasons i voted in favour of the objection procedure.
in writing. ‒ the introduction of genetically modified organisms resistant to herbicides can pose a serious threat to the health of european citizens and the environment. today i voted in favour of the objections to the authorisation of three types of genetically modified soya, including mon 87708 x mon 89788, because i believe that the current regulatory framework does not allow the commission and efsa to provide adequate assessments of the impact of gmos. as regards soybean mon 87708 x mon 89788, in particular, the concern concerns the presence of the dmo protein conferring tolerance to dicamba-based herbicides and the epsps protein conferring tolerance to glyphosate-based herbicides. in march 2015, the international agency for research on cancer, a specialized agency of the who, classified glyphosate as a probable human carcinogen. in view of the potential health hazard, i decided to vote in favour of the objection, reiterating the need for the commission to draw up a comprehensive proposal on gmos and gm-based feed as soon as possible, in order to carefully assess the environmental and health impact of these technologies.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution. i am against gmos and i am - if possible - even more against gmos which, like mon-87705-6 × mon-89788-1 soybean, express tolerance to herbicides, in this case the notorious glyphosate. crops engineered to resist glyphosate are particularly prevalent in the united states. their presence has led to increased use of glyphosate - without, however, increasing yields - and to the emergence of weeds which are themselves resistant to glyphosate: the massive use of glyphosate triggers a kind of accelerated darwinian selection (what else could we expect?) that causes farmers to use even more powerful herbicides. and so on, in a vicious cycle of poisons and poison resistance. i don't want to see any more "darwinian effects" of this chemical escalation on weeds. i would stress that the toxicity and carcinogenicity of glyphosate indicate the need for strict protection and prevention measures. it's obvious to expect glyphosate residues in crops engineered to resist it. all citizens have the right to access quality food products free of contaminants.

in writing. ‒ health protection is a priority for the european union, but unfortunately the continuing pressure from the lobbies has pushed the commission to take big steps backwards. the draft regulation introduced, among other things, an overly high compliance factor, which resulted in a general derogation from the applicable emission limits. ambitious measures are needed to reduce emissions and it is certainly unacceptable to downsize the objectives and content of the previous regulation (ec) no 715/2007. for these reasons i voted in favour of the resolution tabled by the committee on the environment, which opposes the amendments, because the protection of the environment and the protection of citizens cannot and must not be threatened by mere economic interests.
in writing. ‒ the transport sector generated 46% of nitrogen oxides (nox) emissions and around 14% of particulate matter emissions in the eu in 2013; these are two types of pollutants linked to adverse effects on health, the environment and the climate. the outbreak of the vw scandal led the european commission to take note of the discrepancy between the emission values obtained by laboratory tests and those obtained by road tests and to submit a proposal for a regulation to temporarily raise the permissible limits for nitrogen oxide emissions from passenger cars. i supported the objection of the committee on the environment, in the belief that the commission's proposal could constitute a general derogation capable of causing a huge impact on the emission of pollutants into the environment. despite the leadership of european industry - and within it italian industry - in the field of emission reduction technologies, i am convinced that there is still a long way to go. a shared effort is needed to ensure that environmental protection and the protection of public health are reconciled with the needs of industry and the protection of jobs.

in writing. ‒ it is very important to clarify why i voted against this objection, and therefore in favour of this delegated act, especially since some political groups have demagogically speculated on this vote by showing that they have not read the papers. here 's the thing: do we want to measure vehicle emissions under real conditions or under simulated conditions? i prefer the former to the latter (which have been created so far specifically to test with rigged values), and so i appreciated the commission's willingness to adapt the limits to real conditions, revising them downwards in any case compared to what was happening in practice before. in other words, the vehicle that polluted x in the tests actually polluted y times x. now we have taken the real parameter (y times x) as a reference and lowered it in such a way as to improve the quality of the environment. it's a pity that many of my colleagues didn't understand that.
in writing. ‒ i felt i had to vote against this measure which would equate the data derived from tests on vehicles carried out in the laboratory with those under real road driving conditions. in fact, it was found that cars put on the market after laboratory tests did not meet the emission limits on the road, exceeding the limit by an average of 4/5 times. if the objection had been accepted, we would have been faced with a situation in which the cars currently on the road would have continued to emit emissions within the limits approved by the laboratory tests. therefore, the current objective is to get the commission to come forward quickly with a rde package to achieve a short, but sustainable and timely compliance factor of 1 (80 mg/kg) as soon as possible and no later than 2023, restoring consumer confidence, safeguarding air quality and enabling automotive companies to invest in more environmentally friendly technologies without having to cut jobs.
