in writing. following the introduction of new vehicle type-approval tests, in which exhaust gas emissions are measured in road driving rather than in the laboratory, technical changes were necessary to convert the values when switching from one measurement mode to another. the result of our vote is an environmental result because it actually reduces the emissions that the machines will produce, with a review process that will start at the beginning of 2017 and will have an annual monitoring. cars on the road today emit about 360 milligrams per kilometer. this means that manufacturers will have to put cars on the market that emit 168 mg/km from 2017, and 80 mg/km by 2023. today we must defend air quality, but we must also boost european growth. instead of a legislative vacuum, waiting for a new proposal and a new process (which would have taken between 1 and 2 years), our companies will have a certain framework, which will allow investment in technologies that are more environmentally friendly and the protection of hundreds of thousands of jobs, and we will protect our citizens by significantly improving the quality of the air we breathe.
in writing. ‒ the objection under article 106 of the regulation on emissions from passenger and light commercial vehicles (euro6) does not meet my vote in favour. the vote is to support the clear importance of being able to provide a certain framework of rules, thus enabling producers to make a timely investment which can actually lead to a reduction in emissions. this is another key point which justifies the vote, since this will lead to a real progressive reduction in vehicle emissions. finally, it should be stressed that the parameters to be respected must be those of real road tests and not laboratory tests which are not faithful to actual vehicle use situations and therefore not useful for the purpose of effective information.
in writing. ‒ given the seriousness of air pollution, which causes 430 000 premature deaths in europe each year and costs public coffers 940 billion euro, i welcome the objection to the european commission's proposal. the measures mentioned appear inadequate for the effective protection of public health and too weak to send a signal to industry and to guide investment in environmental innovation. the political response to the measurement scandal is also likely to appear weak. in view of our commitment to the inclusion of strict environmental clauses and the promotion of european environmental standards in international trade agreements, we cannot in any way approve a proposal which could potentially weaken the position of the european negotiators in the various trade initiatives and, in particular, in the negotiations with the american counterpart. the commission proposal also appears to be inconsistent and hardly compatible with the ambitious goals set by the paris agreement on climate change. a european diplomatic victory that confirmed the union's role as the main supporter of the fight against global warming. the european union has been able to demonstrate the parallel between growth and environmental protection. we therefore ask the commission to draw up a new proposal that is commensurate with the historic european achievement.
in writing. ‒ a number of criticisms have been raised about the potential harm caused by nitrogen oxides (nox). in order to eliminate these critical points, the text entrusts the commission with a continuous monitoring task; it is therefore foreseen that if the proposed proportions are no longer considered adequate, a revision will be made. i do not think it is appropriate to support the objection and therefore i am voting against the measures adopted by the regulation on emissions from passenger and light commercial vehicles (euro 6).
in writing. ‒ the commission's proposal for a regulation on emission limits for passenger and light commercial vehicles (euro 6) would not only change but also completely overturn the rules established so far. the proposed increase in the maximum emission values for nitrogen oxides is technically unjustifiable and politically unacceptable, because it is contrary to the programme of the european strategy for cleaner air and because the commission, with its proposal, is trying to appropriate powers that are not its own, as clearly established by article 5 (3) of regulation (ec) no 715/2007. it is understandable that the new real driving emissions (rde) test procedure, based on the portable emissions monitoring system (pems), requires an update to take into account the margin of error of the pems systems. the commission proposal, however, goes too far, unjustifiably raising the ceilings, de facto and forever. i therefore voted against this increase proposed by the commission because it is in complete contradiction with the environmental policies that europe has been trying to pursue for years, not forgetting the very high cost of human lives which, according to recent studies on air pollution, is attributed to nox emissions.
in writing. ‒ the second rde package (real drive emissions real road emissions), proposed by the european commission and approved on 28 october 2015 by the technical committee for vehicles, aims to establish a number of quantitative criteria, including the so-called compliance factor, in order to equalise the data from tests on vehicles carried out in the laboratory with those under real road driving conditions and to limit vehicle emissions (euro 6). this technical need arises from the introduction of the new tests, where exhaust emissions are measured in road driving, and does not change the legislative type-approval limit imposed by regulation (ec) no 715/2007, which remains, in the case of nox, 80 mg/km for the euro 6 stage. if this objection had been accepted, we would have been faced with a situation in which the cars currently on the roads in our cities and regions would have continued to emit emissions within the limits approved by laboratory tests, which in real terms, that is to say, in road driving conditions, can be higher by about 400-500%. that is why i voted against its approval.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the objection to reward the result achieved after a long and difficult mediation process, where all the interlocutors took a step towards compromise. parliament thus succeeded in not rejecting the european commission's proposal for a regulation on the transposition of vehicle emission tests from the laboratory to the road, which would have blocked work for another two years. the tests shall be true and adapted to real driving conditions. it is therefore unthinkable that they should produce the same results and that emissions should have the same limits. that is why we must give industry time to improve its technology without imposing unattainable limits. the latest ec proposal introduces a stricter stepwise review of conformity factors, so as to encourage car manufacturers to constantly improve, and establishes more transparent and independent control systems.
in writing. ‒ with the introduction of new real driving conditions (rde) tests, vehicle emissions on the road will be as consistent as possible with those recorded so far during laboratory tests, with the aim of ensuring stricter enforcement of existing regulations and curbing the dangerous increase in pollutant and particulate emissions. it is therefore of paramount importance that the legislative process on ecn tests is not delayed or even halted. for this reason, i voted against the motion for an objection which would have prevented the new procedure from coming into force by causing delays in the implementation of the emission control measures and in fact achieving the opposite of the desired result in terms of improving air quality in the european union.
in writing. ‒ despite the fact that the majority was not achieved by a narrow margin, i voted in favour of the resolution recommending that the european parliament veto the commission's draft delegated act establishing the procedure for real driving emissions (rde) tests for motor vehicles. the text was therefore unfortunately rejected, allowing the temporary increase of the limits on emissions from vehicles in real driving conditions. the european commission considers that the measure is justified by the need to address the technical concerns regarding the use of the new portable emission measurement devices as well as the technical limitations for improving the real driving performance of emission detection for currently produced diesel vehicles. however, in the face of the increase in air pollution and the resulting respiratory diseases, i consider it a mistake and a lack of respect for citizens to fail to meet commitments to protect the environment and human health. today's vote shows that a large part of parliament wants the commitments to be respected and will continue to follow closely future developments on emissions testing and the responses given by the commission and parliament.
in writing. ‒ we in m5s voted in favour of the resolution which favoured the weakening of emission limits, thus vetoing the measures to double emissions. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive. previously, euro 6 cars could emit nitrogen oxides (nox) up to a limit of 80 mg/km. now, thanks to the commission's document, euro 6 cars will be able to emit 168 mg/km of nox until 2020 and still comply with the rules. the car lobbies have managed to win this battle by making parliament believe that if the rejection were to pass, it would mean the end of the car companies and thus the loss of many jobs. it 's obviously a scam . cars exported to the us meet limits half as high as those in the eu. that's because these are the same limits that were introduced in 2007 to give carmakers time to comply. it is clear that the multinationals wanted to circumvent the rules, rather than invest in innovation to reduce emissions.
in writing. with the introduction of new exhaust gas measuring instruments, almost all vehicles would be at risk of being outlawed. the member states have dealt with this problem by introducing amendments which bring the emission limits into line with those traditionally measured from the exhaust pipe. lower limits would have been irreparable economic damage to the lobby of the car manufacturers. the resolution recommended that the european parliament veto the european commission's proposal to introduce new procedures for the approval and monitoring of road emissions by means of portable detectors from 2017. this would have allowed the car industry to adjust to the parameters in a reasonable period of time. in the meantime, cars would be free to pollute twice as much as today's limits. but who can guarantee that more restrictive measures will be adopted in a year's time? i voted in favour of the resolution because the technology to reduce pollution already exists and has been on the car market for some time. the commission has not yet taken any decision on the matter.

in writing. - we in the 5 star movement are strongly opposed to the tisa. that said, it is important to note that m5s did not say yes to tisa, but it did say yes to a certain kind of mandate for tisa negotiators. in particular, the amendments adopted make it clear that essential public services, which guarantee the fundamental rights of european citizens, such as health, the environment, education and cultural services, are inviolable. the european commission will be obliged to negotiate with other countries in a transparent manner and through positive lists, i.e. by publicly stating which services to liberalize. there will also be no irreversible privatisations. the text thus approved makes it difficult to approve it in the future. i voted in favour of this because i think it is extremely dangerous to leave the negotiators with a blank cheque.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the reding report on the european parliament's recommendations to the commission on the negotiations on the trade in services agreement (tisa). the agreement, currently being negotiated in geneva, involves 23 wto countries plus the eu, covering 70% of the world's services sector. this is a fundamental process because the union is the world's largest importer and exporter of services and has a particular interest in the establishment of a sound international framework for international trade in services. i think that the report before parliament effectively underlines the need to ensure greater reciprocity in market access, to ensure a level playing field at global level and to offer concrete benefits to consumers. the future multilateralisation of the treaty will therefore have to be facilitated while keeping public and cultural services, the right to regulate, fundamental rights to data confidentiality and those related to working conditions out of the negotiations.

in writing. ‒ services are a key sector of the union's economy. europe is the world's largest exporter of services, with 25% of the global market. however, there are still many barriers, especially non-tariff barriers, which slow down the internationalisation of smes and prevent them from accessing new markets. since 1995, with the spread of the internet, the economy has changed and services continue to gain increasing importance in international economies; this is one more reason to regulate and ensure greater reciprocity in access to markets, ensuring global equality and fairness in working conditions. the tisa will have to lead to an ambitious level of opening up of the services market to smes. however, parliament rightly calls for public and cultural services and the fundamental right to data privacy to be excluded. today's vote, which i fully support, is not a judgment on the agreement or on the signing of the agreement itself but on the set of clear recommendations which the european parliament has made and which the commission will have to take into account in the negotiation phase. respect for working conditions and the environment is among the main criteria which will guide the definition of the tisa.

in writing. ‒ the report aims to assess the first two and a half years and 13 rounds of negotiations on trade in services (tisa) and to make clear and precise recommendations to the european commission. the tisa negotiations are to ensure greater reciprocity in access to services markets (telecommunications, transport, financial services, energy), create a level playing field globally (including in the procurement market), provide tangible benefits for consumers and ensure the future multilateralisation of the agreement. the report is not perfect but it says loud and clear that public services are not to be touched, that there must be no irreversible privatisations and that citizens' rights come before free trade. it is necessary to negotiate services through positive lists (i.e. by stating which services will be liberalised) and to give local authorities the freedom to decide in the future to suspend liberalisation in certain areas. the signing of the tisa is a long way off and today m5s didn't say yes to tisa, they said yes to a certain kind of mandate for tisa negotiators. my vote is therefore in favour.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament has sought to set clear boundaries for the negotiators involved in negotiating tisa, a new agreement which, according to a study published on the parliament's own website, should be 'a more effective vehicle for wider liberalisation'. tisa is even described as more liberalising than ttip. but we know that behind the word 'liberalisation' there are privatisations which generally coincide with a real assault on public assets and excellences. the liberalization of services through the tisa can conceal pitfalls and dangers for citizens, for employment, for health. just think about what happened with the creation of multi-utilities in the early 2000s in italy: the private sector has gobbled up the public and chased profits for its own sake, with the result that the quality of services provided has declined and prices and tariffs have soared. the vote on the report is therefore a vote to keep the negotiators on the straight and narrow, to set clear limits on their action, to safeguard public services and to consider possible steps backwards in privatisation. in other words, it is a vote necessary to protect the citizens.
in writing. ‒ as in the case of the transatlantic trade and investment treaty with the usa, the european parliament today made clear recommendations to the commission on the ongoing negotiations on the trade in services agreement (tisa). the report states in clear terms that the aim of tisa must be to regulate international trade in services, taking due account of the effects of the digital revolution on this sector, with particular attention to the implications for consumers and workers. we therefore wanted the report to express clearly our 'no' to an agreement without safeguards, but at the same time to recognise that without clear and effective regulation there can be no protection for citizens. we also want this treaty, whose negotiations are proceeding between 23 countries, to be concluded in full compliance with and consistent with the rules established at multilateral level, so that in the future it may include as many states as possible: it is in multilateral fora such as the wto that we can reach ambitious agreements that have the merit of leading to ever more fair trade and equal rules for all. i therefore voted in favour of the report on the negotiations for the agreement on trade in services.
in writing. ‒ in a fragmented and discontinuous process of globalisation, the european union needs to have a long-term vision not only of the international markets in which it is a key player, but also of the social and political scenarios that are interconnected. today, the value chain has taken on a global scale and has allowed for a significant reduction in costs for many european companies, but the data show that only a part of the heterogeneous european business landscape has managed to overcome this global challenge, there are numerous cases instead of companies that have failed to relocate in a way that is advantageous to these new scenarios. the european union should have an appropriate set of measures to meet the challenge of these negotiations with a positive contribution for europe as a whole. it is also important to remember the price of these negotiations in terms of the bargaining and often denial of rights both within the eu and in companies outside its borders that make up its value chain. parliament must be a pragmatic voice for all social, environmental and political actors if europe as a whole and its diversity is to meet this challenge.

in writing. ‒ the trade in services agreement (tisa) is an agreement currently being negotiated between 23 members of the world trade organisation, including the european union and its 28 member states. i voted in favour of the report because it sets out the european parliament's priorities for the continuation of the tisa negotiations, the aim of which is to liberalize trade in services. i would remind you that the eu is the world's largest importer and exporter of services, and 70% of its workforce is employed in the service sector. however, the barriers to entry for european service providers, when translated into corresponding figures, are 15% in canada, 25% in south korea, 44% in turkey and 68% in china, while in the eu the rate corresponding to the restrictions for the provision of services for foreign operators is only 6%. the european union therefore has a particular interest in the creation of a sound regulatory base that guarantees greater reciprocity in market access, ensures a level playing field at global level and offers concrete benefits to consumers.
in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the resolution containing the european parliament's recommendations for the negotiation of the trade in services agreement (tisa), a multilateral trade agreement currently being negotiated between 23 wto members, including the european union. the global rules on the exchange of services are set out in the gats, an agreement signed in 1995 which appears to be obsolete today because of the emergence of online services that did not exist or were not available 20 years ago. the aim of tisa is precisely to update the gats rules in order to continue to facilitate the exchange of services at multilateral level, considering the deadlock in the wto from this point of view. as the socialist group, we have been able to identify a number of precise points for the negotiations on the agreement, such as the complete exclusion of public services from the negotiating mandate, the safeguarding of social and workers' rights, the affirmation of the full right of the states to regulate and legislate in the public interest, greater transparency and involvement of parliament in the negotiating process. the commission should therefore negotiate the agreement in accordance with these guidelines, to avoid parliament opposing the final text of a treaty which does not protect our standards.
in writing. ‒ i am not in favour of the tisa treaty but i voted in favour of these recommendations because they draw important red lines which the european commission will not have to cross during the negotiations: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. this text is far from perfect. i support him insofar as he does not give the negotiators and the lobbies of the big business any free hand. it's a first step just a first step in the right direction: i will also work with all my strength to ensure that the eu and its citizens do not fall into the trap of the international treaties tisa and ttip, which are added to a third treaty, the tpp for the pacific rim countries, and in synergy with the latter form an economic pincer against the usa. it would be reductive to call the tisa a 'free trade agreement'. rather, it (just like ttip and tpp), if it is ever approved, will form part of the web of rules that aims to reshape the layout of the richest part of the world economy. a web woven in the interests of business interests and at the expense of citizens.
in writing. ‒ it is crucial that the ongoing negotiations on the trade in services agreement (tisa) conclude with an agreement that facilitates access for eu businesses to international markets, but it is necessary to ensure that public services, which are crucial to our economies, are not included in the terms of the negotiation. this vote by the european parliament is not a vote for or against the agreement: we need a clear mandate to define the limits, the red lines that will enable us to protect and defend consumers and to respond to the challenges of globalisation and digitalisation. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. it is important to curb restrictive practices by third countries against european companies, such as the forced localisation of data or restrictions on the presence of foreign capital. finally, less bureaucratic procedures are needed for smes, which lack the human and financial resources to navigate the complex rules of international trade.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which contains the european parliament's recommendations to the commission for the negotiation of the tisa agreement, an agreement which aims to update the existing rules on trade in services, which have been blocked in the wto. the tisa agreement is an important opportunity to regulate globalisation, but we have also expressed some concerns, such as the risks to public services or the lowering of the level of protection of workers' rights. the rules underlying international trade clearly need updating, but not at any cost. the commission will have to take account of these recommendations to ensure a favourable vote by parliament.
in writing. ‒ tisa could have a very serious impact on citizens, as its consequences could affect basic services such as health, utilities, education and transport, all in the context of liberalisation driven by pressure from multinationals and lobbyists. the report we have voted on today, however, is limited to an assessment of the first negotiations and to making clear and precise recommendations to the commission. in voting in favour, i did not give my consent to the agreement, but to the type of negotiating mandate. it must ensure greater reciprocity in access to services markets, create a level playing field, offer tangible benefits to consumers and ensure future multilateralisation. public and cultural services, the fundamental rights to data confidentiality and privacy, and fair working conditions must not be negotiable, but categorically excluded from the scope of the agreement. the main objective must be to give a negotiating mandate that does not affect public services, that opposes irreversible privatizations and that puts citizens' rights before free trade. the text is certainly not perfect, but it must serve to prevent the negotiators from being given a free hand, which could play into the hands of the lobbies and the big powers.
in writing. the report aims to assess the progress of this first phase of the trade in services treaty (tisa) negotiations and to make clear recommendations to the european commission. the final text of the agreement will have to ensure greater reciprocity in terms of access to services markets (in the telecommunications, transport, financial services and energy sectors), creating a level playing field at global level (including the procurement market) and at the same time offering tangible benefits to consumers. after the first of 13 rounds of negotiations lasting two and a half years, thanks to the five star movement, the european commission will no longer have a blank cheque, because the recommendations adopted by parliament contain fundamental principles for the protection of public services which can no longer be ignored. services related to culture, data privacy rights and fair working conditions must strictly be excluded from the scope of the agreement, because i consider them non-negotiable. i believe that local consumers and service providers must be protected by appropriate regulation, so that they can make the most of all the opportunities at european level. that is why i am voting in favour.

european parliament for this oral question on support for islands, outermost regions under the european structural and investment funds. i would like to say from the outset that i am particularly concerned about this subject. last year we had two meetings: the annual meeting in guadeloupe and another in réunion, and in the last session in strasbourg i had a meeting with my colleague, commissioner karmenu vella, with all nine members of the european parliament from the outermost regions, precisely to see how far we could, at the beginning of the 2014-2020 programming period, help these regions, which, as you said, in addition to being very far from europe, have a number of specific problems. as you know, our funds, european funds, have a long and successful tradition of supporting regions with specific geographical characteristics, including island regions that face various social, economic and environmental challenges and require a specific case-by-case approach. these aspects are, in my view, reflected in the new regulation, covering the 2014-2020 programming period, which calls on member states, where appropriate, to establish an integrated approach in the framework of partnership agreements, in order to address the specific needs of regions facing severe and sometimes permanent handicaps. this is why a number of islands already benefit from a derogation as regards the thematic concentration of investments from the european regional development fund. other islands benefit from greater flexibility in taking into account their specific needs. in addition, the outermost regions, which are all islands, also benefit from a number of exceptions and specific conditions, thus attempting to compensate for the severe and permanent constraints they face. but of course, as you have pointed out, i think we can do more. the commission shall monitor the situation in the nuts-2 and nuts-3 regions. the commission has developed a series of synthetic indicators which take into account, for example, the regional competitiveness index or the human development index. unfortunately, the data we have and have at our disposal are not sufficiently precise at the moment to reflect the specific characteristics of all island regions, but we are continuing to invest in collecting data and forecasts, which will allow us to present a more detailed analysis of the situation in these regions in the next cohesion report.

in writing. ‒ article 174 tfeu recognises the reduction of regional disparities in social, economic and environmental terms as a fundamental objective of the eu. the development of the territorial characteristics not only contributes to the enrichment of europe's economic and cultural heritage, but also fits perfectly into the strategies of cohesion policies. the european union's support is essential and a priority, given that, unfortunately, the natural handicaps of some mediterranean islands are compounded by economic difficulties and the complexity of managing the flow of migrants. in fact, to fully achieve the objectives of development, growth and jobs, the eu should promote coordinated action and the development of vertical strategies involving all levels of government. for these reasons i voted in favour, because i strongly believe that ensuring the harmonious development of the islands can be an opportunity and a means of growth at local and european level.
in writing. ‒ the european islands represent a common heritage in terms of biodiversity and culture within the union. these areas, which are often located on the borders of the european union, are particularly vulnerable to problems of energy supply, demographic trends, climate change and, in particular, migration flows. my support for the resolution on island status is based on the conviction that strong action is needed to end the disadvantages suffered by the islands and to ensure the achievement of economic, social and territorial cohesion policies. the commission should develop a genuine 'union strategic framework for the islands' linking all instruments that can have a significant impact on the territory. the potential of europe's islands must be exploited, ensuring the development of sustainable tourism systems alongside seasonal tourism, while at the same time not losing sight of the great opportunities offered by islands as sources of alternative energy such as ocean, wind and solar.
in writing. ‒ island regions need special protection, given the greater difficulties they face in accessing services compared to mainland areas. so far, there have been shortcomings in the provision of such protection by the european institutions to these disadvantaged areas. i therefore share the objective of this report in bringing this issue to the eu's attention and i voted in favour.
in writing. i voted in favour of this document because i believe that the insularity and its characteristics are evidence that the european institutions cannot ignore, but that they must work to find solutions to compensate for the disadvantages that insularity brings with it compared to continental regions.
in writing. ‒ the european union has several island regions which, in accordance with article 174 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), are classified as nuts-2 and nuts-3 regions because they have common characteristics and specificities of a permanent nature which clearly distinguish them from regions situated on the mainland. the european union therefore recognises that these regions, because of their shape and geographical location, suffer from specific disadvantages which require specific attention. in the light of the above, the commission considers that the aid should be limited to the minimum necessary to achieve the objective of common interest. we believe that this decision is wrong and problematic and that the commission should clarify which specific instruments and resources under cohesion policy it intends to make available to offset the disadvantages arising from the insularity of these territories.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution by the committee on regional development, which was based on a question on the implementation of article 174 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, because it is clear to everyone that the european commission has not implemented the provisions of that article in the slightest. both island and mountain regions have difficult access to services. the merit of this resolution is to raise the issue and to underline that the objectives of cohesion should also pass through greater protection of the human presence on the islands. this principle certainly seems to be in contradiction with the strict rules against state aid which are faced by the managers who in these territories would like to promote air and sea links (see the ryanair, saremar and tirrenia cases in sardinia). the logic of the free market must therefore be balanced with the need for island and continental citizens to be able to travel without problems and without particular expense. in the case of sardinia, we can clearly say that the member state in question is also guilty of serious faults, having invested very little in recent years to remove the obstacles arising from the principle of insularity.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the status of the islands. the resolution stressed that the common specific characteristics of a permanent nature clearly distinguish island regions from those on the mainland and that the condition of being an island presents permanent natural and geographical disadvantages. the resolution stresses the need to support the balanced territorial development of island regions by promoting innovation and competitiveness in these regions, which are located at great distances from the main administrative and economic centres and which do not have easy access to transport. the resolution stresses the importance of support measures to counter the significant trend towards depopulation of island regions and calls on the european commission to undertake a thorough analysis of the additional costs of insularity in terms of transport systems for people and goods, energy supply and market access, particularly for smes. i therefore decided to vote in favour of the resolutions.
in writing. ‒ the eu, through article 174 tfeu, recognises the disadvantages of island regions which hamper their development and prevent them from achieving economic, social and territorial cohesion. the text calls on the commission to undertake a thorough analysis of the additional costs of insularity in terms of transport systems for passengers and goods and energy supply, and in terms of market access, particularly for smes. in the light of the foregoing, i have voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ reducing the gap between the levels of development of european regions is the main objective of cohesion policy, which, as stated in article 174 of the lisbon treaty, is directed above all to the less-favoured areas, including the islands. however, the peripherality of these areas can become an added value for europe, particularly in relation to the production of alternative energy or the protection of biodiversity. cohesion policy has not so far given the right space to these areas, for which a section should be devoted to addressing the specificities and permanent disadvantages linked to their geographical location. i therefore find it most appropriate that parliament should call for the creation of an island office and a european agenda for island regions, all areas for which cohesion policy funds should be used to initiate and launch development processes adapted to the needs and requirements of these territories. i voted in favour of the resolution because i believe that the gap which still exists between the regions of europe can only be closed by policies and measures which are more closely linked to the needs and natural developmental vocations of these specific areas.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the island status which i tabled and which i strongly supported. the union's islands are peripheral territorial areas at the external borders of the eu and are particularly vulnerable to the challenges facing europe, such as globalisation, demographic change, climate change, energy supply and exposure to illegal immigration. the european islands contribute to the diversity of the union, both from an environmental and cultural point of view. the european islands can contribute to strengthening the union's sustainable development, given their high potential for producing energy from renewable sources by virtue of their privileged exposure to wind, sea and sun. we strongly urge the commission, in the substantial application of article 174 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, to give concrete recognition to the status of insularity by creating, for classification purposes, a homogeneous grouping including all island territories. i hope that the commission will assess the islands of europe as a homogeneous group of regions which deserve ad hoc regional development programmes, and will endeavour to develop statistical indicators which will more accurately measure the disadvantages of island status, and not merely take account of rigid statistical indicators measured as a percentage of gdp.
in writing. ‒ i am very pleased to have voted in favour of this resolution, which is the result of a concerted effort to support my colleague salvatore cicu, the real architect of this political document. it is time for someone to come along and put something in black and white that is in plain sight of everyone except the european bureaucrats: the commission has not yet adopted a proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster. it is said that when, at the end of the second world war, italy voted in the famous referendum to keep the monarchy or go to the republic, the sardinian ballot papers were thrown into the sea to distort the result in favor of the republic, since sardinia was expected, after the stripping that would take place in rome, a strongly pro-monarchist vote. salvatore cicu, to his credit, has been able to make it clear with this resolution that the will of the sardinian people will never again be ignored or trampled underfoot. congratulations on a job well done!
in writing. ‒ i agree with some of my colleagues who, during the debate, highlighted the need to review the priorities within the strategic framework for future programming. the commission has so far proposed measures for the outermost regions, completely ignoring the situation of the islands, which are marginalised not only geographically but also economically and socially. there is no regional continuity, which means a lack of services and competition, a strain on smes, and an environment hostile to low-cost companies and multinationals. i therefore hope that the commission will pay more attention to the situation of the islands, including through the provision of specific funding.

in writing. the economic crisis has severely limited the availability of finance in many sectors, leading to a collapse in public investment. this has had a serious impact on the development of many disadvantaged regions, especially the islands. i have therefore decided to give my full support to this motion for a resolution calling for favourable measures which take account of the specific characteristics of the islands and the territorial discontinuity. our first objective must be to exploit the synergies between the different european resources, to develop our infrastructure and to improve our links in terms of air, rail and sea transport. we must be able to use the funds available effectively, within a strategic vision, and not to plug budgetary holes. only under these conditions can the revival of our territories begin.

in writing. ‒ island regions, classified at community level as nuts-2 and nuts-3 regions, share common characteristics and specificities which distinguish them clearly from regions situated on the mainland. article 174 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) recognises that they suffer from specific disadvantages requiring specific attention. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution to ask the commission to provide a clear definition of the type of permanent natural or demographic handicaps, within the meaning of article 174 tfeu, to which island regions are considered to be exposed. it would be desirable to launch a thorough analysis of the additional costs incurred by islands, such as those related to the transport system or energy supply, and to establish a 'european strategic framework for islands' which provides for a set of concrete instruments that could have a strong territorial impact. the islands of the european union are also very often peripheral regions situated at the eu's external borders and therefore particularly exposed to the arrival of migratory flows. i therefore believe that it is appropriate to maintain the special tax schemes designed to offset not only their permanent geographical disadvantages but also the costs of the large-scale migration phenomena which are taking place.
in writing. ‒ the resolution voted today is based on the need to respect the specificities of each country and region. the island areas, by their very nature, have different geographical conditions than the others, which means that they also have different needs, and for this reason the legislation must take account of these specificities. in this text we ask the commission to review the objectives for the island territories, to provide for greater synergy between the structural funds and the other instruments made available by the eu and to establish an eu strategic framework for the islands.
in writing. ‒ island regions share common characteristics and specificities which clearly distinguish them from regions on the mainland. however, the european union has so far made little effort to adapt its policies to take account of the unique difficulties many islands face in competing successfully with the mainland. i am referring in particular to disadvantages such as accessibility to services, higher prices due to transport costs, difficult access to the single market, lack of infrastructure, vulnerability to environmental risks, scarcity of raw materials and protection against illegal immigration. all these challenges that islands face on a permanent basis have not yet been adequately addressed by european legislation. i therefore voted in favour of the report because it calls for the difficulties of insularity to be recognised and for all possible synergies between the european structural and investment funds and the other instruments of the union to be exploited. i hope that by improving existing policies and using available resources more efficiently, island regions can overcome their obstacles in terms of economic growth, job creation and sustainable development.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the resolution on insularity, which contains some recommendations to deal with the problems associated with it, such as economic and social vulnerability, the additional costs incurred for transport, energy supply and access to markets. as the elected representative of two island regions, i believe it is necessary to support the islands, which have greater difficulties than other regions in overcoming a physiological developmental delay and in pursuing growth in line with the objectives of european cohesion policy. the priority issues include the remoteness of the main production centres and the difficulty of accessing the large european networks, but also the problems linked to the migratory flows to which many mediterranean islands are exposed. instruments such as special tax schemes previously granted to certain island regions are useful tools for counteracting the natural and demographic handicaps of island regions. i am convinced that the handicap of insularity can be overcome by networking the islands immediately, i.e. by ensuring that they have access to digital, energy and transport networks. i therefore hope that the commission will give careful consideration to the proposals contained in this resolution and take concrete action in a timely manner.
in writing. ‒ cohesion policy plays a key role in achieving european objectives by helping to create a growth process that enhances local realities. the introduction of incentive policies and cooperation between the european and local institutions will certainly help to reduce the economic, social and territorial disparities which currently exist between european states and their regions. in fact, adopting a more inclusive strategy can not only improve the quality of life of citizens, but above all make innovation and technology the most suitable tools to stimulate the european market and create new jobs. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the european structural and investment funds (esif) are the main instrument of investment policy and a pillar of the european union's cohesion policy. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution because i consider the role of local and regional authorities to be fundamental in this field. the multi-level governance achieved by cohesion policy allows a good balance to be struck between eu objectives and the territorial impact of policies, while strengthening the democratic dimension of the community institutions. the commission will have to work in the coming years to strengthen the role of regional and local authorities in the management and implementation of the esi funds through partnership agreements and operational programmes.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it underlines the key role of local and regional authorities in defining and implementing eu strategies, while recognising a wide variety of stakeholders, from member states to participatory groups. i also believe that the proximity of these authorities to citizens and the diversity of governance at local and regional level are a strength of the eu. although the chapter on 'eu territorial cohesion' is very often an example of funding projects of dubious utility, i can only support one of the few formal calls by the european parliament for the importance of 'local' governance, calling for greater territorial capacity in the use of these instruments.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of this resolution to underline the key role of local and regional authorities in defining and implementing eu strategies. i believe that the proximity of these authorities to citizens and the diversity of governance at local and regional level are a strength of the eu. our municipalities and regions must be allowed to negotiate, within a stable legal framework, investments in priority areas that are essential to the development of our societies, such as research and innovation, the transition to a low-carbon economy and social inclusion. for the policy to deliver, it is crucial that local and regional authorities are involved in the design, implementation and monitoring of programmes, for example by setting up joint task forces bringing together different levels of governance. strengthening the administrative capacity and addressing the structural weaknesses of local and regional authorities are key aspects of increasing the absorption rate of the european structural and investment funds. i therefore call on the commission to ensure that local and regional authorities and their administrations and institutions are supported in developing their capacities so that they can play a significant role in cohesion policy.
in writing. ‒ cohesion policy aims to reduce economic and social disparities between member states, in particular through the european structural and investment funds (esif), which bring together the european regional development fund (erdf), the european social fund (esf), the cohesion fund (cf), the european agricultural fund for rural development (eafrd) and the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff). to this end, mrs mihaylova's report recognises the importance of multi-level governance which supports these objectives (economic growth, social progress and sustainable development) by strengthening the democratic dimension of the eu and increasing the effectiveness of its political action; so i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ local authorities are the main beneficiaries of the structural and investment funds, which represent a real and tangible development opportunity for the economic revival of regions and municipalities. these are large and secure resources, allocated on the basis of the criteria laid down by cohesion policy. but very often these funds are not spent, not only because of administrative shortcomings, which have also affected some regions, but also because of the difficulty of achieving the objectives decided ex ante by the commission. the european parliament has repeatedly called for greater involvement of local authorities in the definition of objectives and priorities for growth, development and employment. in order to overcome the risk of not reaching the expenditure targets, it is essential that regions and municipalities participate actively in the objective setting phase in order to enable local authorities to present, on the basis of the difficulties encountered in the implementation phase, feasible priorities and objectives. next year will see the start of the process for the revision of cohesion policy post-2020 and it is therefore necessary to start thinking about greater involvement of local actors. i fully agree with the content of the resolution and that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i decided to support the measure as i firmly believe that local and regional authorities should have a key role in defining and implementing eu strategies, as their proximity to citizens and the diversity of governance at local and regional level are essential elements of a proper application of the principle of subsidiarity as expressed in the lisbon treaty. as regards the european structural investment funds (esi funds), i am absolutely in favour of synergies and complementarity between these funds and other eu programmes, where local and regional authorities can make a positive contribution to the achievement of the objectives of cohesion policy.
in writing. ‒ the european commission bases much of its work on the principle of subsidiarity, as laid down in the treaties. in other words, each issue should be addressed and resolved within the narrowest possible territorial framework which allows for an effective solution. however, until now the mechanisms for coordination and cooperation with smaller organisations (and therefore with smaller budgets) had not been defined, and this policy document is a step in this direction. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ in managing the european structural and investment funds, local and regional authorities play a key role in implementing the union's objective of greater economic, social and territorial cohesion and ensuring an effective territorial impact of eu policies. the european commission needs to continue to improve the scope of the esi funds as an important instrument, including through public consultations, in order to identify measures to strengthen the role of regional and local authorities in the management and implementation of the funds for the period 2014-2020. for these reasons i have decided to vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ for the first time, a coherent framework, called the 'common provisions regulation' (cpr), has been created for the period 2014-2020, defining common rules for the five european structural and investment funds (esi funds): the european regional development fund (erdf), the european social fund (esf), the cohesion fund (cf), the european agricultural fund for rural development (eafrd) and the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff) are all part of the same overall programme. it is important to identify measures to strengthen the role of regional and local authorities in the management and implementation of the esi funds through partnership agreements and operational programmes. this will enable local and regional authorities to strike a balance between the union's objective of greater economic, social and territorial cohesion on the one hand, and the particular needs of local communities on the other. in view of the importance of the role played by local authorities and the desire to strengthen the implementation of the principle of subsidiarity, i voted in favour of this resolution.

in writing. ‒ yemen's crisis has dragged on for 10 months and has escalated since the saudi coalition is launching airstrikes to stop the advance of the houthi rebel group, which had seized control of the capital sana'a and forced the government into exile in saudi arabia. the effects of these actions are having devastating effects throughout the country. according to the united nations, 82 percent of the population is in need of humanitarian assistance. the food situation is particularly worrying, with millions of people struggling to feed themselves, 1.3 million children are acutely malnourished (1.8 million out of school) and there is no access to clean water or basic health care. i voted in favour of this resolution to establish an international, independent and impartial commission of inquiry to examine all violations and abuses by the parties to the conflict and to identify the perpetrators in order to ensure that those responsible are held to account. the european union must promote compliance with international humanitarian law as provided for in the eu guidelines and must work to re-establish the conditions for a political dialogue under the auspices of the un, including saudi arabia and iran, which are crucial countries in encouraging an end to the conflict.

president-in-office of the council.– madam president, ungass 2016 is a key opportunity for the international community to take stock of the achievements of the international drug control system today. it also provides an opportunity to elaborate a response to the world drug problem and to find long-term solutions in the framework of the international treaties. as an outcome, ungass should adopt a short and action-oriented document comprising a set of operational recommendations, and the eu supports such an approach. to be more precise, the eu advocates the following priorities. first, we emphasise that the three un drug conventions which provide the international legal framework, and the universal declaration on human rights, should remain the cornerstone of the global response to the world drug problem. indeed, there is sufficient scope and flexibility within the provisions of the un drug conventions to accommodate a wide range of approaches to drug policy in accordance with national and regional specificities. second, we highlight the importance of human rights. we call for the abolition of the death penalty for drug-related offences as well as the abolition of other practices which are not in line with the principles of human dignity, liberty, democracy, equality, solidarity, the rule of law and human rights, and the eu continues to stress that the death penalty undermines human dignity while failing to act as a deterrent to criminal behaviour. also, the eu recalls that the application of the death penalty for drug-related crimes does not meet the threshold of the most serious crimes as set out by the international covenant on civil and political rights. third, we advocate drug policies based on an integrated, balanced and evidence-based approach. clearly, a balance between drug supply and drug demand reduction measures is needed, and we also call for drug policies to be underpinned by a sound public-health approach based on scientific evidence and supported by objective monitoring systems and evaluation. while the international drug conventions call for a balanced approach, we feel that in a number of states, measures to address drug production and trafficking take priority over drug use, prevention, risk and harm reduction, treatment, rehabilitation and recovery. therefore a stronger health approach is needed to redress this balance, and ungass is a unique opportunity to achieve that. the union also calls on state parties to guarantee access to risk- and harm-reduction measures, which are not only related to hiv/aids prevention but also cover a whole spectrum of measures to protect public health and society. the eu consistently stresses that these measures have proved their effectiveness in improving public health. we also advocate the promotion of alternative development as a long-term and holistic approach to tackle the root causes and framework conditions of the illicit cultivation of drug crops. finally, we attach great importance to the role of civil society and science, especially in the field of drug demand reduction. therefore the eu is also calling for the recognition of a role for civil society in drugs policies. these priorities will reflect that, in the common eu position on ungass set out in november last year and in the eu contribution to the ungass outcome document. currently the eu is closely involved in defending these priorities in the negotiations on the ungass outcome document, and we are glad to see that the ungass outcome document already includes many elements that are important to the eu. however, two important issues are still missing: first, a reference to the abolition of the death penalty for drug-related crimes, and second, strong language on risk- and harm-reduction measures. clearly the eu will have to keep on advocating the inclusion of these very important elements.
member of the commission.– madam president, the commission believes that the eu has a very important role to play in promoting a robust outcome at the united nations general assembly special session on drugs and is fully engaged in its preparation. the european union adopted last november a common position for the ungass. we are determined to speak with one strong voice, and you will hear that the commission is very much in agreement with the council at this session. we will ensure that critical issues for the eu’s common position are taken on board in negotiations on the outcome document. commissioner avramopoulos will represent the commission at the special session and seize the opportunity to present and promote the eu’s world—recognised model of drugs policy, and this policy is based on evidence. it drives a balanced approach between drug demand reduction and drug supply reduction and gives attention to the challenges, such as the online trade in drugs and new psychoactive substances. some of the key issues we will focus on have already been mentioned by the minister, but let me emphasise them again. our priorities include respect for human rights and the call for abolition of the death penalty for drug-related crimes, because they do not meet the threshold for the most serious crimes under international law. so, we have proposed from the eu side to organise a side event, during the special session, on the death penalty to explain our views on why capital punishment for drugs-related offences is not a good policy solution – and, by the way, it is never a good solution. we will also plead for proportional criminal justice when dealing with people who use drugs, and we will advocate rebalancing our drug policy towards public health approaches. this is the primary objective of an international drugs control system. we need to do more when it comes to demand reduction, encompassing prevention, early detection and intervention treatment, risk reduction, care, recovery, rehabilitation and social integration, and we are comparatively very well placed to share our experiences and best practices in this area. we will support the draft recommendations on drug supply reduction currently on the table. we want to see greater international cooperation and coordination to prevent and respond to drug-related crimes. primarily, the focus should be on those having a leading role in the trafficking chain. it is equally important to address the links between drug trafficking and other forms of organised crime, money laundering and corruption. the eu will remain active in regional and international networks addressing these issues. europol is contributing decisively to this end, offering experts and facilitating information exchange and best practices. we will also call for effective international cooperation on challenges such as drug trafficking on the internet and on new psychoactive substances – threats that concern all the regions of the world. we will stress the importance of building drug policies on evidence, reliable objective monitoring and evaluation systems. we have our own agency, the european monitoring centre of drugs and drug addiction (emcdda) in lisbon, which is pursuing these goals steadily. last but not least, we wish to see tailored measures for children, women and young people. therefore the eu will be at the forefront of those calling for greater involvement of civil society in the definition and implementation of our drugs policy. we have an expert group of 45 ngos in the form of the eu civil society forum on drugs, and they are a constant adviser to us. so, dear members of parliament, i am looking forward to hearing your interventions, which we will carefully take into account in our preparations and participation in ungass.
in its annual report for 2014, the italian national antimafia directorate felt obliged to highlight the total failure of repressive action to combat the spread of light drugs, in particular cannabis, and invited the italian parliament to assess, in a european context, whether decriminalisation of the matter is appropriate, taking into account the potential positive consequences in terms of deflation of the judicial burden, the release of resources to combat other criminal phenomena and, above all, the fight against the mafias. these are very weighty words from those on the front lines of the battle to enforce the current regulations, and they are part of a debate that has been brought to life by the positive experiences in countries such as uruguay and in several states in the united states of america, also in terms of reducing crime. this should make us reflect, especially in the run-up to the un general assembly's special session on drugs, a unique opportunity to review global drug policies, putting people, their health and human rights at the centre, and having the courage to change course. the repressive policies have failed to reduce the illegal market, overcrowded prisons, stigmatized drug users and fueled the multibillion-dollar trafficking of organized crime. i hope, therefore, that we will take this important opportunity to reflect on a change of course which is now necessary.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, there is one aspect which is often not taken into account in anti-drug strategies. it is not about repressive techniques, but about the environmental impact of the fight against drugs. between 2001 and 2013, over 700,000 acres of forest in latin america were cleared to make way for cocaine plantations. according to a study published by the open society foundations, an ngo headed by george soros, in the most critical areas of the world, the environmental consequences of the international drug war would be even more devastating than the economic and social ones. it is just yet another demonstration of how repressive policies alone have been an uneconomic choice, guaranteeing huge profits to producers, brokers and traffickers. for these reasons i believe that the next special session of the un must also take account of this new question, which has been raised by the independent reports of various organizations. only in this way will it be possible to deal with the harmful effects of the war on drugs, taking account of all aspects and not just the repressive ones.

in writing. ‒ the 1965 hague convention on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil and commercial matters aims to simplify the procedures for the transmission of such documents between the contracting states. this convention facilitates judicial cooperation in the event of transnational civil or commercial litigation. twenty-six of the 28 member states already apply the convention. the only countries missing are austria and malta, which have expressed their wish to join. the european parliament must help to strengthen and improve judicial cooperation in europe and it is therefore its task to ensure the accession of austria and malta to this convention, with the aim of improving mutual judicial assistance to this end by simplifying and speeding up the procedure.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft council decision authorising the republic of austria to sign and ratify and malta to accede, respectively, in the interest of the european union, to the hague convention of 15 november 1965 on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters. the purpose of this convention is to create the means for judicial and extrajudicial documents which are to be served abroad to reach the addressees in good time and thus to improve mutual legal assistance by simplifying and speeding up the procedure. it is therefore in the interest of both the european union and the two states concerned to have a uniform system for the notification of acts in cross-border relations with third countries.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention of 15 november 1965 establishes a system whereby acts may be served in another signatory state. the convention is already applied in 26 of the 28 member states. the two remaining member states, austria and malta, have expressed their wish to join. i therefore voted in favour of the measure.
in writing. ‒ it is common knowledge that the hague convention of 15 november 1965 provides for the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters. at present, 26 of the 28 member states are already parties to it. austria and malta, the last two remaining countries, have expressed their willingness to join. since the convention does not allow for the possibility of accession by international organisations, the eu, which has exclusive external competence in this area, must authorise these states to act on its behalf. i believe it is important that all member states are parties to the convention, and i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention of 15 november 1965 establishes a system whereby acts may be served in another signatory state. the convention applies only to acts intended for or originating in third countries. it is in the interest of both the union as a whole and the member states to have a uniform system for the notification of acts in cross-border relations with third countries. i therefore welcome the fact that austria and malta have expressed their willingness to accede to the hague convention. these are the last two eu member states that had not yet joined. i therefore voted in favour of their accession to the convention.
