in writing. ‒ the serious problem of unemployment in some regions of europe requires a decisive strengthening of the mobility of workers in the union. the amendments to the regulation, which were introduced with the contribution of the five star movement, provide for a number of improvements to the european employment services network (eures) in order to make it easier for users to use it. the member states also undertake to inform citizens about eures and a programme to monitor the performance of the platform is being set up. i have decided to vote in favour of making these substantial improvements to the european network of employment services.
in writing. ‒ following the global economic crisis, which has led to a sharp rise in unemployment rates, there is a growing need for effective measures to promote genuine integration between the labour markets of the eu member states. in this context, the strengthening of the eures network can be a great opportunity for millions of european citizens. i strongly supported the becker report because i believe it is essential to establish a truly accessible european platform that provides complete and adequate information to all those who are looking for a job. the integration of apprenticeships and traineeships, which involve regular employment contracts, can be a further incentive to strengthen internal mobility, including for those who are completing a training course. the development of an effective network requires regular evaluation mechanisms to allow for changes to be made, where necessary, to ensure the success of the european strategy. the report contains these elements and i have therefore decided to support it with my vote.
in writing. ‒ mr becker's report analyses the revision of the rules governing the european network of employment services (eures). i am aware that eures is one of the instruments through which the principle of free movement of workers is applied, that it was created by the schengen agreements, and that the schengen agreements have now lost their raison d'être, since they no longer guarantee freedom and security within the union, but are instead the vehicle of mass immigration and the consequent european social insecurity, so i did not intend to support this report with my vote.
in writing. ‒ since its establishment in 1993, the european network of employment services (eures) has made an important contribution to facilitating employment and mobility within the european economic area. nevertheless, mobility in europe has so far remained relatively low, failing to achieve an effective balance at european level between demand and supply of labour. as the right to work based on free movement is a prerogative of all european citizens and one of the union's founding principles, i welcome this report which aims to make this fundamental instrument more effective. the reinforcement of the eures network, to be achieved in particular through closer cross-border cooperation between the various national employment services and the social partners, will, inter alia, enable: better information for jobseekers and employers; a wider choice of employment opportunities at european level; a better match between job offers and skills through the multilingual common classification system of skills, qualifications and occupations (esco), with the aim of facilitating the meeting of workers and employers from different countries, facilitating access to the opportunities and requirements they seek.
in writing. ‒ in 2015, more than 1.1 million eu citizens living in one eu country crossed the borders to work in a neighbouring country every day. in addition, 7 million european citizens live and work permanently in other eu countries than the one in which they were born. this is a positive development because the free choice of work within the eu is an integral part of freedom of movement, which is one of the four fundamental freedoms of the european union as provided for in the treaty of rome (along with the free movement of goods, services and capital) and therefore a central element of eu citizenship. initiatives to promote the free movement of citizens within the union can be combined with those to tackle the serious problem of unemployment in certain regions of europe: enhancing labour mobility in the union will provide greater opportunities for workers to find the right job offer more quickly and efficiently. this will contribute to the development of a european labour market with a high level of employment.
in writing. - i vote against. it is the revision of the rules governing the european network of employment services (eures), established in implementation of regulation (eu) no 492/2011 on the free movement of workers within the union. the aim of this revision is to give the commission a greater role in order to achieve 'greater integration of labour markets' through increased cross-border labour mobility. in short, eures is part of the instruments for implementing the principle of free movement of labour. this principle - schengen - is one of the two pillars on which the eu is based (the other is the free movement of capital: maastricht). pillars crumbling in plain sight. the final vote must therefore be against.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on a european network of employment services, workers' access to mobility services and the further integration of labour markets. the freedom to seek employment within the eu is one of the fundamental freedoms of the eu and a central element of eu citizenship. the serious problem of unemployment in the regions of southern europe makes it necessary to strengthen labour mobility in the union. this will contribute to the development of a european labour market aimed at achieving the europe 2020 targets of a 75% employment rate for the 20-64 age group. labour mobility within the eu is modest in relation to the size of the labour market and the union's working population: the mobility rate within the eu is only 0.29%. the objective of this regulation is to make the eures network an effective tool for jobseekers or employers interested in labour mobility within the eu by making accessible and transparent a large pool of job vacancies and jobseeker profiles across europe.
in writing. ‒ the level of unemployment in some regions of the union remains extremely worrying. in addition to measures to create new jobs, action is also needed to improve the integration of markets. the mobility of workers, which is still low compared with potential, must therefore be strengthened, and at the same time the immediacy with which employers can meet the supply of labour. to this end, the european employment services network (eures) should become more efficient, thanks to the positive changes this report makes to its rules. the delegation of the five star movement therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the eures network has given many people the opportunity to find employment within the european union and has been a tool that has helped to achieve the free movement of workers, as provided for in article 45 of the treaty. the new needs of the labour market and the growing demand for people looking for work across national borders - the number of portal subscribers is estimated to have increased from 175 000 to 1 200 000 between 2007 and 2013 - demonstrate the explosion in demand, but this has not been followed by an increase in labour mobility. a shortcoming due to the fact that the system needed to be modified because, as it is organized, it was not able to cope with a constantly increasing demand. the extension of the local and transnational partnership network, envisaged in the proposal for a regulation, increases the possibility of meeting the demand for and supply of labour and at the same time increases the mobility of workers. following continued demand, eures will be extended to trainees, a sign that young people see the eu as a single large labour market. i voted in favour of the report because i believe that eures offers real employment opportunities.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure because i believe that the free choice of workplace within the eu is an integral part of the freedom of movement, which is one of the four fundamental freedoms of the european union and therefore a central element of eu citizenship. the aim of the regulation is to make the eures network an effective tool for jobseekers or employers interested in labour mobility within the eu by making accessible and transparent a large pool of job vacancies and jobseeker profiles across europe. the serious problem of unemployment in some regions of europe makes it necessary to strengthen labour mobility in the union, to provide more opportunities for workers and to help employers to meet the labour supply more quickly and efficiently. this will contribute to the development of a european labour market with a high level of employment.
in writing. ‒ i am very pleased that this proposal for a regulation has been adopted, and i am proud to have contributed by voting in favour. in fact, measures such as this one show a europe that is not only obligations and bureaucracy, but also opportunities and work, diversification of life prospects, broadening of one's horizon and increasing the chances of living happily. what's the point of moving from the country to the city if you're going to do a job that doesn't satisfy you humanly? i shall be glad to see, when this regulation is fully implemented, young people making their way on the basis of their passions and not geographical boundaries.
in writing. ‒ labour mobility within the european union is still modest in relation to the size of the labour market and the union's active population. the free choice of workplace in the labour market is an integral part of the freedom of movement, which is one of the main fundamental freedoms of the european union and therefore a central element of european citizenship. the serious problem of unemployment in some regions requires strengthening labour mobility in the union, providing more opportunities for workers and helping employers to meet the labour supply more quickly and efficiently. the purpose of this regulation is to make the eures network an effective tool for jobseekers or employers. the platform will be easily accessible and as user-friendly as possible. for these reasons, i am in favour of this initiative.
in writing. ‒ eures is a network to promote cooperation between the european commission and the public employment services (pes) of the member countries of the european economic area (eea) in order to exchange information on job vacancies and facilitate the mobility of workers within the eu. given the shortcomings identified in the eures network, amendments to the regulation have been made, mainly to improve the incompleteness of information on job vacancies, the shortage of apprenticeships and traineeships, the unequal access to eures services overcome by improving communication between jobseekers and employers, the limited availability to assist jobseekers and employers who have expressed an interest in labour mobility, to facilitate access and dissemination as widely as possible. i am voting in favour of this regulation because its aim is to make eures a more effective, transparent and accessible instrument in a time of serious crisis in the labour market.
in writing. ‒ the increasing interdependence between labour markets requires closer cooperation between employment services in order to ensure greater mobility for workers and to contribute to the social inclusion and integration of people excluded from the labour market across the european union. i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution because it promotes an instrument which i believe is very useful and which is aimed at creating a european network of employment services, workers' access to mobility services and greater integration of labour markets. i voted to promote the movement of workers, to eliminate any discrimination between european citizens and to help workers who have the right to work in another member state to exercise that right effectively and to protect their families.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the above-mentioned proposal for a regulation, which aims to make the eures network an effective tool for jobseekers or employers interested in labour mobility within the eu. through this implementation the meeting between supply and demand will be more accessible and transparent, while keeping labour market policy, including all support measures, within national competence.
in writing. ‒ i am against the proposal because eures is the implementing instrument of schengen, a treaty which should be completely revised.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the agreement reached between the ep and the council on the adoption of a regulation on a european network of employment services, workers' access to mobility services and greater integration of labour markets, because i strongly support the need to revitalize the eures network through a single platform that includes jobseekers and existing job offers in the member states, while improving the matching of supply and demand in the eu labour market. i believe it is very useful for young job seekers and skilled workers in general, who are looking for better job opportunities, that job vacancies in the public services of each member state are available on the new portal, the aim of which is to meet the needs of the market in order to bridge the current gap between the two million job vacancies in the eu and the unemployment rate, which in some member states is reaching high levels, particularly among young people. the extension of the platform's membership to private organisations will further facilitate the meeting of labour supply and demand in a cross-border context.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, one of the essential elements for the development of a more integrated labour market in the union is the free movement of workers. more than 1.1 million european citizens living in one eu country cross national borders to work in a neighbouring country. it is therefore necessary to offer more opportunities to workers and to help employers to meet supply in order to strengthen labour mobility within the community. in this context, the eures network plays a key role as the main communication channel through which the service interacts with all actors, in particular workers and employers. the text voted today aims to improve and make more effective this network by making accessible and transparent a large pool of job vacancies and jobseeker profiles across europe. given the crisis and the unemployment levels in the various member states, today's vote is certainly an example of a do-it-yourself policy which i hope will soon be able to produce tangible results.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on a european network of employment services, workers' access to mobility services and the further integration of labour markets. the free choice of workplace within the european union is a central element of the fundamental freedoms of the european union. the proposal under consideration aims to strengthen the eures (european employment services) network, a network of services designed to facilitate the international mobility of community workers, by making it an effective tool for workers and employers, with a wide range of jobs and jobseeker profiles in europe, accessible and transparent.
in writing. ‒ we welcome the report on european employment services. the agreement reached during the trilogue, together with the european commission and the european council, is ambitious in that it seeks to reform an area of crucial importance for the economic recovery of european countries, namely employment. the new eures format, which has been achieved thanks to the constant efforts of the socialist and democratic group, will allow a better match between demand and supply on the labour market through improvements that will create a completely redesigned platform with new functionalities. in its new structure, eures involves all levels of the social partners involved in the protection of workers' rights. it also provides for the first time the possibility of creating transnational partnerships between the countries of the european union. the agreement will make it easier for young people to undertake traineeships in public and private institutions in other member states, while ensuring that european regulations on rights are respected.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the european network of employment services, workers' access to mobility services and greater integration of labour markets. firstly, i am convinced that greater mobility of workers within the eu will provide them with more employment opportunities and help employers to fill their vacancies more quickly and efficiently. this will contribute to the development of a european labour market characterised by a high level of employment. i also believe that the eures network should be made an effective tool for all eu workers, jobseekers or employers interested in labour mobility within the eu. finally, i would like to emphasize that the advantages of common european standards are obvious: jobseekers and employers will be able to better understand the profile of the other party. a european standard for job descriptions and jobseeker profiles would be a huge step towards a more integrated european labour market.
in writing. ‒ it is clear that one of the four fundamental freedoms is freedom of movement, which includes the freedom to choose one's place of work. the strengthening of eures, which would make it easier for demand and supply to meet, will create the conditions for further development within the eu. in assessing the need to give greater impetus to the labour market, i consider it necessary to strengthen the eures network. i therefore say that i shall vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the high rate of unemployment in europe, particularly among young people, makes it necessary to strengthen labour mobility within the union. we need to provide more opportunities for workers and help employers to meet the labour supply more quickly and efficiently. the objective of this regulation is to make the eures network a more effective tool for jobseekers and employers interested in labour mobility within the eu by making accessible and transparent a large pool of job vacancies and jobseeker profiles across europe. apprenticeships and traineeships should also be included in the european network. i believe that eures is a very important and promising tool which can provide practical help to european citizens looking for a job. i therefore voted in favour of this regulation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the regulation because i agree with its aim of increasing the dynamics of labour mobility by contributing to a better integration of labour markets at european level. turning the existing eures network into an effective tool for jobseekers and employers, and making a large pool of job vacancies accessible and transparent, means helping our young people to build their future.
in writing. ‒ eures is a very useful tool for jobseekers or employers interested in labour mobility within the eu. the european network of employment services makes accessible and transparent a large pool of job vacancies and profiles in demand across europe. statistics show that more than one million eu citizens cross borders to work in a neighbouring country every day, and the number of people living in a member state other than their home country has increased by almost 60% following the 2004 and 2007 enlargements. in this context, i believe that the eures portal is a unique opportunity for those seeking a job within europe. i therefore voted in favour of this report because it aims to make the network more accessible and easier to use, improving transparency, information exchange and functionality. i hope that these measures will help to provide more opportunities for workers and help employers to meet the demand for work more quickly and efficiently.
in writing. ‒ the latest european statistics show very low rates of mobility (0.29%), which is not in favour of the free movement of workers within the european union. this is due to language barriers and difficulties in finding work. i voted in favour of the european network of employment services, because it plays an important role in providing specific information and services, which benefit both employers and frontier workers. europe needs structures that facilitate mobility and create an integrated and balanced labour market, so as to reduce the gap between countries with high unemployment and those with labour shortages. we must not forget the disabled people, who are mentioned in the resolution, who need more support and easier access to services and information when they are looking for work. we at m5s support a labour market that provides more information on working conditions and services at the workplace. we believe that a person seeking employment abroad should have the same level of support as he would have in his home country.
in writing. ‒ free movement of workers is one of the essential elements of the development of a more integrated labour market, allowing greater mobility of workers, increasing diversity and contributing to the social inclusion and integration throughout the european union of people excluded from the labour market. it must be our mission to promote it. member states should be able to exclude certain categories of apprenticeships and traineeships from matching job vacancies and applications in order to ensure the coherence and functioning of their education systems and to take into account the need to tailor their active labour policy measures to the needs of the workers concerned by those measures. improving the quality of traineeships, in particular in relation to the content of learning and training and working conditions, is essential to facilitate the transition from education, unemployment or inactivity to work.
in writing. ‒ the terrorist attacks in tunis and sousse last year have made it difficult for tunisia to consolidate democracy. support for the maghreb country is one of the priorities of the union's foreign policy in the mediterranean area and an objective closely linked to maintaining stability in the middle east region. in an attempt to achieve these objectives, the commission has proposed as an autonomous, unilateral and temporary trade measure a tariff quota of 35 000 tonnes per year, totalling 70 000 tonnes, for tunisian olive oil exports to the union, without increasing the overall volume of imports. although i consider the commission's aim to be noble and to be shared, i voted against the de sarnez report because, as some of the key amendments proposed have been rejected, i believe that this measure could have a negative impact on the european and italian olive sector, without, however, having a positive effect on the tunisian economy. the tunisian producers themselves, moreover, expressed their strong concerns about the measures through the tunisian forum for economic and social rights (ftdes) and the tunisian general labour union (ugtt). i believe that the eu must find more effective and far-reaching options to support the tunisian economy and democratic institutions.
in writing. ‒ the willingness of the european union to help a friendly country such as tunisia, which is unfortunately facing an economic and political crisis and the threat of international terrorism with an islamic origin, which is destabilising large parts of africa and the middle east, is certainly commendable. however, the way to help the tunisian republic is wrong: a genuine aid cannot be reduced to a trade facilitation measure. to really help, we must create the conditions for a free trade area with common rules and parameters, with a view to structural cooperation based on shared principles of protection of civil and citizens' rights, consumers and producers. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's olive oil market is not affected by the crisis.
in writing. ‒ this measure is the result of a personal intervention by high commissioner mogherini to help tunisia, which is suffering from the crisis in the tourism sector following the recent attacks. the commission is also proposing to extend the tariff quota for olive oil to include olive oil from tunisia. it is clear that the price of this 'aid' would be paid only by certain member states such as italy, while for most it would be a zero-impact measure. moreover, this intervention would only favour the multinationals of the fake 'made in italy' who place on the union market huge quantities of olive oil that looks italian but is only partly italian when it is good. it should be added that: eu olive oil labelling rules do not allow consumers to recognise the origin of the oil they buy; there is very little certainty about the standards of plant health controls in tunisia; the commission has also proposed that the italian authorities should be given the possibility of granting a discount to the producers of 100% italian olive oil in comparison with their competitors, since the measure would in fact reduce the cost of raw materials to a discount for multinational companies which already have much lower production costs. i am against the granting of the measures!
in writing. ‒ today i voted against the proposal to introduce emergency autonomous trade measures for the benefit of the tunisian republic and in favour of rejecting the proposal. i believe that the european union is obliged to assist the tunisian economy. however, this aid cannot be at the expense of olive oil producers. at present, the european commission's proposal could have a negative impact on the olive sector in the southern european countries and in particular in italy. i therefore voted in favour of four corrective amendments which i tabled with my colleagues in the agri committee of the european parliament. unfortunately, only two of the four corrective amendments were adopted and i therefore voted against the whole proposal, as announced in my speech in plenary on this point. the ball now goes to the council, where i hope the governments of the member states, particularly those of southern europe, will succeed in promoting the interests of the oil companies.
in writing. i am in favour of free trade because of the usual arguments that we all know about efficiency, the incentive to improve, and so on. i think, however, that an important aspect of the economic models used to prove the free trade theses is often underestimated: there are some assumptions that are not valid when we talk about agricultural goods. my vote to close down tunisian oil is not a protectionist vote, although that is the effect, but a vote to defend consumers who would find on supermarket shelves two products that are apparently identical, but with a huge price difference, without the tools to go and check whether the quality is the same. i have always fought for the quality of agri-food products, and this case is no exception.
in writing. ‒ i thought it appropriate to vote against the proposal for a regulation because, although its aims are right, the instruments used to achieve the objectives are not at all correct, especially when we are talking about the import of over 70 000 tonnes of tunisian oil free of duty. we cannot mortify agriculture and specifically oil production in southern europe, as in the case of italy, which boasts a heritage of 250 million olive trees and is the only country with 533 varieties of olives and 43 oils protected by the european union, but above all a country where oil is one of the products that symbolise made in italy and the mediterranean diet. it is also unfair to all those apulian olive growers who have been fighting xylella for months.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution because the fact that some of the amendments tabled in plenary were not adopted prevented some of the doubts and uncertainties raised by the measure from being dispelled. i have chosen not to vote against the request for the proposal to be rejected because i believe that as the eu we cannot be insensitive or uncommitted to what is happening on the other side of our sea, unless we bear the consequences of it. solidarity and aid cannot be "in words". on the other hand, i have found and find the measure hasty and poorly analytical in predicting the consequences on our productive tissues. that is why i have signed and supported a series of amendments which, without calling into question cooperation and solidarity with our neighbours, introduce important safeguard clauses, taking into account the needs of all, including european producers. unfortunately, only some of these amendments were accepted and this, in my view, has produced a still weak and deficient report which i did not feel i should support. i hope that in the further discussions with the council and the commission the spirit and the letter of the amendments can be recovered so that we have a proposal which is truly in solidarity with all the parties concerned.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the introduction of emergency autonomous trade measures for the republic of tunisia will allow the entry of 70,000 tonnes of zero-duty tunisian oil into the european union over the next two years. the aim of the proposal would be to revive a key sector of the tunisian economy after the tragic terrorist attacks that have brought the other key sector, tourism, into crisis. although the intention is therefore to be shared, the measures as proposed by the european commission do not effectively meet the need to support tunisia's economic recovery in a structural way. i am convinced that a strategy which integrates european cooperation and development policies with trade measures would instead make it possible to consolidate the tunisian olive production system and make it competitive in the long term, supporting more generally the economic and political stability of the country. on the contrary, they will bring limited benefits to tunisia, for a transitional period only. it has also been decided to introduce measures which will damage our products and increase the risk of fraud in the sector, to the detriment of quality and credibility with european consumers. i therefore voted against the proposal.
in writing. ‒ we, like m5s, are opposed to what is an ineffective form of eu solidarity at the expense of farmers in southern europe, in the specific case of olive oil producers. the south of italy, which has been hit hardest by the crisis and where the olive oil sector provides thousands of jobs, will be forced to suffer the most negative consequences of the measures to support tunisia envisaged by the european commission. we believe that there are other ways of helping, such as launching a plan for the establishment of a development fund in all sectors of the tunisian economy. germany and the nordic countries must share in the aid. the oil price is paid by the south of europe, and italy in particular.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report which increases the quantity of tunisian oil duty-free in europe. another mistake of this europe which has lost touch with reality. we must support the political and economic stabilisation of tunisia, but the european commission has completely misused its methods. i believe that a temporary measure in a specific area cannot consolidate the democratization of tunisia. this has been at the expense of an industry which is already in difficulty, owing both to structural factors such as the steady fall in selling prices and the increase in production costs and to extraordinary events, not least the spread of the bacterium 'xylella fastidiosa' in some member states. the entry of additional duty-free olive oil flows into the market would exacerbate these problems.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament voted today in favour of an unacceptable measure which, by allowing the import of 70 000 tonnes of tunisian olive oil for two years on a tax-free basis, is further damaging the situation of small oil producers in several european countries, particularly in italy. we have opposed these measures with other members of the forza italia delegation by submitting an amendment rejecting the commission proposal in order to state clearly our 'no'. although the solidarity motives behind this decision are fully understandable, we cannot accept that our aid depends solely on the sacrifice of italian and european oil producers.
in writing. ‒ supporting a nation that is painstakingly gaining the path to democracy and peace is the task of forward-looking politics. but helping a country does not mean worsening the living and working conditions of those who face the fragility of a sector which can and must be one of the jewels of italy's agricultural economy. it was a very difficult and intense discussion, but the game was finally reopened. the fact that two amendments have been approved allows the european institutions to reconcile their international policies in favour of the mediterranean countries with the support and promotion of olive growing in southern italy and puglia. the final vote has been postponed. it is now up to the italian government to adopt a balanced position in support of the italian farming enterprise system, taking account also of the employment risk in the agricultural sector. i hope that in the coming days we will not continue to "unload the barrel" on those who have made every useful effort to correct the course.
in writing. the commission's proposal to open an extra quota of 35 thousand tonnes of tunisian olive oil duty free for the years 2016 and 2017 is a serious damage to us and, at the same time, will not bring any benefit to the tunisian people. the opening up of the market is not going in the right direction, because i think it is unthinkable to give tunisia practical aid by lowering import duties. fortunately, with our work, we were able to amend part of the proposal in order to limit some negative effects, by eliminating the possibility of extending these extraordinary measures, which will therefore end in 2017, and by requiring that the oil be entirely obtained in tunisia and transported directly to the eu. the adoption of these amendments, which have already been supported by the committee on agriculture, is essential because it blocks the initial proposal and brings the discussion back to the council, so that negotiations with the member states can begin. i voted against it, however, because the aim of solidarity is certainly to be shared, but the instrument chosen is wrong. we cannot continue to trade, as has been done up to now, the agriculture of southern europe for the help of the people of north africa.
in writing. ‒ i do not support the report on the introduction of emergency autonomous trade measures for tunisia. it is important, however, to protect domestic products and to support those facing crises, such as the current crisis affecting the oil production sector. in this case, the vote is due to a need for protection.
in writing. ‒ tunisia is currently in a very difficult time, as its economy was hit hard by the 2015 sousse terrorist attack. the commission has therefore considered whether it would be appropriate to help the aforementioned state by giving it the opportunity to trade oil on favourable economic terms. i repeat my absolute disapproval of these decisions which risk undermining the economies of the mediterranean countries. while i believe that it is our duty to help countries in difficulty, such as tunisia, i do not think it would be appropriate to adopt decisions which would have a very serious economic impact on the agricultural sectors of the countries of southern europe. another way could and should have been found to help tunisia humanitarian and economically, without undermining the economies of some european countries and their citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted against these trade measures in favour of tunisia because i believe they are harmful to the internal markets of europe, especially those of the mediterranean. i do not dispute the idea itself, namely to help tunisia, which is too important for us, even in terms of migration flows, but i do criticise the means chosen by the european commission to help them. the unilateral tariff concessions on 35,000 tonnes of oil over two years mean undermining our market, especially the italian market, and destroying all the smes that produce quality oil.
in writing. ‒ following the terrorist attacks in sousse, tunisia, on 26 june 2015, the european union decided to introduce certain emergency autonomous trade measures in favour of the republic of tunisia. these measures allow the duty-free import of 35 000 tonnes of olive oil for two years, in addition to the 56 700 tonnes already covered by the eu-tunisia association agreement. the commission notes that the agreement between the parties to the agreement, which allows additional temporary access for tunisian olive oil to the european market, risks inevitably undermining the italian olive sector, which has only recently been showing a good level of growth after a severe crisis in 2014. the tunisian olive oil will certainly be marketed at prices lower than those of domestic production, affecting consumption and sales of quality italian olive oil. the oil industry is certainly one of the great assets of the italian agricultural sector, and i believe that it should be defended and protected. i have therefore decided to vote against the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the european commission's proposal to allow the duty-free entry into the eu of 35 000 tonnes of tunisian oil per year for two years. i share the need to help tunisia: however, this is not the right way to go, as the commission's analysis shows that tunisian oil is likely to replace the current inward processing trade: it means that it will remain in the eu and will bring down the price of oil, harming producers in italy and other mediterranean countries, among others already harmed by the eu's austerity policies. i voted in favour of the amendments, which at least impose restrictive conditions: the first prevents the duty-free entry of tunisian oil into the eu from being extended, the second allows tunisian oil to enter the eu only if it comes exclusively from tunisian olives. the eu council will thus be able to discuss the import of tunisian oil again.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) is useful for providing support to redundant workers and self-employed persons whose activity has ceased as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation, or as a result of the continuation of the global financial and economic crisis, or as a result of new economic and financial crises of a supra-regional nature. the fund should be used to assist them in re-entering the labour market by updating their training and providing them with economic support at the same time. the egf should, therefore, be mobilised in order to provide financial assistance to workers in undertakings which have suffered serious physical or mental disorders as a result of these events.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (the egf, set up to provide additional support for workers who suffer from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade) which refers to the application submitted by belgium following the redundancies of 412 workers in the manufacture of other non-metallic mineral processing products. the belgian authorities state that the excesses are due to developments in the glass sector in europe, and in particular in belgium, in recent years, which have had a significant impact on glass production in wallonia. the long tradition of glassmaking in wallonia is confronted with the overcapacity of asia and the higher production costs and stricter environmental standards in europe. the surpluses therefore appear to be linked to changes in the structure of world trade. i therefore voted in favour of this measure.

in writing. the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up to provide support for workers affected by the crisis and the effects of major structural changes in world trade. the reason for the excesses we are discussing is the events which have affected the glass industry in europe, and particularly in belgium, in recent years. in addition to the effects of globalisation, the belgian authorities note that asia's overcapacity in this sector certainly plays a leading role. the application concerned 412 redundant workers and up to 100 young unemployed. i therefore thought i should vote in favour and support those workers in difficulty.
in writing. ‒ the report on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund: the commission considers that the application does not meet the requirements of the specifications of the egf regulation. there is a need for union financial support for redundant workers, which must be made available in an effective and needs-based manner. belgium, having applied for and complying with the requirements, will indeed have a sum to deal with the situation. finally, it should be stressed that there is a provision for neets, i.e. those who are not in training, working or actively seeking work, which contributes to lower productivity in the european union and is a reason for slowing down.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. i voted in favour of the mobilisation of the egf for an amount of about eur 1 million for belgium, involving 412 redundant workers and up to 100 young unemployed people.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in world trade. in view of the serious impact of the economic crisis on employment, belgium submitted an application egf/2015/007 be/hainaut-namur glass for a financial contribution from the egf to support the sector which has been in a deep crisis. i think that the support for the proposal put forward by belgium should be welcomed.
in writing. ‒ i support the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund in respect of the application egf/2015/007 be/hainaut-namur glass submitted by belgium. this application was made following the redundancy of 412 workers. the glass industry has suffered serious difficulties in recent years, due in particular to imports, which have increased dramatically, and foreign producers, who have gained an increasing share of the european market. some companies have been forced to close their production plants and restructure their workforce, resulting in a high number of redundancies. i hope that the mobilisation of the egf, amounting to eur 1 095 544, will prove to be a decisive instrument for supporting these workers and their families, as well as a valuable aid for the companies affected by the crisis.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) is the instrument promoted by the european union to provide support in the face of the challenges posed by the globalisation of markets. this application, the first under the 2016 budget, concerns the mobilisation of the egf in the amount of eur 1 095 544 for belgium. it covers 412 redundant workers and up to 100 young people who are unemployed and not enrolled in education or training (neets) in order to promote their employment. the two plants involved, belonging to the agc europe sa and saint-gobain glass benelux groups, were forced to close, in particular because of the strong competition from asian countries, which can produce without having to comply with the environmental and social constraints to which our companies are subject.
in writing. ‒ we have today approved the request to mobilise the egf from belgium, which applied for around eur 1 million to support 412 redundant workers affected by the crisis in the glass industry. in addition, the belgian authorities will offer personalised services co-financed by the egf to up to 100 young people in the hainaut region who are not in employment and not in any education or training. the event that triggered the redundancies was the closure in 2014 of two production plants in wallonia belonging to two companies, agc europe sa and saint-gobain glass benelux. it should be noted that between 2000 and 2010, with reference to the glass sector as a whole, employment decreased by 32% in europe (in particular in germany, poland, france and belgium) and for the first time since the mid-1960s glass production in belgium fell below 1 million tonnes in 2009, continuing to decrease by 5% in both 2011 and 2012. it should also be added that this is the fifth case of application for egf assistance in this sector, whose crisis is mainly due to very strong competition from the far east.

in writing. ‒ the resolution expresses the european parliament's recommendations on the negotiation of the eu-tunisia free trade agreement, whose negotiations were launched in october 2015. the agreement is aimed at liberalizing goods and services between tunisia and the eu and at preparing joint measures on the mobility of workers and the protection of intellectual property. the text of the resolution recommends that the commission should proceed to a gradual and asymmetrical agreement, with a progressive opening up to tunisian economic sectors. the resolution also calls for the liberalization of certain goods, such as olive oil, which are considered sensitive to our companies, to be excluded from the negotiations. the text also has some weaknesses. however, since many of the compromise amendments proposed by the five star movement have been accepted, i have decided to vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ on 19 october 2015, negotiations were launched for free trade agreements between the european union and tunisia, an agreement that goes beyond tariff reductions in the agricultural and manufacturing sectors and covers services, labour mobility, small and medium-sized enterprises and the protection of intellectual property. the resolution highlights a number of points to be taken into account: the agreement must be gradual and asymmetrical; the opening up of tunisian economic sectors must be gradual and progressive and must include transitional periods for sensitive sectors, excluding from the negotiations certain products which the parties consider sensitive (we have of course asked for the olive oil sector to be excluded). substantial financial, technical and trade negotiating assistance is needed to implement the various provisions of the free trade agreement correctly, and it is required that such assistance be provided in a transparent manner and that it brings real benefits to the recipients. the text is not negative, but since, unfortunately, some of our amendments, which are of fundamental importance, have not been included in the text, such as the one concerning the exclusion of the olive oil sector, i cannot support it. for these reasons i have decided to abstain.

in writing. ‒ the european ombudsman is a person established under article 228 tfeu whose task is to receive complaints concerning maladministration in the activities of the institutions of the european union. on 16 december 2014, at the plenary session in strasbourg, the european parliament re-elected emily o'reilly as the european ombudsman. the cabezón ruiz report, which i supported with my vote, presented a positive picture of the activities carried out by this institutional figure in 2014. of the more than 2 000 complaints received, the ombudsman provided advice in more than a thousand cases and opened a related inquiry in another 325 cases. the strategic surveys, which were carried out on their own initiative and made possible by the appointment of a coordinator, were also important. in general, the ombudsman's work has been positive in that it has paid particular attention to respecting the right of citizens to participate in the eu decision-making process and, in particular, to the functioning of the european citizens' initiative (eci). i therefore welcome the work done by mr o'reilly and have decided to support the report before parliament.

in writing. ‒ the european ombudsman plays a key role in the european union, helping the eu institutions to become more transparent, effective and closer to the citizens, thus strengthening their trust in the union. it is a guarantor figure for the protection of the european citizen and is responsible for ensuring that citizens' rights are fully respected and that the right to good administration reflects the highest standards expected of the union's institutions, bodies, offices or agencies. 2014 was a highly productive year for the institution of the european ombudsman, as it began to implement the new 'towards 2019' strategy, which places particular emphasis on strategic issues of public administration in the european union affecting millions of europeans. the european parliament must continue to support the current european ombudsman, emily o'reilly, as she did a great job in 2014 in her task of assisting the institutions of the european union in providing the best possible service to european citizens and residents, using transparency as a guarantee of better administration.
in writing. - i vote for it. the european ombudsman, although without any real powers of influence, represents a form of control given to european citizens. in the year under review, the ombudsman opened 325 complaint-based inquiries and 17 own-initiative inquiries. the main sources of complaints were individual citizens (335) and businesses, associations and other legal entities (52). these checks have mainly concerned the european commission. where possible, the ombudsman seeks to achieve a positive outcome by working towards a friendly settlement satisfactory to both the complainant and the institution concerned. in 2014, amicable settlements were found in 133 cases and in 163 cases the ombudsman considered that no further investigation was warranted. finally, it is worth mentioning that the european ombudsman works closely with his counterparts in the member states, such as the european network of ombudsmen, which includes national and regional ombudsmen, commissions for petitions and corresponding bodies in the member states of the european union.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the annual report on the activities of the european ombudsman in 2014. as regards the topics of complaints in the ombudsman's annual report, the theme of public access to documents of the eu institutions is clearly predominant and has triggered a large number of complaints. of all investigations closed in 2014, 20-30% of complaints concerned transparency and in particular the refusal of institutions to allow access to documents and/or information. this shows that the eu institutions need to work more transparently in order to promote good governance and ensure the participation of civil society. i believe that the opening up of documents and access to them, particularly by the commission, in accordance with article 15 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union and article 42 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, is an essential part of the system of institutional checks and balances. in particular, there is a need for greater openness in the ongoing negotiations on the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip). the report highlights these elements and i therefore voted in favour of it.

in writing. the european ombudsman was established by the maastricht treaty as a body responsible for eu citizenship. its task is to combat maladministration in the institutions and bodies of the european union. at the same time, it has a duty to strengthen the instruments for protecting the rights of the citizens of the union and to improve the efficiency of the community administration. with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the ombudsman's mandate was extended to include the common foreign and security policy. more generally, the ombudsman seeks to improve the quality of administration by receiving complaints. to this end, a study of its activities is published annually to inform the public about what is being done. i consider that the report fully illustrates the role of the european ombudsman and the work undertaken in 2014, and i have therefore decided to give a favourable opinion.

in writing. ‒ the european central bank under mario draghi launched in 2014 a series of long-term refinancing operations and several programmes to purchase selected financial assets in the private sector in order to support lending to the real economy. in 2015, it then promoted a €1100 billion asset purchase programme. these and other operations, which involved measures of an unconventional nature, have provided a positive, albeit not conclusive, response to the union's economic problems. i have decided to support the marias report with conviction because i believe that the ecb's contribution is essential to increase low-interest loans for smes and, above all, to promote an effective economic recovery in terms of employment, growth and stability. the defence of the single currency, the supervisory role of the banking system and the commitment to price stability are essential contributions to ensuring that the european project moves forward towards greater integration.

in writing. ‒ the role that the ecb has played and continues to play in providing support to the real economy through targeted longer-term refinancing operations and private sector asset purchase programmes, together with its attempt to bring inflation closer to the 2% threshold and thus into a more balanced position, is important in enabling the full economic recovery of the euro area. nevertheless, growth and investment in the euro area have so far been sluggish, and this is clearly because, as we have long argued, monetary policy cannot be the only solution to the economic problems facing europe, but more coordinated and courageous policy action is needed, based on the implementation of structural reforms and the revival of investment, both public and private. the contribution of the ecb is therefore certainly to be acknowledged, but we must remember that monetary policy is a limited instrument and that a comprehensive policy mix is needed, including the completion of banking union and fiscal policy.
in writing. ‒ the ecb under mario draghi has been brave and taken considerable risks in doing everything in its power to save the euro: lowered its main refinancing rates to the effective lower bound and reduced the deposit facility rate to -0.20% and, at the same time, pursued a consistent diplomatic action aimed at reassuring stakeholders and easing market tensions, thus contributing to the stability of the euro area and preventing the emergence of new financial crises. however, we must reiterate that the economic policy of the eurozone cannot be taken by a technical body, however qualified it may be, but must depend on the political will of the european citizens: the european union's action in the economic and financial sector will not be appropriate to the particular historical moment we are living in until we complete the third pillar of the banking union, the single deposit guarantee scheme, and we change the union's economic policy by moving beyond the logic of austerity alone as a way out of the crisis and implementing a genuine policy of supranational public investment.

in writing. - i vote against it. the text calls for the negotiation of a free trade agreement between the eu and australia and new zealand to be launched as soon as possible. our opposition does not mean that we do not regard these two states as reliable trading partners. the quality standards of the regulations are very high on both fronts. what the northern league delegation disputes is that an agricultural reality such as australia could, in the event of a free trade agreement, represent a real danger for our operators in the sector. the lega nord has tabled two important amendments: - one to ask for a careful assessment of the australian and new zealand regulations on intellectual property and quality of production processes; - one to ask that the dairy sector and the meat sector (beef and pig) be excluded from any negotiations. it should be remembered, however, that in countries such as australia and new zealand - as well as in the usa - there is a legal system based on trademarks which sees the latter as having priority over our geographical indications. moreover, in reality, like the anglo-saxon law, geographical indications are considered to be genuine non-tariff barriers to free trade.
in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the motion for a resolution tabled following question for oral answer b8-0101/2016 on the opening of fta negotiations with australia and new zealand. i am particularly pleased that the report states that agriculture is a very sensitive sector and that a balanced final outcome in the agriculture and fisheries chapters must take due account of the interests of all european producers, for example those in the canning sector, meat, dairy, sugar, cereals and textiles. it is also worth noting the call for the inclusion of effective bilateral safeguard measures to avoid a surge in imports which could cause serious damage to european producers in sensitive sectors. in this respect, it is recalled, for example, that australia has imposed customs duties on processed products based on italian tomatoes since 2014. these, together with other key points, such as the request that the opening of negotiations be made conditional on the commitment of all parties to conduct negotiations in the most transparent manner possible, are the reasons why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the resolution stresses the importance for economic growth of deepening the union's trade relations with the asia-pacific region, especially australia and new zealand. they are a key component of the strategy in that they are also markets which can mitigate the potential diversionary effects of the recently concluded tpp with the united states. the text also mentions the need for closer convergence and cooperation on international standards without lowering the level of consumer (e.g. food safety), environmental (e.g. animal health and welfare, plant health) or social and labour protection. the central importance of the agricultural sector and the delicate approach it requires are also underlined. i voted in favour without hesitation.

in writing. ‒ both australia and new zealand have oriented their trade policies towards the eu. today's global economy is highly integrated and global supply chains have largely replaced traditional trade. the eu's trade strategy aims to strengthen the union's policy and to contribute to the promotion of growth, employment and investment. trade relations with australia and new zealand can therefore help to promote common values and interests by addressing investment, trade in goods and services, public procurement, energy, competition, anti-corruption and the needs of smes, without compromising consumer and environmental protection. the agricultural sector must certainly be of strategic importance in relations between countries. i shall vote in favour of this resolution.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution tabled following the question with oral answer under rule 128 on the opening of negotiations on free trade agreements (ftas) with australia and new zealand. i believe that the opening of fta negotiations can give the european union the opportunity to strengthen and deepen relations with these two distant countries in oceania, the only ones at present among the member states of the world trade organisation without privileged trade channels with the eu. with a view to fair, profitable and comprehensive agreements and closer cooperation between the two countries, i believe it is ambitious to follow up the existing investment partnerships with free trade agreements in order to create more trade opportunities, especially for smes. finally, i stress the need to take due account of the interests of all economic operators, especially those in the agricultural and fisheries sectors, when negotiating the agreement, and i call on the commission to carry out as soon as possible an impact assessment of these agreements in the eu territories.
in writing. australia and new zealand are among the eu's oldest partners. both are involved in the recently concluded negotiations for a trans-pacific partnership (tpp) and the ongoing negotiations for a regional comprehensive economic partnership (rcep) in east asia, which includes the major trading partners of australia and new zealand. it is also safe to say that both countries ensure a high level of environmental protection and protection of human, social and employment rights. it is vital for the european union to strengthen its relations with the asia-pacific region and both countries are key to achieving this objective. the negotiation of two separate modern and ambitious free trade agreements certainly has important aspects to address, such as investment, trade in goods and services, energy, state-owned enterprises, competition and, above all, the needs and interests of smes. i believe that these negotiations will be beneficial to all parties concerned and i have therefore decided to give my favourable opinion to this resolution.
in writing. ‒ we welcome the opening of negotiations with australia and new zealand for the definition of a trade agreement aimed at creating a free trade area. the two countries are historic allies of the european union and share the same approach to major global issues. the aim, in line with european trade policy, is to foster economic growth while helping to define the rules of the globalization playing field. the close proximity of values, for example in the exchange of data, the complementarity, particularly strong in the agricultural sector because of the different succession of seasons, and the low volume of trade also ensure a low level of risk for the european manufacturing sector. we are in favour of safeguard clauses, particularly for agri-food imports, in order to ensure maximum protection against any distortions on the european market. we also call on the european commission to negotiate the recognition and greater protection of geographical indications, which are of great interest to the european union. in line with the orientation of european trade policy, we stress the need for the final text of the agreement to include a specific chapter on the needs and facilitation of the internationalisation of small and mediumsized enterprises.

in writing. ‒ animal mobility is closely linked to human mobility. in addition to the normal transport of pets in the schengen area, numerous non-governmental organisations have highlighted the illegal trafficking of pets. in order to harmonize european legislation on the transport of pet animals and to protect the health of citizens and animals, i have decided to vote in favour of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the resolution on the introduction of compatible systems for the registration of pet animals in the member states. several european countries currently have mechanisms for the registration and identification of pet animals, but most of these databases are not yet compatible. this blocking of the flow of information creates a problem of limited traceability, especially in the case of movements within the union. the lack of access to correct information on animals is a major obstacle to the fight against illegal trade. the latter, in addition to being a major source of transport violations, controls being evaded and documents being falsified, represent a real threat to the health and welfare of animals and humans. introducing compatible systems for animal registration therefore means recognising the important role that pets play in the lives of millions of european people and families, while ensuring safe and controlled journeys for them within the eu.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the text of the resolution effectively addresses current animal welfare issues such as the illegal trade in wild animals sold as pets. i think it is important to develop a definite system of identification and registration of pet animals at european level, to fill the current gaps in the legislation on the subject, and for these reasons i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ pet animals in the illegal trade are often poorly bred, poorly socialized and more at risk of disease. illegal trade fuels the escape of exotic or wild animals into an environment devoid of their natural enemies, which can lead to their uncontrolled spread, with deleterious consequences for the environment, public health and the economy. in addition, the illegal trade in wildlife is one of the most widespread activities of transnational organised crime worldwide and is a cause of habitat depletion and species conservation threats. it is therefore important that the european union should draw up a common regulation and start a process of establishing a european pet database with tools for identifying and tracking animals in their cross-border movements, in order to limit illegal trade and protect the health of european citizens and their pets.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in recent years we have had to deal with a number of health emergencies caused by diseases which have been transmitted from animals to humans and which have also caused deaths. swine fever and avian influenza are the worst cases, the ones that are exaggerated in the media, but there are several diseases, threats of communicable diseases, that this animal health regulation is intended to combat. i would like to thank the colleagues who worked with me on this proposal, the rapporteur and mr paulsen, who has concluded his term of office with this regulation, achieving great success and winning wide support among all the groups. there are two aspects i would like to stress today: the first is that we have finally put it in writing, that the health of animals depends on their welfare, that is, on their living conditions. an animal that is abused can never be a healthy animal. article 13 of the treaty recognises that animals are sentient beings and we call on all those who deal with animals, from farmers to owners, to avoid their suffering and pain by applying the principle of good breeding to animals and humane treatment to animals. then there is the prevention aspect: the transmission of diseases should be prevented rather than prevented through better animal husbandry and responsible use of veterinary medicines; the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat this disease. the importance of this regulation lies in its setting up of a single regulatory framework, compared to the 40 different previous legislative acts, some of which were from the 1960s. clear rules on animal welfare and health are still needed in a europe where cases of unjustified violence and outright torture of animals are still too often tolerated or even ignored.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the inadequate use of therapeutic antimicrobials in veterinary medicine, their use for non-therapeutic purposes and environmental pollution have accelerated the emergence and spread of resistant microorganisms, with serious consequences for animal and human health. the actions taken have not succeeded in containing the growing risk of antimicrobial resistance. it is necessary to strengthen the measures currently in force and to adopt a new set of more stringent measures, in particular on the prevention of antimicrobial infections, in order to reduce the pressure on the use of antimicrobials and to prevent their further spread. member states should endeavour to collect relevant, comparable and sufficiently detailed data on the actual use of antimicrobial medicinal products in animals and to transmit them to the commission, in order to allow policies to encourage more prudent use in animals and thus to reduce the risk of antimicrobial resistance. it would be desirable for the commission to undertake to publish a report on the use of antimicrobial medicinal products in the treatment of animals in the european union on the basis of data obtained from individual member states.

and allows us to draw conclusions from it. we have adopted in 2015 a new regulation concerning reporting on irregularities and on that basis we have launched with the participation of national experts the preparation of new guidelines on reporting. on that basis, data would now feed a new improved version of the irregularities reporting systems and i am very pleased to inform you that we expect this new improved system to be operational in the second quarter of 2016. secondly, national anti-fraud strategies. as the rapporteur pointed out, we have obligations together with member states. member states are becoming increasingly more effective in fighting fraud and this is visible by the increase of detection and also prosecution of fraud cases: 1 649 cases overall. this is more than in 2013, but the recovery rate has to be beefed up, it has to be improved, and we believe that a lot more can be done in prevention, detection, reporting, prosecution and sanctioning if we are to have member states embracing what parliament is supporting very much, namely national anti-fraud strategies. so far this is not mandatory, it is voluntary. five member states have adopted such strategies. we encourage others to do it and we work already with those who have done it so we can actually improve the actions on the basis of exchange of best practices and experience. third, the rapporteur mentioned public procurement following the special report of the court of auditors on this issue, on public procurement. the commission is looking at how to improve the functionalities of the irregularities management system which i mentioned, and the possibility to have interoperability between different databases so we can make best possible use of information and, of course, enhance transparency. we know that transparency is the taxpayers’ best friend, so the more we can do in this area, the better for the protection of the financial interests. there is a proposal to publish beneficiaries, and i want to clarify that the current legislation already foresees this and lists the type of information that needs to be published. fourth, corruption indicators. concerning 2016. fifth, the follow-up of olaf recommendations at national level and the establishment of a european prosecutor’s office. we agree that comprehensive prosecution of crimes against the eu’s financial interests is essential and that more has to be done in member states to follow up on olaf’s recommendations and also to provide feedback to olaf on actions taken. we think that the establishment of the european prosecutor’s office will help us in this regard and we also believe that the evaluation of regulation 883/2013 governing olaf’s investigations, to be completed by 2017, will provide an opportunity also in this regard. like the rapporteur, we believe that vat fraud should be part of the work of the european public prosecutor’s office, it should be covered by the pif regulation. we also believe that it is essential that the mandate of the eppo is clear about that and that discussions between the co-legislators should be brought to a successful conclusion as soon vice-president of the commission. – madam president, thank you for the questions we will debate today. they show that it is time to put the right conditions in place for europe to leverage the growth potential of the data-driven economy. the eu data economy is growing fast and is expected to reach at least 3% of gdp by 2020. it must become the building block for our entire economy, creating new jobs, services and business models. in the recent public consultation on platforms, the commission aimed to improve understanding of the role of data markets, access to data and the free flow of data in the european union. the commission will map existing restrictions on the free flow of data and assess emerging issues related to businesses’ access to data, the use and reuse of data, and the ownership of non-personal data. data is the new oil. standards and interoperability are its new pipelines. the commission is working on a set of priorities for standards and standardisation actions in key technology areas for the digital single market, which can guide the standardisation of organisations in their work. regarding cloud, the commission will promote the rapid adoption of cloud computing in all sectors where we are convinced that cloud can boost productivity. in order to digitise public administrations, the digital single market envisages a new e-government action plan. under the action plan, i aim at accelerating the implementation of open, innovative and collaborative government. they will support interoperability and cross-border digital public services. an effective regulatory framework on personal data protection, complemented by revised e-privacy rules plus cyber security and consumer protection, will help to build trust in the data economy. by enhancing legal certainty and providing more uniform rules, it will also help to guarantee equal conditions for businesses to compete across the european union. the specific situation of smes has been taken into account in the proposals for the general data protection regulation. the commission has been careful not to impose undue administrative burdens on them. smes will benefit from the simplified regulatory environment that the regulation provides and the one-stop shop mechanism of the national supervisory authorities. but this is not only about data. the right skills are needed to process data properly and to create new businesses. the commission has included a new skills agenda for europe in its 2016 work programme to promote skills development and maximise the potential of digital jobs. one question raised the issue of data brokerage. the commission is following closely the emergence of data markets and brokerage in europe. to assess the need for policy action, we first need a better understanding of the mechanisms for finding the right price and composition of data to be traded, as well as their effects on the data economy. particular attention will be given to transparency, accountability and non-discrimination.
the objective of restoring growth to the european economy, making it more flourishing, more competitive, can find in the data-driven economy a great opportunity. but we know very well that this will not happen automatically and spontaneously. it must be the result of a european strategy. it will not happen by miracle if things are left to their own devices. we have a lot of catching up to do, because we know that the united states is way ahead, we know that europe is not big in this big data economy. maybe it can be, but it's a long way off. we must do a great deal in terms of investment, as has been said, in terms of interoperability, so that machines and sensors and all technical accessories can communicate with each other, involvement of smes, of society for its uses, preparation of the skills, very integrated, diversified skills that are needed, all things to be done. but to do this, you also need foresight. president buzek said that europe must look ahead, be innovative but defend its values, assert them. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of the information it receives, and i am sure that the commission will be able to take action to ensure that this information is not only used for the purposes for which it is intended, but also for the purposes for which it is intended. there are important legal and, i would even say, ethical aspects, which are also linked to the development of democracy. we have heard very worrying things about the possible combination of data and their use if there are no clear rules that do not want to limit progress and innovation, but want to safeguard, in progress and innovation, the values of europe.
