in writing. ‒ ensuring a high level of human, animal and plant health is one of the objectives of the european union's treaties. the recent amendments to the legislation are intended to improve existing legislation by introducing a common system to improve disease prevention and to encourage the protection of animal health. in view of the remarks made by the council and the commission, i voted against the rejection amendment, thus allowing a large part of the text to be retained at first reading. the european parliament's opinion at first reading is a fair compromise, given the emphasis on the link between animal health and welfare and the prohibition of causing pain, distress or suffering to animals during health checks.
in writing. ‒ the selimovic report, presented today in parliament, outlined the new measures to combat transmissible animal diseases. animal health is a crucial issue for a sector worth 156 billion euros a year, namely livestock farming. the text of the report, which i supported with my vote, amends and repeals certain legislative acts by linking animal health and welfare to human health. the new european legislation will cover animals kept in captivity, wild animals affected by communicable diseases and the 30 million workers who come into contact with animals on a daily basis. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of animals used for scientific purposes. the new rules promote the responsible and prudent use of veterinary medicines, particularly antibiotics, to help combat the growing antimicrobial resistance. the simplification of legislation is linked to the need to ensure that disease control procedures do not cause pain, stress and suffering to animals undergoing healthcare treatment.
in writing. ‒ i do not agree with the overly liberal implementing rules on animal welfare, which create a situation of regulatory chaos for farmers in particular and are a source of additional administrative burdens. i think, however, that every useful opportunity should be taken at community level and not to alter the most burdensome aspects of it: i therefore abstained in the vote on this proposal to reject the council's position.
in writing. ‒ the resolution voted today is an important step forward towards a single legislative text for animal health regulation in the european union, based on the principle, which is always valid, that 'prevention is better than cure'. i welcome in this connection the fact that the text adopted today highlights in particular the link between human and animal health, stressing the role of prevention in relation to transmissible animal diseases and also emphasizing the responsible use of antibiotics in the livestock sector and particularly in livestock farming. protecting animal health is therefore our duty but also a necessity, which can benefit the well-being of all. finally, i fully share the importance of ensuring that animal care and treatment are put in place to minimise pain and suffering.
in writing. ‒ animal health is a concern. this concern arises not only from public health and food safety aspects but also from the economic costs of animal diseases. given the transmissible nature of many animal diseases, a common approach, rather than a series of individual actions, will produce overall benefits. the value of the eu's harmonised approach is widely recognised both because it has helped to reduce the administrative burden for those working in the sector and because it has played a key role in the completion of the single market by facilitating intra-eu trade in animals and products of animal origin through the establishment of harmonised animal health conditions and has contributed to the success of the cap. it is the task of the eu institutions to ensure a high level of public health and food safety by minimising the incidence of biological and chemical risks to humans, and promoting animal health by preventing/reducing the incidence of animal diseases. parliament should therefore promote animal health legislation that takes up the 2007 animal health strategy and establishes the general principles of good animal health in european union legislation. to this end, it is essential to apply uniform rules and to encourage cooperation between member states.
in writing. - i abstained. despite our opposition to the application of animal welfare rules (still cited by farmers today as a negative example of 'regulatory chaos' and a source of administrative burdens), it is undeniable how closely linked animal health and welfare are to the quality of agricultural products and, consequently, to human health. while rejecting a too 'liberal' position on the subject, we would nevertheless point out the need to take advantage of every useful opportunity, at community and national level, to change the most burdensome and impractical aspects of the treaty.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the regulation in question to prevent and combat outbreaks of animal diseases such as avian influenza or african swine fever. the adoption of this animal health regulation is a major step forward. it makes three things possible. first, it links animal health and welfare to human health. this direct link, together with increased focus on responsible use of antibiotics, will help to combat the growing antimicrobial resistance. secondly, the legislation allows authorities and producers to focus more on the prevention and control of transmissible animal diseases. thirdly, in accordance with the principle of simplification, some 40 legal acts are combined into one single act. this new european legislation on communicable diseases should help professionals in the field to keep up with scientific progress and ensure that farmers' and veterinary organisations and animal welfare movements are involved in the preparation of emergency plans.
in writing. ‒ i believe that protecting animal health is our duty and that it can benefit the well-being of each of us. a large part of the european parliament's opinion at first reading was upheld, which allows us to support the final compromise. key references were maintained in important articles highlighting the link between animal health and welfare, and the need to guard against antimicrobial resistance in the conduct of disease prevention and control measures.
in writing. ‒ today marks the end of the legislative process leading to the adoption at second reading of the regulation on transmissible animal diseases, which is part of the wider animal health regulatory framework. for too many years veterinary medicine has over-recourse to the use of antimicrobials for preventive rather than therapeutic purposes only to prevent the spread of disease and infection in livestock. not only has such prolonged use not protected against epidemics, but it has had the side effect of developing strong antimicrobial resistance in animals and indirectly in humans as well. the approved regulation will require member states to collect relevant, comparable and sufficiently detailed data on the actual use of antimicrobials in animals and to transmit such data to the commission in order to monitor and encourage more prudent use of the medicinal products concerned in order to reduce the risk of antimicrobial resistance. i voted in favour of the resolution because it regulates an important sector for health.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is a concrete proposal for a constantly evolving problem. in the face of ever-new diseases, the report's first aim is to record illnesses in a clear and precise manner, in line with the opinion of efsa experts. secondly, the proposal aims to establish national prevention measures by ensuring animal safety by establishing animal welfare obligations and by increasing disease control measures, for example by restricting the movement of animals. for these reasons i voted against the rejection of this proposal. i believe it is our responsibility as members of parliament to engage in constructive dialogue with a view to improving ourselves and not to reject effective proposals such as this one a priori, denying parliament the opportunity to respond to matters of increasing importance.
in writing. ‒ this draft resolution endorses the joint statement by the european parliament, the commission and the council on antimicrobial resistance and the use of veterinary medicinal products. i have decided to vote against the rejection of the text because it emphasises the role of prevention in the regulation on transmissible animal diseases ('animal health regulation') and the consequent reduction of the use of antibiotics in the treatment of animals. in addition to complying with the requirements of that regulation, member states are also required to undertake to collect relevant, comparable and sufficiently detailed data on the actual use of antimicrobials in animals and to transmit such data to the commission in a way that allows for their more prudent use and thereby contributes to reducing the risk of antimicrobial resistance. the commission, for its part, is committed to publishing a report on the use of antimicrobials in animal treatment in the eu on the basis of data obtained from the member states.
in writing. ‒ i am voting against the request to reject the recommendation for the second reading of the council position at first reading with a view to the adoption of the regulation of the european parliament and of the council on animal health legislation. parliament's position at first reading is maintained, which would include in the regulation rules for the prevention and control of animal diseases transmissible to animals or humans and rules governing animal welfare, given the links between animal health and welfare.
in writing. ‒ this is an important initiative that should be supported, because a new impetus is needed for animal health rules. these are fundamental and decisive rules in the prevention and control of communicable diseases and in dealing with risks to health and safety of food and feed. it is important to monitor the control pathways and responsibilities of the different actors veterinarians, breeders and farmers who play a key role in the protection of animal health, ensuring effectiveness at the different levels of surveillance. among other things, it will be essential for member states to have contingency plans for the management of certain diseases, to introduce specific rules for vaccination and consequent control measures to be taken in the event of outbreaks, suspected or confirmed, of pathogenic events. in the event of a public health emergency due to an epidemic, it is essential, as introduced by the regulation, to provide for procedures to be applied at both national and supranational level. the resolution also calls for the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the animal health and welfare legislation is applied in a uniform manner.
in writing. ‒ this legislation will make two things possible: link animal health and welfare to human health and allow authorities and producers to focus more on the prevention and control of transmissible animal diseases. this link, together with increased attention to the responsible use of antibiotics, will help to combat the growing antimicrobial resistance. furthermore, all disease control measures should be aimed at the welfare of the animals and avoid any pain, distress or suffering to those selected for controls, including strays. for these reasons i have decided to vote in favour of the measure.
in writing. ‒ i abstain because other aspects of the question would have to be changed first.
in writing. ‒ the adoption of the animal health regulation, which was approved at second reading today, is a victory. finally, a link is created between the authorities and the producers so that more attention is paid to the prevention and control of diseases such as avian influenza or swine fever. the rules informally agreed with the eu council in june 2015 streamline the matter and allow 40 legal acts to be merged into one basic act. the regulation also puts the emphasis on the responsible use of antibiotics in view of the growing antimicrobial resistance also in the animal world. this is a step forward in the fight against animal diseases.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on transmissible animal diseases and amending and repealing certain acts in the field of animal health, as i believe that the agreement reached between parliament and the council today offers good legislation in the field of animal health. it is important legislation for millions of eu citizens who work with animals and concerns both wild and pet animals, given the consequences for humans of the animal communicable diseases we have seen in recent years. i am in favour of the principle of good animal husbandry, the use of humane treatment and animal health, because it is necessary to avoid unnecessary pain and suffering in the care of animals and the application of health measures. i also welcome the call for the prudent and responsible use of veterinary medicines and the obligation of transparency in the field of antibiotics, because the issue of antimicrobial resistance is of the utmost importance in the fight against animal diseases. finally, the establishment and updating of a list of diseases drawn up with the collaboration of efsa is very positive.
in writing. ‒ i do not support this document, citing the commission's statement on animal welfare that 'the regulation lays down rules for the prevention and control of animal diseases transmissible to animals or humans and does not contain rules specifically governing animal welfare despite the links between animal health and animal welfare'.
in writing. ‒ the measure adopted today improves european animal health legislation by obliging breeders and all other operators in the sector to comply with the principle of good animal husbandry and all biosecurity measures for the protection of animals and human health. the obligation to use veterinary medicinal products, in particular antibiotics, prudently and responsibly will be made even stricter, and a list of diseases covered by the law will be adopted, in accordance with the guidelines expressed by parliament and the council, in accordance with the opinions expressed by experts. we know that antibiotic resistance is a growing problem, posing serious health risks to people and animals. a strategy for the prevention of animal diseases, which does not involve the massive use of antibiotics, is needed. thanks to the efforts of our group, the importance of animal welfare has also been recognized, with the prescription of health treatments that avoid pain, stress and suffering. the link between animal welfare and health is well documented by scientific studies. the measures for pets are also important, with the obligation for breeders and traders to register and the creation of animal databases.
in writing. ‒ the new animal health regulation, which incorporates and updates almost 40 acts of the previous legislation, establishes for the first time a clear link between animal health and public health. the new legislation focuses on the prevention and control of diseases that can be transmitted between animals and potentially to humans, such as avian influenza and african swine fever. it also outlines the responsibilities not only of farmers, traders and animal professionals, but also of veterinarians and pet owners, who will be required to use veterinary medicines more carefully in order to combat the growing antimicrobial resistance. i hope that these measures will be effective in protecting and safeguarding public and animal health, and i have therefore decided to vote in favour of the agreement at second reading.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this regulation which, among other things, provides for the obligation to avoid pain, distress and suffering to animals in carrying out disease control measures: farmed animals are sentient beings and not machines to produce meat, milk and eggs. i also welcome the fact that this regulation links animal welfare and public health at eu level. i hope that further rapid legislative steps will be taken in this direction: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. it is right to try to control these potential bombs with health measures, but the only really effective way is to introduce animal welfare standards that can eliminate overcrowding of farms (which makes it easy and widespread to spread infection) and to eliminate unnatural living conditions, which weaken the immune system of animals. finally, i am in favour of two other principles contained in the regulation: the need to guard against antibiotic resistance and the commitment to conserve biodiversity and valuable genetic resources.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the text presented, which will help to improve animal health legislation by obliging all operators to respect the principles of good animal husbandry. in addition, prudent and responsible use of veterinary medicines will be ensured, with a list of regulated diseases in line with the decisions of the european parliament and the council.
in writing. the animal health report links animal health, also viewed from the perspective of safeguarding animal welfare, with human health. in order to combat the growing antimicrobial resistance in veterinary medicine, it was decided to frame the issue in the light of this direct human-animal link and to place greater emphasis on the responsible use of antibiotics. the report also calls for greater focus by national authorities and producers on the prevention and control of animal diseases. in this sense, all disease control measures should take into account the welfare of animals and avoid any kind of pain, distress or suffering to all animals subject to such measures, including those in captivity such as strays. it also provides for the responsibilities of all animal operators and professionals, who will be required to use medicinal products for animals more carefully. i would have liked the report to be more ambitious and to be more incisive on the subject of animal welfare, but i welcome the elements introduced and that is why i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. ‒ the number of overweight or obese children under the age of five has increased from 31 million in 1990 to 41 million in 2014. it is therefore understandable why it is so important to teach children from an early age the value of a healthy, balanced diet. the eu has therefore decided to establish a legal and financial framework to regulate the distribution of genuine agricultural products, through the 'milk in schools' and 'fruit in schools' programmes. the new rules aim to ensure that more effort is put into not only providing children with healthier food but, above all, educating them to adopt healthier eating habits. i voted in favour because i believe that these programmes can bring considerable benefits to public health and at the same time help to grow the european agricultural sector.
in writing. ‒ more than 20 million european children are now overweight. the average consumption of fruit and vegetables by adolescents is only 30 to 50% of the recommended daily intake. europe as a whole seems to be suffering from a decline in fruit and vegetable consumption, while the risk of diseases linked to poor diet and obesity is steadily increasing. my support for the tarabella report comes from the conviction that increasing the resources devoted to the development of good eating habits is a crucial investment in the future of the younger generation. the €250 million provided, compared with only €20 million provided so far, is a clear confirmation of the eu's commitment to food. the merger of existing school curricula on fruit and vegetables and milk will make it possible to improve the efficiency of european measures, while ensuring better use of funds. the measures adopted exclude all products containing added sugar and sweeteners and give priority to fresh and local products over processed products such as soups, compounds, fruit juices, yoghurt and cheese.

in writing. ‒ after almost two years of legislative work, parliament approved the agreement reached in the trilogue last december on the regulation uniting the two previous regulations establishing the 'milk in schools' and 'fruit in schools' programmes. over the years, these programmes have reached some 30 million children across europe. guiding dietary habits from childhood helps to develop a greater awareness towards balanced nutrition and to prevent obesity. although the two programmes had the same objective - the promotion of healthy eating and the increase of fruit, vegetables and milk consumption by children - they were nevertheless governed by different legal and financial frameworks which contributed to making the administrative burden on local and national authorities excessive. the new regulation aims to simplify the administrative and financial procedures provided for in the previous ones and introduces an interesting novelty for the youngest: the commission has already proposed a number of measures to help the farmers to make the most of the new possibilities. they will learn to make a conscious choice and to have a more direct contact with nature. i voted in favour of this regulation, sharing its purpose and the simplification it provides for wider implementation.

in writing. ‒ with today's vote, parliament supports the extension of the school fruit scheme, complementing it with the milk scheme and strengthening its educational dimension. the aim is to get 30 million children across europe to learn and practice healthy eating. one in three children in europe is overweight or obese: in this context, the role of schools in prevention and food education is crucial. the programme, which is to be implemented by the member states, is aimed at children aged between six and ten years and provides for the possibility of pre-school and secondary education classes to join. the promotion of local and regional products is an integral part of the programme. the funds cannot be cut unilaterally by the member states and they provide for eur 150 million a year for fruit and vegetables and eur 100 million for milk for schools that request it. the european union is close to all its citizens, starting with the youngest.
in writing. ‒ member states are facing major social challenges today. in view of the current decline in the consumption of fresh fruit and vegetables and dairy products, especially among children, and the increase in the incidence of childhood obesity due to consumption patterns oriented towards highly processed foods, union aid for financing the distribution of selected agricultural products to children in educational establishments should further promote the promotion of healthy eating habits and the consumption of local products. i therefore vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ educating children to a healthier lifestyle, starting with dietary habits, is one of the key tasks of our school systems, especially given the high level of childhood obesity, which is a consequence of aggressive advertising campaigns, often targeted at children, that promote the consumption of junk food. thanks to today's vote in the european parliament, 30 million children will eat and learn to eat better. the new legislation will allow free distribution of fruit, vegetables and milk in schools throughout the school year. the clear definition of the funds will enable the member states to plan their action better. the text adopted also states that member states will have to give priority to the distribution of fresh products of local origin. for the first time, sweeteners and other artificial additives are banned altogether in school food. products containing added sugar, salt and fat are also generally prohibited and will be allowed only after explicit authorization by the national health authorities. particular attention is paid to the selection of products and their origin (local, fair and sustainable). finally, products such as honey, olives and olive oil will also be distributed occasionally, for specific educational campaigns.
in writing. ‒ in view of the sharp decline in the consumption of fresh fruit and vegetables and dairy products, especially among children, and the increase in the incidence of childhood obesity due to poor eating habits, i believe it is of great importance to continue and strengthen the two school programmes, the 'distributed fruit and vegetables' and the 'milk in schools' programmes. the european union's aid, which is intended to finance the distribution of selected agricultural products to children, will help to promote healthy food education and educational tools to strengthen the link with the agricultural world. i therefore decided to vote in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ the report on the distribution of certain foods in schools is based on an analysis of young europeans who do not consume the recommended amount of fruit, vegetables and milk products. in order to improve the nutrition of our children, i voted in favour of this report which proposes that school lunches be based on more fruit, vegetables and milk.
in writing. ‒ the 'fruit in schools' and 'milk in schools' programmes are two european initiatives created for the distribution of fresh fruit and vegetables and milk products in schools. the proposal for a regulation voted today will combine the two programmes to make them more effective, reduce administrative burdens and improve overall results. the report also envisages an increase of eur 20 million in annual funding for milk measures, a fairer distribution of funding among the member states that decide to participate and a wider range of eligible products. each country will be free to choose which fresh milk products and milk products to distribute, so that local and regional products are given priority. the statistics speak for themselves: more than 20 million european children are overweight and adolescents on average eat only 30 to 50% of the recommended daily intake of fruit and vegetables. i believe it is essential to raise awareness among students and teachers of the importance of a healthy and balanced diet and that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the proposal for a regulation bringing together the two existing schemes for the financing of aid for the distribution of fruit and vegetables and milk in schools, because i believe it is important to actively promote healthy eating habits and the consumption of local products, especially in the face of the widespread phenomenon of childhood obesity. the aim of the measure is to encourage the distribution of fresh, local and unprocessed fruit and vegetables in schools, in order to combat harmful eating habits linked to the consumption of processed food containing excessive doses of sugars, salt, fats and other additives. this resolution will allow for more efficient management of the two existing aid schemes by bringing them together in a single programme, which should be publicised as a european union initiative and thus make visible the commitment of the european institutions to supporting concrete action to promote the health and well-being of young school children.
in writing. ‒ a healthy diet contributes to better health, but consumption of fruit, vegetables and milk is falling across the eu. member states need to do more to promote healthy eating habits, organic farming, local food chains and the fight against food waste. the school fruit, vegetables and milk programme should be strengthened, with an increased budget and a greater focus on food education. each member state should also provide for accompanying educational measures to bring children back into contact with agriculture and healthy, quality products.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the merger of the 'fruit and vegetables in schools' programme and the 'milk in schools' programme. i strongly believe that promoting the consumption of fresh and natural products in schools is a priority to develop proper eating habits, in a period characterized by high levels of obesity. this text will ensure better effectiveness with a single programme in which the fruit and vegetable component and the milk component can be managed in parallel.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the programme on food health education in lower secondary schools across europe. the proposal, which was strongly supported by the s&d group, provides for the allocation of a european fund which will enable schools to obtain free healthy food produced by local farms to be offered to children. each member state will have to make a regulation to this effect. i believe that by this act the european union is taking another important step towards ensuring the health of its citizens. i also find it particularly useful that the products supplied come from the local area, as a guarantee of quality and respect for the environment.
in writing. ‒ this vote by the european parliament is very important, as it invests in the health of our children. today, unfortunately, the consumption of fruit, vegetables and milk is reported to be falling sharply throughout the union. hence the challenge of encouraging consumption, starting in schools, also focusing on a training action on food education. it is not only right to increase the budget for this measure, but also to prohibit member states from unilaterally cutting their own budgets or changing the criteria for allocating the community funds allocated. betting on the well-being of children is very important for the future of our countries.
in writing. in a continent where 26% of adults are now overweight, we need to start in schools to educate young people on healthy, responsible and sustainable eating, a diet with as little added sugar and salt as possible. i am satisfied that the program to bring fruit and vegetables to school canteens for children between the ages of 6 and 11 meets the requirements for which i have fought. sustainability, seasonality, locality, ethical production and no additives will now be the criteria for selecting food for our children. i am pleased that educational measures have not been neglected to support the simple distribution of fresh and locally sourced products, to make students understand the advantages and benefits of a healthy and balanced lifestyle. i voted in favour of a programme which will bring italy some 16.7 million for the fruit and vegetable programmes, plus another 8 million for the milk programmes. this is almost 25 million compared to the 21.5 million in 2015. that's a great accomplishment. now that the programme is in place, we must ensure that it is implemented in the best possible way at national and local level.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the regulatory framework which is being proposed will make it possible to counteract weak competitive pressure and possible market abuse, in order to increase the efficiency of port services. i would like to stress the concept of independent supervision, which is to provide an independent complaint mechanism. all users should be consulted and informed and should have the possibility to submit complaints to independent bodies. the italian transport system is beset by important and still unresolved structural problems due to the weakness of the regulatory and planning framework and the modesty of private partnerships in the construction of new infrastructure. it is therefore comforting to know that the regulation adopted today, even if postponed for the final vote, should bring legal certainty to ports and have a positive impact on the operation of transport networks. there is time for the final vote and i hope that we will find a way to give more attention to sustainable and green transport services, so as to contribute to better energy efficiency.
in writing. ‒ the union's port system consists of some 1 200 seaports, which are a key resource for the continent's economy. in addition to providing 3 million jobs, european ports provide transit for 74% of imported and exported goods and 37% of intra-eu trade. the existing framework includes considerable variations between the different member states in the organizational models of port services. the fleckenstein report, which i supported, amends the original commission proposal on market access for port services and financial transparency for ports. the proposal, which does not require the adoption of a single system for services, strengthens the principle of port authority autonomy in the organisation of services by allowing port authorities to set minimum requirements for the provision of services. i have personally been committed to focusing on the issue of training workers. in a competitive and complex sector such as ports, training of new recruits and staff is essential to ensure not only the health and safety of workers but also the quality of services and the overall competitiveness of union ports.
in writing. ‒ the commission intends to liberalise, through a regulation, eight typical sectors of port operations in accordance with principles similar to those of the services, procurement and concessions directives. i believe that such a measure would risk creating a new "bolkestein" case, would open the doors of our territories to multinationals, with a devastating impact on our local operators. for all these reasons i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ contributing to a more efficient, interconnected and sustainable operation of the ten-t by defining a framework that allows all ports to improve their efficiency and helps them to cope with changing requirements in the logistics and transport sectors is certainly in the interest of european citizens. the modernisation of port services and operations and the creation of framework conditions to attract investment in ports are a central point in the proposal, which should also be seen as a condition for the implementation of fair competition between ports, on equal terms and in compliance with the community regulatory framework. the prosperity of transport infrastructure and the efficiency of european ports are important pillars for the economic development of the european union in the long term.
in writing. - i vote against the delay. accepting the referral would mean speeding up the procedure by favouring an agreement at first reading. on the substance, our opposition is clear. such a measure, which would come into force without even the member states having to incorporate it into their legislation, would be likely to have very damaging effects on the long-established local operators who have been providing certain services in our ports for decades, if not in some cases for centuries. in short, in the present silence of the media and the political parties, there is a risk of creating a new "bolkestein" case, with entire categories of professionals who would realize that their jobs are at risk only if regulations are adopted. the fact that the multinationals are now entering our reality is more than a mere hypothesis. the declared attempt to harmonize the organization of entire sectors of production in accordance with the principles of free competition is based on nothing more than the desire to centralize at european level important policy choices, such as those concerning the operation of ports. the proposal therefore remains highly controversial. it is a fact that many governments in the council have expressed various concerns.
in writing. ‒ the regulation aims to establish a common framework for regulating port services in europe. the categories involved are many and range from port authorities, service providers, consumers, ship owners, workers. a number of points which are important to us have been incorporated in the final text. the positive elements include the rules on staff training and social rights, financial transparency where there are public funds and state aid, the exclusion of small ports from the application of additional bureaucratic and excessive administrative burdens. my vote was in favour.
in writing. ‒ the tran committee's aim in this report is to achieve better functioning of the ten-t and thus improve the efficiency of all ports. the main objectives of this proposal are to further modernise port services and operations and to create the conditions for attracting investment in ports. that is why i voted in favour. i believe, as this report also stresses, that a prerequisite for fair competition between ports is a level playing field provided by a clear framework on state aid rules. the commission considers that the block exemption (state aid) regulation will, on the one hand, avoid additional burdens for ports already functioning well and, on the other hand, create the optimal conditions for other ports to address their structural problems. i also voted against amendment no 98 on article 10 of the regulation (social clause) because, in line with the italian ministry of infrastructure and transport, i believe that the application of this clause should be optional and that the choice of its application should be left to the member state.
in writing. ‒ considering that recent studies across europe show that very large numbers of goods pass through european ports, i.e. more than 75% of imports and exports representing more than 37% of the internal market, and that this regulation would improve market access by ensuring greater financial transparency, i have decided to vote in favour of this proposal. the drafting of the text revealed some difficulties, starting with the basic differences between the ports of the countries of northern and southern europe, which required convergence on several fronts. the document which has been drawn up has been a satisfactory compromise in order to make ports appear as a key point in the european economy where important investments can be concentrated. i would like to stress, however, that i regret that it has not been possible to clarify the question of the social clause in the text.
in writing. ‒ the regulation aims to establish a common framework for regulating port services in europe. the initial proposal called for the liberalization of services, which was later removed from the parliament's text, mainly due to pressure from northern european countries, such as great britain, where ports are completely privatised. the categories involved are many and range from port authorities, service providers, consumers, ship owners, workers. the chapter on the liberalization of services has been converted into a reorganization of services. the rules on training of staff and social rights, financial transparency in the case of public funds and state aid, and the exclusion of small ports from the application of additional bureaucratic and excessive administrative burdens are positive elements. my vote is in favour of the proposal.
in writing. ‒ i am convinced that the proposed regulation will be essential to establish legal certainty for ports and have a positive impact on the proper functioning of the ten-t network. the amendments adopted will increase the possibilities for trade negotiations between the managing body and port users, while respecting the fundamental principles of transparency. for these reasons i voted in favour of the commission's proposal.
in writing. ‒ i am voting against the report because it is controversial and could put our country's economy at risk by liberalizing.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's position on the regulation of the european parliament and of the council on certain specific aspects of the liberalisation of port services, because i believe that the compromise reached within the parliament's committee on transport (tran) combines the need to increase the efficiency of port services, reduce costs, particularly those due to inefficiency, with the development of intra- and extra-european trade. i note with particular interest the involvement at various points in the debate of the parties directly concerned: the commission has also proposed that the council adopt a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. i welcome the work done by tran to improve the commission's original legislative proposal so that existing port management models at national level could be maintained and further developed while ensuring transparency, preventing abuse of the prices of services offered and thus market distortions, given that ports in the various countries receive public funding. finally, i fully support the introduction in the european parliament's position of minimum requirements for port service providers limited to proof of professional qualifications and compliance with the principles of maritime and environmental safety and national social standards. i therefore hope that a fruitful agreement with the council will be reached as soon as possible.
in writing. union funding for the transport sector amounts to around eur 26 billion over the period 2014-2020, focused on the trans-european networks (ten-t) network, which contains the main transport routes for passengers and businesses across europe. the proposal under consideration aims to increase the level of efficiency, interconnection and sustainability of the ten-t by modernising port services and operations, while creating the necessary conditions to attract investment in ports. i supported the proposal because i share the main objectives and content, but i would like to point out that there are different systems of port organisation within the eu area, and a substantial difference between northern and southern europe as regards the very activities for which ports are intended. it is not always easy to strike a balance between different needs, but i believe that it is also necessary to avoid rigid positions in order to allow everyone the same opportunities for investment and development.
in writing. ‒ favourable to the report on the proposal for a regulation establishing a regulatory framework for market access to port services and financial transparency for ports. the objective is to contribute to a more efficient and sustainable operation of the ten-t by providing a regulatory framework that makes it possible to improve the efficiency of ports in the logistics and transport sectors in order to attract investment in them.
in writing. ‒ the organisation of ports and port services is a very important issue for the european union. the objective of this report is to contribute to a more efficient, interconnected and sustainable operation of the ten-t by defining a framework to improve the efficiency of all ports and to help them cope with changing logistics and transport requirements. the main objectives also include the modernisation of port services and operations and the creation of framework conditions to attract investment in ports. in the present regulation, the commission intends to counter weak competitive pressure and possible market abuse in order to increase the efficiency of port services. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the reform of port services contained in this report supports the modernisation of the 329 main sea ports in the european union. following the two reforms of 2001 and 2004 which dealt with the liberalisation of the sector, the focus is on transparency, workers' rights and safety, social dialogue and environmental protection. for the first time, the reform has been endorsed by all the parties concerned: port managing bodies, operators and trade unions. in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, the different organisational models are protected and, at the same time, a framework is established which will increase the efficiency and strengthen the competitiveness of the maritime ports of the transeuropean transport network. the report provides that social and labour standards will not be affected by the regulation and that port workers will receive appropriate training. it also invited the committee for social dialogue in the port sector at union level to develop guidelines on training requirements to prevent accidents and ensure the highest level of safety and health of port workers. i also think that the provisions on financial transparency, complaints and the prevention of price abuse are equally positive.
in writing. ‒ the text presented in plenary amends the commission's initial proposal which envisaged making free market access the basic principle for the provision of port services. the regulation states that a single system of market access is not appropriate as the eu port system is characterised by a number of different models of organisation of port services. this will allow the current port management models established at national level to be maintained. i believe that ports should be able to decide, by agreement between the various competent bodies, how their services are to be organised. as regards the transparency of public funding to ports, i believe that public funds should be shown in a transparent manner in port budgets and that port managing bodies, which receive public funding and which provide port or dredging services on their own, should keep separate accounts for these activities or investments financed with public funds. for all these reasons, my vote on the commission proposal as amended by parliament is in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the regulation because i believe that the port sector needs to be reformed as soon as possible. the report as a whole is moving in the right direction, although i do not agree with the rapporteur's proposal for a social clause to be imposed only and exclusively on those who make calls for tenders, namely italy and a few other member states. nevertheless, i think that blocking the text in parliament would have resulted in an excessive extension of the legislative time which we simply cannot afford.
in writing. ‒ harmonisation of consumer price indices is a highly sensitive issue, as it is closely linked to the issue of inflation, which is the basis for european economic and monetary policy decisions. the improvements made are far from making these maneuvers acceptable. moreover, by including house prices and taxation, the new index will better reflect reality on the one hand, but on the other will inflate the inflation figure by making the ecb's unconventional policies appear more positive than they actually are. that is why i have decided to vote against.
in writing. ‒ harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) measure inflation in a harmonised way in all member states. the ecb and the commission, as provided for in article 140 tfeu, use these instruments to assess price stability in different countries and national competitiveness in the context of macroeconomic imbalance procedures. the current ipca regulation dates back to 1995 and caused quite a few problems at the time of the outbreak of the economic crisis in 2008. the widespread proliferation of corrupted and poor quality statistics, together with the development of new tools in the field of consumer price statistics, has necessitated a revision of the entire structure to ensure maximum comparability of data between different users. the gualtieri report, which i supported with my vote, made some changes to the proposal for a regulation submitted by the commission. the text approved by parliament further improves the project by introducing more up-to-date and efficient legislation on statistical methodology.
in writing. ‒ this report is moving towards an excessive harmonisation of the categories of expenditure towards which the choices of consumers in economically too heterogeneous countries converge. the commission has also been asked to draw up a report on the implementation of the new financial regulation, which will be published in the official journal of the european communities. for all these reasons i did not intend to support this text with my vote.
in writing. ‒ fallacy statistics and disparities in calculation between member states contributed, among many other factors, to the delay in responding to the 2008 economic crisis. the optimisation of the legislation on harmonised consumer price indices allows for a simplification of the legislation, reducing the scope for possible divergent interpretations at national level. the report aims to create a favourable environment for the effective implementation of monetary policies developed within the european framework by reducing the response times by member states for the production and dissemination of the relevant statistical data. i therefore support the amendments made, in the hope that the european union will be able to respond promptly to future macroeconomic imbalances, also thanks to more homogeneous and objective information for a fundamental area such as price stability.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this document because i believe that an update of the instruments for measuring inflation is necessary to enable policy-makers to take the most appropriate monetary policy decisions, especially in a turbulent period like the present one.
in writing. ‒ the aim of the harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) is to measure inflation in a harmonised way in all member states. the commission and the european central bank use hicps when assessing price stability in the member states in accordance with article 140 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the european parliament should support the commission proposal for a regulation establishing a uniform legal framework for the development, production and dissemination of data on harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) and house prices (hicps) at union, national and sub-national level. the hicp provides a tool for measuring inflation which is used, inter alia, as useful information on the deflation of economic values such as wages, rents and interest rates and thus forms the basis for decisions on economic and monetary policy. it is therefore essential that such statistics are objective, unbiased and comparable in all member states and for all product categories.
in writing. - i vote against it. it is an instrument which will be used to assess the competitiveness of the different member states according to criteria which, in our view, are often interpreted in an arbitrary and instrumental way by the central bank and the european commission. at a time when there is an ideological debate within the eu itself about which inflation rate should be compatible with real growth conditions, an excessive level of harmonisation of the categories that encompass the choices of consumers in member states so different and in economic conditions so opposite to each other is likely to be an exercise that leads to results that are not easily interpretable. in any case, this is a measure which deprives the member states of a substantive assessment which we think they should retain.
in writing. ‒ after careful reflection and debate in the house, i have given my favourable vote to the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on harmonised indices of consumer prices and repealing regulation (ec) no 2494/95, on the basis of the following considerations in my report: the quality of statistics and their comparability are a public good of fundamental importance for all union citizens, researchers and public policy makers in the union; in 2003 the governing council of the ecb decided that, in pursuit of price stability, it would aim to maintain inflation rates below but close to 2% over the medium term; that legal framework should be adapted to current needs and technical progress, including by improving the relevance and comparability of hicps, as well as by monitoring a wider set of additional indicators needed for the measurement, analysis and forecasting of inflation, which should be made available on a harmonised basis.
in writing. ‒ the changes made improve the consumer price index. however, given the link between this index and monetary policy decisions, it is reasonable to assume that the change in the inflation index will have an impact on the monetary policy decisions taken by the ecb. by including house prices and taxation the new index will better reflect reality on the one hand, but on the other will inflate the inflation figure by making the ecb's unconventional policies appear more positive than they actually are. this raised legitimate doubts that the revision of the regulation was necessary at a time when the ecb needed objective data to better justify unconventional policies and to better sponsor their policy at a difficult time when the eu bank was losing more and more credibility in a context of low growth and threatened by deflation. that is why i voted against.
in writing. ‒ harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) allow for an assessment of inflation in a harmonised way across all member states. these indices in particular provide information on price stability, as well as assessing national competitiveness in the context of the commission's macroeconomic imbalance procedure. the proposed regulation clarifies the scope of the hicps by ensuring that the indices are objective, impartial and comparable in all member states and for all product categories, thereby avoiding possible manipulation. the new developments in consumer price statistics have necessitated a revision of the regulation, which has been in force since 1995, in order to ensure maximum comparability of data. i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation because it defines an updated and uniform system of indices which are the basis for decisions on economic and monetary policy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal because it sets out a common legal framework for the development, production and dissemination of harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) and a house price index (hpi) at union, national and sub-national level. a uniform framework is necessary in my view to ensure that these statistics are objective, impartial and comparable in all countries and for all product categories, and thus form the basis for future decisions on economic and monetary policy. i believe that the quality of statistics, their uniformity within the european territory and therefore their comparability are a public good of fundamental importance for all eu citizens.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposal for a regulation lays down a uniform legal framework for the development, production and dissemination of data on the harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) and house prices (hicps) at union, national and sub-national level. the hicp provides a tool for measuring inflation which is used, inter alia, as useful information on the deflation of economic values such as wages, rents and interest rates and thus forms the basis for decisions on economic and monetary policy. in addition, the regulation takes account of the innovations in the union decision-making process introduced by the treaty of lisbon, which give the commission the right to adopt implementing or legislative measures that may amend non-essential elements of a regulation. i voted in favour of the report because i think that these updates are necessary and that these statistics are objective, impartial and comparable in all member states and for all product categories.
in writing. ‒ the consumer price index (cpi) provides a tool for measuring inflation and thus forms the basis for economic and monetary policy decisions. it is therefore necessary that the methods for calculating the index are objective, impartial and comparable in all member states and for all product categories. the 1995 eu hicp production and dissemination regulation should establish a uniform legal framework at union and national level for the development, production and dissemination of data. the changes made improve the consumer price index. however, given the link between this index and monetary policy decisions, it is reasonable to assume that the change in the inflation index will have an impact on the monetary policy decisions taken by the ecb. by including house prices and taxation, the new index will better reflect reality on the one hand, but on the other will inflate the inflation figure by making the ecb's unconventional policies appear more positive than they actually are. for these reasons, i preferred to vote against the motion in plenary.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament resolution approves the regulation on harmonised consumer price indices, which aims to establish a common framework for the development, production and dissemination of harmonised consumer price indices and the house price index at national and union level. i voted in favour of this regulation because i believe that harmonization of these indices is essential if we are to have comparable data which will make it possible to calculate the levels of inflation and other economic aspects in a uniform way in all the member states and, consequently, to adopt the appropriate economic policy measures.
in writing. ‒ this proposal for a regulation is of particular importance at one of the most complex moments in the history of central banks' management of monetary policy. in fact, the dramatic problem of deflation, which has hit japan in the last decade, seems to be affecting europe too, and many economists are beginning to believe that it may be a non-transitory phenomenon. this regulation therefore establishes a coherent legal framework for the management of data on harmonised indices of consumer prices and house prices at both european and national level. this is a decisive step forward in the harmonization of statistical studies, but it is also decisive once these data are used within the european institutions for economic policy decisions. this text also takes account of the institutional developments within the commission as they existed in the treaty of lisbon. the new framework for action by the national institutions, which must provide monthly flash estimates to compile the indices used in monetary policy, is particularly important. for this reason, the text is an important step towards better management of statistical data in the european institutions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because of the importance of the quality of statistics and their comparability for citizens, researchers and policy-makers in the union. i welcome the commission's proposal to create a uniform legal framework for the processing of data on consumer price indices. the use of uniform and comparable data is also essential for a more effective monetary policy in the euro area, as it would make it possible to respond more quickly and concretely to the different critical issues that may arise.
in writing. ‒ i am voting against the report because i do not think that the competitiveness of the member states is assessed by the criteria considered.
in writing. i thank my colleagues on the committee on economic and monetary affairs for this important legislative report. improving the quality of consumer price indices is a very important measure in detecting and correcting macroeconomic imbalances within the eu. indeed, there were many instances of inaccurate statistics that led to the financial crisis in 2008. the creation of a common procedure and a more integrated methodology between the different member states can certainly help in this respect.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the agreement reached between the ep and the council on the proposal for a regulation establishing a uniform framework for the development and dissemination of data on harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) and house prices (hicps) at eu level, as it constitutes an important instrument for harmonising and simplifying existing legislation and also contributes to the functioning of european economic governance, particularly in the context of the surveillance procedure for macroeconomic imbalances. the ep also called for the introduction of a new system of taxation, which would be based on the principle of equal treatment for men and women. this has been achieved by the introduction of the harmonised index of consumer prices for taxation (hicp-ta). the ep also strongly supported the need to introduce an obligation for euro-area countries to provide monthly snap estimates of the hicp in order to support the monetary policy of the euro-area. the regulation will be implemented through a series of delegated acts which the ec will adopt on a proposal from eurostat, taking into account the indispensable support of the ecb, where such acts imply prerogatives in monetary policy, and in compliance with the opinion of the ep. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a regulation on the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation lays down a uniform legal framework for the development, production and dissemination of data on harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) and house prices (hicps) at european, national and sub-national level. with reference to the hicp, it is a tool for measuring inflation and is also useful because it provides information on the deflation of wages, rents and interest rates. it is therefore essential that statistical data are reliable, unbiased and comparable in all member states. in addition to these data, timely provisional information on inflation is needed. i decided to give a favourable opinion because the current ipca regulation dates back to 1995 and it was important to revise its structure and update it accordingly.

in writing. ‒ this proposal for a regulation defines a uniform legal framework for the development, production and dissemination of data on the harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) and house prices (hipps) at union, national and sub-national level. a very relevant point is also the requirement for euro area member states to provide flash estimates on a monthly basis, and that the breakdown of flash estimates of the hicp, the owner occupied housing price index (ooh) and the ipab is adopted by means of implementing acts. i therefore vote in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposal for a regulation lays down a uniform legal framework for the development, production and dissemination of data on the harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) and house prices (hicps) at union, national and sub-national level. the regulation also takes account of the innovations in eu decision-making introduced by the treaty of lisbon, giving the european commission the right to issue implementing measures (implementing acts) or legislative measures that may amend non-essential elements of a regulation (delegated acts). i voted in favour of this draft report which proposes that both the hicp and the hicp-t are broken down by the categories of the european classification of individual consumption by function (ecoicop) and calls on the euro area member states to provide estimates on a monthly basis.
in writing. ‒ the hicp, the harmonised index of consumer prices, measures changes in the prices of consumer goods and services purchased by households over time. it is essential that this index is consistently measured accurately, as it is the basis for many of the eu's monetary and economic decisions. recent developments in consumer price statistics have necessitated a revision of the 1995 regulation on which the hicp is based. i therefore voted in favour of the report because it provides for the introduction of a single simplified regulation which will improve the definition of the categories of products to be covered and the scope of the regulation, reduce the margin for interpretation of the rules, remove redundant parts of the legislation and ensure uniform treatment of groups of similar products in all member states. in addition, in order to have timely information on inflation for the purpose of implementing monetary policy, euro area member states will be asked to provide flash estimates on a monthly basis.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the harmonised index of consumer prices (hicp), which amends the existing statistical methodology by summarising its principles in a single regulation. this index measures inflation in all member states in a harmonised way and is used by the commission and the european central bank to assess price stability in the member states. the report stresses the importance of treating certain sectors such as health, education and other specific sectors separately and autonomously, in order to reduce the interpretative space of the rules, ensuring uniform treatment of similar product categories in all member states. i also believe that it is essential for monetary policy in the euro area to have preliminary information in the form of a quick estimate in the context of the correction of macroeconomic imbalances. moreover, the hicp was designed to assess price stability and should not be understood as an index of the cost of living. in this context, i think it is appropriate to launch pilot studies on harmonised indices of the cost of living, as proposed in the report itself.
in writing. ‒ the revision of the consumer price index regulation was voted on at the last plenary session. this index provides a measure of inflation and thus forms the basis for monetary policy decisions. the regulation was from 1995 and needed to be revised. the revision has made several steps forward, both in terms of harmonisation and through the inclusion of house prices and taxation data. goods that do not cover household final consumption expenditure, such as narcotics, games, prostitution and certain types of insurance, have also been excluded from the basket. however, the timing of the review itself seems rather strange. since these changes will inevitably increase the inflation figure, this raised legitimate doubts that the revision of the regulation was necessary at a time when the ecb needed objective data to better justify unconventional policies and to better sponsor their policy at a difficult time when the eu bank was losing more and more credibility in a context of low growth and threatened by deflation. for these reasons we voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for regulation of the harmonised price indices by the european parliament and the european council. the wrong statistical indices were partly responsible for the financial crisis of 2008. i am convinced that this legislation, which will improve and regularise the statistical methodologies for the formulation of these indices, will improve the quality of the means available to the eu to correct macroeconomic imbalances.
in writing. ‒ the consumer price index provides a tool for measuring inflation and is the basis for economic and monetary policy decisions. it is therefore necessary that its calculation methods are objective, impartial and comparable in all member states and for all product categories. there has been some progress, both in terms of harmonisation and through the inclusion of house price and taxation data, but it is reasonable to assume that the change in the inflation index will have an impact on the monetary policy decisions taken by the ecb. the new index will better reflect reality on the one hand, but on the other it will inflate the inflation figure by making the ecb's unconventional policies appear more positive than they actually are. this raised legitimate doubts that the revision of the regulation was necessary at a time when the ecb needed objective data to justify its unconventional policies at a time of difficulty when it was losing more and more of its credibility, in a context of low growth and threatened by deflation. for these reasons i voted against.

in writing. ‒ gender mainstreaming in eu sectoral policies is a key step towards achieving equality between men and women and towards an inclusive and sustainable society. this is a crucial dimension for the protection of human rights and the functioning of democracy. however, progress remains slow and uncertain, and the commission's assessment of the 2010-2015 strategy identifies several gaps, although there is renewed ambition for the 2016-2019 period. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that introducing a gender perspective at all stages of the political cycle is the only real action to be taken to achieve our goals of equality and cohesion, which are the founding goals of the union itself. i also believe that this is a crucial issue for the european parliament, which already has an organisational structure to promote gender mainstreaming in all its activities, but for this structure to be fully effective it needs to be strengthened through greater cooperation with the council and the commission, facilitating the work of the various bodies responsible for gender mainstreaming within the parliament itself.
in writing. ‒ equality between women and men is recognised by the eu as a fundamental right, a common value of the union and a necessary condition for achieving the eu's objectives of growth, employment and social cohesion. in the european parliament, the committee on women's rights and gender equality (femm) is the main body responsible for promoting gender equality and gender mainstreaming in all of parliament's political and legislative processes. the integration of the gender dimension has a twofold significance: integrate a gender perspective into the content of the various policies and address the issue of the representation of women and men in the various policy areas. unfortunately, once again, the text presented to the plenary is tainted by certain ideological views which prevent the adoption of a balanced report. therefore, although i continue to work for the affirmation of a real equality between men and women, i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the report describes the implementation of gender mainstreaming measures in the european parliament's work. gender mainstreaming is the set of measures and policies adopted to ensure gender equality between men and women in legislative processes. the resolution highlights that there is still a situation of inequality between men and women in parliament. there is still much work to be done to achieve satisfactory goals. it is clear that only some committees are more active in this area, while others have not yet implemented the necessary measures. the report calls for greater efforts between the institutions to achieve the objectives set, such as increased inter-institutional cooperation to support gender mainstreaming, as well as increased funds and specific budget lines. i therefore cannot but vote in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ from the beginning of 2015 to november of that year, some 900 000 people reached europe's shores by crossing the mediterranean sea. thirty-eight percent of these were women and children. girls, fleeing conflict and persecution, represent a particular group within the large category of refugees, more exposed to the risks of early and forced marriage, sexual and physical violence and prostitution. i voted in favour of the honeyball report because i believe it effectively outlines the problems and possible responses to the difficult conditions facing women refugees and asylum seekers in the eu. the report presents several measures to ensure that their specific needs are met both within reception centres and during the asylum application process. the main provisions include the creation of gender-separated sleeping areas and toilets, the presence of female staff and interpreters, counselling for gender-based violence trauma and the care of children during screening. the decision to increase information to explain to women the right to apply for asylum independently of their spouse is also particularly important for the purpose of women's empowerment.
