mr president, ladies and gentlemen, today i voted against the additional duty-free importation into the european union of 35 000 tonnes of tunisian olive oil, because it is a wrong choice which does not help tunisian producers, increases the risk of fraud to the detriment of european consumers and harms italian producers, especially those from apulia who are already suffering from the xylella problem. today's sudden green light from parliament comes after imports of tunisian olive oil to italy increased by 481% in 2015. the new preferential quota will be added to the current 56 700 tonnes at zero duty already provided for in the eu-tunisia association agreement, thus bringing the total of preferential arrivals above the 90 000 quota. the real risk is that this will only encourage the proliferation of fraud, misleading consumers about the origin of the product and encouraging unfair competition against quality producers. i am not questioning the european union's support for the tunisian economy but the way in which it is given. the european union must support the democratization process in tunisia in every way possible, but it cannot be our oil producers who pay for it.
in writing. ‒ the euro-mediterranean agreement regulates relations between the eu and tunisia, establishing economic and financial cooperation with respect for human rights. however, the terrorist attack near sousse, tunisia, on 26 june 2015 prompted member states to adopt exceptional and temporary measures to support the tunisian economy, which was severely damaged by those events. for these reasons, the import of 35 000 tonnes of tunisian oil duty-free was authorised for the years 2016 and 2017, thus causing enormous damage to the italian economy and agriculture. i therefore decided to vote against, considering that such a derogation from the import rules, for such a long period of time, would seriously damage one of the assets of the italian economy, which is already badly affected by the economic crisis and the xylella disease.
in writing. ‒ olive oil is the main agricultural product exported by tunisia to the european union and a key sector for the country's economy. the proposal for a regulation adopted today by parliament was intended to introduce some autonomous emergency trade measures to facilitate the entry of 70 000 tonnes of tunisian oil without increasing the overall volume of imports. i have decided to vote against this measure because i am convinced that these measures do not help the producers in the maghreb country. while i am aware of the fragility of the economic and social situation in tunisia, i believe that the union must help the country with a broader political commitment that can consolidate the democratic process initiated by tunisia without putting consumers and citizens of the union at risk. the import of tunisian oil opens up the european market to a greater risk of fraud, threatening to generate unfair competition which can harm quality producers.
in writing. ‒ this measure is scandalous and will have devastating consequences for italian oil producers and for made in italy. it is yet another eu folly, a decision that goes against our producers and consumers themselves: the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat fraud in the olive oil sector. i have spoken against the adoption of this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the proposal to import an additional 70 000 tonnes of tunisian oil into the eu at zero duty for the 2016-2017 biennium. tunisia is a key player for stability in the north african region and it is in the common interest to support its economic recovery and democratic transition. however, to provide concrete support, appropriate means must be used, capable of producing tangible benefits for the tunisian population, and not counterproductive for european production. my vote today follows a process which has been under way in recent weeks with some members of the s&d group, and in particular the pd delegation, to improve the proposal. we have succeeded in passing the obligation of traceability and the exclusion of extensions to the measure. i believe, however, that the text, without the other improvements we have put forward, remains highly problematic for honest european producers and, ultimately, for consumers, increasing the risk of fraud at the expense of the guarantee of 'made in'.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this document because i believe it is the european union's duty to support tunisia's transition to democracy by all means possible. i believe that the introduction of emergency autonomous trade measures for tunisia will provide tangible support for the tunisian economy and make regime change, whether military or religious, less attractive to the tunisian people. tunisia is the only country where the arab spring has achieved satisfactory results. it is in everyone's interest that the achievements made should not be undone.
in writing. ‒ tunisia is undoubtedly a country whose democratic path needs to be supported and encouraged. however, i am against this measure because it does not really help the tunisians, it penalizes our producers and it certainly does not favour consumers.
in writing. - i vote strongly against it. this measure is the result of a personal intervention by the high representative mogherini, with the aim of helping the tunisian economy, which has been hit by the crisis in the tourism sector following the recent terrorist attacks. what the european commission is therefore proposing is to allow the further entry into the eu of a zero-tariff quota of 35 000 tonnes of tunisian olive oil. it is clear that the price of this 'aid' would be paid only by certain member states (italy, spain, greece and partly france), while for most it would be a zero-impact measure. moreover, this intervention would only favour the multinationals of the fake 'made in italy' who bring huge quantities of olive oil to the union market which looks italian but is only partly italian when it is good.
in writing. ‒ i have reaffirmed my vote against the legislative resolution on the extraordinary aid measures for tunisia, because i believe that the elimination of customs duties on the import of tunisian olive oil could harm a sector already severely affected by the consequences of the continuing economic crisis. in its first plenary vote on 25 february, parliament had succeeded in amending part of the proposal in order to limit the impact of the agreement on european production, particularly italian production. it was a clear and unequivocal position which had given the no's courage and hope that the council could find the conditions for a change of course. there is no doubt that aid to third countries is part of the european union's missions and that measures to accompany the process of democratization and stabilization in the mediterranean area must be taken, but the attempt to help one country in difficulty is risking damaging others. we hope that a debate will soon be opened on the recognition of compensatory measures for those states most exposed to losses of market shares.
in writing. ‒ as before, i have stressed my opposition to the resolution which seeks to introduce emergency measures for tunisia, which would allow the import of 70 000 tonnes of tunisian olive oil to be tax-free for two years, which would further damage the situation of small oil producers in several european countries, particularly in italy. we do not want to question the desire to help another country, which is also strategically important for europe, but we cannot accept the fact that it is always the small producers in italy and/or the countries of southern europe who fail. we must be able to find different solutions to show solidarity with third countries without creating disadvantages for the member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the second time and again strongly against the abolition of the duties on tunisian oil. i did so because i was struck by the comments of several tunisian ngos who said that the measures were insufficient and unable to produce positive effects for the agricultural sector and the economic situation in general. i also did so because i believe that the final resolution is a blow to small producers: the structural nature of the measure is such that it is likely to help only large-scale industry by strengthening the industry lobbies. the failure to adopt important amendments has prevented all the doubts and uncertainties raised by the measure from being dispelled. the final resolution is hasty and lacks analysis, fails to respond to the need for support of the tunisian people and penalizes a part of our productive fabric. that is why i have decided to vote against the measure once again.
in writing. ‒ i am absolutely opposed to the report which allows tunisian oil to enter europe with negative consequences, especially for italian producers.
in writing. today we are called upon to vote on a report which provides for aid to the tunisian economy through community emergency measures which will allow the importation of 70 000 tonnes of tunisian extra virgin olive oil duty-free in 2001 and 2016. we have been working on this decision for many months, which i think is wrong, and i am against the agreement. it should be stressed, however, that our intervention has improved the text compared with the original text of the european commission. i voted against because i believe that the eu must change its approach, because we cannot think of helping outside countries by harming our economy or part of it. and in this case i do not think there is any real help for tunisia either. i ask the european commission to monitor the implementation of the agreement to prevent fraud and counterfeiting, and to proceed as soon as possible with the recognition of compensatory measures for our olive growers, such as the recognition of the pgi mark for sicilian extra virgin olive oil.
in writing. ‒ increasing the quota for oil imports from tunisia is the worst way to help the north african country. the oil companies are trying, with great difficulty, to get out of not only the continuing economic crisis, but also the xylella emergency. this measure will have devastating consequences for the whole sector and for these reasons i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ given the need for the eu to help boost the tunisian economy at an undoubtedly difficult time, this seems to me to be an appropriate decision, but it must be borne in mind that the union's solidarity is solidarity at the expense of southern european farmers who currently constitute that part of the market which has been fragile for some time. the importation of 35 000 tonnes of olive oil from tunisia duty free, if it does not help the tunisian economy much, certainly harms the italian economy, with a collapse in prices and an increase in fraud and consumer damage. the price to be paid will therefore be the highest in the south and its regions. for this reason, as a member of the european parliament, but above all as an italian citizen, i am voting against this report, so that a better solution can be found, such as direct financial support, rather than penalizing the entire olive industry.
in writing. ‒ the european commission proposes the introduction of a tariff-free quota of 35 000 tonnes per year for two years for tunisian olive oil exports to the union. i understand the eu's desire to help boost the tunisian economy at a difficult time for our allies, but i do not think that the union's solidarity should come at the expense of southern european farmers, in the specific case of olive oil producers. the latter have already been severely affected during 2015 by certain diseases affecting their crops. solidarity with tunisia could be demonstrated through funding for the police or investments in the field of culture and youth training. but once again, it's the farmers of the south who will have to pay. i voted against the introduction of these autonomous emergency trade measures and i will continue to work to ensure that europe does not make mistakes of this kind in the future.
in writing. ‒ i reiterated my vote against the duty-free import of 35,000 tonnes of olive oil from tunisia for two years. this decision will force our producers to face unfair competition, since tunisian oil will be placed on the market at prices lower than those of quality italian oil. this is certainly a serious mistake which unfortunately is likely to have a serious impact on the whole european and italian olive sector.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure authorising the duty-free import of an additional quota of oil from tunisia for the next two years, as this is a solidarity measure that makes a concrete contribution to the tunisian economy, which has been seriously weakened after the terrorist attacks of 2015. tunisia is the only country that has steadily moved towards democracy since the 2011 revolutions, and the economic crisis risks weakening it under the looming threat of radical propaganda and terrorist infiltration. thanks to the work done, the measure has been significantly improved with safeguards that meet the concerns expressed by operators in the sector to protect european olive growing: the traceability of the imported product (the oil must come entirely from tunisia, to ensure that the measure is actually helping the tunisian economy and to prevent fraud) and the evaluation of the measure after the first year, to verify its impact on the european market and to make any corrective measures to protect our producers. it is not by denying concrete aid to a fragile economy such as that of tunisia that the interests of european farmers are served, but by making concrete commitments on other fronts such as the promotion of typical products, the protection of quality, traceability and the fight against counterfeiting.
in writing. ‒ i said no to the european commission's proposal to allow the duty-free entry into the eu of 35 000 tonnes of tunisian oil per year for two years. tunisia must be helped in its transition process, but not at the expense of italian and european olive oil producers. the community's position on the question of the status of the oil industry in the community is that it is not possible to determine the exact position of the oil industry in the community. this means that it will remain in the eu and will drive down the price of oil, harming producers in mediterranean countries, who are already suffering from the eu's austerity policies. i am surprised that italy and the other mediterranean countries of the eu have not opposed and renegotiated the measure in the council. during the february plenary session, i voted in favour of several amendments which made it necessary to renegotiate the agreement in the eu council. we hope that in the next elections, both for national politicians and for the european parliament, the olive growers of italy and mediterranean europe will remember the names of the ministers and meps who have damaged their interests.
in writing. to help tunisia, which is in a difficult economic situation, the european commission has proposed to provide substantial support to the olive oil sector to help it recover. this is a trade measure providing for the duty-free importation of 70 000 tonnes of product over two years. olive oil is the main agricultural product that tunisia exports to the eu: in 2015, imports from tunisia increased by 600% and fraud in the oil sector quadrupled in the same year. seizures and judicial investigations throughout italy show that there is a correlation between increased imports and counterfeiting. the union's solidarity is once again solidarity at the expense of the farmers of southern europe. olive oil is an important factor of economic and social support in the producing areas, including italy. europe is thus siding with the multinationals who are interested in selling oil at low cost. this is jeopardizing the survival of many small farmers and landowners in italy who will now suffer the collapse of their oil prices. the 5 star movement is fighting alongside italian farmers: i had no choice but to vote for the rejection of the proposal altogether.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the grossetête report on the proposal for a regulation on veterinary medicinal products. medicinal products for animals are important tools which require particularly complex processing due to the multiplicity of existing species. legislative action in this area must take account of two aspects, firstly the need to simplify legislation as much as possible and secondly to address the serious issue of the increase in antimicrobial resistance. the development of resistant bacteria must not only involve a limitation of the use of antimicrobials, but above all an investment in innovation that will allow research in this field to be strengthened. the who has already warned of the risks to the health and lives of millions of people that could result from the emergence of a post-antibiotic era. europe must do its part by stopping mass treatment and ensuring that the prophylactic use of antibiotics is limited to cases where it is really justified.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the report voted today, which marks an important step forward in the fight against antibiotic resistance, through a more limited and responsible use of existing antimicrobials and the development of new medicines. the text aims to update european legislation on veterinary medicinal products, excluding antibiotic treatment practices for purely preventive or collective purposes, and encouraging research and development of new quality medicines. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the use of antibiotics is not restricted to the use of certain medicinal products. the new regulation aims to facilitate access to such medicines within the union by creating more favourable conditions for their circulation, including through improved authorisation procedures, more effective pharmacovigilance and reduced administrative burdens. this encourages a more deliberate and regulated use of medicines, which can in no case replace good farming practices and must be administered only after a careful assessment by the veterinarian, thereby enhancing the protection of animal health, human health and the environment.
in writing. ‒ the provision is useful to improve access to medicines, particularly in the veterinary sector, where there is a shortage of medicines in many market areas. the main objectives of the provision are to improve access to and availability of medicines, particularly for species improperly described as 'minor'; to reduce administrative burdens, in particular as regards the pharmacovigilance process; stimulate innovation and competitiveness in the sector; ensuring the proper functioning of the internal market for veterinary medicinal products; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of animals used for scientific purposes.
in writing. - i vote against it. the new regulation sets out to separate the rules governing the authorization and placing on the market of veterinary medicinal products from those governing medicinal products for human use. this certainly brings greater clarity. however, the final vote cannot be favourable on the substance for the following essential reasons: the entry into the food chain of animals in clinical trials is not completely avoided; medicinal products containing gmos are allowed (articles 297 and 131 tend to prohibit them). persons other than veterinarians are also entitled to prescribe veterinary medicinal products; the online sale of prescription medicinal products is also allowed; the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation which sets out a regulatory framework specifically designed for the specific characteristics of the veterinary sector. the existing legal framework has been a source of implementation problems, in particular with regard to the shortage of veterinary medicinal products, the functioning of the internal market, the phenomenon of antibiotic resistance, the lack of incentives to support innovation, and the administrative burdens imposed. the proposal adopted today addresses all these shortcomings. the question of antibiotic resistance is saying something that is increasingly worrying: each year, the average meat consumer unknowingly ingests nearly 9 grams of antibiotics (the equivalent of four courses). the responsible use of antibiotics which are important for human medicine, such as fluoroquinolones and cephalosporins, in veterinary medicinal products should therefore be further promoted. the widespread use of these two substances in livestock to combat common infections contributes to the spread of antimicrobial resistance. i think that where no disease has been diagnosed, the administration of antimicrobials for preventive or prophylactic purposes should be prohibited.
in writing. ‒ while the fundamental objective of the industry is to achieve a single market for veterinary medicines, the main objective of m5s europe is to safeguard animal welfare, increase the availability of veterinary medicines across europe and, above all, to move from a culture of mass animal care to a culture where animals are given individual care as humans are. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the legal framework in the veterinary sector has always been a source of problems in its implementation, in particular with regard to the shortage of veterinary medicines (especially for smaller markets), the administrative burdens imposed, the functioning of the internal market and, of course, the phenomenon of antibiotic resistance. for these reasons, the commission proposal lays the foundations for a complete overhaul of the legislation on veterinary medicinal products, currently based on directive 2001/82/ec and regulation (ec) no 726/2004, and is intended to regulate the authorisation, manufacture, placing on the market, distribution and use of veterinary medicinal products throughout their life cycle, as well as the related pharmacovigilance process. i think it is fundamentally in the right direction, both in its objectives and in its desire to make a clear distinction between the market for veterinary medicinal products and that for medicinal products for human use. i agree with the rapporteur's comments and amendments and have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the commission has called for the establishment of rules on veterinary medicinal products from the moment of manufacture to the time of placing on the market, including the moment of import, export and control, in order to pursue the objective of improving the functioning of the internal market, reducing administrative burdens, stimulating competitiveness and innovation and increasing the availability of veterinary medicinal products. the european regulatory framework for veterinary medicinal products must be adapted to scientific progress and must protect animals, seeking to minimise their suffering and ensuring their welfare. since many of our requests have been accepted and since i consider this to be a matter of considerable importance, i am voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ in september 2014, the commission published its new proposal for a regulation on veterinary medicines. the directive lays the foundations for a complete overhaul of the legislation on veterinary medicinal products and is intended to regulate the authorisation, manufacture, placing on the market, distribution and use of veterinary medicinal products throughout their life cycle. among the objectives identified by the commission, emphasis should be placed on combating antibiotic resistance and promoting innovation and competitiveness in the sector. i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is important to make a clear distinction between the market for veterinary medicinal products and that for medicinal products for human use, ensuring the availability of products and promoting administrative simplification, without sacrificing the essential objectives of public health and environmental protection.
in writing. the plenary today dismissed an important text and i would like to thank mr grossetête for the excellent work he has done in recent months. the main objective of the text is to protect animal health and, consequently, human health. it aims to combat antibiotic resistance while increasing the competitiveness of our farms and the veterinary industries. the role of the veterinarian is given a prominent place, the importance of his work and professionalism is emphasised, without reducing the therapeutic arsenal at his disposal. the commission is also proposing to reduce the number of medicines which are still being placed on the market without authorisation. it also lays the foundations for a new pharmacovigilance system that will be more flexible, more effective and less bureaucratic.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on veterinary medicinal products. the availability of such effective and affordable medicinal products at reasonable prices is essential to expand the scope of research and development, increase the production of veterinary medicinal products and their viability in the internal market. clear and as simple as possible legislation is therefore needed to improve access to medicines, reduce administrative burdens, stimulate competitiveness and innovation, so that new and better medicines for the treatment and prevention of animal diseases are available, while avoiding damage to the environment.
in writing. ‒ antibiotic resistance poses a real threat to our health, especially for animals that eat meat. for this reason i am glad that this report calls for a collection of detailed data at the level of the member states, which must be at the forefront of solving these problems.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation voted today, which lays the foundations for a revision of the existing legislation on veterinary medicines. the objectives set out in the report relate to access to and availability of such medicines, innovation and development of new generation medicines, the proper functioning of the internal market for veterinary medicines, the reduction of administrative burdens and antibiotic resistance. on this last point, i think it is important to stress that the proposal regulates the limited use of antimicrobials: the prophylactic use of antibiotics as a preventive measure should only be implemented if fully justified by a veterinarian, and therefore not to improve performance or compensate for inadequate husbandry practices. the european centre for disease prevention and control has released worrying data showing that bacteria in humans, food and animals continue to show resistance to the most common antimicrobials, with the consequence that bacteria such as salmonella continue to proliferate throughout europe. i think it is essential that we invest more and better in research and innovation to develop new medicines.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on veterinary medicinal products, which updates the european rules on the subject in order to protect animal and human health while protecting the environment. the text voted today adds another important aspect to the commission's proposal, which focuses on the availability of veterinary medicines and administrative simplification, while respecting public health and protecting the environment, namely the fight against antibiotic resistance. we in parliament are calling for the preventive use of antibiotics in farmed animals to be restricted, that is to say, antibiotics should not be used as a preventive measure and in the absence of clinical signs of infection, or even as a means of improving the performance of farming. as recently reported by the european centre for disease prevention and control (ecdc), bacteria in humans, food and animals continue to show resistance to the most common antimicrobials, thus reducing options for effective treatment of serious infections. it is therefore necessary for humans and animals to have a clear overview of the use of all antimicrobial medicinal products as soon as possible so that action can be taken without delay to reduce misuse and end abuse.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour, albeit from a particular perspective: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the commission has already proposed a number of measures to improve the quality of veterinary medicines, such as the introduction of a new system of veterinary checks on animals. i particularly welcome the elimination of the administration of antibiotics to farmed animals for prophylactic or metaphylactic purposes. antibiotics are not a substitute for decent living conditions for animals, although farmers too often use them precisely to save on management costs and to increase yields. the massive and routine administration of antibiotics to farm animals is linked to the increasing emergence of antibiotic-resistant strains of bacteria, with serious consequences for human health. antibiotics have saved the lives of the general public at least a couple of times: it would be foolish to let them become increasingly ineffective in exchange for a few cheap steaks.
in writing. ‒ the union regulatory framework for the manufacture, authorisation and distribution of veterinary medicinal products is currently set out in directive 2001/82/ec and the subsequent regulation (ec) no 726/2004 which established the european medicines agency (ema). the commission presented in september 2014 a draft to bring together the veterinary medicines legislation into a single instrument, repealing the 2001 directive and amending the 2004 regulation. the tănăsescu report, which i supported with my vote, welcomed the commission's proposal but correctly highlighted the need to involve parliament in the ema's tariff-setting procedure. it is essential that the full co-decision procedure be used in this area, in accordance with the provisions on pharmacovigilance.
in writing. ‒ while i appreciate the commission's effort to make the rules governing medicines clearer, distinguishing between those for veterinary use and those for human use, i do not agree with the excessive extension of the powers of the european medicines agency. that is why i did not support the text with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the text adopted today, which accompanies the new regulation on veterinary medicinal products, aims to improve the procedure for placing such products on the union market by separating it from that for medicinal products for human use. i particularly appreciate that, as requested by the envi committee, the report provides for the full participation of the european parliament in the activities of the european medicines agency, while preserving its role as co-decision-maker in the definition of the level and structure of the agency's fees, which remains responsible for the evaluation, surveillance and pharmacovigilance of medicinal products for human and veterinary use.
in writing. ‒ in september 2014, following an assessment of the functioning of the internal market in this area, the commission published a proposal to bring together the rules on veterinary medicinal products into a single veterinary medicinal product regulation, repealing and replacing directive 2001/82/ec on veterinary medicinal products and amending regulation (ec) no 726/2004. this is useful in order to remove all references to veterinary medicinal products and thus to completely separate the provisions governing veterinary medicinal products from those governing medicinal products for human use. it is desirable that the union's work should be directed towards increasing the competitiveness of pharmaceutical companies, with the resulting beneficial effects on prices and availability of access to medicines.
in writing. - i vote against it. the commission has proposed to separate completely the provisions governing veterinary medicinal products from those governing medicinal products for human use. this separation is welcome, as it contributes to greater clarity of the legislative framework. in this case, the commission simply proposed to abolish all regulatory references to veterinary medicinal products, which are transferred to a new ad hoc regulation (see the grossetête report). unfortunately, the envi committee took the opportunity to 'communitize' the definition of the fees due to the ema, including the collection procedures, by replacing the implementing acts with an ordinary legislative procedure (see paragraph 31). in addition to being impractical, this appears to be a subtle extension of the ema's powers. the amendments also aim to centralise the authorisation process for veterinary medicinal products at eu level by creating a dedicated division within the ema.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation to protect public health in the european union and to ensure that centralised marketing authorisation for veterinary medicinal products is separated from that for medicinal products for human use. i would stress that, in the interest of public health, authorisation decisions taken under the centralised procedure should be taken on the basis of objective scientific criteria of quality, safety and efficacy as provided for in directives 2001/83/ec and 2001/82/ec. for medicinal products authorised in the union, provision should be made for the risk-benefit assessment of all medicinal products to take place both at the time of placing on the market, at the time of renewal of the authorisation and at any other time deemed appropriate by the competent authority. in order to improve the knowledge and understanding of antimicrobial resistance, the european medicines agency (ema) should publish annually, in cooperation with the european food safety authority (efsa) and the european centre for disease prevention and control (ecdc), a report on the use of antimicrobials in human and veterinary medicine, as well as on the current situation of antimicrobial resistance in the european union.
in writing. ‒ the rapporteur, ms tănăsescu, proposed improvements that could be shared, in particular on the structure and level of fees charged to the european medicines agency and on the fact that the remuneration for the competent national authorities should not be fixed by means of a mere implementing act. in the light of the foregoing, i have voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the union regulatory framework for the manufacture, authorisation and distribution of veterinary medicinal products consisted of directive 2001/82/ec of the european parliament and of the council laying down a community code relating to veterinary medicinal products and regulation (ec) no 726/2004 of the european parliament and of the council establishing community procedures for the authorisation and supervision of medicinal products for human and veterinary use. the commission proposes that the rules on veterinary medicinal products be combined into a single veterinary regulation, which would repeal and replace directive 2001/82/ec on veterinary medicinal products. i voted in favour of this reform because it will lead to a separation between the provisions governing veterinary medicinal products and those governing medicinal products for human use and will therefore bring simplification and consistency.
in writing. ‒ the aim of the resolution is to amend regulation (ec) no 726/2004 establishing community procedures for the authorisation and supervision of medicinal products for human and veterinary use. in 2014, the commission published a proposal to bring together all the rules on veterinary medicinal products into a single regulation, with the aim of completely separating the provisions governing veterinary medicinal products from those governing medicinal products for human use. the proposal therefore aims to delete from regulation no 726/2004 the provisions on the granting and maintenance of marketing authorisations for veterinary medicinal products, to lay down certain principles applicable to the fees of the european medicines agency and to align the implementing powers conferred on the commission under the 2004 regulation. i am in favour of this proposal because i share the improvements which will be made in the resolution on medicinal products for human and veterinary use.
in writing. ‒ i abstain because, despite some positive steps, there is an attempt to centralize the authorisation process for veterinary medicines too much.
in writing. ‒ today's vote is a first step towards changing the process by which medicines are approved at european level and in particular towards drastically reducing the time between the marketing authorisation of a new medicine and the decisions of individual countries on reimbursement. the current procedure creates very marked differences in the timing of access to new medicines, because the same medicinal product is assessed for its efficacy 28 times, once for each member state, although always on the basis of the same data. in some cases, it has taken up to ten years for innovative, life-saving drugs, even those deemed essential by the world health organization, to be actually used and reimbursed. so i really hope that this first step will point us in a new direction to overcome these difficulties.
in writing. the new veterinary medicines regulation covers all the procedures for granting marketing authorisations for veterinary medicines in the union, both at central and national level. the new measures will clearly take account of the specificities of the veterinary sector. the present proposal for an amendment is to be linked to the needs of the veterinary sector which, with regard to medicinal products, are substantially different from those of the human sector. i supported the text because it took account in a balanced way of the different needs to be protected in this sensitive area.
in writing. ‒ the role of the parliament and the european institutions in monitoring what we eat is paramount. the european institutions have always guaranteed high food standards and this report aims to reduce the amount of antibiotics we ingest when eating meat from medically treated animals as well as combating antibiotic resistance. the report's contribution to a new regulation laying down procedures for the authorisation, supervision and distribution of veterinary medicinal products suggests, for example, that the online sale of veterinary antibiotics be phased out and preventive care restricted, while supporting the exchange of best practices and research and innovation in this field.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it amends certain rules on the authorisation and supervision of medicinal products for human and veterinary use in order to completely separate the two areas of regulation. it is clear that the needs of the veterinary sector are substantially different from those of the human sector in relation to medicinal products. the proposal will therefore repeal directive 2001/82/ec and amend regulation (ec) no 726/2004 in order to remove all references to the granting and maintenance of authorisations for veterinary medicinal products and to take account of the specific needs of each sector. the new veterinary medicines regulation will therefore regulate all procedures for the authorisation of veterinary medicines in the union, both at central and national level.
in writing. ‒ the big data market is expanding at an unstoppable speed. it is estimated that over 50 billion in revenue and 16 billion terabytes of data will flow by 2020. the resolution points out that a data-driven economy can be harmonized and properly integrated with privacy-oriented data management. finally, the network, data and the internet can be used in tandem to foster open, transparent and inclusive government. in addition, initiatives to include programming and data processing subjects in national curricula are encouraged, highlighting the many benefits of free software in education. in order to promote the digital economy and the digitisation of the european states, i voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ big data represents one of the great opportunities of the 21st century; this is an opportunity that, according to the latest estimates, should generate a €50 billion market by 2017 with the potential to create jobs for 3.75 million people. the recovery of growth, innovation and investment can only happen through a digital single market strategy based on the development of a strong economy able to exploit the enormous amount of information produced every day. my vote in favour of the resolution tabled in parliament today is based on my deep conviction that big data is a huge opportunity that still needs to be exploited. from industry 4.0 to mhealth, from the theme of smart cities to e-government, the new technological frontier requires the development of advanced skills that can foster job growth. the issue of the intelligent exploitation of opportunities is also linked to that of data protection. in an increasingly connected world, the protection of privacy is a priority to be ensured and it is therefore essential to develop an appropriate and uniform european legal framework in this area.
in writing. ‒ the report is acceptable and does not present any particular criticisms, so i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the union's big data strategy aims to support and accelerate the transition to a digital single market in europe and, ultimately, to a european digital union based on more effective and fully regulated use of data. the potential benefits of an increasingly digitised economy, based on a growing stimulus to innovation and investment in r&d, are many and varied and concern businesses, public administrations and private citizens, and consequently bring significant benefits to society as a whole. the challenge of this important transition also presents more sensitive issues, which deserve to be dealt with with due attention, as underlined in the resolution voted today. the development of a data-driven economy cannot be achieved without providing for and maintaining the highest safeguards for the content of data, the guarantee of confidentiality of the most sensitive information and certainty and transparency about the processing of data. the use of data must therefore be regulated in a timely manner, according to precise and shared standards, which also allow fair opportunities for companies in their use, especially as regards smes. data protection and the opportunities arising from integrated data use should therefore not be mutually exclusive but complementary.

in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the resolution on the development of a european data-based economy, for which i was the shadow rapporteur on behalf of the socialist group. data-driven economy is the collection, analysis and subsequent interpretation of huge databases of information. this is an advanced and rapidly developing sector in which the eu still plays a limited role, but which represents a strategic growth opportunity for our continent. europe, with its 500 million citizens, more than 80% internet penetration and world-class universities, could be one of the largest digital markets in the world. to move from being spectators/users of services to becoming protagonists in the development of the data-driven economy, it is necessary to create a competitive environment by supporting the creation and standardisation of open data, especially with regard to data developed by the public sector, and also by encouraging private companies to open their databases whenever possible while respecting privacy. investing in infrastructure capacity, building specialised skills, promoting entrepreneurship, in a secure but flexible regulatory environment, can create the conditions for the european, joint and coordinated development of the data economy, to enable the eu to compete globally.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, today's debate was not originally on the agenda, but i think it is right that we should be discussing in this house such an important subject which is closely related to human and animal health and the environment, and i am therefore glad that this debate can take place here in front of you all. in recent months, there has been intense discussion about the european commission's decision to renew the authorisation of glyphosate within the regulatory framework of the regulation on the placing of plant protection products on the market. the current authorisation expires in june 2016. as you all know, glyphosate is an active ingredient in a selective herbicide and is currently the most widely produced herbicide worldwide. it has been used for the last 40 years on a global scale and is used in 76% of cases in the agricultural sector. the envi committee of this parliament, on whose behalf i am presenting this position today, raised and approved the objection we are now discussing, asking the european commission to withdraw the draft implementing regulation, not to renew the approval of glyphosate, to draw up a clear timetable for drawing up a list of co-formulants which cannot be included in commercial products. the report also calls on the commission to carry out an independent review of the classification of glyphosate in the short term, in the light of the available scientific evidence on the carcinogenic potential of the substance and on the possible interference properties on the basis of the horizontal scientific criteria for endocrine disruptors. but i would like to take a short step back to better understand what happened after the commission renewed the authorization. in march 2015, the international agency for research on cancer (iarc) classified glyphosate as a probable human carcinogen, based on limited evidence of carcinogenic effects in humans and sufficient evidence of tumours in laboratory animals. in november 2015, efsa, the european food safety authority, in contrast to the opinion of iarc, completed a peer review of glyphosate and concluded that glyphosate is unlikely to pose a cancer threat to humans and that the available evidence does not justify its classification for carcinogenic potential in accordance with the regulation concerning the placing of plant protection products on the market. the envi committee, faced with this situation, decided by a large majority that the precautionary principle should be applied in this case, in order to ensure that active substances or products placed on the market do not have harmful effects on human or animal health or the environment. the regulation on the placing of plant protection products on the market states that, in particular, it does not prevent member states from applying the precautionary principle where there is scientific uncertainty as to the risks to human health, animal health or the environment of plant protection products to be authorised on their territory. the envi committee therefore considers that the draft commission implementing regulation does not ensure a high level of health protection, does not apply the precautionary principle and exceeds the implementing powers laid down by the legislation. it therefore calls on the commission to withdraw the draft regulation, calls on the commission not to renew the approval, calls on the efsa to disclose all scientific evidence. mr commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, this is the position of the committee i chair, on which you must of course express your opinion.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i should like to stress the usefulness of this debate, which has allowed us, in this chamber, in the presence of all our colleagues, to express our views. we have seen that there are very different positions within parliament, as has already been pointed out in the committee on the environment, but now is also the time to look for possible solutions. we have heard in this house the proposal of some amendments by the political groups which could, on the one hand, meet the need for renewal of authorization, but, on the other hand, obviously be able to give guarantees in a shorter time on the actual and not presumed, possibly, carcinogenicity of the product. but one thing is certain, and we must all be aware of it, and that is the importance of this product which is widely used in agriculture today as a herbicide and which, as some colleagues have said, could only be replaced by mechanical interventions, i.e. manual or mechanical felling, which, objectively, if, on the one hand, they are technically possible, on the other hand, would certainly undermine the competitiveness of our production system. so we shall be voting on this tomorrow and in the next few days, and i invite everyone to think about it in a broader way. on the other hand, another element that has emerged and which i would like to emphasize briefly is the role of the food safety agency: is the technical instrument available to the european union. and, as mr aguilera said, it is certainly the instrument we have at our disposal and on which we should also rely for our evaluations, otherwise i would not know what the agencies which burden the budget of europe are for.
in writing. glyphosate is a widely used active substance in herbicides. in 2000, when the patent expired, it was marketed by multiple companies and several hundred plant protection products containing glyphosate are currently registered in europe for use in agriculture. in march 2015, the international agency for research on cancer (iarc) classified glyphosate as 'probably carcinogenic to humans' based on 'limited evidence' of carcinogenic effects in humans, 'sufficient evidence' of cancers in laboratory animals, and 'strong evidence' of mechanistic data regarding the carcinogenicity of 'pure' glyphosate and glyphosate-containing formulations. nevertheless, in november 2015 the european food safety authority (efsa) completed an assessment of glyphosate and concluded that glyphosate is unlikely to pose a cancer threat to humans and that the available evidence does not justify its classification for carcinogenic potential in accordance with regulation (ec) no 1272/2008. the 5-star movement does not intend to renew the authorisation of glyphosate until there is a unanimous opinion on the absence of carcinogenic risk and echa has also taken a decision on the likely endocrine-disrupting properties of the active substance, which is expected by 2017.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, today's vote marks the end of a political process which lays the foundations for a future common migration policy. it was an extraordinary job of aligning the different positions and i thank mr metsola for the work done together in smoothing out individual sensitivities and sharing a common approach: migration is not counteracted but managed. it is managed through all the policies and instruments at our disposal, in the optimal combination of domestic and foreign policy. it is managed through the full involvement of all relevant actors, at european, national and local level. it is managed through concrete short-term actions and forward-looking medium- and long-term policies. it is managed if there is the political will to implement a founding principle of the union, the principle of solidarity and full sharing of responsibilities among all member states. we have taken this political responsibility. the draft resolution provides concrete responses to what is the largest displacement of men and women since the second world war, and outlines structural policies aimed at curbing the phenomenon and combating its root causes. the guiding principle of our proposals is the global approach and the principle of solidarity is at the heart of them. saving lives becomes a top priority, as does the development of mechanisms for the distribution of beneficiaries of international protection across all member states of the european union. it is time for the member states to take up their responsibilities and fulfil their obligations in relation to the relocation measures which this house is so keen on. we insist on the need for a binding and mandatory mechanism for resettling a significant number of asylum seekers directly from refugee camps in third countries to the member states, the so-called 'humanitarian corridors', while at the same time strengthening similar forms of solidarity, such as humanitarian admission and humanitarian visas. we call for specific measures for minors, starting with the right to legal assistance, health care, education, protection and, above all, not to be detained because of their condition. we analyse the critical points of the common european asylum system and decree the end of the dublin regulation. our proposal is clear: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's fishing fleet is not disrupted. we propose to set up a central and collective system for the allocation of responsibilities. a system which could be designed by setting thresholds for each member state in relation to the number of arrivals. the asylum application will no longer be made in italy or greece, but in europe. commissioner timmermans, this is the dublin amendment we expect from you, not cosmetic tweaks to a regulation which has proven in the face of the facts to be unable to meet the migratory challenges of recent years. managing migration also means addressing the root causes of migration. we call for greater cooperation with third countries, the relaunching of certain processes, including rabat and karthoum, and above all for strong measures to combat trafficking in human beings. the european union is also committed to the development of a european asylum system, which will be based on the principles of the european convention on human rights and the european convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. i hope that the amendment to the blue card is ambitious and reflects the needs identified in the labour market. the success of an immigration policy is also measured in terms of integration. we call on the member states to take concrete measures to provide housing, access to education and to intensify intercultural dialogue. mr president, with this resolution we are laying the foundations for a common migration policy that is able to meet the challenges of the 21st century. it is now up to the member states to decide whether they will follow our path or decree the final decline of the process of european integration. the future of europe also depends on how much we share our european dream and our values.

in writing. ‒ council regulation no 1528/2007 lays down the arrangements for certain products originating in the caribbean, the pacific and certain countries in the african states (acp). the regulation aims to codify european legislation on this subject, contained in various agreements establishing or aiming to establish economic partnership agreements. the aim is to provide a temporary instrument to facilitate the entry of products from less developed economies into the european market, thus attempting to progressively intensify trade between the eu and the acp. for these reasons i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the wałęsa report on products originating in certain acp states. it is a technical measure aimed at simplifying eu legislation on market access for products from african, caribbean and pacific countries. this is an important report because the original legal instrument, regulation (ec) no 1528/2007, has generated considerable problems of clarity and a difficulty in implementation due to the numerous amendments that have taken place since 2007. the new proposal for a regulation, which i supported with my vote, provides for a temporary instrument for duty-free access to the eu market for products originating in acp countries. the measure will only be activated before 1 october 2016, for the period preceding the conclusion and application of the new economic partnership agreements (epas) in line with the requirements of the world trade organisation.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the arguments put forward in the report by my colleague on the adaptation to the current legislation of regulation no 1528/2007 governing access to the eu market for certain african, caribbean and pacific countries. i therefore voted in favour of the text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this document because i believe that the codification of these legislative acts is important in order to clarify the legal framework governing access to the single market for products from certain acp states.
in writing. ‒ we consider it an act due to the regulatory and linguistic adjustment linked to the process of recasting the regulations in question, aimed at better transparency and accessibility by the citizens of the eu and partner countries, and we hope that the protection of the rights of individuals will be a central element of any possible future trade and/or partnership agreement with the acp countries (africa, caribbean and pacific) and/or other areas of political or economic interest.
in writing. ‒ the measure itself is not problematic. there are no negative economic consequences for the commercial interests of our regions. in fact, as this is a 'reconstruction' measure, we are faced with the need to adapt regulation no 1528/2007 governing access to the eu market for certain acp countries (africa, caribbean and pacific) to the rules in force in the meantime. since 2007, this regulation has already been amended 9 times, also to align it with the post-lisbon reforms. in particular, the amendments voted on today are to adapt the existing rules to the economic partnership agreement between the eu and the southern african development community concluded in 2014.
in writing. ‒ the proposal is to codify regulation (ec) no 1528/2007 applying the arrangements for products originating in certain states which are part of the african, caribbean and pacific group of states. this is a temporary instrument to ensure that certain products from the least developed acp countries can have access to the european market pending the signing and ratification of the various trade agreements currently under negotiation. i voted in favour of the proposal because it does not go beyond the mere codification of the rules on the recognition of these products.
in writing. ‒ it was easy for me to vote in favour of this proposal, since it is a simple codification of trade in products originating in certain states belonging to the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group of states. i agree with this because it simply aims at legislative clarification and also ensures greater transparency after the many amendments to this original legal instrument. it is, in my view, an improvement in the quality of regulation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is a mere codification of existing acts, without any substantial changes.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of adapting european regulation 1528/2007.
in writing. i voted in favour of the ep resolution on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council applying the arrangements for products originating in certain states which are members of the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group of states provided for in agreements establishing, or leading to the establishment of, economic partnership agreements, because i believe it is important to maintain a form of economic support for those least developed countries in africa and the caribbean in the context of the international negotiation of trade partnership agreements. the vote at this part-session is limited to codifying legislation from 2007 which has been amended several times over the years, thus ensuring the values of legal certainty and transparency which are fundamental to the european union. i also share the merit of the choice, since supporting the world's poorest countries through quota-free and duty-free access to the eu market for products originating in those countries is a fair measure, pending wider agreements establishing regular trade cooperation.
in writing. ‒ i shall vote in favour of the report on products originating in certain acp states. the proposal is merely a codification of the existing provisions which have remained unchanged in substance. the market access regulation covers imports of products originating in certain acp countries, providing for duty-free and quota-free access to the eu market. the codification helps to ensure transparency and clarity in eu legislation, which is another reason why i am in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposal concerns a codification and recast of council regulation (ec) no 1528/2007, the so-called 'market access regulation', which governs imports of products originating in certain acp countries. the aim is to ensure transparency, clarity and simplification of eu legislation by codifying in a single legislative act provisions which are scattered across different acts or adopted at different times in order to make them easier to read and understand. i therefore voted in favour of the measure.

in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the proposal for an agreement replacing certain provisions in the existing bilateral air services agreements between the eu and macau, to allow equal treatment of all european airlines operating in that country and respect for competition rules. bilateral air service agreements between a member state and a third country must include an 'eu designation clause' recognising that the terms of the agreement also apply to all eu airlines and not just to the airlines of the member state concerned, in accordance with internal market rules and the right of establishment. under the 'traditional' designation clauses, the third country could refuse, revoke or suspend authorisations or licences if a significant proportion of the ownership and effective control of the carrier was not held by the designating member state. the text voted on today thus eliminates discrimination against european carriers established in the territory of one member state but owned or controlled by nationals of other member states, thus bringing bilateral agreements with macao into line with european law.

in writing. ‒ in 2004, a working group was set up at the un general assembly to address the issue of conservation and sustainable use of marine resources in areas not under national jurisdiction. in order to create coordinated action with member states, the last report of 2015 stressed the need to develop a legally binding instrument at international level on the law of the sea and, in particular, on the protection of marine biodiversity. in this way, a comprehensive global regime is finally established for those areas which, lacking national jurisdiction, are not subject to any form of control. for these reasons i voted in favour, believing that the eu should have a positive influence on the work of the committee responsible for drawing up the document, thus ensuring that the issue is given the right importance.
in writing. ‒ seas and oceans cover 71% of the earth's surface and contain 97% of the planet's water, representing an incomparable heritage in terms of biodiversity. the european union has played and continues to play a key role in the protection of marine habitats and ecosystems, with its participation in several international fisheries management organisations and its ongoing work to combat illegal, unregulated and unreported fishing. the nicolai report, which i supported with my vote, reiterates the need for the eu to play a proactive role in ensuring a real assertion of science-based marine governance by supporting the draft of a new international agreement at the un that complements the previous agreement on the conservation of fisheries resources (unfsa) signed in 1995. only through a joint commitment at the global level will it be possible to act to stem the consequences of climate change and ocean acidification and the negative impacts of overexploitation, pollution, waste and the destruction of marine habitats and ecosystems

in writing. ‒ the un general assembly working group on the effectiveness of the current framework in addressing the conservation and sustainable use of marine resources in areas beyond national jurisdiction stressed in its latest report the need for a comprehensive global regime and recommended the development of an internationally legally binding instrument. parliament is speaking in order to influence the position of the united nations preparatory committee and, for the rapporteur, it is extremely important that fisheries activities be included in the new instrument. i fully share this approach and have voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ the increasing development of maritime activities is undermining the sustainability and conservation of marine biodiversity, including in areas outside national jurisdiction. the ad hoc working group established by the un general assembly to address the issue identified the need for international coordination for the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity and sees the creation of a legally binding international instrument, under the united nations convention on the law of the sea (unclos), as the most effective way to address the issue globally. the group is already working on the definition of the instrument which should be ready for 2017 in view of the international conference. i believe, as i also said in the report voted in plenary and on which i voted in favour, that this is a path that is now mandatory, but i believe that it is necessary for the new instrument to also include fishing activities, which are among the main causes of the loss of marine biodiversity. in order to make the instrument more effective, i believe that instruments should also be provided for the responsibility of all the actors involved and i hope that the european commission will take up the points made by the house.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the text in which parliament expresses its position on the decision of the united nations general assembly to develop a legally binding international instrument in the context of the un convention on the law of the sea (unclos) focusing on the conservation and sustainable use of marine biological diversity in areas not under national jurisdiction, with a view to addressing current shortcomings. currently, the united nations fish stocks agreement (unfsa) exists within the unclos framework, and is considered a good multilateral agreement that establishes a legal framework for the management of marine resources to address problems such as marine pollution, invasive human activities and other phenomena that threaten marine biodiversity. by the end of 2017, the united nations should present a new legally binding multilateral agreement to include fisheries in the regulatory framework, building on the unfsa agreement now in force. this is an important step in the development of the blue economy, which has enormous potential for growth and jobs and should be achieved within the ecological limits of the marine environment, in particular through responsible and sustainable fishing.

in writing. ‒ the rearing of pigs, cattle, sheep, goats and horses is a huge asset for the union. it occupies a key position within the agricultural sector and represents an important source of income for a large part of the farming community. the dantin report, which i voted on today in parliament, dealt with the zootechnical and genealogical conditions applicable to trade and imports of breeding animals and their germinal products within the union. i have supported this proposal because i believe it is important to support the work of the many breeders' associations which are at the forefront of defending genetic diversity in europe. the commission's proposal for a regulation aims to unify and simplify the existing legislation, which is now defined by four different acts. the new rules will clarify the rules on animal husbandry, leading to greater protection of the great cultural heritage of thousands of native species which have adapted over the centuries to the different regions of the continent.

in writing. ‒ the production and breeding of domestic animals with particular genetic characteristics and the trade of their germinal material to encourage their reproduction have long been recognised and encouraged as some of the main factors capable of ensuring high product quality and protecting the food safety of european consumers. in this sense it is right to try to group together the various european regulations already existing in this field and to harmonize the national ones in order to simplify the rules in the sector and to eliminate those superfluous technical barriers which often penalize international trade. in the context of this harmonization work, in continuity with the advice given by the committee on the environment, it is however necessary to promote high and effective standards and control mechanisms, for example by supporting a policy of competitiveness of european large breeds which is conscious, respects the various local breeds and thus protects biodiversity, and by promoting a privileged role of the international committee for the control of livestock performance in the development of zootechnical legislation. all this while paying particular attention to the welfare and safety of the animals.
in writing. ‒ the measure is very technical; over the past 20 years, the commission has had to respond to a significant number of complaints from breeders and operators carrying out genetic programmes concerning the timing of the transposition and interpretation at national level of union legal acts on reproduction in the various member states. in order to ensure the uniform application of union rules on breeding and to avoid obstacles to trade in breeding animals and their germinal products due to divergent transpositions of those directives at national level, a 'framework' text is proposed which undoubtedly adds burdens to operators. while recognising that such detailed legislation is also a minimal 'barrier' to reciprocity in trade agreements with non-eu countries, some references such as 'non-discrimination' with respect to the (generic) country of origin of animals do not allow us to give full support to the measure. i abstain from voting.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today to promote the free trade of breeding animals and their genetic material, while ensuring the sustainability of breeding programmes and the preservation of genetic resources. in addition, this report simplifies various provisions in various regulations by finally bringing together in a single legal framework the principles governing the recognition and listing of breeding organisations, breeders' associations and private undertakings, the approval of their breeding programmes, the entry of bovine, ovine, caprine and equine animals in the respective stud books and their classification according to their genetic merits, the entry of hybrid breeding pigs in registers, performance testing and genetic evaluation, and the content of zootechnical certificates for breeding animals, their semen and ova and embryos. in addition, that report lays down rules on imports of breeding animals from third countries and improves the legal framework for such imports by creating a model pedigree and zootechnical certificate providing information on the descent, identification and, where appropriate, genetic evaluation of breeding animals and their germinal products.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation is part of the eu's zootechnical legislation package which aims to promote the free trade of breeding animals and their genetic material while ensuring the sustainability of breeding programmes. the proposal contains clarification of the regulatory framework for the recognition of breeding societies, a clearer definition of the term 'breeding animal' and introduces the possibility for breeding operations to produce performance tests according to the different registered breeds. in these respects, the proposal is certainly to be welcomed. however, i decided to abstain because it would have been preferable if the regulation had not dealt with the issue of clones, which in my view should be included in a separate legislative package.

in writing. ‒ the commission wanted to bring together all the directives relating to the zootechnical legislation of the various species in a single legal corpus in the form of a regulation. this is a harmonized structure of animal selection which will have a significant impact on the animal genetics sector in europe. the european union's zootechnical legislation aims to promote free trade within the eu and to facilitate the import of breeding animals and their genetic material, while ensuring the sustainability of breeding and conservation programmes for genetic resources and thus for all breeds existing in europe today. i welcome the commission's simplification work and i vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report which envisages the grouping of all the directives relating to the zootechnical legislation for bovine, porcine, ovine, caprine and equine species into a single, simpler and more harmonised horizontal directive. the new regulation will facilitate the free trade of high-quality breeding animals and their germinal material by contributing to the preservation of animal breeds across the eu and by improving cooperation between the competent authorities of the different member states in this regard. moreover, the regulation will be clearer and more consistent, thanks to a more precise and defined wording. the report also introduces simplified rules on official controls and special provisions for rare or endangered breeds and the equine sector.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this report because the phenomenon of migration is the consequence of epochal geopolitical changes which we cannot stop, but which the european union must address by setting priorities in dealing with a situation which is no longer an emergency. priority of method, priority of content: we must move forward together and have a european approach, we cannot continue to see, every day more, even member states erecting walls and putting up barbed wire and others who are instead engaged in search and rescue at sea of migrants, and then content because i come from sicily, which is one of those regions that sees the lifeless bodies of men, women and children coming to its shores and turning schools into morgues. the dublin review provides for the creation of a single asylum system with centralised handling of applications at european level, automatic and effective relocation of migrants to all european countries and safe returns; that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ according to data provided by frontex, in 2015 1.83 million people attempted to cross the external borders of the european union. this is an unprecedented figure, the result of an international situation characterized by wars, severe imbalances and instability which threaten the lives of millions of people. in this context, it is clear that the current asylum system is not able to provide an adequate solution. i supported the metsola and kyenge reports because i strongly share the need to think holistically about the management of migration flows. the revision of the dublin system must be given priority, and provision must be made for the establishment of hotspots from which to start distributing asylum seekers on the basis of a pre-established system of quotas for each member state. the aim should be to draw up new agreements at community level on readmission, so that member states can only return migrants if their country of origin is considered safe. article 80 tfeu puts the principles of solidarity and fair sharing of responsibility at the heart of the whole union system, and italy and greece cannot be left alone.
