in writing. ‒ the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality are enshrined in article 5 of the treaty on european union (teu) and protocol no 2 to the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu). their value is not merely formal: the principle of subsidiarity and the principle of proportionality govern the exercise of the competences of the european union. in areas where the eu does not have exclusive competence, the principle of subsidiarity is intended to protect the decision-making and action capacity of the member states and local communities, and at the same time it serves to legitimize union intervention if the objectives of an action cannot be sufficiently achieved by the member states but can, 'by reason of the scale or effects of the action in question', be better achieved at union level. the incorporation of this principle into the european treaties was therefore intended to bring the exercise of powers as close as possible to the citizen: the commission's approach to these matters is therefore regrettable, and it is often bureaucratic and redundant. it is in the european parliament's interest to bring the institutions closer to the citizens by concentrating eu action on macro-issues of common interest, limiting its own regulatory over-enlargement and practising the principles of federal institutions: no man is enough by himself, not even european officials.
in writing. ‒ the own-initiative report in question is absolutely positive. the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality as laid down in article 5 of the treaty on european union are the basis of the legislative activity of the brussels institutions and their observance, especially for a political group like ours, is fundamental. for this reason, since the text of the legal affairs committee is very strict towards the european commission, we cannot but support it with a positive vote. the s&d group is proposing a whole series of amendments which seek to reduce the prerogatives of the member states (which we will vote against). the report stresses the important role of national parliaments and suggests that in future the possibility for national legislators to opt out of the eu's respect for the principle of subsidiarity could be further simplified, perhaps with more time available. it is also stressed that the treaties provide for the exception to the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality only at the beginning of the legislative procedure, whereas it would be desirable for national parliaments to be able to express their views also at later stages of the sometimes lengthy codecision procedure.
in writing. ‒ article 5 of the treaty on european union states that the exercise of eu competences should be guided by the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality, so it is important to encourage greater participation and involvement of national parliaments in the european legislative process in order to achieve the same political results together, avoiding fragmentation. the involvement of citizens, who unfortunately still do not feel that the european union is close to their needs, is also essential. i therefore vote in favour of mr karim's report, and i hope that political dialogue will be improved, not just in the case of yellow or orange cards, but as a general rule.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the 2012 and 2013 annual reports on subsidiarity and proportionality because it contains some unacceptable proposals. the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality are guiding principles for the european union's action and the validity, effectiveness and efficiency of the policies implemented depend on their proper application. this should not, however, allow national parliaments to overstep their powers and conflict with the prerogatives of the eu's legislative bodies. the proposal for a 'green card' procedure, which would allow national parliaments, after securing the support of the european parliament, to make constructive proposals to be submitted to the commission, should therefore be rejected. the proposal to introduce an interim evaluation after the start of the adoption procedure and at the end of the legislative process, with the possibility of warning member states which do not respect the principle of subsidiarity, should also be rejected. it represents an unnecessary burden on the procedure and a harmful control by the eu of the member states in the exercise of their prerogatives.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the ep resolution on the 2012 and 2013 annual reports on subsidiarity and proportionality because i did not agree with the report's structure and the approach given by the rapporteur. i believe that the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality are absolute values, since they govern the union's action by ensuring effectiveness and efficiency and by allowing a fair balance between institutional levels: i am therefore convinced that i support the balance achieved in the negotiations on the treaties. i do not, however, agree with an overly broad interpretation of these principles, which would end up weakening the union and its legislative action at a time of crisis and increasingly complex challenges, to which we therefore want a strong and just europe that makes life better for citizens. i did not agree, among other things, with the introduction of a green card and a red card for national parliaments and with the extension of the control of national parliaments both during and at the end of the legislative process, which are in the opposite direction. they risk paralysing the union's action and slowing down the european decision-making process, going in the opposite direction to the recent interinstitutional agreement on better regulation. for all these reasons, i have therefore decided to reject the report as proposed by the rapporteur.
in writing. i have decided to support mr karim's report on the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality, which are relevant to the whole interinstitutional context. these principles form an integral part of the policy framework and aim to determine whether eu action is capable of developing better policy objectives than national or even regional policies. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 26 to supplement this regulation by laying down detailed rules for the application of this regulation. the introduction of the 'green card' which would allow national parliaments to propose the introduction, amendment or repeal of eu legislation and the 'red card' which envisages the extension of the period for consultation of national parliaments under the subsidiarity control and the introduction of a stronger procedure. in the light of the above, i believe that the matter deserves further intervention and measures to increase its potential, and i also believe that the commission must make every effort to ensure that its dialogue with each of the national parliaments is suitable for strengthening its dialogue with them.

in writing. ‒ we reject the 2012-13 annual report on subsidiarity and proportionality. subsidiarity is a key principle of the european union, which aims to define, in a relevant way, the areas of competence shared between the union and the member states. introduced in 1992 by the maastricht treaty, it also helps to establish the union's exclusive competences. the principle of proportionality is a necessary corollary to the definition of the limits of community action and the prerogatives of the member states. it is therefore essential that these principles be respected. the report does not go in the direction we hoped for, unfortunately, and it introduces several controversial elements which are not in line with our view of the relationship between the member states and the european union. the socialist and democratic group in the european parliament believes in a strong and united europe, capable of acting in the interests of its citizens to improve the quality of life and our community institutions. this report does not follow the directions given by our group. that is why i am voting against.

in writing. ‒ with today's vote, parliament reaffirms that the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality are fundamental guiding principles for the european union. the two european commission reports of 2012 and 2013 examine how the two principles in question have been implemented by the various european institutions. in particular, national parliaments, which have a stronger territorial impact, should be more closely involved in the eu legislative process and subsidiarity checks. on this last point, i would argue that in addition to the impact assessments that are usually drawn up at the beginning of the legislative procedure, further assessments should be carried out both at the intermediate stage, at the end of the legislative process and before the adoption of a final text, in order to ensure that subsidiarity and proportionality are respected. i therefore supported the report with my vote in favour, convinced that closer scrutiny by the european and national institutions will make it possible to take legislative action more efficiently, avoiding unnecessary regulatory burdens and bringing tangible benefits to citizens.
in writing. ‒ the principle of subsidiarity and proportionality are cornerstones of the european construction, since they frame the action of the european union in its relations with the member states. under the former, in areas not falling within the eu's exclusive competence, the eu acts only if and to the extent that the objectives of the action in question cannot be achieved by the member states, at central, regional or local level, and, in accordance with the latter, such action cannot go beyond what is necessary to achieve the objectives laid down in the treaties. the application of these two principles to eu actions and policies has over time enabled the creation of the internal market with freedoms of movement and progressive economic and political integration, which progressive forces continue to pursue. unfortunately, the annual reports on the application of the two principles voted on today support a eurosceptic and misleading view, as they propose to introduce a series of procedures to limit eu legislative action in an instrumental way and beyond the conditions provided for by the provisions of the treaties on the basis of the principles mentioned. for these reasons i have voted against the report as a whole.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the annual report on subsidiarity and proportionality. in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, in areas not falling within the union's exclusive competence, action should be taken only if the objectives of the proposed action cannot be achieved by the member states. the principle of proportionality, which applies to all union action, requires that any union action does not go beyond what is necessary to achieve the objectives of the treaties. i firmly believe in a europe that can act and improve the lives of its citizens. this report is not compatible with that objective.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this important report on european regulation, supporting in particular paragraph 47. parliament reiterated to the european commission the principle of 'thinking of smes first' and pointed to them as the reference point for eu policies (since they account for 95% of european industry and production). the vote in favour of paragraph 47 also has a first practical effect for the whole agri-food chain: parliament called on the commission to review the part of regulation (ec) no 1924/2006 which gives the go-ahead to highly punitive labelling for a large number of quality products (pdo, pgi, gts). the regulation would have catalogued foods according to their fat, sugar and salt content, thus providing partial and incorrect information, and classifying a large number of products of the mediterranean diet as harmful to health by introducing new 'nutritional profiles' (the famous 'traffic light labelling' already in use in the united kingdom), with the risk of justifying additional taxation. parliament thus reaffirmed that the correctness of food information to consumers is not improved by implementing existing rules, such as regulation (eu) no 1169/2011, according to which information must be mandatory and complete.
in writing. ‒ the report voted on today on regulatory adequacy and effectiveness aims to underline the importance of legislation that is of quality, meets citizens' expectations and avoids excessive red tape. in this connection, it was called for the concept of nutritional profile to be eliminated, as it was considered redundant and unnecessary, in order to avoid unjustified discrimination against food of mediterranean origin and to avoid negative consequences for the competitiveness of the european agri-food sector. nutrition profiles, in fact, require that foods be classified according to their nutritional composition, and thus according to their salt, sugar and fat content, without taking into account how these foods are actually associated with each other. this type of classification, in addition to having no scientific basis, greatly penalizes the excellence and italian products, paradoxically labeled as "bad food", causing great damage to agri-food enterprises. i therefore voted in favour of the report, hoping that the elimination of the distorted concept of nutritional profile will ensure the safety of our products and the protection of our production.

in writing. ‒ the whole concept of nutritional profiles needs to be reviewed and possibly eliminated. the nutritional profiles are not useful to the consumer and their scientific basis is questionable. nutritional profiles could justify 'traffic light' labelling, which distorts the market and misleads consumers into classifying foods as good or bad. there is no such thing as good or bad food, but there is such a thing as good or bad diet. protecting health means promoting a proper lifestyle by combating the abuse, not the use, of food. the traffic light labelling may be detrimental to the excellent italian products which form the basis of the mediterranean diet, recognised as one of the most complete and balanced. protecting health means promoting a healthy lifestyle and a varied and balanced diet, educating on the right use and avoiding abuse, not misleading the consumer into classifying individual foods as good or bad on the basis of traffic light labelling.
in writing. refit is the programme whose stated aim is to reduce the costs of regulation and red tape. i have defended paragraph 47 of the report in order to prevent the introduction of traffic light labels on products with a high calorific value. the traffic light labelling system is extremely misleading because it focuses only on the amounts of fat, sugar and salt contained in the product. under this system, a flagship of our made in like olive oil would be labeled as harmful, with a big red badge. in contrast, lab-made chemical drinks with low levels of sugar and fat would have a nice green badge. it is not necessary to have scientific knowledge, but only common sense to understand the absurdity of these labels. this system would be a disaster for consumers and for serious businesses. i therefore fought to eliminate any future attempt to create an english-style traffic light label by voting in favour of the paragraph. however, in other areas the report was not sufficiently clear on the impact that a rapid deregulation can have on consumer rights, so i abstained on the final vote.

in writing. ‒ the proper functioning of the single market is one of the vital aspects of the future of the european union and remains an important aspect of the life of the union: each eu institution has a co-responsibility for improving its own legislation. improving regulation does not mean eliminating it, nor does it mean making it less ambitious in terms of environmental protection, consumer protection, safety, quality or social legislation. it means the elimination of redundant rules, red tape and negative effects, as well as the achievement of strategic objectives and the creation of a harmonious regulatory environment in support of employment and business in europe. we must understand that the realisation of a rationally regulated single market does not impose excessive burdens or impede production, innovation and trade: it is a structure that will stimulate growth in europe. it is in this context that shared responsibility can lead to common benefits: a strong and dynamic single market that can contribute to sustainable and long-term growth in europe and thus to the prosperity of its citizens. the european parliament has a moral obligation not to delegate this responsibility to other institutional bodies.
in writing. ‒ the problem with reports like this, which were approved by the committee on the internal market, is that, in addition to the absolutely agreeable points, they contain whole paragraphs which we cannot politically approve. it should be remembered that the internal market and consumer protection are not the exclusive competence of the european institutions, but are shared with the national parliaments. for this reason, respect for the principle of subsidiarity is always a central issue. in our view, the van bossuyt report could have done more to protect the prerogatives of the member states. not only is this not the case, but in some instances the member states are accused of not applying the single market rules correctly or too late. in addition, the report contains statements which, in our opinion, speak excessively of the internal market as a potential driving force for the economy. the facts show that this is not entirely true, but on the contrary, internal market rules create problems for our production system. this example alone is enough to illustrate the problems of transposing the services directive (the so-called bolkestein directive) into italian law. of course, it would be excessive to vote against this report. the text also contains passages that can be shared. i abstain from voting.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the eurobarometer data are a wake-up call for us. almost half of europeans, 40%, admit that they have no real knowledge of the european union, 50% are convinced that europe is really distant and that their voice and interests do not count in the european union. these figures on the perception of the relationship between citizens and the union are then translated into reality, with massive abstentions - the last one we saw that concerns us, in which only 42% of the voters voted. and even more serious is the spread and success of populist anti-european movements which use a simplistic communication that is easily understood by those who do not know europe. i voted in favour of the report because it is essential to go beyond erasmus and to include the union at all levels of education in order to form a new european civic consciousness, to form european citizens who know what a huge opportunity europe really is.
in writing. ‒ the report develops the issue of the institutional structure and activities of the eu in schools in a positive way, highlighting that an eu dimension in education should not only allow for the acquisition of knowledge and the development of a sense of belonging to the union and european citizenship, but also foster critical reflection on the current eu; it also stresses the need to address and close the growing gap between the voice of citizens and the institutions of the european union. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the drăghici report entitled 'learning about the eu at school'. this is an important text, closely linked to the sense of distance which too often characterizes the relationship between citizens and the european institutions. according to a 2014 eurobarometer report, 44 per cent of citizens feel they have limited knowledge of the european institutions, and 52 per cent feel they have no say in its institutional dynamics. these are worrying figures which call for coordinated action to strengthen the sense of belonging and the construction of european identity. the report proposes a european dimension to education, which would involve greater attention to the construction of europe, citizenship education and the history and culture of the continent. many member states have already integrated parts of the curriculum devoted to the study of europe, but there is still a long way to go. it is important that the institutions, and in particular the commission, devote resources to all those projects and platforms such as erasmus+, etwinning, the school education gateway and epale that can foster a genuine education for european citizenship. only then can euroscepticism be defeated.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this document because i believe that the knowledge of the population about the european union is extremely limited and lacking and i therefore believe that it is important that children and young people can come into contact with the european universe from an early age.
in writing. ‒ between economic crisis, democratic deficit and difficulties in bringing european citizens closer to institutional mechanisms that seem increasingly distant and abstract, the european union is today in a very precarious situation, immersed in pluralistic societies whose different components also show a growing discomfort in inter-relating and understanding each other. in this delicate context, we strongly support the resolution on 'learning about the european union at school', which aims to encourage the reintroduction of a greater european dimension in national curricula, which are often too heterogeneous from one country to another, and the promotion of training tools (including, in particular, the erasmus+ programmes, europe for citizens, creative europe or virtual platforms such as etwinning, epale, school education gateway and teacher's corner) capable of improving language skills and promoting greater knowledge of european history, values and decision-making mechanisms. we hope, moreover, that this will further encourage the development of a healthy critical sense on the part of teachers and students, which will facilitate, by promoting renewal, a greater understanding of the european union and will help to develop and consolidate a european citizenship and identity.
in writing. ‒ a report that is totally instrumentalised not in favour of quality education, which of course also teaches our recent history and therefore the european union, but in favour of uncritical support for the eu. i vote against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on 'learning about the eu at school' because i believe it is essential to give school education across the union a uniform 'european dimension'. in order to build a genuine european identity, it is necessary that students - citizens of the union - acquire from school age the knowledge of how the union's institutions work and learn to think critically about european issues. however, it is also essential to avoid disparities within member states in the integration of the eu dimension in school education, and this reasoning concerns not only curricula (often fragmentary and lacking complementarity with other subjects taught), but also teacher training, textbooks (which do not always give the right emphasis to eu themes) and teaching methods (by introducing examples of the relevance of the eu in the daily lives of students). for its part, the eu will have to continue its work to promote language skills, active citizenship, cultural awareness and intercultural understanding through continued financial support and wider access to mobility opportunities.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text focusing on learning about the eu in school. i agree that an eu dimension in education should enable students not only to acquire knowledge and develop a sense of belonging and european citizenship, but also to engage in critical reflection on the eu, studying its core values, and in particular the rule of law and human rights, its governance and decision-making processes and how they affect the member states.
in writing. ‒ the european union is experiencing perhaps the most difficult and complex period in its history, not only because of the continuing economic and social crisis, but also because of the loss of confidence of citizens in the institutions and in the european project, which had its deepest roots in citizenship and membership of europe. the limited knowledge of the functioning and role of the union among citizens fuels the detachment and makes complex decision-making processes appear undemocratic and opaque. we must start again from school and education. many member states have progressively integrated the eu dimension into school curricula and teacher training and this is the way forward. programmes such as erasmus have helped young people to develop a strong sense of belonging and european citizenship, and it is on this type of action that the union must continue to focus in the future. the commission will also continue to support the development of the european union's digital platforms and networks, such as etwinning, epale, the school education gateway and teachers' corner, which provide access to high-quality, up-to-date material to give young people useful tools to learn about the eu. i believe strongly in the role of education and education in rediscovering values and the role of institutions. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it aims to improve the dialogue between the european union and our schools, which is a clear step forward towards better european integration. i believe that the union offers endless possibilities and that it is our task to make all citizens aware of their rights and duties by educating them from the outset and preparing them to be citizens of a complex and globalised world. education in this sense can only broaden one's knowledge and values by helping to form a critical and informed mind so that one can exercise one's rights in the best way. i believe that such education can only encourage intercultural dialogue, helping to combat discrimination and strengthen citizenship, and further reducing the existing gap between citizens and europe.

in writing. ‒ the european dimension of school education needs to be strengthened to enable students not only to acquire knowledge and develop a sense of belonging and european citizenship, but also to engage them in critical reflection on the eu and its fundamental values, enshrined in article 2 teu, in particular the recognition of the rule of law and respect for human rights. the report's criticism of the union's democratic deficits, which is manifested in a growing gap between the voice of the citizens and the eu institutions, is entirely acceptable. in this respect, it is of fundamental importance to re-establish a close link with citizens, through their greater involvement in the democratic decision-making process. we also share the need to strengthen the study of civic education to enable students to think critically and form informed and balanced opinions, by strengthening active and responsible citizenship and encouraging intercultural and interreligious dialogue and the exercise of democratic rights and responsibilities, including the right to vote.

in writing. ‒ i strongly supported the ep resolution 'learning about the eu at school', because today the european union is facing a difficult and long economic crisis which is also having serious effects on europe's political stability and on the union's founding values. the concept of a european dimension in education is essential to raise the awareness of students in the union of the importance of developing a european culture of values which takes into account the study of languages and youth mobility and the system of coordination between educational institutions. given the low level of knowledge of the european union among citizens, learning in schools could be a driving force for the cultural and civic dissemination of european values, through the introduction of a specific subject such as citizenship education. despite the tools already available to the european union and the member states to promote intercultural dialogue, greater efforts are needed to ensure financial support for wider access to the opportunities offered by the eu.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it recognises one of the main challenges that the european union has not yet solved, namely the concept of identity. the economic crisis and the resulting crisis of representativeness have made this area of reflection on europe more slippery, requiring a rethinking of the instruments for integrating and democratizing ideas. education plays a key role in the attempt to recreate a european public space and to restore citizens' confidence in the relevance and inevitability of this process. in practical terms, promoting european education means providing for the teaching and dissemination of the languages of the member states, strengthening measures to promote the mobility of students and teachers, and encouraging cooperation between educational establishments. the union can also promote the exchange of information on member states' education systems and best practices, and encourage civic engagement and participation of young people in democratic life in europe. the pillars of this european education process must be, on the one hand, the acquisition of knowledge of european geography, history and culture, and the functioning of its institutions; the commission's proposal is to be adopted by the council on the basis of a proposal from the commission.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this report because i believe that erasmus, because of what it has built up over the years, because of the people it is aimed at, because of what it represents, is indeed one of the effective ways out of the economic crisis, but even more so because it is a consciousness that invests in europe. strengthening erasmus means supporting our students, our professionals, but also supporting culture in a europe which today seems to be entirely economic in its vocation. there are key areas, however, which still need improvement and on which work can be done: the economic capacity of students to benefit from mobility, for example, because many do not have the resources that erasmus does not finance; the recognition of educational credits; the inclusion of trainees in the programmes; access to the world of work after the training experience. these are some of the knots that must be untied as soon as possible in order to spread as widely as possible the europe that we like and that european citizens especially like.
in writing. ‒ the report as a whole has positive aspects, but these are countered by the timidity with which it addresses the failure of the eu's tools to date to tackle the very high levels of youth unemployment, the widening gaps in socioeconomic protection and labour rights for young people, and early school leaving. all socioeconomic barriers to equality, including those relating to education and vocational training, must be addressed. moreover, these results cannot be expected to be achieved by persevering with the logic that has hitherto guided economic governance in the eu or by not clearly indicating that instruments such as the youth guarantee and the youth employment initiative have failed to achieve the objectives for which they were designed. for these reasons i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the introduction of the erasmus+ programme, which replaced the previous mobility programmes, has represented an important development and simplification, allowing more and more european citizens, especially young people, to benefit from important learning experiences in another eu country. however, there is still a structural deficit in the relationship between training and work, which is reflected in a reduced mobility for vocational training studies. the maragall report, which i supported with my vote today, effectively highlights the relationship between employability and mobility, providing guidance on how to implement policies which encourage the exploitation of mobility opportunities by those involved in vocational education and training. the main way is to remove the obstacles affecting certain groups of citizens which prevent them from appreciating all the direct and indirect benefits of training experiences in another member state. the commission and the member states must strengthen the role of intermediary, territorial and sectoral institutions involved in the management, preparation and control of mobility, while encouraging cofinancing schemes for training centres which are coherent, complementary and well coordinated.
in writing. ‒ the erasmus generation is probably the most tangible result of the sense of belonging to the european family. for 29 years, europe has been enabling students to broaden their horizons and increase their skills by spending a period of their university studies abroad. as in the case of education, vocational training-oriented mobility is now crucial for the integration of young people into the labour market, making the erasmus+ programme a valuable tool that needs to be strengthened. the employment objective of the 2020 strategy also addresses these aspects, posing the challenge of reducing the number of neets (non-educational and non-trained) and reducing the 'skill mismatch', the mismatch between skills possessed and those required by the market. in this sense, the erasmus+ programme offers enormous opportunities: the aim of the project is to develop a european network of trainers and trainers in the field of vocational training. however, there are many challenges, particularly in terms of recognition of acquired skills, the lack of compatibility of training in home countries with programmes abroad and language barriers. we need to work to make erasmus+ more flexible. i therefore strongly supported the text presented by mr maragall.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this document because i believe that it is important, in order to try to solve the employment crisis that has affected the younger generations in the european union, to develop to the maximum the potential of those instruments, such as erasmus+, which promote mobility in vocational education and training.
in writing. ‒ in a context of increasing difficulties for students and young people to integrate adequately into the european labour market, high school drop-out rates and significant differences in the economic and productive systems of the different member states, it is necessary to encourage the development of european programmes capable of promoting the relaunch of the international mobility of young workers, students and teachers and the resources dedicated to them, as essential factors that can facilitate access to stable and quality employment and can facilitate a better adaptation of the workforce to current socioeconomic developments. in particular, particular attention should be paid to developing mechanisms for the recognition of skills acquired through work and exchange programmes, to encouraging the creation of a comprehensive framework capable of adequately presenting existing mobility opportunities to potential beneficiaries, and to harmonising and coordinating existing programmes (such as erasmus+ and the esf), with a view to those most disadvantaged social groups often excluded from such initiatives, which are extremely important, not least for strengthening the sense of belonging to the european project.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report is distinguished by a serious and pragmatic approach to the vast world of training and the challenges/critical issues of this historical period. we support the rapporteur's line, which, as we have been advocating for some time in the school sector, points to the need for greater integration between the world of school and the world of work. the emphasis on the importance of vocational education (especially in a world like ours) makes us appreciate the report even more. that is why we recommend a vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today to ensure that the european resources allocated to erasmus+ and to vocational education and training (vet) programmes are increased and proportionate to the number and needs of potential beneficiaries of the mobility offered by these programmes. i call on the member states to promote bilateral agreements that complement the actions promoted by erasmus+ and the european fp5 programmes, in order to strengthen the mobility of young europeans. it is also necessary to facilitate the implementation of mobility under the erasmus+ programme by taking actions to increase the success rate of applications, by simplifying the use of electronic tools for mobility management, by organising awareness-raising campaigns on the value of mobility programmes in all educational establishments in the union and by providing more targeted information and training to beneficiaries and intermediaries of programmes and actions, including school and university staff. as regards vocational education and training (vet) programmes, i believe that the commission and the member states should increase their visibility and access in order to remove barriers, particularly in the sectors most affected by youth unemployment and for low-skilled workers.
in writing. ‒ in this resolution, parliament calls for better use of the erasmus+ programme to increase the mobility of young trainees and students during vocational training. however, while calling on the commission and the member states to ensure that adequate resources are allocated to the youth guarantee and the youth employment initiative for the entire 2014-2020 programming period, i found that the report only emphasises their importance and does not clearly point to their failure to meet the proposed targets and to the inadequacy of these measures and those taken overall to adequately address the very high youth unemployment and the widening gaps in socio-economic protection and labour rights for young people. that is why i have abstained on the final vote.
in writing. ‒ mobility, promoted by the erasmus+ programme, has given young europeans the opportunity to train in another eu country and has undoubtedly actively contributed to their personal, cultural and professional growth. the encounter with different cultures, languages, working and educational methods has strengthened the sense of belonging and european citizenship. the potential of mobility programmes, in particular erasmus+, is not only for training and education but also for the world of work, as they broaden the employment prospects for young people. the specific occupational profiles required today require careful selection of applicants to match supply and demand in order to make mobility a real tool for job placement. the experience gained from the programme should encourage the commission and the member states to identify complementary and shared measures between the european social fund and the erasmus+ programme in order to enhance their impact and ensure economic sustainability. this is the way we have to think if we want mobility programmes to be sufficiently comprehensive to ensure that the widest possible range of beneficiaries benefit from the opportunities provided. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ this report highlights one of the many advantages that europe offers, so it was my duty to speak in favour of it. i am in favour of the erasmus+ programme, as of all international mobility programmes, because it allows anyone, students, graduates and not, to live, express themselves and relate in an increasingly wider international context. it is a unique opportunity for cultural growth, which promotes knowledge of foreign languages and the ability to communicate, to act, to decide and to adapt to new situations, all of which are fundamental today and which represent specific needs in an increasingly dynamic, international and competitive labour market. i therefore felt it was natural to support such international exchanges because they lead, in my view, to advanced vocational training which can only encourage, support and enrich our countries by providing greater opportunities for professional development and by strengthening cooperation between the various member states. such international projects, involving such close cooperation between often very different countries, are often complex to implement, so i am pleased that this report represents an important step forward in promoting international mobility.
in writing. ‒ mobility within the european area in the field of higher education needs to be strengthened in all member states. in fact, even as a result of the economic crisis since 2008, there has been a structural deficit in programmes relating to mobility and more particularly in the relationship between training and employment: in some regions, unemployment rates are close to zero, while in others, the level of inactivity is above 40% among the youngest, who in many cases have not had the opportunity to complete secondary education or vocational training. rather, an ambitious and concrete offer of mobility would be an integral part of any overall strategy for economic recovery and reducing youth unemployment levels. a framework should be created which presents the possibilities available to students in a simple and clear way. to adopt complementary and shared measures between the european social fund and the erasmus+ programme; define programmes to remove obstacles and create the most favourable environment for the success of mobility initiatives; support the transition between mobility and work, consolidating the fight for the recognition of studies and skills.
in writing. ‒ the report calls on the eu and all member states to address the limitations that prevent equal access for all to vet education and training opportunities. erasmus is without doubt one of the most successful programmes in europe, with more than three million people having chosen to study or teach abroad since its inception in 1987. the report calls for improvements to existing programmes and initiatives in terms of accessibility, openness and inclusion. it is obvious that in erasmus programmes it is necessary to ensure that traineeships remain training opportunities and do not replace professional positions, as is still too often the case. there are criticisms in the report, the measures taken to deal with the enormous youth unemployment and the widening gap in socioeconomic protection and labour rights for young people are not described. i have noted many positive aspects of the report, but also many shortcomings, and i therefore vote for abstention.
in writing. ‒ the eu's mobility programmes are without doubt one of the eu's greatest successes. every year, through mobility programmes such as erasmus+, more and more european citizens choose to study, gain work experience or work for a few months in an eu country or partner country other than their own. the erasmus+ programme has proven to be a tool that strengthens intercultural dialogue and tolerance, while at the same time enabling participants to acquire new skills, both personally and professionally. although erasmus+ can be considered a success, some obstacles to participation remain. many europeans continue to associate the programme mainly with post-secondary education. in fact, the programme also provides opportunities for citizens who want to gain professional experience or are already engaged in a professional activity. in addition, the numerous administrative procedures may hinder participation. finally, while equal access to education is a right promoted by the eu, significant socioeconomic barriers still exist which unfortunately limit the number of participants. i therefore voted in favour of parliament's resolution which promotes mobility in education and vocational training to enable more european citizens to participate in such rewarding experiences.
in writing. ‒ the resolution we adopted today focuses on the importance of a common european area of education focused on mobility, which is of great value for the development of european identity and for the strengthening of a sense of community citizenship. the report reminds us that education, as a fundamental human right, must be easily accessible to all and that in this regard we must make a concrete commitment to remove all socioeconomic barriers which prevent equal access to opportunities for european mobility. as the maragall report points out, i think that the erasmus+ programme is a great opportunity for students and trainees to experience life abroad, as it allows them to develop a common european citizenship and conscience. i therefore voted in favour of the resolution because i believe that it is essential to invest in education and to increase the visibility of mobility programmes in order to remove cultural barriers, reduce youth unemployment and create a deeper european identity.
in writing. ‒ while the report in question has some positive aspects, such as the recognition of education as a fundamental human right and a public good to which everyone must have equal access, it also has some critical elements. in particular, there is a lack of clear denunciation of the failure of the youth guarantee programme and the youth employment initiative to meet the proposed objectives. in particular, there is no mention of the inadequacy of these measures and of those taken overall to deal adequately with the very high youth unemployment and the widening gaps in socioeconomic protection and labour rights for young people. in the final analysis, our opinion of the resolution cannot be entirely favourable.
