in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep resolution on erasmus plus and other tools to promote mobility in the field of fpis a lifelong learning approach - because the erasmus plus programme, which replaces all the different programmes previously implemented, promotes a simpler understanding of the opportunities offered by the european union to young people, as well as the concept of intercultural mobility in higher education. however, the economic disparities existing within the member states and the different development models which create many difficulties in the full implementation of these programmes cannot be overstated. there are situations of severe social crisis caused by the inability to provide employment opportunities for thousands of young people and other situations where there is a lack of qualified young people for a particular production segment. for all these reasons, i believe it is essential to set more far-sighted and ambitious objectives and to define strategies which meet the conditions for the flexibility and operation of education and production systems.
in writing. i support the motion for a resolution to encourage student mobility both in academic and vocational training. we are increasingly seeing a successful erasmus programme, which has started sustainable mobility of young students and enabled the exchange of experiences and the development of skills essential for their academic and professional growth. these skills are most in demand in the increasingly competitive professional sector. i therefore believe that it is essential to promote erasmus+ more generally, but above all professional mobility, which has unfortunately not shown the same positive results as educational mobility. we need to optimise the transition from school to work and erasmus is the right tool to do this.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the report on erasmus+ and other instruments to promote mobility in the field of fpis - a lifelong learning approach. education is a fundamental right which must be accessible to all, taking into account also the needs of people who are victims of different forms of discrimination. learning and training mobility is of primary importance for personal development and helps to contribute to high quality education. learning and vocational training systems need to be made more efficient and accessible, by broadening and improving mobility opportunities, increasing financial resources, removing barriers, so as to contribute to european integration and strengthening the idea of citizenship.
in writing. ‒ we need to do more to end youth unemployment by giving our young people the skills they need for the 21st century economy. in doing so, we must above all promote education and training for non-traditional skills for girls, in order to end discrimination in employment opportunities, close the wage gap. this resolution is an opportunity to resolve these problems as soon as possible, and i have therefore expressed my support for it.
in writing. ‒ i take this opportunity to contribute to the debate by highlighting the achievements already achieved by the region i represent: the region of lombardy. the lombardy region has already responded over the last three years to the concerns we are discussing today. there are personalised work training courses "study in the firm and find a job at school". an interesting combination, which sees a regional law dedicated to the dual system, apprenticeship and internationalisation, giving substance to the school-work alternation (the first region to follow up on the national law 107/2015). the investment in new technologies for all students (web generation) is also important. international mobility and lifelong learning are the two cornerstones of the lombard education system. the regional institutional level is crucial in order to ensure personalised tools and pathways. non-formal skills are the basis of a growth pathway that must accompany institutionalised learning. in the absence of this complementarity, young people risk not seeing the link between their training and the labour market. we must promote a system of recognition of these skills: the only ones that can make a difference are the legal value of the degree itself.
in writing. ‒ we fully support the maragall report which aims to promote the erasmus+ programme and to improve the concept of mobility within the european area. we consider the experience of the leonardo programme, as well as that of the ecvet and europass programmes, to be positive and we consider that it should be continued. vocational training must not be a secondary concern to university education; it is a fundamental tool in the fight against inequalities, offering young people the tools to make a difference in terms of employability and personal fulfilment. we believe that it is in the interest of the member states to support international mobility programmes effectively, also in the context of a comprehensive strategy for economic recovery and the fight against youth unemployment. it is therefore essential to facilitate the mutual recognition between member states of the different pathways and qualifications related to vocational training and, more generally, to remove as far as possible obstacles to international mobility. finally, we believe that it is essential for enterprises to contribute to reducing the gap between the skills required by the world of work and those offered by the education system. we hope that strong cooperation between business and education will strengthen and support mobility programmes.
in writing. ‒ the previous leonardo programme successfully completed the first phase of exchanges and stays for the purpose of studying and working in countries other than the country of residence. its successor, erasmus+, has brought a considerable step forward for the concept of mobility within the european higher education area but at the same time, by compacting everything into a single subject, a structural deficit in the programmes relating to mobility and specifically in the relationship between training and employment has become apparent. i have spoken in favour of this measure, which aims to set more ambitious objectives, both quantitative and qualitative, for some of the lines of activity envisaged by the erasmus+ programme, such as speeding up the completion of the procedures for recognition, accreditation and quality assessment, which should be the common framework for all member states.
in writing. ‒ the differences between member states in curricula and management of schools make it difficult to mobilise young people at european level and require european action which is not only fully applicable to the various national school systems but also respects the educational specificities of each country. all the european initiatives for intra-european mobility for study and work purposes are brought together in a single macro-programme (erasmus plus). however, it noted that the establishment of the erasmus plus programme, while a step forward, had at the same time caused a slowdown in mobility for vocational training. given the existence in some geographical areas of a large gap between the skills and abilities possessed and those required by the market, an ambitious offer of mobility for both categories therefore appears necessary to reduce the high rate of youth unemployment in europe. in view of the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy of creating more jobs and promoting global competitiveness, i thought it appropriate to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i consider that learning and training mobility is extremely important for the socioeconomic inclusion of young people, personal development and the strengthening of multicultural dialogue. the challenges in this regard are many, given the unemployment rate across the union, the need to make lifelong learning and vocational education and training systems not only more efficient but also more accessible and inclusive for disadvantaged groups and people with special needs remains high. in other words, mobility must be facilitated in order to enhance its attractiveness and to balance access opportunities to professional positions in order to generate positive effects on social cohesion and the quality of the labour market. education is a basic human right and a public good and must therefore be accessible on an equal footing. the commission and the member states must work to remove cultural and socio-economic barriers to ensure that fdi programmes are accessible to all citizens without discrimination, and to increase the capacity of women in fields such as science, technology, engineering and mathematics to reduce the current skills and representation gap in these fields.
in writing. ‒ the erasmus+ programme was created to replace several previous programmes. while the adoption of the erasmus+ programme has brought a significant step forward for the concept of mobility within the european higher education area, it is also important to note the specific weight of mobility in terms of vocational training studies. the previous leonardo programme had successfully completed the first phase of exchanges and stays for the purpose of studying and working in countries other than the country of residence. but the consolidation of all these into a single programme and the fallout from the economic crisis have revealed a structural deficit in programmes relating to mobility and in particular in the relationship between training and employment. i voted in favour of this report in order to allow the new strategies envisaged in the erasmus+ programme to offer maximum flexibility, to adapt to very different realities and to facilitate coordination and maximum operationality in the service of mobility, which is conceived as a useful tool for promoting employment and social inclusion.
in writing. ‒ we abstained on the report on the promotion of mobility in vocational education and training (vet). we believe that high unemployment is even more dramatic and worrying for certain particular categories such as young people and women. this calls for determined action at european level, starting with lifelong learning programmes such as erasmus+. we recognize that, in general, the report proposes good measures to strengthen these programmes, with the aim of eliminating all socioeconomic and linguistic barriers. we voted in favour of those paragraphs that called for greater coordination with civil society in the programming phase, decent working conditions and pay for students and trainees, and a focus of vet on areas such as the circular economy, sustainable mobility and decarbonisation. however, we believe that the report does not take a sufficiently firm position in condemning the failure of the measures taken so far to combat youth unemployment and in excluding the fossil fuel energy sectors and the companies operating in them from the ifp programming. in view of these serious criticisms, which jeopardise the promotion of a truly equitable, sustainable and future-oriented access to mobility in vet, we did not vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ learning and training mobility is important for personal development, social inclusion of young people, multicultural dialogue, tolerance, the ability to work in an intercultural environment and active citizenship have clearly demonstrated potential for high quality education and occupational skills. in particular, i welcome the call in the report to the commission, the member states and public employment services to implement the dissemination and awareness raising of the erasmus+ programme and other instruments for smes to promote worker mobility.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the erasmus+ and vet programmes and the proposal to pay more attention to their socioeconomic impact. these programmes are not only an important means for young european citizens to travel and develop their european consciousness, but also a concrete political response to combat the serious phenomenon of youth unemployment, which now exceeds the 20% threshold in our continent. i particularly appreciate the emphasis on vocational education and training (vet), which is the kind of learning that is not based on traditional university studies but on the practice of manual trades. the report calls for the extension of the european network of exchanges in this field, thus enabling both young jobseekers to meet a wider offer and companies to find more motivated future workers.
in writing. ‒ the erasmus+ programme enables the training of european citizens who share the same heritage of values common to all the member states of the union. while welcoming the report of the committee on culture and education, it is nevertheless necessary to emphasize the importance of making the programme even more accessible and usable, in particular by reducing and simplifying bureaucratic procedures, which are a real obstacle to mobility, perhaps by creating a single online management platform where all the necessary documents can be entered by the participants and the institutions involved. it is also important to provide financing tailored to the cost of living in the specific destinations, covering a larger share of the costs. improving the service we offer can strengthen the eu and support a programme which creates more union and more europe every year.
in writing. the report has some positive aspects in that it makes it clear that education is a fundamental human right and a public good that must be accessible to all. the eu and the member states are called upon to work towards the elimination of all socioeconomic barriers which hinder equal access for all citizens to education and vocational training opportunities, including mobility. however, while the commission and the member states are asked to ensure that adequate resources are allocated to the youth guarantee and the youth employment initiative, the reason for the failure of the policies implemented so far is not analysed. measures to deal adequately with the very high youth unemployment, the widening gap in socioeconomic conditions and the loss of labour rights by young people have proved insufficient. we need to do more. in the context of the policies for the implementation of the erasmus+ programme, the text mentions only one reference framework: the european schoolnet. it is a non-profit organisation which brings together in partnership ministries of education, schools, teachers, researchers but also industries, including shell. in view of these factors, i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ some of the premises and considerations expressed in the report are shared, especially where there is a lack of transparency and democratic accountability in the functioning of certain financial institutions and bodies. however, the problem arises when solutions are proposed to make these bodies more efficient and democratic. firstly, it is proposed that a european code of conduct on transparency, integrity and accountability be established to guide the action of eu representatives in international organisations and bodies: the european union is not a political union, but a political union, and it is not a political union, but a political union. the second step is to create a single representation for the eu in these organisations, thus also limiting the possibilities for national intervention. the last important proposal would be to create a new world financial organization, the consequences of which are difficult to fathom today. for the reasons i have given, i have decided to vote against.
in writing. ‒ the global economic crisis has made the interdependence of the world's economic and financial systems increasingly apparent. the need for a new type of global democratic governance is becoming increasingly evident, as is the lack of a single european voice within international institutions. i have decided to vote in favour of the goulard report because i believe it provides a timely analysis of the relationship between the eu and international institutions in economic matters, while also pointing out the problems that need to be addressed. the most important challenges relate in particular to the issues of transparency and accountability which pass through a clear statement of the principle of verification of commitments made in the different venues. the role of parliament can be extremely important in this context, as it is the privileged forum for public debate on issues concerning international economics and finance. the basic objective must remain to protect the strategic interests of the eu and the euro area with the ambitious goal of single representation in international bodies.
in writing. ‒ it is sheer folly to want to deprive the member states of their little decision-making power in the economic field in order to delegate it to those supranational bodies which do not serve the interests of our citizens and our territories. that is why i voted against.
in writing. ‒ in the light of the strategic importance of the financial sector for growth and employment, the role of the european union in multilateral cooperation needs to be reviewed. the eu has always proved stronger when it has been able to speak with one voice on the international stage. the aim of our action must therefore be to strengthen this practice, with the ambition of achieving in the near future a single european representation also within the world financial institutions and bodies, especially the imf. the eu must be able to shape its own future and defend common interests, especially those of euro-zone members, when discussing the main issues of global finance. but all this must be accompanied by increased democratic control and greater openness to our citizens. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft budget for the financial year. the european parliament can play a decisive role in this game. i believe that the resolution we have adopted is an important step forward, because it aims to combine a more united and influential eu, but at the same time more open to its citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this document because i believe that the role of the eu in the international monetary and financial institutions needs to be re-examined, both in terms of external representation and in terms of the union's internal decision-making procedures, with particular attention to the role of the european parliament, which, as the body representing the citizens of the union, should be given greater weight.
in writing. ‒ financial stability is crucial to the investment needed for growth, but we cannot have a truly stable financial system if as europeans we are not able to define and enforce common rules and standards of conduct at supranational level. and we cannot adopt common rules of conduct which are not based on full transparency and the assumption of responsibility by all market players. it is important to stress that in the face of private interests and outside experts, it is parliament, as the representative of the interests of all citizens, which must have the last word. european institutions and national governments have often struggled to provide satisfactory answers to simple and legitimate questions from citizens about security and transparency in the financial dynamics of the international market: it is time for the union to make the qualitative leap necessary to respond to citizens' demands by implementing all the necessary decisions, both technical and political.
in writing. ‒ the text outlines nightmarish scenarios of 'hyper-globalisation' and an even more marked shift of economic power to supranational organisations. for the northern league, most of these bodies are the negation of democracy and popular sovereignty. the eurogroup, which is already a place of production of mischief as an informal body, is explicitly mentioned, let alone if it were to receive official status. the 'censorship' that is being applied to suppress the voices of dissent in the international arena by those countries which do not conform to the european majority is incredible.
in writing. ‒ after careful reflection and debate in the house, i voted in favour of the report on the role of the eu in the framework of international financial, monetary and regulatory institutions and bodies, as i believe that as we become increasingly sensitive to the issues of a democratic framework for global governance, to meet the challenges of an effective allocation of resources for growth and jobs, the panama papers revelation represents a serious threat to the stability of the financial system, which is now a global public good. i can only stress that the issues of inconsistency and fragmentation of financing methods, the need for a concept of 'natural' transparency in financial processes and not just imposed, and the need to protect sensitive market information are all coming up forcefully. i therefore expect that the commission's proposal to promote greater tax transparency by companies with a turnover of over eur 750 million, with a duty to disclose, will not meet with any resistance in the member states.
in writing. ‒ the report covers parliament's position on how to strengthen the eu's role in international organisations. although some aspects of the report were certainly agreeable, such as the criticism of a lack of transparency and democratic accountability in the functioning of some institutions, the text is equally controversial as regards the solutions envisaged in order to make these bodies more efficient and democratic. the proposal for a european code of conduct on transparency on the one hand, and the creation of a single representative for the eu from the top, are in fact solutions that would tend to severely limit the possibility of national intervention by the member states, which would be forced to respect the will expressed by the union without any possibility of dissent. in view of these criticisms, i have decided to vote against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it aims to improve cooperation between member states in the financial field. i believe that the european union itself could make a useful contribution to the emergence of a multilateral dialogue on economic and financial matters. i feel it is my duty as a member of the european parliament to make practical progress towards financial stability and growth in our countries. i believe that the european union is a major financial power and that this is possible through continuous dialogue between its member states. for these reasons i voted in favour, because this dialogue gives concrete answers to the problems of the citizens. the report also calls for such cooperation to be transparent and consistent with the union's fundamental values, all of which i have always defended politically.
in writing. ‒ the report highlights the malfunctioning of some international financial institutions and bodies, such as the international monetary fund, the oecd, the g20 and the financial stability board (fsb). the solution proposed in the report to solve the malfunctioning of these bodies does not seem to be adequate at all, but it offers the possibility of creating a sort of 'european code of conduct' on the issues of transparency and accountability to guide eu action. this proposal is a clear denial of the freedom of action of the representatives of the states in favour of hegemonic positions within the union, and it is no coincidence that the report has been entrusted to one of the leading voices of european federalists, who are in favour of a federal europe. the report also proposes the establishment of a single eu representation in international financial organisations, which would undermine pluralism and the possibility for individual member states to oppose. for the reasons i have mentioned, i am voting against.
in writing. ‒ at the global and regional level, numerous institutions have been created with the aim of ensuring responsible global governance and ensuring the stability of the international system. the eu, through its various institutions, is itself an integral part of this network. however, there are indications that this system of actors may need to be reviewed and reorganised. firstly, this system is still based on operating procedures without any real democratic controls. in addition, the distribution of respective tasks and missions within this network is unclear and is a cause for concern within the eu. finally, it cannot be overlooked that the representation of states in international organizations still suffers from an under-representation of the developing countries, which are therefore in a clearly disadvantaged position. i voted in favour of parliament's resolution which calls for a better representation of the euro area in international institutions through more effective coordination, greater coherence and effective transparency in the international system.
in writing. ‒ i am absolutely opposed to the report, which in some passages goes against democracy and popular sovereignty, but instead helps unbridled globalisation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the role of the eu in the framework of international financial, monetary and regulatory institutions and bodies, because i believe that there should be greater clarity on who should make decisions at international level and particularly in the financial sector. as far as the eurozone is concerned, this need is felt even more strongly. it expresses first of all a need for democracy for the eurozone to defend its strategic interests. so far we have representation of the interests of europe and the euro area, which has been very fragmented, and this is a deplorable situation given the crucial importance of what is at stake for financial stability and in particular for growth and employment. on the contrary, the eu could make a significant contribution to the emergence of a more balanced multilateral cooperation in economic and financial matters. i also strongly shared, in the light of the 2008 crisis, the need to strengthen global economic governance through the promotion of international bodies with a capacity to act and governed by clear rules and thus to develop a concerted eu strategy within supranational bodies. last but not least, the need to give a stronger voice to the emergence of a new and inclusive approach in the european parliament.
in writing. ‒ we welcome the report on the role of the european union in the framework of international financial, monetary and regulatory institutions and bodies. the report highlights some essential aspects of financial transactions. first, the need for a strengthened european governance is highlighted. the commission is therefore proposing to set up a european network of experts in the field of environmental protection. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu's financial instruments and the implementation of the euro. the free movement of capital, a pillar of the european single market, requires mechanisms for the regulation and stability of the financial system to be defined at supranational level. in addition, the verification of commitments should be determined by global implementation procedures. the failure to take effective measures to combat illicit activities has led to a growing distrust of citizens over the years. for this reason, the european parliament must be given a leading role, it must regain its centrality. the elected representatives, together with the rest of the european institutions, have shown their capacity to act and to set up supervisory, banking resolution and rescue bodies in response to the crisis that has hit the continent in recent years. financial markets also need new regulation and it is crucial that parliament plays a central role in the definition of new rules.
in writing. - on the issue at hand, i voted in favour. i am convinced that the stability of the financial system must be guaranteed at european level and that the european institutions therefore have a central role to play. i would nevertheless like to see more attention paid to citizens, through greater involvement of the european parliament and the national parliaments. moreover, increased cooperation at european level on financial matters can strengthen the eu's position vis-à-vis other international partners.
in writing. ‒ in the light of the global nature of capital flows and financial professions, the role of public action in regulating the financial sector should be modified. the eu has created a world-class internal market for financial services, has recognised financial centres, a committee to prevent systemic risks (esrb) and has experience in supranational democracy and the monitoring of state defaults. given the strategic importance of the financial sector for growth and employment, i believe that reviewing the eu's role in multilateral cooperation at the global level can strengthen our influence and better ensure the protection of the interests of the euro area. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the own-initiative report calling for a strengthening of international regulatory cooperation, taking stock of the eu's role in this area and expressing the need for greater involvement of the european parliament. in the current international economic and financial framework, the fragmentation and diversity of the various private organisations and actors (imf, g20, oecd to name a few) create a lack of coherence which is causing delays in regulatory action at international level, for example in the fight against tax evasion. the powers and functioning of the organisations involved should therefore be clarified to ensure the independence and transparency of the decisions taken. as regards the role of the eu in the framework of international financial institutions and bodies, i support the need to rationalise its presence in multilateral organisations, for example by considering the unification of the two seats allocated to the european council and the commission at the g20 meetings, in order to be able to defend european interests more strongly and play a more decisive role in international economic and financial bodies.
in writing. ‒ the report addresses the sensitive issue of the eu's role in international organisations. different solutions are proposed. the first calls for the creation of a european code of conduct on transparency to guide the action of eu representatives in international organisations and the second calls for the creation of a single representation for the eu in international organisations. this would mean obliging the member states to respect the will expressed by the eu by depriving them of any freedom of action and dissent from choices dictated by those who impose hegemonic positions. finally, there is a call for a new world financial organization, which is difficult to achieve, especially because of the consequences it could entail. on the one hand, we believe that greater cooperation between states is needed at international level, both at the level of eu countries and with the various global partners, but on the other hand, we believe that the solution cannot be to standardize everything in a single model. that is why we have opposed this approach from the outset, which marks the watershed between those who want more europe at all costs and those who want a different, collaborative and supportive europe, without impositions and technocratic approaches brought down from above but democratically authenticated by the citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ini report on the role of the european union in the context of international financial, monetary and regulatory institutions. the report suggests greater international cooperation and greater transparency with strong involvement of the european parliament. the european union should optimise and codify its representation in multilateral organisations. the european commission should also be more accountable to its citizens. finally, the report suggests a careful assessment of the two positions taken by the european council and the european commission at the g20. i am firmly convinced that these measures are necessary to improve the international financial, monetary and regulatory system.
in writing. ‒ the role of the eu in international organisations is one of the issues that is increasingly being stressed by advocates of a federal europe. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the european union. the problem arises when solutions are sought to make these bodies more 'efficient' and 'democratic'. it is proposed that a european code of conduct on transparency, integrity and accountability be established to guide the action of eu representatives in international organisations and bodies. the second step is to create a single representation for the eu in these organisations, thus also limiting national possibilities for intervention. the last important proposal would be to create a new world financial organization, the consequences of which are difficult to fathom today. it is clear that greater cooperation between states is needed at international level, but the solution cannot be to standardize everything on a single model, which has already proved to be unsuccessful in its application in the form of a single currency.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this report because traditional fishing, especially in coastal and island areas, is an identity and a way of life, as well as the main source of economic livelihood for thousands of micro-enterprises, often family-run. it is traditional fishing that is suffering most, both in terms of compliance with the standards imposed by the european union and in terms of the management of fishing quotas by the member states, which are regularly excluding traditional fishing in favour of large shipowners. if we really want to support our fishing communities and districts, and we must, there are two ways: firstly, derogations must be granted on the basis of regionalisation in order to create a fisheries policy which favours the productive environment rather than hindering it, and secondly, these fishermen must be supported by giving them priority in the allocation of emff funds and by progressively increasing the quotas allocated to small-scale fishermen.
in writing. ‒ coastal fisheries have always been a key area of european policy. considering that 80% of the european fleet is currently made up of vessels engaged in small-scale coastal fishing, it is clear that the sector makes a huge contribution to economic growth and employment. the tomasic report, however, highlighted the need for a review of technical measures to make better use of regional specificities. the creation of marine protected areas and investments to finance the development of activities complementary to fishing, which highlight the multi-purpose nature and the enormous variety of fisheries at regional level, are encouraged. for these reasons i voted in favour, particularly considering the incredible benefits that both islands and coastal regions could derive from the introduction of socially and ecologically sustainable fisheries.
in writing. ‒ in recent years, revenues from small-scale fishing have been severely reduced by rising fuel costs and the reduction in the value of fish at first sale, affecting many small fishing communities. from the coasts of french guiana to those of the adriatic, however, coastal and island fisheries continue to be an important source of employment and a way of life for many citizens of the union. 80% of the european fleet is engaged in this activity, together with the collection of shellfish, but the methods used vary widely depending on the geographical area in which it is practised. the tomašić report, which i support, calls on the commission to use regionalisation to adapt the definition of coastal fishing to the specificities of the different areas, and also calls for particular attention to be paid, when drawing up legislative proposals, to the different impact that fishing techniques and gear can have in the different areas. attention to coastal fisheries requires a holistic view of the dynamics between environment, tourism, economy and innovation. the blue economy is linked to the resources devoted to innovation under horizon 2020, but this must be exploited to the full by creating transnational public-private partnerships that can foster the growth of coastal regions.
in writing. ‒ the enhancement of small-scale fisheries in the member states and the reduction of the burden on operators through improved regional governance are important goals. for these reasons i voted in favour of the text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this document because i believe that coastal fishing plays a fundamental role in the development and economy of very large areas of the union and that it should therefore be supported in a consistent manner, especially in the drive towards innovation, so as to improve its profitability and sustainability.
in writing. ‒ coastal fishing is of particular importance in some eu countries. it provides a high level of employment and is a socially and environmentally sustainable form of fishing. for most coastal and island areas, fishing is a way of life and a significant source of livelihood. areas dependent on coastal fisheries require specific measures and support in order to grow and develop. coastal regions often face decline and depopulation, mainly for employment reasons. the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff) should therefore help to expand coastal economies by investing in data collection and promoting more scientific research. a change in community law is needed to preserve traditional fishing gear and techniques used in coastal fishing and to define a clear distinction between commercial and coastal fishing.
in writing. ‒ good own-initiative report on the development of artisanal (and commercial) fishing with references to the cfp and regional governance with some relief for operators. i'm voting for it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today because i believe that the commission should support innovative projects and legal provisions to facilitate the development of regions dependent on fisheries. in particular, priority should be given to projects focusing on the sustainable creation and maintenance of jobs, the introduction of new technologies in the promotion and marketing of fisheries products and services, the promotion of fisheries tourism and gastronomy linked to artisanal fisheries products, and all activities related to environmental protection, the development of renewable marine resources and the promotion of sustainable growth. the commission and the member states should also progressively increase the quotas allocated to small-scale fishermen in order to promote this type of fishing which is socially and ecologically sustainable. it is also essential to give priority to small-scale coastal fishing in the allocation of funding from the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff).
in writing. ‒ coastal fishing accounts for 80% of the eu fleet and provides a large number of jobs. the report states that the revision of the technical measures framework must take account of the specificities of regional coastal fisheries and encourages the introduction of marine protected areas to promote sustainable fishing and facilitate the fight against irregular fishing. the commission is invited to promote investment in diversifying fishing activities through the development of complementary activities and the multipurpose of careers in order to promote the development of tourism. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ the economy of coastal and island areas is strongly linked to fishing activities, especially the artisanal fisheries sector, which is the main and sometimes the only source of income for many communities. the economic crisis we are experiencing has not spared this sector, and in particular that of small-scale coastal fishing, which is also affected by the imposition of technical measures on the use of fishing gear and techniques provided for in the so-called 'mediterranean' regulation. the protection of coastal fisheries requires a detailed characterisation of small-scale fisheries, and for this reason a comprehensive and complete picture is needed, without which there is a high risk of decisions not being appropriate to the sector. data are needed to design actions and interventions adapted to local needs and to chart the path to a biologically, environmentally, socially and economically sustainable coastal fishery before reviewing existing legislation. as small-scale fishing is an activity linked to local traditions, plans to safeguard them and to develop complementary activities compatible with the vocations of the area, such as nautical tourism or recreational fishing, could help to revive these areas. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it not only protects coastal fisheries but also lays a solid foundation for their development. this report proposes to regionalise the rules for coastal fishing by adapting them on a case-by-case basis, country by country. i think this is an important step forward because i believe it allows this practice to develop in an appropriate way, while fully respecting the individual countries and the individual specificities of this activity. i also voted in favour of this because i believe that coastal fishing is not only a source of high employment but also a socially and environmentally sustainable form of fishing. i therefore think it is essential to strengthen this activity by regionalising its regulation, because it is full of positive externalities not only in terms of social and economic cohesion but also in terms of environmental protection and development. i believe that strengthening this activity could lead to an increase in employment and also to greater profitability in the sector.
in writing. ‒ in some island territories, artisanal and traditional fishing is an important, if not the main, source of income at local level, making these regions highly dependent on this type of fishing. although there is a well-established common fisheries policy at european level, the commission has not taken sufficient account of the specific socioeconomic characteristics of the areas dependent on artisanal and traditional fishing. it therefore seems essential to pay more attention to this type of fishing, which is also more socially and ecologically sustainable. i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution that the commission should take account of the specificities and socioeconomic characteristics of the areas where traditional and artisanal fishing is a key economic sector.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because of the fundamental role that coastal fishing plays as a source of livelihood and development for many regions of the eu. as already recognised in the previous regulations on the common fisheries policy and the european maritime fund, these areas require further support to foster economically and environmentally sustainable growth. i am particularly pleased that the report considers the possibility of using instruments which make it possible to implement activities which are complementary to traditional fishing such as catering, environmental services, cultural activities linked to fishing and tourism linked to sport fishing. i welcome the recommendation that legislation should protect and promote the different coastal fishing practices, taking into account the specificities of the individual areas concerned, and in particular supporting small-scale fishermen.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the report because it promotes and supports small-scale fishing and also provides for some relief of the burden on operators.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the basis that it will support non-industrial-scale fishing in general, and that this is important because these smaller and often family-run fisheries play an important role in many rural coastal communities all around europe. this resolution and the support it could provide would not only support the local fisheries themselves but also the surrounding community and countryside and it could help to maintain an important historic way of life. with this report we also stress the great social and economic impact of small-scale fishery. support of small costal fisheries means that we promote a more sustainable way of fishing and support the availability of local products for the local consumer. both of these effects can help save us from negative environmental impacts.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep resolution on innovation and the diversification of small-scale coastal fishing in regions dependent on fishing because i am convinced that coastal fishing is a fundamental and indispensable activity for the economic, environmental and social fabric of those southern european territories which are experiencing sustainable growth and which have always been nourished by genuine forms of economy. i am convinced of the importance of the blue economy as a new driving force for the development of coastal areas, as a means of countering emigration and the desertification of those areas and as a source of jobs for small and very small producers. i welcome the call on the commission to adapt the definition of coastal fishing by involving the regional level and by taking account of the characteristics of the territories, and to support innovative projects and legal provisions which facilitate the development of this activity in coastal, island and outermost regions. i also welcome the call for better use of the emff to promote coastal areas, the call for instruments to promote female employment in coastal fishing and the references to the social economy sector and to groups promoting local development: the commission has also proposed that the european union should be able to provide the necessary financial support to the coastal regions.

in writing. ‒ regulation 380/2013 on the common fisheries policy promotes the economic development of coastal and island areas, and that the fisheries in question contribute to the growth of employment in these areas, and regulation 508/2014 on the emff recognises a strong focus on this type of fisheries and that in the current programming period 2014-2020, research and innovation benefit from significant european funding through the horizon 2020 programme. the current lack of information and difficulty in accessing data on the state of the seas and oceans requires greater investment in research and innovation. finally, diversification in the coastal fisheries sector would make it possible to cope with the economic difficulties of certain geographical areas due to the over-exploitation of resources, with a consequent drop in profits, and for these reasons i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ coastal fishing is a very important type of fishery in eu countries, and is particularly important because it provides a high employment rate and is socially and environmentally sustainable. i voted in favour of this resolution because i support the idea that areas dependent on coastal fishing require specific measures and support which offer them opportunities for growth and development. this requires closing the various gaps in areas which are crucial to the viability of the sector. investment in sea and ocean monitoring systems has increased in recent years, but is still insufficient, and the process of obtaining and obtaining the appropriate authorisations for the use of data is itself time-consuming and requires additional financial resources. this is a major constraint on the development of innovation and the use of resources, which is also affected by the lack of collaboration between the public and private sectors. another important aspect concerns the diversification of the fisheries sector, which is necessary to cope with the decline in employment and profitability. given the importance of the environment and a sustainable economy, the diversification of fisheries must make use of the contribution of activities linked to renewable energy sources and environmental protection.
in writing. ‒ definitions and classifications of coastal fisheries vary from one member state to another. for most coastal and island areas it is a traditional form of fishing which is a way of life and a significant source of livelihood; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the environment is protected and that the environment is protected. the basic regulation of the new 2013 cfp focuses on the economic development of coastal areas. the emff (european maritime fund) also pays particular attention to the sector. considering that some coastal and island areas are facing a significant economic decline, the european commission was invited to invest and support investment in diversification through the development of complementary activities linked to traditional fishing. the commission is therefore invited to initiate a procedure to amend existing legislation, in particular the 2006 regulation on management measures for the sustainable development of fisheries resources in the mediterranean, which has been adopted and which must be aligned with the new cfp. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ small-scale fishing accounts for about 80% of the european fleet. italy has one of the largest small-scale fishing sectors in europe, with some 7 500 vessels and more than 13 000 workers on board. this sector has always represented for our country not only an important economic and commercial resource, but also an opportunity to combine an activity with a strong social and cultural value with a more sustainable management of fisheries and environmental resources. our artisanal fishermen can be considered as the "guardians of the coastal zone", with traditions and knowledge that cannot be lost because of the serious crisis that is dangerously undermining the sector. within the eu, coastal fishing varies significantly between member states and within member states. it is therefore important to adopt a regionalised approach in order to define small-scale coastal fishing activities correctly and to adapt the existing european rules to the characteristics and socioeconomic specificities of the various areas. i hope that the commission will take up parliament's recommendations in order to protect small-scale fishing and to promote its development through innovation and diversification. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ for coastal and island regions, small-scale fishing is not only of particular importance for local development and employment, but also represents a socially and environmentally sustainable economic activity that must be protected and promoted. i therefore voted in favour of the report which calls on the european commission to support, by specific measures, new opportunities for growth and development in coastal regions, through innovation and diversification of activities complementary to fishing, through investment in cleaner fishing vessels, environmental services linked to fishing, cultural and educational activities linked to fishing and tourism linked to sport fishing. i also fully support the call for the regulatory framework on the sustainable management of fisheries resources in the mediterranean to be amended to allow the preservation and enhancement of traditional coastal fishing techniques, such as tuna fishing, so that a clear distinction is made between commercial and traditional fisheries in line with the different impacts on marine resources caused by the two types of fishing.

in writing. ‒ the common fisheries policy (cfp) aims to make the fisheries and aquaculture sectors increasingly sustainable from an ecological, economic and social point of view. the aim is therefore to promote a dynamic fisheries industry while ensuring a decent standard of living for the fishing communities. for these reasons, the eu has committed itself to ensuring that sustainable fisheries agreements with third countries respect the environmental standards and the ecosystem approach that underpin the cfp. for these reasons, it was requested that the european parliament should play a more active role in the approval procedures, with the recognition of a full and immediate right of information, which undoubtedly ensures transparency and controllability of the protocols. in view of these considerations, i voted in favour, confident in the commitment of the european institutions to the protection and promotion of environmentally sustainable fisheries, including agreements with third countries.
in writing. ‒ the european union is one of the world's leading fish markets, the largest importer of fishery products and the third largest fleet on the planet. the fish processing industry plays a key role in the european economy, providing a large number of jobs that need to be safeguarded. the report on the external dimension of the common fisheries policy, which i supported today, effectively illustrates the strategic priorities that must be pursued. in a global context of the emergence of new players such as china, taiwan and korea, operating with fleets operating to standards less stringent than those required by community rules, there is an increasing need to exploit the union's potential for influence. the crucial issue must be that of transparency. the commitment to information on the fishing activities of other actors operating in third countries with which agreements are signed must be accompanied by the creation of an eu-wide database covering all private agreements between union shipowners and third countries, as well as joint ventures between eu and third country companies. the new eu cfp, if properly implemented, will significantly improve the standards of the union's ocean fisheries.

in writing. ‒ the eu is currently the largest market for fishery products and has one of the largest fleets in the world. in the eu, the external dimension concerns fishing by eu-flagged vessels on the high seas and in waters under the jurisdiction of third countries, such as in the case of a partnership agreement. many fleets from countries such as china, korea and taiwan operate under less stringent environmental, safety and social regulations. the best strategy to achieve the goal of promoting sustainable fisheries is to use the eu's influence on the international scene to improve fisheries management and transparency standards, by promoting the harmonisation of eu and non-eu fleet rules on access to non-eez areas, fighting iuu fishing, improving fish supply for food security and supporting the work done mainly by women in the fisheries sector.

member of the commission.– madam president, first of all i would like to express my thanks for your meaningful contributions, many of which are very much in line with the commission’s thinking and objectives. let me clarify some points. our relationship with turkey is not about antagonism in terms of power dynamics. it is about an agreement to address an issue in a joint way. both europe and turkey are under great pressure. we are confronted with the same challenges and an unprecedented situation. cooperation is necessary. it is true that turkey considers this cooperation to be a catalyst to reenergise our relations as well as its european perspective. this new chapter in eu-turkey relations is not interpreted as a concession on our basic principles and values of european democracy. on the contrary, it is an opportunity for turkey to come closer to european standards on all issues: democratic values, rule of law, freedom of expression, respect for minority rights, and resolution of the cyprus issue. it is in europe’s interest to have a democratic and stable turkey as a neighbour, and it is in the interest of turkey to have the european union as a stable supporter and partner. the refugee crisis brought us closer in a spirit of mutual understanding. it needs to be proved whether we mean what we say and what we agree. we are monitoring to ensure that every single aspect of this agreement happens in full accordance with european union and international law. i do not have any doubt about it, and we persist on that. for example, the turkish authorities have passed legislation to ensure protection for syrians. we told them very explicitly that guarantees are needed for all those who are in need of protection, whether they are syrians or non-syrians. on visa liberalisation, 35 out of the 72 requirements are fulfilled, but the commission has been crystal clear: we can only make a proposal to lift visa requirements if all benchmarks are met. turkey knows this, and it is making efforts to further accelerate the fulfilment of the benchmarks so that we can lift the visa requirements by june 2016. the deal has only started being implemented, with just over 300 people who had not applied for asylum being returned and 74 syrians resettled directly from turkey so far. this is only the start. next week the commission will formally report on the state of play of implementation of all elements of this agreement. let me say this: this agreement is an important step for a long-term renewed relationship. a common goal is also to come closer to one another when it comes to values, as i stressed at the beginning of my remarks. in the meantime, the commission is heavily involved in the situation on the ground in greece. we are doing everything to support greece in expanding reception capacities and in making sure that vulnerable applicants, such as women and children, are being treated appropriately. our people are there, deployed all around the greek islands, as well as on the greek mainland, providing our help to the greek government and the greek authorities. member states need to continue relocating massively from greece, and i fully agree with what was said in this house today, that all member states must take their share of their responsibilities. of the more than 50 000 people stuck in greece, at least 70% are eligible for relocation. this is important for those who were stranded in idomeni and pireus before 20 march. let us also look at other routes. the arrivals from libya to italy show that as long as there is instability, as long as there are smugglers taking advantage of this situation, people will continue to migrate. it is as simple as that. so we have to keep working on the bigger picture. this means continuing our political efforts to bring back stability to syria and libya. this also means turning into reality our proposal for a european border and coast guard. we are very happy that this house has presented a draft report and has a timetable which reflects our commitments. we have no time to lose here – indeed, summer is already here. this also means enhancing legal pathways so that people do not have to resort to irregular arrangements. i would like to thank those members of this house who have raised this and who support our view. stepping up our efforts on resettlement is an essential part of the solution, primarily from turkey now but also from lebanon and jordan, which are hosting hundreds and thousands of refugees. i have said this before: if we genuinely want to close the irregular backdoor, we have to open a safe and legal window. fortress europe is neither desirable nor feasible, simply because as long as people have reasons to flee, they will continue to do so, and they will continue to try to come to europe. and not only is it our moral and legal responsibility to offer a safe haven for those in need, we also need to make our policies and our approach future-proof. resettlement is the way forward to ensure orderly, legal and controlled admission from third countries for those who are in need of protection. some of you also mentioned dublin. we do not want a cosmetic reform. the president was very clear today on that. we need to reform and improve dublin to ensure that solidarity and a fair sharing of responsibility is engrained in the new system, because the current one is simply not sustainable. we all know that there is no easy solution to the challenge we face, but one thing is sure: we have to work together and not against each other. this is valid for the european union institutions, the member states and also our relations with our neighbours.
president of the european council.– madam president, there are several aspects of our debate to which i would like to refer. firstly, regarding relocation: this is – and will be – one of the key elements of the european solution to the crisis. in this aspect, of course, we need solidarity. i have no doubt about that. but we would be making a mistake if it became the main tool of our policy, because it would be a simple incentive for further, even greater, migration flows, something like an encouragement for possible new migrants. this is why i think we have to be very cautious, especially when it comes to communication with the outside world. in the debate, mr kamall and mr verhofstadt referred to statistics on irregular migration in the context of the mediterranean route. i am always very cautious when it comes to statistics. i have some reason to be cautious, but today it is indeed worth considering them. first, concerning the balkan route, it is true that 150 000 irregular migrants have arrived in europe since the beginning of this year, but the numbers are falling, month after month, from close to 70 000 in january, to 50 000 in february, to 30 000 in march, and to about 1 000 in april. just imagine if only in the month of january, in the middle of winter, there were 70 000 migrants, how many of them would have come in april if we had not taken action? second, it is also true that since the start of this year, 20 000 irregular migrants have come to europe via the central mediterranean route and that the numbers are growing. but no syrians are among them. they are nationals of africa and countries such as nigeria, somalia, gambia, the republic of guinea and ivory coast. what does this mean in fact? if we had not closed the western balkans route, we would now have three or five times more migrants – those from africa coming to us through libya, as well as those who have now been stopped at the border or discouraged from crossing the border. many have said today that our priority should be to set up the european coast guard. i am in favour, even if this coast guard will not be operational this year. that is obviously impossible. but we must ask ourselves the question: what exactly should the eu coast guard do? let all through who want to enter europe, or stop and control them? i think it is obvious – not only for me – that they should stop and control them, which means in fact the same very controversial action that we are applying right now. in the first place we must expect national coastguards to enforce our law on european borders. the european coastguards should support those who need help but cannot replace them.

president of the portuguese republic. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, thank you very much, mr president, for the honour you have bestowed on me by inviting me to the house of democracy, one month after i took office as president of the portuguese republic. i thank you, mr president martin schulz, for allowing me to address the legitimate representative of the european people, whom i now wish to confirm. house of democracy because no other european institution of this scale is based on the principles of freedom, security, humanism and citizen participation which this house and each of its members represents and guarantees. the fact that we are here today is a sign of the importance that european integration has assumed in the birth and affirmation of portuguese democracy. but it's also a sign of a personal commitment, born of a very ancient design. i belong to a generation of portuguese people for whom europe and integration into it was a dream, inseparable from democracy, decolonisation, economic development and social justice. the conversion of the dictatorship into democracy involved the end of the empire, but not least the affirmation of portugal's belonging to europe, its geographical, historical and cultural cradle. it is more clearly, since the 1960s, the destination of their main emigration and the origin and destination of their trade. we believed in europe itself, in what it represented as an example of peace, solidarity, growth, social equity, cultural life. but we still saw it as an incentive to build a new portugal. i therefore recall with nostalgia the first university delegation to the communities, which i was a member of at the most complex period of the revolution; mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to humbly remind the house that a country is free to join the european union, no one can force it, its citizens choose it, but when it joins the european union it is obliged to respect the rules and decisions of the european union. so no interference, but a legitimate and proper interest on the part of a european institution in what happens within its own family, because poland is part of our family and we are interested in the fate of polish citizens. this resolution is nothing but the follow-up to the outcome of the venice convention, which has spoken clearly and we ask that it be respected by the polish authorities.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was created to balance markets against the imbalances caused by increased international trade. the negrescu report concerns the volvo group truck in sweden, and aims to re-employ 500 workers affected by the crisis in the truck industry. in the absence of viable alternatives, we believe that the egf can support the local swedish economy. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of mobilising the european globalisation adjustment fund for sweden following the redundancies of 647 workers at volvo truck operations, emea, and four other suppliers and downstream manufacturers in the norrland region in the north. the establishment of the truck industry in asia, particularly in china and india, has led to a profound change in the global market, forcing european producers to intervene on costs in order to improve international competitiveness. the measures taken by the five swedish companies have, however, led to the redundancy of some workers who must be supported by appropriate social protection measures. the mobilisation of the egf is an important opportunity to support workers in finding a new job and it helps to strengthen the social dimension of europe, which is why i supported the negrescu report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the mobilisation of almost eur 1.8 million from the egf to help 500 swedish workers and 5 companies in the car, trailer and semi-trailer manufacturing sector. the globalisation adjustment fund is a very important tool to support citizens in this time of crisis, but the eu should focus on addressing the failures of the internal market as a whole, rather than just looking after its victims.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this document because i believe it is the union's duty to support and help those workers, such as those at the volvo trucks plant in umeå, who have lost their jobs as a result of globalisation and outsourcing practices.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) is useful to provide support for redundant workers and self-employed persons whose activity has ceased as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation, or as a result of the continuation of the global financial and economic crisis, or as a result of new economic and financial crises of a supra-regional nature. the fund should be used to assist them in re-entering the labour market by updating their training and providing them with economic support at the same time. the egf should, therefore, be mobilised in order to provide financial assistance to the workers of volvo trucks who have suffered serious injury as a result of these events.
in writing. ‒ eur 1 793 710 for 500 redundancies in five enterprises in the sector of 'manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers'. the sector is struggling with asian competition and the difficulties of adaptation, which are forcing it to increase efficiency and reduce costs. support the workers and vote for it!
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today in order to support the reintegration into the labour market of some 500 workers made redundant as a result of globalisation by volvo group truck operation emea, a company in north norrland which manufactures cars and trailers. the manufacture of commercial vehicles is no longer dominated by european manufacturers due to new asian truck manufacturers. the commission established the profitability of the sampled union producers by expressing the pre-tax net profit of the sales of the like product to unrelated customers in the union as a percentage of the turnover of those sales. i regret that italian companies are not able to benefit more from this fund because of the lack of support from local and national institutions. between 2007 and 2015, italy submitted only 15 applications to the european globalisation adjustment fund, 3 of which in 2007, only one in 2008, zero between 2009 and 2010, 7 in 2011, 2 in 2012, zero in 2013, one in 2014 and one in 2015.
in writing. ‒ the report concerns sweden's request to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund for the volvo group trucks in sweden. the request amounts to approximately eur 1 800 000 to help re-employ 500 workers affected by the crisis in the truck industry, in particular volvo trucks and some companies in the industry, which have been heavily affected by asian competition in recent years. in the absence of any viable alternative to help redundant workers, i voted in favour of the mobilisation of the fund.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it seeks to direct part of european funds to support a swedish company for the protection of redundant workers. i believe that the union has all the means to support individual countries with their enterprises in this time of great economic difficulty and that is why i have spoken in favour of: i think that, wherever possible, it is necessary not only for policy to respond but also for action to be taken. in this particular case, the report also deals with the protection of workers and as a member of parliament i have had to take their side in defence of those who are victims of this crisis.
in writing. ‒ the demand in question is particularly strong in the truck industry, which has suffered a decline in production in recent years due to asian competition. in this specific area, 22 applications for egf assistance were received, 12 of which were due to the globalisation of trade and 10 to the global financial and economic crisis. while i am in favour of granting egf assistance for the 500 workers laid off by volvo trucks, i agree with the rapporteur in calling on the commission to look carefully at cases where egf funds have been called in for redundancies due to business relocation strategies dictated by the search for low-cost labour.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the report which supports work and workers in firms in difficulty because of asian competition.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the proposal for a european parliament and council decision to mobilise a contribution from the european globalisation adjustment fund of eur 1 793 710 in respect of redundancies in the volvo trucks company because i believe it is important to provide support for redundant workers in a region, västerbotten, which is suffering from both the volvo crisis and the crisis of the subsidiary companies that depend on it. volvo trucks, like all companies in the commercial and heavy-duty vehicle sector, is suffering from the effects of the decrease in physical production in europe due to competition from third countries. this represents a decrease of almost 11% in european volumes, compared with a 10% increase in vehicle imports: in fact, the sector already has 22 applications for egf assistance. i therefore believe that the funding of personalised services such as individual planning services, job search and coaching activities, measures for motivation and health, for entrepreneurship and business creation, education and training and job search allowances is going in the right direction and shows citizens the value and effectiveness of eu action.
in writing. the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) aims to provide support for workers who are unfortunately losing their jobs as a result of the changes in the structure of world trade due to globalisation. the changes are being brought about by the global economic crisis which is persisting within our system, and it is because of this that we must urgently ensure the reintegration into the world of work of all those who are contributing to this state. in this case, the financial aid for training courses and research into new job activities, which i support, will go to volvo's swedish employees.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund is an indispensable instrument through which the european union can effectively intervene in support of workers who have lost their jobs as a result of the economic and financial crisis. the proposal aims to support the reintegration into the labour market of the 500 employees laid off by volvo group trucks, a manufacturer of cars and trailers, and downstream producers in sweden. that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ today we voted on the annual request for technical assistance from the european commission for the year 2016. the novakov report concerns the request for the mobilisation of eur 380 000 from the fund to cover technical assistance at the initiative of the commission. the objective of the technical assistance is to finance monitoring and information, to create a knowledge base/interface and to provide advice to member states in relation to the use, continuity and evaluation of the egf. i am generally in favour of the mobilisation of this fund, although i am aware that it is probably not the instrument that can best help redundant workers, but in the absence of viable alternatives i still think it should be supported. the question of technical assistance is slightly different, as in my view it should be provided at no extra cost by the european commission, leaving the full resources of this instrument to support the firms and workers affected by the crisis; the novakov report stresses the need for some changes in this area, but without specifying exactly in which direction we should go. that's why i abstained.

in writing. ‒ the migration crisis has put and continues to put to the test the responses that europe is able to provide, both in terms of humanitarian support and in terms of policies, to address the economic and social difficulties that are developing at its borders and within it. the european commission has decided to create a new eu budget line to rapidly finance aid measures that member states have decided to implement to cope with humanitarian emergencies. i voted in favour of the fernandes report because i believe that this decision of the commission should be strongly supported. since the beginning of the crisis, the european parliament has been mobilizing to demand rapid responses and to initiate a project to amend existing legislation in order to make the union capable of responding to new, profound and sudden changes. the adoption of the amending budget is a further demonstration of this will.

in writing. ‒ pbr no 1/2016 is used to finance the new instrument for the provision of emergency support within the union. the first appropriation consists of 100 million in commitments and 80.2 million in payments; the commission forecasts a total need of 300 million for 2016 and 200 million per year for 2017 and 2018. the commission notes that the aid is granted to the beneficiaries of the aid, who are the beneficiaries of the aid, and that the aid is granted to the beneficiaries of the aid. all signs point to floods, earthquakes, fires, and the like. instead, reading the recitals, we find that mass immigration is equated with a "catastrophe", the impact of which on the eu is due to "circumstances occurring in the union's neighbourhood". the silver lining of this masterpiece of ambiguity is that it is not fresh money, but a transfer from the asylum, migration and integration fund (amif), which corresponds to about 10% of the billion spent on the relocation of 160 000 immigrants in the period 2015-17. i voted in favour of the proposal, considering the small sum and the purpose.
