in writing. ‒ i am in favour of the creation of this new tool, in the hope that it can really be of some use in the management of this emergency which has been going on for many months now. the budget presented provides for 100 million in commitments and 80.2 million in payments for immediate financial needs, so i am very puzzled that they come from the budget line for the asylum, migration and integration fund, which is an absolute priority. i chose to abstain.
in writing. ‒ by voting in favour of this report, i wanted to allow the eu budget to provide emergency aid in the eu territory to respond to the humanitarian consequences of the current refugee crisis. i believe that a shift in resources is essential to respond effectively to the situation of migrants and asylum seekers, which is getting worse and worse and where immediate help is increasingly needed. we must be in solidarity with the member states facing such an emergency situation on their territory and that is precisely why i voted in favour, because i believe that one of the countries which needs effective cooperation in this area is italy. the report also aims to increase the staff of the european counter-terrorism centre at europol, which was another reason for voting in favour. in fact, in the light of the present situation, i think that more resources must be invested, especially when it is clear that the work in this direction is not enough. we need more and europe, in my view, has all the means to make up for these shortcomings.
in writing. ‒ the report on draft amending budget (dab) no 1 for 2016 deals with the new instrument providing emergency assistance within member states to respond to the humanitarian needs caused by the current migration emergency. the humanitarian emergency we are experiencing in these years must include assistance, rescue and protection operations to protect the lives and integrity of people in emergency and post-emergency conditions. eu funding should support emergency support operations, such as the construction of housing or shelters for groups of people concerned. the budget presented provides for 100 million in commitments and 80.2 million in payments for immediate financial needs. i am in favour of the creation of an instrument for the provision of emergency support within the eu, in order to be able to manage the humanitarian emergency in which we have been involved for several years now. i think it is necessary to understand the source of these funds and to ensure that they are not part of the amif (asylum, migration and integration) fund, but are drawn from other budget lines. that is why i am abstaining.

in writing. ‒ the continuing influx of refugees into europe is putting a strain on the reception capacity of the states at the forefront of dealing with the crisis. the european union must intervene to support these countries. it has been repeatedly stated that solidarity is a fundamental principle of the union and that only by acting together as europe can we overcome this situation, guaranteeing human rights and dignity to men, women and children who are forced to risk their lives in desperate journeys to escape war and persecution. i therefore welcome the commission's proposal to set up a european instrument to provide aid within the territory of the union and i hope that, in addition to the emergency, more structured and sustainable measures will be provided to deal with a situation which, as we all know, will not be resolved in the short term. i also welcome the commission's commitment not to withdraw funds from the budget for external humanitarian aid. i support the decision to finance this new instrument by reallocating the appropriations from the asylum, migration and integration fund. but at the same time i ask that this funding be offset at a later date to ensure that amif can carry out the work of relocating refugees for which it was set up.

in writing. ‒ on 10 march, the european commission presented draft amending budget (dab) no 1 for 2016, which concerns in particular the new instrument providing emergency support within the union, i.e. to cover the financing of support operations to respond to the urgent and exceptional humanitarian needs encountered in the member states as a result of the massive influx of third-country nationals (refugees and migrants) into their territories. emergency response may include assistance, rescue and protection operations aimed at saving and protecting lives in disaster or post-emergency situations. this amending budget thus makes available, through reallocation under heading 3 of the mff, 100 million in commitments and 80.2 million in payments to meet the immediate financial need. i am pleased that the commission has made an effort to find these funds within the eu budget without any new increases, but i am very puzzled that these transfers come from the budget line concerning the amif (asylum, migration and integration) fund, which is an absolute priority.

in writing. ‒ the court of auditors is a major european institution which acts as the external and independent auditor of the union's accounts. established in 1977, it became a full eu institution only in 1993 and has continued to provide its support for improving the management of the community budget. it is composed of one member from each member state of the union, each of whom is appointed by the council after consulting parliament and serves for six years. parliament was asked to give its opinion on the appointment of mr jereb. i have taken note of the contents of the report of the committee on budgetary control and, following the instructions of my political group (s&d), i have voted in secret on the name proposed.

in writing. ‒ the court of auditors is a collegiate body composed of 28 members, one from each member state. the latter are appointed by the council, after consulting the european parliament, for a renewable term of six years. i welcome the appointment of mr samo jereb as a member of the court of auditors and wish him well in his work, with the hope that he will be able to play his role with the utmost independence and transparency in the general interest of the european union.
in writing. ‒ it has become necessary to appoint five new members of the court of auditors. the procedure laid down in article 286 tfeu provides that the members of the court of auditors shall be chosen from among persons who are or have been members of the external audit institutions in their respective states or who possess specific qualifications for that function and who must offer all guarantees of independence. the council, after consulting the european parliament, which is not bound by the treaty, shall adopt the list of members, on a proposal from each member state. the six new candidates have a rather varied curriculum and very different characteristics, which also points to the lack of a certain "gender parity" in the candidates presented. the court of auditors already has a rather large imbalance (of 28 members, 5 are women) and it is believed that the member states and the council should send a strong signal to promote gender equality in all institutions and at all levels. finally, the system of appointment of members continues to be a system of political appointment rather than merit: this has led to a negative vote for all the candidates.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this motion was born as a democratic call for the precautionary principle to be respected, which the commission proposal does not actually apply. it was also born in the defence of the public interest which must prevail, which we appeal to for the publication of those studies which monsanto, let us remember, efsa has declared to be fundamental in formulating its negative opinion on the carcinogenicity of glyphosate. we asked for their publication and what did we get? a physical reading room that we don't even know how it's gonna work. what we want is very clear: studies must be totally public. i am not saying that, but article 10 of the regulation on the marketing of plant protection products says so. commissioner andriukaitis still has responsibilities, and he cannot and must not go through this process alone. we voted for a resolution which is absolutely absurd, we cannot allow the authorization of glyphosate to be renewed for another seven years, it is absolutely unconscious of us and of you to have voted for it and to have allowed it to be disrespectful of the health of all citizens.
i also voted against the commission's proposal to extend the use of glyphosate for another 15 years. i am convinced that when there is clear scientific evidence that casts doubt on the health acceptability of this substance, responsible politicians cannot simply prolong the use of this substance for another 15 years. there are clear conclusions from the international agency for research on cancer, which in its march 2015 materials made it clear that glyphosate belongs and belongs in the category of probable human carcinogens. this is why i think that a 15-year extension is a gamble, a gamble with the health of our citizens. i therefore think it is good that the commission has not exceeded that deadline and that parliament has expressed its opinion.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as long as there are concerns about the carcinogenicity of the endocrine disruptor glyphosate, the commission should not renew any authorization. the precautionary principle must always prevail in such cases, because the primary objective of the european union is to protect the health of its citizens. the fact that we had to resort to a parliamentary objection shows that something has gone wrong in the decision-making process. glyphosate is classified as a probable carcinogen by the world health organization. the french agency for the environment, food and health (anses) has recently expressed its opinion, pointing out that certain mixtures of glyphosate with other substances may present important health risks, both for citizens and for those working in the agricultural sector. france has, in fact, decided to ban herbicides combining glyphosate and tallow amine (tallow amine) because of uncertainty about possible health risks. the commission's intention is nevertheless to extend the licence. this is an absurd position when the health of citizens is at stake. rather, the commission should submit an independent review of the classification of glyphosate based on all available scientific data on carcinogenicity as well as its possible impacts on the human hormonal system.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european parliament had the opportunity to express a strong and clear political position against the renewal of the authorization of glyphosate, a herbicide which the iarc has defined as a probable carcinogen. we are well aware that the european commission, as an executive body, has full discretion to decide to adopt acts and measures autonomously. it was important, however, that this house should express its views, and that is a great pity. the five star movement was among the strongest supporters of the motion to object to this act and, in the light of the amendments tabled and the result obtained in the end, we were forced to vote against. in fact, we have turned an objection motion into a motion in support of a renewal for another seven years, simply, the health of citizens and the environment cannot be traded, but must come before business opportunities for companies.
in writing. ‒ glyphosate is a systemic herbicide used mainly in agriculture, forestry and horticulture. it is a non-selective herbicide which kills grass vegetation and which, according to studies published by the international agency for research on cancer, is likely to be carcinogenic to humans. the data, confirmed by tests on humans, animals and based on mechanistic data, are still contested by the efsa opinion. the european food safety authority denies the carcinogenicity of glyphosate, while refusing to publish the studies in its possession. for these reasons i voted against the resulting text, which in effect renews the use of glyphosate for another seven years.
in writing. ‒ glyphosate is a particular type of non-selective herbicide that is capable of causing the death of all herbaceous vegetation on which it is applied. scientific studies have shown that it also acts on other types of organisms such as algae, fungi and bacteria, on which it acts, as in plants, by interfering with the shikimate pathway. this is the kind of action that, in the case of bacteria, causes changes in the response to antibiotics. according to the international agency for research on cancer, glyphosate is a probable human carcinogen, although efsa's conclusions, based on unpublished studies, are the opposite. the existence of a number of doubts as to the carcinogenic potential of glyphosate is also linked to concerns about its endocrine interference and the consequences it appears to have on the metabolic pathways of vertebrates, in particular with regard to hepato-renal damage found in several studies. for all these reasons, and because i believe that the commission's implementing regulation does not ensure high standards of protection of health and the environment, i have decided to vote in favour of the objection tabled in parliament today.
in writing. ‒ because of its carcinogenic potential for human health, i did not support this text which moves in the direction of granting the renewal of the authorizations for the application of 'glyphosate' in europe. the health of our citizens must always be the first priority and i believe that it would only be truly protected if the use of this substance were immediately banned.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this objection because i consider that the draft commission implementing regulation does not ensure a high level of protection of human and animal health and the environment, does not apply the precautionary principle and exceeds the implementing powers laid down in regulation (ec) no 1107/2009.
in writing. i said no to the use of glyphosate in agriculture, the substance used to produce almost all pesticides. i have rejected the european commission's proposal to renew the authorization of glyphosate for the next 15 years on the basis of the precautionary principle, since there is no reliable data on its potential carcinogenic effects. with my italian colleagues in the group we also opposed the amendments of the european people's party which proposed authorization for a shorter period of time. parliament has expressed its opinion and sent a clear message to the european commission and the member states, which will be called upon to discuss and decide again in the coming weeks.
in writing. ‒ efsa found that glyphosate (the main ingredient in monsanto's roundup herbicide) is unlikely to be carcinogenic or genotoxic (damaging dna), to the enthusiastic applause of monsanto itself. however, the who's international agency for research on cancer (iarc) has found glyphosate to be "probably" carcinogenic to humans (group 2a). the review of the risk assessment of the active substance glyphosate by efsa is limited to glyphosate itself; while the iarc reviewed glyphosate together with its formulated products, which are more relevant in the assessment of risks to human health and biodiversity. the commission decision which is the subject of this objection therefore appears to be a unilateral act which does not take into account the risks and the intergovernmental consensus.
in writing. ‒ glyphosate is the most widely produced systemic herbicide worldwide; it is a non-selective herbicide that kills all herbaceous vegetation and is used in 76% of cases in the agricultural sector but also in forestry, urban and horticultural applications. in march 2015, the international agency for research on cancer classified glyphosate as 'probably carcinogenic to humans' based on 'limited evidence' of carcinogenic effects in humans (derived from actual and actual exposure cases), 'sufficient evidence' of cancers in laboratory animals (from studies on 'pure' glyphosate), and 'strong evidence' of mechanistic data on the carcinogenicity (toxicity and oxidative stress) of 'pure' glyphosate and glyphosate-containing formulations. however, the european food safety authority has completed a peer review of glyphosate and concluded that glyphosate is unlikely to pose a cancer threat to humans and has refused to make the studies public. i therefore voted against the renewal of the authorisation of glyphosate.
in writing. ‒ there has been a lot of discussion in parliament these days about the use of glyphosate and the health implications that this substance can have, and with this vote i wanted to clarify my position on this. it is clear that glyphosate is now the most widely used herbicide in the world, and its use has increased its need for agricultural production. recent studies have attempted to clarify the implications of glyphosate for human health, in particular the european food safety authority (efsa) has concluded that 'glyphosate is unlikely to pose a carcinogenic hazard to humans'. my intention in voting was to seek a balanced compromise which takes account of scientific uncertainty and the fact that there are no viable alternatives at present. i therefore voted in favour of the proposal because i fully agree with the proposal to raise new safety standards which will make the monitoring of glyphosate residues in food more stringent, because i believe that, especially when it comes to health, prevention can never be too much.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the objection to the renewal of the approval of glyphosate. the primary objective of the european union must continue to be the protection of the health of its citizens. the world health organization considers glyphosate to be "probably carcinogenic". it is an indication that we cannot ignore and that we cannot ignore. we have only achieved a partial positive result today, but we must re-launch this positive aspect and send the commission a clear message that it is not possible, as was attempted, to renew the authorization of a dangerous product without further analysis for 15 years.
in writing. ‒ i am against this report because it does not take into account the risks of glyphosate and intergovernmental opinions.
in writing. ‒ given the considerable uncertainty surrounding the safety of glyphosate, the divergent views of the european food safety authority and the world health organisation's agency for research on melanoma, and the reluctance of the european food safety authority to disclose the studies on which its opinion is based, i welcome the hope that the european commission will not proceed with the renewal of the marketing of this substance for a maximum of 15 years until it is ruled out that it may be harmful to human health. the massive use of this type of herbicide in agricultural production and in our city parks would, if it were proved harmful, pose a serious threat to the health of european citizens. in addition, in view of the restrictive and precautionary measures taken by some member states and the opposition of some of them in the council of the european union, i believe it is of the utmost importance that the european commission postpone the decision on the extension of the marketing authorization for glyphosate and that, in the meantime, it carries out more in-depth studies on the effects of the substance on the environment and health. finally, in order to ensure maximum institutional credibility, i would like to see the efsi refrain from any further reservations about the publication of its studies.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the commission's draft implementing regulation renewing the approval of glyphosate, as some evidence has shown that, despite an increase in its use in recent years, this substance could pose a health hazard to people living in the vicinity of places where glyphosate is used. furthermore, it is not possible to say with certainty that glyphosate residues do not pose a danger to human health, as well as to animals and the environment. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the epp, together with a large majority in parliament, has reached an important compromise between the demands of agricultural production and those of health and environmental protection. the vote asked the commission to submit a new proposal for the renewal of the authorisation of glyphosate, which would take account of some fundamental changes. the ppe did not oppose this authorization on ideological grounds, but on the contrary, it distinguished itself by rejecting those amendments which proposed an absolute ban on the use of this substance for agricultural and professional use, voting in favour of an authorization reduced from 15 to 7 years, revocable and monitored. parliament called on the commission to review the classification of glyphosate on the basis of independent scientific studies and to disclose fully the scientific data used in the evaluation. by voting on this report on a point on which it is difficult for the member states to reach agreement, parliament is making its strength and representative weight felt, indicating a political line for the commission's action and offering the european council a position to which it can refer.
in writing. - i voted no to this resolution, which i consider shamefully hypocritical. most of the premises are in fact fully shared: point out that the weedkiller glyphosate is a pervasive chemical (it is present in the food chain and in our bodies), which has been declared "probably carcinogenic to humans" by the iarc but which has been deemed safe by efsa based on information contained in studies that are not made public because the producers of glyphosate believe that this would harm their commercial interests. these premises and the precautionary principle, which is also repeatedly invoked in the resolution, have only one possible logical consequence: the request to the european commission not to renew the authorisation for glyphosate. the resolution, however, is unreasonable and explicitly calls for the authorization to be renewed. it is simply outrageous. hence my no. i hope, however, that the european commission will give effect to two minor requests contained in the resolution: the independent review of all scientific literature on the toxicity of glyphosate (meaning: review of the efsa assessment) and the publication of the secret studies used by efsa to declare glyphosate safe.
in writing. i voted against this resolution which, thanks to a last-minute amendment by the ppe group, was transformed into a call to renew the authorisation for glyphosate for another 7 years, although the original text submitted for voting contained an unconditional objection to the renewal of the licence, for which the movement fought hard. glyphosate is currently the most widely used herbicide in the world, but it has been classified as "probably carcinogenic to humans" by the international agency for research on cancer (iarc), based on studies that are certainly more reliable than those conducted by the european food safety authority, which, using data provided by the same companies that produce glyphosate, came to the opposite conclusion that the substance is "probably non-carcinogenic". the data, however, has not been published in order to "not harm the commercial interests" of these large companies. european legislation and the precautionary principle allow the eu to block the use of a substance that is potentially dangerous to human health and the environment, even in the presence of the slightest scientific doubt. however, in order not to damage the commercial interests of multinational companies and lobbies, the majority of parliament has preferred to accept such a serious risk to man and the environment. this is unfortunately what matters to the health of citizens and the environment in europe.
in writing. i voted against the resolution by which parliament calls on the european commission to renew for another seven years the authorisation of the use in agriculture of glyphosate, the active ingredient of a herbicide produced by the multinational monsanto. the commission's intention was to renew the authorization of glyphosate for a full 15 years and parliament's motion was originally designed to ask for the precautionary principle to be applied and to refuse the renewal altogether. the final text of the resolution as it came out would have allowed the european commission to reach a committee (where the fate of glyphosate is actually decided together with the member states) proposing 7 years, with the support of parliament. a scandalous concession which we of the five star movement could only forcefully reject. as a possible carcinogen, glyphosate is a real danger to humans. the heinrich böll foundation recently published a study with shocking results showing that glyphosate residues were detected in the urine of 99.6% of the more than 2 000 people monitored. the most significant values were found in children and adolescents. mine was a resounding no to glyphosate.

in writing. ‒ in recent years, the european union has been confronted with an extremely complex international scenario, characterised by a succession of perennial crises. economic difficulties, migration, instability and the development of conflicts on its borders result in a chronic lack of common solutions adapted to the challenges of our time. the kalniete report, which i supported with my vote today, effectively illustrates the scale of these threats and offers a range of practical solutions to bring the eu to the centre of the global stage. the main objective to be achieved is that of common defence. the full implementation of article 42 (7) teu must be the starting point for developing and defining a common defence policy framework leading to the achievement of a european defence union. permanent multinational military units, a joint defence force and the establishment of a permanent eu military headquarters are key elements of a plan to improve military crisis management capability. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy.

in writing. ‒ we europeans find ourselves in a more fragile and divided world today than we did 20 years ago: the problems of the international scene are approaching our doors, they are known to us and the answers they require are more pressing. the shortsightedness of many national governments is astonishing, however, as they persist in spending their energies on petty internal disputes rather than investing them in the federal progress that the globalized world today demands of europe. a europe that is still strong and has soft power throughout the world, but which is in danger of losing it if it does not return to strong international leadership and if it does not abide by its own values. the soft power that europe has in the world is that it is the home of welfare and rights, of peace and freedom, of art and technological development: without these elements, it is weak and its influence melts like snow in the sun. it is the responsibility of each of us in this parliament to do everything possible to overcome national selfishness and to safeguard the security and well-being of our citizens in a europe that we want to be more cohesive, more solidary and more in tune with its role in the world.
in writing. ‒ according to the report, the eu strategy should be based on: the identification and prioritisation of addressing threats and challenges; (b) the definition of the responses to be adopted in relation to them; (c) the determination of the resources to be allocated to them. the report stresses that the borders of each member state are the borders of the union and as such must be defended, but calls for the strengthening of the schengen system, the european border and coast guard and frontex. it also considers it of paramount importance to strengthen eu-nato cooperation. the transition to multinational military units, joint defence forces and the definition of a framework for a common defence policy leading ultimately to a european defence union must be considered. the eu must deliver on its commitments to enlargement and integration, based on policies designed to stimulate economic growth and an inclusive society. the current refugee crisis requires a holistic european approach and urgent and concerted action, using both external and internal instruments; calls for a long-term strategy and sustainable management of asylum, migration and readmission policies based on common principles and solidarity. i strongly oppose it.
in writing. ‒ the report addresses the european parliament's recommendations to the high representative on the elaboration of the new eu comprehensive strategy on the common foreign and security policy. as a member of the committee on foreign affairs i have tabled a number of amendments to overcome the criticisms of the draft report. the latter, in fact, had from the outset many controversial aspects, such as the approval of the decision requiring member states to spend 2% of their annual gdp on defence expenditure and the complete absence of any criticism of member states still reluctant to make a fair allocation of asylum seekers. the text of the report is also rather weak on the question of the creation of a genuine european intelligence service. i have to say that i am very pleased that the commission has taken the necessary steps to ensure that the amendments which i have proposed are not taken into account in the final drafting of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which gives an account of the relationship between the european union and the current global context as it sets out important objectives with which i could not agree more. i am in favour of such aims as greater security for our citizens and the safeguarding of our values and models of society, or even the attempt to stabilise the relationship of europe itself with its member states and individual regions with the aim of strengthening the existing coalition. i am in favour of this report in essence because it moves towards a more interconnected european union at home and in foreign policy as a concrete response to the global changes to which we are constantly exposed.
in writing. ‒ the report aims to clarify the european parliament's position on the overall strategy of the european union on foreign and security policy. the report sets out the eu's objectives on these issues. the eu now faces internal and external threats (including climate change, large migration flows and international terrorism) that are very different from those identified in the 2003 security strategy. i think that the desire to seek greater solidarity between member states on security issues is fully understandable, as is parliament's call for effective use of the many international instruments available for managing the migration crisis and the attention paid to sustainable development and the protection of human rights. nevertheless, several critical aspects emerge from the report, including the decision to reserve 2% of the gdp of the member states for military resources. the report also fails to provide adequate and sufficient information on the fair distribution of asylum seekers in the various eu countries and on the creation of european intelligence. i am voting against.
in writing. ‒ this resolution re-emphasises the importance of a european strategy, in line with its core values, to respond to common threats to the eu and its member states. issues such as internal and external security, the refugee crisis, regional conflicts, arms exports and climate change affect all member states and their citizens. they therefore require a unified, concrete and proactive response at european level. my vote in favour expresses my support for a european strategy for the effective management of these issues. in particular, i agree that the eu should contribute more to stability, security and respect for human rights in neighbouring countries and in the southern neighbourhood, and at the same time involve national parliaments, regional actors and civil society in the process of implementing the strategy.
in writing. ‒ today, the european union is surrounded by an arc of instability stretching from eastern europe to north africa and the middle east: the policies of migration and the threat of terrorism from the jihadist "isis" are two clear examples. as the kalniete report points out, the eu is divided internally and unable to react because of different strategic visions among member states which have so far prevented coordination of foreign and defence policy. as the resolution recalls, one of the eu's fundamental objectives is to promote peace, its values and the well-being of its citizens, while ensuring their security (article 21 teu). i therefore believe that in order to deal with the threats and challenges facing the eu, there must be greater cooperation between member states in implementing a common framework for defence policy. the report stresses the importance of improving intelligence exchanges between member states in order to ensure adequate control mechanisms that strengthen international security.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe it is a priority for the union to strengthen its foreign policy action by identifying the interests shared by all 28 member states in every region of the world and in every relevant policy area. the global challenges we face today call for coherent and structured cooperation in defence research, the industrial base and cyber defence through the sharing of data, resources and good practices, in order to use national defence budgets more efficiently. i also support the importance of urging the commission to achieve the objectives set in 2013 for a comprehensive security regime, as well as to deploy joint defence forces to improve military crisis management capability and ensure emergency planning. eu-nato cooperation should therefore be strengthened, ensuring coordination between operations and supporting action beyond the eu's borders. finally, the union must commit itself to filling the security gap in the neighbouring areas and creating conditions of stability in line with its values, by addressing the causes of the current conflicts, migratory flows and refugee crisis.
in writing. ‒ in recent years, the european union has faced several threats to its security. a more connected world requires a comprehensive european strategy for participation. we must think of a strategy that can withstand prolonged crises. there are some shared parts of the report, such as the need to move towards collective solidarity between member states on security issues, the necessary long-term strategy to manage migration crises, the many references to sustainable development and respect for human rights as the guiding principles of the security strategy. despite the positive aspects, there are a number of critical aspects such as the reference to the need for enhanced cooperation between the eu and nato and the call for member states to spend at least 2% of their gdp on military resources. but nothing about the efficient use of europol and nothing about the sharing of information between the investigative agencies. although some of our amendments have been accepted, the final text is still unacceptable and i therefore voted against.

in writing. ‒ in the two-year period 2013-2015, the volume of trade between the european union and central asia increased by 8%. kazakhstan alone (with which an enhanced partnership and cooperation agreement was recently concluded) absorbed 88% of the total eu-central asia trade volume, worth eur 31 million. the final partnership agreements have already been concluded with kyrgyzstan, tajikistan and uzbekistan, while a provisional agreement is still pending with turkmenistan. the situation is different for accession to the wto: some of these countries are recent members, others have a long-term objective. wto membership provides greater guarantees and legal protection for investors, but corruption remains a problem throughout the region. in revising the eu-central asia strategy, the commission has included economic development, trade, investment, energy and transport as its main objectives. for all these reasons, i voted in favour and i hope that the eu will call for more efforts to combat corruption, reduce bureaucratic burdens and provide greater protection for foreign investors.

in writing. ‒ in the early months of 2016, the zika virus outbreak and spread was seen in tropical and subtropical regions of the americas. it is a viral disease, transmitted by mosquitoes of the genus aedes, which generally causes a mild infection, except for pregnant women, in which case there is a high probability for newborns to develop fetal microcephaly. the who has declared the spread of the virus to be a public health emergency of international concern. the eu has therefore decided to allocate €10 million from the horizon 2020 programme for research and development of a vaccine, while a further €40 million could be earmarked for research on malaria and infectious diseases. for these reasons i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the zika virus, first isolated in 1947 in uganda, is transmitted by mosquitoes of the genus aedes. on february 1, 2016, the who declared the zika virus epidemic a public health emergency of international concern, following the serious events that affected the northeastern part of brazil. the emergence of the virus has been associated, in this situation, with a concentration of cases of microcephaly and other neurological diseases, among which guillain-barré syndrome stands out in particular. some transmission incidents have already occurred in the outermost regions of the eu but the greatest risk for the continent could occur in the summer of 2016 through autochthonous transmission of the virus via vectors. the resolution adopted by parliament and supported by me calls on the commission to consult member states and third countries which have experience in monitoring and combating the aedes mosquito, to draw up an action plan to prevent the spread of the virus in europe and to provide assistance to the most affected states and regions. in addition to the funds already allocated for research, provision should be made for the free and targeted distribution of sufficient mechanical barriers such as mosquito nets and condoms, in particular to prevent sexual transmission.
in writing. ‒ the world health organisation has classified the zika virus as an 'international public health emergency' because it poses a potential threat to the health of european citizens. i agree with the text that stresses the need to provide assistance to third countries affected by the epidemic and i think it is appropriate that the european centre for disease prevention and control (ecdc) establish a committee of experts to monitor the situation and prepare a clear plan of action to prevent the spread of this virus in europe. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ as declared by the who last february, the zika virus epidemic is a public health emergency of international concern. if we are to help stop the epidemic and prevent it from spreading further to other parts of the world, including europe, we must provide a rapid and coordinated response at european level, capable of acting on several fronts. these include support for research into the virus, for which there is as yet no vaccine, and, of vital importance, prevention. as the resolution adopted today underlines, we must coordinate with our international partners, and in particular with the countries most affected by the epidemic, on both fronts. it is necessary to clarify the possible causal links between the virus and cases of severe brain malformations in latin america, as well as the actual transmission of the virus, while contributing to the development of effective cures and vaccines available to the most vulnerable segments of society. finally, we must take appropriate measures quickly to prevent crossborder transmission of the infection and its spread in europe.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this document because i believe that the zika virus, which is currently affecting south america and has serious side effects, especially on foetuses, must be eradicated as soon as possible and that the european union must make a consistent effort to do so.
in writing. ‒ recent major outbreaks of zika virus, notably in french polynesia in 2013, brazil and colombia in 2015, have led to the declaration of a public health emergency by the international health regulations emergency committee. although not yet scientifically proven, there is a more than probable relationship between malformations and microcephaly in children born to mothers who contracted the virus during pregnancy. in this context, the european union must intensify its efforts to support more scientific studies on the nature of the virus and its development in europe and the world, and promote the implementation of a prevention and response programme at european level and in cooperation with the main affected countries, with means and resources commensurate with a situation that should not be underestimated. in particular, work on the development of an effective vaccine in the short term needs to be intensified, and closer coordination between the member states and their national and european health authorities, including the european centre for disease prevention and control, needs to be supported.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the resolution in question, calling on the commission to propose an action plan to prevent the spread of the zika virus in europe and to provide assistance to member states and third countries involved in combating the epidemic. i call on the european centre for disease prevention and control (ecdc) to update its risk assessments and epidemiological bulletins regularly and to set up a committee of experts on communicable tropical diseases to effectively coordinate and monitor all measures to be implemented in the eu. i welcome the commission's decision to allocate eur 10 million for zika virus research and i think it is appropriate to focus on cases of severe congenital brain malformations in latin america and their suspected link with zika virus infection. i would stress that, in view of the likely further spread of zika virus infection, it is necessary for the international community to quickly put into practice the lessons learned from last year's ebola crisis.

author of the book. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the purpose of this question is to contribute to the process of reviewing the sme supporting factor, which is a key measure for access to credit for small and mediumsized enterprises. smes are the engine of our economy, generating 55% of europe's gross domestic product and employing almost 80 million of our fellow citizens. however, in order to continue contributing to growth, small and mediumsized enterprises need to be supported with funding that enables them to go international, to keep up with the times, to invest in new projects, to hire new employees. the monetary policy of the european central bank is not sufficient to achieve this objective. quantitative easing, for example, and rate cuts can only support policies that are in favour of the real economy, but they cannot replace them. to avoid deflation - or worse, as the international monetary fund warned us just yesterday, a secular stagnation in europe - we need concrete measures, such as the ems supporting factor, a virtuous example of the balance between regulatory constraints and flexibility. this support factor has led to a 2% increase in bank credit to small and mediumsized enterprises over the past year and a half, compared with a 7% reduction in bank credit to large enterprises, and to a reduction in interest rates of some 20 basis points. in view of the end-of-year review, we call for the ems supporting factor to be confirmed and strengthened, extending its application also to loans above one and a half million euro, thus eliminating the threshold currently provided for. this would allow more companies, especially medium-sized ones, to benefit from the discount factor. i also share and support commissioner hill's commitment to make this instrument an international standard, through the basel committee.

in writing. ‒ today i supported the albrecht report on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data. the measure adopted today repeals directive 95/46/ec and sets new standards for the digital age, in a context of the increasingly widespread use of the internet and related technologies. the main objective is to protect citizens' data by establishing rules introducing a number of concepts such as the right to be forgotten, parental control and the provision of a minimum age for the use of online services. the one-stop shop system is particularly relevant for the business world, as the new legislation will provide important services to entrepreneurs. the adoption of the report is a major step forward in data protection and ensures full implementation of the rights enshrined in the lisbon treaty.
in writing. ‒ the new regulation on the protection of individuals modernises and updates the principles contained in the 1995 data protection directive, giving european citizens greater control over their personal data. in particular, the new legislation more clearly defines the rights of natural persons and the obligations of those who process data or who are responsible for their processing, by reorganising and completing the methods for ensuring compliance with the rules and the scope of the sanctions for those who violate them. among the new measures, some of the most interesting are the right for european citizens to transfer their data to a new internet provider, to know if their data has been hacked or the ban on mass surveillance and the introduction of a time limit for the retention of personal data. the new regulation, which applies to all companies handling data on european citizens, even if they are not established in the european union, is an important step forward in clarifying and updating the regulatory framework in a fundamental and highly sensitive area.
in writing. ‒ the data protection package had a very long parliamentary process, lasting for a number of years. in short, we are satisfied with the final result, because a real regulation of data is fundamental and necessary. the most critical point to be made is the legislative distortion of some of the provisions, but overall the safeguards in the handling and processing of personal data and the consequent guarantees for the privacy of all citizens that are provided meet the minimum criteria we have always demanded.
in writing. ‒ after careful reading and discussion in the house, i have voted in favour of the report on the motion for a resolution on the following grounds: the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data, as well as the free movement of data and thus the related issue of privacy, in the form of aggregated data, and the systems used to protect them (encryption), require solutions at european, if not global, level. this is in line with the ethical principles of careful evaluation of the use of new technologies and with my recent question on pnr, in which i pointed out that it has considerable costs and takes a long time to implement which may not correspond to the real needs of law enforcement, especially in the case of the notorious terrorist emergencies. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment. the creation of a clear legal framework on the use of personal data is therefore necessary in the personal data protection package, since an aggregate amount of information could violate privacy and, paradoxically, refine terrorist techniques.
in writing. ‒ the 2015 eurobarometer data show that european citizens are particularly sensitive to the online disclosure and control of personal information. the protection of personal data is a fundamental right of the european union enshrined in the treaty of lisbon: the commission has therefore taken effective and up-to-date measures to protect it. the commission's proposal to introduce two new legislative instruments to protect both citizens and businesses is therefore to be welcomed. the general data protection regulation, by ensuring first of all better information on what happens to personal data once it is shared, contains two other points of particular interest: the so-called right to be forgotten and the minimum age for using online services. a single set of rules applying to businesses offering online services in the union can further facilitate cross-border data exchange and ensure greater economic and social integration. the new proposal for a directive, the first instrument to harmonise 28 different legal systems on data exchange, facilitates the work of both national law enforcement agencies and european agencies at a time, such as the present, which requires the greatest possible cooperation. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation, on which parliament has been working for almost four years. it was time to replace the old 1995 directive, since the traffic of data has changed a lot since then and at the same time it has become necessary to find a balance between the sacred right to the protection of personal data, enshrined in the european charter of human rights, and the unstoppability of the flow of data in the world. i think that the european parliament's negotiating team has done a good job, but i am prepared to question the whole text if problems of any kind should arise from its application.

in writing. ‒ by voting in favour of this resolution, i wanted to support the european parliament's endorsement of the council's position at first reading on the adoption of the regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data. i believe that this resolution represents a historic milestone in providing a single legal framework in europe which will eliminate the current divergences between national data protection laws. this is a step towards a compromise between the needs of privacy and consumer rights on the one hand and the needs of a competitive digital market and a transnational security system on the other. european citizens will finally be informed about the use and breach of their personal data, without compromising the innovation of the digital single market and the fight against crime.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the recommendation for second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data and repealing directive 95/46/ec (data protection regulation). i believe that in the present context it is essential to protect the fundamental rights and freedoms of individuals, and in particular their right to the protection of personal data, and at the same time i believe that it is essential to guarantee free movement within the borders of the european union.
in writing. directive 95/46/ec of the european parliament and of the council aims to harmonise the protection of the fundamental rights and freedoms of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data. the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data is a fundamental and also inviolable right, which must be recognised and guaranteed irrespective of the nationality or residence of the data subject. although its objectives remain valid today, directive 95/46 ec has not been able to prevent the fragmentation of the way in which the protection of personal data is applied in the eu, not least because it was conceived and approved in the pre-internet and pre-social network era, which undoubtedly changed and revolutionized the way we handle personal data and information. for these reasons, a revision of the legislation was necessary, which was made on the basis of the needs of the digital age in order to give citizens greater control over their private information, with greater confidence and legal certainty also for european companies.
in writing. ‒ in view of the council's position at first reading on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data, i would like to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the rapid pace of technological change has made it imperative to update the legislation governing the processing and protection of personal data. the old 1995 directive was adopted when only a small percentage of citizens had access to the internet and social networks, online banking and e-commerce did not yet exist. today the internet affects almost every aspect of our lives and an ever-increasing amount of personal data is being put online. it is of paramount importance that this data is handled appropriately. that is why an update of the regulation is so important. it is up to date and gives citizens back control over their personal data. for the first time, we have a harmonised system of protection covering all 28 member states of the union. building trust in online environments is crucial for economic development. lack of trust is holding consumers back from buying online and using new services and risks slowing down the development of innovative technological applications. the new package makes it clear to everyone that the eu is serious about protecting the rights of european citizens, helping to create the necessary climate of trust.
in writing. ‒ the new eu data protection rules aim to give citizens greater control over their personal data and to create a high and uniform level of data protection across the eu in the digital age. the reform sets minimum standards for the use of data for judicial and police purposes. the draft also provides for the establishment of a european data protection board, which will include representatives of all 28 independent supervisory authorities and replace the existing article 29 committee. the project also provides for the transfer of personal data to third countries and international organisations. for all these reasons i voted in favour of the regulation.
in writing. ‒ the internet is no longer just a useful platform for finding information, but a tool that is part of our lives and contains a part of them. the law of persons must therefore find a way to adapt to these changes. that is why i voted in favour of the recommendation proposed by parliament on this regulation, because it represents a further step forward by europe in protecting people in the digital age. it aims to ensure that personal data are respected (the right to be forgotten) and requires that they be used as transparently and clearly as possible (informed consent), so that the citizen-user can know and make an informed decision about the use of his data. the vote aims to harmonise european policy on the protection of individuals, putting their rights at the centre, including in the digital sphere, and providing a clear framework for eu businesses, to the benefit of their competitiveness. the opportunities offered to businesses by the digital market should not be underestimated, given the greater integration of the single market. but these opportunities can only be such if they also guarantee respect for the rights of citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which aims to update the directive on the protection of personal data and to give greater protection to natural persons. in recent years, we have seen an exponential growth in the sharing, collection and global flow of data. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data by the community institutions and bodies. this has necessitated more modern and uniform regulation at european level to protect citizens. the new regulation defines the rights of natural persons, such as the need for consent to the processing of personal data, the right to rectification and erasure of data and facilitated access to their personal data. it also sets out the general obligations of those who process or are responsible for the processing of personal data, including the obligation to implement appropriate security measures in relation to the risk associated with the operations carried out and to report personal data breaches.
in writing. ‒ after four years of long and complex negotiations, we have finally approved today the data protection package, which updates the european privacy framework to the challenges posed by the digital evolution to the rights of citizens and businesses. the first element of the package is the regulation on the processing of personal data by industry and public authorities, which will ensure a high and uniform level of data protection throughout the union. the regulation will enable citizens to better manage their data, while businesses will be able to seize the opportunities offered by the digital single market through a simplification of administrative burdens. the new rules include provisions on the right to be forgotten, conditions for 'clear consent' to the processing of personal data, the right to know about the breach of one's personal data, clarity of information on privacy policies, stricter enforcement of these provisions and administrative fines of up to 4% of annual turnover for companies that breach these provisions. for these reasons i voted in favour of the measure.
in writing. ‒ the recently adopted directive on the protection of personal data in the field of activities to combat illegal activities aims to protect data processed for the purposes of the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences or the execution of criminal sanctions. in accordance with article 8 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, as well as article 16 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which enshrine the right of every person to the protection of personal data concerning him or her, it is essential to ensure a high and uniform level of protection of personal data at european level. at the same time, however, it is necessary to facilitate the exchange of personal data between the respective national intelligence services in order to ensure greater security and prevent crime. in this sense, i think that the directive in question strikes a good balance between these two different requirements, guaranteeing the right to confidentiality and, at the same time, giving the police the possibility of better countering and preventing the occurrence of illegal activities.

in writing. ‒ the directive on the processing of personal data by the competent authorities for criminal proceedings and investigations ensures strong protection of the rights of all european citizens. this is a fundamental guarantee. in fact, if data concerning suspects, witnesses or victims were not properly processed, their security as well as their right to privacy or to a fair trial would be compromised. for the first time, strict rules are now established, which apply equally to all european citizens. and all police forces in europe must respect these fundamental rights. this harmonisation will make it much easier to exchange information between member states, so as to ensure that law enforcement agencies have the information they need to prosecute suspected terrorists and international criminals. the tragic events in paris and brussels have made it clear that the real problem is not the lack of information on terrorist suspects, but the fact that this information has not been used or shared effectively by national police forces. the approved package will play an important role in correcting this by providing police and judicial authorities with harmonised rules on how to process and share data.
in writing. ‒ the data protection directive for police and criminal justice authorities is part of a data protection reform package proposed by the commission, which also includes a general data protection regulation. ensuring a uniform and high level of protection of personal data of natural persons and facilitating the exchange of personal data between the competent authorities of the member states is essential in order to ensure effective cooperation between judicial and police authorities in criminal matters. this requires that the rights and freedoms of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data by the competent authorities for the purposes of the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences enjoy an equivalent level of protection in all member states. the reform package will benefit individuals by strengthening their fundamental rights and freedoms in relation to the processing of personal data and confidence in the digital environment. i voted in favour of all of this.
in writing. ‒ this new directive on the processing of personal data of natural persons will facilitate the free movement of such information for the purposes of the prevention, investigation and detection of crime. however, judicial and police authorities will have to both ensure that personal data are processed lawfully and collected for specific, explicit and legitimate purposes and provide clear and understandable information to the data subject, who will have the right to request any restriction of processing. i believe that in the fight against transnational crime and terrorism, clear and consistent data protection rules at european level and closer cooperation between the competent authorities in each member state are necessary to ensure the safety of citizens. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ in the context of the personal data protection package, i voted in favour of the draft directive on the processing of personal data transferred for the purposes of judicial and police cooperation. the measure sets out, for the first time, minimum standards for the processing of data on victims, witnesses and suspects in each member state in the areas of preventing, combating and prosecuting crime and the enforcement of criminal sanctions, thus facilitating cooperation between law enforcement agencies in the eu against transnational criminal and terrorist acts. only by establishing common rules for the exchange of information between the competent authorities will they be able to overcome the distrust which has hitherto prevented genuine judicial and police cooperation to prevent the occurrence of crimes planned and committed in more than one member state. for these reasons i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive.
in writing. ‒ i strongly supported the directive on the protection of trade and business secrets. the proposal, which unifies the policy of the 28 member states on this subject, will provide firm guarantees of protection for companies, making european soil even more attractive for future investment. in the age of digitisation, sharing and 'given money', it was necessary to build a set of rules to protect businesses, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, from the risk of losing their trade secrets and, therefore, their wealth. with this directive, europe is taking the lead in the world in terms of protection in the digital market, while maintaining its principles of freedom of expression and movement. the s&d group's efforts have led to the introduction of special safeguards for journalists, whistle blowers and workers with sensitive data who wish to change their working environment.
in writing. ‒ the collection of passenger data (european pnr) is, according to the commission, a way of collecting data on individuals and increasing the safety of european citizens. we believe that systematic and general data collection can be useful for ensuring security if and only if there is a related obligation to cooperate and exchange relevant information. in our view, this directive sacrifices the right to privacy without guaranteeing the security of european citizens. for these reasons i would have voted against.
in writing. ‒ pnr codes, linked to the information that all passengers provide to airlines when booking flights, are one of the most important tools for preventing and detecting serious crime and terrorist-related acts. the kirkhope report, which i supported in parliament today, effectively describes the innovations approved in the collection, sharing and analysis of pnr information. the new directive requires member states to set up a passenger information unit (piu) to collect booking codes from airlines and store them for a period of five years. six months after the transfer of data, certain elements such as name, address and contacts will be masked to ensure the protection of passengers' privacy. the new procedure will make it possible to store, process and transfer data more efficiently, while at the same time providing protection for passengers and enhancing the action of law enforcement and intelligence services.

in writing. ‒ the dramatic attacks in paris and brussels in recent months have accelerated the approval of the pnr register, an important new tool that will facilitate the collection of data on air travellers to and from the european union, facilitating checks by police forces and the various judicial authorities, thus making an important contribution to the fight against terrorism. despite the positive elements that the new pnr introduces, i would point out that there are some critical points, such as the fact that the new measure does not provide for a form of automatic exchange of pnr data between the member states. once again, the blind opposition of the more conservative fringes of parliament has prevented the approval of an important element which would have further increased the effectiveness of the whole system. but unless the governments of the member states decide to deepen cooperation further, by means of dialogue and the continuous and timely exchange of information in their possession, we shall never be able to give a complete and exhaustive answer to the difficult problems we are facing. the hope is that we will soon have a single european intelligence service.
