in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the new directive regulating the use of reservation number data (pnr) for the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of terrorist offences and serious crime. this is an important new tool in the fight against terrorists and traffickers. by collecting, sharing and analysing pnr information, our intelligence agencies are able to detect suspicious patterns of behaviour that need to be verified. pnrs are not a magic formula, but member states with national pnr systems have once again demonstrated that such systems are highly effective. understandably, concerns have been expressed about the collection and retention of personal data. as a member of the s&d group, i fought for the pnr to be voted in plenary alongside the data protection package, because i strongly believe that the exchange of personal data must be accompanied by the creation of a clear legal framework on their use.
in writing. ‒ the use and exchange of passenger data has raised many concerns and fears among citizens and practitioners about the various implications of privacy legislation. pnr data, which is information provided by passengers when booking air tickets, will be shared by carriers with member states and managed by a dedicated national authority passenger information unit (pii) which will use it to investigate persons who may be involved in terrorist offences or serious crime. in fact, many countries already collect such data and have followed international standards in the absence of european provisions. the directive, on the other hand, harmonises the system of collection and processing and avoids disparities in the protection of personal data. it is an important tool in countering the terrorist threat, but it will not protect against attacks if it is not accompanied by greater cooperation between national law enforcement authorities and the intelligence systems of the eu countries. i voted in favour of this because i think it is a good compromise which has managed to strike a balance between data protection and security requirements. it was not an easy task, nor was it a given.
in writing. ‒ this is one of the most sensitive and at the same time most important issues we are dealing with given the recent terrorist attacks. this proposal deals with the use of passenger name record (pnr) data for the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of terrorist offences and other serious criminal offences. i believe that the basis for an effective way of combating this new type of crime is the exchange of information, without which any police system would be fruitless. that is the direction this report is taking and that is why i voted in favour of it, because if carefully analysed, pnr data can be an effective tool for detecting and controlling criminal and terrorist activities. it is clear that more decisive action is needed today and cooperation between member states in the exchange of such information is, in my view, the first step in this direction of preventing and prosecuting terrorist offences. my group was right to insist on the timing of this measure, which has long since been forgotten in a drawer.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the establishment of the pnr for the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of terrorist offences. under the new directive, airlines will be required to provide the competent authorities with pnr data (each passenger's name, travel dates, itinerary, ticket details, travel agent with whom the flight was booked, payment methods used, seat number and baggage information) of flights arriving and departing from europe, all of this while protecting the privacy and personal data of individuals. this is a fundamental measure to ensure security and control in the transport sector, which has unfortunately been the target of attention by terrorists and violent organised groups over the years.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution of 14 april 2016 on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the use of booking reference data for the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of terrorist offences and serious crime. in fact, recent events have shown us that terrorist networks exploit the possibilities of links between eu countries, which have not been sufficiently controlled, to carry out their operations. the eu's inability to know who is entering or leaving its borders is seriously undermining its efforts to combat terrorism and other serious forms of crime. the need now arises for the eu to develop a document, the passenger name record, which lists information concerning individuals entering or leaving the eu. it is also important that this data is used for the sole purpose of ensuring better security for european citizens and with respect for their privacy.
in writing. ‒ eu countries will exchange data on passengers on flights. the pnr (passenger name record) directive, which is essentially the collection and sharing of passenger data/flight plans across europe, provides a single community regulation for the collection and exchange of information by authorities for prevention, investigation and prosecution purposes. a step forward in the fight against terrorism: the pnr tool will allow a closer fight to the so-called foreign fighters. five years to vote on the measure in plenary is too long. in any case, today's result is an important one which will make european citizens safer.
in writing. ‒ i abstain from the report which i consider to be good in some parts, but more could be done towards greater control and security.
in writing. ‒ today's vote on the pnr marks a victory for common sense in protecting citizens who, in the light of recent events, are calling for greater security. the european unions have for years prevented us, by voting against, from adopting the pnr directive. they sacrificed the possibility of greater security in the name of an instrumental, ideological and irresponsible vision of privacy protection that today, with the use of technological tools such as cameras, mobile phone tracking and social media, appears anachronistic. it took three attacks in just over a year and one of them could have been prevented according to the french authorities if the pnr had been in force to make the european left understand that there is no room for ideological positions when the lives of our citizens are at risk. it is now up to governments to make the directive operational as soon as possible.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the second report on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on the use of pnr data for the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of terrorist offences and serious crime, and i regard the adoption of this instrument and the legislation on the protection of personal data as a very important moment for the european union. i believe that the pnr directive is the solution to all problems and the ultimate weapon against terrorism, but i strongly support the need to increase the sharing and circulation of information on potential dangers between the authorities of individual states: the tragic events in paris and brussels clearly demonstrate how better sharing and exchange of information and intelligence could have saved countless lives and perhaps even prevented attacks. i believe that the directive ensures a balanced legal framework for the sharing and use of such data. it is now up to the member states to implement the legislation both in law and in practice, by organising real and fruitful cooperation between the competent national authorities in order to guarantee the security required by all european citizens.
in writing. ‒ after years of work, parliament has succeeded in passing this important measure on the air passenger data register. the commission is proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the following areas: these measures will certainly play an important role in the fight against terrorism, but they are by no means the only ones. once collected, this information must be processed and transferred and used effectively by the competent national authorities. and above all, the data being exchanged should serve primarily as a criminal intelligence tool and not as a border control tool. i also welcome all safeguards relating to the protection of passenger data, in particular those prohibiting the processing of data revealing the racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religion or philosophical beliefs, trade union membership, state of health, life or sexual orientation of the data subject.
in writing. following the tragic terrorist events that have struck some european capitals, there is a clear demand from our citizens to increase security levels. that is why we have been pushing for the unblocking of the so-called pnr, the register of passengers on flights, and we have won the political battle after four years of work, and have now got it approved. we now have an additional, strategic tool for the fight against terrorism and organised crime, which will allow us to monitor suspicious persons and their movements, to prevent possible attacks. the proposal creates a system whereby airlines operating flights between a third country and at least one eu state are required to provide pnr data (including name, address, route and credit card used) to law enforcement authorities and allows the rules under which these authorities will be able to use the data received to investigate and prosecute potential crimes to be determined. we've given up a small portion of our privacy for important reasons of safety for all of our citizens.
in writing. ‒ finally, after months and months of delay, parliament has finally approved the pnr directive. i am convinced that it will be a useful tool in assessing any threats arising from so-called foreign fighters. in a time of emergency we must give concrete answers to our citizens to ensure their safety.
in writing. ‒ in view of the recent and despicable attacks perpetrated on the borders of the european union, we could only support the call for greater data and information sharing and closer cooperation at european level. the gravity of the terrorist phenomenon, the interconnectedness of the challenges it poses and the common character of the threats and dangers facing the people of europe cannot, in fact, be separated from common responses and measures. the cowardly attacks have exposed the weakness of a security system based on fragmentation. however, we welcome the report only as a first step towards greater integration and information sharing, in full respect of the rights to privacy and data processing, more systematic and structured. in the face of the terrorist threat, there is no other possibility of a common front and common struggle. we hope, however, that the member states will adopt the measure swiftly and we call on national governments to make better and more effective use of the legislative instruments, starting with the sharing of vehicle registration information already available to them.
in writing. ‒ whereas the commission adopted a proposal for a council framework decision on the use of reservation code data as early as 2007 and whereas this proposal is now considered to be obsolete; whereas the use of such information would be for the purpose of intercepting, monitoring and prosecuting criminals; whereas there has been an increase in criminal and terrorist activities in recent years and the use of passenger reservation codes would allow for more effective tracking of persons without thereby conflicting with the rules on the protection of personal data; finally, given that a decentralised operating system would impose less burden on the member states than a centralised mechanism, i would vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i supported the pnr directive because i believe it is a fundamental tool for monitoring our security, as i believe it is necessary to have a common and single european standard on this issue and not 28 fragmented regulations which would of course guarantee us much less effectively. on the other hand, we must not think that such legislation alone will enable us to defeat terrorism in europe. a broader and more complex action of intelligence, police coordination and investment in education can really take terror off our streets. only genuine joint action and solidarity by each member state can protect us from attacks such as those that have struck paris and brussels. as we have said many times, our group has been very keen to see the pnr directive adopted at the same time as the data protection package, precisely because it is clear that our need for greater security does not mean a reduction in our right to privacy, although some freedoms as we have known them up to now will inevitably have to change. i believe that with this vote we have taken a decisive step forward in the fight against terrorism, but we must not forget that this is only a small part of it and that much more concrete action will have to follow.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposal has two main objectives: (i) harmonise the obligation for air carriers operating flights between a third country and the territory of at least one member state to transmit pnr data to law enforcement authorities and (ii) identify the criteria under which law enforcement authorities may use such information, in particular for the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of terrorist offences and serious crime. the proposed system is compulsory and each member state will have two years to set up an operational system. this is a major step forward in the fight against international terrorism and finally, overcoming the obstructionism expressed earlier by the socialists and democrats, the european parliament has succeeded in passing this important piece of legislation. the measures taken regarding the transmission and use of pnr data do not impede the freedom of movement and do not compromise the right of entry of citizens or their privacy, but contribute to protecting their security. i voted in favour of this resolution, convinced that the eu still has a long way to go before it can defeat all its internal and external enemies.
in writing. ‒ the extraordinary situation we are experiencing in europe, symbolized by the attacks in paris and brussels, required europe to raise its security standards to protect the freedom and life of all its citizens. that is why i voted in favour of a proposal for which the epp has long campaigned, namely the establishment of a european passenger name record (pnr) system for air carriers. it's not about collecting additional data. the collection of passenger data (in particular from air carriers) will be for the sole purpose of finally making available the information already collected by airlines, to help prevent serious crime. each member state of the union will therefore be called upon to make effective the sharing at european level of information of value to the security forces, particularly in the fight against terrorism. in the spirit of a civilization based on the right of the person, the directive explicitly includes, in addition to the right to privacy, the reference to international conventions signed by the member states, including the convention on human rights, to prevent any ideological abuse in the use of such data.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the compromise reached on the pnr directive on reservation code data which aims to regulate uniformly the processing and sharing of such data by member states in the fight against terrorism and serious crime. under the directive, airlines will be obliged to transfer pnr data such as names, travel dates, itineraries and payment methods of passengers on non-eu flights to the member state where the flight is scheduled to land or take off. in addition, each member state will have to set up a passenger information unit to identify individuals to be subject to further verification by the competent authorities. i believe that this proposal represents a real step forward and a useful tool in the fight against terrorism and international crime, especially in view of the recent events in paris and brussels, where so-called foreign fighters have been targeted. i hope that the pnr directive will make it possible to identify not only those who are already suspected, but also those who are not yet known to the authorities.
in writing. ‒ achieving the best possible balance between ensuring the safety and protection of the privacy of european citizens has been the concern of the european parliament in the long legislative process of adopting the directive on the use of reservation code data (pnr), the system for exchanging information between member states' investigating authorities on airline passengers on international flights. that is why we, as a socialist group, have called for the adoption of the data protection package and the pnr directive together, in order to create an appropriate regulatory framework for the processing of data and the fight against transnational crime and terrorism. the pnr directive provides for the possibility for law enforcement agencies to have unrestricted access for 6 months to all personal data of passengers on international flights for the purposes of prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of serious crime such as terrorism; after six months, these data will still be available for five years but through a more complex procedure and only for some specific offences. passenger information communicated by airlines to member states will be handled by appropriate national authorities in accordance with specific criteria, conditions and rights for citizens.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the directive on the processing of reservation number data (pnr). the legislation will oblige airlines to pass on data on passengers on transcontinental flights to the authorities of european countries, in order to help fight terrorism. the interinstitutional process has been very long and arduous. the need to develop more stringent security measures has been reconciled with the need to protect the privacy of our fellow citizens. the socialist and democratic group has played an important role in this, firmly affirming the principle that security without respect for the democratic principles of the rule of law is unacceptable. with this vote we have voted to reject a package which is certainly more balanced than the initial proposal. the attention of the socialists and democrats to the subject, however, will remain very high. the security policies of the various member states will need to be coordinated more closely in the future to ensure that we can respond as effectively as possible to the global challenges we are now facing.

in writing. ‒ the harmonious development of an efficient market economy requires that a difficult balance be struck between the free movement of information and the right to protection of business secrets. that is why i have today supported the le grip report on the proposal for a directive on the protection of confidential know-how and business information against their unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure. the directive aims to bring together national rules, which differ widely, by providing for common definitions, measures and penalties capable of providing greater legal certainty for operators and strengthening the european single market. it is an effective instrument which will ensure the protection of the rights of workers, whistleblowers and the freedom of the press while not hindering those who report illegal or unlawful practices by their companies.
in writing. ‒ this report highlights that the protection of sensitive information in the field of trade is a cross-border problem, which must be solved at community level. our companies need a common system of rules and protection in all the member states to prevent the theft of information covered by trade secrets and a legal instrument to defend themselves at international level. i have always fought to defend our businesses, hence my vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the draft directive adopted today marks an important step towards creating a more uniform and effective legal framework at european level for the protection of professional know-how and confidential commercial information which underpin the development and competitiveness of our companies. parliament has succeeded in making considerable improvements to the commission's initial proposal, arriving at a balanced text which, it should be stressed, is not intended to defend illegal or improper conduct by companies by masking it as trade secrets, but which aims to protect the intangible assets of european companies, in particular smes, by guaranteeing them equal conditions and legal certainty in all member states, to the benefit of the functioning of the european single market. not only that: we have succeeded in inserting in the final text specific exceptions to protect freedom of expression and information, workers and those who disseminate certain information not necessarily relating to illegal conduct, but also irregular or incorrect in the public interest. the so-called whistleblowers are therefore protected by the directive, although we ask the commission to submit new proposals to deal specifically with the system of guarantees to be reserved for these persons.

in writing. ‒ businesses and not-for-profit research institutes invest in the acquisition, development and application of know-how and information, which are the currency of the knowledge economy and allow for competitive advantage. it is this capacity for investment, innovation and efficiency that constitutes the added value of most of the products - goods and services - produced by european union enterprises: goods and services which are world-renowned for their high quality, for their scientific and technological excellence and for the wealth of knowledge and skills which underpin them. these products, due to the investments in research and development by the companies that produce them and the high quality they represent, tend to have a significantly higher initial fixed cost to the producer than less advanced and lower quality products made in third countries. it is therefore in the urgent interest of all eu member states to protect the trade secrets and know-how of european companies and to do everything necessary to block the dissemination of illegal information, while also ensuring fair processes for all companies.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on trade secrets because it is concerned with pursuing a point which i believe is fundamental to the development and growth of our countries under the banner of the european union. it is clear that collective development is easier and faster in a space of mutual sharing of commercial information and cooperation between the various companies spread over the territory. i believe, however, that it is also necessary to protect the so-called 'trade secret' which rewards the initiative and innovation of the individual company and also allows the various products to be distinguished from one another by the quality label, a quality to which i am particularly sensitive. i therefore voted in favour of this report because it seeks to strike the right balance between these two elements, with the main aim of laying the foundations for a further development engine for the whole of the european union, while at the same time ensuring, in this shared space, an adequate level of protection against unfair trading practices. i believe that protection against the unlawful acquisition, disclosure and use of trade secrets is essential to ensuring a fair business environment for businesses.
in writing. ‒ this proposal for a directive is particularly important because its main objective is to identify rules to improve the competitiveness of our enterprises. in particular, smes place a high value on trade secrets as they allow the creator to profit from his creation and innovations and to invest in research, development and innovation. our main objective is to protect smes from fraudulent practices to which they are increasingly exposed, such as theft, economic espionage, breach of confidentiality obligations, or all those practices which are aimed at the illegal appropriation of trade secrets. without effective and comparable legal instruments to protect trade secrets across europe, the incentives to undertake activities and invest in research and innovation will only decrease. it is therefore necessary to address the fragmentation of the legal system and to approximate national legislative systems, as well as to define at european level the situations in which the acquisition, use and disclosure of a trade secret is lawful or unlawful and to reduce the period of application of appeal procedures.

in writing. unlike intellectual property rights, which confer exclusivity on the possession of such a right, trade secrets, which also include manufacturing, and industrial secrets confer on third parties the right to use and develop their formula freely, and are not an exclusive right to the creation. it is well known that the processing of sensitive data is authorised only by the data controller and not by third parties who are not the holders of those rights, which is why infringement of those rights is to be regarded as unfair practice, that is to say, as infringement of an inalienable right. in particular, the report on the protection of trade secrets against their unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure sets out the safeguards to be adopted in the event of their unlawful acquisition by third parties, such as the award of damages for damage caused by them.

in writing. ‒ more than ten years have passed since the formal accession negotiations for turkey with the european union began. since then, the eu has made significant progress, moving considerably closer to meeting the copenhagen criteria and incorporating much of the acquis communautaire. however, the pace of reforms has slowed considerably in recent months. we are also witnessing a growing and worrying involution in the protection of freedom of expression and association, as well as an increasingly unstable situation characterized by the non-respect of the rights of ethnic-religious minorities and the lgbt community. despite a strong commitment to, for example, welcoming refugees, turkey is one of the countries with the highest number of imprisoned journalists in the world, and also has a critical level of corruption. a european, democratic, transparent turkey with an independent legal system which respects its minorities could be an important intermediary with the middle east and the muslim world, and could help to promote stability in the whole region. in this sense, we must continue to work and dialogue to ensure that this fundamental process of integration is completed.
in writing. ‒ the vote against the resolution is not only for the usual reasons but also because it calls for turkish to become an official language of the eu; there is still no reference to the armenian genocide. the resolution calls for eu-turkey cooperation on migrants to be separated from the ongoing negotiations on turkey's own accession to the european union. the text praises turkey for hosting the largest number of refugees in the world and stresses that it remains "a key strategic partner for the european union". the eu is also calling for the establishment of a european union-wide network of experts in the field of human rights. the general pace of reform in turkey has not only slowed, but in some areas, such as freedom of expression and the independence of the judiciary, there have been setbacks. the eu-turkey joint action plan on refugees and migration management should be implemented immediately. the urgent need for reforms of the judiciary, justice, freedom and security is reiterated.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the 2015 report on turkey. the country remains a strategic partner for the eu. with the launch of the eu-turkey action plan to tackle the refugee crisis, ankara is called upon to play a key role in resolving one of the most serious emergencies in recent decades. however, turkey is called upon to do much more to meet the copenhagen criteria. the time has come to align with eu standards, which necessarily requires the implementation of appropriate and effective reforms. the efforts which we are sure turkey will make in carrying out the eu-turkey action plan must be matched by efforts to strengthen the institutions and the process of democratization and modernisation in the country.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, particularly in view of the particular historical and political situation in which we find ourselves, in which it is necessary to strengthen cooperation between the european union and turkey. the aim is to offer support to turkey in ending hostilities in syria and to provide humanitarian aid to people in need. i also think it is essential not to forget the strategic importance of turkey for the energy security of the european union and that is why cooperation must be stimulated so that growth and development can be derived from this relationship for both sides.
in writing. ‒ i am voting against the report which calls, among other things, for turkish to become an official language of the european union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the 2015 report on turkey because i support the need to give greater democratic impetus to the country, especially in the areas of freedom of expression, media freedom, the rule of law and minority rights. today the european union and turkey face many challenges that still lack effective solutions, from immigration to respect for human rights, and above all respect for the freedom of expression of journalists. there is no doubt that turkey is an essential partner in solving the migrant crisis, but at the same time it is necessary to ensure that the rights of asylum seekers are fully respected. in addition, in this resolution the european parliament wishes to strongly condemn the intimidation of the media environment and i agree to express my deep concern at the deterioration over the last two years of the situation regarding freedom of speech, expression and opinion in the country. it is essential for turkey to fully align itself with european values, principles and criteria in order to continue on the path of european integration: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament.
in writing. ‒ whereas in 2005 the commission opened negotiations for the accession of turkey to the european union; whereas, pursuant to article 49 of the treaty on european union, any european state which respects and is committed to promoting the values of the eu may apply for membership and, to this end, turkey has already embarked on the path of economic and democratic reforms in order to align itself with the principles and values on which the european union is founded; whereas, however, many fundamental freedoms are still not guaranteed in the country and there is, on the contrary, a decline in respect for democracy; whereas, moreover, turkey has seen its security and territorial stability seriously undermined in recent weeks; whereas, finally, an agreement between the eu and the turkish government on the migrant crisis has recently been concluded; finally, considering that, on the basis of the comments made so far, greater eu-turkey cooperation is needed, i would vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's 2015 report on turkey and the advancement of the rule of law in this country is currently in a delicate situation. parliament cannot help but point out the serious shortcomings that still exist in turkey as regards respect for fundamental human rights, particularly those of minorities, freedom of the media and the independence of the judiciary. on the other hand, turkey is now undeniably a strategic partner of the european union in addressing the migration crisis that has been going on for several years and that led to the important agreement of 2016. the agreement now provides for a management of the migratory flows to europe which europe alone would not be able to cope with. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution because it strikes the right balance between the issues that dominate the panorama of eu-turkey relations today, urging the government in ankara to become aware of its democratic deficit and demanding that progress in cooperation and bilateral relations between the two countries be conditional on compliance with the conditions set by europe in this regard.
in writing. ‒ turkey is a key strategic partner for the european union. i believe that it is mutually beneficial to intensify political dialogue between the european union and turkey on foreign and security policy, the fight against terrorism and the management of migration flows. the threat of daesh and terrorism is a common threat which can be best and most rapidly defeated if we tackle it together. the agreement signed between the european union and turkey on migration is a first step towards joint management of borders and migration flows, but much remains to be done. the defence of human rights, the protection of minorities and the maintenance of the rule of law cannot be put on the back burner. we can do a lot together, but we must commit ourselves to each other.

in writing. ‒ the recent agreement concluded by the european council with turkey has been supported by parliament but raises some important issues. on the one hand, turkey's strategic role in addressing the refugee crisis is undeniable, considering that it took in two million and 700 thousand syrians in 2015 alone. the socialist and democratic group, on the other hand, is concerned about the current political situation in turkey, where freedom of expression and the press are not fully guaranteed and the kurdish conflict remains unresolved, and the consequent opportunity to conclude political agreements with it. i therefore voted in favour of the report by my socialist colleague, mrs kati piri, in line with the group. this report commits the european institutions to monitoring the state of democracy in turkey and to working for a ceasefire on the kurdish border. only if fundamental human rights are respected will it be possible to open negotiations for turkey's integration into the framework of european unification.

in writing. ‒ in 2009, alongside nato membership, the republic of albania applied for membership of the european union following the broad support of albanian political forces, and public opinion, for the european integration process. during these years, the country has made considerable efforts in the reform process, which have been embodied in plans and strategies for the reform of the public administration and the management of public finances. i voted in favour of the 2015 report on albania because i believe it is crucial to support its path of change and strengthening of the democratic system. corruption remains one of the country's major problems, but the government and the opposition have initiated effective measures that can be translated into a systematic reform of the judicial system, aimed at strengthening the independence of the authorities and cooperation between them. more efforts are needed in the area of the protection of minors, the creation of adequate environmental legislation and the tackling of gender inequalities, but the republic of albania appears to be positively moving towards future eu membership.

in writing. ‒ the outbreak of the international economic crisis has had a profound impact on the economic and social conditions of european households. the contraction of incomes, the rise in unemployment and the rise in the prices of basic goods and services have led to a downward movement that has brought an impressive number of citizens into the social risk bracket: 122.6 million people. the europe 2020 strategy adopted by the union set itself the strategic objective of reducing by 20 million by 2020 the number of people living in poverty and social exclusion on our continent, but this objective requires adaptation to new conditions. the commission and the member states must take extraordinary action to put in place all the measures necessary to deal with the scale of the problem. the development of new housing policies, more effective energy policies, the introduction of sustainable pension systems and minimum income systems can be appropriate tools to combat a challenge of this magnitude. although i was unable to vote because of a technical problem with the recording, i did say that i would support the meszerics report.

in writing. ‒ in recent years, the number of europeans at risk of poverty and those suffering from severe material deprivation has been increasing alarmingly and continuously, as a result of the economic crisis that began in 2008, putting at serious risk the achievement of the ambitious target of 20 million people lifted out of poverty under the horizon 2020 strategy. in order to respond adequately to this crisis situation and to ensure that the commission's intention to have a 'triple a social' does not remain a dead letter, it is necessary to revive the debate as soon as possible on the possible adoption of a framework directive on the introduction of an adequate minimum income above the poverty threshold and on the introduction of new forms of taxation of large energy-intensive industries in order to find new resources to finance more effective measures to combat poverty, while discouraging energy inefficiency. in this connection, particular attention should also be paid to people, often elderly or young, who are in precarious situations, for example by promoting, as the motion for a resolution in question proposes, a moratorium on cutting off heating in the winter months, by facilitating the use of cross-financing mechanisms between the various european funds.

in writing. ‒ since 2008, the number of people at risk of poverty or social exclusion has gradually increased in most member states. in 2014, one in four people living in the eu was at serious risk of poverty, and the most at risk groups were women, children, young people with low levels of education and migrants. the economic crisis is undoubtedly the cause of the increase in poverty, and the resulting austerity policies have certainly not helped the already difficult recovery. the commitment of the member states and the commission must be unequivocal: the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the establishment of a european union agency for fundamental rights. it is not conceivable, nor is it acceptable, that there should be many families in europe who are unable to meet the costs of heating their homes. the social dimension is also needed in energy policy: the union's fight against poverty and poverty also involves reducing expenditure on energy consumption, which is the most important item in the household budget. investments in energy-efficient housing and public buildings and the development of renewable sources should be a priority for the member states and the commission. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ this report is a clear example of a policy to combat poverty, which is why i voted in favour of it. the data presented to us today are alarming and i therefore believe that a concrete political response is needed as soon as possible. this report lays the foundations for this, focusing on renewable energy and energy efficiency for households exposed to energy insecurity. it also seeks to redirect funds to the most vulnerable households with the further aim of removing barriers to access to these resources. it is clear that energy and consumer price policies can have an impact on poverty, particularly in disadvantaged groups, and i therefore believe that cooperation by all member states is needed to move towards the objectives highlighted in this report.
in writing. ‒ i consider the objective of fighting poverty to be a top priority for all member states, in line with the europe 2020 strategy. in recent years, the rising cost of living, the economic crisis and youth unemployment have created favourable conditions for the proliferation of poverty in all its forms and a vicious circle from which it is increasingly difficult to break out. in particular, it is clear that high housing costs in the presence of low incomes and, at the same time, the not always guaranteed right of access to healthy housing are issues that have a negative impact on the lives of european citizens and on the economic recovery in the member states. i therefore intend to vote in favour of a european strategy to end poverty, energy poverty and social exclusion, combining the commission's action, diversified according to the specific socioeconomic contexts of each member state, with action by the member states to make more effective use of european funds and to ensure the continuity of social services such as minimum income schemes, reduction of household energy costs and equitable access to adequate housing and health care.

in writing. ‒ we welcome with great interest and full agreement the meszerics report, whose main objective is to combat poverty by bringing social policy and energy policy closer together in the european debate. given that inequalities in the european union are increasing, mainly due to the crisis and the risk that a european citizen may be exposed to risks of poverty, it is clear that adequate countermeasures must be found in a short time. we therefore believe that the proposal to introduce a reference framework on minimum income and an improvement in social labour rights are necessary tools to enable the european union to make progress in its social commitment. we also believe that reducing family expenditure through better targeting of funds to the most vulnerable families and the removal of barriers to access to resources is necessary to reduce the level of poverty. we are confident that better targeting of eu funds to households in energy-insecure conditions can be the key to achieving this goal faster. the proposal introduces the concept of a european moratorium on the suspension of heating services during the winter months, to protect households in the most difficult situation because of energy shortages or at risk of interruption of heating due to non-payment of bills.

in writing. ‒ the level of poverty in europe is intolerably high. between 2008 and 2013, as a result of the economic crisis and the austerity policies that followed, the number of poor people in the european union rose from 117 million to more than 122 million. poor families spend a large part of their income on housing, bills, and food. according to european union statistics, in 2015, 10% of citizens had bills that were not paid and in 2014, 12% were unable to heat their homes properly, while 16% lived in damp accommodation due to water infiltration. in this situation, with house prices continuing to rise, the eu needs to do much more if it is to achieve its poverty reduction targets. in particular, member states should focus more on energy efficiency projects (which italy is already doing) to help disadvantaged households and, at the same time, promote models of environmental sustainability. another equally important measure envisaged in the report is the approval of a winter moratorium to avoid cuts in the supply of energy to households in difficulty. finally, i am also in favour of the creation of a european energy observatory.
in writing. ‒ social policy and energy policy should be closely linked. the european union is moving further and further away from the poverty reduction target set by the europe 2020 strategy. reducing the main expenditure of poor households for private consumption by targeting existing renewable energy and energy efficiency projects to households affected by energy poverty. increasing the income of the poorest households is the basis for a robust and lasting economic recovery. i would also like to draw attention to the fact that the number of women living in poverty is 12 million more than that of men and that throughout the union women and the children they care for are disproportionately exposed to the risk of poverty or social exclusion.
in writing. ‒ i consider the report on the fight against poverty to be fundamental. since the start of the crisis, the number of people living in poverty in europe has increased from 117 million to 122 million. these large-scale data are also reflected in a small way in my hometown, padua: for example, in the last two years, the number of caritas users has increased by 39%. fighting poverty is a political commitment. i therefore took an active part in drafting the text, which was tabled by my colleague from the s&d group, ruza tomasic, and i tabled a number of amendments. i would particularly like to stress the importance of the articles on housing, which call on the member states and the european institutions to put forward concrete proposals to solve the serious problem of public housing. in fact, too many families today live in uncomfortable conditions because of homes that are too small or unhealthy. the socialist and democratic group will ensure that these commitments are respected both at european level and in the various member states.
in writing. ‒ this report addresses one of the key issues in development policy: the role of the private sector in the framework of those policies. we believe that this report is grossly unbalanced in favour of the private sector and corporate profit, which is described as the panacea for all ills. this view of the economy also affects sectors such as essential public services. i would have voted against because these positions are incompatible with our political programme.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the deva report on the private sector and development. this is an important text which effectively underlines the strong and positive link between public investment, private investment and development in many international contexts. the full implementation of the new sustainable development goals, presented by the united nations in 2015, is an important test case for how a virtuous partnership between public and private entities can ensure a reduction in the poverty rate and positive growth of small and medium-sized enterprises. the european union can do a lot in this context thanks to the experience it has gained over the years in supporting the business world. the launch of public-private partnerships at local and regional level in the agri-food sector, in training programmes and in occupational health care can be a model for many poor countries embarking on the path of development. through its experience, the eu can play a key facilitating and mediating role in many contexts, by providing appropriate sectoral and multilateral platforms that, involving ngos, governments, business and civil society, can overcome the unintended difficulties that can arise in collaboration between different realities.
in writing. ‒ the report on the private sector and development, while not resulting in any fully agreeable steps, is overall not very transparent. the role, competences and powers of the various key players in projects of interest to our territories are not fully defined. for this and other unclear reasons, i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the report highlights several aspects, some of which are also shared, of the importance of the private sector in eu development and cooperation initiatives and projects; the transition to agriculture (with specific reference to the preventive involvement of the resident population) and the development of social services is largely sustainable. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the european investment bank (eib) is too 'general', and the arrangements for involving the eib (european investment bank) whose actual activity has not been widely reported, and the call for cooperation from the developing countries, which is still too weak. however, since the necessary assumption on the balance of current activities (which is mentioned in the introduction) is lacking, which could justify a new impetus in the field of private sector involvement, i abstained.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of this report to ensure that the private sector plays a more prominent role in development cooperation. i welcome the commission's initiative to support the private sector in becoming, together with other governmental and non-governmental development organisations and inclusive business models such as cooperative and social enterprises, an important partner in achieving inclusive and sustainable development in the framework of the united nations millennium development goals, which requires a commitment by the private sector to good governance, poverty reduction and wealth creation through sustainable investment, as well as reducing inequalities, promoting human rights and environmental standards and empowering local economies. i stress the need to examine how the private sector can be further involved in the framework of the european neighbourhood policy, to help create economic growth and jobs in europe's neighbourhood, for example through access to capital. i believe that the public and private sectors are most efficient when they work together to create a healthy environment for investment and business activity and lay the foundations for economic growth.
in writing. ‒ i could not agree more with the content of this report, especially since i am aware of the importance of the private sector for the development of third countries and its many benefits in a wide range of sectors (from employment to agricultural production), making it an essential partner in the fight against poverty. the aim of this report is to establish a framework for action to give the private sector in developing countries a stronger role and to make it a more active player in the economic and social growth of these countries. i am therefore in full agreement with this, especially when the premises of this document are to aim at inclusive growth and to create decent employment. i believe that involving the european and international business sector is the fundamental prerequisite for achieving sustainable development.
in writing. ‒ the public sector now provides a significant part of the aid granted to promote sustainable economies in developing countries. however, in these countries the private sector accounts for 90% of jobs and the same percentage of wages. thus, while government intervention remains an important tool of development policy, the role of the private sector should be further considered. for example, in these countries, it would be useful to promote partnerships based on cooperation between private and public actors. however, although private actors have played and continue to play a key role in the economies of these countries, they should ensure an environmentally sustainable economic model and one that promotes the economic empowerment of women. the european parliament's resolution on the private sector and development recognises and encourages the role of private actors in development policy, but also sets out the conditions for greater coordination with private actors. i think that these recommendations are important and i voted in favour of the resolution on the private sector and development.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the implementation of a more decisive role for the private sector in the growth of developing countries. there is not a single significant development project in the world today that is not consulted and worked with private investors. moreover, recent estimates clearly show that private sector investment in developing countries often achieves high rates of return on energy and transport projects. in particular, there is tremendous potential in engaging the private sector in developing market-based solutions to agricultural challenges and food security, such as training local farmers to improve farming techniques, increasing their access to finance. i believe that supporting the private sector is a winning development strategy for the european union.
in writing. ‒ i abstain because, despite some positive points, there are only weak calls and plans for the future.
in writing. having reached compromises on certain points in the resolution, i support the system proposed by the commission to promote the private sector in developing countries. today, 90% of jobs in these countries are provided by private individuals who contribute to the sustainable growth of the country, thus making it possible to fight poverty. for the reasons mentioned above, the private sector continues to grow by creating agreements with governments, sponsors and non-governmental organizations (ngos). the commission's efforts so far have been positive, and i therefore support the implementation of new, more strategic projects that will help create jobs and promote inclusive and sustainable development.
in writing. ‒ we welcome the report on the private sector and development. the european union must be able to stimulate more private investment in the community economy. this is because there is already a lack of public investment and the involvement of the private sector seems to be the most appropriate solution. the european commission, led by president juncker, launched a strategic investment fund in 2014 which, as early as 2015, was able to generate a significant leverage effect, thus increasing the amount of investment in the union. the capacity of investment, especially in manufacturing, to reduce market-related poverty by creating employment and welfare among working citizens is also well known. in the coming decades, the growth of the global population and the rise in income in today's developing countries will generate greater demands for food, water and energy. for this reason, it is necessary for community actors to concentrate part of their investments in developing countries, where, although greater volatility and uncertainty remain, returns on capital are surprisingly high and guarantee well-being and employment for indigenous peoples, especially if they are geared to the creation of sustainable wealth.
in writing. ‒ considering that population growth in developing countries will require more investment in development support in the coming years, considering that, according to some estimates, private sector investment in pvs is often associated with high rates of return, considering also that the involvement of private investors in agricultural development could be a stimulus for the development of farming techniques, encourage employment and promote sustainable development, considering, finally, that greater public-private partnership can be beneficial for these countries, i would like to vote in favour of the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ the private sector provides 90% of jobs in developing countries and is therefore a key partner in the fight against poverty and hunger. the report sets out a strategic framework to ensure that investments made by private enterprises benefit all of society, in particular women, young people and the disadvantaged. the priority of investment must therefore be to create lasting jobs, especially for the weakest sections of society, and to promote the gradual transition from an informal to a formal economy. by ensuring a more favourable and secure environment for businesses, they will be able to invest more and more responsibly and everyone will be able to benefit from the economic opportunities created by the private sector. i voted in favour of this report because only by making the private sector an active partner in development cooperation will the european union be able to live up to its commitment to promoting justice and peace in the world.

president of the european investment bank. – mr president, it is a pleasure and an honour to be back at parliament and to report to you about the annual report for 2014 and to respond to the remarks by the rapporteur, mr pirinski, whom i thank for his great work and very good, close cooperation with the services of the bank and myself. having said this, let me start by expressing my appreciation for the support you, as the european parliament, give us to ensure that the eu bank will continue to deliver benefits for the eu economy and for eu citizens, as well as contribute to common european objectives in our external activities. let me recap on what we have achieved since 2014, the year under review. our plans were ambitious both in form and substance. higher volumes of traditional lending and advising activities were and are still needed to make an imperative contribution to european goals and to respect the eib’s ongoing responsibilities as the eu bank. at the same time the eu bank took upon itself an unprecedented challenge and gladly accepted to play a central role in the investment plan for europe, a role which required a quantum change in the business, in the bank’s business profile, for some years to come. after the crisis began in 2007, we increased our lending by 60% in two years. following up with a eur 10 billion capital increase in 2012, we increased lending by eur 60 billion, supporting an extra eur 180 billion of investment not, as was foreseen, by the end of 2015 but already in march 2015. above target and ahead of time. the investment plan for europe, the juncker plan, with its three pillars, is another exceptional response to exceptional needs. negotiations between the council, parliament and the commission to finalise the regulation were concluded in may last year. that was in record time and we are very grateful for that. the plan consists, of course, of three elements. we only talk about one normally – the efsi, the european fund for strategic investments – backed by a eur 16 billion eu budget guarantee and eur 5 billion of cash from the european investment bank in order to increase the risk-taking capacity of the eib group. i take it from the rapporteur that we do indeed have an obligation to demonstrate that, with this additional manoeuvre space, we are targeting investments which make a difference and which are additional to what we would have been able to do, at least on this scale, under normal circumstances. and i think we can prove that. then of course we have the enhancement of our advisory capacities within the framework of the european advisory hub, and the third pillar is all about removing barriers to investment and structural reforms. let me take the opportunity to update you. so far the eib group, that is both the eib and the european investment fund (which supports smaller businesses) has approved through efsi financing an amount of eur 11.2 billion to more than 220 projects in 25 member states, which will trigger an overall additional investment in europe of over eur 82.1 billion. in other words, although the institutional setup was only completed at the beginning of this year, we have also done more than 25% of the volumes we have promised within three years. so you can see that the pace of our delivery has taken up speed. very importantly, the advisory hub is also proving to be a successful initiative, having as of march 2016 received and processed 108 requests, of which 87 are project-specific. simultaneously a network of partner institutions keen to work in cooperation with the hub is being established across the eu. fifteen memoranda of understanding have been signed with the national promotion institutions, with an additional seven in the pipeline. the investment plan for europe is important for our economy but europe also has global responsibilities and the council, the commission and sometimes parliament remind us of that as well. we need to ensure that in future the eu bank will have the necessary personnel and financial resources, instruments and platforms to support eu external policy and development efforts, all the way to climate policies in particular. while eu member states already provide considerable official development assistance to the nations, the challenges in the developing world need a more coordinated approach and the financial instruments that we use to leverage private capital within the european union every day. as such i foresee a situation where we will reach the limits of the bank’s current 10% level for activities outside the european union. first among these current pressing issues is the eib’s response to the refugee crisis and how the eib can contribute beyond what is already being done both in europe and in the region of the middle east and north africa. we have proposed to our board that the eib could do more both in europe, to finance the infrastructure needed to cope with the new arrivals, and outside europe, on private sector development in countries of origin and transit. we are currently actively working on concrete proposals that will be presented to the european council in june, as we have been asked to do. we also look forward to continuing our very close cooperation with the commission in this crucial effort. a final word about our parliamentary responsibility, our responsibility vis-à-vis parliament: for me, as a parliamentary veteran of 25 years, it goes without saying that europe’s citizens expect and deserve parliamentary oversight for their bank. therefore it goes without saying that i am ready, just like my colleagues are, to report to parliament and its committees and parliamentary groups when you so wish. your bank, the eu bank, is nowadays the world’s biggest international financial institution in terms of lending volume, operating in many different sectors in parts of the world. over past years we have been delivering approximately eur 70 to 80 billion a year of investments in sound and sustainable projects, mostly inside the eu and increasingly also in our partner countries. we will continue to do so, including by using the additional firepower under efsi, because we have to address the huge investment needs. the last year has been particularly intense and challenging, with the eib under sharp scrutiny because what we do matters, and people and parliaments care. the message we get from your report is one of support, encouragement and urgency, and i take the remarks also on transparency, the remarks on ncj policies, very seriously and i think we will report to the relevant committees separately on this very issue. let me assure you that we are willing to live up fully to our institutional responsibilities and will continue to exchange with you regularly on our activities and their impact on the ground. thank you very much for your attention.

efficiency alongside the commission. the last aspect i would like to discuss in more detail concerns external action. like parliament, i welcome the renewal of the mandate for 2014-2020 with a €27 billion eu guarantee. we will prepare a mid-term evaluation report by the end of 2016 to measure the overall implementation of the current external mandate and to consider a commission proposal for an plan and then launched it - it is showing itself to be able to support companies that take risks more than in the past. this is because the bulk of the investment is private. all this is under way, the rapporteur. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would first like to thank all the shadow rapporteurs with whom you have had fruitful meetings and constructive discussions. and then i would also like to thank all the citizens who contributed with suggestions and proposals to the drafting of the resolution, the draft of which was published on the online platform of the five star movement. the result of the work carried out in close synergy over the past months is a good text and i am satisfied that it is moving in the direction of ensuring greater transparency and greater and better involvement of citizens in the work carried out in the institutions. this step forward is all the more important because it comes at a historic moment when citizens' confidence in the european union is faltering: the european institutions' buildings are seen as opaque places where decisions are taken that directly affect them but of which they often know little or nothing. it is important to note that there is a lot of talk about transparency, but unfortunately words do not always follow deeds. it is enough to think that many of the recommendations made in similar resolutions of parliament in previous years have not been followed up. yet transparency, like participatory democracy, is a fundamental democratic principle, recognised by the treaty on european union. it is therefore in the spirit of the principle of participatory democracy on which the european union is founded that the text was drawn up, which calls for the establishment of a public electronic register of the work of citizens' representatives, the decision-making process and the way public money is allocated and spent and the results achieved. the committee calls for the accessibility of information to be improved, increased and simplified by developing a common access point to the portals of the eu institutions, including access arrangements which take account of the needs of people with disabilities. the transparency of the institutions cannot, on the other hand, be achieved without adequate protection for whistleblowers, who must be protected both morally and financially. we therefore call on the commission to come forward with a proposal to protect whistleblowers as part of the democratic system. the transparency of the whole legislative process is also of central importance. in this context, the consolidation of the practice of trilogues, of which the citizens know practically nothing, eliminates the necessary public control, which is inherent in the ordinary legislative procedure, favouring the hidden work of lobbyists who can, thanks to the leakage of documents, have easier access to the information necessary to influence the decision-making process. we therefore call for greater transparency in informal trilogues and, consequently, for greater control by the public, while recognising the importance and effectiveness of such meetings. as regards lobbyists, we also call on the commission to submit without delay its proposal for an agreement on the establishment of a mandatory interinstitutional register of lobbyists. we also stress the need to ensure greater transparency in the negotiations for international agreements. the public should have access to as many documents as possible. we also believe that there is a need for greater transparency in the procedures for suspension and infringement vis-à-vis the member states: we know little or nothing about that, either. secondly, with regard to the structural funds, data on procedures and beneficiaries should be made easily accessible in order to combat and prevent abuse, fraud and corruption. as i said at the beginning of my speech, lack of transparency is one of the main causes of the loss of confidence in the european institutions and it would be a fatal mistake to pretend nothing, trying to forget about the growing abstentionism, the resurgence of nationalist sentiments, the risk of corruption and conflicts of interest. as one of the founders of the five star movement, gian roberto casaleggio, said: "it is not right that someone should make decisions for the citizens based on inscrutable logic and without being aware of it. the member of parliament is an employee of the citizens: you can't escape their control. otherwise there can be no direct democracy, or perhaps no democracy at all". as a member of the european parliament who believes in the values of freedom and democratic participation, i call on you to work together to ensure real public access to information.

in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation concerns the creation of a common european legislative framework for the rail network. this regulation specifically concerns the european union agency for railways. the purpose of this technical part is to make european railways more interoperable while maintaining a high level of safety. this regulation gives the european railway agency (era) more powers, including the power to issue authorisations and safety certificates directly to the relevant sector. the era will thus have a greater role in the ertms (european rail traffic management system). a single point of contact for requests is provided and the era will adopt rules for conflict and litigation prevention. in order to promote the development of an efficient european rail network, i voted against the rejection amendment.

in writing. ‒ railway interoperability and safety is a central element of the sustainable development model for the europe of the future. to improve them, the european railway agency (era) was established by regulation (ec) no 881/2004 of 29 april 2004, with offices in lille and valenciennes (france). the agency shall promote the progressive harmonisation, registration and monitoring of technical specifications for interoperability (tsis) across the european rail system and the development of common safety objectives for european railways. although the era does not have autonomous decision-making powers, it contributes to drafting proposals for decisions for the european commission. regulation (ec) no 1335/2008 of 16 december 2008 has conferred new tasks on the era, which are related to the amendments to the directives on railway safety (2004/49/ec) and on the interoperability of the rail system (2008/57/ec). now, with the adoption of the fourth railway package, the era's powers of investigation and audit in its fields of competence will finally be strengthened. this will help to avoid having 28 different systems for the type approval of trains: the agency will act as a single point of contact for issuing authorisations for vehicles intended for cross-border operations and safety certificates to railway undertakings operating in different eu states.
in writing. ‒ this measure is part of the so-called 'fourth railway package' (qpf), a series of legislative measures aimed at modernising the eu's rail transport sector. in particular, the zile report (ecr) concerns changes to the rules governing the european railway agency (era), which was established in 2004 and has two sites, both in france (valenciennes and lille). our position on the qpf is not negative, but this is perhaps the only dossier which we find dubious. on the one hand, we are absolutely convinced that there is a need for coordination of railway activities at european level, especially at a time when concepts such as the harmonization of technical standards or non-discriminatory access to the market will be the rule. on the other hand, however, we are sceptical about the agency's instrument and whether the new functions it will be given will really be carried out in the interests of the user citizens and all market players. the era will have the competence to issue vehicle authorisations and safety certificates. there are doubts about how the european commission will manage to allocate the necessary funds to supplement existing staff with the additional staff needed. i mean, there's also a cost-increasing problem that we hoped would be more limited. i abstain from voting.

in writing. ‒ the price of many financial instruments is closely linked to the accuracy and integrity of the indices used as benchmarks. these indices are statistical measures, representative of a set of data, which are used as a reference for contracts and financial instruments. recent incidents of manipulation of the london interbank offered rate (libor) and other cases of alleged manipulation have brought the vulnerability of these measures to the attention of the public. the van nieuwenhuizen report addresses this issue and that of macroprudential risks in benchmarks by proposing a strategy based on improving governance measures and mitigating conflicts of interest. the text, which i supported with my vote, places particular emphasis on the fundamental distinction between critical and less critical reference values, establishing a two-tiered approach to their determination. for critical benchmarks in particular, the new legislation will impose binding governance requirements in line with and based on the internationally agreed iosco principles. the entire package of measures will ensure increased transparency while maintaining the supply and access to a wide variety of benchmarks.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation introducing a common framework to ensure the accuracy and integrity of indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts in the union. serious cases of manipulation of interest rate benchmarks such as libor and euribor and of currency benchmarks, which cause considerable losses to consumers and investors (as well as destroying public confidence in the financial sector), have necessitated a comprehensive approach to the issue. the regulation has three main objectives: first, strengthen governance systems and standards to reduce their vulnerability to manipulation and abuse; secondly, to enhance transparency by making more information available to users of all benchmarks in order to enable them to make informed decisions; third, to maintain the supply of and access to a wide variety of benchmarks by applying governance requirements in a proportionate manner. for all these reasons i have decided to vote in favour of the regulation.
in writing. ‒ the regulation provides for specific regulation of the benchmarks of financial instruments and related contracts at european level. the need for such a measure was brought to light by the recent euribor and libor value manipulation scandals involving some large banks. unfortunately, although the provisions of the regulation do not contain any major criticisms, the worrying fact emerges that it is precisely the large central banks, public authorities and central counterparties that are exempted from the scope of application. therefore, as this is half-baked legislation which does not meet the needs of the real economy, i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it seeks to give an effective answer to the question of the manipulation of reference values for currencies and all related issues. i think it is essential to make it clear that this manipulation is illegal and i also think it is necessary to provide for criminal prosecution. i voted in favour of this because i think that this issue should not be underestimated, especially given its importance for the normal functioning and stability of financial and commodity markets. i also think it is essential, especially when it comes to the economy, to ensure the greatest possible transparency and i believe that this report is moving in that direction. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts directly or indirectly affect the vast majority of european citizens, but also various markets such as energy. given the scale and impact of indices on the european financial system, it is necessary to provide for appropriate regulation that reduces vulnerability to manipulation and abuse of indices, that enhances transparency by providing users with all necessary information on all benchmarks to enable them to make informed decisions, and that maintains the supply of and access to a wide variety of benchmarks by applying governance requirements in a proportionate manner, while also ensuring a level playing field for all administrators, both european and those located in third countries. in view of these considerations, i felt i had to vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the agreement reached with the council on the regulation of the european parliament and of the council on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts, because i believe that the new regulation will prevent stock market index manipulation in the future. the need for regulation was triggered by the scandals surrounding the serious manipulation of libor and euribor and foreign currency reference values, which caused considerable losses for consumers and investors, and which further undermined public confidence in the financial sector, which had already been put to the test by the crisis and confronted with the need for new rules to ensure the stability of the financial system as a whole. although this is a regulation which is mainly directed at the interbank credit market, in reality it also applies inter alia to the assessment of the performance of investment funds, and citizens are also interested in the integrity and proper functioning of these indices, since the euribor rate is measured as part of the cost of obtaining mortgage loans. i agreed with the extension of the scope of the regulation, the introduction of the systemic index category, the exclusive supervisory and proposing role of esma.

in writing. ‒ recent cases of manipulation of interest rate benchmarks, such as libor and euribor, have highlighted the importance and weaknesses of benchmarks used in financial products. the regulation adopted today has three main objectives: strengthen governance systems and standards, in particular for widely used benchmarks, enhance transparency by making more information available to users and maintain the supply and access to a wide variety of benchmarks by ensuring a level playing field for all administrators, both european and third country. i believe that the adoption of this new regulation can help to increase the robustness and reliability of benchmarks and to prevent their manipulation, thus strengthening consumer and investor confidence in financial markets. i therefore decided to vote in favour of the report.
in writing. this regulation provided an opportunity to introduce effective measures against the risks of manipulation of indices used as benchmarks for financial instruments and contracts, which can have a significant negative impact on the real economy, consumers, financial stability, or the financing of households and businesses. while i acknowledge that some progress has been made in terms of strengthening governance and control requirements, introducing mechanisms for managing conflicts of interest, and with stricter supervision, or even with the requirement for prior authorisation for all index managers, i nevertheless believe that this regulation has sacrificed the most important pillar for effectively tackling abuse, transparency. there is no transparency regarding the data used to construct the indices, and the obligation to publish the methodology is limited to key elements that are not well defined. i therefore believe that, despite the significant improvements in governance and supervision, this regulation will not be able to prevent the recurrence of scandals such as the one involving the euribor and libor indices, with losses of over eur 3 billion for the 2.5 million italian households who had taken out a euribor-linked mortgage. for these reasons i could not support this regulation.
