in writing. ‒ the discharge procedure is a key instrument in the hands of the european parliament to monitor the implementation of the budget of the various european institutions and agencies and thus to exercise in-depth political control over the use of public funds. this is a well-established practice, essential to ensure the transparency and democratic accountability of the institutions towards eu taxpayers. however, for this prerogative to be fully exercised, all the european institutions must cooperate openly and constructively with the committee on budgetary control of the european parliament, providing all the necessary information and documents, answering written questions and participating in the hearings and discussions on the implementation of the budget envisaged. in this sense, while most of the institutions are cooperative in facilitating parliament's control over the implementation of their budgets, some institutions are not cooperating satisfactorily, in breach of the principles of loyal cooperation and transparency enshrined in the treaties. i am thinking in particular of the council, which since 2009 has refused to submit to the discharge exercise, effectively evading political control over over 3 billion of european public funds spent, thus fuelling the feeling of mistrust towards the european institutions.

in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the position of the committee on budgetary control granting discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2014, section i european parliament because, on the whole, the audits carried out by the court of auditors show that expenditure under the heading 'administration' is not affected by a significant level of error and that the estimated error rate under heading 5 'administration' of the mff is 0,5% (down from 1% in 2013). the only comment i have to make is on the age-old question of the single seat of the european parliament. the court of auditors' report adopted on 11 july 2014 shows that if parliament centralised its activities, the potential savings for the union budget would be around eur 114 million per year: a waste we can no longer afford. the european parliament and the council should, in order to achieve long-term savings, address the question of the need for a roadmap for the establishment of a single seat, as has already been supported by parliament in many previous resolutions.

in writing. ‒ the budget discharge procedure is an important moment in the institutional life of the european union. on this occasion, the european parliament, the only institution elected by universal suffrage, decides, on a recommendation from the council, whether or not to grant final discharge for the implementation of the budget for a given financial year. this is a key step which also provides an opportunity to address specific recommendations to the institutions and agencies which make up the community structure. following the instructions of the committee on budgetary control (cont), i have today decided to vote in favour of the czarnecki report on the postponement of the discharge for the 2014 budget for the council and the european council. for years now, parliament has been asking the council to provide full data on the implementation of the budget, but has received little cooperation from this institution. in view of the lack of transparency in budgetary and accounting data, parliament decided, as in previous years, to vote for a postponement of discharge, as the conditions were not present for expressing an appropriate assessment of council expenditure.

in writing. ‒ the discharge procedure is a key instrument in the hands of the european parliament to monitor the implementation of the budget of the various european institutions and agencies and thus to exercise in-depth political control over the use of public funds. this is a well-established practice, essential to ensure the transparency and democratic accountability of the institutions towards eu taxpayers. however, in order to exercise this prerogative fully, all the european institutions must cooperate openly and constructively with the committee on budgetary control of the european parliament, providing all the necessary information and documents, answering written questions and participating in the hearings and discussions on the implementation of the budget envisaged. in this sense, while most of the institutions are cooperative in facilitating parliament's control over the implementation of their budgets, some institutions are not cooperating satisfactorily, in breach of the principles of loyal cooperation and transparency enshrined in the treaties. i am thinking in particular of the council, which since 2009 has refused to submit to the discharge exercise, effectively evading political control over the more than 3 billion of european public funds spent, thus fuelling the feeling of mistrust towards the european institutions.

in writing. ‒ the court of justice, as is well known, enjoys the status of an institution of the european union and therefore has the same dignity as the parliament and the council. while the latter institutions are called upon to play the key role of co-legislator, the court has the delicate task of ensuring that union law is correctly applied and interpreted. it contributes, in a certain sense, to the very formation of that body of legislation, since its case-law makes it possible to define more precisely the scope and the contours of the provisions of the treaties and of secondary legislation. it also ensures that all those who are subject to eu law, including eu member states and the institutions that make the law, comply with it. the court of justice is therefore the ultimate expression of the rule of law framework in which the union operates. it is therefore essential that it should be able to exercise its mandate fully and therefore not only enjoy the prerogatives of independence but also have adequate resources for its task. for these reasons i thought i should vote in favour of the discharge for the financial item for this institution.

in writing. ‒ the discharge procedure is a key instrument in the hands of the european parliament to monitor the implementation of the budget of the various european institutions and agencies and thus to exercise in-depth political control over the use of public funds. this is a well-established practice, essential to ensure the transparency and democratic accountability of the institutions towards eu taxpayers. however, in order to exercise this prerogative fully, all the european institutions must cooperate openly and constructively with the committee on budgetary control of the european parliament, providing all the necessary information and documents, answering written questions and participating in the hearings and discussions on the implementation of the budget envisaged. in this sense, while most of the institutions are cooperative in facilitating parliament's control over the implementation of their budgets, some institutions are not cooperating satisfactorily, in breach of the principles of loyal cooperation and transparency enshrined in the treaties. i am thinking in particular of the council, which since 2009 has refused to submit to the discharge exercise, effectively evading political control over the more than 3 billion of european public funds spent, thus fuelling the feeling of mistrust towards the european institutions.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it highlights the horizontal issues of eu agencies in a relevant way. firstly, the high level of cancellations of appropriations for previous years, as noted by the court of auditors, shows that the amounts were based on an overestimation of needs or were not justified. a lack of guidance on whistleblowing and whistleblower protection remains in many agencies, which is worrying as protection problems have occurred in many agencies. the report then focuses on other important issues: the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the whole of the eu, including the member states, and to extend it to cover the whole of the european union. the report also stresses the need for the strict application of the measures on discretion and exclusion in public procurement to procurement procedures, which are a real weakness and a dark spot for agencies, with appropriate checks on previous cases and the application of exclusion criteria to exclude companies in the event of a conflict of interest.

in writing. ‒ the budget discharge procedure is an important moment in the institutional life of the european union. on this occasion, the european parliament, the only institution elected by universal suffrage, decides, on a recommendation from the council, whether or not to grant final discharge for the implementation of the budget for a given financial year. this is a key step which also provides an opportunity to address specific recommendations to the institutions and agencies which make up the community structure. following the instructions of the committee on budgetary control (cont), i have today decided to vote in favour of the vaughan report on the discharge for the 2014 budget for the agency for the cooperation of national energy regulators.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of discharge for the 2014 budget of the agency for the cooperation of energy regulators (acer) because i believe that its finances have been managed in a prudent manner and in line with the budget forecasts for the year in question.
in writing. ‒ the discharge procedure is a key instrument in the hands of the european parliament to monitor the implementation of the budget of the various european institutions and agencies and thus to exercise in-depth political control over the use of public funds. this is a well-established practice, essential to ensure the transparency and democratic accountability of the institutions towards eu taxpayers. however, in order to exercise this prerogative fully, all the european institutions must cooperate openly and constructively with the committee on budgetary control of the european parliament, providing all the necessary information and documents, answering written questions and participating in the hearings and discussions on the implementation of the budget envisaged. in this sense, while most of the institutions are cooperative in facilitating parliament's control over the implementation of their budgets, some institutions are not cooperating satisfactorily, in breach of the principles of loyal cooperation and transparency enshrined in the treaties. i am thinking in particular of the council, which since 2009 has refused to submit to the discharge exercise, effectively evading political control over the more than 3 billion of european public funds spent, thus fuelling the feeling of mistrust towards the european institutions.

in writing. ‒ the discharge procedure is a key instrument in the hands of the european parliament to monitor the implementation of the budget of the various european institutions and agencies and thus to exercise in-depth political control over the use of public funds. this is a well-established practice, essential to ensure the transparency and democratic accountability of the institutions towards eu taxpayers. however, in order to exercise this prerogative fully, all the european institutions must cooperate openly and constructively with the committee on budgetary control of the european parliament, providing all the necessary information and documents, answering written questions and participating in the hearings and discussions on the implementation of the budget envisaged. in this sense, while most of the institutions are cooperative in facilitating parliament's control over the implementation of their budgets, some institutions are not cooperating satisfactorily, in breach of the principles of loyal cooperation and transparency enshrined in the treaties. i am thinking in particular of the council, which since 2009 has refused to submit to the discharge exercise, effectively evading political control over the more than 3 billion of european public funds spent, thus fuelling the feeling of mistrust towards the european institutions.
in writing. ‒ there are no specific references to the work of the agency and there are some critical points in the financial management of the agency; the instruments which should ensure the transparency of operations, especially ex ante and ex post controls vis-à-vis beneficiaries, appear to be ineffective. i vote against.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the position of the committee on budgetary control granting discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european environment agency for the financial year 2014 because the court of auditors, in its report on the annual accounts of the european environment agency for the financial year 2014, states that it has obtained reasonable assurances as to the reliability of the agency's annual accounts for the financial year 2014. i am concerned, however, as the court of auditors' report shows, that, as regards internal controls, although ex ante and ex post controls are incompatible tasks, the internal auditor was involved in both. i hope that the agency will follow through on its promises by developing a formal ex post control strategy that ensures compatibility with the agency's internal audit capability. finally, i am pleased that in november 2014 the management board of the agency adopted the anti-fraud strategy to ensure the proper management of matters concerning conflicts of interest and to develop anti-fraud activities, in particular through prevention, detection, awareness raising and closer cooperation with the european anti-fraud office (olaf).

in writing. ‒ the discharge procedure is a key instrument in the hands of the european parliament to monitor the implementation of the budget of the various european institutions and agencies and thus to exercise in-depth political control over the use of public funds. this is a well-established practice, essential to ensure the transparency and democratic accountability of the institutions towards eu taxpayers. however, in order to exercise this prerogative fully, all the european institutions must cooperate openly and constructively with the committee on budgetary control of the european parliament, providing all the necessary information and documents, answering written questions and participating in the hearings and discussions on the implementation of the budget envisaged. in this sense, while most of the institutions are cooperative in facilitating parliament's control over the implementation of their budgets, some institutions are not cooperating satisfactorily, in breach of the principles of loyal cooperation and transparency enshrined in the treaties. i am thinking in particular of the council, which since 2009 has refused to submit to the discharge exercise, effectively evading political control over the more than 3 billion of european public funds spent, thus fuelling the feeling of mistrust towards the european institutions.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the position of the committee on budgetary control granting discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european institute of innovation and technology for the financial year 2014 because the court of auditors, in its report on the institute's annual accounts for the financial year 2014, stated that it had obtained reasonable assurance as to the reliability of the institute's annual accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions. according to the institute's financial statements, the overall union contribution to the institute's budget for 2014 amounted to eur 169 807 303, representing an increase of 81,69% compared to 2013. i also welcome the fact that the institute has gradually improved its financial audit of the knowledge and innovation communities' (kics) expenditure declarations, but i note that the operational audit of outputs has lagged behind and that the annual business plans of the kics still include an inadequate definition of 'outputs'. finally, there is concern about the cases identified by the court where the full amount of the grant granted by the institute was paid, although some of the objectives set in the business plan were not achieved.

in writing. ‒ the discharge procedure is a key instrument in the hands of the european parliament to monitor the implementation of the budget of the various european institutions and agencies and thus to exercise in-depth political control over the use of public funds. this is a well-established practice, essential to ensure the transparency and democratic accountability of the institutions towards eu taxpayers. however, in order to exercise this prerogative fully, all the european institutions must cooperate openly and constructively with the committee on budgetary control of the european parliament, providing all the necessary information and documents, answering written questions and participating in the hearings and discussions on the implementation of the budget envisaged. in this sense, while most of the institutions are cooperative in facilitating parliament's control over the implementation of their budgets, some institutions are not cooperating satisfactorily, in breach of the principles of loyal cooperation and transparency enshrined in the treaties. i am thinking in particular of the council, which since 2009 has refused to submit to the discharge exercise, effectively evading political control over the more than 3 billion of european public funds spent, thus fuelling the feeling of mistrust towards the european institutions.
in writing. ‒ esma will need more resources in line with the increased responsibilities linked to the completion of the european system of financial supervision (esfs), of which esma is a part. the commission is also proposing to introduce a new system of financing, based on a separate budget line in the union budget and the total replacement of contributions from national authorities by fees charged by market operators. i vote against.

in writing. ‒ the discharge procedure is a key instrument in the hands of the european parliament to monitor the implementation of the budget of the various european institutions and agencies and thus to exercise in-depth political control over the use of public funds. this is a well-established practice, essential to ensure the transparency and democratic accountability of the institutions towards eu taxpayers. however, in order to exercise this prerogative fully, all the european institutions must cooperate openly and constructively with the committee on budgetary control of the european parliament, providing all the necessary information and documents, answering written questions and participating in the hearings and discussions on the implementation of the budget envisaged. in this sense, while most of the institutions are cooperative in facilitating parliament's control over the implementation of their budgets, some institutions are not cooperating satisfactorily, in breach of the principles of loyal cooperation and transparency enshrined in the treaties. i am thinking in particular of the council, which since 2009 has refused to submit to the discharge exercise, effectively evading political control over the more than 3 billion of european public funds spent, thus fuelling the feeling of mistrust towards the european institutions.

in writing. ‒ transparent institutions and decision-making processes are essential to enhance the trust of european citizens in the eu and to make them more involved and aware of their rights and duties. in this context, the right of access to documents is a fundamental right protected by the charter of fundamental rights, the treaties and implemented in particular by regulation 1049/2001. although the process of increasing the transparency of the work of the european institutions has been under way for some time and is gradually leading to a significant improvement in the environment, it still presents several criticisms. citizens often do not have satisfactory access to many working documents, which creates the perception of an opaque decision-making process and reduces the effective capacity of citizens to exercise sound democratic control over the work of the institutions. in this context, i believe that citizens should be able to monitor more closely the actions of their representatives and the european institutions. i therefore support the development of a common approach between the institutions to facilitate full access for european citizens to the main working documents and to promote greater transparency in the trilogue negotiations and in the negotiations of the international agreements under discussion.

in writing. ‒ after careful reflection and debate in the chamber, i voted in favour of the report on public access to documents for 2014-15, as i believe that creating added value in the administrative and legislative procedures of individual member states and the community institutions is not only a matter of prudent political activity but also, and in these times especially, of the implementation of democratic sharing processes. it should be stressed that the right of access, protected by the charter of fundamental rights and vigorously defended by the constant case law of the court of justice and the national courts, is a fundamental right that has been severely tested by the lack of a harmonised body of rules on the aspects of access, privacy, correct and timely information to citizens, classification of confidential documents. the same is felt to be urgently needed for trilogue procedures, for amendments in plenary, for contact with lobbies, for delegated acts, which violate the principle of representative democracy if they are not fully shared and accessible.

in writing. ‒ i have decided to express a favourable assessment of the subject of this report, because the eu institutions must be guided by representative democracy in their activities and policies and ensure that the principles of transparency, sharing and timely and appropriate information for citizens are respected. following the entry into force of the teu and the tfeu, the right of access to documents covers all eu institutions, bodies and agencies, which is why the same institutions cannot exempt themselves from providing the appropriate information to those who request it. it is therefore necessary to update regulation (ec) no 1049/2001 as a matter of urgency, with substantial amendments in the light of the provisions of the treaty and the relevant case-law of the court of justice of the eu and the european court of human rights, in order to provide for an approach allowing for easy access to documents.

in writing. i voted in favour of this excellent report by the five star movement on public access to documents. the current context of secrecy and opacity in which public decisions are taken and the legislative process takes place means that the european institutions provide the greatest representation of major private interests and a privileged channel of access to confidential information and documents, while citizens and civil society are completely excluded. this report calls for putting citizens back at the centre of public decision-making, through public access to all documents relating to institutional activities and the legislative process in the eu, in line with the principles of direct democracy advanced by the movement. the citizens must be able to know who is representing the interests of the lobbies and who is representing the general interest, what the commission is doing in the ttip negotiations, what is said at ecb meetings, how decisions on banks are taken, what is happening inside the agencies, how the structural funds are managed, or on the basis of what scientific data the commission approves, for example, the granting of substances that are potentially dangerous to health. to get closer to the institutions, citizens need not more effective marketing of the 'eu' brand, but maximum transparency and the possibility of exercising effective control over decision-makers.
in writing. ‒ this annual own-initiative report by the european parliament concerns public access to the documents of the institutions and, ultimately, their level of transparency and the possibility for citizens to exercise democratic scrutiny over the activities of the european institutions and the legislative process in particular. the report raises some important points about the lack of transparency in the institutions. calls in particular for the establishment of an effective interinstitutional policy geared towards the citizen and characterised by full transparency, communication and direct democracy; a rapid revision of regulation 1049/2001 which is still blocked in the council; the establishment of a mandatory lobby register for all institutions; enhanced transparency of the legislative process and of the negotiations on the conclusion of international agreements; the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the budget. a particularly controversial point concerns the transparency of trilogues, a crucial stage in the legislative process, which should be public, as should documents relating to the negotiations. i voted in favour of this report to put an end to off-limits meetings and to make european citizens fully involved in the decision-making process.
in writing. ‒ domestic work is defined by the international labour organisation (ilo) as work done by an individual in or for one or more households. these types of work, although widespread, especially among women, do not yet enjoy a common regulation on occupational treatment. the report presented aims to address the precarious situation of the sector by proposing the professionalization of domestic and care work, in such a way as to guarantee the workers concerned protection and legal certainty. i therefore decided to vote in favour of the proposal, believing that a clear regulation of the sector in all member states will put an end to the forms of discrimination, violence and abuse to which such individuals are often subject.
in writing. ‒ convention no 189 of the international labour organisation defines 'domestic worker' as any person with a working relationship with one or more households. although this is the only definition provided by an international organisation, it excludes a wide range of people engaged in parttime, occasional or sporadic work and care providers. the kuneva report, which i supported with my vote today, seeks to fill the gaps in this definition by bringing to the attention of the european legislator a condition which in 2010 affected over 52 million people worldwide, the vast majority of whom were women. the text voted by parliament today addresses the various risk aspects of the conditions of these workers, including the risk of harassment, the existence of illegal relationships and, in particular, the lack of cover in the field of labour law. according to the ilo, 29.9% of domestic workers are in fact completely excluded from national labour legislation. the commission should propose a legislative initiative to define common rules on domestic and care work in the eu, pushing states to include domestic and care workers in national labour laws and fighting underemployment.
in writing. ‒ the kuneva report contains controversial and critical elements which have led me not to support it with my vote.
in writing. ‒ domestic and care work is playing an increasingly important role in ensuring the well-being of a constantly ageing european population, which is facing a contemporary context of major economic difficulties and the burden of continuous and drastic austerity policies. despite its increasingly central role in our societies, this is a sector which nevertheless has to deal with a number of extremely insidious problems: the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. the situation is even more alarming when one considers that exploitation situations are often not reported, as in most cases the workers (mostly migrant women) do not know the language of the country in which they live, are not aware of their rights or are in an irregular situation. in order to respond to this difficult situation, i wholeheartedly support the motion for a resolution in question, which calls for the introduction of new common rules to promote the professionalisation and recognition of the rights of workers in the sector.
in writing. ‒ the general line of recognising domestic and care work in national labour laws may be acceptable, but the report is not objective: focuses mainly on the discrimination against (and often irregular) immigrant women in domestic and care work. with regard to the employment of immigrant workers (a large part of the report) it is argued that the integration of migrants into the labour market is an important step towards social and cultural inclusion. the report also calls for the establishment of a european framework for the protection of workers from harmful organisms and for the establishment of a european framework for the protection of workers from harmful organisms. i vote against.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on domestic workers and carers in the eu, because these are workers who benefit from an atypical employment relationship (no working hours and no holidays), which makes them invisible to the outside world and often allows employers to easily break labour laws. according to the european commission, there are 2.6 million people working as domestic helpers in europe, about 90% of whom are women. it is important to promote the professional recognition of the skills and qualifications of domestic workers and carers, in order to provide them with greater prospects for professional development. in short, we need to build a regulatory framework that allows for better working conditions, including the conclusion of regular contracts and the fight against precarious and submerged work.
in writing. ‒ the report suggests that the european parliament should take measures to tackle the precariousness of domestic work. there are no common standards in europe at present for the professional treatment of domestic workers and carers. it is therefore a recommendation which is entirely acceptable and for which i have voted in favour. the text has been particularly improved by the introduction of some of our proposals aimed at the professionalization of these categories of work, the protection of maternity and health, and the encouragement of indirect home care practices.
in writing. ‒ many, too many domestic workers and carers are forced to live in the shadows. according to the ilo, about 30% of these workers do not fully benefit from national labour legislation, with limited access to rights and social protection. the awareness of the need for these figures and the role they play in and for society is at odds with the lack of regulations that contribute to fostering undeclared work, creating social marginalization, precariousness and instability typical of undeclared work. and that is what is happening in several member states. in the face of rising unemployment and an ageing population, such jobs could be a choice of occupation rather than a replacement. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of the protection of workers' rights. the time has come for action at both national and european level. we expect the commission to draw up soon a proposal for a directive laying down common rules for the recognition at european level of such workers and ensuring the professionalisation of such figures at both european and national level. i can only agree with the content of the report and that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the report when it stresses that the issue of domestic workers and carers is unfortunately first and foremost a matter of respect for people and, in this particular context, for the dignity of women. and i also agree, as the report points out, that unfortunately the political positions taken in the past on this matter are practically nil. but despite these elements, i have only been able to observe how, despite the sensitivity of the subject, these issues have been treated superficially with the sole purpose of laying a simple foundation for better legislation on the subject in the future. i believe that when it comes to human rights it is not right to act in an incomplete way and i also think that, given the cultural sensitivity inherent in the subject, the union should check the position of the member states before imposing itself as strongly as this report intends to do. i therefore agree with the arguments, but i am absolutely against the procedure, so i could only abstain.

in writing. ‒ i supported this report on the basis that there is very much that can be done to improve the situation for domestic workers in the eu and specifically for women as they are, in many cases, the most affected. workers in the domestic sector face severe challenges as they often are not covered by national labour laws and even if that is the case, it is often hard to find the right information or to get help, legal or otherwise. the report suggests several solutions that i think can have a positive impact in our countries and for the individuals affected. these suggestions include expanding national labour and anti-discrimination laws to domestic workers, to tackle undeclared work and for the commission to adopt and duplicate the best practices from regions or member states to other regions or member states so we can use each other’s ideas and solutions.
in writing. ‒ i welcomed the resolution on domestic workers and carers in the eu, because i have always been convinced of the need to implement sector-specific policies in a society that approaches the issue of ageing with particular urgency. demographic changes in europe are transforming our societies: the average age and life expectancy of citizens are increasing and the birth rate is falling sharply. in such a scenario, domestic helpers and carers provide an essential service that families can no longer afford to forgo. for this reason, the regulation of this new form of employment, which is actually more suitable as a type of underground work, cannot be postponed. the main providers of these services are women. in most cases, they do not have access to the protection of a normal worker and cannot enjoy rights in terms of wage-setting, pension contributions and other benefits provided for by labour law. it is therefore essential to implement effective labour policies at european and national level, taking account of the evolution of society and guaranteeing respect for the rights, access to social protection and a decent life for domestic workers.

in writing. ‒ the protection of domestic workers is a subject that deserves particular attention from the institutions, as it is a sector that is not well regulated in many respects. i voted in favour of this report because i support the idea of a concrete commitment by the commission and the member states to work towards common european standards for domestic and care work. the first step is to draw up a regulatory framework which includes measures to professionalize these sectors so that all the protections provided for by labour law, such as wage fixing, the organization of working hours, weekly leave, maternity leave and other similar benefits, can be implemented. establishing a framework of legal relations between workers and employers, in accordance with the ilo convention no 189 on decent work for domestic workers, would simultaneously help to combat the proliferation of the shadow economy and the erosion of social security systems. specific measures are also needed to take into account the gender and rights of migrants and their placement in the labour market, as these are the groups of the population that perform the most domestic and care work.
in writing. ‒ this report stresses the need to provide for adequate protection of domestic workers and carers in all national laws on labour, health and social welfare, as well as the possibility for domestic workers to join trade unions. this would discourage the illegal recruitment of carers and provide a career opportunity. the 'professionalisation' of domestic work could thus transform precarious and submerged female work into a recognised job, which would allow domestic workers and carers to enjoy adequate social rights. in addition, the majority of domestic workers and carers are immigrant women, many of whom are living in irregular conditions. therefore, their integration into the labour market would facilitate their social and cultural integration as well as compliance with immigration rules. i therefore voted in favour.

member of the commission.– mr president, it is my pleasure to be here to address with honourable members the issue of the nord stream 2 project and the impact it may have on central and eastern european member states. nord stream 2 is a subject of huge concern for many members in this house, but also for member states and in particular for the central and eastern european member states, as was reflected in the letter of nine prime ministers and leaders addressed to president juncker on 17 march. the concerns are of various natures, be they legal, geopolitical or economic. as regards the legal aspect, let me reiterate what we stated in this house some weeks ago. if built, nord stream 2 will have to fully comply, just like any other infrastructure project, with applicable european union law, including on energy and environment. the construction of such an important infrastructure project as nord stream 2 cannot happen in a legal void. this would also run counter to the interests of economic operators in having legal certainty. nor can it be exclusively operated only according to russian law. against the background of colliding legal regimes, nord stream 2, if built, has to be operated under a legal framework which also takes due account of the key principles of our energy market rules. while respect for these legal principles is in our view a necessary precondition, we also recognise that for the central and eastern european member states the issues of the impact on the security of supply of the region and on the central and eastern european gas market are of particular importance. let me remind you that most of the central and eastern european gas market remains highly dependent on a dominant gas supplier, namely gazprom, as well as on a limited number of transport corridors. in the last few years, the commission’s most important objective with regard to the central and eastern european member states has been to foster progress in making the gas market more secure, competitive and diversified, thanks to the european union’s internal energy market infrastructure, development and competition enforcement. in this context, let me mention the commission’s energy security strategy of may 2014, supported by european union member states and this parliament, and the security of supply package originally proposed, with legislative proposals aimed at improving the security of supply of the european union and in particular the more vulnerable regions. regarding infrastructure development, the commission has provided strong support to the central and eastern european member states in terms of improving their connectivity across markets through regional groupings such as bemip and cesec, improving access to lng through building of new lng terminals in lithuania and poland, while another important terminal is planned in croatia, and promoting the development of liquid gas haps not only in the mediterranean, but also in bulgaria. we will continue our efforts together with member states to ensure that other key diversification projects are also completed in the coming years. nord stream 2 will, due to its route, alter the landscape of the european union’s gas markets, and we will have to carefully assess its impact on our own priorities in terms of security of supply, diversification and creation of competitive gas markets, including in central and eastern europe. clearly, nord stream 2 will not give access to a new source of supply or of a supplier and further increase excess capacity from russia to the european union. as regards transit rules, nord stream 2 could lead to gas transportation corridors being decreased from three to at least two – abandoning the route through ukraine – and the german route via poland could also be in danger. such a reduction of routes would not improve security of supply. regarding the market impact of the nord stream 2 project, we are carefully analysing what impact it can have on competition on our gas markets, including in central and eastern europe. we have made a lot of progress in implementing the third energy package across europe and we have to make sure that no market operator is able to leverage its dominant position to the detriment of consumers. let me say at the end of my statement a few words on ukraine. despite economic and political challenges, ukraine continues to be a reliable gas partner and transit country. it is in the interests of all parties, including and notably the central and eastern european countries, that ukraine remains a significant gas transit corridor. the successful implementation of the gas winter package, with the constructive engagement of both russia and ukraine and facilitated by the commission, has helped to secure domestic consumption in ukraine and contributed to a smooth transit in supply of russian gas to the european union. the commission stands ready to continue this successfully proven format and to enlarge the trilateral talks to the negotiation of a new transit contract with russia and ukraine as the current one comes to an end in 2019.
i am in favour of the creation of energy infrastructure such as the strengthening of external supplies and the identification of solutions to expand energy supplies so as to better modulate supply and costs in europe. there is no doubt that we need more instruments, more infrastructure, to respond more flexibly to changes in the energy market and consumption. however, it seems clear to me - and i share what we have heard from president buzek - that the project to double the nord stream gas pipeline does not go in this direction and represents a step backwards compared to the ambitions for the coordination of energy policies that the european commission outlined just a few months ago, in february 2015, in its communication on the energy union, and that this parliament amended and endorsed with the resolution of 15 december. what are the elements? firstly, nord stream increases energy dependence on a single supplier, namely the russian gas giant gazprom, and creates the conditions for the exercise of a dominant market position. at this stage, there is no need to double nord stream, as the current nord stream 1 is operating below capacity. furthermore, nord stream 2 involves almost exclusively players from a single member state. in other words, it is a project for the use and consumption of certain national interests only and not for the general interests of the european union. finally, it is a vulnus in the definition of the future european energy architecture because it is a precedent, according to which a member state has completely free hands in deciding the energy strategy which must involve all european countries. we are therefore opposed to it not for ideological reasons but for reasons connected with a specific policy which europe has adopted.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i will not repeat things to you that you know very well. the data concerning this project have been in your possession for some time and you have also commented on them very explicitly. anyone in europe and the world who has any familiarity with energy and the european union is smiling at the development of this project, because if we were to sit down and try to create an example of a school that could contradict all the objectives that the european union is setting itself in the field of energy, we would not find a suitable example like this. so the first theme is: we are doing the european union a great honour and we are not proving ourselves to be so contradictory. secondly: we are aware that if such a project were to be carried out, there would be a whole section of europe which would not be able to benefit from the gas that will be coming to europe from russia through this pipeline, because there are not enough connections. so it is politically stupid and economically stupid, so help us not to make a fool of ourselves and block this project with us.
member of the commission.– madam president, i would like to thank all the honourable members for their contributions to this debate that have enlightened the views of the commission on this very difficult issue. let me say from the very beginning that i heard some honourable members stressing that we were discussing gas too much and we should concentrate on other sources of energy. it is clear that after the paris agreement on climate change, we are on a path of decarbonising our economies and developing renewables and energy efficiency, but it is also clear that it will take some time. in the meanwhile the cleanest fossil fuel is gas and we have to ensure security of supply for the 28 member states of the european union – not for a single member state but for the 28 member states of the european union. that is why the commission is implementing a security of supply policy, trying to diversify sources, suppliers and routes. that is why we have come along with an lng gas strategy on one side and that is why we are developing interconnectors in central and south-eastern europe, that is why we have implemented reverse flows and that is why the commission is supporting the southern corridor, which is another alternative source of supply. so the commission will keep on applying these policies which are the ones needed to assure security supply all over the european union. there were two specific clear questions. one was by mr hökmark who asked whether this project would make us more or less dependent on russian gas. the answer is very clear, and you know it already, because we speak of about 100 bcm going through a single corridor. that would mean 26% of all european union gas consumption and 80% of russian gas imports on a single route. the answer is very clear. due to the size, the route and the strategic character, it would probably change the architecture of today’s european gas market and further increase the dominance of gazprom in the western european gas market. the european union has made a lot of progress in opening up and integrating energy markets. that is why the european union should therefore make sure that no market operator is able to leverage its dominant position to the detriment of competitors and consumers. so it is clear that this may change. it is also clear that we have to review those changes and apply european laws. european laws must be applied in all aspects. i come back to mr buzek’s questions. he asked whether we were in contact with the german authorities. i can say that, following the mandate of the european council, we have made contact with the german authorities on all levels and my services are in contact with the german regulators to have a complete picture of all the facts needed to assess the project. this is a complex project – it has an onshore part which touches the waters of five different member states – and is difficult to evaluate. but what i can say is that in the commission we are convinced that european union law needs to be applied, including the principles of energy law, which also need to be applied in the case of the offshore part. we will continue our discussions with the german authorities on what this entails in practice. but beyond the application of the legal framework this project has very clear geopolitical consequences and all the members who have intervened have pointed out those consequences. thus this also needs to be discussed at a political level and that is why both vice—president šefčovič and i have explained exactly the same political concerns to the german government on several occasions. what i can say in conclusion is that we all agree that energy produced in the european union must be fully aligned with european union core policy objectives, including energy security. we cannot look in an isolated way at infrastructure projects. we have to find comprehensive and well—balanced solutions which benefit all member states alike, as well as our neighbours. so the commission will take very seriously the remarks of the honourable members. we will continue monitoring this process and applying european union legislation. there was another question at the end on whether we have the opinion of the united states. we have the opinion, we hear the honourable members, but i must say that just last wednesday we had the energy council with the united states and we also discussed this topic, because it is a problem of geopolitical importance and is worth discussing in our bilateral relations with the united states.
in writing. the nord stream 2 project, operated by the russian gas company gazprom, runs counter to the objectives of the energy union and undermines solidarity between member states. at the moment this project is not necessary as nord stream 1 is operating below its capacity. with nord stream 2, the russian giant gazprom would have virtually full control of a significant part of the gas distribution and storage system in central europe, by gaining shares of fields in the north sea and bypassing or cutting out not only ukraine, but several countries in central and eastern europe. there are also legal and environmental concerns. the project is not economically justified and would have negative consequences for the marine environment of the baltic sea. furthermore, nord stream 2 operates only on the basis of russian laws and does not comply with european energy and environmental standards. i therefore ask the commission to put an end to the nord stream 2 project as soon as possible and to concentrate on south stream which is the real long-term solution to ensure energy supplies to european citizens.

the first item on the agenda is the debate on the council and commission statements on china's market economy status (2016/2667 ((rsp)).
i would like to make it very clear that the socialist and democratic group is opposed to the present status of china as a market economy. and that 's for one simple reason: today, china, despite its progress, is not a market economy. let's not get bogged down in technicalities. the future of european industry and millions of jobs are at stake. we have a duty to listen to the legitimate concerns of those workers who fear for their jobs. the steel industry has been dumping chinese industries for years, but unfair competition could affect the whole manufacturing industry. in the face of this risk, in the name of the precautionary principle, we have a duty to stop. the recognition of market economy status would be an irreversible choice, and there can be no compromise solutions or mitigation measures in relation to this. there are only two possibilities: either china fully meets the five criteria that define a market economy (and i challenge anyone to say that the conditions are there today) or china cannot be accorded this status. this is by no means to deny the friendship between china and the european union, which is and will remain strong, but today a risky decision would contribute to the suicide of european industry. we do not want to be partly responsible for a historical error. for these reasons, my group has asked that this parliament debate this issue today and vote tomorrow on a resolution which sends a strong message: the sme to china cannot be recognised.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to make it very clear that china is not a market economy. there is no market economy where the state intervenes heavily to narcotize a world market against real costs. there are two main points, mr president, because we can never accept that. we have fought so hard for workers' rights, environmental rights, fundamental rights in this europe which may or may not be liked, but it is there, perhaps it must be changed but it must not be closed, i would like to say this. but a step like this is crucial for my country, but i believe it is also crucial for europe. it is not possible to think that one can, with the money of the collective of a country, attack a world-wide industry such as the steel industry, which is clear that the cost of ore is higher than the finished product, steel. in view of these facts, i believe that no one, not even those who have the greatest interest, perhaps with a single sector export to china, can decide to vote in favour of recognition.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i think it is useless to repeat concepts which we have already heard. i think it is more useful to understand what the effects and consequences would be if we were to grant china the status of a market economy. i think that immediately there would be a reduction in the trade defenses of the countries of europe, particularly italy, and i think that this could be indicated by an estimated percentage of 30%. what are the consequences of this 30% reduction? there is an economic impact, but above all an employment and employment impact, so we are concerned above all about our workers, our industrial system which would realize the loss of thousands and thousands and thousands of jobs. i think it is important to think about these two concepts above all, because our job is to suggest solutions. the solutions must be those which parliament must propose immediately, beyond a yes or no (and we say no) to the recognition of china's market economy status. but at the same time we are also realizing the condition that a legislative procedure should be activated which in any case provides for trade defence and therefore new anti-dumping defence formulas against chinese products.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have two comments to make to the commission. the first point concerns the defence of the market. we must not defend ourselves against the market, we must defend ourselves in the market. i do not want to spoil my entrepreneurs by convincing them that it is not necessary to have good products and that it is enough to have a state to protect them. i want them to continue, in italy and in europe, to be the leaders of world manufacturing. that is why i want to defend them in a market which defends itself against china, because it does not respect this fundamental rule. second point: i heard someone here say, rather naively, that it's good to buy cheap products from china. that is a typical statement of someone who unfortunately lives more in the here than in the outside, in reality. because those who enter our market with low prices will destroy our industry and then raise prices. that means dumping predators. it means you don't have a choice. we need less ingenuity, less theory and more defence of true excellence, of a strong and sustainable development model like the european one. that is why i say no to the recognition of china's market economy status.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, china is not a market economy, and yet the european commission seems to want to recognize it as such, and if it does we will no longer be able to defend ourselves against its unfair trade practices and we will be invaded by its products. what are we talking about? we are talking about a potential invasion of chinese products worth 145 billion euros, we are talking about a loss of jobs for 3.5 million people in europe, of which about 400 000 in italy alone. we're talking about a drop in gdp of 1 to 2%. the sectors most affected will be steel, ceramics, technology and textiles, but in the future also chemicals and advanced machinery. for italy, as for many other countries in the european union, it would be the final blow. mr president, when we talk about china, we are talking about an economy which produces 80% of its energy from coal, which uses 40 different types of subsidies to enterprises and which ruthlessly practices unfair competition aimed at destroying european industries and slaughtering our workers. so saying "no to mes china" is a definite duty for us today.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, china claims that the wto accession protocol would guarantee automatic recognition of market economy status after 15 years of membership, an interpretation which is totally unacceptable. the recognition of china's market economy status must first be conditional on verification of compliance with the five criteria. in any case, whatever decision the european union may take, it is necessary to think of a plan b, which includes equivalent trade defence measures capable of countering unfair competition practices, ensuring a level playing field between companies from third countries and those in europe. these instruments play a crucial role in safeguarding key sectors of european manufacturing industry which contribute fundamentally to growth and innovation and employment in the member states. it is therefore essential for the european union to maintain trade protection mechanisms by applying first of all the principle of reciprocity in the union's trade policy in order to ensure fair competition and ensure a level playing field. the conditions for granting china market economy status do not currently exist. the commission should therefore make proposals to protect europe's interests by identifying a third way, capable of finding a solution satisfactory to both sides.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by expressing my great satisfaction that parliament is finally adopting a formal position in this plenary session on a matter of strategic importance, after months of being guilty of preventing this house from expressing itself by a vote. the decision we have to make is not whether china is a market economy or not: everyone knows that it is not, neither formally nor substantially. the decision to be made is whether or not to off-load our production system. if this is a legitimate question for an entrepreneur, it is not a question for the institutions, which must govern and guide the future of europe. our institutions must be able to look into the eyes of those small and large entrepreneurs who are opening up their businesses every day, who are competing in the global market with quality and innovation and who are guaranteeing jobs and high standards against artificially subsidized foreign companies. important decisions are to be taken in the coming months, but no deadline can dictate the strategic choices for europe's future.
member of the commission.– mr president, i have taken good note of all the interventions. i think that this debate today has highlighted the fact that, despite the technical complexity of this file, the european union is strongly committed to ensuring that our industry competes on a level playing field. for this to happen, we need to act on the causes of unfair trade, but also on its symptoms. our trade defence instruments must be efficient and effective, independently of the expiry of certain provisions of chinese accession and protocol to the wto. so this object requires action by member states in the council to ensure that the modernisation of our trade defence instruments moves forward quickly. in the meantime, the commission is continuing the impact assessment so that we take account of the views of all those affected, as many of you have mentioned. it is imperative that work is complete in order to enable the commission to make a decision that will reflect all of our interests.
president-in-office of the council. – mr president, it is clearly a complicated file. on the one hand, we entered into agreements with the accession of china to the wto 15 years ago and we cannot just ignore our obligations. on the other hand, china is by no means a market economy, as the commissioner and many meps have rightly stated, and yes, we need to protect european industry and european workers against unfair trade practices. in other words, we will need to balance our international obligations and our strategic commercial interests, the interests of our producers, consumers and users. the council has full confidence that the commissioner, the commission, will act accordingly. mr caspary, and others also, stated that the council should have the necessary political will and unity to overcome the blockade. let me assure you that the dutch presidency is doing everything to do so and let me also underline once more that our ultimate objective is the very same as that of the members of this house: strong and effective trade defence systems in order to tackle unfair trade practices and thus ensure a global level playing field. that is why, as i stated earlier today, the foreign affairs council will discuss the commission’s communication, as well as other proposals and ideas, this friday, 13 may. i am convinced that the exchanges today are a very good basis for further work between our institutions, and again you can rest assured that the council will take into consideration the legitimate interests and concerns of european consumers and producers.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament is invited to give its recommendation to approve or reject the eu-liberia fisheries agreement. the agreement covers a quota of almost 6 500 tonnes. part of the eu contribution is earmarked for the sustainable development of the area. the terms of the agreement allow for greater transparency, so as to foster a culture of sustainable development. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ fishing is a key sector of liberia's economy, and the country's more than 500 kilometres of coastline provide it with a vast eez rich in valuable fish species, including tuna. 3% of liberian gdp and 12% of its agricultural gdp depend on the exploitation of these resources which provide the liberian population with 65% of animal protein. the outbreak of the last civil war has severely affected the sector, leading to an increase in illegal, unregulated and unreported fishing. in particular, foreign fishing vessels have severely compromised liberian fish stocks through their activity, damaging not only the marine ecosystem but also the potential sources of income of indigenous fishermen. the wałęsa report, which i supported with my vote, approves the conclusion of the new sustainable fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and liberia. this is a major agreement which, in return for funding to liberia for scientific research, artisanal fishing and the monitoring and combating of illegal fishing, will guarantee the european ocean fleet access to the liberian eez and its fish resources, while strictly adhering to the principles of sustainable fisheries and aquaculture management.

in writing. ‒ today, eu-liberia fisheries cooperation is part of the wider framework of multilateral agreements or the field of action of organisations operating at regional level. i therefore welcome the conclusion of a first bilateral agreement between the eu and liberia to foster the development of increasingly sophisticated and sustainable fishing practices, while at the same time tackling illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, in line with the eu's overall strategy on this matter. the sustainable fisheries partnership agreement (sfp) and its protocol will strengthen eu-liberia cooperation in tackling this phenomenon, allowing for increased capacity to control fish stocks, enhanced protection of marine ecosystems and a more responsible use of marine resources. the implementation protocol to the agreement grants european access to the liberian fishing zone in a more transparent and regulated framework, which will benefit both parties. the partnership will contribute to the development of the liberian fisheries sector through the promotion of scientific cooperation and the strengthening of infrastructure, encouraging employment among local coastal communities and the economic recovery of the country.

in writing. - the new agreement is only for tuna. for a total of €3.25 million over five years, eu vessels can catch a total of 6 500 tonnes of tuna per year. the financial contributions shall be equally divided between an amount intended for access to fishery resources and an amount intended for support of liberia's sectoral fisheries policy. other elements of the reform are also included, such as the 'exclusivity' clause, a human rights clause and a principle that no other country fishing in deep-sea fisheries can enjoy more favourable conditions than the eu. although the italian interest at stake is relative (the italian fleet fishing in the oceans is relatively small and is directed at other countries), i am in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ in view of the widespread use of practices harmful to the environment and wildlife in the atlantic tuna fishery, we warmly welcome the sustainable fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and liberia. the agreement will serve the dual purpose of promoting sustainable conditions and practices in fishing and ensuring good growth opportunities for european operators. the partnership, through cooperation between the agency for the control of marine resources and the european commission, the reference to the conventions of the international labour organisation, and the imposition of rules to protect marine biodiversity, with particular reference to the populations of tuna, will ensure conditions of greater environmental and social sustainability. the text of the agreement obliges the liberian authorities not to grant fishing licences to third country fleets which do not comply with the terms of the agreement. the contribution will also support job creation and the construction of infrastructure for the fisheries sector, thus supporting measures to stimulate the growth of the economic system, which has been torn apart by years of civil war. during the conflict, the lack of control over fish stocks led to the exploitation of the marine ecosystem by foreign fleets and a decline in the atlantic population.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the legislative resolution by which the european parliament gives its consent to the conclusion of the first sustainable fisheries partnership agreement and its implementation protocol between the european union and the republic of liberia. for a total of €3.25 million over five years, eu vessels will be able to fish 6,500 tonnes of tuna per year in liberian waters. the financial contributions shall be equally divided between an amount intended for access to fishery resources and an amount intended to support liberia's sectoral fisheries policy. the exclusive clause, a human rights clause and a principle that no other country fishing in deep-sea fisheries can enjoy more favourable conditions than the eu have also been included. i believe that this agreement can not only bring many economic benefits to both parties, but also help to strengthen monitoring, control and surveillance in order to prevent iuu fishing and ensure the sustainable exploitation of fishery resources in the region.

in writing. ‒ mauritania, a link between black africa and the maghreb world, is one of the poorest and least developed countries in the world. its weak economy is based on mining and fishing, given the very limited agricultural land on the banks of the senegal river. mauritania's waters are among the richest fishing grounds on the planet, and although the fisheries sector accounts for about 10% of the country's gdp, it still appears to be under-exploited. from 1989 to 2014, the european union and mauritania concluded several fisheries agreements which were replaced in 2015 by the new agreement, which is already provisionally applied. i supported the mato report on the eu-mauritania fisheries partnership because i share its content. the agreement, which provides for a financial contribution for access rights and support for the promotion of sustainable fishing, will give european vessels access to the country's exclusive economic zone for four years and allow them to exploit the country's fish stocks, in particular shrimp, tuna, demersal and pelagic fish.
in writing. ‒ the mato report on the eu-mauritania fisheries partnership agreement is well-articulated and contains no problematic passages. i therefore voted in favour of the text.
in writing. ‒ the first fisheries agreement between the european union and mauritania was signed in 1989 and has been followed by many others, giving the eu access to the country's fisheries resources. the new protocol, which has been provisionally applied since last november, extends fishing opportunities in mauritanian waters and the country's exclusive zone for a further four years and opens up new opportunities for european vessels. it also represents a considerable step forward compared with the provisions of the previous agreement, which covered a number of shortcomings both in terms of the guarantees of non-discrimination and preferential access for the european fleet and in terms of greater transparency, which mauritania is committed to ensuring by making public all agreements concluded in this field with third countries. i therefore support the adoption of this new protocol, which is more balanced and transparent, and which also gives greater weight to environmental sustainability and the socioeconomic dimension of the agreement, for example by providing for the obligation to recruit a substantial proportion of crews from mauritanian fishermen, to the benefit of local employment.

in writing. ‒ on 10 july 2015, the european union and mauritania signed a new protocol, which will allow eu vessels to fish in mauritanian waters for a period of four years. the protocol has already been applied provisionally since 16 november 2015. the financial contribution which the european union will pay to mauritania each year for allowing european vessels access to its exclusive fishing zone amounts to eur 55 million, compared with eur 67 million under the previous protocol. in addition, a financial contribution of 16.5 million for the entire period of the agreement (4,125 million per year, compared with 3 million under the previous protocol) is intended to stimulate the sustainable development of the fisheries sector; the agreement would provide for equal treatment of eu fleets (in the past, sometimes penalized compared to those of other states). mauritania is a medium-interest fishing zone for italian vessels, although it too is penalized by eu technical rules (later extended to its apps agreements with third countries). i vote in favour.
