in writing. ‒ cohesion policy plays a central role in the development of european strategies and objectives. finally, the implementation of the partnership principle, in line with the 2014-2020 strategy, will undoubtedly improve the effectiveness of the implementation of european programmes. two new instruments have been introduced to this end: integrated territorial investment (iti) and participatory local development (clld). while the itil aims to bring together funds from different programmes to make them multidimensional, the clld aims to develop and implement 'bottom-up' strategies for local development. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the report, confident that a multi-level approach is necessary for the successful implementation of regional policies.
in writing. ‒ in 2014, eurostat reported that 63 regions in 7 eu member states had unemployment rates between 2.5% and 4.9%, while at the same time 7 member states had rates above 30%. in a highly diversified context such as this, the role of the eu's core objective in the area of territorial cohesion is becoming increasingly evident. to achieve this, the european union has, over the period 2014-2020, put in place a number of innovative instruments to promote territorial governance and economic and social cohesion. these are integrated territorial investment (iti) and participatory local development (clld). the tomašić report, which i supported with my vote today, effectively describes the complexity of the challenges and opportunities offered by these new instruments, particularly highlighting the significant changes they bring both in terms of combining funding flows and planning local initiatives. the european union must commit itself to providing all possible support, training and guidance to ensure that local development strategies have as their priority objectives the fight against youth unemployment and the financing of smes.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the approach of the two funds, which envisage starting from the needs of the territories to develop investment policies for local development. however, these financial instruments are difficult to manage and excessively burdensome for local authorities: the commission has already proposed a number of amendments to the directive. for these reasons i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ cohesion funds are often used inadequately and partially because of the intricate multi-level management that limits and slows down their use. territorial cohesion is a fundamental objective of the eu, enshrined in the lisbon treaty, and its achievement needs to be underpinned by a clear division of responsibilities and an integrated approach to the territory. two new instruments, participatory local development (plc) and integrated territorial investment (iti), were introduced for the 2014-2020 programming period in order to strengthen a bottom-up approach by consolidating synergies between public and private local actors and allowing to identify priority programmes for funding. but the challenges are still many: the eu's external assistance to the countries of central and eastern europe is limited by administrative burdens, management capacities, implementation responsibilities, constraints on eu funding and poor alignment with other development strategies. we must ensure that the financing measures are used to the maximum extent possible and that the bottom-up approach to the management of the funds is strengthened. that is why i support the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this document because i believe that cohesion policy is one of the main growth tools for the european economy and that its role can be further expanded to make it more effective and efficient. i believe it is particularly important to achieve greater coordination between national and local policies and european policies, and that the short- and medium-term objectives to be pursued are to combat youth unemployment and to support smes, the real backbone of the european economy.
in writing. ‒ cohesion policy is an essential tool for improving the employment of european citizens, while reducing inequalities, poverty and fostering environmentally friendly and inclusive economic growth. in this context, i welcome the introduction, in the new programming period 2014-2020, of new instruments such as local participatory development (clld) and integrated territorial investment (iti) under the european structural and investment funds. these are new arrangements which, by delegating greater responsibility and management powers to the local level, can help to develop a kind of bottom-up approach which i believe is essential for the full achievement of the objectives of cohesion policy. however, we must work together to facilitate the use of these new mechanisms, in particular by simplifying the administrative burden required and fostering greater cooperation and trust between different levels of government, which is essential to ensure that these instruments deliver real results. it is also necessary for national states and the european institutions to actively intervene to support local actors, who often encounter difficulties in conceiving and implementing local development strategies, in developing and implementing them.
in writing. ‒ the rapporteur, from the ecr group, considers it difficult to assess the two financial instruments, which came into force with the current mff. although the bottom-up approach of the two funds (i.e. based on the needs of the territories) is positive, it is noted that the two instruments are complicated to manage for local authorities and onerous in administrative terms. the report is critical, although it could have been more so. on that basis, i will abstain.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the new instruments for territorial development in cohesion policy 2014-2020 which calls on the member states to make greater use of the instruments of integrated territorial investment (iti) and participatory local development (clld) for the implementation of the territorial approach of cohesion policies. the bottom-up approach and the participation of local actors are essential elements for the effectiveness of the structural funds and the effective achievement of its objectives. clld also offers opportunities for urban and peri-urban areas and should be an integral part of wider urban development strategies. however, its implementation through a single fund approach may result in missed opportunities in creating more effective local development strategies. as regards itis, they should not be limited to urban areas only, but could concern geographical areas such as metropolitan, urban and rural or cross-border areas. it is essential that local partners play their role as key actors in the preparation of the territorial development strategy, since this instrument allows for the specific territorial needs to be taken into account by determining their scope more flexibly.
in writing. ‒ the report analyses two new instruments of cohesion policy: integrated territorial investment (iti) and participatory local development (clld). the first is a new allocation method designed to combine funds from different priority axes of one or more operational programmes. clld is a tool to be used at sub-regional level and is designed to promote the implementation of local development strategies characterised by a bottom-up approach. i voted in favour of the report. the text analyses the effectiveness and added value of the two instruments, and provides a comprehensive overview of the challenges and possible critical points. the report also stresses the crucial importance of minimising potential conflicts of interest in interactions between public and private actors, and of a non-discriminatory and transparent approach in relations between the european, national and regional levels.
in writing. ‒ participatory local development (pla) and integrated territorial investment (iti) are the new instruments envisaged by cohesion policy for the period 2014-2020 to promote integrated strategies for sustainable urban development. the report voted on today in plenary highlighted the weaknesses of the two instruments, which local actors consider to be too complex and require specific skills that are often not available in administrations, especially if they are small. in italy, these instruments concern the four southern regions where, in addition to the objective difficulties encountered by other european regions, there is the problem of programming by supplementing the financial resources provided for by the various structural and investment funds. while i share the view that iti and clld can play an important role in addressing the multiple, closely interlinked challenges facing urban areas (social, demographic, economic and environmental) and that they can therefore only be overcome through an integrated approach, i believe that action is needed to simplify them also in order to reduce administrative costs. i hope that the high-level group set up by the commission will soon be able to identify useful guidelines to promote accessibility by local authorities. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it aims at a very important objective for the european union, namely cohesion between the various territories. i believe that in order to achieve this objective the report takes account of a fundamental element which i myself have learned over the years of my political work: if we want to achieve strong cohesion, we need a bottom-up approach involving local actors. support is therefore needed at both national and european level with targeted funding. having noted that the report in question takes account of all these elements, which i consider to be fundamental, i voted in favour, hoping to achieve this important goal as soon as possible, for a europe united not only on paper but also in fact.
in writing. ‒ territorial cohesion is one of the fundamental objectives of the european union enshrined in the treaty of lisbon. by offering the potential to improve employment opportunities, promoting sustainable and inclusive growth and fostering poverty reduction and social inclusion, cohesion policy is shaping up as a tool for territorial development. in this regard, two new instruments have been introduced under the european structural and investment funds in the 2014-2020 programming period to achieve the territorial cohesion objective: participatory local development and integrated territorial investment. i voted in favour of the report, but i also took into account the considerable challenges that integrated territorial investments pose to the implementation by local authorities, who are often unprepared in the management of funding. the eu should therefore encourage the use of integrated, territory-based approaches to foster economic, social and territorial cohesion, while also promoting territorial governance.
in writing. ‒ the tomasic report looks at territorial development strategies and the delegation of responsibilities and resources at decision-making levels in the 2014-2020 cohesion policy programme. the report states that stakeholder involvement can strengthen the integrated and local approach, especially where the use of clld (participatory local development) and iti (integrated territorial investment) is limited. local actors require technical and financial support from the regional, national and european levels, particularly in the early stages of the implementation process. the report also calls on the member states to provide support to smaller local bodies with limited capacity, stressing that the definition of adequate and quality strategies is still a challenge. the report is well done and touches on issues of fundamental importance, which is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ coordination between local and regional actors in territorial development strategies is an essential element for the success of territorial policies for the development of urban and rural areas. cohesion policy 2014-2020 identified two important tools to foster synergies between the various stakeholders: integrated territorial investment and participatory local development. my vote in favour of this resolution is to support integrated national and regional policies aimed at concrete and sustainable results that meet the objectives identified by the eu programmes. i believe that the smaller and less developed local communities should be given special support, where the lack of resources and skills not only aggravates general phenomena such as youth unemployment, but also makes it more difficult to implement cohesion policy instruments effectively. i am convinced that territorial cohesion starts from the bottom up and that all regions, including the smallest and most remote regions and rural areas, must be able to use the instruments for planning and implementing local development strategies without having to bear the administrative and financial burdens at national, regional and local level.
in writing. ‒ the late adoption of many 2014-2020 operational programmes, the complexity of innovative cohesion policy instruments, iti - integrated territorial investments and clld - participatory local development, implemented for the first time and by only a few member states, do not allow an analysis of their effectiveness and added value. the bottom-up approach and the involvement of local actors are essential to achieving the objectives, but it must be recognised that local actors often lack the capacity to implement development strategies that affect their territory and therefore need adequate support, both at national and european level. in my view, the commission should present a roadmap indicating which states and operational programmes are most at risk of automatically decommitting resources. we also need the late payment directive and the public procurement regulations to be properly applied, so that there is a real balance between simplification and preventive measures against errors and fraud, so as to prevent both misuse of the many billions at our disposal and infiltration by organised crime. my vote on the resolution is in favour.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote in favour of this report because i believe it is essential to encourage local actors to use the new instruments for territorial investment. this would ensure better coordination and targeted use of the european structural and investment funds. it will therefore be important to provide for ad hoc activities to bring these instruments closer to local actors so that they can effectively participate in the development strategies of their territory.
in writing. ‒ i abstain because the instruments in question are complicated for local authorities to manage and the report in question is not sufficiently critical.
in writing. ‒ i support these new cohesion policy instruments as they will give new tools to the eu in order to provide local actors and governments with better funding for crucial development projects, part of the cohesion policy. this ‘bottom-up’ approach to development and financing is crucial if the eu is to achieve the objectives of the cohesion policy and we must face all the challenges that these instruments will face in the short term. i believe that the cohesion policy must be a constantly evolving programme to face our modern challenges and i hope that these new instruments can play their part in this. it is very important to overcome any lack of administrative capacity on the side of local actors and then proceed with addressing our changing realities; changing demographics and high unemployment, especially among youths.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the non-legislative resolution of the ep on the new instruments for territorial development in cohesion policy 2014-2020: integrated territorial investment (iti) and participatory local development (clld), as i believe that the active involvement of regional and local organisations is crucial for the full implementation of economic, social and territorial cohesion policy, and i am convinced that innovative approaches that promote local knowledge and aim at local solutions are needed to tackle local problems. in other words, we need economic, social and territorial cohesion policy more than ever to tackle the territorial imbalances that still exist between the various regions of europe and to give the poorest and most disadvantaged regions the opportunity to converge towards higher levels of growth and income and to move towards those of the richer regions. i believe that it is in the interest of the european single market to have regions which do not differ too much from one another, because competition in the global economy with the stronger countries can only be sustained if europe has less inequality within itself. at the same time, we need to involve local actors more and more in the implementation of cohesion policy.
in writing. i vote in favour of the report which envisages the establishment of new instruments for territorial development in cohesion policy 2014-2020. territorial cohesion is one of the eu's key objectives, supported by integrated approaches that improve the efficiency of public intervention in the territory. in this respect, the framework of the european structural and investment funds (esi funds) introduced two new measures to achieve the objectives of territorial cohesion. these new instruments provide for local participatory development (clld) and integrated territorial investment (iti). the report to be voted on today aims to analyse the programming and implementation of the clld and the iti, identifying the main problems they face and possible recommendations for better implementation of these instruments. in putting these measures into practice we want to allow for greater participation by local members and thus promote an approach that starts right in our communities and leads, in the long run, to the achievement of our common objectives.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on new instruments for territorial development in cohesion policy 2014-2020. cohesion policy and territorial cohesion are among the european union's priority objectives enshrined in the lisbon treaty. in the framework of the european structural and investment funds, two new instruments have been introduced for the 2014-2020 programming period to achieve the territorial cohesion objective: participatory local development (clld), a new instrument to be used at subregional level, and integrated territorial investments (iti), used to achieve the objective of sustainable urban development, as well as being used for other types of territory.
in writing. ‒ the bottom-up approach to territorial development requires more support from the eu level, as well as from regional and national governments. as the report says, local actors need better funding and technology to be more effective in their actions. the eu should encourage the exchange of good practice between european regions. in the end, job creation is the most important issue along with support for smes in underdeveloped regions. in too many of these regions, young people and women are hampered by a lack of education and opportunities, so this should be our first priority when working in these regions. i voted in favour of the report because all the issues mentioned are addressed.
in writing. ‒ the harmonious development of the union by strengthening its economic, social and territorial integration is a central objective of the eu's cohesion policy. the allocation by the european regional development fund (erdf) of a budget of 5% of the expenditure (eur 16 billion) for the introduction of two new instruments in the 2014-2020 programming period is a step in the right direction and i therefore voted in favour of it. on the one hand, local participatory development (clld) with the aim of strengthening synergies between local actors, both public and private, on the other hand, integrated territorial investments (iti) that can be used to achieve the objective of sustainable urban development, as well as being used for other types of territory. two important initiatives towards ever closer cooperation between local actors and an incentive to a bottom-up approach to cohesion policies. our commitment at european level to implement these instruments together with local actors and to strengthen their capacities, while respecting their national constraints, cannot be undermined. i therefore hope that these instruments will become increasingly important in the practice of cohesion policy in the future.
in writing. ‒ with reference to the proposal by mrs tomašić, i thought it appropriate to vote in favour, as i believe that the adoption of an integrated territorial approach is a particularly valuable tool for the development of european cohesion policy for the period 2014-2020. i am convinced that these approaches will make it possible to pay particular attention to the specific features of the territory and to attract more investment. i also believe that focusing on local, bottom-up development can be particularly beneficial in enhancing the role of local and regional actors. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i support the need to devise new strategies involving local and regional actors who need to be given technical and financial support in the context of an effective partnership between the regions, the member states and the eu. the interest in an integrated approach on a territorial basis is supported by the new cohesion policy for the 2014-2020 programming period, and is important for the purpose of greater flexibility of eu programmes and better use of european funds allocated in a manner consistent with local specificities, in order to achieve sustainable economic outcomes and to address structural problems, first and foremost youth unemployment. the commission and the member states should provide additional support, training and guidance to smaller and less developed local actors, who have more limited resources and capacity and for whom the administrative burden and complexity of implementing these instruments may be difficult to manage in the planning and implementation phases.
in writing. ‒ cohesion policy for the 2014-2020 programming period places greater emphasis on the use of integrated approaches based on the needs of territories to promote economic, social and territorial cohesion. the new erdf regulation provides for 5% of its budget to be allocated to sustainable urban development. two new instruments have been introduced under the european structural and investment funds to achieve this objective: the local community-led development (clld). as mentioned earlier, it is expected that around 5% of the cohesion policy budget (around eur 16 billion) will be used for these instruments. if the objectives of cohesion policy are to have the desired effect, adequate economic support at european level is needed, especially for the most remote and disadvantaged areas such as islands and mountain areas. i voted in favour of the report and i hope that instruments such as the iti and the clld will play an increasingly central role.

in writing. ‒ the development of reliable statistics is a key element in ensuring the consistency of the economic policies of the eu member states with the community's legal framework and economic governance system. the monitoring of economic developments within the union is carried out through a general framework based on regulation (ec) no 184/2005 on balance of payments (bp) statistics, international trade in services (iss) and foreign direct investment (fdi). the giegold report, which i have supported today, has effectively tackled the problem of the revision of regulation 184/2005 by linking it to the increasing complexity of international financial flows. the text adopted indicates two priorities in particular: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a european statistical office. the commission's overall priority must be to strengthen cooperation with other international organisations providing economic statistics, such as the imf and the oecd, in order to establish a comprehensive system which will provide increasingly reliable statistics for monitoring macroeconomic imbalances.
in writing. ‒ i do not agree with the giegold report, which updates the legislation on delegated and implementing acts conferred on the european commission. i believe that the eu legislation on the collection of macroeconomic data, a field which is often subject to manipulation of statistics, needs to be completely reviewed, in line with the guidelines set out by the union institutions. i consider the commission, an institution outside democratic and citizen control, to be unable to guarantee the transparency of statistical processing. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ the text voted today aims to revise regulation 184/2005 and has a twofold objective: to improve the quality and standardisation of community statistics on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment. such harmonisation is of fundamental importance in order to formulate correct and effective economic forecasts and, consequently, to allow for better management of macroeconomic imbalances and of any future crises. i welcome the fact that, in promoting the collection of increasingly reliable and comparable data, the report supports greater coordination between eurostat and the other international organisations which provide most of the statistics in this field, such as the oecd and the international monetary fund, as well as further differentiation with regard to foreign direct investment in particular. in this respect, the distinction between greenfield investment flows, which give rise to real gross investment and generate new opportunities, and mere acquisitions, which only change the ownership of pre-existing economic activities, is certainly a positive one. the revised text will therefore provide more valuable data, allowing better traceability and understanding of flows, and thus of economic and trade trends in an increasingly globalised world.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this document because i believe it is important that the union should have the most up-to-date and accurate statistics, which will enable it to devise and implement its policies in the most appropriate way to the current fluid and multifaceted reality.
in writing. ‒ the regulation in question, as its title suggests, concerns eu statistics on certain performance of the member states. it is a matter of course, almost a text to be overlooked without paying too much attention. the problem, however, is that our delegation is sceptical of the powers delegated to the ec, the real european institution, which is far from democratic control and far from the citizens. we can also say that we are not particularly keen on the conflict between the ep and the council over the use of delegated acts (which parliament normally prefers) or implementing acts (which are more in the interests of the council). the basic problem for the league is the lack of confidence in the work of the ec and the fact that, in such a sensitive area as the collection of macroeconomic data, there is very frequent politically fraudulent or self-interested use of the interpretation of numbers and data flows. the issue of 'manipulation' of statistics is, in our view, central. the council has succeeded in including some additional guarantees of transparency in the final agreement, but overall this is still a measure which i voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today because the revision of regulation (ec) no 184/2005 represents a real opportunity to increase the transparency and granularity of balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment statistics. i believe that an update should also be made to ensure alignment with the rules laid down in the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu). it is therefore necessary to take full advantage of recent legal innovations and to make these statistics an increasingly reliable instrument for supporting economic policy decisions. my vote in favour is also due to the need to strengthen reporting and publication requirements to provide a better overview of gross capital flows. the benefit that can be derived from recent innovations, such as the international legal entity identifier (lei code), part of the organisation for economic co-operation and development (oecd) framework for improving the transmission of financial information for tax purposes, is not of secondary importance.
in writing. ‒ the measure aims to amend the regulation on community statistics relating to balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment in the light of the new provisions of the tfeu. therefore, the main objective is to give the european commission more powers in the issuing of delegated and implementing acts. i abstained because, although the final text of the econ committee accepted all our amendments, it was completely distorted in the trilogues. the final text also provides for the creation of a new executive agency of the commission and thus a further waste of public money from the citizens of the european union.
in writing. ‒ statistics are a key tool for economic policy decisions, and their reliability is crucial to the ability to anticipate the emergence of new financial crises in the future. it has been shown that in 2008 poor quality statistics underestimated the scale of the crisis that would have hit our economies hard. the updating of the existing regulation on the eu statistical framework for balance of payments, international trade in services and direct investment, adopted in plenary, is essential in particular to verify and monitor developments in current accounts and financial flows within and outside the union, which have intensified in recent years and become more complex and difficult to analyse. eurostat's cooperation with international organisations such as the oecd and the international monetary fund (imf) should also be strengthened and the evaluation of the quality of national contributions to statistics should be publicly disseminated. i therefore thought i should vote in favour of amending the regulation because it introduces measures to improve and make statistics more transparent at european level, which will also allow us to understand better the impact of direct investment on employment.
in writing. ‒ the statistics in the report are clear: i think this amendment should be seen as a positive opportunity to increase transparency and to take advantage of recent legal innovations and to make these statistics a more reliable instrument for economic policy decisions. it is in line with these objectives, which the report itself seeks to achieve, that i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the production of reliable statistics on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment is essential in order to monitor developments in current accounts and financial flows within and outside the eu. statistics in these areas help to ensure the consistency of the economic policies of the member states with the broad guidelines of the union, as well as with the legal obligations arising from the community economic governance framework. international financial flows have intensified and become more complex, and in particular the increased use of vehicle companies and legal arrangements for the transfer of both incoming and outgoing capital flows has made it more difficult to monitor these flows to ensure their proper traceability and to avoid double or multiple accounting, thus making it more difficult to combat tax evasion and aggressive tax planning. i therefore voted in favour of the regulation on the harmonization of community statistics in the field of taxation.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the agreement with the council on the proposal for a regulation amending regulation (ec) no 184/2005 on community statistics relating to balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment. i believe that high quality and comparable statistics on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment (fdi) are essential for eu policy-makers, researchers and all european citizens. i therefore supported the need to empower the commission (eurostat) to take all necessary measures to allow easy and user-friendly online access to data sets and to provide users with an intuitive presentation of the data. this type of statistics is of fundamental importance in ensuring the informed formulation of economic policies and the correct formulation of economic forecasts. i shared the position, supported by the ep, to update the levels of geographical breakdown, the levels of breakdown by institutional sector and the levels of breakdown by economic activity provided that such updates do not affect the reporting burden or change the applicable underlying conceptual framework. i also share the need to give the ecb more consultative powers.
in writing. with regard to balance of payments (bp) statistics, international trade in services (its) and foreign direct investment (fdi), eu intervention is aimed at monitoring economic developments in individual member states but also in the european union as a whole. the aim of this proposal is to amend the regulation to adapt it to the new institutional context. the problem arises from the emerging conflict between the ecb and the commission on statistics. in the previous system, the ecb was consulted on matters within its competence, whereas the commission's proposal seeks to exclude the ecb from obtaining relevant statistics. i therefore believe that the revision of this regulation represents an opportunity to increase the transparency and flow of statistics in relation to the olaf, the sis and the fdi, and thus to make it possible to benefit from these instruments in a clearer and more reliable way.

in writing. ‒ we welcome regulation no 184/2005 on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment statistics as part of the eu's overall framework for monitoring economic developments in each member state and in the union as a whole. the production of reliable statistics in these areas is essential, especially to verify key aspects such as developments in current accounts and financial flows within and outside the eu. they therefore help to ensure that the economic policies of the member states are consistent with the broad guidelines of the union, as well as with the legal obligations arising from the eu economic governance framework. more specifically, the availability of reliable statistics is essential for the monitoring process established under the macroeconomic imbalance procedures. the revision of the regulation represents a genuine opportunity to increase the transparency and granularity of statistics and to take advantage of recent legal innovations and make statistics a more reliable tool for economic policy decisions. secondly, the regulation needs to be updated to ensure its alignment with the rules contained in the tfeu, by conferring on the commission the necessary powers to adopt delegated and/or implementing acts.

in writing. ‒ mountain regions are an area that is fundamental to the economic, social and sustainable development of many member states and, in general, a source of ecosystem services that are essential for the whole union. the iotova report, which i supported with my vote today, focuses on the need to define the terms 'mountain region' and 'regional policy' precisely, in order to move effectively towards the implementation of a concrete policy proposal for these emerging regions. despite occupying 30% of the eu's territory, they are rarely considered today in cohesion policy and national policies, often also because of the additional costs arising from chronic infrastructure deficiencies and their peripheral location. a change of perspective is needed, starting with the establishment of an eu mountain agenda and an increase in esi funds for underdeveloped mountain regions. increased connectivity and accessibility, together with a strong investment in renewable energy, can make europe's mountains real centres of green growth. only by creating these new catalysts for sustainable development within the eu can we stop the depopulation of our mountains and make them more suitable places to live and work.

in writing. ‒ the richness of natural resources and the invaluable agricultural and manufacturing heritage of mountain areas represent a huge resource for the european union, both in environmental and employment terms. we can think of the abundance of renewable energy sources or the opportunities for developing quality green jobs, offering sustainable economic development to mountain areas. unfortunately, the lack of infrastructure and the high costs of living in these areas make it difficult to invest in them. it is therefore necessary to include these areas in a 'regional strategy' covering surrounding areas and urban areas within cohesion policy, so that the next programming period of eu funding is managed in a more integrated and efficient way than the current one. i therefore voted in favour of the report, which aims to provide better conditions, compensatory measures and support for farmers, producers, businesses and people in these areas.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this document because i believe it is important that the union adopt a targeted strategy for the eu's mountain regions, which represent 30% of the eu's territory and one of its main biodiversity basins, to enable them to be safeguarded and developed sustainably.
in writing. ‒ a significant part of europe's territory (about 30%) is made up of mountain regions. these are highly sensitive areas, with unique and contrasting characteristics, which require special attention: while they suffer from problems of peripheral location, depopulation, ageing of the population and a particular territorial configuration, which places major constraints on many economic and productive activities, they make a fundamental contribution, through their rich ecosystems, to the fight against climate change and the protection of biodiversity. in addition, precisely in response to these problems and their management, mountain areas can become - and in some cases already are - privileged laboratories for promoting the development of new practices capable of combining economic well-being and ecological sustainability. in this sense, in accordance with article 174 (3) tfeu, i believe that all eu policies should provide for a specific new approach that takes account of their particularities. in addition, in order to respond adequately to the needs of mountain regions, the coordination of the various policies and programmes (cap, natura 2000, horizon 2020, etc.) that have an impact on these territories needs to be strengthened, increasing the funds available to them and promoting the creation of macro-regional strategies.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report is a long and exhaustive list of policies and actions for mountain people and mountain areas in general. the report does not contain any criticisms worthy of note and we also find positive references to the alpine macro-region. i vote for it.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on cohesion policy which calls for a strategy for the 'mountain regions' too, following on from what has already been done for the macro-regions and the alpine region, which allows for an integrated and coordinated approach to the use of the funds available. the report calls, first of all, for a definition of 'mountain region'. the current definition of 'mountain' was conceived mainly in the context of agricultural policy and therefore takes into account only certain aspects. a definition is needed which allows a global approach. secondly, there is a call for an agenda for the eu's mountain regions. many policies have been developed that indirectly concern mountain regions, but only a specific agenda could provide an even more targeted framework for cohesion policy and lay the foundations for a territorial approach for the next programming period. finally, great emphasis was also placed on the issues of connectivity and accessibility of mountain regions, often isolated, which can only become more attractive for living in or for sme settlement if it is possible to envisage and achieve growth that is at the same time smart, sustainable and inclusive.
in writing. ‒ the report addresses the issue of cohesion for the eu's mountain regions by highlighting the specific challenges and opportunities of these territories. there are several aspects of the text which we agree with, such as the call on the commission to present an agenda for mountain regions in the wake of the urban agenda. it also calls for a definition of the term 'mountain regions', which is still absent and often the basis for choices in the programming of the funds. finally, the reference to the fundamental role of small and medium-sized enterprises in the development of mountain regions, the role of social enterprise and alternative business models for inclusive development and environmental protection should also be appreciated. despite the many positive aspects, i have decided to abstain on the report, as i have noted some important shortcomings. i am referring, among other things, to the presence of far too positive references to financial instruments or forms of public-private partnership, since the lack of economies of scale would make the provision of such services unattractive from a commercial point of view.
in writing. ‒ due to the specific characteristics of their geographical location, mountain regions face difficulties and challenges that are not fully covered by the union's policies, and in particular by cohesion policy, which should, instead, help more than others to limit and overcome territorial disadvantages. what is lacking are specific objectives and instruments more suited to the particular needs of the territory. the request to the european commission to draw up an agenda for the eu's mountain regions arises from the need to have a specific framework on which to develop cohesion policy, and to adapt the european structural and investment funds accordingly in the next programming period. it is undeniable that these areas are facing serious difficulties, mainly due to the lack of accessibility, infrastructure, connectivity and human resources. moreover, the development needs of smes in mountain areas are not compatible with those indicated in european programmes such as horizon 2020 or cosme, in which they are unable to participate. the commission must therefore proceed as soon as possible to identify a specific strategy to take account of the mountain dimension in future european programmes and policies. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this report is to respond to an obvious territorial problem, namely to alleviate the difficulties faced by european mountain areas both because of the lack of infrastructure and because of their peripheral location. the answer is to improve cohesion between the various mountain regions in europe through targeted investment to protect the great natural wealth that mountains represent on the one hand and jobs throughout the union on the other. indeed, mountain areas have much to offer, including employment! i therefore voted in favour of this report, which i believe lays a solid foundation for better social, economic and territorial cohesion, offering sustainable economic development to mountain areas.
in writing. ‒ given the size of the eu's mountain regions, insufficient attention is paid to the difficulties of investing in mountain areas due to the lack of infrastructure and the additional costs of peripheral location. given that mountain regions offer a number of opportunities to achieve the eu's employment, cohesion and environmental objectives through the sustainable use of their natural resources, i believe it is necessary to give priority to the territorial dimension of cohesion policy through targeted initiatives for territorial development and additional support for territorial cooperation at european level. moreover, by virtue of the abundance and variety of renewable energy sources and their dependence on resource and energy efficiency, mountain regions can contribute to the development of new technologies and to innovation more generally. i voted in favour also because of the particular nature of mountain areas and the ecosystems that characterise them, and because it is therefore necessary to promote measures to protect the representative species of the high mountains. a coordinated approach is essential in whatever form it is implemented, in order to ensure that eu funding is strategically directed towards achieving sustainable and inclusive growth.
in writing. ‒ mountain regions play an essential role in the economic, social and sustainable development of the member states: can contribute to the development of new technologies and increase the use of renewable energy; manage ecosystems with specificities in terms of biodiversity; their activities have a crucial impact on many economic sectors. this wealth exposes mountain areas to specific needs and significant challenges, including the scarcity of usable land, climate change, off-season employment and environmental protection. i therefore support the resolution's vision of a specific european policy for the eu's mountain regions, taking account of their structural disadvantages and proposing transnational and interregional strategies to turn these disadvantages into opportunities and territorial development. in particular, i hope that the new european agenda for the development of mountain regions will take account of the shortcomings of local smes in terms of infrastructure, connectivity and human resources, providing effective instruments to encourage a multi-faceted agricultural production linked to the development of tourism and environmental protection activities, and to strengthen sectors such as forestry which can create new employment opportunities, as well as the preservation of forest resources.

excluding the united states and canada - with which the european union has not yet signed a trade agreement. in addition, in recent years the distance between the two sides of the atlantic has seemed to increase, due to a strategic shift of latin american countries towards asia, and in particular towards china, as evidenced by the conclusion of plurilateral treaties such as the tpp and some bilateral agreements such as china-chile and china-peru. today, however, the mercosur partners are showing a new willingness, and the relaunch of negotiations on an association agreement is a significant opportunity to strengthen the links already existing with this area in the wider context of a transatlantic strategy of the european union. the exchange of offers which will take place in the next few days will be a key stage in this renewed commitment. the agreement would provide not only for a reduction in tariffs but also for the reduction of non-tariff barriers and greater cooperation on controls and compliance with mutual standards. but as with all agreements, we are asking that trade should be seen as a new opportunity and not just as a source of imbalance. we ask the commission to be ambitious in the negotiations but also to be cautious, taking into account the needs of the most sensitive sectors of our production fabric. i hope that today's debate will show the political support of the european parliament for the relaunch of the negotiations, so that a balanced agreement can be reached which will be a real factor in the economic development of our continent.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, managing the migration phenomenon responsibly also means, and above all, opening up legal and regular channels of legal immigration. in adopting this directive, parliament and the council acknowledge the need to harmonize procedures and to make it easier for researchers, students, pupils, volunteers and young people alike to enter and stay in the community. today's vote opens the way to a future common migration policy based on regular access to the european union. of course, these are temporary economic migration measures, but a first step has been taken. the amendments which this house has made during the legislative procedure will give third-country nationals the right to enter, reside and carry out part of their research or studies in one or more member states. the same right will also be granted to pupils, volunteers and workers on equal terms. we recognize that these same people are entitled to equal treatment with the member state concerned. we recognise the possibility for students and researchers to stay for a period after the end of their studies or research in order to enable them to find employment or start a business. demographic challenges and the multiple shortages of labour, not just highly skilled labour, require us to review the fragmented national policies on economic migration, to focus on general rules on the entry and residence of workers from third countries. the opening of channels for economic migrants would also be the most effective measure to counter the modern slavery which is increasingly taking root in our territories through the exploitation of migrant workers, especially women. it is a fact, mr president: europe can only prosper if it facilitates the mobility of knowledge, goods and people.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i thank mrs wikström for her work. the directive we are voting on today has a strong symbolic value. it not only establishes a coordinated and transparent regulatory framework to make it easier for third-country nationals to enter europe for study purposes, but it also sets the conditions for student mobility, not flight but the circulation of brains, in order to create a labour market open to researchers not only from europe. we are giving the opportunity to increase the skills of those who, and there are many, who want to come to europe to train, to acquire knowledge and to experience internships that will be of use not only in the union but also in their countries of origin. the fact that we have succeeded, for example, in raising the minimum weekly hours limit to allow students to work part-time means that we have given them the practical opportunity of training in the field in order to develop professional profiles which are immediately usable in the labour market and in the enterprise. the directive sets out the arrangements for welcoming into the world of training, research and, therefore, work those who believe in and appreciate the european design and see europe as a centre of excellence, culture but also of opportunity. and they are mutual opportunities, because europe needs highly qualified people in different areas of research and innovation to remain competitive on the world stage. i also consider this directive to be an important part of european immigration policy, which paves the way for legal migration by focusing on young people, particularly students and researchers, and by promoting and supporting intra- and extra-european mobility.

in writing. ‒ today's vote in favour of the diaz report is a testament to the european parliament's strong commitment to strengthening the protection and security of citizens of the european union. the text has positive elements in that it strengthens the mandate of the european police agency by providing it with new governance rules and, at the same time, new responsibilities. in addition, the call for greater efforts in the fight against international terrorism, including through the monitoring of internet content, is an important signal of prevention against fundamentalism. the new powers conferred on europol will not weaken the data protection safeguards. the european data protection supervisor will monitor the activities of the police agency, while a joint parliamentary control group will supervise its work. the report as a whole must therefore be regarded positively because, in addition to testifying to the european parliament's strong commitment to combating terrorism, it is a step forward towards greater exchange of information between the police forces of the individual member states.
in writing. ‒ the eu and its member states share responsibilities for maintaining the security, justice, freedom and fundamental rights of the citizens of the union: this requires the creation of an effective level of data protection in the judicial and police activities of the eu and its member states. pushing for the creation of common institutions that harmonise activities, implementing genuine cooperation between supervisory authorities at national and union level, is essential to enhance strategic and operational cooperation between the member states of the european union, their intelligence and police forces and partner countries in order to make the fight against terrorism, mafias, smuggling and international crime more effective, bearing in mind that the ultimate goal of making the system more efficient must be the creation of an eu police and intelligence force subject to democratic control by european citizens.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of this recommendation to allow the european police agency, europol, to step up efforts to fight terrorism, cybercrime and other crimes and to respond more quickly to threats. in particular, it will be easier for europol to set up specialised units to respond immediately to emerging threats. in some cases, europol will be able to exchange information directly with private parties, such as companies or ngos, in order to act more quickly. for example, europol's special unit for internet monitoring will be able to contact directly the providers responsible for a social network such as facebook and ask that a web page operated by isis be deleted, thus more quickly blocking the spread of terrorist propaganda. these new powers conferred on europol will go hand in hand with stronger data protection safeguards and instruments of democratic parliamentary scrutiny. the european data protection supervisor (edps) will be responsible for monitoring europol's activities and a clear complaints procedure for eu citizens will be established. a joint parliamentary monitoring group will also be set up to oversee europol's work.
in writing. ‒ this is the vote on second reading on the new draft regulation establishing the european union agency for law enforcement cooperation and training (europol). the new regulation aims to bring the decision currently underpinning europol into line with the requirements of the lisbon treaty and introduces a mechanism for the ep to scrutinise europol's activities in association with national parliaments. a stronger data protection regime applicable to the agency is also introduced, in particular by ensuring the full independence of the data protection officer of europol. further elements of improved governance of europol will also be introduced, so that it can provide more effective support to member states in the fight against terrorism and other serious forms of crime. i certainly voted for it.

in writing. ‒ in the face of the severe economic crisis, which has led to liquidity problems and a severe shortage of available public funds, cohesion funds have become the main source of public investment in many member states. despite the absolute need for these funds, the absorption capacity of many member states remains surprisingly low. the main obstacles are lack of information, lack of transparency and the separate management of the different european funds. to fully exploit the potential of financing, effective structural reforms, pro-investment policies and the full application of the flexibility provided for in the stability pact should be encouraged. this report, which i support, clarifies the main challenges for the future in implementing operational programmes, promoting cooperation, synergy and transparency to avoid the dispersion of funds and helping europe's regions to become more competitive.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this document because i believe it is important to make the implementation of cohesion policy faster and more efficient, because the financial instruments made available by the structural funds, if applied effectively on the basis of an appropriate ex ante evaluation and in strategic combination with grants, can significantly increase the impact of funding, thus helping to offset the negative effects of public budgetary contractions and to develop revenue-generating projects.
in writing. ‒ thanks to the union's misguided economic policies, cohesion between the eu's regions is getting weaker by the day. thus, implementing the europe 2020 objectives means widening macroeconomic inequalities between and within member states (think of the gap between padania and italy, which, due to the crisis and austerity policies, has never been so wide). in other words, there is this paradox: the more european funding you use (so you are "virtuous"), the more you have to increase public spending (co-financing) but, at the same time, cut services because of the constraints of the stability pact. it follows that it would be more efficient and profitable if each member state spent this money on its own, without having it transit through brussels. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft budget. the union funds, although conceived as an instrument for compensating for imbalances between member states, are in practice a mechanism for amplifying these imbalances, which takes place through the use of the two principles of co-financing and conditionality; the commission's proposal is to set up a european monetary institute (emi) to monitor the budgetary policies of the member states. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the resolution calling on the commission to take all the necessary measures to accelerate the implementation of cohesion policy 2014-2020. due to the accumulated delays in the approval of regulations, regional operational programmes (rops) were not created before 2015 and this led to a shift and accumulation of funds to be spent. i share the request to the commission to assess the state of play of the implementation of the cohesion funds for the period 2014-2020 and to prepare a detailed analysis of the risks of decommitment and to indicate the measures envisaged in order to avoid decommitment as far as possible. it is also appropriate that the task force on programming 2007-2013 continue to support and accelerate the implementation of the 2014-2020 programmes in all member states to make up the backlog already accumulated, and that the european parliament be informed of the action plan on the activities of the task force. member states are also invited to play their part by fulfilling the ex-ante conditionalities by the end of 2016 in order to ensure a smooth implementation of the programmes and avoid any suspension of interim payments.
in writing. ‒ this report proposes some changes in the name of accelerating the eu's cohesion policy, which is currently the main form of investment and development the european union reserves for its regions. i decided to abstain because i believe that to really encourage the development of the union's territories, it is essential to proceed with the elaboration of more significant action plans. in fact, looking at the previous programming period, the results obtained were not the best: the commission has also been asked to provide information on the implementation of the new rules on the protection of the environment.
in writing. ‒ two years have passed since the start of the new programming period and the implementation of cohesion policy for the period 2014-2020, and delays are already being experienced, partly due to the late adoption of operational programmes. the economic crisis is causing a lot of liquidity problems for the member states and consequently for the regions which, associated with the constraints of the stability pact, are at serious risk of compromising the implementation of the esi funds and with them the benefits for businesses and for the territories. cohesion policy funds are often the only source of public funding. i therefore believe that the commission must be more open to considering the use of flexibility if we want to see development processes in our territories take off. with the resolution adopted today, which i voted for, we wanted to call on the commission to engage in a permanent dialogue with the member states with a view to maximising flexibility in relation to investment for growth and employment.
in writing. ‒ i believe that we must respond as quickly as possible to the lack of cohesion between the various member states that make up our european union. we are talking about a very large cultural, social and economic heritage and although we are really united in many things it is clear that there is still a lot of work to be done in this respect. the cohesion policies must therefore be accelerated to reduce as much as possible the territorial disparities, to enable all regions to become more competitive and to facilitate investment, including private investment. that is why i voted in favour of this report, which in my view expresses a clear political position, in that it seeks to direct part of the european structural and investment funds towards improving cohesion between the various member states.
in writing. ‒ progress in the implementation of cohesion policy in several member states and regions for the period 2007-2013 has been partly hampered by obstacles due to insufficient information available to potential beneficiaries, resulting in the submission of ineligible projects, slow project approval, long and complex award procedures, difficulties of member states and local authorities in complying with the requirements for internal and external implementation of the stability and growth pact. i therefore support, by voting in favour, the objective of this resolution to provide for the period 2014-2020 information on the obstacles already encountered and strategies to overcome them with a view to effective implementation of cohesion policy.
in writing. ‒ in the previous programming period, delays were caused by, among other things, insufficient information available to potential beneficiaries, slow approval of major projects, the absence of administrative structures responsible for managing investment in major projects, complex and unclear award procedures, and difficulties in accessing funding. we cannot, for the sake of the credibility of cohesion policy itself, allow ourselves to accumulate delays on delays, from the approval of the multiannual financial framework to the incredible case of some operational programmes approved only six months ago. we will also never agree on the link introduced in this programming between 'sound economic governance' and the structural funds (with possible suspension of the latter as provided for in the infamous article 23) or on the assumption of the need to promote the so-called 'structural reforms', which some even say are essential for a more effective cohesion policy. unfortunately, the structural reforms which the italian government is proposing to its citizens are anything but in favour of transparency, participation, development and the fight against unemployment. for these reasons, i shall abstain in voting on this resolution.
in writing. ‒ i am voting against the resolution which would only have the opposite effect, namely to widen the macroeconomic disparities between member states.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution as there has been significant delay in the implementation of the cohesion policy funds and efsi funds for the 2014-2020 periods. at a time when parts of europe are still experiencing significant economic problems and when there is urgent need for public investment in the economy, the funds available must be put to use as fast as possible. i hope the commission will push forward with these implementations and provide technical assistance where local or regional governance capacity does not fit the set out criteria for receiving funds.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the non-legislative resolution on the acceleration of the implementation of cohesion policy because i believe that cohesion policy is one of the eu's most important investment instruments, as it has enabled entire regions to converge economically, emerge from the crisis and boost growth in times of crisis. therefore, an assessment of it at this stage could provide the commission with useful information to feed into the debate on future cohesion policy post-2020. in the 2007-2013 programming period, major problems were identified in the implementation of cohesion policy in several member states; in many cases this was due to insufficient information available to potential beneficiaries, which resulted in lack of access to the relevant funds. i therefore believe that the increase in the use of funds by the regions will also depend on administrative capacity at national, regional and local level. finally, i agree with the ep's position that strengthening administrative capacity for the implementation and policy evaluation phases and good governance can help to improve absorption capacity, and i share the need to encourage relevant structural reforms in line with the objectives of territorial cohesion policy and sustainable growth and employment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on speeding up the implementation of cohesion policy. with a budget of over €350 billion until 2020, cohesion policy represents the union's main method of investment and development for all its regions. for some member states, the structural funds are the main source of public investment and the instrument by which the union is closest to its citizens. the objectives of strategy 2020 are achieved through a coherent interaction between growth and development policies. this policy plays a key role and should be harmonised with other eu policies such as the macro-regional strategy, the digital single market, the energy union, research and innovation in order to better contribute to the achievement of its objectives. the implementation of cohesion policy has been delayed by two years since the start of the new programming period. the commission will send the ep a summary report on the programmes of the funds each year, and a strategic report will be drawn up to monitor and summarise the progress report of the member states.
in writing. ‒ the proper link between growth and development policies and structural reforms is necessary to ensure the full implementation of the europe 2020 strategy. with a budget of over eur 350 billion, cohesion policy is the instrument through which the european union invests in its regions and gets closer to its citizens. i therefore believe that the call to the commission to provide detailed analyses and the call for greater coordination between the parties concerned can help to achieve the objectives set. i vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the union's cohesion policy, with a budget of over €350 billion until 2020, is the main source of public investment in some member states and thus plays a key role in the growth and development of europe's regions and cities. the 2014-2020 regulations introduced important reforms in cohesion policy, such as thematic concentration, a greater focus on results and better coordination with economic and social policy. however, two years after the start of the new programming period, the implementation of cohesion policy continues to suffer from significant delays. we therefore call on the commission and the member states to do more to fully exploit the potential of the european structural funds, in line with the europe 2020 strategy, to strengthen social and economic cohesion and to reduce territorial disparities. the analysis of the period 2007-2013 shows that the main problems were due to insufficient information available to potential beneficiaries and to long and complex award procedures. the commission's establishment of a high-level group to ensure greater transparency and simplify procedures is therefore very positive.
in writing. ‒ this motion for a resolution calls on the commission and the member states to take action to ensure that the union's cohesion policies are effectively implemented. the report calls in particular for a review and relaunch of these policies by exploiting the potential of the structural funds and the european investment fund. i voted in favour of this resolution, together with the ppe group.
in writing. the european union aims to achieve five concrete objectives by 2020 in the areas of employment, innovation, education, social inclusion and climate/energy. in order to achieve these and to address the different development needs of all european regions, eur 351,8 billion has been earmarked for cohesion policy for the period 2014-2020. in this resolution, parliament called on the commission to accelerate the work on the introduction of simplified procedures in order to strengthen social and economic cohesion and thus reduce territorial disparities in the european union. to this end, administrative competence at national, regional and local level becomes a key prerequisite for achieving timely and positive results in cohesion policy. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution.
