in writing. ‒ a policy coherence report on development is produced every two years to assess progress, improve strategies and give further impetus to sustainable development. the report covers a number of themes, such as security, trade, finance, migration and food security. following extensive consultation with ngos, calls were made for improved cooperation, particularly in the form of bilateral agreements between the eu and third countries, with a focus on the need to ensure greater transparency and control, particularly with regard to european investment in developing countries. for these reasons i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ in 2016, more than 1.5 billion people were living in poverty, suffering from deprivation in health, education and living standards. a large proportion of them are women. the adoption by the united nations of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development was a milestone in the definition of strategic objectives to combat this and other serious problems that threaten our planet. the dan preda report, which i supported with my vote today, not only evaluates the progress made on policy coherence for development, but also makes concrete proposals for the eu to take a leading role in promoting a universal agenda for sps. the text focuses on a number of priority areas of intervention: the commission has also been active in the field of migration, trade and finance, food security, health, climate change and gender, but the most important aspect is the definition of the link between security and development. the eu should implement the sps as part of the union's foreign policy. only by creating an effective link between humanitarian aid, development cooperation and disaster resilience will a more flexible and effective response to growing global needs be achieved.
in writing. ‒ the european union's development policies lack effectiveness and coherence, and this report does not present any acceptable proposal to break the deadlock of these failed policies. for these reasons i voted against.
in writing. ‒ the european union must act in a coordinated and coherent way in its development policies, whether they are directed at territories within the union or to territories outside it. policy coherence presupposes an agreement on values and principles to which to conform and converge. governance and coordination at different levels and scales are therefore essential to promote dialogue and foster agreement and political commitment by each institution in transforming its policies, integrating, implementing and monitoring them as intended, in a constant process of review and renewal. we cannot risk promoting the values of democracy, respect for human rights and the fight against poverty and then implementing policies or trade agreements with third countries in certain areas which indirectly create the conditions for the breach or non-fulfilment of commitments. in particular, attention must be paid in the coming years to partnership and cooperation agreements with non-democratic developing countries where, without a proper procedure for reporting on aid provided, there is a risk of unintentionally strengthening the darkest parts of the same countries we would like to help.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report in question, which calls on the commission to give coherence to development policies (cps). although the lisbon treaty provides for this strategy, there is still no common interpretation. i share the view of the report that it advocates a human rights approach, because it would give a better understanding of policy coherence for development. in fact, without addressing the obstacles to the realization of rights, there can be no progress towards sustainable development and poverty eradication. the main tool for the implementation of the sgp is impact assessments, but more investment is needed from the european union, as studies are currently scarce and do not adequately address the potential impact on developing countries. the report calls for future impact assessments to focus on identifying inconsistencies and developing appropriate mechanisms to monitor and control progress on cps, including proposals on how to avoid and address inconsistencies between policies.
in writing. ‒ the biannual report on policy coherence for development, drawn up by the deve committee, takes stock of the progress reported by the european commission in this area. the report also seeks to identify ways of improving the existing european coherence mechanisms and to stimulate debate on this concept at union level. the amendments tabled by the five star movement, calling for greater coordination in bilateral agreements between member states and third countries and for greater transparency and control over european companies' investments in the various developing countries, were largely incorporated in the compromises. the report is therefore highly acceptable and i voted in favour of it in the plenary.
in writing. ‒ policies for the development of third countries play a key role in the work of the european union, which is the leading donor on the international scene. however, in order to make action in these countries more effective, there needs to be a better understanding of policy coherence for development (cps). the european union and the oecd were among the first to bring the issue to the attention of major international actors such as the united states, japan and the brics countries in order to share the concept of cps needed to define policies and intervention actions. the migration crisis can be an important moment in the implementation of european development policy and in addressing more fully the root causes of the phenomenon: the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. i voted in favour of the report because i believe that policy coherence must be the basis for action by the eu and other international actors towards third countries.
in writing. ‒ i thought i would vote in favour of the measure as the council conclusions on the ec's fifth biennial report, adopted in october 2015, underline that the cps will be an important part of the eu's contribution to achieving the broader objective of policy coherence for sustainable development (pcsd). in addition to taking stock of the progress reported by the european commission and identifying areas for improving existing european cps mechanisms, the report aims to give impetus to the debate on the future of this concept at eu level. the 2030 agenda for sustainable development represents a unique opportunity to address the interrelated challenges of poverty eradication and sustainable development. the sps remains a political and economic imperative for the european union.
in writing. ‒ the current european development framework does not have the necessary mechanisms to prevent and remedy inconsistencies arising from the policies pursued by the european union. i agree with calling for a european-level debate on the coherence of development policies (cps) so that they are fully integrated into the decision-making process of the european union. i also believe that institutional coordination must be improved so that the member states can incorporate the spc into a legally binding act and draw up an action plan to this end.
in writing. ‒ policy coherence for development is an important contribution of the european union to the implementation of sustainable development policies. however, consideration should be given to how this european commitment can be realised through the adoption of far-reaching measures and synergies between union development and non-development policies. the use of existing instruments needs to be optimised in order to ensure the efficient and systematic implementation of policy coherence for development. i voted in favour of the report because it is a useful tool for raising awareness of the subject of the cfsp, and i hope that the debate on the cfsp will be brought to fruition in the future.
in writing. ‒ the european union must ensure the consistency of its development policies (cps), working to ensure that there are strong synergies between development objectives and other european policies. the report we are debating today is aimed at improving the coherence of european development policies, a subject which has been the subject of frequent debate. the union's commitment to policy coherence for development is mainly articulated around issues such as trade, environment, climate change, security, agriculture, social dimension, employment, decent work, migration and energy. europe must improve coherence at regional, national and european levels and increase its potential in the production and use of knowledge to provide concrete solutions to the challenges it faces today. we have tabled several amendments to this report and have had discussions with a number of ngos. we are looking forward to greater consistency in bilateral agreements with third countries. i am voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ the lisbon treaty included for the first time a legal obligation to pursue policy coherence for development, further strengthening it between the eu's internal and external policies. the adoption of the 2030 agenda introduces a single set of development goals, going beyond the donor-recipient model. the eu should therefore take a leading role in promoting a universal agenda that shifts the concept towards sustainable development. the report introduces important innovations which should be supported, including a closer link between development policies and the sustainable development goals and greater involvement of local and regional governments and civil society organisations. in particular, i am very much in favour of ex ante impact assessments, which can become an important tool in defining strategies and approaches for the future of migrants and refugees and in trying to build mechanisms that can limit or stem the recurrence of humanitarian crises at source.
in writing. ‒ i am voting against the report, which does not bring about any substantial changes to the deadlock in the union's development policies.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the non-legislative resolution on the eu's 2015 report on policy coherence for development, as i believe it is essential to open a debate on this issue within the european council in order to foster an interinstitutional debate both at european and member state level. as will be recalled, the lisbon treaty requires that any legal obligation assumed at international level in the context of the union's objectives is consistent with development policies (cps). however, today more than ever it is necessary to move beyond this paradigm, as the adoption of the 2030 agenda envisages establishing a single and universal set of objectives and thus moving beyond the donor-recipient paradigm on which the union's development policy has been based, to promote a development policy coherence agenda based on sustainable development. i strongly supported the s&d group's view that there is a strong link between the coherence of eu development policies and the sustainable development goals (sdgs), and that local and regional authorities and organised civil society should be involved in a substantial way. only greater coherence between eu policies will allow the sdgs of the 2030 agenda to be achieved and thus poverty eradication in the developing countries to be achieved once and for all.
in writing. ‒ i fully support this report on policy coherence for development, which has become essential to create synergies between development cooperation and other policies to enhance the action that the union and the commission are already taking, mainly through the funds and cohesion policy. on this front, a more pragmatic and timely approach is needed to address not only the objectives already outlined in the 2030 agenda for sustainable development, but above all the challenges that everyday life poses to us today. i am referring first of all to the question of migration, the exodus of thousands of people from the south to the north in search of peace and rights. the refugee crisis and the destabilisation of the eu's neighbourhood are challenging the very foundations of the eu itself, and i, as an italian and a sicilian, live with this phenomenon on a daily basis. i believe that there is an urgent need to find a system to harmonize and strengthen community efforts in the areas of reception and migration policies, in addition to the five priority areas already identified (trade and finance, food security, climate change, migration and security).
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the eu's 2015 report on policy coherence for development (pdc). the cfsp is a key element of the eu's contribution to achieving the goal of policy coherence for sustainable development, as well as contributing to the consolidation of the rule of law and impartial institutions. policy coherence for development is one of the european union's primary objectives in order to increase the effectiveness of its development aid and has become a necessary tool for seeking synergies between development cooperation and other policies and for correcting existing inconsistencies. for cps to become international and not just a european concept, more efforts are needed from the eu, taking the lead in promoting a universal agenda for cps and working towards a common approach to make the concept universal.
in writing. ‒ we welcome the 2015 report on policy coherence for development. in line with the commitments made when the lisbon treaty was adopted, the european union is moving towards the convergence of community rules through a set of policies which are consistent with each other. the report presented today sets out the progress of the work done so far to bring about the convergence of european policies, of the organisational mechanisms in the union and of europe's development objectives. in this context, the progress made by the european union in policy coherence in 12 areas is highlighted: trade, environment, climate change, security, agriculture, fisheries, the social dimension of globalisation and employment, migration, research, the information society, transport and energy. in particular, in the area of trade, the union aims to promote more effectively the conclusion of economic and trade partnership agreements, as well as the system of generalised preferences (so-called gsp+) and trade-related measures, with a view to initiating a process of economic integration with developing countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of mr preda's proposal, as i share the need for greater synergy between the objectives of sustainable development and the union's policies. in my view, policy coherence for development is essential to pursue the objectives of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development and therefore i believe that greater harmonisation between the sps and the sdgs is appropriate. similarly, bringing sps into the global debate and promoting the involvement of other key actors can effectively contribute to the achievement of development goals. i am convinced that a greater awareness of coherence for development policies both at european and national level is of priority importance, and i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the european union should do much more to ensure greater coherence and synergy in its development policies, both horizontally across sectors such as trade, agriculture and immigration, and vertically across global, regional and national levels. it should also work to ensure that other major players on the international scene (the usa, japan and the brics countries) adopt a similar strategy, to make the implementation of the sustainable development goals truly possible. the lisbon treaty provides for the obligation to pursue policy coherence for development (pcd) and to strengthen the objective of coherence between the union's internal and external policies. today there is a growing consensus that we need to go even further than this paradigm. the adoption of the 2030 agenda sets out a single, universal set of development goals, applicable to all, which goes beyond the donor-recipient scheme. the eu should therefore take the lead in promoting a universal pcd agenda, aimed at achieving sustainable development. a specific european council meeting on the cfp, before the publication of the next commission report in 2017, would make a significant contribution to raising awareness of the importance of the cfp and to better defining the responsibilities of the different actors involved.
in writing. ‒ with the adoption of the sustainable development goals, 2015 was a milestone in the evolution of csp (policy coherence for development). the sustainable development goals have called for a more integrated approach to policy-making, with a greater focus on coherence. the achievement of the cps will thus have a very decisive impact on the implementation of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development. cps, however, is not yet widely used internationally, but remains a purely european concept. the eu and the oecd (organization for economic cooperation and development) are the forerunners of the sps debate. in an increasingly interconnected world, a common approach is needed to make this concept more universal. therefore, i believe that parliament should call for an eu-level debate on cps in the framework of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development, to understand how cps can fit into the more universal concept of cpss (policy coherence for sustainable development). that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's role is increasingly important in advancing the concept of policy coherence for development (pcd), a primary objective of the european union and a key element of the united nations' 2030 agenda. the report presented in this house on this subject aims to take stock of the progress made by the european commission in the field of development policies. it also identifies areas where existing cps mechanisms can be improved and strengthened. i have decided to vote in favour of the text as i agree with the call for a union active in the field of the cfsp. europe has always been a key player in development and aid to developing third countries. i also agree with the rapporteur's call for the commission to draw attention to inconsistencies and costs in the area of cps and to develop appropriate tools to monitor progress in this area in order to better assess the impact of european policies on development.

in writing. ‒ the g8 in may 2012 launched the new alliance for food security and nutrition, a public-private partnership, with the aim of stimulating private investment in sub-saharan agriculture. the eu has so far invested eur 1.2 billion in particular in cooperation with the territories of malawi and côte d'ivoire. the report presented, however, highlights a number of criticisms of the new alliance, which it considers will not bring about a real improvement in the living conditions of millions of farming and small-scale farming families. in view of these considerations, the eu is urged to review its participation in the alliance. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ one in four people in sub-saharan africa suffers from malnutrition, a condition that causes the death of about half of children under five. this is a very serious situation, and the eu has decided to respond by launching the new alliance for food security and nutrition with the g8 in 2012. this project aims to strengthen food security and nutrition, helping 50 million people in sub-saharan africa to escape poverty by 2020, by making changes to the legislation of the countries involved in the field of seeds, land and foreign investment. i have supported the heubuch report because i believe it highlights the risks associated with the application of nafsn, particularly for small producers and women. the text expresses the need to make the cooperation frameworks for the different countries monitorable and accessible, including performance indicators and requiring private companies to publish annual reports. the union's priority must be to protect family farms and smallholders, who are largely excluded from the negotiations, and to avoid the adoption of models based on large-scale industrial production, which have negative consequences for health and the environment.
in writing. ‒ the report on the new alliance for food security and nutrition is well-articulated and contains no problematic passages. that is why i wanted to support it with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the new alliance for food security and nutrition in africa (nafsn), established in 2012, aims to innovate, develop and modernise african agriculture by unlocking major investment through a broad public-private partnership. the agreed policies are aimed at overcoming the limitations and risks of the african agricultural system, creating a more business-friendly environment, easier and controlled access to land and a more sustainable use of resources, with the aim of combating food and nutritional poverty. the strategy has, however, revealed some gaps which need to be filled, and in particular calls for a closer involvement of the local economy and small farmers in investment choices. greater transparency on public-private partnerships is equally essential, as is a commitment to empowering businesses to respect human rights, land rights, environmental sustainability and gender equality. i therefore agree with mrs heubuch's report.
in writing. ‒ with a growing and continuously growing population, africa needs adequate investment in agriculture to meet the growing demand for food. in this context, the new alliance for food security and nutrition in africa, drawn up within the g8, could be an interesting opportunity to mobilise private investment in african agriculture, thus contributing to the improvement of living conditions and nutrition of the population. this particular device, however, was developed on an ecologically and socially unsustainable model, that of the asian "green revolution" of the 1960s and 1970s, based on dependence on fertilisers, intensive crops for export, biotechnology and long distribution channels. a production model, the product of outdated developmental logics, which are ill-suited to the culture, needs and reality of the territory in question. a model whose implementation is expressed in paternalistic logics, the subject of widespread criticism even by important figures, such as the united nations special rapporteur on the right to food, which leave little room for comparison with small owners and civil society and which, for these reasons, needs to be deeply reconsidered and updated.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it raises constructive criticisms of the way in which the objectives of the public-private partnership, known as the 'new alliance for food security and nutrition in africa', are being achieved. it is right to invest in agriculture in sub-saharan africa to improve the food security of the african population, but we must avoid reproducing a model based on monocultures, biotechnology, dependence on fertilisers and long distribution channels. it is necessary to review the country cooperation frameworks with a view to improving contractual arrangements between local buyers and suppliers and to provide a favourable legal framework in terms of price agreements, respect for women's rights, the establishment of appropriate dispute resolution mechanisms and the strengthening of farmers' organisations to improve their negotiating position in agricultural contracts. it is the responsibility of the union and the member states to ensure that the public-private partnership in question becomes a genuine instrument of support for family farming and local economies in sub-saharan africa, with the aim of combating poverty and food and nutrition insecurity.
in writing. ‒ the new alliance for food security and nutrition is a partnership launched in 2012 by the g8 with the aim of stimulating private investment in agriculture in sub-saharan africa. the eu is participating in the new alliance for eur 1.2 billion, leading the cooperation frameworks with malawi and côte d'ivoire. the report on this initiative, drawn up by the deve committee, has rightly highlighted the critical and controversial aspects of this initiative and i have therefore voted in favour of adopting this text. indeed, the new alliance is highly criticized by ngos and civil society as it seems to only promote the entry of corporate agribusiness led by multinationals such as monsanto, cargill and unilever.

in writing. ‒ the new alliance for food security and nutrition in africa (nafsn) is a broad public-private partnership that aims to mobilise private investment in agriculture to improve food security and nutrition in sub-saharan africa. while the overall objective of nafsn is more than valid, there are several shortcomings, which are highlighted in this report. the most obvious problems are: the need to move towards sustainable forms of agricultural production and support farmers' seed systems; the risks associated with the emergence of a market in securities; the commission has also been active in the fight against malnutrition and in the recognition of women's rights. agricultural investment policies should therefore be conditional on the development of the local economy and small producers. cooperation projects should be fully transparent and subject to strict control mechanisms, which also provide for remedies for the local populations concerned. the fao guidelines on responsible land, fisheries and forest management must be applied to each project. other basic principles must be the fight against land grabbing and, finally, the responsibility of contractors with regard to human rights and social, environmental and labour standards.
in writing. ‒ launched in 2012, the nafsn (new alliance for food security and nutrition in africa) aims to leverage financial support from donor countries to help large companies invest in african agriculture. in return, the ten participating sub-saharan african states are required to amend their legislation on land, seeds and foreign investment. however, when the country cooperation frameworks were being drawn up, consultation of smallholders was minimal, despite the fact that they should be the final beneficiaries of the nafsn. for this, nafsn has been the subject of severe criticism. it is believed that nafsn risks facilitating land grabbing and further marginalizing smallholder farmers and women, while supporting unsustainable agriculture. agricultural investment policies aim to support local economic development, enabling african governments to invest in local food systems to boost rural economies, ensure decent jobs and the right to work. to identify the best development goals, the eu should address some shortcomings, including transparency and governance. i therefore voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal as it underlines the role of international accounting standards in european financial services legislation. in the present economic and financial context, however, a revision of these principles, in the sense of their modernisation and adaptation, is necessary. the european union therefore has an important role to play in this process. the european parliament is also called upon to play a more active role in the process of adopting international financial reporting standards. i am convinced that these amendments are useful and i voted in favour of them.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report entitled 'evaluation of international accounting standards'. these principles, known as isas and ifrss, are an essential component of the proper functioning of the internal market and capital markets. they constitute an important legal and regulatory framework for the european union in the field of financial services. these principles can be understood as a public good, serving the common interest and not only the interests of investors, financiers and creditors. once again we see the eu's efforts to create a financial environment that is as stable and as risk-free as possible. european policies aim to create a climate of confidence and stability that can stimulate investment. the european commission has given a major boost to this by drawing up the juncker plan, whose outcome, one year after its entry into force, can be described as entirely positive.
in writing. ‒ we live in a globalised world today, where companies are free to move to every continent to look for new business. this economic scenario, however, requires that there be internationally recognised accounting principles in order to prevent fraud or wrongdoing. the own-initiative report adopted today recognises that the balance between the mandatory scope of the international accounting standards (ias) regulation and the possibility for member states to benefit from the use of ifrs (international financial reporting standards foundation) at national level must ensure appropriate subsidiarity and proportionality. this report also assesses the activities of the ifrs foundation, the european financial reporting advisory group (efrag) and the public interest oversight board (piob) and addresses general issues about the process of adopting ifrs accounting principles in european law. international accounting standards are an important part of the eu regulatory and supervisory framework for financial services and i have therefore decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the report addresses the issue of international accounting standards (ifrss) which form an important part of the regulatory and supervisory framework for financial services. these principles are developed by the international accounting standards board (iasb), a private, independent self-regulatory body that is creating a common language for financial reporting on a global scale. ifrs have been in place for 10 years, but the financial crisis has shown their total inefficiency. this is because these standards are too complex and their management too unclear. other critical points: the principle of compulsory reporting between states is lacking. although they were conceived as global standards, there are some counterparts, such as the usa, which do not use them at all and others, such as the eu, which are not involved in the development process. we do not share the urgency of adopting harmonised accounting principles at eu level because this is aimed at a greater and better development of the single capital market, a project which we strongly oppose as it would increase the financialization of the economy at the expense of the real economy. the report stresses the major shortcomings of this system, but calls for further development of the overall framework. that is why we have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ peace support operations are generally responses to crisis situations, with the particular aim of restoring, maintaining or creating peace. the commission has also proposed that the european union should be given the task of ensuring that the community's financial resources are used to finance the development of the african continent. in this context, member states and the eu were invited to strengthen cooperation in terms of financial assistance, logistical support and political dialogue. i voted against, however, because, apart from certain provisions which are certainly acceptable, the strong militaristic footprint cannot be supported, particularly with regard to the renewal of european armed forces on the ground.
in writing. ‒ the question of stability in the african and european neighbourhood is increasingly a topical issue. peace support operations, conducted under a united nations mandate, are used precisely in those situations where external support is required to restore, build or maintain peace in contexts where states are dissolving or showing marked fragility. the van orden report, which i supported today with my vote in favour, recognises the need to evaluate and rationalise existing structures, avoiding too many overlapping operations which persist in the same areas. the lack of coordination is also a factor often linked to difficulties in using funds and in the correct use of resources. while the eu's contributions are important, particularly through the african peace facility and african union funding, more ambitious measures are needed. strengthening european military cooperation could increase the efficiency and effectiveness of european contribution to un and african union peacekeeping missions by providing better assistance in training, equipping, logistical support and the definition of rules of engagement of troops.
in writing. ‒ the van orden report, while being sustainable as a whole, contains some criticisms which have led me to express my abstention.
in writing. ‒ the european union is the world's most important area of freedom, democracy and peace. most developing countries look to europe as a model and a guide. for this reason, as well as for the commercial and diplomatic relations we have with them, we have a moral duty to help them. today, unfortunately, ungoverned spaces are spreading, both in so-called "failed states" and in vast areas of africa and west asia that are beyond the control of state authorities. these spaces allow crime, religious fundamentalism, land and sea banditry to flourish. it is in these spaces that the most vulnerable people are exploited, sold and killed. reducing these gaps means improving people's lives, protecting the most vulnerable and working towards a better society. it is not a waste of resources to help the african union. it's not just fair. making african states more just and secure is a way of making the european union more just and secure. let us remember, as zygmunt bauman says, that "locks and chains cannot tame or weaken the forces that cause emigration; "they may help to conceal problems from the eyesight and mind, but they do not make them go away".
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on peace support operations european union engagement with the united nations and the african union. africa is the most important point of engagement in the difficult peace-building effort. the present action of the united nations must be strengthened and made more effective by the contribution of all the countries with the technical and economic means. the african union must also be progressively strengthened not only to build peace but also to promote economic cooperation and the policies needed for the future of the continent. europe and the international community must be able to meet this challenge not only through peacekeeping missions but also through the necessary conflict prevention action.
in writing. ‒ the report covers multilateral cooperation between the european union, the united nations and the african union to prepare operations to ensure the maintenance of peace in african regions. i have followed the report in the security and defence subcommittee, of which i am a member, and i have identified from the first draft some fundamental problems which have not been overcome even after my amendments to the report were tabled. i am referring in particular to the excessive use of military means in the context of the operations and the use of the concept of 'imposing peace' rather than maintaining it. these are aspects which are highly contrary to my view of the support that the european union should provide for the stability of the african regions and i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ the european union makes support for the activities of the un and the african union a key element of its foreign policy. in the light of a phenomenon as vast and complex as the current migration crisis, it is clear that the european union is called upon once again to play an important role in supporting various african states to create stable, secure and prosperous environments in the long term. the european union is also calling for the immediate release of all political prisoners and for the immediate release of all political prisoners. a strong partnership between the eu, the african union and the un is therefore needed, a genuine policy of support for peace to respond in a comprehensive and coherent way to the needs of the region. security and development are the two things to which we should refer. there can be no stabilisation of the area without cohesion and development policies. we must therefore find alternative sources of funding for the african peace fund if we are to really help the country in the peace process. the security of the union and of the african continent itself will only be achieved if we make africa a political and action priority. i voted in favour of the resolution because it calls for a greater effort by all the international actors in the peace process.
in writing. ‒ in recent years, the agreements concluded between the european union, the united nations and the african union have brought many benefits to the african country. a number of activities have been carried out to manage the crisis in africa, to maintain peace and to strengthen international security. however, there is still a lot of work to be done and i am convinced that the eu cannot and should not back down now. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the objective of un peace support operations in africa is to help create stable and secure environments in the long term, where fundamental and civil rights are respected and where economies can be more prosperous. in order to develop effective reconciliation, reconstruction and development programmes, the european union should cooperate more with the un and partner organisations, sharing information, establishing synergies and providing training, equipment and resources to help local actors manage crises on their own. i voted in favour of the report because it aims to strengthen cooperation between the european union and the un, with a view to mutual information sharing, in the planning of activities and in the conduct of missions.
in writing. ‒ the report stresses the need for coordinated external action using diplomacy, security and development tools to restore confidence and to address the challenges posed by wars, internal conflicts, insecurity and the fragility of the african situation. peace operations are increasingly characterized by military missions authorized by the united nations and the report too is too "militaristic". the european union should focus on more appropriate conflict resolution. we recall that the importance of the eu-africa partnership lies primarily in political dialogue to ensure peace and security and not in new military actions. we therefore recommend that there be agreements which can encompass shared objectives for the security of africa and to ensure the protection of civilians and the end of any armed conflict. member states are already engaged in operations in africa. it is time for the european union to bring real added value by supporting dialogue more. for the reasons i have just given, i shall vote against the report.
in writing. ‒ peace support operations are essential to create stable, secure and human rights-respecting environments in the long term, as a prerequisite for economic development and for society as a whole. in this respect, the united nations remains an important reference point as a guarantor of international peace and security, while the eu cooperates with the african union mainly through the african peace fund. the crisis in africa requires a coordinated approach between the various actors involved and across the sectors involved, and my vote in favour is to support the european union's action alongside the un, nato and the african union to increase the sharing of information for crisis management and the organisation of missions. i believe that this resolution takes account of one essential aspect, namely that in an increasingly complex global context a global approach to security and peace is needed, one which makes use not only of military instruments but also of humanitarian, diplomatic, economic and technological ones. all these elements together contribute to the knowledge of the territories and to the fight against common critical factors, primarily terrorism and crime.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the european union's engagement in peacekeeping missions with the united nations and the african union, arguing for a review of the way in which the funds used for these missions are used. the eu must focus on humanitarian interventions that can bring real added value, for example through training and logistical support.

in writing. ‒ i voted to adopt this report on the basis that the eu’s relationship with the african union needs to evolve to counter security and stability threats facing africa and indirectly europe; and to get the best effective results with the resources provided to supporting peace operations on that continent. it is in the interest of the eu that the african continent is as stable as possible and in order for the eu to cooperate with the african union in the most effective manner there are several issues that this report addresses. we need better cooperation and a clearer division of labour with our african partners and to increase our military commitments to un peacekeeping operations and for the eu to facilitate these.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on peace support operations european union engagement with the united nations and the african union, because i believe that strong and shared commitment to providing an effective response to international crisis situations is of paramount importance. the success of these operations, which must necessarily be conducted under the auspices of international organizations, in the first place the united nations, and regional organizations such as the african union, cannot be achieved without the serious involvement and constant commitment of the european union. in the last decade, political instability and insecurity in many parts of the world, especially in africa, have led to the emergence and strengthening of a number of terrorist groups, some of which are already active in somalia, nigeria and the sahel-saharan region. the fragile governments of these countries have been unable to contain the advance of these groups, who are well armed and trained in all kinds of brutality, and have made civilians pay the highest price. i therefore share the need for external peace-keeping and peace-building measures aimed at restoring stability and security in the countries concerned, as well as protecting the civilian population from violence and guaranteeing access to health care and food supplies.
in writing. ‒ as a member of parliament, i support this report not only because peace is one of the founding objectives of the union, but because it is a cornerstone of my country's constitutional charter and a personal value. the african continent has been ravaged by war for decades and the instruments developed by europe to support the work of the united nations and the african union are able to achieve a useful coordination of human, economic and diplomatic forces. there is no doubt that the stability of the african and european neighbourhood would be of great benefit to all our countries. the crises in africa require a coherent global response, which goes beyond simple security aspects, because peace and security are necessary prerequisites for development in a long-term perspective. the african peace fund is an effective instrument whose full use is essential to maintain the close involvement of the institutions and member states of the european union. equally essential is that the african union demonstrate higher levels of efficiency and transparency in the use of funds, focusing on more structural support.
in writing. the eu is conducting peace support operations (psos) that support the un and the african union in ensuring international peace and security. these are operations with a high humanitarian impact, but with complex levels of management, also due to the large number of actors involved in these operations. the need therefore arises to improve communication, planning, mission analysis and coordination between regional and international institutions so that they can act effectively. the ultimate aim is to ensure that the african union is able to maintain a security situation in africa, independent of external aid. in this respect, the eu needs to focus its aid on developing africa's skills and responsibility. given the essential contribution of our union, and with the hope that this will lead to the development of a more equitable and secure society, i vote in favour of the peace support operations report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on peace support operations european union engagement with the united nations and the african union. the aim of this report is to strengthen the european union's contribution to peace support operations and cooperation with the united nations and the african union. the primary purpose of these operations is to create stable and secure environments, to ensure justice, good governance and to strengthen the rule of law and respect for human rights where, as in africa, operations to restore peace and combat terrorism are now ongoing. it is essential that the union, together with its member states, commits itself to increasing support for these states through a comprehensive approach, including not only the use of military or diplomatic instruments but also other factors such as the exchange of information, modern technology, the provision of humanitarian aid and the resumption of political dialogue.

in writing. ‒ the report harmonises national rules on unfair trading practices in the food sector. the legislation does not standardise practices and is based on the countermeasures put in place by the national states. the provisions contained therein do not therefore harmonise downwards but look at best regulatory practice. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ unfair trading practices develop when, within the framework of trade relations, one party finds itself in a position of strength vis-à-vis the other, creating bargaining imbalances. these are behaviours that are extremely damaging to the union economy as they primarily affect small and medium-sized enterprises, thereby losing their capacity to invest and innovate and not expanding their activities in the single market. the czesak report, which i supported today, considers it essential to define the concept of unfair trading practices as a matter of priority, while at the same time laying down appropriate sanctions for anyone who engages in them. the food chain, according to a survey launched in 2011, appears to be among the most affected by these behaviours and therefore one of the first to be addressed. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. only by adopting eu rules that ensure the proper functioning of markets and fair and transparent relationships between all parties involved in the food chain will the european economy and smes be truly protected.
in writing. ‒ the report on unfair trading practices in the food chain highlights some of the most important issues hampering the business of our agri-businesses, such as late payments and the strong downward pressure on the cost of goods. i agree with the text on the concerns of the agri-food sector today, for which i have been fighting constantly, and i therefore wanted to support it with my vote.
in writing. ‒ small producers and retailers of food products are very often victims of unfair trading practices, due in particular to the asymmetry of financial resources between the parties to the contract, a phenomenon which constitutes a major constraint on the ability of smes to invest, expand and innovate. while many member states have developed measures to address this problem, their interventions have developed in a disorderly and uneven way, resulting in an intricate and partly ineffective regulatory framework. to combat this, the eu should take on the task of developing common rules for all member states, in particular by defining more precisely what behaviour constitutes unfair trading practices and by identifying clear and strict sanctions for those who engage in them.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report in question because it allows the italian and european agri-food industry to keep the issue of unfair trading practices on the political agenda of the european union. the dossier takes a strong and unequivocal stance against the abuses of large organized distribution (ldo). some competition authorities have identified specific practices that transfer excessive risk to suppliers and that could undermine their competitiveness. the report also highlights that the dispute settlement mechanism proposed under a self-regulatory initiative (the so-called 'supply chain initiative') cannot go beyond certain limits as trade imbalances are unlikely to be adequately resolved through free trade between the parties. i therefore agree with the european commission's adoption of a proposal for a framework regulation, which would allow member states to adopt, maintain or amend national legislation based on common principles, including a proper combination of voluntary and regulatory frameworks through the control of an independent public authority with investigative powers and the power to impose dissuasive penalties.
in writing. ‒ the report calls for a clear framework in relation to the fight against unfair trading practices. it should be borne in mind that there is still no european list of recognised unfair trading practices, which can only be deduced from the countermeasures taken by the individual member states. the report is certainly to be welcomed, as it proposes upward harmonisation, thus referring to those member states which have achieved higher standards of protection. i fully share the approach just outlined and therefore voted in favour.
in writing. in the world i have in mind, farmers pull healthy, good products out of the ground and traders place them on the market. this division of labour includes fair remuneration for all and an equitable sharing of risks. when, for external reasons, one of the two sides of the value chain acquires disproportionate contractual power, the imbalances affect all the other upstream and downstream actors. we are not talking about illegal behaviour, but it is appropriate to draw a line between what is right and what is wrong even in apparently free contractual relations which are in fact marred by particular dynamics. this report is a first step in that direction and i voted in favour of it, firmly convinced that it is in the interests of producers, consumers and, through them, also of traders themselves.
in writing. ‒ delayed payments, difficulty in accessing the market, unilateral changes in contractual conditions, selling below production cost. these are some of the unfair practices that often characterize the commercial sector of the food chain, with increasing difficulties for farmers and lower quality and information for consumers. this is why the european parliament has asked the commission to define as soon as possible measures to ensure greater transparency in a sector so strategic for the european economy and society, especially in relation to the so-called large retail sector, which often, because of its size and its presence in the territory, ends up penalizing small and medium-sized production and sales activities, also limiting the possibilities and purchasing power of citizens. we therefore expect the commission to come forward with an operational proposal to extend and strengthen existing legislation in order to put quality, equal rights and support for work at the heart of european policy, also in this area.
in writing. ‒ delays in payments and reimbursements, unilateral changes to contractual terms, and cost-shifting to trading partners are practices that are creating many difficulties for operators in the food supply chain. nor are voluntary initiatives taken at national and european level sufficient to encourage market operators to respect the principle of fair trading. the increasing fragmentation of rules in the internal market makes it urgent to have a coherent european framework that clearly defines common principles in the fight against unfair trading practices. i am in favour of this report, which is a first step in building a fair competitive environment between member states, which can allow fair and transparent relations between producers, suppliers and distributors. rebalancing the bargaining power throughout the chain will strengthen competitiveness, contributing to sustainable development and a diversified choice of quality food at affordable prices for all consumers.
in writing. ‒ the czesak report sets out the european parliament's overall position on the growing phenomenon of unfair trading practices in the food chain. it calls on the european commission to come forward with a legislative proposal to stem the many forms of misconduct that are increasingly harming consumers and businesses. i have assured my support for this report precisely because its main objective is to safeguard farms and small and mediumsized enterprises in the agri-food sector, which are often forced to suffer unfair practices such as selling at a loss, delays in payments or sudden changes in contractual conditions, to the sole advantage of the large retailers. this is why it is necessary to establish as soon as possible a regulatory framework at european level, defining common rules and effective control mechanisms and ensuring transparent relations and fair contract conditions between all actors in the agri-food chain, in particular the weakest ones. only in this way will our european consumers also benefit from a wider choice of innovative and quality products at fair and competitive prices.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because delays in payments, limited market access and pressure to reduce prices are just some of the unfair practices, often undertaken 'business to business', which must be brought to an end. the weakest link in the chain is left behind, namely small farmers and retailers in the food chain, a sector which is the beating heart of the italian economic fabric and which employs 47 million people in europe. the eu must define unfair practices clearly and provide for clear sanctions. it is also essential to combat the 'fear effect', which causes companies to accept malicious misconduct by the stronger party, for fear that this will end the business relationship. since 2009, the european parliament has adopted five resolutions and the commission three reports on this issue. we have had enough of analysis, now we must act concretely once and for all.

in writing. ‒ unfair practices in the food supply chain are a growing problem, affecting smes in particular and having a detrimental effect on the european internal market. a march 2011 interview by the european federation of food industries revealed that as many as 96% of respondents said they had been exposed to at least one form of unfair trading practice. increasingly, there are cases of late payments, restrictions on access to the capital market, abusive changes to contractual clauses and pressure to cut prices. as rapporteur for the opinion on the report on access to credit for smes, i am well aware of these problems and have therefore decided to vote in favour of european action to identify measures which go beyond the existing voluntary mechanisms. we must not forget that unfair practices occur where there are imbalances in financial resources and in the power of contract between the parties. the so-called 'fear factor' is increasingly driving weaker trading partners to avoid legal action to avoid retaliation. that is why our coordinated efforts at european level to combat these phenomena must not fail.
in writing. ‒ given the importance of small and medium-sized enterprises, the backbone of europe's economic and social fabric, and their particular vulnerability to unfair trading practices, we vote in favour of the czesak report. the imbalances and distortions resulting from the abuse of a dominant position are a serious threat to smes and the functioning of the single market itself. this phenomenon, helped by globalisation and the integration of production chains, particularly affects operators in the agri-food sector. in fact, according to a 2011 study, about 96 percent of respondents said they had been the victim of dishonest practices. some member states, recognising the size and scope of the damage, have developed national rules and policies. it is clear, however, that for the single market to function properly, a community and holistic response from the european union is needed, a concrete solution which guarantees fair and transparent trade relations without sanctions. to this end, and given the threat of repercussions, i share the wish for investigations to ensure the anonymity of the companies making complaints.

in writing. ‒ unfair commercial practices consist of late payment, restricted market access, unilateral changes to contractual terms (including with retroactive effect), sudden and unjustified termination of the contract, unfair transfer of commercial risk and transfer of transport and storage costs to suppliers. the eu already has legislation to combat unfair trading practices between businesses and consumers (directive 2005/29/ec), but there are no eu rules to combat unfair trading practices between the different operators in the agri-food chain. farmers and smes are particularly vulnerable to unfair trading practices. the aim of this report is to put forward proposals against unfair trading practices in the food chain, so as to ensure a fair income for farmers and a wide choice for consumers. the objective should be to ensure transparent relations between food producers, suppliers and distributors. i voted in favour of this report in order to achieve the objective of fair trade which can in turn help to avoid overproduction and food waste.

in writing. unfair trading practices in agriculture harm the two weak links in the chain: consumers and small producers. the big retailers have too often profited by abusing their dominant position to impose their conditions on others. the european commission, in its report, acknowledges the prevalence of these abuses and notes that only a few member states have implemented legislation to combat them. however, it only supports voluntary resolution initiatives based on the exchange of good practice, such as the supply chain initiative, which have proven to be insufficient to adequately protect producers. in this resolution we have therefore called on the european commission to come forward with concrete legislative proposals to define a minimum and uniform regulatory framework at community level against unfair trading practices in the food chain, so as to ensure a fair income for farmers and a wider choice for consumers. we in the m5s want the relations between producers, suppliers and distributors of food products to be more transparent. i have therefore insisted that we should have common and harmonized rules which avoid a levelling down of standards and instead develop a level playing field between businesses of all origins, while ensuring the protection of the particularities of the culture and history of each territory.
in writing. ‒ the report calls for productivity and export-led agriculture. we cannot help but notice that this is the exact opposite of what is called 'sustainable' agriculture. the argument "we must produce more" is the usual one of the pesticide industries pushing for mass production and the introduction of gmos. i am opposed to an incomplete assessment of the risk arising from the introduction of new substances, as i am opposed to speeding up the approval processes for chemical pesticides. for these reasons i voted against.
in writing. the experience of expo 2015 feeding the planet has put one of the main issues for the global future on the agenda. today, the growing population, and the resulting demand for healthy and nutritious food, is being met by a steady decline in the availability of land, environmental loss and degradation, water shortages, increasing energy demands, and the emergence of new pests and diseases - factors that are putting our natural environment under considerable stress. technological innovation, if well used, can certainly provide a valuable contribution to addressing these challenges. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of the mcintyre report today. the union must make it more cost-effective to invest in basic and applied research and technology in agriculture, with the primary objective of protecting the genetic diversity of animal and plant species. the benefits of technological innovation must be made available to all european farmers and a holistic approach to developing skills and expertise must be strengthened. only by focusing on innovation and forward-looking scientific development can the fight against malnutrition and the protection of the environment and jobs be kept together.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the commission's proposal is in fact a reworking of the migration compact of the italian prime minister renzi, in which a logic of cooperation prevails, not disinterested, ambiguous, with few new elements, based on exchange rather than on the needs and rights of those who flee and those who welcome. the european union will seek to achieve cooperation in the management of migration flows through yet another billion on billions of euros, on the model of the eu-turkey agreement, which is achieved at the expense of european dignity and the european value system. little is said about the nature of the oppressive and dictatorial governments and regimes that would receive aid, the levels of corruption in those countries, and the instability of governments such as libya, which makes it difficult to think about possible operations. so we are in favour, in general terms, of development cooperation and saving lives, but without hypocrisy. for decades we have been talking about aid to a continent which has been mainly exploited and destabilised by the major western and european powers.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, allow me to thank, also on behalf of my group, the high representative, mrs mogherini, for her words of condolence and also all the members of this house who have been close to us at this time. beyond that, going back to the subject, i have to say that i think there are two things that should be emphasized. the first is that it is true that there are migration flows. it is also true that these flows are often encouraged and often benefited by criminal organizations, which are also sometimes terrorist organizations that may then carry out attacks in our countries and sometimes ally themselves with european criminal organizations. so we have a moral duty to block these flows. on the other hand, there is a right which i believe is inalienable, which is the right to allow a person to live and grow up in the country in which he was born. so aid to african countries is certainly fine, but let us be careful, because we have to see that these african countries then apply all those policies to make sure that these people can stay in their territories and that perhaps we do not, unfortunately as we have done in part with turkey, make alliances with countries that unfortunately do not respect human rights and create great difficulties even in what are our policies.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the recent migrant tragedies off the coast of libya and crete remind us that this phenomenon is still in a state of emergency. after the closure of the balkan route, the only viable option for asylum seekers to reach europe remains the mediterranean. the proposals presented today in this house seek to tackle the migration crisis in a new way, by focusing on new cooperation between the european union and the countries of origin and transit of migration flows. investing in the economies of these countries, through specific infrastructure projects and with resources coming not only from the community budget, is certainly a good starting point for improving european action in this field. italy has long been calling for policies in this direction. the phenomenon of migration flows to europe will certainly not be exhausted in a short time, but the success of the actions announced today will require the contribution of all, because it is good to remember that this is a european issue and not a matter of a few individual states.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, no policy, no instrument, no agreement, taken individually, can by itself provide a response to the phenomenon of migration. we reiterated this just a few weeks ago when we adopted the resolution on the holistic approach to migration. to tackle this phenomenon also means, and above all, opening up legal channels of immigration and subsequently ensuring the adoption of ambitious measures and policies aimed at integrating migrants into the social, economic and political fabric of the host countries. the commission is taking a step further towards our demands, recognising that europe can only prosper if it facilitates the mobility of knowledge and people. the legislative proposal on the amendment of the blue card is a good one. however, demographic challenges and multiple labour shortages require europe to go beyond the concept of a highly skilled worker. we must respond to the needs and new demands of the labour market and the various member states by investing in human capital. the s&d group is therefore calling for the adoption of a new framework agreement on partnership and cooperation between the european union and the republic of the philippines. as the s&d shadow rapporteur, i thank all my colleagues, but especially mr brok, who took account of our amendments with great balance and intelligence, and thus reached compromises which were supported by a large majority. this approval of the agreement confirms the impetus that we europeans want to give to trade and its freedom, also as an opportunity for the development of democracy and human rights, which are decisive conditions for concluding any agreement in the field of trade. however, the particular significance of this agreement is that the proposal covers a region of the world which is undergoing enormous expansion. southeast asia has countries that are growing much faster than europe and have young, active, life-hungry populations. among these countries are the philippines: a great and beautiful land, with an ancient history and a traditional relationship with the west. the philippines, like many other countries, still has serious problems of crime, corruption and abuse by law enforcement, but it should not be forgotten that it is a great democracy, with a constitution that defends the fundamental principles of freedom and respect for people. that is why the calls we have made for improvements in human rights, poverty and climate action are part of a desire for cooperation, support and friendship with the philippines, and are not destructive. i hope that in the coming months this cooperation with the philippines will go a long way, also on the cultural and political level more generally, and i hope that this government which has been elected by a large majority can really improve the situation.
on behalf of the efdd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we can only welcome the idea of a partnership agreement with the philippines, although there are also some very important criticisms which must necessarily be stressed. the granting of gsp+ human rights status may also have been a bit too hasty, in light of the fact that, as reported by many reports, including amnesty international, there is still torture and degrading treatment, mainly by the police, enforced disappearances, impunity and attacks on freedom of expression, as well as abuses by irregular armed militias. i also stress how inappropriate it is for us to uncritically interfere in the tensions in the south china sea, the frontier of the confrontation between blocs between china and the united states, exemplified also by the signing of the tpp. we must instead prepare a different kind of trade defence against chinese aggression against our products and not get involved in territorial disputes which are a direct continuation of the geopolitical priorities of others. we expect this new government of rodrigo duterte to make real and consistent steps forward with what he promised in the election campaign.
on behalf of the enf group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the assessment of this agreement is somewhat clouded by the consequences it may have, consequences which i consider to be heavy and damaging for some important sectors of european production, particularly that of my country, italy. for example, the agreement which allows the philippines to export duty-free 66% of its products, including footwear and textiles: this is certainly not going in the direction we want. the european union's objective for the philippines also seems to be to reach a free trade agreement. but in the report, in the agreement, they consider that today, if you wanted to do business in the philippines, perhaps from europe, you would be forced, whether you wanted to or not, to make agreements with a local partner, who by law must have a majority. and that with the freedom of enterprise and free trade is punching, in my humble opinion. president duterte has announced big projects, big investment plans, public works, but will our small and medium enterprises be able to participate? i doubt that very much.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the philippines is a strategic partner in a crucial region of the global chessboard with very high development potential. the cooperation agreement is a tool for deepening the dialogue on economic and trade matters, as well as for strengthening cooperation on human rights and strategic cooperation. the partnership and the opening of trade negotiations will have to be based on a greater coherence between economic interests and democratic principles, in line with the gsp+ system in force. the cooperation agreement and the future free trade agreement are the evolution of a natural path which sees the european union alongside the philippines. given the economic dynamism of the philippines and the importance of establishing new and close links with the country in the region, the whole strategy should aim at creating a common ground, made up of shared values, from which citizens and workers on both sides can benefit, by reinforcing cooperation and enhancing exchanges.
