vice-president of the commission. – madam president, i would like to thank the honourable members of the european parliament for joining us in this debate. hopefully there are a few more meps around because the topic is so important, boosting investments and by doing so strengthening job creation in europe. i will not go to the root causes as to why we are lacking investments. everybody knows many of the reasons, but i would just like to raise some points on what we have already done in order to promote investments and strengthen job creation in europe. as everybody remembers, in the investment plan for europe we had three different parts which are mutually reinforcing. the most important part of the plan is the removal of barriers to investments. there we have national barriers but also european-wide barriers. the commission has paid more attention than before to investment barriers at national levels. for instance, in annual growth surveys and when analysing member states’ economies, we have identified national barriers for investments and some of those findings ended up in the country-specific recommendations. so we are encouraging member states to carry out structural reforms which will boost an investment environment at national and local level. at the same time, we are putting more focus and emphasis on deepening and widening the internal market. the internal market and the whole third pillar of the investment plan, in my mind, is the most influential part in terms of job creation. we have some major projects like the digital single market, the energy union, and the capital market union but one should add to this list also the circular economy package which the commission proposed last year and also decarbonisation of transport. they will all reshape the internal market in europe. just to give you some ideas of what we have already done in terms of creating a better investment environment, we are lowering capital charges for insurance companies investing in long-term infrastructure. we are also making it more possible to find venture capital in europe for small and medium-sized enterprises by launching a new venture capital fund of funds later this year. we are giving guidance on what constitutes state aid. we are making it easier for service providers to expand to the other member states and creating a digital single market. so lots of things are happening on this front and i hope parliament will support these projects. the faster we can deliver on the internal market side, the faster we can get a better business environment and a better investment environment. a second pillar of the investment plan consists of two major initiatives. the first one is an investment advisory hub which is providing technical assistance and advice to private investors, but also to public entities. this is functioning quite well. we already have more than 100 requests, mostly from private companies. they are asking for advice and technical assistance to improve the quality of the projects. for instance, some of the investors are asking for technical assistance on how to benefit from various eu funds. so this is a very elementary and important part of the investment plan because it makes it easier for member states to use the european fund for strategic investments (efsi) but also the other funds and also to create investment platforms collecting together smaller investments, and by doing so it is easier to get financing for smaller projects. the newest creation under the second pillar is the european investment project portal. the idea came from the uk. i visited london and the financiers, for instance investment banks, said that they are able and willing to invest more in european infrastructure but it is sometimes very difficult to find good projects from different countries. their idea was to create a transparent open portal to which both public and private project promoters could send their projects, and the promoters could get better visibility for their projects. so it is some sort of dating service for project promoters and financiers, and it is up and running now. we disclosed it at the beginning of june and i am quite excited to see how well it functions. we have designed the portal together with the private sector in order to make it as pragmatic and practical as possible. so over time there should be thousands of investment projects, and hopefully it functions as we have planned. finally, the first pillar of the efsi plan is also up and running. so far we have used efsi to the tune of eur 12.8 billion for the infrastructure and innovation window but also for sme financing. this eur 12.8 billion is expected to trigger mostly private investment, or public-private partnership investments worth eur 100 billion. of this, 80%, in other words, eur 80 billion out of eur 100 billion, comes from the private sector, so efsi seems to function as planned. it provides risk financing mostly to private investors and by doing so it crowds in private money, which is currently peacefully resting in bank accounts. so there seems to be a lack of risk financing in europe. there is plenty of liquidity everywhere, this is not a problem at the moment, but because we have changed banking regulations this is one of the reasons the banks cannot take as much risk as they did a few years ago. that is why efsi is providing something which is lacking, at least to a large extent, in the market. we have around 65 projects, i mean infrastructure or industrial investment projects, which have got financing from efsi. in addition to this, and i would say more importantly, we have 185 agreements between the european investment fund (eif) and intermediary banks, between the fund and private banks, on sme financing. these 185 agreements between the eif, which has support from efsi, and banks, will provide financing to approximately 150 000 european smes. in italy alone we have 28 banks which have made an agreement with the eif, and 44 000 italian smes will get financing because of these agreements. this is sometimes the fastest way to stimulate the economy. there seems to be a lack of sme financing, especially equity financing, everywhere in europe, even in the most developed markets. that is why i think in the future we have to pay special attention to this sme window, especially in equity financing, because this is something which the market does not offer that much at the moment. of course, we are developing the capital market union in order to improve the capital market environment in europe, but it will always take some time and meanwhile we have to address the market gap by providing efsi financing. the uk has been very active on this issue. the uk is a country which is familiar with financial instruments and that is why british banks have been actively contacting the eif and providing more financing to british businesses. the commission will present a new proposal to prolong efsi later this year. we have to analyse efsi, its achievements and possible weaknesses, and once we have done the analysis we will make a new proposal, which will continue efsi beyond the expiry date which we have at the moment. the main issue in this is to focus on addressing market failure. the main issue is not to make it larger. the main thing is to focus efsi financing on the areas where market does not function properly. also one thing on which we have to be very careful is to provide financing for new innovations which will strengthen the sustainable development of our economies in social terms, in environmental terms, and for instance provide financing to the investments which will promote the circular economy. we are also going to propose some kind of external investment plan. efsi has functioned very well in europe, but we could use the same model also for external financing, especially when trying to achieve development goals. so the commission is looking at the opportunities, how we could use existing development resources in a more efficient way by establishing a new fund which could function in a similar way as the efsi functions but in third countries. the aim is to address the root causes of migration. having said this i do not want to oversell the idea; we cannot address the root causes for migration overnight, or very fast, but anyway we could use our development resources more efficiently and by establishing a new external investment fund we could encourage private investment in third countries and by doing so strengthen economic structures and address the root causes of migration. this idea is at the initial stage but we will come with a proposal hopefully later this year. honourable members, i will stop here and i am very interested to hear your views, how you have seen the investment plan as a whole and maybe the final word here is that we need to cooperate very closely, because meps are representing the european people. you are representing our regions, and the more you are raising awareness amongst investors about the opportunities that efsi can offer, the better. even though we are working very hard every single day advertising efsi opportunities, we are never as efficient as you are if you are meeting local investors, local entrepreneurs and bankers explaining how efsi can help the situation in the regions.

but more can and must be done! there are three critical issues that need to be addressed. first, additionality is a very important aspect. these funds must be additional, not substitute. it cannot be business as usual, the normal work of the eib, otherwise we would not need an investment plan and a special fund. secondly: you have to take a higher risk. i say to the eib that triple a must not be a dogma, otherwise we would not need an investment plan if the projects with the highest risk cannot be financed. thirdly, relations with parliament. you recognized that a moment ago, vice-president katainen. we are the elected citizens, and this plan comes from our intuition and our request. we need a constant relationship with the commission and the european investment bank. we need more listening. we need to work together on the points of suffering, on the points of greatest need for change. we need to work together to get more information from local realities, who need to know and need to be able to apply for these opportunities. in conclusion, we must make this plan a reality by means of an extension, but it must not be an extension for its own sake, it must be an extension aimed at making this plan a serious, convincing and concrete response to the economic and social crisis which europe is deeply experiencing.

vice-president of the commission. – madam president, i will make a few comments. i will try to group my answers to your questions together. first, around 30% of efsi projects are in the energy field and mostly in the renewable energy efficiency field. some of our colleagues said that there were no projects in energy efficiency. that is a complete mistake. efsi provides risk financing for new technologies and innovative projects and that is very good because this is what we all wanted. for everybody who is concerned about projects already financed – or if there are some areas which have not been covered, like the circular economy for instance – i strongly encourage everybody to be active with the people who are operating in, for instance, the circular economy field to raise awareness of what efsi can provide for them. i do this every single day. i go around europe explaining the opportunities efsi has to offer, for instance, new innovations and circular economy projects, but unfortunately the level of awareness varies between the member states. now, i will come to the point concerning why some member states have not benefited very much from efsi already. it is mostly – if you look at it very concretely – because public authorities have not been active in promoting efsi opportunities. as we all know, efsi does not finance pure public projects, but very often regional authorities, national authorities and ministers play a role when raising awareness about what efsi can do among the private sector – private investors – and there are huge differences between member states. some ministers have even indicated very clearly when i met them that if there were not more trains coming to their country, then they were not interested in efsi at all. i asked them, if they were not interested, to please convey the message to investors in the private sector that they could contact the eib directly. private investors in many countries are hearing for the first time, even though we have repeated it over and over again, that they do not need any public sector approval if they want to apply for resources from efsi. we just have to repeat this over and over again. that is why i have repeated here a couple of times that we need your help. in some member states some meps have been very active at regional level, conveying the message that companies can apply directly for resources from the eib. another point is that we have commission representations in all the member states, which are ready to serve both public authorities and regional authorities, but also the private sector, to explain what efsi can do. in most member states too we have eib offices, which are there for technical assistance and advice. in many member states we have seen excellent events organised by the private sector itself or by political parties, for instance, or by public authorities, to which they have invited private investors, entrepreneurs, industrialists and regional leaders, and to which the eib has sent its representatives and the commission has sent its representatives to explain what efsi has done in other countries. we have to do this more in all the member states. so there are some attitude problems. some member states are very passive but we try to contact the private sector directly in those member states where the public authorities have not been the most active. when looking at the projects, there were a few concerns about whether efsi has financed motorways without good reason. actually the few motorway investments which have benefited from efsi have been technically the most difficult, there has been uncertainty about the traffic and it has been very difficult to attract private financing for those projects. before you condemn those projects, i really encourage you to look at them and discuss them, for instance, with the efsi management because they can explain in more detail why they have selected those projects. we are helping – although it is not our primary duty – member states to create platforms for green shipping, for instance. this means that we try to collect together port investment and other green shipping types of investment in order to spread efsi to the areas where there have not been any projects so far. i visited greece for the second time a month ago. i met representatives from the five biggest banks in greece and tried to explain what they could do for smes for instance. in greece too it was the first time that greek banks had heard that they could apply directly for resources from efsi for smes. i understand all the difficulties that the greek banks have, but another idea which i raised there was to build an investment platform, for instance in the tourism sector, which means, basically that the platform could collect together a large amount of small—sized investment – for instance hotel renovation projects or things like that – and the private sector could put some equity in the platform while efsi could provide, for instance, long—term, very low interest rate loans to the entrepreneurs. i am a hundred percent sure that these would function in greece. i spoke about it with the greek authorities and the greek government and we have very close cooperation with the greek government on this issue. so i do want to see this happening in greece. the same thing would also function in cyprus. there were lots of other issues. mr nicholson, you raised northern ireland and why northern ireland has not benefited from the efsi yet. i do not know what the northern ireland authorities have done or have not done, but we have our representation there at the authorities’ disposal. i visited there personally and i tried to convey the message to the private sector in northern ireland that they could apply resources directly from efsi and it would be good to establish a platform for smaller projects. so everything is possible, in northern ireland too. all member states have the same opportunities and in those member states which have been the least active, the commission, and even my cabinet directly, try to help the authorities understand how they could utilise the opportunities we have at our disposal. i will stop here. we have mostly been talking about efsi and this is only one part of the investment plan. i want to underline the importance of the single market project. i will repeat once more that hopefully parliament and the council can adopt and approve the proposals from mr ansip on the digital single market and from commissioner vella on the circular economy, etc. this is even more important than what efsi can do because, when we take down barriers to investment, it has a big impact on growth and on sustainable growth.
in writing. in today's debate in the house, the commission presented a first budget for the juncker plan, one year after its launch; on the one hand, it is possible to say that important results have been achieved over 100 billion investments disbursed, with 65 projects funded and more than 150 000 smes involved on the other hand, i am convinced that more needs to be done. i believe that the efsi should focus on additionality and finance innovative projects with higher risk, which would otherwise not find regular funding opportunities, in order to maximise its leverage and create added value for the european industrial and social fabric. secondly, i believe that the success of the juncker plan must come from better integration with the existing structural funds, with the aim of involving more local authorities and the poorest and most deprived areas. the juncker plan is already providing a tangible stimulus to economic growth, offering vital new oxygen to our companies and smes. it is the most effective response to the economic and social crisis of recent years and to the lack of investment in europe. we must work to make it even more ambitious and effective.

in writing. i supported the establishment of the panama papers commission of inquiry which will be mandated to investigate the failure of banks and authorities to apply european laws against money laundering, evasion and avoidance. the spotlight will be on the role played by banks in creating a parallel world where they launder dirty money and hide vast sums of stolen money from the public, with the support of thousands of eu-based consultancies and law firms, at the intolerable complaisance of european governments and regulators. it is precisely in the obscure banking system protected by europe's false transparency and 'banking secrecy' that the origin of the problem and the solution must be sought. this will suffice: introduction of exemplary sanctions, up to the withdrawal of the banking licence, for banks that are complicit in abuses; maximum transparency, traceability and publicity of financial flows and tax information; effective and seamless anti-money laundering legislation, including trusts, and introducing a mandatory publicly accessible register of ultimate beneficiaries. these are obviously simple measures whose implementation depends solely on the political will to change. the problem is that the status quo is too convenient for this europe that is subservient to the interests of big business and the banks.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the gabriel report approving the agreement between the eu and palau on the short-stay visa waiver. the text provides for an exemption for citizens of the union and palau who travel to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa exemption applies to all categories of persons, regardless of the reason for their stay, provided that it is not linked to the pursuit of an activity for which they are paid. this is an important agreement which will help to intensify relations with the pacific state and to develop a more regular political dialogue.

in writing. ‒ the visa waiver agreement was signed in brussels on 7 december 2015 and will be fully implemented after the approval of the european parliament. the document provides for visa-free travel for citizens of the union and for citizens of palau when travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for a short stay. the agreement excludes stays, even if short, for the purpose of carrying out a paid activity. the political and economic stability of the republic of palau and the absence of situations of repatriation or irregular immigration by palau citizens are the basis for the conclusion of the agreement which can have positive effects for both parties. the simplification of visa procedures will facilitate investment in the island which, together with the increase in the number of flights to this destination, will be able to promote the development of tourism, which is an important part of the territory's economy. for the reasons i have just given, i therefore voted in favour of the agreement.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament today gave its approval to the extension of an important, though little-known, agreement, the information technology agreement (ita), concluded in the wto. the agreement, signed in singapore in 1996 and entering into force the following year, has expanded over time to include more and more participants, from the original 29 signatories to the 82 of today, representing over 90% of world trade in computer goods. after more than 20 years, in the light of the rapid and many developments in this field, the agreement needed to be revised in a comprehensive way and this is what the european parliament has said today. the extension of the agreement agreed by the strasbourg assembly provides for the liberalization of 201 new articles, including gps, touch-screen, telecommunications satellites and medical equipment. in addition to strengthening the multilateral trading system in the information technology sector, the enlargement of the agreement should encourage exports of these products from the eu, to the benefit of our manufacturing sector, and translate into greater supply and lower prices for consumers.

in writing. ‒ the objective of the 2010 hns convention is to ensure the accountability and payment of adequate, prompt and effective compensation for loss or damage to persons, property and the environment resulting from the transport of dangerous and harmful substances by sea through a specialised international hns compensation fund. it is obviously an important legal instrument, but only states are allowed to ratify it. i voted in favour of the svoboda report because i share the need to ensure certainty in the application of legislation which, with the council's decision, could be compromised. the interim report adopted is therefore intended to put pressure on the council to amend the proposal submitted to request a uniform ratification of the hns convention, without leaving the uncertainty about the timing of the first formulation.

in writing. ‒ the 2010 hns convention establishes the objective liability of the owner of a ship carrying dangerous and harmful substances for damage resulting from an event related to the transport of such substances by sea on board. there are limited exceptions to the owner's strict liability, which is related to the owner's obligation to take out insurance or other financial security in order to cover his liability for damages in accordance with the provisions of the convention. the establishment of the special compensation fund to compensate anyone who has suffered damage resulting from the transport of dangerous and harmful substances by sea, to the extent that such person has not been able to obtain full and adequate compensation for the damage from the ship owner and his insurer, up to a maximum of 250 million units of account (approximately eur 310 million), on the basis of a system of contributions paid to the hns fund by the recipients of dangerous and harmful substances in each contracting state is also positive. it should nevertheless be noted that it is in the interest of the union as a whole to have a uniform liability regime applicable to environmental damage: the council and the commission must therefore follow the instructions of the european parliament.

in writing. ‒ in 2010, the hns protocol introduced liability and compensation for damage resulting from the transport of dangerous and harmful substances by sea, including liquefied natural gas (lng) and liquefied petroleum gas (lpg). the main objective of the hsn convention is to enable international cooperation to protect the marine environment from harmful and hazardous substances. in addition, the hns convention establishes the objective liability of the owner of a ship carrying dangerous and noxious substances for damage resulting from an event related to the transport of dangerous and noxious substances by sea on board that ship. as this convention is very important for the environment of the european union, i have decided to vote in favour of this interim recommendation which is intended to open a dialogue on this subject with the council and the commission.
in writing. ‒ parliament is called upon to approve the accession of the member states to the 2010 protocol to the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea (hns), with the exception of the aspects relating to judicial cooperation in civil matters. accession to the convention is desirable as it offers more specific rules and much more specialised and effective legal instruments. the evaluation of these reports was therefore positive.
in writing. ‒ the objective of the 2010 hns convention is to ensure the accountability and payment of adequate, prompt and effective compensation for loss or damage to persons, property and the environment resulting from the transport of dangerous and harmful substances by sea through a specialised international hns compensation fund. it is obviously an important legal instrument, but only states are allowed to ratify it. i voted in favour of the svoboda report because i share the need to ensure certainty in the application of legislation which, with the council's decision, could be compromised. the interim report adopted is therefore intended to put pressure on the council to amend the proposal submitted to request a uniform ratification of the hns convention, without leaving the uncertainty about the timing of the first formulation.
in writing. ‒ the report is well-written, interesting and uncritical, and i therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ taking note of the discussion on the subject, the positive contribution of the relevant commissions and working groups, and in the light of the significant share of dangerous and harmful substances in the transport of goods by sea, the worldwide nature of the shipping industry and the possible cross-border impact of accidents involving dangerous or harmful substances, we believe that it is in the interest of the union as a whole to have a uniform liability regime applicable to environmental damage resulting from the transport of dangerous and harmful substances by sea, which can only be achieved if, as already stated and hoped, the council and the commission take due account of the recommendations of the european parliament.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report today because it provides valuable insights and constructive criticism with a view to the ratification by member states of the 2010 protocol to the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea. the file notes that the above convention and directive 2004/35/ec operate in the same field as regards the liability of professional operators, with clear differences. in particular, eu legislation is not binding on third countries, including those that are important flag states, which could prove problematic when dealing with complaints about leakages of hazardous and noxious substances with international aspects. moreover, if countries neighbouring eu member states were parties to the convention and an accident occurred involving both an eu member state and a neighbouring country, the claimants and the ship owners would be subject to different (and contradictory) regimes. the ep also calls for the commission to be given the right to adopt a new directive on the protection of the environment.
in writing. ‒ the second report by mr svoboda concerns a council decision on the ratification and accession of the member states to the 2010 protocol to the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea (hns). in the absence of a reio (regional economic integration organisation) clause in the text of the convention or the protocol, member states should conclude such an international agreement on behalf of the union, subject to authorisation by the council and approval by the european parliament on a proposal from the commission. the rapporteur believes that parliament should not give its consent until the uniformity, integrity and effectiveness of union law and the fundamental principle of the conferral of eu competences have been guaranteed. accession to the international convention on harmful substances is desirable because it offers more specific rules and legal instruments that are much more specialized and effective than those offered by the community regulatory framework. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ justice wants, as the italian civil code states, that any damage obliges the one who caused it to compensate the one who suffered it. and that's where we all agree. however, there are cases where the amount of damage is far beyond the means of the person who caused it. i voted in favour of this proposal because it provides a concrete answer to these cases and is a step towards a just solution.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the council decision on the ratification and accession by the member states, in the interest of the european union, to the 2010 protocol to the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea as regards aspects of judicial cooperation in civil matters, because i believe it is important to send a signal to the council about the importance of the timely implementation of the protocol by all member states (ms). i believe that the council's proposal to leave the ms free to decide when to ratify this convention is a step in the wrong direction, as it risks creating legal disparities and legal uncertainties by creating different jurisdictional regimes in the event of accidents caused by ships carrying dangerous substances. the 2010 convention overlaps with the brussels 1a regulation with regard to jurisdiction and recognition of decisions, introducing a more stringent regime than eu law in order to limit the phenomenon of 'forum shopping'. it is therefore important that parliament exert pressure on the council to ensure that all member states ratify the international legislation at the same time.
in writing. the 2010 hns convention establishes the objective liability of the owner of a ship carrying harmful substances, while regulating the liability of the owner for damage resulting from improper transport. the convention itself lays down rules on the jurisdiction of courts and the recognition and enforcement of judgments, superimposing itself on the application of the rules contained in the brussels i regulation. we therefore believe that the conclusion of this protocol will ensure the full application of the rules on liability and compensation for damage in respect of accidents occurring during maritime transport. we will also engage in a dialogue with the council and the commission to develop a coherent eu policy on liability and compensation for environmental damage caused by the transport of dangerous and harmful substances by sea.

in writing. ‒ tunisia is the only example of democracy that emerged from the arab spring. the process of consolidating the democratic system, threatened by numerous terrorist attacks, has succeeded in establishing itself and in defining a constitutional charter that protects the rights of citizens and constitutes a stable institutional system. the economic crisis affecting the maghreb country, however, represents a serious risk factor, which is combined with the persistence of areas of instability in the neighboring areas, especially in neighboring libya where military formations linked to isis are active. i voted in favour of the de sarnez report because i believe that it is essential to mobilise macrofinancial assistance for tunisia. the european union will be able to provide concrete support to an important country which is successfully embarking on the path of democracy, respect for human rights and the rule of law through this instrument. the programme, with a budget of eur 500 million, will support the reforms undertaken by tunisia to improve its fiscal situation, balance its balance of payments and create a favourable investment climate.
in writing. ‒ i do not agree with this report and the allocation of eur 500 million to tunisia. i am sceptical about the real usefulness of this type of macrofinancial assistance and even more sceptical about the way in which it is monitored for its correct and transparent use. i am increasingly wondering how it is that the eu is always at the forefront of helping third countries and never our own citizens and businesses. for these reasons i did not intend to vote in favour of this measure.
in writing. ‒ economic aid in exchange for democratic reforms and civil progress is one of the eu's most widely used instruments in its neighbourhood and partnership relations with third countries. this has often produced positive results for the citizens of both sides and has increased the range of influence of the european union's soft power. tunisia is now one of the few (or perhaps the only) arab countries where the so-called "arab spring" has resulted in a modern type of democracy, which looks to the west and the development of the rule of law. a friendly democracy, which we must support by allowing it to develop under appropriate conditions, gradually, and to be gradually integrated into the common free trade area.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a european parliament and council decision on the granting of additional macrofinancial assistance to tunisia because at the moment tunisia represents a hope in the arab mediterranean context. many problems remain, the country has been repeatedly targeted by terrorist attacks and bombings, which have particularly affected the tourism sector, which has always been a central element for the tunisian economy. it is therefore necessary for europe to be able to take all the necessary steps to support this delicate phase of transition in the country. in this way, by means of concrete actions, we will be able to show solidarity and determination, encouraging the country from which the arab spring began and which certainly represents a model for all those who want to try to promote peace and democracy in the middle east, north africa and the rest of the world.
in writing. ‒ in view of the strong impact of the security situation on the tunisian economy and the need for external financing during the consolidation of the political transition, the european commission is submitting to the european parliament and the council a proposal for a second macro-financial assistance to the republic of tunisia of up to eur 500 million in the form of medium-term loans. the new proposal would help tunisia to cover part of its residual external financing needs, estimated at around usd 2,9 billion for the period 2016-17, under the new imf programme and would reduce the short-term vulnerabilities of the economy with regard to balance of payments and public finances, complementing the economic adjustment and reform programme agreed with the imf and the world bank, as well as reforms agreed under the eu budget support operations. i am convinced that the tunisian people must be supported and that the eu must give real aid to tunisia, so i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i believe that in recent years tunisia has demonstrated its potential by making a great step forward in the drafting of a constitution that safeguards the rights and freedoms of citizens. it has also made substantial progress in establishing a democratic regime and modernising its economy to achieve stable political conditions. however, the multiple terrorist attacks in the country have severely damaged the economic sector. for these reasons, i believe that the european union should contribute to supporting tunisia by providing liquidity through soft loans so that the country can strengthen the security of its citizens and improve the local economic sector.
in writing. ‒ following the changes in the political landscape since 2011, the eu has committed itself to supporting tunisia in the process of economic and political reforms and has increased its financial support to this end. in particular, eur 524 million in grants was made available for the period 2011-2015 under the ordinary convention programme, and eur 155 million under the 'support for partnership, reform and inclusive growth' programme for the period 2011-2013. in my vote in favour, i intend to support macrofinancial assistance to tunisia so that this country can make progress in its economic and social development, close the external financial deficit in the balance of payments and implement structural reforms. i believe that tunisia is a positive example in the post-2011 regional political instability landscape and that it is therefore the eu's duty to concretely support its efforts towards democratisation, especially given that, at this stage, it is a vulnerable target for terrorist attacks. i also believe that the macrofinancial assistance programme can play a proactive role in supporting tunisia's democratization process by making the granting of assistance conditional on certain preconditions, such as respect for the rule of law and human rights.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament today approved the report on the proposal for a decision on a eur 500 million loan to tunisia, which will be available for a period of two and a half years. this measure is part of a wider policy of support which the european union is pursuing in this country. it is only a few months ago that parliament voted in favour of the introduction of emergency trade measures for tunisia. the main objective is to consolidate relations with this strategic partner, the only country in the north african region facing the difficult transition to full democracy, and to provide structural support for its economic recovery. the accession of tunisia to the loan is conditional on the signing of a memorandum of understanding with the european commission, which tunisia will have to respect by ensuring the implementation of effective reforms. the appropriation of this loan is all the more important following the heavy blow inflicted by the terrorist attacks of march 2015, which severely weakened a key sector such as tourism, increasing unemployment and instability in the country. that is why i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ i fully support the actions the european commission is taking to support tunisia. this was the only country where the arab spring was followed by real improvements in the social and economic conditions of the population, in what can be described as a democratic transition. the country finally has a constitution that protects rights and freedoms, a well-established justice system and media that are able to observe and exercise the right to criticize. as an italian, i cannot help but be concerned about the situation in a country so close to the coast of sicily, where the regional political and security context is unfortunately still extremely unstable, particularly because of the border it shares with libya. this is why europe must contribute to a process of stabilisation in the country, for which macrofinancial assistance is a key instrument, since it directly contributes to improving the quality of life of the population.
in writing. some third countries with which the eu has agreements are experiencing difficulties, including tunisia. in fact, tunisia's economic situation has deteriorated further after the terrorist attacks in 2015. for these reasons, the eu wants to make a concrete contribution to its economic development and to the promotion of the democratic process. the aid consists of a temporary loan of eur 500 million, to be paid in instalments. it is important to remember, however, that financial agreements will only be granted if the country successfully completes the programmes set out in the agreements. in order to improve living conditions in the countries of the southern shore of the mediterranean, and in the context of a long-term strategy against irregular migration, as proposed in the migration compact, i believe that it is useful to act in this direction.
in writing. ‒ tunisia is going through a period of great economic difficulties, mainly caused by the various terrorist attacks and attacks it has suffered, with a number of consequences, such as negative effects in various economic sectors, first and foremost tourism, the growth of unemployment, mainly of women, instability in the regional political and security environment. despite all these problems, tunisia is trying to respond, but needs support to bring about real improvements in the management of public finances, the tax system, social security, financial sector reform and to improve the regulatory framework for trade and investment. it is necessary to strengthen its relations with its main partners, first and foremost the european union. since macrofinancial assistance is an instrument for a third country which is in a crisis situation and since tunisia has all the necessary conditions for the granting of macrofinancial assistance, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ tunisia, which is in the process of democratizing the country, is now led by a coalition government, elected in full transparency, with an independent media and an independent judiciary. because of this success, supported by an active civil society and a nobel prize winner, the country is now threatened by destabilization attempts, supported by enemies of freedom and pluralistic values. terrorist attacks against westerners in seaside resorts have in fact undermined the tourism industry, the first line of tunisia's gdp which last season saw foreign visits drop by 80 percent. the high levels of unemployment, particularly among young people and in rural areas, the threats of proliferation of weapons in the event of new nato operations in the region and the proximity to libya, which is home to 1.8 million citizens, could ultimately increase the risk of radicalization of the population with clear repercussions throughout the mediterranean area. in view of all these factors, we can only express our most sincere support for the financial assistance measures which, in the form of long-term loans, can contribute to the stabilization of the country and the future of the tunisians.
in writing. ‒ given the considerable steps tunisia has taken in its transition to democracy, i believe that macrofinancial assistance can both support the country and, at the same time, counter those who want to destabilise the situation. the reforms implemented by tunisia fully meet the requirements for the granting of macrofinancial assistance by the european union, and i therefore feel that i should vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ tunisia has made enormous progress on its path to democratic transition. it has a constitution that protects rights and freedoms, an independent judiciary and an independent media. the dynamic and modern civil society has actively contributed to this transformation. however, the country is experiencing great difficulties due to terrorist attacks that have targeted its main economic sectors, such as tourism, with the aim of destabilizing it. economic growth has slowed down and unemployment, especially for women and young people, remains very high. despite all these problems, tunisia is courageously pursuing its reform agenda to modernise its economic structures and is strengthening relations with its partners, including the eu. it is therefore important that europe shows solidarity and does everything possible to support its development by taking concrete action to the direct benefit of the population. macro-financial assistance (mfa) is the most appropriate instrument in this context to accompany the modernisation programme. tunisia fulfils all the conditions for the granting of the mfa and i therefore support the commission's proposal, supported by parliament's report, to grant aid.
in writing. ‒ tunisia's economy has been in serious trouble since the beginning of the so-called "arab spring" revolution in 2011. in 2015, the country was hit by terrorist attacks that disrupted tourist flows and worsened its already weak fiscal balance and credit position. the eu provided €300 million in financial aid to tunisia in 2014. in august 2015, the tunisian government requested the eu to contribute eur 500 million to a second programme of assistance and additional loans from the international monetary fund (imf). in order to access the credit, tunisia will have to sign a memorandum of understanding with the european commission, committing itself to implementing structural reforms and to pursuing sound public financial management. it will also have to ensure respect for democratic mechanisms, the rule of law and human rights, under eu supervision. once these conditions are met, tunisia will be able to benefit from the loan for a period of two and a half years. i voted in favour of this report and i believe that these are the kinds of aid that should be pursued by the eu institutions and not agreements, wicked ones, like those concerning olive oil.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution tabled by mr de sarnez on the granting of macrofinancial assistance to tunisia. the text adopted provides for a loan of eur 500 million to be granted to tunisia by the commission on behalf of the eu, which will cover at least part of the country's balance of payments-related residual external financing needs. the loan will be disbursed in three tranches, the first of 200 million euro and the subsequent of 150 million euro each. as is usual in the case of financial assistance, the aid is not an end in itself, since it is conditional on the successful implementation of the programme envisaged by the international monetary fund. the commission and the tunisian authorities would also agree on specific structural reforms in the framework of a memorandum of understanding.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the bayet report on the proposal for a directive on tax avoidance practices which have a direct impact on the functioning of the internal market. harmful tax competition, often taking advantage of the lack of harmonisation in regulation, is, together with aggressive tax planning by multinationals, one of the most important causes of the loss of resources to states, estimated at between 100 and 240 billion dollars a year worldwide. the need to create a genuine european single market cannot but pass through an agreement on the taxation question, based on fair and efficient taxation of enterprises. we must prevent multinational companies from shifting profits to tax havens without paying taxes where they are made. the text adopted improves the commission's proposal by strengthening the patent proposal and generally strengthening the role of the european parliament as the body responsible for monitoring and evaluating the application of the directive in the 28 member states.

in writing. ‒ aggressive tax planning and related practices have a high cost to government budgets, resulting in considerable losses in revenue that could otherwise be used to promote employment, more resilient social systems and the realisation of targeted investments. i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the question of the taxation of capital, and whether he is aware that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the question of the taxation of capital. the report adopted today aims to define common anti-tax avoidance rules in some specific areas, as well as more general anti-abuse rules. it was important to stress that taxes should be paid where they generate profits and it is good to have introduced precise and binding definitions, such as that of 'stable organisation' or 'tax haven', which make it possible to verify more clearly where a multinational is actually established, so as to oblige companies to pay their taxes in a fair way.
in writing. ‒ tax evasion by multinational companies is a serious act which, besides being immoral, is a real problem for european citizens who see an estimated tax shortfall in state coffers of between 100 and 240 billion dollars every year worldwide. this represents between 4 and 10% of global corporate tax revenues and, above all, a huge loss of income for states, which reduces their ability to invest to promote employment, fight poverty and develop effective universal health systems. this shortfall is often made up by public debt, by cuts in services or by raising taxes on resident citizens: the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat fraud in the area of the internal market.
in writing. ‒ after careful examination of the documentation and discussion in the chamber, i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive because i believe that harmful tax competition, which exploits information lag and the lack of harmonisation in regulation, together with aggressive tax planning by multinationals, cause huge losses of income for states, reducing their capacity to invest and delaying the implementation of reforms for employment, poverty and universal health. i therefore support the report which deals with the delicate issues of introducing definitions of 'stable organisation', 'double deduction' and 'minimum economic substance', because the elements which allow an undertaking to be defined on the basis of factual criteria, taking into account human and material resources, management autonomy, legal reality and the nature of assets, must be established in a harmonized and coherent way, once and for all. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of electronic data interchange systems, such as the internet, to the provision of services in the field of telecommunications.

in writing. ‒ several studies by the organisation for economic co-operation and development (oecd) have shown that aggressive tax planning by multinational groups costs member states hundreds of billions of euros each year in lost tax revenues. it is a phenomenon which reduces the resources available to member states to promote employment or improve health systems; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the taxation of small and mediumsized enterprises is not distorted. the directive is part of the package of anti-tax evasion rules announced in january by european commissioner moscovici and contains the principle that tax must be paid where profits and value are generated, providing specific anti-avoidance rules in six specific areas: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be given the opportunity to present its opinion on the draft directive on the taxation of savings income in the event of a tax dispute. today we have taken a major step forward in the fight against corporate tax evasion and in the protection of citizens.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the council directive on rules against certain tax avoidance practices which have a direct impact on the functioning of the internal market because i believe that the adoption of the directive is urgent as it will effectively help to combat tax evasion. parliament has made this a qualifying objective, well aware that taxation is a matter for the sovereignty of the member states, but convinced that the current situation, in which there are companies that can avoid paying their fair share of tax, is no longer sustainable, and the recent panama papers scandal requires that we go further and deeper. i shared the clear message of the european parliament to put an end to double taxation, the mechanism which allows multinationals to avoid paying taxes where they make their profits, or not to pay taxes at all, and to control intra-multinational group lending. the average taxation in europe, according to oecd and commission studies, is 19%, a figure in line with that of other industrialized countries. i hope that the eu will be ambitious and that it can make progress in this area. the european parliament will be a strong ally, because fairly shared taxation can help to support sustainable growth.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i believe that the eu's objective of building an economic and monetary union must be a priority, achievable through the harmonisation of european taxation. taxation of businesses, particularly multinational companies, must be fair and effective and must become the cornerstone of the single market. if we want to have a reliable single market, it is imperative that the member states reach an agreement on taxation. a coordinated and harmonised approach to the implementation of tax systems is vital to ensure the smooth functioning of the single market and the success of the capital markets union. the main objective of this report is to ensure that multinational companies pay taxes where they make profits. an oecd study estimated that tax avoidance by multinational corporations costs governments worldwide between $100 billion and $240 billion annually. this represents a significant loss of revenue for states, thus reducing their ability to invest in actions that can promote employment, combat poverty and develop effective health systems for all.
in writing. following the panama papers scandal and in connection with previous work in parliament, a report is presented on the implementation of rules against tax evasion. if we are to achieve a reliable single market and promote the success of the capital markets union, it is necessary for member states to reach agreement, creating fair and efficient corporate taxation. the main objective of the report is to create a strong and harmonised system throughout the union which is capable of combating tax evasion, with the essential participation of member states, companies and international partners. the report envisages the implementation of a system which ensures that companies pay taxes in the country where profits are made, and sets out the parameters for a company to be established in a given country. in response to the practice of multinationals of shifting their profits to so-called tax havens, i vote in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ aggressive tax planning by multinationals costs the state budget hundreds of billions of euros every year. the package of measures we are approving today is a clear signal to the member states of the need to make ambitious progress in the fight against tax evasion, on the basis of the principle that taxes should be paid where profits are generated. to this end, it is envisaged that: the introduction of precise and binding definitions of the establishment of multinational companies in a given country, to make it impossible to transfer profits to tax havens in order to avoid paying taxes; the creation of a blacklist of tax havens and countries, including european countries, that distort competition through tax regimes favourable to multinationals; clarification of patent rules and more effective controls on lending between entities belonging to the same multinational to prevent abuse. the present system, in which the vast majority of citizens pay their taxes honestly while a few economic giants manage to evade tax obligations, is intolerable. it is time for everyone to contribute equally to the financing of health care, security, schools, universities and youth work policies. i therefore wholeheartedly support the bayet report.

in writing. ‒ the fight against international terrorism has been a priority on the political agenda for the last decade. the succession of attacks in various parts of the world, the increase in damage and casualties, has been a major feature of the history of the first two decades of the 21st century, a factor which has required a wider intervention by states to curb and defeat the terrorist phenomenon. on some occasions, however, this intervention has been dangerous, using instruments which clearly violate human rights. in a resolution of february 2015, the european parliament strongly condemned the use of torture, unlawful detention and inhuman and degrading treatment by the cia, which had already been denounced in a report by the us senate. the failure to act on the requests made in that house is the reason for this new motion for a resolution which i have decided to support. the text strongly reiterates the need to continue investigating and prosecuting the perpetrators of human rights violations resulting from the cia's extraordinary rendition and secret detention programmes and calls on the council and the commission to report on these events by june 2016.

in writing. ‒ investing in space means pushing companies and research centres to exceed the limits of their current technical and scientific capabilities and knowledge: it means encouraging them to face new problems and to invent new solutions. this has positive implications for all areas of technology for civilian life, from new materials to telecommunications, from satellite positioning systems to energy efficiency. many of the great inventions we use in our daily lives are the products of investments in space research and security and defense: the internet, smartphones, microwaves, many heat-resistant polymers, gps navigators and much more. investing in this sector is therefore investing in the future. it also means investing in the protection of the security of our citizens, because already today and even more so in the coming decades, european states must be prepared to deal with long-range and mixed threats, and any progress in prevention, satellite monitoring and missile interception capabilities is essential to prevent disasters and save many lives.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today because i believe it is essential that the european union strengthens its role as a guarantor of security within and beyond its borders, thereby ensuring the necessary stability in its neighbourhood and in the international arena. at this particular juncture in history, terrorist attacks are making the eu's internal and external security more challenging. we must have the necessary confidence in the space sector's ability to curb terrorism and terrorist organisations. this is possible, for example, through the skills of locating and monitoring training camps. the eu's objective of ensuring autonomy in space facilities is of vital importance for both the civil and the security and defence sectors. it is estimated that in western countries between 6% and 7% of gdp is directly dependent on satellite positioning and navigation technologies. the copernicus programme and its excellent contribution to security should be particularly commended. its useful application can be seen in crisis prevention, humanitarian cooperation and maritime surveillance.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on space capability for european security and defence, because i believe it is crucial to strengthen the common security and defence policy at a time when the security environment, inside and outside the european union, is becoming increasingly dangerous and challenging. the new challenges of terrorism and wars on europe's borders require us to make the union's defence and security policy a more effective political instrument and a real guarantee for the security of citizens and for the promotion and protection of european norms and values. i would also like to point out that satellite capabilities can also be used to better assess and identify the flow of irregular migrants and their routes, as well as to identify the boarding areas on ships, so that we can intervene quickly and save lives. the copernicus space-based earth observation programme can help prevent conflict, promote humanitarian support and cooperation, and represent a major scientific advance.
in writing. ‒ in the current international context, deeply destabilised by terrorism and various armed conflicts, space programmes can become an important element of the defence and security policies of the member states. in particular, i believe that european aerospace expertise should also be used to monitor the ground and provide information on the location of strategic targets such as training camps for terrorist groups. the eu has developed an important satellite policy over the years and therefore systems such as copernicus and galileo could play a role in the common security and defence policy (csdp) and, thanks to their versatility, could also be used to identify the routes used by irregular migrants to identify boarding areas on ships and thus prevent further massacres in the mediterranean. however, activities in outer space need to be in line with an international code of conduct to enhance protection and sustainability in space. i share the european union's multilateral initiative in this regard, not only to protect space infrastructure but also to avoid the militarization of space, a risk which we must avoid. for the reasons stated above, i voted in favour of the report.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the deadline for the commission to adopt delegated acts for the establishment of scientific criteria for endocrine disruptors has been over for more than two and a half years. it was a clear, precise and unconditional obligation. however, as early as march 2013, an ad hoc scientific committee set up by the commission itself had made a comprehensive proposal on the scientific criteria based on three years of work by experts. however, the commission has never taken this into account because the commission, in open violation of european law and the treaties, felt the need to carry out an impact assessment, a socioeconomic impact assessment only, an absolutely inadequate instrument for deciding on a scientific issue affecting health and the environment. we cannot tolerate this arrogance of the commission for much longer. that reason fully supported the motion for a resolution voted today. parliament is a democratic expression of the will of the european citizens and it is its duty to condemn the commission for failing to fulfil its obligations and we ask that it be determined as soon as possible what is an endocrine disruptor or not, and only on the basis of sound scientific criteria. we must protect our citizens and above all we, their representatives, must do so.
in writing. ‒ the world health organisation has identified endocrine disruptors as a global threat, with particular reference to the increasing trend of many endocrine disorders in humans and animals. the hazardous nature of these chemicals would require rapid regulatory action to define scientific criteria for the determination of endocrine-disrupting properties. the commission, which was to have fulfilled this role by the end of 2013, did not do so, and the court of justice of the european union ruled last december that the commission had breached eu law by failing to adopt the appropriate delegated acts. the motion for a resolution which i have voted for today condemns the commission for its failure to comply with the directive and calls on it to submit scientific criteria for the determination of endocrine-disrupting properties by the summer, thus putting an end to this dangerous lack of legislation.
in writing. ‒ under the biocidal products regulation, the commission was required to adopt delegated acts by 13 december 2013 concerning the definition of scientific criteria for the determination of endocrine-disrupting properties of active substances and biocides. however, it has not yet adopted such acts, despite a judgment of the court of justice. this is scandalous and i certainly do not intend to support this resolution with my vote, which sounds like little more than a slight reproach from this parliament to the commission.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the resolution in question to condemn the commission's delay in publishing the scientific criteria needed to identify and reduce exposure to hormone-disrupting chemicals, which are considered a global threat by the world health organisation and the un environment programme (unep). the commission's continued delays in publishing those criteria, which were due to be made public by the end of 2013, constitute a breach of community law and its institutional obligations under the treaties. i would stress that, according to the judgment of the court of justice of the eu of 16 december 2015, the determination of these scientific criteria by the commission can only be made in an objective manner on the basis of scientific data relating to the endocrine system, independently of any other considerations, in particular of an economic nature. endocrine disruptors pose a danger to the health and well-being of citizens. the commission must start protecting european citizens, not the chemical industry.
in writing. ‒ the report aims to send an important political message to the european commission. the latter has not yet fulfilled its obligation to adopt specific criteria for the determination of endocrine-disrupting properties of active substances and biocides. the court of justice has also ruled on this failure. i therefore voted in favour of the report which expresses parliament's dissatisfaction with the commission's failings and calls on it to do its utmost to comply with eu law.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the european institutions must stand by the citizens and try to give maximum attention to their health. there are some active substances which are considered to have endocrine disrupting properties capable of producing harmful effects in humans and which are not, for obvious reasons, approved. however, more than 2 years after the expiry date, the commission has not yet adopted those acts concerning the definition of the scientific criteria. i therefore agree with this resolution, since there is no doubt that the commission has not yet complied with the judgment of the court of justice, and i hope that it will comply with its obligations as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ following the judgment of the court of justice where it is recognised that the commission had a clear and precise obligation to adopt delegated acts concerning the definition of scientific criteria for the detection of endocrine disruptors in the context of the implementation of the regulation on plant protection products and biocides, it is recognised that the above criteria are not yet in place. i therefore support the call on the commission to honour its commitment and i vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ regulation (eu) no 528/2012 required the commission to adopt delegated acts by 13 december 2013 concerning the establishment of scientific criteria for the determination of endocrine-disrupting properties of active substances and biocidal products. sweden, with the support of, inter alia, the european parliament, has sued the commission for failure to adopt those delegated acts. the court of justice of the european union has held that the commission has breached eu law in this area, has not yet complied with the judgment of the court of justice and continues to breach eu law. the judgment of the court of justice emphasises that the determination of scientific criteria must be made only in an objective manner on the basis of scientific data relating to the endocrine system. i, along with other members from various groups, had proposed that the juncker commission should be discredited: i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in this. the resolution voted today is less strong but has the merit of bringing together large and small groups and of sending a political signal to the commission that parliament still does not believe it has fulfilled its obligations as 'guardian of the treaties'.
in writing. this resolution, which i voted in favour of, condemns the european commission's delay in publishing the scientific criteria needed to identify and reduce exposure to chemicals that interfere with hormonal activities in humans and animals. the report of the united nations environment and world health organization calls endocrine disruptors a "global threat", referring to the trend of increasing numbers of endocrine disorders in humans and wildlife. it is considered that there is sufficient evidence to demonstrate the harmful effects on reproduction (infertility, tumours, malformations) caused by exposure to these substances, which could also affect the normal functioning of the thyroid gland and brain, and interfere with obesity, metabolism, insulin and glucose homeostasis. the european court of justice ruled in december 2015 that the eu executive had breached community law by failing to publish these criteria, which were supposed to be made public by the end of 2013 under community law. the commission is therefore guilty not only of failing to comply with the obligation to adopt scientific criteria but also of failing to comply with its institutional obligations as laid down in the eu treaties.
in writing. ‒ president juncker promised to democratize the process of marketing gmos. the authorisation concerns a transgenic maize resistant to two pesticides with active substances glufosinate and glyphosate. glyphosate in particular is a product that is potentially dangerous to human health and there is currently no consensus in the scientific community. that is why i voted in favour of the objection.
in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the objection to a commission delegated act authorising the placing on the market of foods, food ingredients and feed containing, consisting of, or produced from bt11 × mir162 × mir604 × ga21 maize. one of these maize contains the pat protein, which gives tolerance to herbicides and is found to be based on glyphosate, a substance considered to be a potential carcinogen by the international agency for research on cancer. in view of the potential health hazard, i therefore decided to vote in favour of the objection, reiterating the need for the commission to draw up as soon as possible a comprehensive proposal on gmos and gm-based feed in order to carefully assess the environmental and health impact of these technologies.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the objection to the authorisation of the placing on the market of genetically modified maize bt11 x mir162 x mir604 x ga21
in writing. ‒ the widespread use of gm products is a very worrying practice, which i believe needs to be carefully limited, because of the risk of significant adverse effects on natural ecosystems and human health resulting from their use. the gradual and growing use of gm crops is in fact the cause of an increase in the use of herbicides (such as glyphosate or glufosinate) which can seriously affect the delicate biological balance of nature, while threatening the human health of consumers. several authoritative studies have highlighted the high risk of carcinogenicity following the use of many herbicides (including glyphosate), a risk which increases significantly in the event of cultivation of gmo products. i therefore believe that the draft commission implementing decision authorising the placing on the market of products containing genetically modified maize and cloves should be strongly opposed. the commission has not received any comments from interested parties on the draft measures, which it considers to be a manifest error of assessment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the objection in question today, which calls on the commission to withdraw the draft implementing act authorising the placing on the market of products containing a particular type of genetically modified maize. i am of the opinion that as long as there are concerns about the harmful effects on health resulting from the consumption of food containing genetically modified organisms, the commission should not authorise the sale of such food. in these cases, the precautionary principle must always prevail because the primary objective of the european union is to protect the health of all citizens. the objection relates to the fact that the maize in question has been treated to tolerate glyphosate-based herbicides. a few months ago the european parliament voted in favour of another objection which opposed the renewal of the approval of the active substance itself on the basis of the opinion of the international agency for research on cancer which classified it as probably carcinogenic to humans. in the light of all these factors, i thought it appropriate to oppose the marketing of this maize.
in writing. ‒ the authorisation concerns a transgenic maize resistant to two pesticides with active ingredients glufosinate and glyphosate. the dangers of glyphosate are the subject of a controversy between the international agency for research on cancer (iarc) in lyon, which classifies it as a probable carcinogen, and efsa, which does not. the degradation products are also likely to interfere with the proper functioning of the endocrine system. i therefore oppose this authorization. the aim is to put pressure on the commission to come forward with a new proposal to democratize the process of marketing gmos as promised by mr junker at the beginning of his mandate.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i am in favour of stopping trade in this product. or at least i think the eu should act more consistently when it comes to gmos: it is not sensible for our domestic production to allow trade and not allow cultivation. until this inconsistency is resolved, i think it is appropriate that trade should not be allowed either.
in writing. ‒ i vote in favour of the resolution which challenges the placing on the market of a gmo.
in writing. ‒ the commission's draft authorisation concerns the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of or produced from genetically modified maize, resistant to two pesticides with active ingredients glufosinate and glyphosate. it should be noted that despite the divergent opinions on the matter, the international agency for research on cancer (iarc), part of the world health organization (who), has classified glyphosate as a probable human carcinogen. opposition to this and other gmo authorizations issued by the commission without the support of the majority of either the member states or the european parliament is intended as a form of protest against the current authorization system and an invitation to the commission to suspend the decision in the event that the technical committee does not issue a majority opinion. i therefore oppose this authorization as well, pending a substantial democratic change in the current system for the authorization of gmos.
in writing. ‒ president juncker promised during his election campaign to democratize the process of marketing gmos. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a directive on the protection of the environment against the dangers of ionising radiation. that is why i voted in favour of the objection.
