in writing. ‒ the widespread use of gm products is a very worrying practice, which i believe needs to be carefully limited, because of the risk of significant adverse effects on natural ecosystems and human health resulting from their use. the gradual and growing use of gm crops is in fact the cause of an increase in the use of herbicides (such as glyphosate or glufosinate) which can seriously affect the delicate biological balance of nature, while threatening the human health of consumers. several authoritative studies have highlighted the high risk of carcinogenicity following the use of many herbicides (including glyphosate), a risk which increases significantly in the event of cultivation of gmo products. i therefore believe that the draft commission implementing decision authorising the placing on the market of products containing genetically modified maize and cloves should be strongly opposed. the commission has not received any comments from interested parties on the draft measures, which it considers to be a manifest error of assessment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the objection in question today, which calls on the commission to withdraw the draft implementing act authorising the placing on the market of a particular type of genetically modified carnation. i believe that the precautionary principle must always prevail when environmental protection is at stake. the efsa studies state that the potential for pollen spread by lepidopterans of this particular type of carnation cannot be excluded and that its stems cut with vegetative shoots may spread into the environment by rooting or micropropagation. in addition, once their ornamental function is over, gm carnations become waste which, in accordance with the principles of the circular economy, can be disposed of by composting and used as fertilisers. in the light of all these factors, i have considered it appropriate to oppose the placing on the market of this carnation.
in writing. ‒ the authorisation in question concerns the marketing of a transgenic carnation intended for cut-up sale. although many of the reasons for opposing the risks posed by gmos are missing in this case, since these are cut flowers and not intended for human consumption, the request not to authorise the product remains a form of protest against the current authorisation system. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the trade in genetically modified carnations must be stopped. this trade is a major handicap for the main carnation-producing countries, such as italy and france. i do not think that this trade is fair, and it is a serious threat to small producers. they would find unfair competition because producers of gm carnations can benefit from high production at a much lower cost to the small business owner. carcinogens have also been found in the genetically modified carnation which could cause problems in humans and animals if consumed intentionally or accidentally.
in writing. ‒ i vote in favour of this resolution which is against the inclusion of a gmo.
in writing. ‒ the draft commission implementing decision concerns the placing on the market of a genetically modified carnation for ornamental purposes. from a substantive point of view, there are some problematic aspects. for example, once the ornamental function of carnations is over, they become waste which, in accordance with the principles of the circular economy, can be disposed of by composting. however, efsa has not yet examined the impact of these emissions on the environment, nor has it assessed the possible consequences for humans of the intentional consumption of carnations. from a formal point of view, opposition to this and other gmo authorizations issued by the commission without the support of the majority of either the member states or the european parliament is intended as a form of protest against the current authorization system and an invitation to the commission to suspend the decision in the event that the technical committee does not issue a majority opinion. for the reasons stated above, i am also opposed to this authorization and support this objection, hoping for a decisive democratic change in the current system of authorization of gmos.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this report on simplifying the presentation of public documents because the mobility of citizens of the union is a reality today which we must defend at all levels. some 12 million europeans study, work or live in a member state of which they are not nationals. citizens and businesses in the union already exercise their right to free movement or the freedoms of the internal market is the greatest success of a united europe but unfortunately they can still encounter administrative complications when they have to submit public documents to the authorities of another member state. we are talking, for example, about making life easier for students who deal with different administrative systems, for tourists who need the health system when they are travelling, and for european citizens who do not know but are subject to different tax systems. the free movement of citizens and businesses does not stop with the abolition of visas or border controls. it is the administrative practices that have an impact on daily life and this is what needs to be simplified.

in writing. article 41 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union guarantees the right of european citizens to good administration, through an open, efficient and independent administration. in a context of a gradual increase in the overall powers of the european institutions, the development of transparent and simple administration and bureaucratic practices should be encouraged and promoted. in this context, i call on the commission to examine carefully and promptly the proposal for a regulation tabled by colleagues heidi hautala and pavel svoboda on behalf of the committee on legal affairs, adopted in plenary on 9 june 2016, which is an interesting starting point that can improve the functioning of the bureaucratic practices and procedures of the european institutions, as well as guarantee the right of citizens to a fair, prompt and effective administration.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution today to remind the commission that in its resolution of 15 january 2013 parliament called for the adoption of a regulation for an open, efficient and independent administration of the european union. although the resolution was adopted by a large majority (572 votes in favour, 16 against, 12 abstentions), parliament's request was not followed up by any action by the commission. with the development of the european union's competences, citizens are increasingly confronted directly with the union's institutions, bodies and agencies, but too often they do not receive adequate answers. over the years, the european union has developed a large number of sectoral administrative procedures, in the form of binding and non-binding provisions, without necessarily taking into account the overall coherence of the system and the need for transparency, particularly towards european citizens. this complex set of different procedures results in gaps and inconsistencies between the procedures themselves. today's vote was essentially a call on the commission to propose, in the general interest, a regulation to make the union's administration more efficient and open. citizens have the right to expect a high level of transparency, efficiency, speed of implementation and responsiveness from the union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.

in writing. ‒ the resolution on the competitiveness of the european rail industry is balanced and acceptable. it is essential for our smes operating in third countries to be able to obtain greater access to credit in order to ensure the necessary competitiveness on the market, and it is equally important for the eu to strengthen supervision of non-european investments made in the member states. for all these reasons i have voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ studies show that rail interoperability and safety is a central element of the sustainable development model for the europe of the future. to improve them, the european railway agency (era) was established by regulation (ec) no 881/2004 of 29 april 2004, with offices in lille and valenciennes (france). the agency shall promote the progressive harmonisation, registration and monitoring of technical specifications for interoperability (tsis) across the european rail system and the development of common safety objectives for european railways. although the era does not have autonomous decision-making powers, it contributes to drafting proposals for decisions for the european commission. regulation (ec) no 1335/2008 of 16 december 2008 has conferred new tasks on the era, which are related to the amendments to the directives on railway safety (2004/49/ec) and on the interoperability of the rail system (2008/57/ec). now, with the adoption of the fourth railway package, the era's powers of investigation and audit in its fields of competence will finally be strengthened. this will help to avoid having 28 different systems for the type approval of trains: the agency will act as a single point of contact for issuing authorisations for vehicles intended for cross-border operations and safety certificates to railway undertakings operating in different eu states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution today to remind the commission that in its resolution of 15 january 2013 parliament called for the adoption of a regulation for an open, efficient and independent administration of the european union. although the resolution was adopted by a large majority (572 votes in favour, 16 against, 12 abstentions), parliament's request was not followed up by any action by the commission. with the development of the european union's competences, citizens are increasingly confronted directly with the union's institutions, bodies and agencies, but too often they do not receive adequate answers. over the years, the european union has developed a large number of sectoral administrative procedures, in the form of binding and non-binding provisions, without necessarily taking into account the overall coherence of the system and the need for transparency, particularly towards european citizens. this complex set of different procedures results in gaps and inconsistencies between the procedures themselves. today's vote was essentially a call on the commission to propose, in the general interest, a regulation to make the union's administration more efficient and open. citizens have the right to expect a high level of transparency, efficiency, speed of implementation and responsiveness from the union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
in writing. ‒ the european rail industry employs 400 000 people in europe. while i am concerned about the slow pace of payments to smes in the european railway industry, i would point out that the report by my colleague martina werner asks the commission to monitor the proper implementation of the eu directive on late payment and therefore i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the european rail industry provides more than two million jobs for eu citizens and accounts for almost half of the world market for the rail industry. i think that we should pay close attention to this area, which i believe is very important for europe. as it is difficult and costly for many companies to operate across national borders because of the fragmentation of the market, i am convinced that the creation of a single european railway area can be the solution to these problems. i also think it is appropriate to mobilise the european union's funding instruments and private research funds so that we can continue to invest in research and development. this will enable the best possible development of railway technologies and maintain the world leadership of the european railway industry. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the competitiveness of european industry should be boosted by the full, effective and uniform implementation of the regulation on the european rail network for competitive freight transport, which is beneficial for both passengers and industry. in addition, efforts should be made to remove the main non-tariff barriers to the european railway industry's access to foreign markets, including obstacles to investment, discrimination and lack of transparency in public procurement procedures.
in writing. ‒ the railway industry is a strategic sector for the european industrial recovery. it employs 400 000 people, invests 2.7% of its annual turnover in research and development and represents 46% of the world market for the railway industry. in the light of these data, i believe, in line with what was adopted in the resolution, that concrete measures and investments can be put in place to achieve the objectives of modal shift towards rail transport, both for passengers and for freight, as announced in the 2011 transport white paper. moreover, in view of the conditions which are essential for the competitiveness of the european railway industry, such as the capacity for innovation, the creation of clusters and investment in research and development, i believe that the commission should take account in the near future of the measures and initiatives developed by the european parliament, and in particular: the full and more efficient mobilisation of all european funding instruments, especially for the benefit of smes operating in the sector; the establishment of a european forum bringing together innovative enterprises, start-ups and spin-offs in the railway sector; targeted investment in innovation and digitalisation of rail services, including the integrated electronic ticketing system.
in writing. ‒ as many as 400 000 people are employed in the railway industry in europe, an industry that covers 46% of the needs of the entire world railway market. however, europe is in danger of losing market share due to the import of low-cost rail supplies from non-european countries such as china and the lack of a coherent trade policy. while the european union market is largely open to competitors from third countries, they do not give up barriers that discriminate against the european rail industry, operating unfair competition that puts jobs at risk. in this resolution we asked the commission to include provisions to improve market access in third countries in future trade agreements and in the revision of existing ones. it will also be appropriate to develop an industrial policy that promotes sustainable transport, supports innovation in the railway sector, including small and medium-sized enterprises, and allows for the training of specialised staff. i believe that these elements, contained in the resolution i supported, are essential if the european railway industry is to remain competitive on the world stage.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the motion for a resolution because it underlines the importance of the railway industry (iff) in the process of reindustrialising europe.
in writing. ‒ recognising the importance of the european rail industry for employment, innovation and r & d and the contribution it can make to boosting european competitiveness, i would support my group's line on the proposal under consideration.
in writing. ‒ the european rail supply industry (iff) is a world leader, with 46% of the global rail industry market. it employs 400 000 people and makes a significant contribution to investment in research and innovation. the railway sector as a whole employs over one million workers and 1.2 million in the industry. these figures clearly illustrate the importance of the iff for industrial growth, employment and innovation, also considering the objective of reindustrialising 20% of the european economy. competitors from third countries, in particular china, are expanding rapidly and aggressively, often with the political and financial support of their home countries. it is therefore important that europe should be able to guarantee a level playing field in world competition, in order to safeguard jobs and industrial know-how. to maintain the global dominance of the european iff, it will be essential to create a single european railway area, launch innovation programmes, encourage the formation of local clusters, make the best use of the structural and investment funds, support smes and boost demand for rail products. in order to make it future-proof, it will also be important to invest in the training of young workers in the sector. this report shares this approach and calls on the commission to do its part, and i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the european iff (rail supply industry) comprises the production of locomotives, rolling stock and tracks, electrification, signalling and telecommunications equipment, as well as maintenance and spare parts services. it employs 400 000 people, invests 2.7% of its annual turnover in research and development and accounts for 46% of the world market for the railway industry. the rail sector as a whole, including operators and infrastructure, accounts for over 1 million direct jobs and 1.2 million indirect jobs in the eu. the increase in imports of low-cost railway supplies (such as engines or signals) from non-eu countries such as china is undermining the conditions for the competitiveness of european suppliers. hence the need for a trade strategy which guarantees respect for the principle of reciprocity, particularly in relation to japan, china and the united states. i voted in favour of new legislation to allow the eu to respond more quickly and effectively to dumped and subsidised imports, in view of the possible change in the administration of the eu anti-dumping law for china from december 2016 and the huge 'human costs' for eu workers due to the current crisis in the steel sector.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the competitiveness of the european railway industry, which is at the heart of the transition to sustainable mobility. the railway industry in the european union is a sector characterised by a high presence of smes. the competitiveness of this sector, especially in the face of the strong and often unfair competition from third countries, requires investment in innovation. in this regard, the eu has launched a joint technology initiative programme which has encountered a number of obstacles in the launch process. the resolution we have adopted may be a further step in the right direction.
in writing. ‒ the european rail industry (eri) is a key sector for the eu's competitiveness and innovation capacity, employing 400 000 people and some 2.2 million workers, both direct and indirect, if the rail sector as a whole is taken into account. despite the good environmental performance that the sector is able to offer and the great capacity to transport large volumes, there are still competition problems. while the european union is open to competitors from other countries, the latter have adopted barriers which discriminate against the iff, in particular china, which is expanding rapidly and aggressively thanks to the political and financial support of its own country, thus putting jobs in europe at risk. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution because it calls for fairer conditions of competition in the world through reciprocal access to markets. we also call on the commission to work with the railway sector to ensure more effective use of the european structural investment funds (esi funds) and in particular the european regional development fund (erdf), while seeking to simplify business procedures for smes and to remove all tariff and non-tariff barriers.
in writing. ‒ the motion for a resolution on the competitiveness of the european railway industry, tabled by martina werner, a member of the socialist and democratic group, was voted in favour. investing in the railway sector today is a necessity from many points of view: the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the transport of dangerous goods, which is a matter of urgency. i particularly appreciate the fact that this proposal aims at an integrated electronic ticketing system, so as to facilitate the movement of workers and tourists in europe, and that it considers the railway sector, which is currently in a state of shortage of qualified personnel, as an opportunity for young european engineers.
in writing. ‒ the european rail industry plays a very important role in achieving the decarbonisation targets of the transport sector. although still largely dependent on public investment, smes are central to the supply of railway equipment and technology, which is essential for the modernisation and efficiency of rail passenger and freight transport. but it is necessary to recognise the danger posed by non-european companies financed by third countries such as china and to protect european companies from unfair competition by creating a market with a level playing field, preserving european industrial know-how so as to protect existing jobs and create new ones.
member of the commission. – mr president, i would like to express my thanks to the seven remaining meps here, and, of course, to you. i feel very lonely tonight. but this issue is very important and i would like to remind all our colleagues here that at the hearing, a year and a half ago, i committed myself to work in order to enhance and deepen inter-institutional cooperation. i never forget that i am a parliamentarian myself, and the fact that i am from the other side does not mean that i do not share all these views expressed here today. this debate allows the commission to understand better where members of this house see the need for improving the information about negotiations for international agreements. first vice-president timmermans, as the commissioner in charge of that, will represent the commission in order to engage, together with the european parliament and the council, in a reflection on how to better implement parliament’s rights, under the treaty of course: the right to be fully and immediately informed at all stages of international negotiations. but let me also remind you that the obligation to inform parliament on international negotiations falls on both the commission and the council. moreover, we cannot disregard or circumvent the need to protect confidential or classified information related to international obligations or interinstitutional agreements. i would like once again to thank you for your contribution to this debate, and for your attention, and to wish you a nice weekend.
president of the state of israel. – mr president, madam vice-president of the commission/ high representative of the union, honourable members, my wife nechama, ladies and gentlemen, with your permission i will speak my words in hebrew. (official translation of president rivlin’s speech, which was delivered in hebrew) a mere four hours: that is the flight time from tel-aviv to brussels. i could say that four hours, and light years, separate brussels and tel-aviv, but in truth there is not much difference between them, be it in awareness or in essence: two cosmopolitan cities, practically neighbours, not far from each other, both recently struck by a wave of terrorism. seated here are many delegates from numerous european countries. some share the mediterranean sea with us, all share a rich and painful history with the jewish people. about a month ago, the leaders of europe marked 100 years since the battle of verdun, the longest battle of world war i, with 900 000 casualties, including 300 000 fatalities. some half a million jewish soldiers served in the armies of the countries at war, often poised against each other, firing upon each other. but this ‘patriotic bloodletting’ did not bestow any privilege on the jewish people. quite the contrary: jews in every country were accused of spying and treason. germany started a ‘head-count’ of jewish soldiers. in eastern europe, jews were accused of bolshevism and of anti-bolshevism. it is estimated that more than 170 000 jewish soldiers were killed in world war i, and around 100 000 more were murdered in post-war pogroms. that horrible war, world war i, was the herald of the ‘exodus’ of the jewish people from europe. many jews saw in the united states of america their new home. others, zionist leaders, shaken and shocked from having had to face their own jewish brothers as foes on the battlefield, took action to fulfil the dream of a national home for the jewish people, in its ancient and eternal homeland, the land of israel. from where we stand today, the great war was but a promo to a much more horrendous war that followed suit: world war ii. in world war ii, the annihilation of the jewish people was a defined target of the axis powers headed by nazi germany. the second ‘european exodus’ of the jewish people occurred upon the defeat of the third reich. this was a traumatic emigration: one of refugees and agony, of a culture destroyed, of a people which lost one third of its sons and daughters. distinguished audience, even the wildest of imaginations could not have foreseen a course of events in which an ancient people returned from years of exile and rebuilt its historic homeland. a wild imagination could neither have foreseen such a convoluted historic course of events in which an utterly torn and bleeding continent, awash with the blood of war and strife, would have paved the way to a joint european parliament. and yes, no less important are the solid, steadfast ties created between us: ties embodied today in a wide array of joint ventures and cooperation, in research and innovation, in health and the environment, education and culture and many more areas. regardless of the perspective from which we look at this – our past, our present or the future we are awaiting – we intrinsically linked, israel and europe, in an unbreakable bond. just as humanity could not be what it is without europe, so europe could not be what it is without the jewish people. it would be difficult to imagine what humanity would have been like without plato, thomas aquinas, galileo galilei, martin luther or marie curie, just as it would be difficult to imagine what europe would be without maimonides, spinoza, freud or einstein. our common interests – and, moreover, our common values – dictate our present and shape our future. liberty, equality, justice, pluralism and religious tolerance, democracy: these are the basic tenets inscribed in israel’s declaration of independence. these are the constitutive values of the european union. the european union, and within it this distinguished parliament, is an audacious endeavour of politics and statehood. tomorrow this endeavour will be put to a complex test in the united kingdom, while, day in day out, it stands the test of refugees and migration on a historic scale. the state of israel too is an audacious endeavour of statehood, of a people returning to its land after two thousand years of exile. and, just like you, israel faces difficult and complex challenges. but unlike europe, which embarked upon a process of removing partitions between nations and states, israel wishes, and indeed must, remain first and foremost a national homeland, a safe haven for the jewish people. the state of israel is by no means a compensation for the holocaust, but the holocaust has posited as a basic tenet the necessity and vitality of the return of the jewish people to history, as a nation taking its fate in its own hands. i feel that the massive criticism aimed at israel in europe stems from, inter alia, a misunderstanding and an impatience toward this existential need of the jewish nation and the state of israel. on the other hand, and much to my regret, israel has a growing sense of impatience when it comes to europe. there are those who feel anger and frustration toward certain european actions, vis-à-vis what they perceive as sometimes unfair criticism, sometimes even contaminated by elements of condescension and, some would say, double standards. my european friends, we cannot agree on everything, but, as friends and as true allies, i call upon you and ask you: let us be patient. please respect the israeli considerations, even when different from your own. respect israel’s sovereignty and the democratic process of its decision-making. respect israel’s staunch commitment, indeed its very duty, to protect its citizens. for us it is the most sacred commandment of all. a few years ago, a french friend turned to me and said: ‘if we and the germans have made peace and put an end to conflict once and for all – and, believe me, what happened between us and them overshadows any other conflict i can think of – then there is no reason for you not to succeed.’ he continued: ‘how long have you and the arabs been fighting, all in all? one hundred years? fifty years? we have been fighting for a thousand years, and now it is over, forever.’ this is what he said to me. i am standing here today and saying in no uncertain manner: from 1993, the year in which the oslo accords were signed, the elected israeli leadership has been – as it still is – in support of the solution of ‘two-states for two peoples’. furthermore, being well versed in the israeli parliament, i know that any political agreement brought before the israeli knesset by an elected government will be approved. nevertheless, and with all the difficulty and pain involved, we must look reality straight in the eye and tell the truth. currently the practical conditions, the political and regional circumstances, which would enable us to reach a permanent agreement between us – the israelis and the palestinians – are failing to materialise. first, in order to achieve a comprehensive permanent agreement, an effective leadership is required. however, the palestinian leadership today is divided in (at least) two: the palestinian authority ruling over judea and samaria and, on the other hand, hamas, which rules gaza and is ideologically committed – in both its political and its military leadership – to the annihilation of israel. second, in order to achieve a stable and viable agreement, a reasonable regional and economic infrastructure is required. but we are living in a reality where the plague of murderous jihadi fundamentalism, religious fanaticism and incitement – embodied in the islamic state and hezbollah – are at our very borders and have not missed out gaza and the west bank either. we live in a reality of a chaos-stricken middle east in which uncertainty is the only certainty. to this worrisome picture, add the dire economic straits, poverty and lack of infrastructure in gaza and judea and samaria, which in turn will continue the destabilisation and nurture violence. in this respect, israel is making, and will continue to make, vast efforts: more than any other actor in the region, and even at the price of complex security risk-taking. but israeli intervention alone will not suffice. finally, one should bear in mind the most fundamental trait of israeli-palestinian relations today, which is, to my deep regret, a total lack of trust between the parties on all levels; between the leaderships and the peoples. i am afraid that, for years, the international community has been acting as a mediator between the parties based on one inflexible paradigm, that of striving to renew negotiations toward a permanent agreement. this paradigm leads to a dichotomy: ‘two states or a bi-national state’, ‘all or nothing’, ‘here and now or nevermore’. it is, by the way, by virtue of that same paradigm that various european states opposed the peace agreement between israel and egypt, claiming that it does not provide a solution for the israeli-palestinian conflict. had that concept been accepted then, imagine where we would be today. this paradigm relies on the assumption that the problem which is the crux of the matter in this bloody and painful conflict is simply the lack of good faith on both sides, and that, if only pressure is exerted on ‘them’ and on ‘us’, they will adhere to a permanent agreement and to a state of peace. however, as years go by and rounds of negotiations fail one by one, bringing in their wake waves of murderous violence and terror, it seems that this assumption of a ‘lack of good will’ is proving not only to be fundamentally erroneous but also to ignore the circumstances, the capabilities, and the present situation on the ground. and that, by definition, would lead to the failure of any attempt to negotiate a permanent agreement. ladies and gentlemen, i speak before you today in the name of the citizens of israel, grandfathers and grandmothers, fathers and mothers, sick and tired of this bloody vicious cycle which soaks up the blood of our loved ones, the blood of our sons and daughters. i speak before you in the name of these young men and women who wish to live in their country, and not die in their homeland. i speak to you today in the name of a nation that abhors war and desires life and peace. and, i must say, one cannot hope to achieve better results while resorting to the same outlooks and tools that have previously failed time after time. the french initiative, adopted by the eu institutions only a few days ago, suffers from those very fundamental faults. the attempt to return to negotiations for negotiations’ sake not only does not bring us near the long-awaited solution, but rather drags us further away from it. this striving for a permanent agreement ‘now’, is the chronicle of a predictable failure, which will only push the two peoples deeper into despair. this despair is the hottest bed for extremism, and undermines the endeavours of moderates. and this despair, ladies and gentlemen, today seizes not just members of my generation but also boys and girls growing up in this part of the world, whose worldview and awareness are shaped by the violent present. this despair is the gravest danger looming over us, israelis and palestinians alike. if the international community really wishes and truly aspires to be a constructive player, it must divert its efforts away from the renewal of negotiations for negotiations’ sake, and toward building trust between the parties and creating the necessary terms for the success of negotiations in the future. in the current circumstances, we must all ask ourselves ‘what can be done today?’ rather than ‘what cannot be done?’ and things can be done. this mission of creating the terms for a future agreement, creating an infrastructure for trust, and for a life of dignity for both peoples, demands of us today – the international community and israel alike – that we invest tremendous efforts in four main avenues. the first is harnessing the moderate powers in the region. the cooperation with jordan and egypt is a supreme common interest of israel and the international community as well, with the aim of preventing military build-ups beyond our borders, and in order to eradicate extremism and preserve the stability of the region. similarly, the involvement and effective guaranties of friendly states in the region may also reduce the violent friction and serve as a warranty for future action. the second avenue is developing palestinian economy and infrastructures for quality of life. one cannot speak about a future agreement when people live with a basic existential feeling of having no future, no opportunities, no hope and no horizon. with the backdrop of economic difficulties in judea and samaria, and the situation in gaza, a broad economic course of action is called for. infrastructures must be developed – gas, electricity, water, sewerage and housing – in gaza and judea and samaria. at the same time, a solution must be found to the human tragedy in gaza – whereby around 1.5 million palestinians are held hostage by a jihadist terrorist organisation, hamas – just as solutions must be found to the movement of residents, the transfer of trade and the enabling the appropriate security. on this issue, the state of israel has repeatedly stated its willingness to join hands with the international community in a joint endeavour. israel considers the rehabilitation of gaza and the economic development and equalising of standards of life on both the palestinian and israeli sides to be both an ethical and a security interest. sources of livelihood and employment must be developed too, as israeli and international companies that identify the potential of investing in the human capital between the jordan and the sea, have already begun to do. the development of a stable palestinian economy must be carried out, laying the emphasis on developing a real, independent and vital private sector as a stabilising factor free of political interests. furthermore, developing the economy must take into account the need for developing infrastructures for quality of life, for a life of dignity and wellbeing. rawabi, the first planned palestinian city ever built in the palestinian authority, is a model of the power and significance of basic wellbeing in creating a breathing space and a feeling of movement and progress. the third avenue is investing in joint ventures aimed at creating joint interests. whether we wish it or not, we – israelis and palestinians – share a small and common area, with common regional resources and assets, and common regional challenges. together, we live on what is equal to one third of austria. in such small and crowded space, creating common interests is a crucial factor in strengthening stability, and in creating the terms needed to replace the next war with programmes benefiting both parties. we should foster and promote joint israeli-palestinian development ventures in the fields of renewable energy, infrastructure and the environment, joint industrial and tourism ventures and cultural and social ventures: between israeli and palestinian local authorities, and between private corporations and business people on both sides. for instance, the ecological park being developed through cooperation between the regional council of gilboa and the palestinian city of jenin, with the support of the international community, in which the shared kishon river is undergoing cleaning and purification processes, with the aim of providing a solution to one of the most complex issues of the conflict – the water problem. you, ladies and gentlemen, know better than i do how joint ventures create a horizon for another reality. fourthly and ultimately there is the avenue of education. increasing stability, developing infrastructures and strategic terms are essential conditions, but are not enough. creating the conditions for any future agreement requires conditioning hearts on both sides for the possibility of living with mutual respect. peace is made between leaders but peace is also made between peoples. changing present trends requires addressing deep-rooted hatred and fear. otherwise fear will have the upper hand, if only because it is, to our regret, much more tangible than hope. building trust demands an investment in the creation of wide channels of communication, not only in security contexts but also in academic, cultural, and governance contexts – and, at the same time, educating future generations to become acquainted with our neighbours, their culture and language. distinguished audience, the state of israel values the efforts invested by the international community in general, and by the european union in particular, in seeking a peaceful future between the parties. the responsibility for building trust between us and our neighbours rests, first and foremost, on the shoulders of the two parties. but if europe is interested in serving as a constructive factor in striving for a future agreement it will be incumbent upon you, its leaders, to focus efforts at this time in a patient and methodical building of trust: not through divestments, but through investment; not by boycotts, but by cooperation. it is no easy task for me to stand here before you today and say that, at this time, a permanent agreement for peace between us and the palestinians cannot be achieved – because, first and foremost, i stand before the israeli people, before my children and grandchildren, before the israeli and palestinian children wherever they are. it is to them that i and we, and all of us, are to be held accountable: to ask ourselves what we have actually done to promise them, someday, another future? i believe in the capability of both these peoples to live with each other, for the simple reason that we have no other choice. if we desire life, we must, today, invest our utmost efforts in what can be achieved, not in that which cannot – for the sake of our future, and that of our children. i would like to thank my friend, the president of the european parliament, martin schulz, for the invitation to come here, in the same week as the president of the palestinian authority, mahmoud abbas. there can be no substitute for direct and joint conversation. in this act you have taken a step, albeit small, to bolster trust between the parties. distinguished audience, 100 years ago the thought of a joint european parliament was inconceivable. cooperation in the fields of electricity, gas and coal started this miracle of a europe living in peace with itself. small steps created a great reality. help us step forward, step together with us, for the sake of the possibility that one day, an israeli president will tell another world leader: ‘if we and the palestinians have made peace and put an end to conflict once and for all, there is really no reason whatsoever that you cannot succeed. we fought for many dozens of years and now it is over, forever.’ on behalf of the people in israel, i wish all europe’s muslims, and the muslim believers throughout the entire world, ramadan karim, kul am wa antum bikhair. ladies and gentlemen, ‘pray for the peace of jerusalem, may all who love her prosper. peace be within thy walls and prosperity within thy palaces. for my brethren and companions’ sake, i will now say, peace be within thee.’ (psalm 122, 6-8). god bless you all. on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. – mr president, this house has adopted a number of resolutions on the situation in the democratic republic of congo (drc), and more specifically on the situation in the eastern border areas, including the kivus. we are all aware of the shocking violence which has been reported since last autumn, especially in north kivu. some localities have been especially badly affected. the number of dead in beni territory alone is estimated by civil society sources at over 550 since september 2014. in addition, tens of thousands of people have been displaced. naturally, the eu’s immediate priority is humanitarian access, and we call once again for a stop to the targeting and kidnapping of humanitarian workers. i recall, of course, that when serving the needs of afflicted populations, the european commission humanitarian aid office (echo) acts in accordance with the principles laid down in council regulation (ec) no 1257/96, notably those of impartiality and non-discrimination. the recent violence has been made possible by an ongoing absence of state control. institutions and services to deal with the prevention and elimination of violence, and legal action against those responsible, are missing. regrettably, state-building activities in drc are also held back by the current uncertainty over the organisation of elections, which are due this year under the constitution. another aspect which continues to be relevant is the exploitation by armed groups of both wildlife and mineral natural resources. the recent report by the united nations group of experts on the drc underlines the ongoing involvement of the lord’s resistance army in poaching, and also draws particular attention to the laundering by armed groups of gold into the supply chain and onto the international market. it is of some consolation that armed groups have had fewer opportunities to benefit from illegal involvement in tin, tungsten and tantalum, thanks to due diligence and traceability systems. the eu will continue its effort to address the natural resources dimension of the great lake region stabilisation effort. while understanding the root causes of violence and instability is important, it does not excuse perpetrators, who must submit to the rule of law. this applies equally to incitement of violence and hate speech. it is individuals, not entire communities or ethnic groups, who must account for their actions. as has been stated many times before in this house, the activities of armed groups in eastern drc are an affront to citizens, undermining their human and legal rights, holding back development, destroying peace of mind and, in short, making it difficult to plan ahead or to think of the future. for armed groups to be put out of action, an effective and operational level of cooperation between the congolese armed forces and the un stabilisation mission in the democratic republic of the congo (monusco) is needed, and it is needed quickly. an agreement in principle was realised in february, but it needs to be put into practice. the justice angle is also important. as a supporter of both civil and military justice reform in drc, the eu insists that those found to be assisting or conspiring with armed groups must be prosecuted. as regards serious atrocities committed in eastern drc, we encourage the exploration of all legal options for the investigation and prosecution of those crimes. the primary responsibility for investigating and prosecuting lies with the state where the crime took place or the state where the perpetrator is a national. the eu will continue to offer assistance to the drc to assure structures are established and backed up with strong legislative frameworks in order to enable this. i want to turn now to the broader but critical issue of governance. with elections due in only a few months, drc finds itself at a key moment. un security council resolution 2277 (2016) is a starting point for all of us. this resolution was adopted unanimously in march. it underlines the primary and everyone was against us. and yet in italy, after only ten years, the same people are now telling us: "you were right, hang in there, keep going, represent hope". the wind of change that we then boldly proposed is now blowing strongly in our country. perhaps you have sensed it too. but we, ladies and gentlemen, do not want to stop in italy, we want to bring the utopia of change to europe, to these rooms, to all the member states. energy is the topic of today. we want the union to set binding targets of 40% for energy efficiency and at least 30% for renewables, translated into specific national targets. we want to see a chapter on prosumers, which will no longer leave them to the dancing moods of the various governments, and we want to see a common definition of the term, the rights to self-production, self-consumption, storage and sale of excess energy, forms of support, investment and the elimination of the main administrative and market barriers. we simply want the energy union to be truly citizen-centred and to enable europeans to escape the constraints of energy geopolitics once and for all. we want to respect the paris agreement and leave fossil fuels in the ground, the only guarantee to avoid climate catastrophe. none of us can predict today's vote and especially our future, but we know for sure that nature is giving us signals: floods, droughts, migration, competition for resources. it will be technological innovation and social innovation that will bring about the necessary changes. politics and economics will have to, sooner or later, willingly or unwillingly, bend their heads to change and adapt to the facts. that is a certainty, because it has always been so. but we do not want, as europe and as humanity, to be late. we have to be the flywheel, the human flywheel... (the president cut off the speaker)
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the debate on renewable energy and energy efficiency is a debate which is very passionate and unfortunately often has a strong potential for rhetorical decay, so that many of my colleagues sometimes take very strong positions and are very much concerned with environmental protection when they speak in this house and then perhaps they are invited to a conference organized by the steel industry in an eastern country and in that place, after saying that we must protect the environment, they say that jobs come first. so we have to find a balance, a point of balance that these two relationships are trying to reach. but beware of some risks. the first: europe has historically achieved excellent levels of sustainability in the context of economic development that also protects the environment, without the need for a gun to the head. he did it because it's in our entrepreneurial culture -- with the good will of the opponents of liberal culture -- to build a development model around humans, sure with flaws, but that's the way our entrepreneurs work. so be careful to impose absolute constraints on individual countries, because in europe we have countries like my own, italy, which can comply with those constraints without any problems, but we also have other countries which are trying to start over with difficulty. so let us give europe a reasoning which is capable of speaking of true sustainability, that is, investment that is sustained over time. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the five star movement considers it essential to move quickly away from reliance on fossil fuels in order to facilitate widespread self-production and self-sufficiency in energy based on renewable sources. the european union's commitment to reducing co2 emissions, but also the urgency of taking action to drastically reduce the level of pollutants such as heavy metals and dioxins in the air, water and soil, should oblige all states to put in place effective measures in a timely manner. it's about our health and our environment, but it's also about our financial resources, given the health and social costs of an environment devastated by our dependence on fossil fuels like oil, coal and gas. a major effort is needed to ensure that the transition is rapid, and this can be supported by research, innovation and the effective and efficient use of all available european funds to increase energy efficiency and renewable energy production. this effort should not be held back, as we have unfortunately seen in countries like mine, by so-called structural reforms which in fact translate into policies of...
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the current combination of binding national targets, national action plans for renewable energy and biennial monitoring has been the driving force behind the development of renewable energy production capacity in the member states. the commission should, however, ensure full implementation of the 2020 renewable energy targets and should present an ambitious regulatory framework for the period afterwards. in this regard, a stable long-term regulatory framework is needed, including renewable energy targets at national and union level. the production of electricity from renewable sources should be integrated into distribution systems. unfortunately, in many member states the networks are simply unsuitable to receive electricity generated from variable renewable sources. a modernisation of energy networks is therefore essential. it is therefore essential to achieve our energy efficiency objectives by moving away from fossil fuels and phasing out subsidies for these fuels.
in writing. ‒ every infringement of eu law and every case of money laundering or tax evasion must be punished and sanctioned as swiftly as possible. the maintenance of a democratic system depends on the respect of the rules and the capacity of its institutions to act: we are all called, ethically and politically, to act so that the union enforces the rules and prosecutes those who break them.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the appointment of the members of the parliamentary committee of inquiry which will be responsible for investigating alleged cases of breaches and maladministration in the application of union law in relation to money laundering, tax evasion and avoidance. the european parliament decided to set up this committee in the wake of the panama papers scandal, the millions of documents leaked to the international media that allegedly revealed the existence of a gigantic pool of money being diverted from international law firms and banks to tax havens on behalf of political leaders, criminals, intelligence officials and sports and entertainment vips. the documents refer to transactions dating from 1977 to the end of 2015, and if confirmed, would offer a new look at the handling of large cash flows through the global financial system.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposed appointments to the commission of inquiry into alleged cases of breaches and maladministration in the application of eu law in relation to money laundering, tax evasion and avoidance.
in writing. ‒ tax evasion does not only affect the economic and financial sphere of our societies: it is about equity and the political and social balances of our countries. in fact, tax evasion and avoidance in europe costs between 50 and 70 billion euros each year. the panama papers have shed light on the extra-european dimension of the phenomenon: more than 200,000 companies, 550 banks and 14,000 customers are suspected of evading or avoiding taxes and laundering money. this kind of behaviour and practices are no longer acceptable. the s&d group therefore called for the creation of a parliamentary committee of inquiry to investigate whether existing european legislation is adequate to deal with the phenomenon. the committee's tasks include drawing up the necessary recommendations to improve the existing legislative framework not only on tax avoidance but also on money laundering, including to see whether action will be needed to amend european legislation. it will also be an opportunity to investigate whether states have implemented existing directives and to check how the commission has acted towards eu states to effectively enforce the existing body of legislation. i therefore voted in favour of the composition of the committee of inquiry.
in writing. ‒ in response to the recent panama papers scandals, the fight against tax evasion and avoidance is proving to be a priority. to this end, all measures must be taken to reduce these situations as much as possible and to ensure greater fiscal justice. the establishment of the parliamentary committee of inquiry to investigate alleged cases of breach and maladministration in the application of union law in relation to money laundering, tax evasion and avoidance, i believe, can help to achieve this. that is why i voted for its constitution. this committee is just one of the instruments at european level and will be alongside the other measures adopted by the commission in the field of taxation. in twelve months' time we will produce a report which will examine complaints about member states' failure to comply with taxation and state aid rules, as well as the commission's failures to ensure that the relevant legislation is properly applied at national level. it is essential that there be loyal cooperation between the member states and this committee of inquiry will ensure that certain injustices are properly combated.
in writing. ‒ i thank the s&d group and all my colleagues for the confidence they have shown in me by nominating me as a member of the new special committee of inquiry to examine allegations of money laundering, tax evasion and tax avoidance. i will be committed to ensuring that the events known as the 'panama papers' are properly investigated, with the aim of ensuring the utmost transparency about the facts and preventing the recurrence of new cases of circumvention and evasion to the detriment of citizens and growth.
in writing. ‒ in favour of the 'nominations for the commission of inquiry into alleged contraventions and maladministration in the application of union law in relation to money laundering, tax evasion and avoidance'. this is certainly one of the priorities which the european union cannot ignore as it concerns the protection of all those citizens who comply with the regulations and pay taxes. being able to identify instances of maladministration reduces waste, increases the efficiency of the system and instills confidence in our european citizens, and that is precisely the aim.
in writing. ‒ in view of the process of association of the republic of lebanon with the european union, parliament called for the conclusion of a protocol to facilitate the participation of the partner country in european programmes. the text, in line with the neighbourhood policies, aims to put in place all the necessary measures to support lebanon in achieving the objectives and standards laid down in the union. by establishing fruitful cooperation with lebanon, the eu will be able to assist the new partner in the transition and harmonisation process. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the mănescu report approving the protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement establishing an association between the european community and its member states, of the one part, and the lebanese republic, of the other part. this is an important text which sets out a framework agreement between the eu and lebanon on the general principles for the participation of the lebanese republic in union programmes. this vote strengthens the neighbourhood policy by responding to two requirements: on the one hand, it will meet the 2013 demand of the middle eastern state for closer ties with the union, and on the other hand, it will strengthen the reform processes and the stability of a country which, occupying a strategic position in a highly vulnerable area, is a key ally in the fight against daesh and islamic terrorism. the framework agreement specifically defines a set of technical and financial rules to ensure lebanon's access to a wide range of eu programmes.
in writing. ‒ i find the manescu report unbalanced and not to be shared, so i did not intend to support it with my vote.
in writing. ‒ economic aid in exchange for democratic reforms and civil progress is one of the eu's most widely used instruments in its neighbourhood and partnership relations with third countries. this has often produced positive results for the citizens of both sides and has increased the range of influence of the european union's soft power. lebanon, in particular, is one of the few countries in the middle east where the social and political system holds up despite the enormous problems it faces: an exceptional case of welcoming and tenacity that looks to the west and the development of the rule of law despite the still serious structural deficiencies, its own internal social problems, the difficult relationship with minorities and the jihadist militias still active in many areas of the country. the european union as a whole can look to the republic of lebanon as a friendly democracy in a key area which we must support, ensuring its territorial integrity and political survival, and allowing it to stabilise under appropriate conditions and to gradually enter the area of joint cooperation and joint management of the middle east crisis.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation today because i believe it is important to establish financial and technical rules to enable the lebanese republic to participate effectively in the union's programmes. the horizontal framework established by the protocol lays down principles for economic, financial and technical cooperation and allows the republic of lebanon to receive technical assistance, in particular financial assistance, from the european union under eu programmes. this framework shall apply only to union programmes in which the relevant legal acts establishing them provide for the possibility of participation by the republic of lebanon. i also stress that the standard terms set out in the protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement establishing an association between the eu and its member states, of the one part, and the republic of lebanon, of the other part, should be applied to all the european neighbourhood policy partner countries with which similar protocols are to be concluded. under the protocol, representatives of lebanon may participate, as observers and only for matters concerning their country, in the management committees responsible for monitoring union programmes to which the republic of lebanon contributes financially.
in writing. ‒ the procedure concerns parliament's consent to the conclusion of a protocol to the eu-lebanon association agreement already in force, which will allow lebanon to participate in eu programmes. it is an instrument to help achieve the objectives of the euro-mediterranean agreement and to promote the development and stability of one of the countries bordering the union which plays a key role in the neighbourhood policy. the measure is therefore entirely compatible with our positions. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i agree that the european union should provide financial assistance to the lebanese republic: it is a country that is suffering a lot because of the continuous armed conflict that is taking place within the country and this phenomenon is especially affecting the many innocent citizens who live there and have no possibility to move. i therefore believe that it is right for the european union to allocate part of its funds to help ensure the security of citizens living in lebanon. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal, which lays the foundations for closer cooperation between europe and the lebanese republic by establishing a well-defined cooperation programme.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament approved the protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement establishing an association between the european community and its member states, of the one part, and the republic of lebanon, of the other part, within the framework of a framework agreement between the european union and the republic of lebanon on the participation of the republic of lebanon in union programmes. i voted in favour of the conclusion of this protocol because i believe that it provides a fundamental financial and technical framework for allowing lebanon to participate in community programmes and, as such, to receive financial assistance from the union. the protocol lays down clear rules on economic, financial and technical cooperation in respect of eu programmes which allow lebanon to participate. this protocol strengthens cooperation between the eu and lebanon, already trading partners and partners in human rights, democracy, political dialogue, cooperation in the fight against terrorism and money laundering.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft council decision on the euromed agreement on the participation of the republic of lebanon in union programmes. our neighbourhood policy allows for privileged relations with the middle east, increasing bilateral trade that is beneficial for all eu member states. the european union is the largest trading partner for lebanon, accounting for around one third of all lebanese trade, and this partnership needs to be maintained and encouraged in order to pursue greater economic integration with mutual commitments and gains.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation concerning the draft council decision on the conclusion of the protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement establishing an association between the european community and its member states, of the one part, and the republic of lebanon, of the other part, on a framework agreement between the european union and the republic of lebanon on the general principles for the participation of lebanon in union programmes. the objective of the protocol is to define the financial and technical rules enabling the lebanese republic to participate in some of the union's programmes and to consolidate financial, social and cultural cooperation and political dialogue between the two sides of the mediterranean. relations between the eu and lebanon are certainly one of the cornerstones of the foreign policy of the small country in the middle east. the country, which has suffered a dramatic civil war for 16 years, plays an important role in the complex context of the middle east and it is essential to ensure the political, economic and cultural closeness of the european union as a whole in order to facilitate a full democratic transition process and to resist the islamist demands that would further provoke unrest and tensions in a country that is based on a fragile governmental balance.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i am absolutely in favour of an agreement which includes and gives access to lebanon to all european union programmes. lebanon is an extraordinary country, a key strategic partner, a country that is demonstrating far more strength and resilience than the european union in managing the humanitarian emergency that is affecting and overwhelming it. lebanon is hosting 1.5 million refugees from syria who are living in absolute poverty. the country is not able to provide economic assistance or ensure adequate reception conditions. most refugee camps are spontaneous, there are no facilities. lebanon needs europe and it is together, through effective cooperation, that solutions can be found to a situation of violence which is forcing thousands of people to flee. from syria first to lebanon, then turkey to get to europe, all to escape from isis. it is precisely because we are all involved that cooperation and dialogue must be constant.
in writing. the protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement between the eu and lebanon contains provisions which must be applied and enforced by all the partner countries of european policy with which these protocols are to be concluded. the aim is to ensure that the financial rules are adequate to enable the republic of lebanon to join certain european union programmes. the programme contained in the protocol therefore lays down the principles for economic, financial and technical cooperation, enabling the republic of lebanon to receive assistance, in particular financial assistance from the union, under these programmes. i think, however, that parliament's recommendation is to be welcomed and adopted, and i therefore express my support for it.
in writing. ‒ given the historical links and shared values underlying the proximity and interdependence between the european union and lebanon, and given the desire of the member states and lebanon to consolidate those links and establish lasting relations based on reciprocity, solidarity, partnership and participation in development, i welcome the draft council decision on the conclusion of the protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement establishing an association between the european community and its member states, of the one part, and the republic of lebanon, of the other part. lebanon is a strategically important partner for the european union in the middle east. the country is currently experiencing precarious security conditions, as it is embroiled in the syrian civil war, with over one million refugees out of a total population of four million. i support the need to support the european union's commitment to promoting stability, prosperity and security in lebanon, in a continuous dialogue between the parties which will seek to find new forms of cooperation for the achievement of common objectives. relations between the parties shall be based on respect for the democratic principles and fundamental human rights enshrined in the universal declaration of human rights, which is an essential element of this agreement.
in writing. ‒ i thought it appropriate to vote in favour of the proposal by mrs mănescu. today, a truly functioning european union neighbourhood policy requires the gradual opening up of certain eu programmes and agencies to partner countries concerned by the policy. i therefore believe that the protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement represents a significant step in this direction, since it regulates the financial and technical aspects which allow the lebanese republic to benefit from eu assistance, especially financial assistance, and to participate in union programmes. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ among the many measures of the european neighbourhood policy (enp) to promote reform and modernisation in the eu's neighbouring states, there is the gradual opening up of certain eu programmes and agencies to the participation of the partner countries concerned. protocols have been signed with armenia, georgia, israel, jordan, moldova, morocco and ukraine. in december 2013, the republic of lebanon expressed its interest in participating in the wide variety of programmes open to the european neighbourhood policy partner countries. the protocol contains a framework agreement on the general principles for the participation of lebanon in union programmes. in accordance with article 218 (6) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the council is to obtain the assent of the european parliament before concluding this protocol. i voted in favour of the european parliament's approval so that cooperation between the eu and lebanon can be strengthened.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the conclusion of the protocol to the framework agreement between the european union and the lebanese republic. the agreement is part of the eu's neighbourhood policy, one of the pillars of the eu's relations with third countries. often described as a weak civil power at international level, europe has over the years demonstrated the goodness of its foreign policy, capable of establishing friendly and lasting relations with its neighbours. they can receive european financial assistance in the case of lebanon, subject to the conditions laid down in the european programmes in question. we should remember that lebanon is currently facing a migration crisis much more serious than the european one, with migration flows three times higher than those in europe. the country's geographical location is the destination for millions of syrian refugees who, because of the war, seek shelter there.
in writing. ‒ lebanon is a member of the euro-mediterranean partnership (euromed) which promotes integration and democratic reforms in the 16 countries bordering north africa and the middle east with the european union. since trade relations between lebanon and the eu have been growing by an average of 12.7% since 2008 and considering that the european neighbourhood policy provides for privileged relations with the members of euromed, i have decided to vote in favour of this recommendation allowing the lebanese republic to participate in the european union programmes.
in writing. ‒ under article 218 tfeu, parliament must give its consent to the conclusion of association agreements between the eu, member states and third countries. the euro-mediterranean agreement between the european union and lebanon is an indispensable instrument for the implementation of a coherent and innovative neighbourhood policy aimed at strengthening the prosperity, stability and security of the neighbouring countries. this establishes a political dialogue not only on economic issues such as public procurement and state aid, but also on social issues such as respect for human rights, access to services and labour standards. i have voted in favour of this, confident in the value of such political and social cooperation.

in writing. ‒ between 1998 and 2005, the european union concluded euro-mediterranean association agreements with nine mediterranean countries to replace the cooperation agreements of the 1970s. the provisions of these association agreements, which govern bilateral relations, vary from one mediterranean partner to another. these agreements provide the necessary framework for political dialogue between the north and the south and serve as a basis for the gradual liberalisation of trade in the mediterranean area, setting the conditions for cooperation in the economic, social and cultural fields between the european union and the partner countries. the aim of these agreements, and in particular of this recommendation with lebanon (whose agreement entered into force on 1 april 2006), is to make the mediterranean a common area of prosperity, peace and stability through economic, social, cultural and financial cooperation and the strengthening of political and security dialogue.

in writing. ‒ the exchange of financial information between different political entities is one of the key prerequisites for effectively combating phenomena of transnational scope such as fraud and tax evasion. in this context, the new agreement between the european union and the principality of monaco represents an important instrument to speed up the detection and fight against possible cases of tax fraud. more specifically, the agreement in question, reinforcing the pact already concluded in 2004, establishes the automatic exchange of information concerning interest, dividends, current account balances and proceeds from the sale of financial assets of citizens and companies of the two respective areas, favouring the application, also within the principality of monaco, of reinforced measures equivalent to those existing today in the european union. for all these reasons, i hope that the agreement will be concluded, ratified and come into force as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ in voting on the report, i gave my favourable opinion on the signing of the agreement between the european union and the principality of monaco on the automatic exchange of financial information for tax purposes, which is intended to improve cooperation and compliance with international tax obligations. the agreement represents an important step forward in the ongoing efforts to combat tax fraud and evasion and improves on the 2004 agreement which ensured that monaco applied measures equivalent to those contained in the eu directive on taxation of savings income. the purpose of the arrangement is to ensure that monaco applies enhanced measures equivalent to those provided for in the eu legal framework as updated in december 2014, and complies with the procedures for the automatic exchange of financial information for tax purposes promoted by the 2014 oecd global standard. the eu and monaco have agreed that the agreement will enter into force on 1 january 2017, if necessary in the form of provisional application, after completion of their respective internal procedures for conclusion and ratification.

in writing. ‒ in the current economic system based on the absolute mobility of capital, the exchange of information between national authorities is the most effective tool to combat crossborder tax fraud and evasion. following the adoption of the european directive on taxation of savings income and in order to maintain conditions of fair competition between economic operators, the european union signed on 22 february 2016 an agreement with the principality of monaco providing for the introduction of measures equivalent to those laid down in the directive, which will enter into force on 1 january 2017. the information to be exchanged between the competent authorities will include information on current accounts held by non-residents, which will be used to identify those seeking to conceal funds for which taxes have not been paid. i have joined the vote in this house in giving the council its approval for the conclusion of the protocol with the principality of monaco, which i hope will be ratified as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ the fight against tax evasion is a very sensitive issue. the european institutions have been fighting this phenomenon for years, which enriches a few societies at the expense of thousands of citizens every year. agreements on the exchange of financial information with other countries can help to limit this phenomenon, since the taxpayers concerned can be correctly identified. i am therefore pleased with this agreement, which establishes the good relationship between the european union and the principality of monaco and extends the pool of information available to the union for the fight against tax fraud. i believe that this cooperation represents a major step forward in the fight against this phenomenon and therefore i could only vote in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the agreement between the european union and the principality of monaco on the automatic exchange of financial information for tax purposes, aimed at improving cooperation and compliance with obligations in the tax and international fields, as the agreement represents an important step forward in the ongoing efforts to combat tax fraud and tax evasion. the agreement, which will enter into force in 2017, is a significant step forward compared to the 2004 agreement currently in force, as the latter is limited to ensuring the application of equivalent measures by monaco, with regard to the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. the new agreement improves on the 2004 agreement and is in line with the oecd standard. under the agreement, eu member states and monaco will exchange information on accounts held in their territories by their residents automatically and unconditionally. the new agreement will enable the tax administrations of the member states and monaco to correctly and unequivocally identify the taxpayers concerned, to apply and enforce their tax laws in cross-border situations, and to assess the likelihood of tax evasion and avoid further unnecessary investigations.

in writing. ‒ the eu and the principality of monaco signed an agreement on 22 february 2016 that will make it harder for eu citizens to evade taxes and hide money in monegasque bank accounts. the information to be exchanged will not only cover income such as interest and dividends, but also account balances and proceeds from the sale of financial assets. under that agreement, the eu and monaco will automatically exchange information on the bank accounts of their respective residents, starting in 2018, and for information collected since 1 january 2017. the tax administrations of the member states and monaco will thus be able to correctly and unequivocally identify the taxpayers concerned, apply and enforce their tax legislation in cross-border situations, assess the likelihood of tax evasion and avoid further unnecessary investigations. for all these reasons i voted in favour of approving this agreement.
