mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this report because it is good that the iccat plan has been a real success and that our seas, the mediterranean in particular, are now full of bluefin tuna. but i would like to stress that it was the fishermen who made the greatest efforts to respect the limits imposed and it is the fishermen who must now return to fishing. but unfortunately, that is not the case. the increase in quotas as a result of the restocking of bluefin tuna has not affected small-scale fishing at all. it is always the big ship owners who benefit and who can thus exploit a sea which has become rich again and which could therefore once again be the economic backbone of thousands of small fishermen and small family businesses living at sea. the european fisheries policy must therefore take a stand, choose a right direction, and i suggest that of supporting artisanal and traditional fishing, i choose small-scale fishing, operators who for centuries have relied on the sea and who today are crushed by rules and economic interests that have little to do with environmental sustainability.
in writing. ‒ the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) has the power to adopt binding recommendations for the conservation and management of fisheries. among the fish species protected by iccat, bluefin tuna is undoubtedly of central importance, considering the numerous decisions taken since 2006 to limit its catches to a maximum allowable percentage, for example. i therefore voted in favour of it because i believe that such strategies will not only benefit the environment and biodiversity but also ensure sustainable economic development.
in writing. ‒ in 2006, the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) adopted a multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan, which includes a series of measures to be followed until 2022. the european union, which is part of this regional fisheries management organisation, is called upon to adopt a series of regulatory instruments to implement the binding decisions adopted there, in particular for the period 2012-2014. the mato report, which i supported with my vote, makes some changes to the commission proposal which aims to implement the iccat recommendations. the text adopted emphasises in particular the key role played by artisanal tuna in the conservation of fish stocks. the recovery plan should encourage a greater use of these traditional means, which not only ensure greater selectivity but also have a very small impact on marine ecosystems.
in writing. ‒ while the objective of this proposal to include in a regulation all the measures of the bluefin tuna recovery plan adopted between 2012 and 2014, in order to ensure more uniform implementation throughout the eu, is to be welcomed, i must point out that some of the provisions applied have caused an excessive increase in bureaucracy with negative effects on the activities of the fleets. i have therefore decided to abstain and not to support this text in its entirety.
in writing. ‒ as we know, the european union, together with the member states, is a contracting party to iccat and in 2014, at the iccat annual assembly, we welcomed the news of positive data on the good health status of bluefin tuna and a 20% increase in the quotas allocated to contracting states. the quota for bluefin tuna is set by icat, but the distribution criteria are decided by individual member countries at their discretion. unfortunately, in many cases only a few shipowners benefit from these quotas, while small-scale fishermen are largely excluded. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fishermen are not caught. in the agreement reached with the council we make a clear call for the protection of artisanal and traditional fisheries in the allocation of bluefin tuna quotas.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report in question, which aims to include in a single regulation all the measures of the bluefin tuna recovery plan adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) between 2012 and 2014, in order to ensure their uniform and effective implementation throughout the eu. uniform application should ensure a level playing field for all operators in the tuna fisheries, including in particular operators from third countries. i would stress that all the efforts of eu fishermen and the restrictions imposed on them would be in vain if different rules were applied to foreign fleets. eu operators should not be penalised by the imposition of stricter measures than those agreed, because the european commission has failed to impose such measures in the iccat negotiations. finally, we must raise the question of the absence of the european parliament in these international negotiations. i would stress that the implementation of the recommendations of the regional fisheries management organisations (rfmos), such as iccat, must remain a joint responsibility of the european parliament and the council under the ordinary procedure.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan, which is a measure to implement the recent recommendations of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas in the european regulatory framework.
in writing. ‒ unfair and illegal fishing practices are a threat to marine ecosystems, which have put the survival of fish species at risk, in particular bluefin tuna. the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) has issued recommendations and measures which, in order to become operational within the eu, need to be transposed into eu law in order to ensure uniform and effective implementation throughout the european union. hence the need for the regulation we voted in plenary which includes all the measures of the icatt reconstitution plan adopted between 2012 and 2014. the various technical measures envisaged: from live bluefin tuna transfer and caging operations to the use of stereoscopic cameras for bluefin tuna stock estimation. the measures implemented in previous years are beginning to bear fruit and fish stocks are gradually being rebuilt. this year, european fleets have benefited from a 20% increase in their quota compared to the previous year, i.e. 9 372 tonnes of eligible catches for the eu in 2015. all legislative instruments must be supported to protect fisheries resources and to enable our seas to be repopulated. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i agree with this proposal because it is simply an evolution of a regulation already implemented in 2006. the regulation provided for a reduction in the fishing of bluefin tuna, which was thought to be in danger of being overfished. in this light, i am pleased to note that the quantity of tuna caught has decreased considerably since 2006, by more than half. however, such a drastic reduction means fewer jobs, less food available to many countries that actually need it. therefore, since the quantity of bluefin tuna has developed very positively in recent years, i agree to moderately increase its catch so that there is a good balance between the safety of the species and the possibility of trade in the species by small entrepreneurs.
in writing. ‒ this is a positive report to ensure the recovery and preservation of bluefin tuna stocks. the mediterranean fishermen, especially the small ones, have suffered in recent years because of the restrictions imposed and because of the imbalance in the allocation of quotas, which have benefited the large companies and the large shipowners, putting many small companies in difficulty and often forcing them to give up. this policy must be overturned: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fishing industry is not affected by the current situation. it is true that the distribution criteria are decided by the member states, but the commission and the institutions can do a lot, especially by introducing criteria and mechanisms for the protection and safeguarding of bluefin tuna quotas in favour of small-scale artisanal fishing. i believe we owe it to the many families and small fishermen who, day after day, contribute to the protection of our seas.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation because i believe that the conservation and recovery of bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean is essential. to do this, all measures adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat), to which the eu is a contracting party, need to be applied in a uniform and effective way throughout the eu through a specific regulation. in particular, i welcome the existence of important technical measures, such as the use of stereoscopic cameras for estimating bluefin tuna and quantities released at sea, and catch reporting obligations.
in writing. ‒ i abstain from the report because it creates excessive obligations and bureaucracy that could have been avoided.
in writing. ‒ respect for the diversity of fisheries and the sustainability of our seas are unquestioned priorities in european fisheries, environment and sea policies. these objectives are even more sensitive when they concern endangered species and are of particular relevance to the fauna, gastronomy and cultural heritage of the mediterranean basin, the heart of european civilization. i therefore voted strongly in favour of parliament's position on this regulation, whereby we support the proposal to rationalise and harmonise all measures of the restructuring plan adopted between 2012 and 2014 in order to ensure their uniform and effective implementation throughout the eu.
in writing. the proposal under consideration aims to bring together in a single regulation all the measures that were adopted up to 2014 in order to ensure their implementation throughout the european union. it provides for the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean (bft). the measures provided for in the plan adopted in 2006 by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat), which will expire in 2022, had in fact required necessary but costly sacrifices. in view of the gradual recovery of bluefin tuna stocks in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean, catches were then increased sustainably, with an annual increase of 20%, which means that the quantity caught by italy rose from 2 302.8 to 2 752 tonnes. the conservation of the ecosystem and the increase in the reserve, while at the same time keeping employment levels in mind, was the objective we set ourselves and which we can now say we have achieved. thanks to eu environmental policies and the efforts of fishermen to limit catches of bluefin tuna, we are now in a position to raise fishing levels.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council concerning a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean and repealing regulation (ec) no 302/2009. the proposal aims to transpose into community law the measures contained in the multiannual plan for the recovery of atlantic and mediterranean bluefin tuna adopted by iccat. this plan aims to rebuild the bluefin tuna stock by reducing the total allowable catch and selectivity of catches for biodiversity.
in writing. ‒ given the need to protect bluefin tuna from overexploitation in the atlantic and the importance of cooperating to maintain the consumption of this species at maximum sustainable levels, i welcome the proposal to incorporate into union law all the amendments to the recovery plan adopted by iccat in 2012, 2013 and 2014 that have not yet been transposed. in 2006, iccat adopted a multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan, which is expected to be completed by 2022. to restore the stock, the plan provides for a progressive reduction in the total allowable catch (tac), restrictions on fishing activity in certain zones and periods, a new minimum size, measures applicable to sport and recreational fishing activities, measures concerning fishing and farming capacity and a strengthening of the iccat joint international inspection programme. since 2008, the bluefin tuna biomass has shown a markedly positive trend. in the light of these improvements, i consider it important to support the decision of iccat to bring forward to 2016 the tac foreseen for 2017, which would still be well below the tac in force before the entry into force of the recovery plan.
in writing. ‒ i think that mr mato's proposal should be voted in favour. the role of the european union in iccat reflects the particular attention that the union pays to the recovery of bluefin tuna stocks. the results achieved so far far far exceed the expectations and objectives initially set. i therefore support the proposal of my colleague to include in a regulation all the measures adopted between 2012 and 2014 as this would allow for their uniform and effective implementation in all eu member states. i also think it is appropriate to stress that the commission's proposal to implement future amendments to the restructuring plan by means of delegated acts risks further marginalizing the role of the european parliament in such an important issue at international level. i therefore feel obliged to vote in favour of the proposal as formulated by my colleague.
in writing. ‒ in the light of the positive development of bluefin tuna stocks in recent years, the international commission for the conservation of tunas (iccat) decided to increase the maximum allowable catch limits by 20% for the next three years (2015 to 2017), as scientific data showed that stocks are at optimal levels of abundance. in mid-december 2015, the eu council of ministers responsible for fisheries and agriculture finally decided on the 20% increase and proceeded to allocate the community quota among the member states concerned. in addition, the iccat recommendations take into account the specificities of the different gear used for tuna fishing. in this context, the role of artisanal tuna vessels, such as traditional tuna vessels, is important for the conservation of stocks. i believe that in implementing the recovery plan the european union should pay particular attention to these traditional tuna traps, which contribute to the recovery of tuna stocks by virtue of their considerable selectivity. in addition, such gears have a very low impact on marine ecosystems due to their low level of energy consumption and bycatch. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna, as did the ppe group. the frequent use of intensive fishing practices has severely affected the numbers of bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean. to deal with this problem, iccat, the regional fisheries management organisation, has developed a multiannual plan to restore bluefin tuna in the areas mentioned. needless to say, without action at community level the problem will be almost insoluble. i would also like to point out that the decisive intervention of mr mato, of the ppe group, made it possible to open negotiations with the council on the text under consideration and to approve an amendment in favour of small-scale artisanal fishing, a sector which is also increasingly in decline in the italian economy and which the european parliament is trying to protect.
in writing. ‒ the new bluefin tuna recovery plan aims to transpose into eu law some of the measures adopted by iccat to improve the management of this important species in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean. the new regulation, which i supported, recognises the need to pay more attention to craft-based equipment, such as tuna boats, which have a low impact on marine ecosystems, a high level of selectivity and contribute to job creation. the proposal includes technical measures, such as those concerning the transfer and caging of live bluefin tuna, measures involving the use of stereoscopic cameras, provisions on the declaration of catches and the implementation of the iccat regional observation programme.
in writing. ‒ since 2008, the european union has launched a cod management plan to ensure the sustainable development of fisheries. last march, however, the council signed the new multiannual fisheries pact for the baltic sea, not only updating the rules for the management of certain fish species, but above all introducing new concepts of sustainability. the ecosystem approach, which emphasises the biological interaction between species, is accompanied by the provision of a maximum sustainable yield, which imposes a maximum allowable catch. i therefore voted in favour, considering that protecting the biodiversity of our seas and the environment is without doubt one of the european priorities.
in writing. ‒ the baltic sea is a highly sensitive ecosystem, a virtually closed water basin in which the mutual relationships between the various marine species are of paramount importance. the wałęsa report, which i supported in parliament today, improves the commission's proposal, while at the same time stressing the importance of the multiannual plan presented. the multi-species management of cod, herring and sprat stocks is a major step forward in fisheries management and a model for future such plans. the regionalised approach envisaged by the reform of the common fisheries policy should be strengthened, while allowing for a timely response to those sudden changes affecting the state of the stocks of the species concerned. ensuring flexibility in the plan is crucial and therefore a review of the plan in three years' time is required.
in writing. ‒ the aim of the proposal is to establish a framework for the 'multi-species' management of cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea in areas where fishing is primarily directed at these three species. although i agree with the 'multi-species' approach of this plan, i cannot fully support this text, as it does not provide sufficient information on the impact it will have on the economies of the areas concerned, so i abstained.
in writing. ‒ cod, herring and sprat are important fisheries in the baltic sea. the scientific advice of the international council for the exploration of the sea (ices) indicates that for some of these stocks the current exploitation rates are not compatible with the achievement of the maximum sustainable yield as provided for by the cfp. while a management plan has been in place for the baltic cod stocks since 2007, the herring and sprat stocks are not yet subject to a management plan. this plan is the first to be approved since the entry into force of the cfp and is an example to follow.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today to express my satisfaction that the member states and the european parliament have reached a valid agreement on the new multiannual plan for the baltic. a management plan for cod stocks in the baltic sea has already been in place since 2008. however, it is widely considered to be inadequate in relation to the current situation of cod stocks and the fisheries that depend on them. given the strong influence of biological interactions and environmental effects on the baltic sea stocks, i think it is desirable to be able to adapt the patterns and rates of exploitation of these stocks in the light of the progress made in the scientific understanding of the interactions and changes in environmental conditions. this would give the plan much needed flexibility. i also stress the importance of ensuring that the new plan draws on the input of those who know the region best as they will be able to adapt measures at regional level to the specificities of the fisheries concerned.
in writing. ‒ the new multiannual plan for cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea includes new concepts such as the ecosystem approach and biological interaction between fish species. this is an important innovation, since for the first time the fact that an increase in the natural prey of predators will correspond to a catch of predators is taken into account in the calculation of catchable quotas. the plan as a whole is much better than the previous measures and i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the baltic sea is an area with a very high fishing stock, particularly cod, herring and sprat. i think it is important that a control plan is created because biological interactions and environmental effects have a strong influence on fisheries. i agree with this proposal that aims to establish a framework for the multispecies management of the stocks of the three species mentioned above. in my view, this instrument can bring many benefits both in recognising the interactions between regulated species and in understanding the influence of cod on herring and sprat stocks and vice versa. better information on these issues will certainly improve the balanced and sustainable exploitation of these stocks, ensure the stability of fishing opportunities and, as a result, bring many benefits to fishermen. for these reasons i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the text is the result of a long process and represents a compromise that was not easy to find. this is the first multiannual plan to take account of the interactions between species, to ensure balanced and sustainable exploitation of fisheries and better economic conditions for fishermen in the long term. thanks to parliament, strong safeguard measures have been secured to keep stocks at sustainable levels and to ensure a rapid return to acceptable levels in the event of depletion. the management plan must enter into force immediately, as stocks are declining, with negative consequences also for fishermen. a model for sustainable fisheries management, in ecological, economic and social terms, is the only approach capable of avoiding cyclical crises in the long term, which, in addition to serious environmental damage, have repercussions on the sector, putting at risk the jobs and safety of thousands of families.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the commission's proposal. a multispecies management approach is certainly more advantageous and effective than a single-species management approach. this vision has the merit of aiming at a balanced and sustainable management of stocks, and ensuring a level of fishing that ensures a stable income for fishermen.
in writing. ‒ i abstain from this report because the european union should give member states more autonomy in fisheries matters.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a multiannual plan for cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea and for the fisheries exploiting those stocks, amending council regulation (ec) no 2187/2005 and repealing council regulation (ec) no 1098/2007, as it is the first real implementation plan of the reform of the common fisheries policy and can serve as a model for future negotiations. the difficulties of the approach to the common fisheries policy arise from the need to find a compromise between the two opposing requirements of the sustainability of fish stocks on the one hand and the necessary flexibility for operators in the sector and member states in applying the rules on the conservation of fish species on the other. the compromise reached between parliament and the council in the trilogue is a good agreement, which will allow the parties concerned to assess the practical effects and consequences of the measures and their transferability to other species. in particular, i am in favour of including in the plan forecasts relating to the regionalisation and economic, social and environmental sustainability of fishing activities.
in writing. environmental effects and biological interactions have an effect on marine stocks and therefore it is necessary to implement rules for the protection of certain species. in fact, in 2014 the commission published a multiannual plan for cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea and for the fisheries exploiting those stocks. this proposal, which was agreed after months of negotiations, is now intended to regulate a framework for the management of the above stocks in the seas where they are most exploited, and sees a transition to a new adaptive management. finally, agreement was reached on the first multiannual plan under the new cfp and, for these reasons, i am voting in favour of the commission's proposal for a sustainable fishery for the stocks in the baltic sea.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of the multiannual plan for cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea. the aim of the proposal is to establish a multi-species stock plan which is much more effective than the management of a single species. this plan allows for the balanced and sustainable exploitation of these stocks and ensures the stability of fishing opportunities and the livelihoods of fishermen, while ensuring that management is based on the most up-to-date scientific advice on the state of the stocks concerned, interactions between species and other aspects of the ecosystem and fishing activities.
in writing. ‒ having regard to the european commission's multiannual plan for cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea, whereas the three species account for 94% of the catches in the baltic sea in recent years and whereas, although a cod stock management plan exists, it is not adequate to the current situation; whereas, with regard to the other two species, there is a lack of legislation and regulation and that this deficiency must necessarily be corrected, also in the light of the protection of the ecosystem; i therefore consider that the drawing up of a single plan, including other fish species and based on up-to-date scientific studies, would be an appropriate way of filling the regulatory gap and ensuring greater protection of the stocks, and i therefore consider it appropriate to vote in favour of the proposal in question.
in writing. ‒ i believe that a management plan covering several species in the baltic sea is more effective than management of a single species, because it allows for a balanced and sustainable exploitation of cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea and guarantees the stability of fishing opportunities and, consequently, the livelihoods of fishermen. in addition, there are good reasons for maintaining certain rules already in force, which protect cod stocks during the breeding season and protect small-scale artisanal fisheries. i therefore voted in favour of the multiannual plan in question and hope that such a solution will allow for a more flexible approach in the annual fixing of fishing opportunities.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by mr walesa (epp) on the proposal for a regulation establishing a multiannual plan for the management of cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea and the fisheries exploiting those stocks. the text presented to the plenary was the result of a series of negotiations between parliament, the council and the commission (the 'trilogue') which resulted in a compromise on a controversial issue, namely the maximum acceptable level of mortality caused by fishing activities. the baltic sea stock plan is the first of its kind to be adopted under the new common fisheries policy; it ensures that fishing activities in the area concerned are environmentally sound and economically sustainable. for these reasons the plan will be used as a model for other areas, first of all the north sea and the atlantic. i think that these are very good reasons for supporting the text presented in plenary.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the establishment of a multiannual plan for cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea. the aim of the regulation is to allow for the balanced and sustainable exploitation of these fish species, which together account for 94% of total catches. the multi-species management plan established by this regulation requires that more account be taken of the different ecological functions and roles of the species covered by the plan. as this is the first such plan adopted under the new cfp, i hope that it will serve as a model or test bed for future multiannual plans for the management of fisheries in other european seas.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this report because, as we know, reality moves much faster than the rules and regulations must adapt quickly to the challenges and, above all, to the new balances in society. schengen, erasmus, mobility between countries have helped to create and spread an increasing number of european couples - we can call them that - families who live in one member state, have houses in another, inherit property in yet another. it is a society which, fortunately, has had the courage to break down barriers and which therefore needs new rules today. the european union must support these european families, above all by facilitating dialogue between member states and by clearly deciding on jurisdiction in matters of property regimes, in order to give couples certainty and clarity as to which court has jurisdiction.
in writing. ‒ given the globalised and international character of modern society, family law must necessarily adapt to the new needs of citizens. to this end, the commission has, following the adoption of the enhanced cooperation procedure, made a new proposal on matrimonial property regimes. in summary, it is intended to regulate and clarify, in the case of crossborder decisions, which court has jurisdiction, which rule is applicable and, finally, how the judgment should be recognised and enforced. legal certainty, especially in the management of family matters, is a fundamental right of citizens. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the cavada report on the proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matrimonial property regimes. following the deadlock in the negotiations, the launch of enhanced cooperation led to a proposal that was much more in line with the indications expressed by parliament in 2013. the text contains important innovations, since it clearly defines which court has jurisdiction to rule on questions of matrimonial property regimes. a major step forward is the principle of the unity of the applicable law, which provides that the law of matrimonial property regimes applies to all property held in the context of the union, wherever it may be. in general terms, this new regulation is an effective response to overcome the confusion and legal difficulties, which is why i have decided to support it with my vote.
in writing. ‒ although this report is well structured and can be shared, there are still some passages which could open up the door to future criticism and exploitation which prevent me from fully supporting this text. i therefore voted in favour of the request.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation, which is part of enhanced cooperation involving the vast majority of member states and which aims to clarify and better regulate, within the countries concerned, jurisdiction, the applicable law and the procedures for the recognition and enforcement of decisions on matrimonial property regimes, is an important step forward which will facilitate access to rights and simplify life for a large number of european citizens. the new proposal for a regulation would allow for greater flexibility (for example in the choice of the applicable law or in the facilitation of the circulation of official documents) which would meet the needs, in particular, of those couples composed of nationals from different member states, while clarifying certain legal situations which are currently unclear and thus providing greater legal certainty. this is further progress towards an increasingly effective circulation of acts and decisions between member states, which will strengthen the creation of a homogeneous, harmonised and functional legal area capable of meeting the challenge of increased mobility and of promoting the development of effective european citizenship.
in writing. ‒ after careful reading and discussion in the chamber, i have voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matrimonial property regimes. the italian supreme court, in confirming the adoption of the homosexual couple, has now stated that this 'does not in the abstract create a conflict of interest between the biological parent and the minor adopting, but requires that any conflict be established in practice by the court', and has thus established principles of law which, as they are applicable to domestic law, raise questions, increasingly important, also within the law of international couples of the european union. i therefore support the rapporteur's words and have voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i vote in favour of the report on the proposed regulation, as it provides greater clarity and sets out specific rules for the identification of the competent court and the applicable law in cases of crossborder decisions in matters of matrimonial property regimes.
in writing. ‒ despite the progress made in the process of european integration, millions of citizens linked by marriage or by an international registered partnership face practical problems in managing their assets. it is often difficult for such couples to know which court has jurisdiction and which property regime applies to their property situation, particularly in the event of separation or succession. in the field of family law, the council acts unanimously. however, in the specific case, 18 member states requested an enhanced cooperation procedure, as it was not possible to reach unanimous approval of the proposals. i joined the house in voting in favour of the council authorising enhanced cooperation on matrimonial property regimes for international couples, so as to provide the states which have acceded to european legislation with a clear and comprehensive legal framework on jurisdiction, applicable law, recognition and enforcement of decisions on matrimonial property regimes which will make it easier for many international couples to resolve their problems in this area.
in writing. ‒ international couples are currently still too insecure about their property regimes. too often, spouses find unclear legislative blocks that extend waiting times excessively, and this can lead to various problems for couples. i think that greater protection of the rights of those in this situation is needed and this proposal is aimed at putting an end to the many cases of confusion and legal difficulties. for these reasons i have decided to vote in favour of this proposal.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament has repeatedly called on the other european institutions, but also on the member states, in its non-legislative resolutions, to guarantee equal rights for couples, both heterosexual and homosexual, who opt for so-called civil unions. the full mutual recognition of the property rights of registered partnerships within the european union is therefore a fundamental step towards the recognition of the much-needed equality of rights and is also indispensable in order to reduce discriminatory legal and administrative obstacles for citizens exercising their right to free movement. the proposal for a regulation on the property consequences of registered partnerships will, it seems, put an end to many cases of confusion and legal difficulties and will consequently guarantee greater legal certainty. as already mentioned, this is a concrete commitment by the union to equality and equal rights. a concrete commitment that we cannot help but share.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's legislative resolution on the proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions on the property consequences of registered partnerships between persons belonging to different member states, because i believe that we need to move forward on the path of extension and granting of rights in the eu. the principle of equal treatment for married couples and registered partnerships is a principle which i cannot abandon. it is therefore essential that the negotiation of the regulatory framework for matrimonial property regimes should be accompanied by the negotiation of the regulatory framework for registered partnerships. this is also an issue on which parliament has a clear and firm position, which is unfortunately hampered by the reticence and myopia of some member states. i therefore strongly support the choice of enhanced cooperation among a majority of member states, because i believe that it is necessary to go ahead with this important legislation.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to reiterate what i said in my previous statement and welcome the proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matters of matrimonial property regimes. this is an important measure aimed at regulating the property effects of relationships between couples, which need clarity, simplification and legal certainty.
in writing. ‒ i thought it appropriate to vote in favour of mr cavada's proposal, given the scope of the regulation under consideration. while this regulation concerns the property effects of registered partnerships, jurisdiction and the applicable law as well as the recognition and enforcement of decisions, it seeks to safeguard national competences in matters of family law, while ensuring that the principle of the unity of the law applicable to all property within the territory of the union is respected. i am convinced that the proposal as it stands should be welcomed, and i have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the major step forward in this new regulation is the principle of the unity of the applicable law, which provides that the law on the property effects of a registered partnership applies to all assets held within the partnership, wherever they are located. this therefore puts an end to the division of the legal regime of the couple's property. the regulation allows the choice of law applicable to the property effects of registered partnerships, but is limited by the requirement of being a national or habitual resident of the state concerned. the difference with the regulation on matrimonial property regimes is that registered partners can choose the law of the state of registration. in the absence of a choice, the law applicable is that of the place of registration. i voted in favour of the new regulation because it is in the interest of international couples and because it puts an end to many cases of confusion and legal difficulties.

in writing. ‒ the development of renewable energy is a key factor in achieving our climate and energy goals and a key element in our decarbonisation journey. the european union is on track to meet its 2020 renewable energy targets overall, but further efforts are needed by member states that have fallen further behind. such efforts are all the more necessary in the light of the gradual decrease in the costs of such energy, which, together with technological advances in production and storage, has made renewable energy increasingly competitive and cost-effective. it is therefore important that support for these energy sources continues beyond 2020, maintaining the effective combination of binding targets and national action plans that have enabled us to achieve tangible results so far, in an ambitious and effective regulatory framework that is able to send appropriate and long-term signals to investors. the commission, for its part, must continue to actively monitor progress in the field of renewables, promoting transparency, consistency and the absence of technical obstacles to the development of these key energies.
in writing. ‒ renewable energy is the future of the eu's long-term development. we must implement economic policies that make them the fundamental pillar of the european union's energy model. we have a historic task: to combat climate change and reduce our dependence on the rest of the world's energy resources to restructure our production model and create quality jobs, as well as safeguard our territory and the future of our descendants. the transition to a sustainable energy production model is also a social priority that cannot be left to the market alone: we need to understand that regulation and democratic participation are necessary to avoid serious social and environmental crises. we must prevent energy oligopolies from defining the future of energy for europe, but instead ensure an integrated, efficient and clean european energy model by 2050.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of this report to ensure that the eu's renewable energy target of 20% of total consumption by 2020 is met by all eu member states. the commission should ensure the full implementation of the 2020 renewable energy directive and should present an ambitious regulatory framework for the period after 2020. in this context, i stress the need for a stable long-term regulatory framework, including renewable energy targets at national and eu level, to achieve the eu's long-term climate goals (2050). i would remind you that the european parliament's request for binding targets of at least 30% of energy from renewable sources in energy consumption must be implemented by means of national targets in order to provide the necessary security for investors and legal certainty. i also believe that, in the light of the recent cop 21 agreement, considerably higher ambition with clear targets is desirable in order to ensure that the eu is a world leader in renewables.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the own-initiative report on progress on renewable energy. the report addresses a critical review of the framework resulting from directive 2009/28/ec and provides insights to use the decentralised and democratized energy model to implement the energy transition and derive the related results in terms of independence, efficiency and sustainability.
in writing. ‒ although fossil fuels are still economically irreplaceable, the development of renewable energy is strategic for the future of a europe that has no oil but has sun and wind. progress so far is encouraging and citizens, if properly incentivised, respond positively by showing openness to new technologies. however, it is important that these incentives do not overburden communities and that they are always used in a transparent way so that companies know what each technology costs, including in terms of taxes and public money that could also be used for other purposes.
in writing. ‒ the target of 20% of total renewable energy consumption by 2020 is implemented differently in different member states. this is why i support the call for full implementation of the legislation to achieve the objectives in a uniform way across the continent. at the same time, i support the re-launch of the 2050 targets towards a sovereign, efficient and clean energy model. we have to be ambitious. we have a duty and a responsibility to combat climate change by reducing our dependence on resources that we are forced to import from the rest of the world. we must increasingly ensure that sustainable and indigenous energy production is a key element in the recovery of our economy, in conjunction with job creation. the eu renewable energy directive is a legal instrument that needs to be supported and implemented, with binding targets and clear rules. but often it's not enough. we need to act at a lower level, raising awareness and stimulating the active contribution of our citizens and consumers, through campaigns and incentives that can make them truly protagonists of a season of renewed sustainability on our continent.
in writing. ‒ the need to move away from fossil fuel dependence is urgent, to facilitate widespread self-production and energy self-sufficiency. the eu's commitment to reducing co2 emissions, but also the need to drastically reduce pollutants such as heavy metals and dioxins in air, water and soil, should require all eu states to put effective measures into practice in a timely manner. it is our health and our environment that is at stake, but also our financial resources, given the health and social costs of an environment devastated by our dependence on fossil fuels like oil and its derivatives, coal and gas. a rapid transition requires research, innovation and the effective and efficient use of all available european funds for energy efficiency and renewable energy production. and we must avoid the brake on structural reforms which in effect translate into austerity policies or senseless cuts. in short, europe's cities and regions need to achieve a paradigm shift, but to do so, there must be clear and binding commitments to rely on a truly renewable energy mix. for these reasons, i am voting in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the own-initiative report on progress on renewable energy because, in addition to containing a number of important recommendations for the new 2030 renewable energy directive, it refers to 'prosumers', a revolutionary new model of energy production and consumption that sees citizens fully involved in cooperative and self-production models. an important step towards the energy transition referred to by the 5 star movement, a decentralised and democratic energy model that guarantees independence, efficiency and sustainability.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the development of renewable energy requires a different approach that makes it the fundamental pillar of the european union's energy model. our fundamental responsibility as representatives of the european people is to fight climate change, a historic duty that we must not neglect. it is also becoming essential to reduce dependence on the rest of the world's energy resources if we are to structure our production model and generate quality jobs, as well as drive the development of strategic technologies for the energy transition.
in writing. ‒ i am voting against the report, which is confusing and over-liberalising risks weakening sovereignty.
in writing. ‒ the fight against climate change is made up of concrete commitments that the eu and its member states must follow up on year after year. it is therefore very important to monitor progress in renewables, which are one of the key areas for achieving the targets set in paris at cop21. unfortunately, some countries are still far behind in this respect. i therefore share the call in the report we are voting on today for the commission to increase its overall political commitment, precisely to monitor the action of the states and above all to introduce concrete instruments - for example, an ad hoc financial mechanism - aimed at reducing the cost of capital and the risks associated with renewable energy projects.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep resolution on progress in renewable energy because i believe that the development of renewable energy requires a new approach that makes it the fundamental pillar of the eu's energy model. in the face of climate change, the eu must reduce its dependence on the rest of the world's energy resources if it is to truly structure its production model and create quality jobs, as well as drive the development of strategic technologies for the transition to a sustainable energy production model, which is a social priority. this transition cannot be left to the market alone, but must be regulated by the eu in such a way that unfair competition between eu member states is not created, which would result in harm to citizens in the form of social and environmental externalities. i believe that the current combination of binding national targets, national renewable energy action plans and biennial monitoring has been the driving force behind the development of renewable energy capacity in the member states. a regulatory framework that respects the principle of proportionality, recognising a key role for local authorities, communities, households and individuals in the energy transition, is needed.
in writing. ‒ favourable to the progress report on renewable energy. while the progress made by member states in achieving their national renewable energy targets attests to the merits of the union's renewable energy policy, it is necessary to further encourage member states that have been slower to step up their efforts in order to ensure the achievement of ambitious 2030 energy and climate targets that allow for a secure inflow of investment and financing in the renewable energy sector. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's energy policy and its implementation in the member states.
in writing. ‒ in the face of a steady rise in global temperature to 1.5°c above pre-industrial levels, due to the disproportionate use of non-renewable and non-sustainable energy resources, we warmly welcome the proposal. the development of renewable energy sources through directive 2009/28/ec has significantly reduced production costs and thus fostered eu technological leadership that will create up to 20 million jobs in the green economy by 2020. therefore, it is of key importance not only to increase cooperation and coordination between member states but above all to combine binding national action plans with common objectives, verified by biennial controls, in order to meet the commitments made under the paris agreement (cop 21). this is possible through powerful economic incentives, such as the implementation of tax breaks and the promotion of public investment, in order to facilitate a transition to a fully self-sustaining, efficient and clean energy model by 2050. in order to achieve this, we also believe that it is necessary to support research and development activities and to provide support to member states to take additional measures in order to achieve these ambitious objectives in time.
in writing. ‒ the fight against climate change and the search for alternative methods to reduce the eu's dependence on external energy sources are addressed in the renewable energy directive (2009/28/ec). the process of transforming the energy mix of the member states is creating a favourable environment for the development of the renewable energy sector. however, i do acknowledge the concerns expressed in the report and support what has been said about the need to solve these problems. i declare that i shall vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the transition to a sustainable energy production model is a political, economic, social and environmental priority for the european union. the renewable energy directive has proven to be an effective tool to start the process of transforming the energy mix of its member states, with binding targets and clear rules for supervision and control. we are close to achieving the 2020 targets and now it is necessary to send a strong political signal for the continuation of this strategy by setting targets significantly higher than those proposed by the council. the report states that by 2030, at least 30% of energy must come from renewable sources. the commission is proposing to increase the number of member states that have not yet adopted the euro by a factor of two. at the same time, the report stresses the need for these objectives to be pursued by all member states as laid down in the old directive, and not just at european level as the new council proposal would suggest. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. the report promotes the development of renewables as a fundamental pillar of the european union's energy model and i therefore vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ one of our key responsibilities is to combat climate change and reduce our dependence on energy from the rest of the world if we are to generate quality jobs and drive the development of strategic technologies for the energy transition. the eu has provided a legal instrument to achieve these objectives with the renewable energy directive (2009/28/ec). this legal instrument has created a favourable environment for the development of the renewable energy sector and has contributed to the growth of a diverse and diversified sector. i believe that the next revision of the renewable energy directive should include measures to promote and encourage investment in these areas. a more integrated market is essential for the development of renewable energy and the reduction of energy costs. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the progress report on renewable energy, a subject which is receiving a lot of attention at european level and on which the commission is expected to present a new proposal by the end of 2016, following the communication published in june last year. the text discussed in the itre committee, of which i am a member, contains many strengths necessary to achieve the 2020 energy targets. these include cost-effectiveness and competitiveness of renewable energy, safeguarding national competences for the energy mix and promoting diversification of energy supply sources. it goes without saying that renewables represent an increasingly tangible future in the energy landscape, with an increasingly renewable-oriented union. however, the project of a 100% renewable energy economy seems to me frankly unrealistic, especially in the short term. that is why i believe that gas is a resource that should not be underestimated in the eu's energy needs.
in writing. ‒ this report puts renewable energy at the heart of the european union's energy model and we therefore voted in favour. we have won many of our demands in the report, such as the call for a more ambitious target of at least 30% renewable energy to be broken down into individual national targets, and the creation of a sound and transparent governance system that values the participation of citizens. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a directive on the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment against pollution caused by nitrates from agricultural sources. the commission has also asked the member states to develop a community energy strategy and to define a more favourable investment environment for self-production and self-consumption, together with the creation of single support offices. in the transport sector, we asked for and were granted an evaluation of the potential of technologies based on trolley-trucks.
in writing. this resolution, which i voted for, argues that in order to reduce the eu's dependence on energy imports, it is necessary to invest in renewable energy and energy efficiency policies. this is intended to meet the challenges posed by climate change by promoting a renewal of the production model but also ensuring energy security as a social priority. the eu's renewable energy target of 20% of total consumption by 2020 has already been achieved by many eu member states. others, however, are behind schedule and must do more. the report examines the eu's progress on renewable energy and sets out the ambitious targets for the next revision of the renewable energy directive. the importance of self-production and self-consumption of energy is emphasised, as the role of citizens and consumers is crucial for the achievement of energy efficiency objectives. the emphasis is therefore on building renovation, district heating and cooling systems. it also calls for the eu to invest in programmes that promote new technical advances in energy efficiency. i believe that the creation of a more integrated market is essential for the development of renewable energy and the reduction of energy costs.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the report on energy efficiency because this has been a crucial year for reflection and for setting new environmental, energy and climate objectives. it was the year of cop21, which set ambitious targets for an environment that is clearly suffering. yet it seems that europe is not able to meet its target of reducing co2 emissions by 20% by 2020. so let's ask ourselves what's not working. i believe that the problem facing europe in the field of the environment and energy is also the rigidity of its rules and bureaucracy, which are in sharp contrast to the economic crisis europe is facing at the same time. the objectives of energy policy, like those of environmental policy and many others, cannot be effective without the flexibility needed to adapt them to changes in the economic landscape and to global transformations. the way forward is to achieve energy efficiency and to focus on green economy as the flywheel for the economy.
in writing. ‒ in line with european priorities, the 2012 energy efficiency directive set out a set of binding measures to achieve 20% energy efficiency by 2020. unfortunately, the text has not been fully implemented by all member states, due to industrial and economic interests, which often undermine the objectives of such policies. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the directive, considering it a priority to protect the environment and the health of citizens through better cooperation between the member states in the energy sector.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the pieper report on the implementation of the energy efficiency directive. the issues of energy saving and efficiency are crucial not only for the protection of the environment and the climate, in line with the objectives set at cop21 in paris, but also for the development of european competitiveness and for an increase in employment. the 2012 energy efficiency directive and the 2010 buildings directive have been key tools in providing important innovative impetus to member states' systems of obligations and incentives. however, many countries have not implemented all the provisions in this document. the achievement of the 20% savings target is at risk and therefore efforts must be accelerated and all obstacles to investment removed. states must make full use of the subsidy system. the commission must take additional action to ensure a coherent climate and energy policy by establishing appropriate rules. the text calls on the eu to develop a long-term strategy for reducing energy demand, extending and making more ambitious the targets set by the current directives which expire in 2020.
in writing. ‒ the pieper report is biased and not acceptable. it laments the lack of implementation of the energy efficiency directive in the member states, but deliberately never mentions the real cause of this lack of implementation by the states: the eu-imposed stability pact regime, which prevents the investments needed to comply with the legislation. that is why i did not vote for this text.
in writing. ‒ in the context of the objectives set at cop21 in paris and the actions needed to achieve a resilient energy union with an effective and far-sighted climate policy, energy efficiency is clearly a key issue. nevertheless, the results achieved so far under the energy efficiency directive appear to be insufficient, with a considerable gap in actual implementation between the various european countries. some member states have not complied, or at least not fully, with their obligations to establish internal rules to promote energy efficiency, resulting in a very heterogeneous overall picture which indicates some difficulty in achieving the 2020 targets. this trend must certainly change, and that is what the european parliament has called for today. if the european union is to continue to lead on climate action, while increasing the energy security of its citizens and reducing its dependence on external supplies, a stronger and more coordinated effort at european level is needed, based on binding targets and not just for 2020, but for 2030 and beyond, as the socialist and democratic group has called for.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the energy efficiency directive because the references to ambitious and binding targets at european and national level were not removed during the vote on the amendments in plenary. we want the european union to set binding targets of 40% for energy efficiency and at least 30% for renewables, always translated into specific national targets. and the role of citizens in the broader energy transition towards a decentralised renewable energy generation model will need to be enhanced. it is crucial that the energy union really puts citizens at the centre and thus allows all europeans to escape the constraints and balances of energy geopolitics.
in writing. ‒ the european union is the world's leading territorial entity in terms of reducing greenhouse gas emissions, which have fallen by 23% over the last 20 years. european businesses and citizens have started to grow, creating jobs and generating tax revenues in an environmentally sustainable way. the eu and its member states are therefore on the right track, but need to do more to achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. the commission has already proposed a number of measures to improve the energy efficiency of buildings, such as the reduction of co2 emissions by 20%, the increase in the share of renewable energy sources in total consumption by 20%, and the improvement of energy efficiency by 20%. the commission and parliament should support efforts to achieve the objectives, in particular by working to reduce red tape in the energy sector and to reduce high price levels for medium-sized businesses and households: the calming effects of energy savings are countered by national specific tax burdens and a complex reporting procedure. energy efficiency is an important advance: the implementation of the directive will be crucial for saving citizens and businesses, as well as for achieving the europe 2020 objectives. reducing waste and improving energy efficiency are the cornerstones of a sustainable future.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of this report to ensure that the eu's energy efficiency legislation is fully implemented and accelerated and that the eu's key target of 20% energy savings by 2020 is achieved. i also reiterate parliament's call for binding targets to be introduced to ensure that renewable energy accounts for at least 30% of total energy consumption by 2030. more investment is needed in information and support programmes in the member states, which could help increase participation in the current mandatory local energy efficiency schemes, as well as promote new technical advances in areas such as cooling, lighting and insulation. in fact, the role of consumers is crucial for the achievement of energy efficiency targets, for example through the renovation of buildings, district heating and cooling systems. i would stress that energy-efficient renovation of buildings should be a priority, so as to help energy-poor residents. finally, it is essential to achieve our energy efficiency objectives by moving away from fossil fuels and phasing out subsidies for these fuels.

in writing. ‒ i regretfully voted against this proposal, which i thought was partly useful for the union. i regret to say this because i agree with better energy savings by businesses, but i am not at all in favour of a 40% mandatory saving. in addition to energy savings, what the european union needs is better efficiency in the sector, but we cannot ask companies to be more efficient if we impose such a high savings rate on them. in doing so we put entrepreneurs who will be forced to reduce industrial production considerably and workers who will be potentially unemployed at serious risk. i therefore voted against this proposal.
in writing. ‒ overall, member states are on track to meet the 20-20-20 targets. this positive development was largely due to the results of the incentive system for lower emissions, which could trigger investment in more efficient technologies. as is often the case, however, the picture is not uniform and there are strong pockets of resistance where targets are at risk. this is generally due to the greater or lesser impact of the economic crisis, but also to the greater or lesser capacity to involve businesses and citizens who, only where they perceive a direct interest in efficiency, are proactive in applying the rules. we have to go in two directions. from a regulatory point of view, we must safeguard the gains made, which could be lost if we do not act immediately by revising the directive to extend its provisions beyond 2030. secondly, member states in difficulty need to act to maximise the availability and sensitivity of consumers and businesses towards the achievement of the targets. without their support and involvement, the rules will only be perceived as punitive and restrictive and this will jeopardise the objectives.

in writing. ‒ energy efficiency and saving are important factors for protecting the environment and climate, for strengthening economic competitiveness and job creation, for security of supply and for tackling energy poverty. this report on the implementation of the 2012 energy efficiency directive recognises that we are behind the 2020 targets and at the same time calls for a much more ambitious approach for 2030, reiterating parliament's position on the need for a 40% target instead of the modest 27% proposed by the council. it also calls for these objectives to be binding on the member states, so as to make their attainment more certain. the report also sets out a number of measures to tackle energy poverty, such as the priority member states should give to energy-efficient refurbishment of public or vulnerable household buildings. the s&d group did a great job, improving the text in committee and leading the coalition of political groups to secure its adoption in plenary. i therefore thank my colleagues and vote in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the text discussed in the itre committee and presented in plenary by mr pieper concerns the implementation of the energy efficiency directive 2012/27. this directive establishes a strategic framework for the promotion of energy efficiency in the eu and imposes a non-binding 20% target for energy efficiency to be achieved by 2020. although much remains to be done to close the energy gap between member states, the commission recognised the commitment and efforts made to improve energy efficiency. the text presented and discussed in the itre committee, of which i am a member, contains interesting insights on the implementation of the legislation, with a particular focus on the period after 2020 and the strategies to be put in place on how to ensure the stability and security needed for investors. the report also refers to the measures contained in the european commission's text, but it makes changes with which i do not agree. in line with the positions i have always taken on energy efficiency, such as the achievement of ambitious but flexible targets, and in line with the ppe group, i voted against the pieper report.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the report because it contains many of our requests made in committee. the report considers energy efficiency to be key to achieving the eu's climate and energy objectives. stresses that efficiency is of paramount importance in order to reduce our dependence on energy imports, create jobs, reduce energy poverty, improve well-being and health and stimulate the economy; calls for the phasing out of fossil fuel subsidies and for the resources freed up to be channelled towards improving energy efficiency and the decarbonisation process. important victories of the m5s were the inclusion in the report of the binding eu target of 40% by 2030, with specific national targets, and the call to consider energy efficiency as a priority to increase the resilience of the energy system. we also asked that the energy saved be considered as a stand-alone resource, expressed in "negawatts". this report also calls on the eu and member states to recognise the importance of local authorities and citizens as key actors in energy efficiency in the transition to a more sustainable economy. so overall the report is ambitious and progressive, although it still includes some conservative approaches.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because, in the context of the eu's energy and climate policy, it is of great importance in setting out a set of binding measures to guide the eu in achieving the targets of increasing energy efficiency by 20%, increasing renewable energy production by 20% and reducing co2 emissions by 20%, all by 2020. unfortunately, the directive has not been fully implemented in the various member states and although it is possible that the emission reduction target will be achieved in any case, the economic and industrial crisis that has hit the eu over the last eight years will be more to the credit than the work done by the various member states. the epp rapporteur had tried to read this failure of the directive in a way that pitted industrial interests against climate and environmental objectives, calling for repeated deregulation and flexibility in the revision of the directive due in the autumn. the political and amendment work carried out by us and by the other more progressive and green forces has, however, made it possible to assess more critically the problems of implementing the directive, such as the lack of binding objectives, by putting the more conservative forces in the minority and by significantly improving the text.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, tomorrow we shall be voting on the agreement reached with the council on 6 april on the regulation on the emission limit and type approval requirements for internal combustion engines for non-road mobile machinery. this new regulation for non-road mobile machinery will replace the existing directive, covering all types of internal combustion engine installed on different types of machinery, which include small portable equipment, construction machinery, electric generators, motor cars and locomotives, inland waterway vessels, agricultural machinery such as cotton picking machines, and narrow tractors. new power ranges and new types of machinery such as cranes have been introduced into this regulation, for example, compared with the old regulation. i must say that the work on this dossier has been long and demanding and that it has also taken six trilogues - four with the luxembourg presidency and two with the dutch presidency - to reach this agreement. but i think we have reached a good agreement, a very good agreement. the work was long because the dossier was technical but also because we had to wait for the conclusion of other dossiers, such as the regulation on emissions in real driving conditions and the interinstitutional agreement on better regulation. but in the end the co-legislators did a very good job and i would of course like to thank, in addition to the council and the commission, all the shadow rapporteurs from the other political groups for this fruitful cooperation which we were able to establish from the outset and i believe that the sign of how fruitful this cooperation was was also the vote in the envi committee, where our work was almost unanimous. i think that this fruitful work has also led to a negotiating package in which parliament's priorities are clearly set out and which i believe has improved on the original commission text. i would also like to thank my colleagues in my group who supported me in my role as rapporteur and the chairman of the envi committee, mr giovanni la via, for his support in the final trilogues and, of course, also all the staff of all the institutions involved in the work, because they had to do, precisely because of the technicality of the dossier, a really great job. i say this with a certain melancholy feeling, because, apart from the fact that we have worked through several presidencies which we are now greeting - the dutch presidency to welcome and therefore wish good work to the polish presidency - i remind you that two of the shadow rapporteurs who worked with us are british and so on this, let us say, there is the melancholy of the vote on 23 june. i think the final agreement is extremely positive and i explain why: i want to do this very briefly, without going into the technical details, because i want to give the discussion time, perhaps take a few minutes to answer and then conclude. i think we have struck a really important balance between protecting the environment and safeguarding the competitiveness of european industry. we in europe will have the strictest emission limits in the world from 2019: we are talking about nitrogen oxide emissions, particulate matter emissions, and therefore air pollutants responsible for 15% of global emissions in this sector. that is why i stress the importance of the rules of procedure and also of tomorrow's vote.
member of the commission. – mr president, i would like to thank the committee on the environment, public health and food safety (envi) and warmly congratulate the rapporteur, mrs gardini, for her hard work on this file, which made it possible to find a satisfactory compromise and to swiftly adopt the regulation at first reading. a fairer and deeper single market should also care about environmental protection and health. this regulation demonstrates that the commission is delivering. in simple terms, this new regulation has two main goals: cutting emissions and cutting red tape. the new regulation provides for more stringent limits for pollutant emissions for engines installed in non—road mobile machinery. at the same time, it sets out harmonised rules for the eu markets and aligns with international standards. in this way, it is good for the environment and good for jobs and growth. it is thus not surprising that this proposal received – and still receives – broad support from the entire stakeholder community. member states count on it to fulfil their obligations on air quality targets, industries rely on it to increase their competitiveness and to gain investment and legal certainty, and social partners and ngos call for it to improve workers’ health and to protect the environment. last but not least, the european citizens deserve it as they can legitimately expect their health to be protected to the best extent possible. indeed, engines installed in non-road mobile machinery contribute significantly to air pollution and account for roughly 15% of the nitrogen oxides and 5% of the particulate matter emissions in the european union. recent studies indicate that their relative contribution to total nox emissions could become bigger over time if nothing is done. the commission has acted to propose stricter emission limits, resulting in a very significant emission reduction overall. the new regulation addresses the major air pollutants: nitrogen oxides, hydrocarbons, carbon monoxide and particulate matters, including limits for the so-called ultrafine particles, taking up the most recent conclusive evidence on their adverse health effects. let me also address briefly an important aspect for the internal market: jobs and growth. with this regulation the competitive position of european industries is strengthened in many regards: additional business potential through access to a genuine european internal market, reduced costs through reduction of administrative burden and new business opportunities through harmonising technical requirements, which give industry access to other important world markets such as the us and japan. in this way the regulation contributes to maintaining a leader position in the field of technologies through the supply of products of highest quality standards. hence, in this way we lay the foundations to create more jobs and boost growth. the adoption of this regulation will have a positive effect on the environment and on health, as well as on entrepreneurship and competitiveness in europe and this is, of course, good news.
draftsman of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection. mr president, this draft regulation was also discussed by the internal market committee (imco) and, although we are not a guarantee committee, we supported the proposal as such. the arguments put forward in support of this material have already been summarised by the rapporteur. i also want to congratulate her, because most of the amendments that were adopted in the imco committee were eventually reflected in the envi committee's opinion. and we're very pleased. our philosophy has been to support a regulation that would remove a directive that essentially introduced 28 different legal regimes in each country. replace it with a uniform regulation for the whole of europe, while adopting a regulation that preserves the competitiveness of european industry. that's our main duty, too. that's why we've included our amendments in the material. they were also discussed here. the big issue was the setting of transition periods for the different engine types. we therefore support the proposal and hope that it will be put into effect soon.
