the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am truly honoured to have the opportunity today to present my report on social inclusion and the integration of refugees into the labour market in the house. this is obviously a very serious matter, and one of the most complex challenges we have to face. i will not hide from you that i approached the drafting of the document with a certain apprehension, fully aware of the complexity and importance of the subject. i would therefore like to begin my speech by extending my sincere thanks to my shadow rapporteurs for their extraordinary contribution to the drafting of the text, and in particular for their excellent cooperation during all phases of the parliamentary work. only the enf group has shown itself to be opposed to our work, the group of marine le pen and matteo salvini, who for a change is not even in the chamber now, when we are talking about a matter such as the refugees that are often mentioned on television. as the european parliament, we are called upon to present an analysis of the situation, policies and practices of integrating refugees into the labour market and society. in preparing the document, i based my reflection on a few starting assumptions. for example, the fact that all humanitarian migrants are people who have been forced to leave their own countries and therefore represent an extremely vulnerable group. i have highlighted the current state of health of the european economy, which is still trying to emerge from a severe and protracted period of crisis, with record levels of unemployment, particularly among young people. i have pointed out that too often the public and political debate on the measures to be taken to support refugees and asylum seekers is poisoned by false myths, prejudice and discrimination, various forms of populism and, in the worst cases, even racism. let me give you some of the key points in the report. giving refugees access to the labour market is necessary to restore their human dignity and self-esteem, and is a cost-effective public policy measure, as it allows them to become self-sufficient and gain economic independence. intervening with social and employment inclusion policies in a timely manner is essential to the success of such policies. in addition, labour market conditions in host countries are a determining factor in the success and sustainability of refugee integration. the commission and member states must therefore continue to give priority to policies and investments that create jobs and generate economic growth. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on migration and asylum, in particular by ensuring that the union's policies are consistent with the union's policy on migration and integration. it would be a serious political mistake and create competition between the weaker ones, which would only lead to more social injustice. the european social fund should therefore be reduced to 25% of the cohesion policy budget. the reception conditions directive should be amended to allow applicants for international protection to access the labour market within six months of the date of submission of their asylum application. the need to increase available public investment and provide additional financial resources to be allocated directly to local and regional public administrations, civil society and voluntary organisations. they are, in fact, at the forefront of welcoming refugees into our society and therefore deserve appropriate support and greater recognition in policy-making. i hope, therefore, that the house will be able to support the report voted in the committee on employment, which i believe can be a useful document in identifying the social and occupational integration of refugees as a challenge, but also an opportunity for our society, our economy and our european union. i shall be happy to answer your questions and comments.

answer to a blue-card question. i know this very well, because i come from a land, veneto, where so many people have left. my uncles have emigrated abroad. but i also know that in italy there are many unemployed: there are people who are struggling to make ends meet, there are elderly people who no longer have money to buy medicines to treat themselves. and so i, here in the european parliament, want to defend them first of all, because we cannot save the world. i want to save and help my citizens.
member of the commission. your rapporteur, mr benifei, has produced a very comprehensive and in-depth report, and i would like to thank him again for it. several of you have said it: there are more people on the run than ever before. these are people who seek protection from us, who see a beacon of hope in the european union and who hope and count on our solidarity. we have a legal and ethical duty to provide protection to people who are entitled to international protection, and i am personally convinced that it is in the best interests of all that those who are receiving protection should also be integrated as quickly and as well as possible into our society and into our labour market. we all know that's not an easy task for anyone. the effort must come from both sides. we live in a society of rights and duties. that's the way our society is set up. but having said that, we also know that refugees are a very vulnerable group of people. if we look at their situation, they have, of course, traumas that some people have talked about, but we also know that they have degrees that they've acquired elsewhere, qualifications that they've acquired elsewhere. it is often very difficult to compare their skills, if they are already documented, with what is needed in our labour market. they are often poorly educated. we must give them the opportunity to be educated and to have basic skills. this is what we are trying to do with a number of elements of our skills agenda. we must give these people the opportunity to learn languages, which is something we have also taken up in our action programme for the integration of migrants. there are already some budgets in there that will be spent to give those people the opportunity to learn the language of the host country. i think we should not deny that there is still a lot of pure discrimination in our society, including in our labour market. we must also oppose this, and we must do something about it. what are we doing from europe? this semester we will look at the situation of migrants in the labour market. a number of member states have received specific recommendations on how they could perform better in terms of integrating people with a migrant background, sometimes even the second or third generation. and this is also true for countries other than those which have received specific recommendations. we are also using all the means at our disposal, because some of you have rightly said that this is primarily a task for the member states. but we in europe can help the member states in this difficult task. we'll do that with everything we have at our disposal. we are doing so with our action programme for the integration of people from third countries. we do this through our skills agenda, which has a number of specific elements to increase the chances of integration of refugees. we're doing the same with our blue card approach. we also use our funds: the european social fund and the feat are funds which can also be used for the integration of refugees and are being used for that purpose. we are exchanging best practice and we are ensuring that capacity building can take place in the member states. because in that area too our countries can learn from each other. we also use, again, the tools that we have at our disposal during the semester. i referred to the country specific member of the commission. – madam president, europe is on a path to recovery. we see that employment figures continue to rise and that unemployment is starting to drop. but, as we all know, the effects of the crisis are still being felt in many member states and regions, and young people in particular have borne the worst of it. fighting youth unemployment remains a top priority for the commission. therefore, i want to thank thomas händel and the committee on employment and social affairs of this house for their question on the youth guarantee and youth employment initiative. as you know, we have acted by adopting a solid policy framework on youth employment, the youth guarantee, and by dedicated funding to the youth employment initiative for those young people not in employment, education or training. this funding comes in addition to substantial european social fund (esf) intervention and on top of national funding, which is equally needed to fight youth unemployment. the youth guarantee is a driver for real reform. it is the central plank in our efforts to improve access pathways to the labour market and facilitate the transition from education to the job market, and it has already started to bring results. as regards the commission’s findings on the member states’ evaluations, it is important to stress that youth guarantee implementation has started in all member states following the planning phase. in 2014 all the member states presented their youth guarantee implementation plans, which identify precisely the measures to be taken to implement the youth guarantee. they outline the timeframe for youth employment reforms and measures, the roles of public authorities and other organisations and how the measures will be financed. the implementation of the national plans is now underway. member states are making substantial efforts to implement the youth guarantee, which has proven to be a driver for structural reforms. the joint employment reports for 2015 and 2016 list promising steps, with concrete examples in many countries. for example, member states are strengthening their public employment services to improve the outreach to those furthest from the labour market. in addition, they are building closer partnerships with the private sector to increase the number and improve the quality of job offers, apprenticeships and traineeship opportunities. the youth guarantee has also accelerated progress on delivering the skills that employers are actually seeking. the substantial european financial support available underpins the successful implementation of the youth guarantee. three years into its implementation, the youth employment initiative, worth eur 6.4 billion when including the esf contribution, is proving to be a key lever for those member states worst hit by youth unemployment. there is an indication that the youth employment initiative and the esf have an important influence on the design of youth employment policy in member states. for instance, the youth employment initiative and the esf have supported a shift to demand-based delivery of active labour market policies for young people, with a much stronger focus on individualised assistance. furthermore, the commission urges member states to continue paying special attention to the quality of offers delivered. over the past three years, member states have allocated youth employment initiative resources to concrete measures such as traineeships and apprenticeships, first job experiences and support for youth entrepreneurship. as a result, more than 1.3 million young people in europe have benefited from work and training opportunities. these are strong indications that the youth guarantee schemes are on track now, even if much still needs to be done. as regards uptake of the youth employment initiative, the additional pre-financing swiftly decided on by the european co-legislators in 2015 concretely helped to increase the work opportunities for young people on the ground. it is therefore of the utmost importance to use the available european money swiftly. in this context the 2017 draft budget includes a technical adjustment of the cohesion policy national envelopes for 2017-2020 in line with article 7 of the multiannual financial framework (mff) regulation. all member states’ allocations under the investment for growth and jobs goal of cohesion policy for the years 2017-2020 were reviewed and compared to the actual evolution of gdp. the effect of the adjustment is an increase of eur 4.6 billion, at current prices, in the 2017-2020 ceiling for commitments under economic, social and territorial cohesion – heading 1b – and concerns member states particularly affected by the economic slowdown of the past few years. we urge these member states to use the additional funds for stimulating youth employment as well as for the integration of refugees and promoting investment. i believe that all member states have to pursue the youth guarantee including by directing the necessary national resources to those dedicated actions. as regards a possible extension of the youth employment initiative, the upcoming report on progress with the implementation of the youth guarantee and the youth employment initiative and the midterm review of the mff will provide the opportunity to consider how further to provide financial support for youth employment. addressing youth unemployment and embarking on reforms in line with the youth guarantee remain a key political priority of the european union. that is what our social market economy is about. as i have said many times before, it is the commission’s firm intention to steer the european union more strongly towards social fairness. this means that no one should be left behind, in particular our youth. europe cannot afford to let the human resources that our young people represent go to waste. therefore, together with member states, we should continue our efforts for the implementation of the youth guarantee and provide the appropriate financial support.

the rapporteur. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the energy label is a european success story, begun more than 20 years ago and copied by everyone in the world. it is the commonly recognised passport that guarantees many products that are on the market and that enter the homes of 500 million citizens, to inform them about energy efficiency performance and other key characteristics. together with eco-design, the energy label has enabled european citizens to buy increasingly time-efficient washing machines, refrigerators, ovens, light bulbs and heaters in just a few years, thus saving enormous amounts of energy, harmful emissions and money, thus reducing disease, environmental damage and, not least, partially reducing the political dependence of our continent. the information capacity of the label has, however, lost its efficiency in recent years, and this is a matter of record. consumers are confused by too many different scales. the advent of the so-called "+" classes has made the difference between the steps and thus between the products less clear, in terms of energy consumption, price and other things. it is therefore right that this passport should be renewed and made more effective, taking advantage of the advances in information technology which are essential for representing and communicating the present and future market. in drawing up the draft report which i had the honour of chairing, i adopted the objectives of the original proposal with the aim of putting things back in order, eliminating the '+'s as soon as possible, digitising information and strengthening market surveillance. in recent months i have listened to the voices of consumers, industry, small and mediumsized enterprises, supervisory authorities, traders, standardisation bodies, non-governmental organisations, citizens registered with various political bodies. i have proposed a report which is deliberately broad and complex, with the aim of decisively strengthening the confidence of european citizens after the automobile scandals, which, let us remember, threaten the credibility of all our regulatory efforts. i hope that i have contributed to the proposal for a modern label, let's call it 2.0, in step with the times, able to be not only a sticker, but also a gateway to a product database, usable by everyone, with more information, comparable and finally described in their own language. the negotiations have led to a vote in committee on a solid text, which i believe is shared and balanced, and which was then unanimously approved by the itre committee and which will come to this house on wednesday for confirmation, i hope, with the same enthusiasm. among the various improvements in the text, the emphasis is on parliament's desire to strengthen the standard-setting mechanism underlying the allocation of efficiency classes; more transparency and more control and full consideration of the conditions of actual use of products; the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the new rules and will continue to monitor the implementation of the new rules. we have agreed to set up a database in two sections, one public and one with access reserved for the competent authorities; a database, which will be available as soon as possible and will also be accessible via a label query code, will allow the evaluation and comparison of data and characteristics entered by manufacturers. we have identified an automatic mechanism for eliminating the "+" from the labels and therefore the a+, a++, a+++ classes in a certain and short time, with the only exception being the group of boilers which, due to their peculiar characteristics and market dynamics, require a longer time. we have also identified a general rule for so-called "scaling" based on the employment of the upper classes. a reassignment mechanism will be activated... member of the commission. – mr president, i want to thank you for this very useful debate. i think there is a strong consensus and there is indeed a strong support to revise the energy label and make it more efficient in order to facilitate for the consumer. just a few words on the database. it is not going to be a huge administrative burden. it is actually only creating an obligation on manufacturers and importers to register the product model by uploading information that is already required under the different existing delegated acts. the technical documentation will only be accessible to market surveillance authorities, so thereby the data security will be secured. the commission already has experience with such databases, for instance in cosmetics. and regarding the costs, the actual costs could in fact be less than today because manufacturers no longer need to keep technical documentation available for market surveillance authorities for five years after the last product was manufactured. so hopefully this will be a useful tool for consumers, and not an extra burden. i agree that we need more, better and simpler standards for the whole of the internal market. unfortunately, we cannot solve that particular problem here today, but today we can send a strong signal that we are agreeing to do something important, to facilitate for the consumers, to do important work here to revise energy labelling and the commission very much looks forward to continuing working with the european parliament to finalise this proposal, and again i want to thank the rapporteur and the different shadow rapporteurs for the work that has been done here.

in writing. today's vote on energy efficiency labelling is a major milestone, coming at the end of a long process that has seen me at the forefront of the environment and industry committees. i am very pleased to say that this work has certainly borne fruit: the text which has been adopted today by the plenary reflects the progress and improvements made to the original commission text already during the work of the two parliamentary committees, in which we had succeeded in achieving important results in various respects. by returning to a single a-g scale for all products, we have tried to make the energy label clear again to consumers. we have established clear and predictable criteria for the periodic updating of labels, the so-called 're-scaling', to be implemented in line with the degree of technological development of each product group and in such a way as to ensure the durability and representativeness of the label; we have included more detailed and stringent provisions on market surveillance and conformity checks on products. i am glad that the text adopted in strasbourg does contain some new features, such as the possibility of including in the labels a reference to 'intelligent appliances', which are interconnected and can achieve greater energy savings.
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, madam commissioner, the report i am about to present concerns, in my view, fundamental aspects of the european union's trade policy, namely the relationship between international trade and human rights, social rights, environmental standards and corporate social responsibility. i think that the report makes a clear call to the commission: the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment and the protection of the health of workers from the risks arising from exposure to asbestos is a welcome one. we have too often found - and this is the point of the report - a sharp discrepancy between the verbal assertion of rights and their effective defence and enforcement. let us therefore try to give concrete indications on how to relaunch, through trade policy, the union's commitment to promote and protect human, social and environmental rights, along with democracy and the rule of law. we can't just go on like this. brexit, as well as the growing distrust of the european peoples towards this european union, should have given a clear signal about the need for discontinuity. the european union is not a mere institution, but a political body. i believe that this discontinuity is also necessary in trade policy, at a time when negotiations such as ttip and ceta, which could have enormous consequences for the lives of women and men in europe, are raising legitimate concerns, which are becoming more and more widespread in public opinion, also on the issues covered by this report: human rights, social and environmental standards. more generally, we could say, the relationship between commercial development and democracy. i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware of the fact that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter. we think it is deeply wrong, for example, not to involve national parliaments in the ratification of ceta: we need more democracy and more participation, not less democracy and less participation. we know that the union plays a crucial role in world trade: as the world's largest exporter of goods and services and the largest source of foreign direct investment, the union is taking a leading position in the global market, both through its participation in the wto and through its trade and investment agreements, which have helped to build an important piece of that extremely complex and contradictory process we call globalisation. the european union is a key player in this process. the european parliament has repeatedly expressed the need for trade policy not to be directed solely at the profit of a few companies but to be part of a strategy of international relations aimed at promoting respect for human and social rights and the protection of the environment. to do that, and that is the very purpose of this report, for the first time in the committee on international trade, a report has emerged from an impact reflection and follow-up of three reports previously approved in 2010, while providing an assessment and guidance to the commission in the implementation of our trade policy. it was a long process of discussion and mediation, of rigorous discussion with the other shadow rapporteurs, whom i wish to thank here, as well as the shadow rapporteurs of the afet, deve, femm and empl committees. the report also gives some guidance on some of the key points which i want to briefly outline here. first of all, the need for legislative consistency. the union's trade policies must be developed in a manner consistent with policies on social protection, development, human rights and the environment. we affirm the centrality of a gender reading of impact assessments and trade policy choices and it is in the perspective of gender mainstreaming, which we are also working on in the committee on international trade, that we hope for a policy that is finally gender sensitive and no longer gender blind.
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, what is international trade? i have too often, in following the debates in this parliament, had the impression that this was an objective in itself, an end in itself. but colleagues, no! trade is not the goal, it is only a means to other ends. trade is not the end, it is the race, the race to greater prosperity, equality and social progress for all. that is why the document which we want to guide the trade policy of the european union starts with this idea and goes on to lay down the conditions for the world's leading trading power to fulfil its role with responsibility, courage and prudence for its citizens and for all the citizens of the world. trade is not the end but the means. as rapporteur i am very proud of this first message, but it is the content of the resolution that makes me really proud. of course, this is a compromise text, but the fact remains that we have approved by a large majority in the committee a number of requests and priorities to make trade policy more transparent, accountable and effective. we have recognized the opportunities of trade and called for a trade policy that works for small and mediumsized enterprises, that creates opportunities in foreign markets for our farmers, for our service providers and, not least, for our industry, with agreements that bring tangible benefits to citizens, perhaps by exploring new markets. i am thinking in particular of australia and new zealand, but also of mercosur and africa. we know that trade is not just opportunity and it is not always a win-win. we have therefore called on the commission and the member states to implement policies to support the so-called losers of globalisation, and i personally think that this is another opportunity to reflect on social policies that dissociate income from work, such as minimum income or citizenship. but prevention is better than cure. that is why the resolution clearly speaks of the importance of careful impact studies, both ex ante and ex post, and of reform of trade defence instruments, clearly opposing the granting of market economy status to china, but also speaking of the defence of geographical indications and the fight against counterfeiting, in order to protect european excellence in the world. i am also very proud of all the paragraphs that insist on our responsibility for fair trade, respectful of rights and oriented towards the objectives of sustainable development. now, all the products we use every day, from cars to cell phones, are the result of a production chain that spans the entire world, with a small part of the value added in each country. the european parliament, in this document, calls for these global supply chains to be clean, sustainable and respectful; that there is a duty of care to know whether the goods you buy are bloodstained, whether they are produced by child labour or human rights violations. we have not stopped there, because we have called for the environment and animals to be included in the sustainability of trade, and we have called for greater control over compliance with the rules governing trade in protected species and farm animals. to ensure that our partners keep to these commitments, we are calling loudly for new free trade agreements to include binding sustainable development chapters with clear sanction mechanisms for those who do not respect their commitments in terms of respect for human rights and the environment and with investigations, which we want to be able to be initiated also at the request of the european parliament. the great opportunities for trade must of course be built on a solid foundation, which is the protection of european consumers and environmental, health and social standards. the resolution also calls for further reflection on those treaties and systems, such as isds and ics, which could put the interests of a few powerful people ahead of those of many citizens. citizens must be able to assess freely and at any time whether they are properly protected. we therefore call on the commission to step up its efforts to make trade policy more transparent, more understandable and more visible to the public, without more secret documents and meetings. we also make a clear appeal to the council to make it a matter of principle that parliament is consulted when negotiating mandates are drawn up and that its opinion is binding, and we also ask that all mandates approved be published. finally, the new media have increased the possibilities for citizens to participate and control the political life of the institutions. i come from a movement which has direct democracy as its flag, and i would therefore like to conclude by wishing the commission to be able to initiate more and more exchanges and dialogues with citizens on trade policy and to use the internet and the new media to give an ever more accurate account of its trade choices, thus directly ascertaining the opinion of those who are the main stakeholders, that is, the citizens. it is also possible that the negotiations on international treaties will one day be streamed live instead of being held behind closed doors, and that trade policy will become the first area of application of quasi-direct democracy. given the time, perhaps, this may seem like a dream but it is certainly a good dream. i would like to thank all my colleagues for their hard work and cooperation.

rapporteurs. when the commission presented its trade for all strategy it had three main objectives. first, of course, that the trade agreements we conclude should have effect: that they should difficult to address this. however, we do follow it very closely with our trading partners – we have, for example, the gsp+ monitoring system – and we will continue to do so. trade is, as i said, debated, and this is good. we need to do more from the commission side and from parliament’s side. member states need to do more to make sure, too, that the trade agreements we conclude are beneficial for our citizens and also complementary vis-à-vis social policy and different protection measures. we are looking now, in the commission, at how the globalisation fund can be used in a more intelligent way to protect people who are not benefiting from globalisation or trade, and we are, of course, reaching out to a number of countries – both developing countries and developed countries – the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i just want to say, in conclusion, and thank the shadow rapporteurs and the speakers again for their cooperation, that many of the recommendations that this parliament made in 2010 have been ignored by the commission. today we are giving you a clear indication of a concept: the commission has also been asked to provide a report on the implementation of the new rules on the protection of the environment. we call for a reform of the wto which will ensure respect for human rights, and for the ilo to be a permanent observer to the wto. we are calling for a reformulation of the human rights clause and the sustainable development clauses, for example, so that they are truly binding, and for the possibility of derogating from trade agreements when the real enjoyment of human rights is not guaranteed. we call for the ratification and transposition into national law of the eight plus four fundamental ilo conventions: we know how delicate this knot is when negotiating ttip with the united states, which has not signed all of them. we are calling for clear criteria for the identification of environmental assets. we are asking for action on issues such as the current intellectual property regimes. we strongly call for a shift from voluntary csr to a binding regulatory framework for multinationals. as you can see, these are very concrete indications which are intended to reiterate a concept: i am sorry to contradict the commissioner, but i do not think that ttip and ceta have gone in the right direction. greater transparency and greater democracy means giving everyone access to information; it is a matter of ensuring that human rights are not subordinated to the protection of profits.
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank all the colleagues who have contributed to this report, which has not been an easy task, because it has clearly been a compromise between very different ideas and opinions, including on trade. we have heard people tonight who are railing against free trade and competition and others who have emphasized it. i think what we have done is to send a clear message anyway - and i really appreciate the support we have had in the inta committee, which i hope to confirm tomorrow - that trade must be seen as a driver of development and well-being in an equitable way: the european union is a global community of citizens, not just for european citizens but for citizens everywhere. it is true that what we have achieved with this report is not a copernican revolution, but it is certainly a step in a better direction. to observe a reality, to see what is wrong, is not an exercise in great skill. we all can do that. the difference is that you start laying the foundation for something different. we are dealing with an economy which is already well established and with business practices which are already well established. our duty and our task is to make improvements. i believe that with these reports - both ours, as far as trade strategy is concerned, and the forenza report - we have laid the right foundations for taking trade in the desired direction, which is to create greater prosperity and not simply increase trade by a percentage, not knowing who will benefit from it. so i thank you all anyway and i look forward to a vote tomorrow that is in line.
in writing. unchecked globalisation risks having significant negative effects on social protection standards and employment levels. it is therefore important not to be spectators, and the union must instead organise itself strategically to be proactive. the commission's trade and investment strategy adopted in 2015 is therefore central, but it must be implemented within the broader framework of a coherent foreign policy. trade relations can and must also be a tool for promoting high standards of protection and promotion of human rights, as well as social protection and sustainable development. it is essential, i mean, that we be actors and not spectators of the phenomenon.
in writing. as shadow rapporteur for the s&d group on the committee on employment's opinion to the inta committee, i have been in favour of encouraging the application of social and environmental standards, human rights and corporate social responsibility in international trade agreements, both bilateral and multilateral, from the outset, ensuring not only ratification but also effective implementation of these agreements, in line with the ilo recommendations. in order to provide incentives for the application of those standards, it is necessary to provide for the possibility of incentives for companies that promote corporate social responsibility (csr) and consider proactive measures to prevent human rights or environmental violations, to identify and prevent all human rights and environmental violations, including in relation to their branches and supply chain. the horizontal introduction of these standards can promote quality work and decent work. the involvement of the social partners in the monitoring mechanism which the commission is to put in place is essential. csr can play an important role in ensuring socially and economically sustainable growth and preventing corruption at european and international level. finally, i would like to see gender mainstreaming in trade policy and greater coordination between eu policies.

president of the european council. – mr president, first of all i would like to thank the honourable members for their contributions to today’s debate. it is fully understandable that the events of the past days have produced a lot of negative emotions, but we cannot give in to these emotions. we have to preserve the ability to make sober assessments and rational decisions. first, i would like to stress that the eu is ready to proceed with an amicable divorce with the uk even today. in this process we will stand firmly on the grounds of the treaties, which have prepared us for such a situation. and one thing must be clear: the treaties have left the decision on the initiation of the divorce proceedings to the member state that wishes to leave the eu. in other words, we cannot effectively force this decision on the uk. secondly, before launching the divorce proceedings we will not undertake any negotiations on the future shape of relations between the eu and the uk. future relations will be based on a balance of rights and obligations. i would like to reassure you that, wherever there may be a conflict of interest, we will act in the interests of the eu and we will do so effectively. thirdly, today we have heard a lot of severe and critical comments aimed at member states. i want to tell you that in our talks with the leaders of member states i always repeat that there is no eu without the eu institutions. in the current situation, attacks on the eu institutions, including the commission and parliament, can only deepen the confusion. the national capitals must make an effort to stop accusing the eu and its institutions of weaknesses and failures. (applause) the referendum in the uk was lost in part because the political elite have for years been building a negative and often unfair vision of the eu. but there is no eu without the member states either. it is impossible to solve serious problems in the eu against the will of the member states. taking responsibility for one’s own words applies also to the representatives of eu institutions. today, we must combine all our efforts to agree on what our common interest is, as opposed to constantly demonstrating our individual importance in some kind of perpetual vanity fair.

in writing. ‒ the european union is strongly committed to establishing better economic, commercial and political relations with the territory of peru. the granting of visa-free short-stay visas on the basis of reciprocity is therefore an important step forward in the further and gradual rapprochement of the two cultures. given that peru poses no threat to public security and order, such an exemption will certainly make it easier for european citizens to stay in the country for work or tourism. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the gabriel report on the eu-peru agreement on the short-stay visa waiver. the text provides for an exemption for citizens of the union and for peruvian citizens travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa exemption applies to all categories of persons, regardless of the reason for their stay, provided that it is not linked to the pursuit of an activity for which they are paid. peru is a key partner in the fight against organised crime. a strengthening of relations can only encourage effective future action in this area, also ensuring a more regular political dialogue.
in writing. ‒ the text of the agreement between the european union and the republic of peru on the short-stay visa waiver is well structured and does not present any problems, which is why i voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i wholeheartedly support the new agreement between the european union and peru on the short-stay visa waiver as a privileged instrument to promote economic exchanges and foster the development of tourism in both territories. peru is one of the leading emerging countries in latin america, with stable and steady economic growth over the last decade and a relatively strong democracy. the european union is peru's third largest trading partner in terms of imports, the main recipient of its exports and the main foreign investor in the territory, particularly in the banking and mining sectors. i believe that this new arrangement will also strengthen cultural relations between the two areas and intensify cooperation on a wide range of issues, not least the protection of human rights and the fight against drug trafficking.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation today because i believe that the agreement on the short-stay visa waiver is an important step in the process of deepening relations between the european union and the republic of peru. this measure not only helps to strengthen economic and cultural relations but also intensifies political dialogue on sensitive issues such as human rights and fundamental freedoms. the agreement will boost tourism and help to strengthen trade and investment relations. peru, we recall, with 5% in 2013 and 2.4% in 2014, has recorded the highest economic growth in latin america. in terms of trade, the eu is peru's third largest trading partner in terms of imports and the main recipient of its exports, mainly in the agri-food and mineral sectors. the republic of peru supports a number of investment projects, particularly in water infrastructure. the mining sector is still the main driver, but major efforts are being made to diversify the sector in order to promote tourism as much as possible. the tourism sector is experiencing a very strong expansion, becoming the second sector of the peruvian economy since 2012.
in writing. ‒ the short-stay visa waiver has political significance and marks an important milestone in the eu's relations with other countries. it is also an instrument for strengthening economic and cultural relations and intensifying political dialogue on a range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms. peru has fulfilled the conditions for accession.
in writing. ‒ over the past decade, relations between the european union and the republic of peru have strengthened considerably to the point that the eu is now the main recipient of peruvian exports as well as the largest investor in the country. political and economic stability underpinned the conditions which made it possible to grant peruvian nationals visa-free entry conditions to the territory of the member states for short stays. the visa agreement will further strengthen relations between the two parties and give new impetus to trade and to the tourism sector, which has become the second sector of the peruvian economy. cooperation with the country will be equally important in the fight against organised crime, in particular drug trafficking and human trafficking. the signing of the strategic cooperation agreement between peru and europol is a source of hope. i voted in favour of the mandate for the conclusion of the eu-peru agreement because i believe there is no risk of illegal migration by peruvian citizens and also because the information campaign carried out by the peruvian government on visa provisions protects the eu from such phenomena.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of an 'agreement between the european union and the republic of peru on the short-stay visa waiver', because i believe that the agreement can be a tool to increase economic, cultural and political relations between the european union and the republic of peru and a tool to strengthen relations in the field of trade and investment.
in writing. ‒ this agreement with peru follows several others on the short-stay visa waiver. i agree with this proposal because i believe that giving greater freedom of movement can benefit both european citizens and the citizens of peru. i believe that greater opportunities for travel, without the long and complicated bureaucratic procedures, will greatly facilitate both the influx of tourists into europe and the movement of businessmen who are obliged to travel frequently for work. therefore, as a stable democracy and an important partner in latin america, the republic of peru deserves equal treatment. i therefore decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the conclusion of the bilateral agreement between the european union and the republic of peru is a useful tool for strengthening economic, political and cultural relations. the result is also positive for the intensification of the dialogue on the respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. i voted in favour of the agreement, which also allows the harmonization of the visa regime for the state of peru with the other latin american countries which have already liberalized visas for short stays in third countries. the agreement will boost tourism and help to strengthen trade and financial relations between the european union and peru. in addition, peru can become an important partner in the fight against organised crime by strategically cooperating with the european police office.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament has today delivered a recommendation to the european commission on the implementation and monitoring of the agreement between the eu and the republic of peru on the short-stay visa waiver signed on 9 june 2015. this agreement is an important step in the deepening of relations between the european union and peru, allowing the economic, social and cultural relations between the two continents to be further intensified and the political dialogue to be encouraged. the recommendation today calls on the commission to monitor closely the possible developments in the criteria which made the agreement possible. those criteria include not only security, public order and the control of illegal immigration, but also the union's external relations with the third country concerned, including in particular issues related to respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. the measure also calls on the commission and the peruvian authorities to ensure full reciprocity of the visa waiver in order to allow equal treatment of all citizens, in particular of all citizens of the union. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the recommendation.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement between the european union and the republic of peru on the short-stay visa waiver. this agreement represents the final step in a process of strengthening diplomatic, cultural, social and economic relations between the eu and peru and will give a further impetus to the process of strengthening democratic institutions and the rule of law in the andean country. the agreement provides for visa-free travel for community and peruvian citizens to peru and the member states of the european union respectively for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. this exemption will apply irrespective of the reason for the stay, unless it is an activity for which payment is due and which requires the normal procedures. finally, it contributes to a strong boost to tourism, trade relations and economic growth, and to a greater dynamism in relations with peru. nevertheless, it can facilitate and make more effective the fight against organised crime, in particular drug trafficking and human trafficking in the territories of both contracting parties.

in writing. ‒ the signed agreement provides for visa-free travel for citizens of the european union and for citizens of peru who are visiting the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa exemption applies to all categories of persons (holders of ordinary, diplomatic, service, official or special passports) regardless of the purpose of their stay, except for stays for the purpose of gainful employment. i would like to point out that peru has the highest economic growth in latin america (5% in 2013, 2.4% in 2014). in terms of trade, the eu is peru's third largest trading partner in terms of imports (mainly transport machinery and equipment) and the main recipient of its exports (agro-food and mining products). i am convinced that this agreement can foster cooperation between the eu and peru and create greater growth opportunities for both sides. i therefore voted in favour of adopting this agreement.
in writing. ‒ in line with the majority in the parliament, i voted in favour of the recommendation on the conclusion of the eu-peru agreement on the short-stay visa waiver. the european union is not new to such agreements, and in fact, during the june plenary session, the european parliament was asked to give its approval to a series of agreements aimed at exempting third-country nationals from visa requirements when travelling to europe for short periods. i look positively at this kind of simplification, which seems to me to be in line with one of the pillars on which the eu itself is founded, namely the right to free movement. in a rather dark period for the union, in which nationalist impulses have produced the results we all know by now, this administrative simplification seems to me to be an important sign of europe's opening up to the outside world and an interesting move from an economic point of view. that is why i voted in favour of the text.

in writing. ‒ the category of 'non-road mobile machinery' (nrmm) covers a wide variety of engines and tools, generally installed in machines intended for the transport of persons or goods. their use in europe is thought to be responsible for 15% of nitrogen oxides and 5% of particulate matter. the eu has therefore started an interinstitutional negotiation procedure with the aim of revising the emission limits for these substances. the text of the agreement has been substantially amended during the negotiations, providing for a number of concessions, derogations and significantly lowering expectations, particularly for engines intended for inland waterway navigation. for these reasons, i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ according to the european commission, air pollution in the union costs between eur 330 and 940 billion annually. in addition to these economic costs, there are also the human costs of poor air quality. the european environment agency has estimated that about 72,000 premature deaths are attributable to nitrogen dioxide and another 403,000 to particulate matter. these are worrying figures and require a more decisive eu response. i am voting in favour of the gardini report because i believe this. the proposal for a regulation adopted reduces the limits imposed by the commission, but undertakes to maintain a balance between the competitiveness of enterprises and the protection of the environment. the legislation provides in particular for the definition of different categories and subcategories of engines, setting for each of them emission limits for carbon monoxide (co), hydrocarbons (hc), nitrogen oxides (nox) and particulate matter (pm), and also foresees deadlines for their implementation from 2018.
in writing. ‒ the text is well structured and free of criticism. in addition, the new legislation on emission limits for non-road mobile machinery has been drawn up taking into account the difficulties that our companies may encounter in adapting to the new community provisions. i therefore intend to support the report by my vote.
in writing. ‒ non-road mobile engines are responsible for around 15% of carbon dioxide emissions and 5% of particulate matter emissions in the european union. this regulation has struck an acceptable balance between the need to protect the health of our citizens and the environment on the one hand, and the need to ensure the competitiveness of european industry on the other. we hope that this approach to harmonisation and the pursuit of balanced and sustainable progress will always be the practice of the eu, which must put the protection of the health of its citizens and of the businesses producing and operating in the eu first.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the regulation in question because it will make it possible to overcome the shortcomings of the current directive 68/97 on emission limits for non-road mobile machinery, which is being implemented due to its limited scope and the difficulties in adapting rapidly to technological developments in the field of engines. firstly, i think it is most appropriate that this time we have chosen to use a regulation, which will ensure, on the one hand, that the provisions apply immediately to manufacturers, type-approval authorities and technical services; the commission has also proposed that the council adopt a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. furthermore, the extension of the scope in order to promote market harmonisation will minimise the risk of (market) distortions, while the envisaged general and specific transitional periods will allow engine and machine manufacturers sufficient time to adapt to the new constraints. it is regrettable that the trilogue was not able to close the door on certain exemptions which, however, will not have much impact on the proper functioning of this regulation.
in writing. ‒ i abstained from the vote on this report because i am not satisfied with the outcome of the negotiations with the council and the commission on the need to update the emission limits for non-road mobile machinery.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation on 'emission limits and type approval for internal combustion engines for non-road mobile machinery' as i believe that its effective implementation would bring significant environmental benefits and could contribute to the competitiveness of european industry and the proper functioning of the internal market for the sector, improving transparency and reducing administrative burdens. i believe that the regulation could also remove external trade barriers and regulatory barriers by aligning the eu and us emissions requirements, also in the interests of the ongoing ttip agreement between the eu and the us.
in writing. ‒ air pollution is a very sensitive issue. i am convinced that a reduction in polluting emissions can greatly benefit the environment around us and in which we live. i agree with the proposal by my colleague, the rapporteur, elisabetta gardini, to revise the current directive in order to bring it into line with the technical progress that has been and is still being made. technology is making great strides every year, and i believe we should take advantage of these innovations to have a cleaner and healthier environment. for these reasons i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. ‒ this proposal for a regulation is positive because it has the dual objective of improving health and environmental protection standards and ensuring the proper functioning of the internal market by removing trade barriers for combustion engines. as regards environmental protection, the implementation of this regulation would bring significant benefits by reducing emissions from new engines which will, over time, replace older and more polluting engines. as regards the competitiveness of european industry, the aim is to reduce the risks of market distortion by simplifying type-approval legislation, improving transparency and reducing administrative burdens. moreover, by aligning eu and us emissions requirements, it removes barriers to foreign trade and reduces regulatory barriers. in order to allow manufacturers of combustion engines to adapt to changes in production while respecting the requirements of this regulation, it is appropriate to introduce a sufficient degree of flexibility, allowing for adaptation to new production standards without hampering the competitiveness of eu companies.
in writing. ‒ the non-road mobile machinery sector is a major contributor to air pollution, because of its harmful emissions in the form of gases or particulate matter. according to recent data from the european commission, this represents 15% of all nitrogen oxides (nox) and 5% of all particulate matter in the union, with very serious consequences for both the environment and health. these reasons made a review of directive 97/68/ec urgent. the new regulation adopted today introduces stricter limits on the emission of pollutant gases from vehicles and defines a 'tiered' approach, i.e. differentiated according to engine size and machine type. this is a reasonable choice because it allows for the gradual introduction of the sector concerned by the new requirements and takes into account the wide variety of machines and engines being produced. i believe that effective and rapid implementation of the rules laid down in this regulation will help to improve the impact of non-road mobile machinery on air quality, with considerable benefits for our citizens both in terms of the environment and health. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on 'emission and type-approval limits for internal combustion engines for non-road mobile machinery' because i share the eu's air quality policies aimed at protecting health and the environment. the resolution proposes a gradual reduction in emissions and the replacement of older engines which cause the most pollution, thus providing for legislation common to all member states aimed at the proper functioning of the internal market.
in writing. ‒ in the eu, emissions from non-road mobile machinery (a wide range of engines, from the smallest powered hand tools to locomotive engines) are estimated to account for 15% of nitrogen oxides and 5% of particulate matter and their use, particularly in urban centres where their concentration becomes a significant source of air pollution. the revision of the current legislation was necessary in order to establish stricter limits that took account of technological progress. the negotiation of the package, after extensive concessions to the council, has undergone major changes aimed at extending both the categories to be granted derogations and their duration, delaying the implementation of the legislation and reducing the level of ambition for the reduction of both nox and particulate matter and, finally, a low commitment to ensure retrofitting on existing machinery. the only positive aspect of the negotiations is that they have resulted in the definition of important technical details through delegated acts rather than implementing acts. therefore, in the final vote, i decided to abstain.

in writing. ‒ the commission's proposal for a regulation aims, firstly, to help address public health concerns, improve air quality and create a barrier-free market, not only at union level but also with its main trading partners worldwide. the non-road mobile machinery sector is one of many sectors contributing to harmful emissions in the form of gases or particulate matter. to address this problem, the commission proposes to set stricter standards for most engines already covered by the current directive 97/68/ec and to extend this scope to new engine power ranges, new types of combustion and fuels, and a number of new categories of machinery, with the aim of closing the gaps in the legislation. the regulation therefore sets new emission limits for engines installed in non-road machinery such as construction, agricultural, locomotive and inland waterway vessels. this is certainly a legislative act that increases the protection of the health of citizens and helps to combat global warming. for these reasons, i have decided to vote in favour of the adoption of this regulation.
