vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. – mr president, let me join you in welcoming our dear friends here. this is also, as you said, a concrete result of the work that sometimes we do silently but with good outcomes so i am glad to see you here. let me touch upon a few points you raised. i have noticed an overwhelming feeling of ownership in this house. that is something good on which i count because, as some of you mentioned, this has been collective work that now acquires a collective follow-up to make sure that we move from the vision into action. first of all, some asked whether we stress more the values or the interests, and whether we define more as an important element of our action in the future our values or our interests. the ground of the strategy, the clear indication of the strategy, is that our values and our interests coincide very much. there is one element in our values that the strategy underlines, which is that, to make our action consistent, we have to be true to our values first of all in our internal policies, and in our own behaviour, and this is something that echoes also some of the elements that some of you underlined. any global strategy starts at home and any external credibility is rooted in our internal strength. this is why, in these difficult moments for the european union, it is so important that we think of our common responsibilities towards our citizens and towards the rest of the world. second, as i was saying, values and interests coincide here. think of the resilience that is so much at the centre of our strategy, as was mentioned in the first intervention. resilience of societies around us is indeed an investment in our own security, and when we mention resilience of societies in the strategy we do not mention the strength of institutions only, but we mention the resilience of societies as such, which includes the space for civil society, human rights defenders and the place for every citizen in their own society. is this responding to our values only, or is this also responding to our interests? i believe, and the strategy reflects this common indication, that in this case, as well as many other cases, following our values also responds to our interests and we would be making a mistake if we were to put this in contradiction. third, i would like to refer to one point that a couple of you raised, one in a negative sense, and another one, mr danjean, in a positive one, on the so-called ‘train and equip’ or capacity-building in security and development. it is true it took us three years to come to that. yesterday the college as you might know adopted the package on capacity building on security and development, and let me tell you very clearly: this is not at all a diversion of our development tools into a security or military approach. on the contrary, this is a response to what, especially our african friends, not only governments and institutions, but also civil society, are telling us, that if in a territory, be it in the sahel, be it in nigeria, be it in the horn of africa, if you have a lack of basic security conditions for the populations, you can do all the development you want but, first of all, it does not get there, and second, it is not effective at all because the first basic right to security has also to be guaranteed. this does not mean that again we are diverting resources from one chapter to the other. this simply says that we need to use our resources in a coherent way and respond to the needs of the populations we are working with, and all the messages we are getting are in the sense that we need to also work on security as we continue to work on development. we always say there is no security without development, but there is no development without security. it is now also a matter of turning this into practice, so that is why i think that the package we adopted yesterday is something that is going to be extremely important in our capacity to implement also part of the strategy, using our different instruments, keeping in mind that they are different and covering different areas but in a coherent and integrated way. i received a specific question on part of the strategy that refers to the fact that member states can be asked or tasked to actively contribute to specific common foreign policies that are determined all together. it is a part of the strategy that was carefully thought of, as you can imagine, and it responds to the fact that, on one side, we need to keep the unity not only of the 28 member states, but also the different institutions, including this parliament, and this is what is done in the framework of the common institutions, but there might be occasions where we might want or we might need or we might want to encourage one or a group of member states or – why not? – some parliamentary delegations, to complement the work that we do all together. there can be specific added value that one or the other can bring. the important thing is that this is done in a coordinated manner with a clear, transparent link to common decisions and with common approaches and reporting back to the common instances. so i would never be afraid of initiatives, whether they are from parliamentary delegations or from a group of member states, or a group of commissioners that i lead quite often in our partner countries or in other countries. the important thing is that all of this is in a common framework and towards a common goal. we do not have to be afraid of our added value, even when it is a partial one. the important thing is that this is part of a coherent and concerted policy. here i come to the basic needs we have now and many of you mentioned that. the basic need we have now is to guarantee that the european citizens are guaranteed their right to security, and this requires the european union to act as a european union, united. there is one thing that i would not follow, one suggestion i would not follow, that one of you mentioned in your intervention – it was not mentioned in the english language, but you said there is the need to take more into account opinions that are contrary, that are opposed to working more together. you have to listen to those who say ‘the european way is not the way’. i am sorry but i am not going to hear those voices in this field because if there is one field where it is self-evident that the security of the european citizens require european action, it is our work in the world. there is no single field in our external action where one member state alone, whether it is the biggest, the strongest, the richest, the smallest, is more effective alone than all together. there is not one single thing, be it counter-terrorism, be it trade, be it development, be it migration management, there is not one single issue where we are stronger alone than stronger together. and i believe our citizens in this field see it very clearly. threats are global, opportunities are global, all of our countries, compared to the rest of the countries in the world, are small-sized countries, at the maximum medium-sized countries. we are not living in the era of empires anymore, not for a couple of centuries. and we have to wake up to reality. our strength is our european union in the world, and our partners around the world see it very clearly and recognise our strengths in the world. what we sometimes do not do is recognise this strength inside our union, but we have to come out of this sort of depression we have entered and make use of our strength, because you can be strong, but if you know you are strong you do not use your strength and it is useless. so i hope that we can indeed, as some of you said, use a strategy to turn our common vision and action into those of a self-confident, global player. i think this is the basic thing we have to do now. i have noted that some of you said that this strategy is too ambitious and unrealistic. others have said it is too realistic and not ambitious enough. we need both. we need both realism and ambition, also because we see these days that things change, internally and externally. things change in a way that was unforeseeable just a few months or years ago. the point here is whether we want to react to a change that is produced somewhere else, or if we are confident enough to try and shape the change that is happening around us, and i believe that we have all the tools, all the strength if we have the political will to do it exactly as our citizens have an interest in us doing this. thank you.

the commission's proposal for a regulation on the application of the principle of subsidiarity to the regulation of the european communities is a step in the right direction. however, certain essential elements will have to be taken into account when finalising the work to ensure that these objectives are actually achieved and that there are no negative repercussions on the real economy. firstly, the commission will have to make sure that the basle committee follows what the central bank governors responsible for supervision said last january, namely that the reform should be completed without significantly increasing the overall capital requirements of the banking system. the commission will also have to ensure that the basel committee draws up this reform package on the basis of a comprehensive and transparent analysis and takes into account, in its calibration, not only the overall effects but also the distribution of the impact on the different business models, avoiding negative spillovers, especially on commercial banks. these banks, despite the difficulties of recent years, have shown greater strength than investment banks and have been key to supporting the economic and employment recovery and it would be wrong to penalise them with a sharp tightening of capital requirements, especially if not justified by an actual increase in riskiness. i therefore hope that the commission will make sure that the calibration of operational risk is not too punitive for commercial banks. finally, the commission will have to work to ensure that the reduction of the volatility of the value of risk-weighted assets, which was a primary objective of the basel reform package, retains its centrality and that a level playing field is ensured between banks using internal valuation models and banks using standard models, for example by limiting the results of internal models downwards and anchoring them to those of standard models.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, banks are companies and cannot think of escaping the normal rules of the market to which all companies are subject. the bank, like a company that makes spoons or chairs, produces products and has to sell them. in order to sell them, it must have a capital base which allows it to be economically and financially balanced, but it cannot do without taking risks, because the risk is delivered within the normal market size. if there were no risks for banks and only for companies, banks and companies would not be able to talk. so we want the bank to be safe on the one hand, and therefore the risk to be weighed but not to be cancelled out, so that in the dialogue with the companies that take risks every day to generate value, we can play on equal terms. we have an entrepreneurial fabric which, as the honourable members have pointed out, in europe, especially in the small and mediumsized enterprises, generates about 80% of employment. my country, italy, is being dragged towards one side, that of northern italy, where almost all the businesses are small and mediumsized and need banks that are fairly efficient, that are absolutely balanced in terms of capital, but that are willing to look at the ability of companies to produce value, not just able to look at their internal condition. we need a banking management that looks at the quality of the business to be financed and that finances what is worthwhile and eliminates what is not. so, risk sharing is the essential element for the system to hold.
in writing. i believe that the basel revision proposal represents an unfinished but positive step forward in the absurd problem of disparities and asymmetries in the internal risk assessment models that banks can use to calculate capital requirements. partial and late revision, which must be supported in any case. in fact, giving banks the possibility to rely on internal rating models not only creates complexity and difficulties in assessing and comparing the actual risk exposure of banks, thereby hindering transparency and supervisory activity, but above all opens the way to manipulation of the models, thanks to which large investment banks have often succeeded in lowering their capital requirements. however, i cannot help criticizing the basle approach which, by focusing all its attention on credit risk and the capitalisation of individual banks, neglects the most important aspect from the point of view of the stability of the financial system, namely exposure to derivatives and speculative activities with enormous systemic risk. unfortunately, until we limit leverage, reduce interconnectedness, curb speculation and address the problem of too-big-to-fail banks, the root causes of the 2008 financial crisis, nothing can reassure us of the threat of a systemic crisis of even more catastrophic proportions than the previous one.

in writing. ‒ studies show that 68% of adolescents and 18% of children regularly consume energy drinks, mainly in the form of cans. a single 250-ml can can contains up to 27 grams of sugar and about 80 milligrams of caffeine. these are widely consumed drinks, but their consumption has been associated with headaches, sleep disturbances and behavioural problems in children and adolescents who use them regularly. my vote in favour of the objection tabled today in parliament is motivated by the belief that it may be harmful to allow the presence of nutritional claims on sugar-sweetened beverages and energy drinks containing caffeine which promote their ability to increase attention or concentration. i am convinced that the use of nutrition labels in this case may encourage excessive consumption of energy drinks, which is why i strongly supported the motion for a resolution by the envi committee.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the title of the report we are discussing today may make one think of problems far away, but in reality it deals with issues that are very close to the european citizens and of the utmost relevance. the africa trust fund is a very delicate instrument which must be planned well, operated effectively and communicated properly. europe is at a crossroads today. it has the potential to positively impact the lives of millions of people, or it can be driven by fear and national selfishness and therefore fail in its objectives. the trust fund for africa is designed to respond to the need to address the root causes of migration through interventions aimed at creating development in those countries experiencing mass migration. the effectiveness of the fund requires: 1) to operate in the long term in a defined and programmatic manner, thus avoiding intervention in an emergency only; 2. pay particular attention to the least developed countries, making appropriate differentiations between the different contexts; (3) investing in education, health, training and essential public services; 4) involve ngos and local civil society in the planning and implementation of all projects in the field; (5) to provide for forms of control and periodic monitoring by this parliament of the use of the funds; (6) to provide for transparency, information and dissemination obligations for results which are easily verifiable by the public; 7) to require the member states to honour their promises of additional funding. for these reasons, the report i am presenting in this house seeks to make it clear that we agree both on the need to pool more resources to deal with the root causes of the problem and on the nature of a tool which will allow us to act quickly and flexibly in the face of urgent situations, just as we agree to restore the necessary budgetary units. at the same time, however, we cannot fail to point out that some questions remain. the accession countries, for example, make promises with pomp and circumstance, as we saw at the valletta summit last november, but then, behind closed doors, they forget their promises and commitments. we must also point out the real risk that development funds may be diverted to other areas, such as border controls in the countries concerned. this type of intervention has nothing to do with development and will never solve the root of the problem. i would like to conclude by stressing that all these issues have been the subject of constructive debate between the political parties, which has continued during the amendment phase and after the vote in the committee on development. similarly, thanks to the online democratic participation tools we use as the five star movement, such as the rousseau system, many citizens have had the opportunity to learn about the draft report and to express their views, and some of these comments have been transformed into amendments for my signature and have been included in the text voted in committee. finally, i would like to thank all the shadow rapporteurs for their willingness to contribute over the past few months to the preparation of a good parliamentary report on such a sensitive subject.

growth and restore confidence. i think that in a context of questions, this challenge was important, and it was met. we have presented a number of cases in which the european union is at the forefront. i am thinking of everything that goes in the direction of a comprehensive growth strategy, in the idea of pursuing structural reforms, but also of positioning ourselves as an example in the field of taxation, the fight against tax evasion and being a promoter of international trade and a defender of investment. these were the top priorities of the world's leading leaders. our strategy has been to show that our european triangle - investment, structural reforms, responsible public finances - is working, but we must continue along this path to ensure change is sustainable and positive in the long term. you could accuse me of complacency for saying that. no, there is no point in complacency, it was said and repeated in most of the interventions during our two days in hangzhou as a call for urgent action to provide tangible results for our citizens who are waiting for them. our major economies are very closely interlinked, and slow global growth is facing, as we know, multiple obstacles. the risk of a vicious circle was well identified: low productivity growth, inequalities also growing, all provoking a populist response 'we don't have the privilege' which in turn slows down reforms and, consequently, slows down growth even more and so on. the g20 therefore decided to use all policy tools - monetary, budgetary and structural - to stimulate growth and to focus on reform efforts. cooperation has also been launched on innovation and the digital economy to increase productivity and long-term growth. in addition, the g20 leaders delivered a strong message: after a long period of crisis, we must look to the future; the benefits of growth, of globalization, of innovation, must be enjoyed by all, not just by a privileged few. for the first time, and i have been attending these summits for a number of years now, a concept has entered the public debate, and that is a good thing. this is the concept of inclusion, a fundamental principle which should be observed by placing more emphasis on skills, on social protection, but also on the definition of fiscal, commercial and other policies which must take into account this parameter of inclusive growth. the priorities of this commission, like those of the g20, are, as you know, already geared towards social justice. trade was also on the agenda. international trade is a driver of jobs, growth and development. that is why we are concerned about the slow growth of world trade and why we continue to defend free trade vigorously against the emerging protectionist temptations. but the commission has also stressed very strongly that free trade must be fair if it is to have the support of our peoples and this parliament. to be in favour of free trade is not to be in favour of free trade under any conditions, on any terms, without reservation or regulation. the g20 has a key role to play in supporting a robust and rules-based multilateral trading system. we have stressed this point in our discussions at the g20 and the president of the commission has personally been involved in a fight which i know is very important to this parliament: defending the interests of the european steel industry and workers affected by a situation of global overcapacity and, let us say, chinese overcapacity. this is also an issue on which an important step was taken in hangzhou, with the g20 agreement, to form a global forum on steel capacity with the support of the oecd and of course the approval of the chinese presidency. fair international taxation is another essential condition for restoring our citizens' confidence in the global economy and also for enabling government to provide the investments and services so necessary to our economies. all companies, i keep saying here, as the tax commissioner, must pay their fair share of taxes in the countries where they make their profits. you know that the european union is at the forefront of these efforts and that it has already adopted several very ambitious proposals last year. we were encouraged to see the g20 countries as a whole once again firmly and strongly committed not only to implementing past agreements but also to going further in the wake of the panama papers, which, it is true, continues to weigh on people's minds. the g20 therefore agreed to establish a list of non-cooperative jurisdictions for the next summit in 2017 and to consider defensive measures in case of non-compliance. this international g20 list is complementary to the list that the european union itself is about to launch and which should also be operational in 2017, with the issues that are complementary and which, i believe, fit well together. the g20 will continue to lead the work of the fatf in the fight against terrorist financing. the leaders called for swift and resolute implementation of its new strategy against terrorist financing and for enhanced coordination with those outside the task force, particularly vulnerable countries. the hangzhou meeting also provided an opportunity to discuss the reform of financial regulation, which, i would remind you, was a flagship initiative of the g20. the focus is now on the consistent implementation of agreed reforms, such as the basel iii framework and its finalisation by the end of 2016. the chinese presidency also intensified discussions on the international financial architecture. we know there is continuing risk to the global economy. the unanimous agreement to maintain a strong imf with sufficient resources is a welcome achievement. last year in antalya, we called on the g20 to recognize the refugee crisis for what it is: a global challenge that requires a global response. with the help of this parliament, the european union has put in place a comprehensive package of measures to manage this crisis, but we can only meet this challenge if the international community as a whole makes a concerted effort. we have sent a clear message to our g20 partners that we want the level of solidarity between nations needed to solve this still-missing problem to emerge now. the answer is one of resolute but cautious optimism. g20 members said they were ready to share the burden of the refugee crisis, specifically calling for increased financial assistance and resettlement of refugees. the g20's cooperation to support development, food security, particularly in africa, is also important from the point of view of controlling migration flows. the summit also provided an opportunity for the g20 to reaffirm its commitment to the paris agreement. the pace of ratification is good and it is now very likely that the threshold for the entry into force of the agreement - i am talking about cop 21 - will be reached this year. the main message from the european union to the g20 members in this regard is that they must act now just as quickly to implement this agreement. of course, as you can imagine, many of the leaders at the summit wanted to hear the european public's response to the uk referendum. president juncker reassured them that we were ready to deal with this once the uk government had communicated its intentions. you know that the commission has appointed its negotiator, my compatriot, the french commissioner's predecessor, michel barnier. we want to build a new partnership with britain that works for everyone. i always think of one formula, and i share it with the british government: britain, by its own choice, will no longer be a member of the european union after these negotiations, but it will remain a european nation that is decisive for a whole series of policies that we have to pursue together. at the same time, the president stressed that there was much that the eu-27 could achieve together. that is our objective for the future and it is in that spirit that the president will address the house tomorrow in his state of the union address, speaking at the same time of the europe of the 28, which is ours, the europe of the 27, which is our future, and the europe of the 19, that of the euro zone, which is the beating heart of europe. but i do not want to prejudge what he will say to you, i think it will be an important moment for the commission, for parliament, for the european union, before the meeting of the leaders of the 27 which will take place in bratislava on 16 september. these are some of the things i wanted to share with you. i would not like to go on, i can come back later to this g20 meeting, which i believe was once again organised in an impressive way by china, very well conducted by the chinese president, with many results that are quite in line with what the european union could expect.
president-in-office of the council. – madam president, i am grateful for the invitation to discuss the outcome of the g20 summit which took place last week in china and where the european union was represented by president tusk and president juncker. g20 leaders discussed various topics of global importance and, crucially, issues on which the g20 should provide leadership. i will focus on issues which i find are of particular relevance from the point of view of the council, including migration, the global economy, trade, taxation and climate. let me start with an issue which is very high on our agenda, namely the management of migration. i consider the g20’s recognition of the current crisis as an issue of global concern to be a very positive signal. the eu has stated in international forums on various occasions that migration requires efficient and coordinated action and it calls for all stakeholders to take responsibility in a spirit of partnership and burden sharing. the eu and its member states are fully assuming their responsibilities, but expect other partners, namely our g20 partners, also to do their part. the communiqué by g20 leaders is a step in the right direction, as it calls for scaled-up support to refugees and host communities. the eu will certainly use the opportunity of the forthcoming new york summit on refugees and migration, which you will discuss with high representative mogherini later today, to take the g20 conclusions forward and pursue more equitable sharing of responsibility for what is clearly a global challenge. my second point is the global economy. g20 leaders in china pointed to the progressing global economic recovery, while recognising that growth was still weaker than desirable and that downside risks remained. challenges originating from geopolitical developments were also mentioned. accordingly, leaders declared their determination to use all policy tools –monetary, fiscal and structural – individually and collectively to achieve the intended growth. importantly, there was the recognition that growth needs to be inclusive in order to ensure that it serves the needs of everyone and benefits all countries and people so that no one is left behind. this is recognised in the hangzhou action plan, which summarises the main commitments by g20 members. the g20 summit also made a strong case for international trade as a driver of global economic recovery. to this end, g20 leaders committed to strengthening an open world economy by working towards trade and investment facilitation and liberalisation. the establishment of the g20 trade and investment working group is an important step in this regard. the g20 reaffirmed its commitment to the multilateral trading system, with the wto at its core, and to advancing the post—nairobi work in the wto, including the outstanding issues of the doha development round, with a view to achieving positive outcomes at the next wto ministerial conference in 2017. i also welcome the g20 commitment to ratifying the trade facilitation agreement by the end of this year and its call for other wto members to do the same. the eu, for its part, has already ratified. however, we need to recognise that anti-globalisation sentiment and opposition to trade are increasing. the g20 therefore emphasised the need to communicate the benefits of trade and open markets more effectively and to ensure that the benefits of trade are spread more widely. it also recognised the structural problems caused by excess capacity in some industries, most notably in the steel sector, and agreed that this required a collective response. g20 leaders therefore agreed to establish a global forum on steel access capacity, which should report to the relevant g20 ministers in 2017. let me mention two more issues. taxation is another priority that the eu shares with the g20. i particularly welcome the establishment of the g20/oecd inclusive framework for the implementation of the base erosion and profit shifting initiative (beps) as well as its first meeting in kyoto. the eu has pioneered beps implementation with the recent adoption of the anti-tax avoidance directive (atad), but timely, consistent and widespread implementation of the beps package at global level remains critical in order to establish an international level playing field and avoid further loopholes. i am also satisfied with the endorsement of the proposal for objective criteria to identify non-cooperative jurisdictions with respect to tax transparency and with the objective to prepare, by july 2017, a list of jurisdictions that have not yet sufficiently progressed towards a satisfactory level of implementation, as well as to consider defensive measures against them. following the adoption of conclusions on taxation last may, the council has already started to determine, on the basis of a first screening by the commission, non-cooperative third country jurisdictions with which dialogues should begin during the course of next year. the objective is to establish an eu list of such jurisdictions and explore defensive measures at eu level, in the tax as well as in the non-tax area, to be endorsed by the council by the end of this year. finally, the g20 summit reaffirmed the commitment of its members to sustainable development and strong and effective action to tackle climate change. the g20 leaders are committed to countries’ ratifying and implementing in a timely fashion all aspects of the paris climate agreement, including financial assistance for developing countries. in particular, the g20 supported efforts to enable the paris agreement to enter into force by the end of 2016.
on behalf of the s&d group, madam president, ladies and gentlemen, reglobalization, rule sharing and inclusion: the g20's key words are these, but they must be implemented now so that they are not empty words. reglobalization, because we have a duty, as the european union, first of all, to create a new globalization that assesses the impact of global phenomena, trade agreements, the digital revolution, migration flows and introduces appropriate corrective measures to leave no one behind. sharing, because we need rules and trust between partners. the establishment of a forum to monitor excess capacity, starting with steel, is a first positive sign. finally, inclusion, so that everyone is part of it and does their part. significantly for the first time this summit recognises the importance of women's inclusion as drivers of growth. in the face of the failures of the old globalisation, a protectionist response is as easy as it is harmful. it's up to us to come up with a new proposal that keeps the world connected without leaving anyone behind.
on behalf of the efdd group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the last g20 meeting in china did not produce the results that we would all have the right to expect from such a summit, nor the decisions that the gravity of the world situation would require. however, positions which are useful for moving towards a more genuine and more shared progress have emerged and in some cases have been affirmed. i would like to emphasize the few positive factors, rather than the problematic ones, which are there, especially in terms of omissions. i believe that a reality such as the european union must demonstrate its capacity to design and implement in order to be credible in the world and thus to have an impact on it. firstly, there is support for the fight against climate change. now that the major polluters in the world - i am thinking of the united states and china - have ratified the paris agreement, the european union must not only ensure that all member states do so swiftly, but also ensure that the third countries involved do the same. the green finance initiative and the proposal to channel a significant share of the funds currently allocated to fossil fuels towards clean energy solutions should also be considered in this context. in this sense, we expect the commission to give substance to the circular economy project. the declaration to build an open and resilient financial system based on international cooperation on taxation and financial transparency is also an element that should not be overlooked, but it must be put into practice very quickly. i hope that this parliament will want to tackle these issues and that the commission will do so as soon as possible with the 2017 work plan.

in writing. at the g20 hangzhou summit on 4 and 5 september, the eu reiterated the need for joint action to achieve objectives such as the fight against international terrorism and corruption, increased cooperation in the field of taxation, combating overproduction in the steel sector and finally resolving the migration and refugee crisis. the g20 summit's responses to these last two priorities are particularly noteworthy. finally, there is a growing awareness that we must tackle together the effects of the migration crisis that has hit europe, in order to respond to the needs of refugees for protection and to the root causes of a crisis that has caused the death of thousands of human lives. moreover, as promised by the g20 leaders, a collective response will be needed to combat the excess production of some countries in the steel sector, china over all. it would therefore be useful to set up a specific forum to monitor these countries and thus combat a phenomenon which is likely to endanger production in the steel sector and the millions of workers who work in what must remain a vital sector for european and italian industry.

on behalf of the efdd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, despite the low expectations for the effectiveness of the committee of inquiry, i believe that its work is yielding a number of significant elements which are useful in identifying the shortcomings, the weaknesses, the opacity of the whole system of vehicle typeapproval and emission control. one thing is for sure: the defeat devices are just the tip of the iceberg of the entire system. i do not want to dwell on the report, but i would like to take this opportunity of speaking in plenary to denounce publicly that the report on the investigation into euro 5 diesel cars sold in italy, a report drawn up by the italian ministry of infrastructure and transport, is an insult to the work of the committee of inquiry of this parliament and above all is gravely offensive to european citizens, who deserve seriousness, competence and maximum transparency from the institutions. the report is intentionally incomplete and omissive: the investigations into the 15 cars initially mentioned in the report follow different procedures depending on whether they are cars of the fca group or not; the commission has also taken the view that the aid granted to the italian authorities is compatible with the internal market. the traces of some fiat and jeep models are completely lost, literally disappearing from the charts and tables in the document. it just so happens that these are the models for which there are the strongest suspicions of illegal devices, in one case devices that seem to turn off after twenty-two minutes, exactly two minutes after the end of the type approval test cycle and, in the other, a model that in the hot test has shown emissions of nitrogen oxides three times the norm. we are facing a clumsy attempt to hide the real values of fiat cars. the five star movement proposes that this report be returned to the sender, which is an insult to the emis committee, parliament and the italian and european citizens.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the work of the committee of inquiry has made it clear that the volkswagen scandal is only the tip of the iceberg. it's not just the fraudulent use of devices designed to protect engines in particular conditions, it's more. as early as 2007, but officially since 2011, it was known that cars on the road had 7-8 times higher emissions than those tested in the laboratory during the homologation process. it is a serious fraud against users and a blow to the air quality of our cities, a fraud all the more serious because the technologies to reduce nox emissions have been around for a long time. that is why it is essential to move forward with real-world emissions controls on the road, to change the type approval rules profoundly, to go beyond controls which are only entrusted to individual national states and to have clearer and stricter rules for consumer protection.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we have repeatedly stressed the leading role of the european union in the fight against environmental pollution: the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the eu's emissions trading system is not disrupted by the introduction of new technologies. however, such leadership comes with obligations. the commission of inquiry into dieselgate which this parliament has set up must send a strong signal of great rigour and thoroughness in its conduct of the inquiry, so that the world does not have to say that europe is the first to break those rules. we must take a firm stand, and if necessary have the courage to denounce any failure to take appropriate measures to enforce the explicit ban on handling equipment. the credibility of the european union also depends very much on this inquiry.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this report because it is a comprehensive and convincing text and i believe that assessing the implementation of research and innovation strategies is very important in order to guide the european programming that is under way. unfortunately, many countries - including italy - are still lagging behind in terms of public investment in innovation and technological research, and this gap needs to be closed as soon as possible for the benefit of the whole economy, especially at a time when innovation is a valid response to the crisis. the ris are also essential for the implementation of cohesion policy itself. only innovative solutions can and should be used, for example, to increase the administrative capacity of local authorities. the small and mediumsized enterprises are also asking for this, because they are forced to deal with systems which are still archaic and complex. i support an assessment and review in 2017 of what has been done to date to make up for the backlog and to meet commitments.
in writing. ‒ the smart specialisation strategy (ris3) comprises multiple policies covering different areas such as entrepreneurship, education and innovation and is therefore a key element for the allocation of eu funds to member states and regions. given the crucial role of smes and start-ups in regional development, the importance of business support systems and the need to adopt reliable systems to monitor efficiency at all levels of governance, i decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the valcárcel siso report on cohesion policy and research and innovation strategies for smart specialisation. this is an important text that underlines the need to step up efforts to create smart, sustainable and inclusive economic growth. this is a necessary choice, especially at a time when europe still seems to be suffering the effects of the world economic crisis. the report stresses the central role of the ris3 in achieving the europe 2020 objectives, while highlighting those aspects which should be considered of particular importance, i.e. first and foremost the correct analysis of the priorities, strengths and potential of the different regions, but also the use of appropriate methodologies which provide for the development of periodic quantitative and qualitative monitoring. the development of participatory processes and the creation of synergies between public and private actors is another crucial point closely linked to the theme of multilevel governance. a serious bottom-up approach needs to be revived as soon as possible to foster new synergies and innovation-driven growth.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today because strengthening research, technological development and innovation is of fundamental importance for achieving the objectives of cohesion policy. in particular, national or regional innovation strategies for smart specialisation (ris3) are needed to foster a more efficient use of the european structural and investment funds and to support the transition to a smart and sustainable economy. within the framework of the innovation strategies for smart specialisation (ris3), i believe that regions should develop innovative support services schemes that complement or replace existing support services in order to enable a given region to fully exploit its competitive potential, help businesses absorb new knowledge and technologies to remain competitive, and ensure that research and innovation resources reach a critical mass.

in writing. ‒ the european regional development fund (erdf) states that in the 2014-2020 programming period, regions should focus investments in rdi through smart specialisation strategies. in this context, ris3 is an ex ante condition for the granting of european structural and investment funds (esi funds) to eu member states and regions. the granting of these funds can only take place, as a matter of right, following the achievement of certain objectives, among which are: the development of periodic quantitative and qualitative monitoring; the development of participatory processes; involving stakeholders, with a particular focus on the private sector; creating synergies between public and private actors; coordinating across all levels of governance and identifying alternative funding modalities. i believe it is vital that the european union continues to strengthen its capacity to invest in research and development. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this resolution.

in writing. ‒ following the scandals that followed revelations of rigged devices used to reduce pollutant emissions during official car tests, the european parliament decided last december to set up a committee of inquiry. the aim is to examine complaints of infringement and maladministration in the application of union legislation on emission measurements in the automotive sector. the emis committee started its work in march, setting a precise timetable for the final report due in spring 2017. the interim report presented to parliament today, which i have decided to support with my vote, calls on the committee of inquiry to continue its work and to support all actions and initiatives aimed at ensuring that its mandate is fulfilled. the text calls on the member states and the commission to provide all the necessary technical and political support and in particular calls on the commission to submit rapidly the required documentation on vehicle emission measurements, including the work carried out by the joint research centre (jrc) and all records of the activities of the various expert groups dealing with legislation on vehicle type-approval procedures.
in writing. ‒ the report takes stock of the progress of the work of the committee of inquiry on emission measurements in the automotive sector and provides a detailed outline of the future work programme. i think the text is clear, acceptable and free of criticism, and i therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ on 16 december 2015, the european parliament decided to set up a committee of inquiry to investigate infringements and maladministration in the application of union law in relation to emission measurements in the automotive sector. the committee of inquiry was set up following revelations that the volkswagen group had circumvented the nox (nitrogen oxides) emission limits for diesel vehicles. the mandate of the european parliament must be respected and it is important that the european citizens are informed about what has happened and that the truth is established. the laws must be the same for everyone and those who have done wrong must be held accountable, both for the sake of justice and to avoid undermining citizens' confidence in the impartial role of guarantee and control played by the institutions.
in writing. ‒ in today's vote i voted in favour of the interim report on the work done so far by the committee of inquiry set up by the european parliament in the wake of the volkswagen scandal over infringements of eu rules on car emissions measurements. the commission of inquiry will work for one year (we are halfway through its mandate), with the task of investigating the alleged failure of the commission to verify the test cycles used, the alleged failure of the commission and the member states authorities to take appropriate measures to enforce the explicit prohibition of 'manipulation devices' and the alleged failure of the commission to introduce tests reflecting real driving conditions. the european union is a world leader in the fight against environmental pollution. just think of the driving role it played in achieving the paris climate agreement or the role it is playing within icao in extending the ets scheme worldwide. the credibility of the european union in the eyes of the world also depends very much on this inquiry.
in writing. ‒ the report under consideration is the mid-term report by which the emis special committee of inquiry informs parliament of the progress of its work. there is no direct reference to the substance of the inquiry or to the verification of the conditions under which the eu and member states are applying the legislation on the control of emissions from passenger cars , but the report calls on member states and the commission to cooperate fully in providing all information useful to the inquiry. i voted for it without question.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the interim report on the inquiry into emission measurements in the automotive sector by colleagues pablo zalba bidegain and gerben-jan gerbrandy, because i share the importance of the parliamentary inquiry and the call for all european institutions to support the commission's work in a constructive way. the scandal of emissions in the automobile sector last year is a dark page which deserves to be examined in detail in order to clarify any political responsibilities, and for this reason the socialist and democratic group has already pushed for the formation of a parliamentary body which, in compliance with national court systems, would verify any responsibilities of public regulators. i think that after six months the work of the committee of inquiry can be assessed positively and i hope that, thanks also to the cooperation of the political and administrative staff of the european commission, the inquiry can be concluded quickly and with excellent results.
in writing. the european parliament set up a committee of inquiry on emission measurement in the automotive sector (emis) on 17 december 2015. in the wake of the volkswagen scandal, we have decided to look at the situation and see how it was possible for volkswagen to use mechanisms to circumvent the rules on car type-approval in relation to emission levels. specifically, its function appears to be to collect and analyse information to determine whether the commission and the member states have evidence to determine whether manipulation mechanisms have actually been used that could alter the actual car emissions results. i think it is essential that we continue to carry out the most transparent and thorough investigation possible in order to establish what really happened and to prevent, thanks to the new legislation, that this can happen again to the detriment of our consumers and the environment.
in writing. – the european union is on a regular process of improvement. we all in the epp group certainly want a better and smarter europe, but only by correcting our mistakes we will be able to accomplish the aforementioned goal. the promised investigation is important and any objections to carrying it out would only go against the principle of loyal cooperation established in union law. therefore, i voted in favour of the report on the inquiry into emission measurements in the automotive sector.
in writing. ‒ on 17 december 2015, the european parliament decided to set up a 45-member committee of inquiry to investigate allegations of infringement or maladministration in the application of union legislation relating to emission measurement in the automotive sector. i am convinced that one of the most important prerogatives of the european parliament is to monitor the work of the other institutions of the union, representing the interests of the european citizens. as regards the merits of this inquiry, i believe it is my duty to help restore full consumer confidence and to establish individual responsibility without damaging the whole automotive sector, which is a european excellence. i voted in favour of this interim report.
in writing. ‒ since march 2016, following the volkswagen scandal, the emis committee of inquiry has been investigating alleged breaches of european standards and cases of maladministration in relation to emission measurements in the automotive sector. the interim report gives an overview of the work programme of the committee: to date, emis has held 12 meetings, totalling some 50 hours, and 37 hearings with experts from research institutes and non-governmental organisations, industry representatives and the european commission. as the investigation is still ongoing, the report does not draw any conclusions. i therefore voted in favour of the text in which parliament simply asks the member states and the european commission to provide the technical and political support necessary for the commission of inquiry to fulfil its mandate.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the inquiry report on emission measurements in the automotive sector. in december 2015, parliament decided to set up a committee of inquiry to investigate alleged breaches and maladministration in the application of eu emissions law in the automotive sector, requesting a report within six months of the start of the work. given the nature of the committee of inquiry, it cannot reach final conclusions before it has heard all the witnesses and before it has collected sufficient evidence. it is therefore premature for it to submit any comments. the interlocutory report is purely technical in nature, but it stresses procedural aspects and reaffirms the principle of good cooperation between the institutions, insisting on greater transparency.
in writing. ‒ we have today approved the mid-term report by which the special committee of inquiry into emission measurements in the motor vehicle sector informs parliament of the state of play of its work. this report does not yet contain any direct reference to the merits of the inquiry or to verify possible maladministration by the european institutions and member states in the application of the legislation in force on the control of emissions from passenger cars , but it does stress, albeit in a rather general way, the need for greater cooperation between the member states and the commission in order to provide the information needed for the inquiry.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report today because i believe that the circumstances of the case justify the application of article 8 of protocol no 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union. the committee on legal affairs, too, invoking article 9 (3) of the regulation and after a careful analysis of the case, recommended that the european parliament should uphold the immunities and privileges of rosario crocetta. the concept of 'opinion', in the light of article 8 of the protocol, includes speeches and statements which, as regards their content, correspond to subjective assessments. the committee on legal affairs and citizens' rights considered that the circumstances of the case showed that mr crocetta's statements had a clear and direct link with the exercise of his parliamentary functions. mr crocetta also took a particular interest in the fight against organised crime and its influence on politics and the economy at european level. he was first vice-chairman of the european parliament's special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering and a member of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation today because i believe it is right that the people's republic of china should be restored to its trading rights. these were partly reduced following the enlargement of the eu customs union with the accession of croatia. the rules of the world trade organisation (wto), in particular article xxiv:6 of gatt 1994, require the european union to enter into negotiations with the wto members with negotiating rights attached to the tariff list of croatia in order to allow for a compensatory adjustment. this adjustment is necessary where the adoption of the eu external tariff regime would result in a higher increase in duties than the level to which the acceding country has committed itself in the light of the wto framework. the commission also found that the chinese exporting producers were not able to obtain sufficient spare capacity to meet the demand for the product concerned. the first provides for an increase in the tariff quota and the second for a reduction in the consolidated tariff rates.

in writing. ‒ regulation (ec) no 223/2009 of the european parliament and of the council of 11 march 2009 on european statistics defines the european statistical system (ess) as a partnership between the european statistical authority, namely the commission (eurostat), the national statistical institutes (nsis) and the other national authorities responsible in each member state for the development, production and dissemination of european statistics. the european statistical system committee (ess committee) established by article 7 of regulation (ec) no 223/2009 shall be considered as the umbrella committee within the ess. it shall assist the commission in the exercise of implementing powers in certain statistical areas. these areas did not include the trade aspect and the analysis of import/export flows between the union and third countries. this regulation extends the scope of statistical analysis, streamlines and harmonises the methodology and makes the data available for public consultation more useful.

in writing. ‒ the european union's energy policy on heating and cooling must aim to reduce member states' energy dependence, lower costs for consumers and reduce emissions in line with the targets set at the paris climate change conference (cop 21). to date, almost 40% of the eu's final energy demand is used for heating and cooling buildings. it is necessary to increase the energy efficiency of buildings through renovation and refurbishment, in particular by improving their thermal insulation. i thought i would vote in favour of the report because it calls on the member states to put in place strategies to enable consumers to be more involved in the energy market and to take action to control energy consumption. it is also appropriate to continue to support the construction of nearly zero-energy buildings. i believe that the member states should provide incentives for the promotion and use of renewable energy. and it is essential to invest in research and innovation in order to develop energy-efficient technologies. finally, i believe that member states should ensure that a share of the funding for energy efficiency goes to households by helping them to invest in more efficient heating and cooling equipment.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the report by the committee on industry which sets out a vital european strategy on heating and cooling, as i consider this a priority issue in the context of sustainable growth. the european energy policy includes reducing the use of fossil fuels and boosting renewable energy (which today has a use, although increasing, limited to 18%) to ensure cleaner, safer, competitive, persistent and affordable energy for all. excessive reliance on a limited number of sources also makes countries vulnerable to supply disruptions. at a time when affordability of energy and competitive energy prices are increasingly a concern for households and businesses, we need to reduce our dependence on fossil fuels and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. the proposal i have approved calls on the member states to phase out the use of backward equipment in urban areas and to phase out the use of wood-burning fireplaces in cities. these measures require, during the transition, investments to be managed in accordance with the principles of efficiency and effectiveness, so cooperation with local authorities is essential.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because, in defining the european union's strategy for heating and cooling, it puts the emphasis on the energy retrofitting of buildings, stressing that action by the european energy efficiency fund is needed to help citizens bear the costs of modernising their buildings by covering at least 25% of the total cost. the strategy should focus on new architectural solutions, thermal insulation and reverse heat pumps, with particular attention to the latter, given their enormous potential for both heating and cooling.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament resolution presents a european strategy for improving heating and cooling in buildings at european level, contributing to the overall objectives of decarbonisation and energy efficiency. the european parliament, in its resolution, notes that the share of primary energy from fossil fuels used for heating and cooling remains very high and represents a major obstacle to decarbonisation, thereby accelerating climate change and causing significant damage to the environment. i voted in favour of the resolution because my vote is intended to support this process of modernising heating and cooling systems. this process must involve the different actors at all levels: the commission should use a major financial mechanism, for example to accelerate the rate of building renovation and to allocate a higher share of eu funds to energy efficiency programmes and the use of energy from renewable sources; member states must take measures to provide strong incentives for energy efficiency improvements; national and local authorities must ensure that consumers are fully aware of and can benefit from the technical and economic benefits of new heating and cooling systems.
in writing. ‒ this strategy is a useful opportunity and an important commitment to the development of renewable energy and the reduction of co2 emissions. in addition, investments in the technologies and management of new insulating equipment and constructions, such as reverse heat pumps and prefabricated panels, are becoming increasingly important in combating global warming. the report takes the climate challenge seriously and protects the well-being of citizens and the environment, which is why i have decided to support it.
in writing. ‒ improving heating and cooling systems must be at the heart of our efforts to achieve the energy efficiency target within the union. this objective is all the more important in a historical context and in an economic, climatic and environmental context which call for europe to break the chains of its energy dependence and to exploit, as far as possible, renewable energy sources, responding virtuously to the growing needs of households and businesses. i note that the strategy proposed by the rapporteur takes account of many of the m5s requests. for example, i find myself in the need, highlighted in the text that has come to the plenary, to decentralize energy production and to redevelop the building stock as a whole. there are some aspects of the strategy with which i do not entirely agree. i am thinking, for example, of some references to geothermal energy, district heating and waste generation (by incineration) as methods of contributing to decentralized and efficient energy production. i believe that the strategy does not sufficiently address the environmental problems that can be triggered by the use of such technologies. however, the approach that emerges from the heating and cooling strategy is overall a good one. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ i vote in favour of this report on an eu strategy on heating and cooling. the commission has the merit of addressing the issue adequately, giving priority to the achievement of objectives such as: a strategy for decarbonisation, renovation of existing buildings to allow for lower energy consumption, integration of electricity systems with those of cooling and heating.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the report as it is right to take account of climate differences within europe and to support new instruments for energy efficiency.
in writing. ‒ i voted in support of this very important report by mr gierek. if we wish to move to a more energy efficient and effective society, we must not forget that heating and cooling stands for close to 50% of the eu’s final energy demand. given this, action from our part in increasing the efficiency and sustainability of heating and cooling in the eu will play a major role in the overall effectiveness of the energy market. due to the importance of this topic, i think that a modern solution to the financing of research and new methods is needed; this should include a magnitude of actors including eu research instruments such as horizon 2020 as well as private investors.
in writing. ‒ europe made very significant commitments last year at the cop21 climate conference. to achieve the reductions in consumption and emissions, a profound change in our energy systems is needed, starting with our daily habits. a key weight in the distribution of emissions is represented by heating and cooling in buildings, which in themselves also constitute a significant financial commitment for many households in europe. to achieve the paris target of a 40% reduction in energy consumption, extraordinary action is needed: we call on the commission, in the context of the announced reform proposal on the energy efficiency of buildings, to introduce ambitious and demanding measures.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on a european union strategy for heating and cooling because i believe that one of the main challenges facing our planet today is to protect the environment, reduce energy consumption and ensure the sustainability of energy sources. considering that approximately 50% of the eu's final energy demand is for heating and cooling, it is crucial that these sectors are compatible with the eu's climate and energy targets, which call for the full use of renewable energy by 2050. i believe that these objectives are a good starting point for discussing a serious and effective global strategy that delivers concrete results and offers important job opportunities for businesses and consumers in the eu. i welcome the commission's communication on the eu's strategy for heating and cooling, which sets out a holistic approach to priorities and objectives. finally, i support the need to develop new technologies relating to renewable energy sources, thanks also to incentives from the member states and to facilities for the retirement of obsolete heating systems.
in writing. among the priorities of the european union, the commission has designed the first strategy aimed at supporting the correct and moderate use of energy and fossil fuels in a specific sector, such as heating and cooling. it is the most common use of energy, accounting for 50% of the total, of which only 18% is renewable and 75% fossil coal. the strategy therefore aims to optimise energy efficiency, increase the use of renewable energy and encourage the reuse of waste energy from industrial heating and cooling. in practical terms, member states are asked to phase out all obsolete heating systems and to promote a phase-out of inefficient wood-burning stoves. finally, the importance of research and technological innovation and access to investment funds for the modernisation of the heating and cooling sector is emphasised.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the eu's strategy for heating and cooling, a very important issue to ensure more efficient use of energy and a significant reduction in co2 emissions. i believe that the financial resources for the thermal rehabilitation of entire blocks of flats, especially those built using prefabricated panel technology, should be significantly increased. to that end, a financial envelope of at least 25% of the total should be allocated from the european energy efficiency and renewable energy fund. the specific problems of buildings in rural areas, which tend to be older, less energy efficient, less healthy and less thermally comfortable, also need to be addressed.
in writing. ‒ heating and cooling account for 40% of all primary energy and 50% of all usable energy in the form of heat, and much of this is wasted. however, the heating and cooling system and the electricity system can support each other in efforts to reduce carbon emissions. in february, the commission proposed an 'eu heating and cooling strategy' to propose measures to eliminate energy dissipation in buildings by maximising the efficiency and sustainability of heating and cooling systems, including through the use of advanced technologies. the report by the committee on energy, research and technology on the commission's initiative on heating and cooling contains some important points which i fully support, such as the dismantling of obsolete power stations, the replacement of household appliances which cause the most pollution, an increase in the rate of building renewal, especially in view of the objectives of having zero emission buildings by 2050, etc. however, the report retains some ambiguities in relation to district heating, geothermal energy and the committee's strategy on energy production, which seems to support the use of incinerators. for the reasons stated above, i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the issue of heating and cooling affects member states differently. i agree with the rapporteur that there is a need to increase significantly the financial resources allocated to the thermal rehabilitation of entire blocks of flats, particularly those built using prefabricated panel technology. to that end, a financial envelope of at least 25% of the total should be allocated from the european energy efficiency and renewable energy fund. i also think it is essential to replace old thermal power stations with small, high-performance cogeneration plants. the draft report stresses the importance of the district heating network, emphasises the local character and the heating and cooling potential, calls on the member states to phase out the use of obsolete heating systems in urban areas and, where possible, to encourage the phase-out of inefficient wood-burning fireplaces in cities. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ in the area of heating and cooling, the european strategy should aim to increase the share of renewable energy, whereas 75% of the fuels used in this sector are still of fossil origin. the existing technology would allow a smarter and more sustainable use of resources, contributing to a transition to a green economy. the improvement could come through new investment, wealth creation and reduced spending on fossil fuels. the amendments proposed by m5s to the gierek report were aimed at decentralising energy production, increasing the share of renewables in heating and cooling and energy retrofitting in the industrial sector. the report contains some points about certain forms of district heating, biogas without specifying its origin and, above all, about generic energy production from waste (which implies the use of incinerators) with which i disagree. for these reasons, despite the many positive elements and the excellent cooperation with the rapporteur, i abstained.

in writing. heating and cooling account for half of the eu's energy consumption, but much of the energy produced for heating and cooling is lost. one of the union's strategic priorities in the energy field can only be to make these two major consumer items more efficient and sustainable. this will reduce energy import dependency and costs for households and businesses, but also contribute to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and to the commitments made in the paris climate agreement cop21. it is important to remember that 75% of the fuels used in the heating and cooling sector are still fossil fuels, and about half of them are gas. we in the m5s have succeeded in getting this report to say that energy production for heating and cooling is increasingly coming from renewable sources and that there is a need for energy-efficient upgrading of existing buildings, both private and industrial. however, the report contains elements which i do not share, such as the strategy on waste-to-energy which involves the use of incinerators. i therefore voted against.
