mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to explain why i voted against the resolution signed by mr bresso. we, as the gue/ngl group, have tabled a number of amendments to this text to clarify a point which is fundamental to us: the commission has already made it clear that there can be no alpine strategy which does not respect the will of the people. in particular, i believe that the failure to involve the "no tav" movement in the consultation on the alpine region launched by the european commission in 2014 is unfortunately a very, very serious shortcoming. we therefore strongly urge that the tav, the high-speed turin-lyon line, be stopped, as it has been shown to be harmful to the health of citizens, and as it has been shown to be unnecessary for the strategy and for transport needs. we really think that the people must be involved and their will in that region respected.
in writing. ‒ the report is somewhat appreciated in many respects, but still very problematic in others. for example, among the positive points, the approach to biodiversity and the preservation of the region's ecosystem is noteworthy, underlining the urgent need to develop new strategies to combat air pollution. however, the report also contains references to the turin-lyon treaty. there are also other points which should be dealt with differently. for these reasons i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the alpine regions, thanks to a strong bottom-up approach, have led to the development of the eusalp strategy, with the aim of effectively addressing the challenges common to the entire alpine area. the environment, agriculture, the risk of depopulation, employment, transport, research and governance are just some of the issues addressed in the commission's proposal, issues which have been taken up with particular effectiveness by the bresso report, which i have decided to support with conviction. the union's strategy must aim to reconcile environmental sustainability with economic development in a natural area that is already a major tourist destination. the 48 regions involved, divided between seven states, retain many differences but share common problems and high capacities. however, resources are needed to unlock the potential of the territories. the european institutions and the commission must create a genuine investment platform for the alpine region, a flexible instrument that makes it possible to mobilise public and private funding. a pipeline project for the region is needed to attract investors and new forms of multi-level governance with community contributions. eusalp is a great opportunity to make the alps one of the innovation centres of europe.
in writing. ‒ the alpine macro-region is a project of fundamental importance for the regions of northern italy, primarily veneto and lombardy, which, together with the other 46 european regions involved, are the beating heart of the european economy. thanks to the eusalp macro-regional strategy, which covers a territory of 80 million citizens, our northern regions will be able to manage the large amounts of eu funding for joint projects in the fields of environment, tourism, transport and energy on their own. i have supported the eusalp project from the outset, together with the northern league, because it is a unique opportunity for economic development and governance for our territories, our companies and our citizens. for all these reasons i supported the text with my vote.
in writing. ‒ given the strategic importance of the alpine region, given its geographical position in the heart of europe, but also as a 'water reservoir' for the energy challenges facing the eu, the alpine strategy is intended as a macro-regional framework for enhanced cooperation. the alpine region is made up of a wide variety of territories, which share common characteristics and therefore require joint governance; eusalp would bring together seven countries, five of which are eu members (including italy) and two non-members. the report, which i support, highlights the potential of the alpine region for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, which combines social, economic and environmental interests. the eusalp action plan is a valuable opportunity to increase crossborder cooperation between the alpine states, identifying common objectives for the region and facilitating the creation of common policies. the ultimate aim of this strategy is to enhance the attractiveness and competitiveness of the alpine area, focusing on the sustainable use of natural resources and the protection of cultural heritage, starting with local communities.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today because i am convinced that the eu strategy for the alpine region can play a significant role in efforts to revive the alpine economy and to combat the depopulation of the area, in particular the exodus of young people. i appreciate that the european structural investment funds offer potentially significant resources and a wide range of tools and options for the eu strategy for the alpine region. however, greater synergies and the promotion of coordination and complementarities with the european structural and investment fund (esif) and other relevant funds and instruments under the pillars of the strategy, in particular horizon 2020, the connecting europe facility, the life programme, the cosme programme for smes, the interreg programme 'alpine space' and the european fund for strategic investments (efsi), for which the commission should examine the possible added value of specific calls focusing on challenges of particular relevance to the alpine region, are needed. i also invite the eib, in cooperation with the commission, to consider the possibility of creating an ad hoc investment platform for the alpine region which would enable public and private finance to be mobilised.
in writing. ‒ although the report deals comprehensively with several important issues, such as the issue of biodiversity and the preservation of the region's ecosystem, the issues of employment and innovation, and stresses the importance of ensuring fast and efficient access to high-speed internet, i regret that no mention is made of any of them in the tav. the delegation of the five star movement had tabled four amendments, three of which concerned the tav and one the public water supply, all of which were rejected. the text also calls for the creation of a pipeline project for the region to attract investors and explicitly calls on the commission, the eib and the participating countries to make full use of the opportunities offered by the european fund for strategic investments (efsi) to finance projects in the region. for these reasons i have decided to abstain on the final vote.
in writing. ‒ the european union has dedicated a strategic development plan for the alpine region (eusalp) which affects 80 million inhabitants in 7 states and 48 regions, inside and outside the european union. although the region is already covered by various cooperation agreements, connectivity is limited, logistical problems and climate change create disadvantages and limit production activities. eusalp's strategy is built on three pillars: improving competitiveness, prosperity and cohesion; ensuring accessibility and connectivity; promoting the alpine cultural heritage and the sustainable use of natural resources. i voted in favour of this important report because it provides solutions to common problems and challenges in the alpine region, which includes six italian regions.
in writing. ‒ i support the report by mrs bresso on the need to increase and fully implement the eu strategy for the alpine region. this is an ambitious project of territorial cohesion which would allow the full and complete development of the strong potential characteristic of the whole macro-region and from which our country will be able to derive great benefit. the juncker plan introduced an investment plan for the european union, establishing the european fund for strategic investments, further opportunities for the macro-region to undertake new investment projects and to complete those already under way. synergies between the various funding instruments available to the union and coordination systems between local and supranational bodies are intended to encourage innovation and the development of new technologies, while maintaining traditional forms of economic activity, which are the engines of local productivity. it is therefore essential to ensure better accessibility and connectivity to the whole area in a manner consistent with the protection of the alpine environment. alpine flora and fauna are in fact valuable assets in their own right, capable of ensuring a distinctive well-being and therefore needing to be protected and developed. i hope that, in terms of greater coordination between the different institutional levels, a lean governance will be established, free from any bureaucratic burdens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because, through the eusalp plan, the alpine macro-region will benefit from new funding from the european fund for strategic investments and will have the opportunity to implement joint projects with a european impact. i also believe that the strategy structured around three pillars, including improving the competitiveness and cohesion of the alpine region, increasing accessibility and strengthening the region's transport sector and promoting the alpine heritage and the sustainable use of natural and cultural resources, represents a good starting point.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote in favour of the strategy as i consider it an important initiative for the development of the alpine area in the context of international cooperation in the commercial, tourist and cultural fields. in addition, this initiative represents another point in favour of european integration also at macro-regional level in the sharing of stable economic growth and common cultural values.
in writing. ‒ although the report contains a number of positive elements, the rapporteur's intention to promote the construction of major projects such as the high-speed rail link between turin and lyon is clearly stated. m5s has tabled amendments to the text to prevent projects harmful to health and the environment, not economically viable and, in particular, in the case of the tav, completely useless as the existing track is functional, recently renovated and underused, from being carried out today and in the future. the amendments tabled were rejected, so i abstained in the final vote.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the alpine strategy because it represents a good opportunity to relaunch and complete joint investments for the countries of the region. the potential of the alpine region is vast, so a joint planning capacity of the alpine countries and regions, local authorities and all public and private actors in the area is needed in line with the major european objectives of europe 2020. i believe that this requires the design and implementation of projects with a macro-regional dimension, which do not overlap with existing interregional cooperation but which are capable of adding value.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the report because i agree with the planning of a series of ad hoc investments for the alpine region which will enable public and private funding to be mobilised.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report as it aims to improve the eus policies in regards to the alpine region and give existing eu instruments more flexibility to act according to this regions special needs and prospects. the report underlines many important areas of priority for the region and outlines which issues the eu should invest in and support. if there is one thing that is important in this alpine strategy then it is the development of the regional labour market and to develop opportunities for agriculture, forestry and craft based economic activities in the region. other major priorities in the alpine region are better digital connections and to promote the self-generation of energy.
in writing. ‒ i agreed with the draft resolution of the european parliament on a european union strategy for the alpine region because i believe that macro-regional strategies are an essential tool for rethinking the development of territories in a new perspective of economic, territorial, cultural, historical and social cohesion of the european union. the objective of the macro-regions is to ensure that better and more tangible results are achieved for the different regions that are part of them, through a common approach and a focus on the coordination of different interests. it can therefore be considered as a model of multi-level governance in which all the parties involved, i.e. local entities, national and regional authorities, play a primary and equal role. as with other macro-regional strategies, the alpine macro-region also contributes to the consolidation of regional identities and cultural heritage, as well as to the protection of a folk heritage and biodiversity that must not be lost. i share the rapporteur's call for the european commission, in collaboration with the european investment bank, to consider the possibility of creating an investment platform capable of attracting public and private finance in a region of some 80 million people.
in writing. today we are approving the action plan for the alpine strategy (eusalp). this strategy is based on the concept of macro-regions and their importance as a means of cooperation and development of synergies between the different eu funding instruments. it also encourages innovation and the use of new technologies in the economy; promotes tourism and the importance of transport connectivity; and enhances the biodiversity of regions. finally, it calls on the member states to coordinate their national and regional policies in order to achieve the objectives of european action effectively.
in writing. ‒ cohesion policy is one of the tools alongside citizens, whose resources fall entirely to the territories, and remains one of the sources of direct eu investment in regions and local authorities. in particular, the alpine strategy offers an opportunity to invest in joint projects, developing new forms of multi-level governance where the eu and regions interact effectively. investing in eusalp means adding value to existing crossborder cooperation in territories with 80 million inhabitants and 48 regions. i therefore welcomed the proposal to create an investment platform for the alpine region which would enable public and private funding to be mobilised, including through the eib and the opportunities of the efsi. in particular, i support the idea that a digital policy is needed for this region, which offers more possibilities for openness and contact. the internet can be a tool for improving infrastructure, services and communication, to the benefit of both the region's inhabitants and the tourists who visit these areas every year. i therefore voted in favour of this report because i believe it will make a fundamental contribution to the recovery and development of the regions concerned.
in writing. ‒ we welcome the report on the eu strategy for the alpine region. this macro-region has a strategic role for the union from a cultural, geographical and commercial point of view, making effective cross-border cooperation between those areas indispensable. however, due to its specificities, this macro-region is exposed to challenges that threaten it and at the same time hinder its enormous potential. difficult connections, high sensitivity to climate change, critical issues in the development of energy infrastructure and promotion of start-ups and small and medium-sized enterprises are some of the issues to which the report offers concrete solutions. the role of the strategy is to maximise synergies between existing cooperation and to ensure that they are in line with the european macro-objectives, while also strengthening them in the areas most critical to achieving sustainable development in the area. the european parliament, in promoting this report, also wants to stress the need for an approach which starts from the territory, but which at the same time allows for a large-scale impact, in accordance with an intelligent application of the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality.
in writing. ‒ in addition to thanking the rapporteur for her work, i would like to reiterate my idea and the importance of key projects for sustainable european transport and as an incentive for the whole territory and the neighbouring regions. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ european macro-regions can provide the institutional framework within which to promote the exchange of good practice and the implementation of ambitious joint projects. europe is rich in different geographical areas, each with its own peculiarities. the alpine region is undoubtedly a part of the eu territory which offers countless opportunities for economic and social development. this report stresses in particular the importance of encouraging innovation and the development of new technologies in key sectors of the economy, while also maintaining traditional forms of economic activity; supports the diversification of tourism, stresses the importance of improving transport and energy connectivity and protecting and enhancing the biodiversity of the alpine region. all of these objectives are central to the implementation of a strategy which combines tradition and modernity. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that crossborder cooperation between regions is the key to better management of europe's territory.
in writing. ‒ the eu strategy for the alpine region involves several member states, including italy and france, through the turin-lyon rail link. although the bresso report refers to the issues of depopulation in mountain areas, the importance of ensuring fast internet access to enable digital and online services, including e-commerce and teleworking, and although the theme of biodiversity and the preservation of the ecosystem is also mentioned, many critical issues still remain. the main problem we are facing is the danger of a great waste of money on the existing and recently modernized turin-lyon line. this route could already eliminate the traffic of goods between italy and france. the project therefore appears to us to be a useless transfer of wealth to the large companies which will be awarded the contracts. although the report shows signs of improvement, the system of contracts and subcontracts envisaged for the construction of the project will make it difficult to monitor the regularity of the work. for the reasons stated above, i have abstained.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the eu strategy for the alpine region, which envisages an investment that will benefit 80 million people, 7 different countries and 48 regions inside and outside the eu. the alpine region is already involved in several cooperation agreements but needs improved transport links, a solution to the logistical problems of smes and is suffering the negative effects of climate change. this strategy will help to develop employment, economic growth and innovation in the territory. through the investment plan and the european fund for strategic investments, the report will support small and medium-sized enterprises in the alpine area, promote sustainable and competitive tourism, enhance transport infrastructure by making the construction of cross-border corridors fully operational, protect the alpine heritage by promoting a sustainable use of natural and cultural resources and protect alpine agriculture, biodiversity and ecosystems.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the creation of the alpine macro-region, bringing together very rich and similar economic, productive and tourist realities, is an important vehicle for increasing the competitiveness of these areas, but i also believe that it should promote social inclusion and the protection of local populations. to do this, it is essential to address the enormous disparities in social, medical and structural services between the various areas of the regions concerned: mountain areas and urban centres in the first place. the same applies to the employment and study opportunities available to people in the most remote areas. i am convinced that great attention must also be paid to the demographic question, which, in addition to the ageing of the population and the depopulation of mountain areas, is also characterized by new migratory flows. i believe that these phenomena must be tackled actively. finally, i believe that it is essential to develop public services linking remote areas to urban centres, as well as strong support for smes and the promotion of local products. to do this, and to stimulate the creation of quality jobs, it is essential to bridge the digital divide and make new technologies more widespread and accessible to the whole population.
in writing. following our contributions, the report has improved considerably from the first draft, and now also calls for safeguarding the existing alpine convention, managing the risk of natural disasters and climate change, ensuring participation and access to documents, promoting renewable, local and self-production energy, smes and sustainable tourism, renewing and making optimal use of existing networks and infrastructure, protecting biodiversity, soil and water, and taking action against air pollution. however, one of the main aims of the report is to pursue potentially dangerous and environmentally harmful projects such as tav, according to the explanatory statement of the report itself. the report does not even mention the turin-lyon issue and it wants to finance projects through the eib which we fear are yet another new infrastructure project which might not have been possible using the structural funds because they are not in line with the objectives of europe 2020 and the eu. i have therefore refrained from making any judgments now, but will give an estimate in a few years' time, in the light of how this strategy has been implemented in practice, beyond the stated aims.
in writing. ‒ the eu trust fund for africa is a very important tool for promoting social and economic development in african regions, for example by providing young people with the education and skills they need to fulfil their potential and create job opportunities. i believe that promoting the economic and social development of these areas is also of fundamental importance in combating regular migration, which has been a serious problem for the member states for some years now. that is why i spoke positively.
in writing. ‒ the valletta summit on migration on 15 november 2015 launched the eu trust fund for africa, which aims to promote stability in the regions concerned and contribute to better migration management. the corrao report, which i supported today, effectively underlines the objectives of the fund and the difficulties it has encountered to date. there is a clear funding problem. the member states have paid little and not followed up on their promises with concrete action. the etf's financial envelope should be increased to allow for a rapid and flexible disbursement of funds in emergency situations. the new instrument should be used to contribute to the development of migrants' countries of transit and origin by improving local public services, political participation and governance, mainly through community-based projects. the european response to the migration crisis must be multi-pronged, but the etuf can be a concrete support to improve security and ensure the development of the least developed african countries.
in writing. ‒ although it is a more balanced text than many others which have in the past dealt with africa as the subject of european cooperation interventions, i believe that it contains criticisms and gaps which have led me to express my abstention.
in writing. ‒ given the crisis situation and general instability in the sahel, north africa and horn of africa regions and the clear humanitarian impact on europe in terms of large migratory flows, a coordinated european union intervention in the regions concerned is essential. that is why i support the initiative on the european trust funds for africa. i believe that long-term planning is needed, including measures to eradicate the root causes of migration, starting with poverty and socio-political instability in the countries of mass emigration. the need is to go beyond programmes of a purely emergency nature, such as border controls, and to provide funds for regional and local development, establishing a genuine partnership between member states, ngos and local communities. in the resolution adopted today, parliament stresses the need for monitoring and transparency in the disbursement of funds where respect for human rights is a necessary condition for appropriation. a clear commitment by member states is therefore essential to deal with a transnational emergency which requires a coherent response by the european union.
in writing. ‒ the migration problem cannot be tackled effectively without putting the need to bring stability, development and peace to the regions of origin of migrants at the heart of the matter. a purely military or legal approach to the problem cannot solve the phenomenon which, with its dramatic humanitarian consequences and the suffering we see every day, is likely to worsen every day. it is necessary to understand that the majority of migrants do not leave their homes for ideological reasons or in search of exaggerated expectations about their standard of living but, much more concretely, because their survival is at risk in their country of origin because of poverty, war, disease, famine, ethnic or religious persecution. if we are to solve this 21st century drama at its root, we must bring peace and development to those regions: the eu trust fund for africa is an important first step in this direction.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of this report to support the eu trust fund for africa (eutf) which helps to promote stability in the regions of the area and contributes to better management of migration. however, i am concerned about the lack of coordination between all actors involved in the management of the eu trust fund, in particular between the commission's directorate-general for international cooperation and development (dg devco) and its department for humanitarian aid and civil protection (echo), and the lack of clear guidelines on how to access the available funds. the funding criteria and the funds available to civil society under the eu trust fund should be clearer and more transparent. the commission should also systematically monitor the way in which the eu trust fund resources are used and the allocation arrangements, and enhance parliament's scrutiny prerogatives in relation to the eu trust fund. i call on the commission to undertake a more systematic assessment of the impact of its policies and funding, including the eu trust fund, especially in relation to their effects on sustainable development, human rights and gender equality.
in writing. ‒ the trust fund for africa responds to the need to address the root causes of migration by acting to create development. to this end, it is necessary to work in the long term, with planning and not just in an emergency mode, investing above all in essential services such as education, health, vocational training and primary public services. the text does not fail to point out that the real problem is that states, at international summits and summits, make a big deal of themselves, but then, once the spotlight is turned off, they forget the promises made. all this is well expressed in the report by mr corrao, for which i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the eu trust fund for africa, signed by the commission, 25 member states, norway and switzerland, was launched at the valletta migration summit on 12 november. i consider the establishment of this fund to be significant, since its main objective is to promote stability in the region and to contribute to better management of migration. more specifically, the fund should address the causes of destabilisation, forced displacement and illegal migration on the one hand and promote resilience, economic opportunities, security, equal opportunities and development on the other. i am interested to see this initiative address some important aspects of the migration crisis. however, it is unlikely that action will be effective as long as the member states do not keep their promises to contribute. i voted in favour because the priority of european action must be to try to restore stability and security and to promote development in the countries from which migration originates. it is also necessary to ensure that the fund, which is used for cooperation projects, is used mainly for the purposes of education and protection of minors, job creation and environmental projects.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the corrao report on the implications for development and humanitarian aid in africa. launched in valletta in 2015, the eu trust fund for africa (eutf) is a hot topic. in particular, addressing the root causes of migration, the report proposes effective solutions, such as simplifying the disbursement of funds to promote stability, sustainable economic growth, social cohesion and development in the african region. in fact, in the face of the serious migration crisis, i believe it is important to concentrate resources on the completion of long-term objectives capable of ensuring peace and stability on the african continent.
in writing. ‒ the european trust fund for africa aims to help promote stability, security and development in african regions affected by migratory flows. the fund also aims to identify and address the root causes of destabilisation and irregular migration. i share these objectives and believe that the member states should contribute to the fund in such a way as to make it stronger and more effective. understanding the complexity and multi-dimensional nature of the migration crisis, i also believe that it is appropriate to monitor the proper use of european funds in the territories concerned. the final objective of the european fund for africa is to promote peace and stability in critical territories by providing resources and strengthening local governance capacity.
in writing. ‒ the eu trust fund for africa was conceived as a financial assistance instrument for 23 countries in three african regions comprising some of the african states most affected by migratory movements and situations of social and economic instability. by voting in favour of this resolution, i express my support for this important instrument for promoting economic growth, regional stability and the integrated management of migration flows. the trust fund shall be established in accordance with the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality, as set out in article 5 of the treaty on european union. i believe that the eu has a responsibility to provide targeted responses to global humanitarian crises and post-emergency crisis situations. this fund, which is mainly drawn from the 11th european development fund (edf), helps to make up for shortcomings in member states' official development assistance and the insufficient resources and flexibility of the eu budget and the multiannual financial framework. finally, the eu trust fund for africa should foster policy coherence for sustainable development and complementarity between all development actors and programmes.
in writing. ‒ i believe it is important to establish a european trust fund for africa in order to have the necessary resources available in a shared and flexible way to enable a rapid and comprehensive response to the migration phenomenon. the fund will ensure a better balance of funding to governments and trusted actors of civil society in the beneficiary countries. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ solidarity and respect for human rights must remain the fundamental values of the european union and the objectives to be pursued at all times. however, europe needs to concentrate its resources and efforts by selecting the most effective means at its disposal, avoiding first of all the fragmentation of the financial instruments which are the responsibility of the european union. i voted against the report on the trust fund for africa because there is too high a risk of misuse of european union development aid, particularly in those countries most affected by conflict where security, migration and development are closely interlinked, and therefore a complex and multi-dimensional crisis.
in writing. ‒ i am abstaining from the report because it could be more incisive and detailed about the projects that would be developed.
in writing. ‒ the trust fund for africa risks remaining an empty instrument if the pledge of commitments is not followed by concrete action by member states. the national contributions which have been allocated to date are in fact insignificant: the commission has already announced that it will be providing eur 81.71 million, less than 5% of the eur 1.8 billion planned. the eu trust fund aims to address the root causes of destabilisation, forced displacement and irregular migration by promoting resilience, economic prospects, equal opportunities, security and development. in order to achieve these objectives, we call for promises and commitments to be translated into concrete action. and we remind the commission that the trust fund for africa should contribute to development in the countries of transit and origin of migrants, as well as to strengthening and improving local public services mainly through community-based projects. we believe that the fund should help to create employment in local sectors, while ensuring respect for human rights and the protection of the environment. the commission should monitor how the fund's resources are used and the way they are allocated, while this house should exercise a monitoring function on the way the fund is implemented.
in writing. ‒ i appreciate the work of my colleague and i am convinced that thanks to the contribution of my group we now have an improved text. i reiterate my contribution to the fight against discrimination based on religion or belief, sex, race or ethnic origin, disability and sexual orientation.
in writing. ‒ the trust fund for africa is a development cooperation mechanism that aims to address the causes of irregular migration from the most fragile and migration-affected african countries and provides for relocation to cities of origin, transit and destination through a number of priority areas. i am voting in favour of the report by my colleague, and i hope that this development mechanism will allow a real, rapid and collective response to the problem of migration on the ground and in the transit regions. i hope that the trust fund for africa will also help to ensure respect for human rights and have a positive impact on the lives of millions of people, especially in the light of the current crisis in the mediterranean.
in writing. ‒ the european commission has allocated €1.8 billion of eu financial resources to set up an 'emergency trust fund for stability and to address the root causes of illegal migration in africa'. a trust fund is a mechanism used in development cooperation to pool large resources from different donors. in particular, the european union wants to help the sahel region as a whole to face the growing challenges of demographic pressure, environmental stress, extreme poverty, internal tensions, weak institutions, weak social and economic infrastructure. this report addresses the many questions and concerns raised by the creation of the eutf (european trust fund for africa) in terms of funding, implementation and monitoring. the report provides a critical assessment of budgetary aspects and funding shortfalls by member states and calls on all stakeholders to promptly uphold their commitments and responsibilities. i think it is well worded and that is why i have decided to vote in favour of its adoption.
in writing. ‒ the report by our colleague ignazio corrao on the trust fund for africa, for which the five star movement has always fought, was a success as it was approved by a large majority. the report calls for europe to allocate €1.8 billion for education, health, training and essential public services, and for the member states to do their part by contributing to the fund. if we really want to stop the flow of migrants to europe, we must root out the root causes of migration. if operated with specific periodic controls, involving ngos and local civil society in the planning and implementation of projects, the trust fund will prove to be an effective tool to achieve the objectives pursued. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the eu trust fund for africa: the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the programme. in particular, the report highlights the importance of using the entire amount of the trust fund for purely development-oriented projects, including education, healthcare and infrastructure.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to explain why i voted in favour of this report, which deals very specifically with various aspects of the gender pay gap, which is still very much present on our continent. overall, this is a good report, highlighting the impact of care work on women's employment: some 3.3 million women aged 15 to 34 have had to leave work to help members of their family. the report also highlights the need for targeted policies for work-life balance, as well as for women with disabilities, young people, migrants and lgbtqi people, who are often even more affected by discrimination in the workplace. the commission and the member states are therefore called upon to develop effective policies to combat gender stereotypes. we also voted in favour of the non-transferability of parental leave, as we believe that this is a strong signal that the european union must send to the member states. it also deals with the question of pensions. it 's a very delicate subject . the period of maternity is not counted as a period of maturation, a step forward in the career path, and we think that it should be equated.
in writing. ‒ the aim of the report is to increase women's participation in the labour market by making the current eu legal and policy framework more modern and adapted to today's labour market, to enable people with children or other dependent family members to better balance family and working life, to allow for greater sharing of caring responsibilities between women and men and to strengthen gender equality in the labour market. for these reasons i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ work-life balance must be a guiding principle within the eu, especially at a time when it is facing a serious demographic challenge due to the steady decline in birth rates in the member states. the ždanoka and blinkevičiūtė report is an important step towards a series of reflections on this subject, which is why i have decided to support it. the text stresses the need for a cultural change, which targets gender stereotypes and allows for a more equal distribution of care work and activities between men and women. global packages of legislative and policy measures concerning work-life balance are needed. the proposals from the social partners must be complemented by action by the commission in the context of the announced european pillar of social rights. relevant policies and measures are needed to take account of the growing diversity of family relationships, such as civil unions and agreements between parents or grandparents, and to redefine the overall approach to the issue. thinking about work-life balance is an important part of creating a solid foundation for economic and social growth.
in writing. ‒ i believe that, while the report exposes real problems and offers ideas that can be shared, it does not formulate concrete solutions, nor does it acknowledge europe's role in aggravating the current social emergency. with these initiatives, the eu is only feeding propaganda, publicly defending the right of citizens to a healthy work-life balance, but in practice forcing member states to give up national agencies and other services. in italy, the cost of substitute services for domestic work and childcare in the absence of grandparents or other family members is on average about 500 euros per month. if there is no work to enable young people to start and maintain a family, if the supply of employment requires maximum flexibility for the couple, but public services are being reduced in order not to increase the expenditure constrained by the eu's covenants, what is the point of this initiative if not to feed a sterile and self-serving rhetoric? for these reasons i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ the right to work, family and private life has been recognised as a fundamental right for decades. some measures in this area have already been taken at european level (for example in support of women's work and maternity rights) and by some member states, but further steps are needed to ensure that everyone has an appropriate work-life balance: the balance benefits not only the individual in terms of personal well-being but also society as a whole; it has been shown that people who have a good work-life balance are more productive at work and less likely to seek public health services for conditions linked to psychological problems or stress. to this end, the working environment must be transformed by overcoming the notion that only time spent at work (paid) has utility and value. it is important that work-life balance policies adopt a life-cycle approach so that everyone can be supported at different points in their lives and can actively participate in the labour market and society as a whole.
in writing. ‒ the report in question, which i voted for, focuses on the causes that prevent individuals from achieving a balance between family and professional life and proposes a modernisation of the european legislative framework. the analysis focuses primarily on demographic changes in society, which create greater care needs, and the emergence of new ways of working. it then highlights the still markedly negative impact of parenting on female employment rates and the inadequacy of the current eu framework to address this all-important aspect of the continuing gender gap. the creation of conditions conducive to work-life balance and the achievement of a good quality of life is only possible if people have sufficient time outside work to devote to personal development. the report therefore calls on the commission to take more action against member states which do not implement the working time directive properly and encourages member states to introduce measures to support leave for education or training and interruption of work.
in writing. ‒ the report aims to increase women's participation in the labour market. in particular, the commission is asked to revise the maternity leave directive, to extend the minimum duration of parental leave with adequate substitute income and social protection from four to at least six months, to adopt a paternity leave directive providing for a minimum of two weeks of compulsory leave with full pay, to adopt a careers leave directive integrating the provision of occupational care, allowing workers to care for dependants and offering care providers adequate pay and social protection, and to support the development of 'smart working', an approach to work organisation based on a combination of flexibility, autonomy and collaboration, which does not necessarily require the worker to be present at the workplace or at another predetermined workplace and in any case allows the worker to manage his own working hours and to comply with the maximum working hours and working weeks established by law. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ there are still many disparities in the world of work: the most common are the gender pay gap or the lack of equal responsibility sharing. there is a need to adapt working conditions to the new requirements of changes and changes in society which inevitably have an impact on the labour market. i am thinking, for example, of the ageing population, which requires care and assistance, mostly provided by women. gender inequality has weakened the position of women in terms of employment, pay and career advancement. the solution must be found in new legislative instruments. we have therefore asked the commission to prepare new paternity leave directives providing for a mandatory, non-transferable minimum paid leave for fathers and a new proposal on leave for carers so that it is not only women who take up family leave. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it takes account of the need to protect the basic nucleus of human society, the family. in particular, i am pleased with the positive results achieved in the field of equal opportunities. the report provides a clear legislative framework which promotes women's participation in the labour market not only by calling for the elimination of gender inequalities but also by protecting parental leave. furthermore, given the current socio-economic challenges, i believe that promoting the concept of 'agile work' will facilitate work-life balance. the introduction of work from home and flexible working hours will give workers with dependent children the opportunity to manage their own commitments better.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report in order to ensure that the best interests of the child are a priority in the implementation of policies for the work-life balance of parents. let us not forget that women's work is still undervalued and that many employers regard motherhood as a negative discrimination. effective public and private support policies for children and parents are therefore needed to enable them to assume and share their educational and care responsibilities. i very much hope that the commission will present an ambitious new draft directive on maternity leave, not only to ensure the right balance between social and working life, but also to support families and combat inequalities, while protecting pregnant women and new mothers who are working.
in writing. ‒ the importance of work-life balance is to promote a balance between the different aspects of people's lives. this requires cross-cutting, structural and coherent policies, including effective incentives and measures to promote the reconciliation of work, family time, leisure and personal development. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the commission and the member states must adopt policies which improve the working environment, create good working conditions and social and occupational well-being, and at the same time a good work-life balance. this requires policies that also take into account the welfare and best interests of children and improve women's access to the labour market and the equitable sharing of domestic and caring responsibilities between women and men.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i believe it is important to support families in their professional and private lives and to ensure equal participation of men and women in the labour market. i have always fought for equal pay and promotion with the possibility of a satisfactory private life.
in writing. ‒ i abstain because, while the report exposes real problems and offers ideas that can be shared, it does not formulate concrete solutions.
in writing. ‒ i think that this is a very important report that highlight the significant challenges that europe is facing in terms of its demographic future. to counter this, it is of crucial importance that the eu does what it can to promote a more family friendly approach to work. this is in order to give all of our citizens the possibility of have children without being penalised. a better work-life balance is also key in promoting the participation of women in the labour market. another point is that general well-being is an important factor in overall economic productivity in a modern society.
in writing. ‒ the message we have given today by adopting this text is that of a strong commitment by the eu parliament to the protection of human rights and freedoms. europe must use all the means at its disposal to ensure that the labour market is no longer threatened by discrimination of any kind. the global crisis we are facing already makes the situation dire, and the risk of poverty and social exclusion is too high: it is up to us to invest in measures that provide adequate social protection for workers, families, children and the most vulnerable. i therefore find it extremely important to stress the need to adopt urgently strengthened instruments for reconciling private and working life, for social and health care, for the right to the welfare of children and for the fight against poverty, for a europe which makes social policies the first pillar of our commitment in parliament.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on creating favourable labour market conditions for work-life balance, for which i was shadow rapporteur for the s-d group in the empl committee, because it was necessary to give a convinced and broad response to the commission's proposal for a roadmap on work-life balance and to the various proposals for initiatives aimed at modernising the legislation in force on the revision of the maternity leave directive by improving parental leave, and the adoption of new directives on paternity and carer's leave. in the preparation of the report we have tried to highlight some good practices in relation to flexible working time arrangements as a useful tool for increasing the participation of women carers in the world of work. the unprecedented demographic challenges facing the eu, the insecurity of work and the difficulty of working conditions with a negative impact on work-life balance require precise responses from the eu and i look forward to a rather swift and targeted reaction in each of the areas we have addressed and finally adopted with the resolution.
in writing. i vote in favour of the report on the creation of labour market conditions favourable to work-life balance. the report aims to modernise and adapt the eu's political and legal framework to the labour market and highlights several issues that should be reviewed, both at legislative and non-legislative level. the main point is clearly equal opportunities for men and women. the modernisation of these policies would enable families to achieve a balance between family and working life, ensuring that family responsibilities are shared equitably. the report also focuses on the development of children's potential, and therefore the need to provide quality, affordable and accessible childcare services, and the importance of spending more time with parents. these initiatives, which i support, are aimed at ensuring a better quality of life and greater safety for all those close to us.
in writing. ‒ we welcome this own-initiative report on work-life balance. the disparity between men and women in the use of leave is still very evident today: only 10% of fathers take at least one day of paternity leave, while 97% of women take the parental leave available to both parents. the european parliament decided to draw up this own-initiative report in order to give greater attention to the debate and to ask the commission to intensify its work in this field. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the iwg and will continue to monitor the implementation of the iwg. the report takes into account the link between the current unprecedented demographic challenges, job insecurity and difficult working conditions that have a negative impact on work-life balance. the primary focus is on the need to invest in social services, in particular care services for children, the elderly and other dependants. the importance of promoting quality employment, workers' rights and labour market security is also underlined.
in writing. ‒ i can only recall that the welfare and best interests of children must be a priority consideration in the design, monitoring and implementation of work-life balance policies. the text as a whole, with the exception of certain amendments tabled by other groups, is a good compromise and i therefore vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the family is the backbone of european society and that much work still needs to be done to ensure the conditions for an effective reconciliation of work, private and family life. this is an area where, although some measures have already been taken at european and national level, further progress is needed to ensure that all citizens, and in particular women, have an appropriate work-life balance. we must not force women to choose between their careers and their families. women must be able to play their fundamental role as mothers, alongside the irreplaceable father figure, with the support of public policies that favour their work. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted strongly in favour of the resolution on the creation of favourable labour market conditions for work-life balance for a number of reasons. firstly, because reconciliation between working life and professional life is a right which must be available to everyone, and i hope that the commission will take action as soon as possible to adapt the legislation in force. secondly, i am pleased that parliament has once again recognised that there is no such thing as a 'family', but 'families': single-parent families, rainbow families, families where the partners are not married. eu and member state policies in this area must take account of this beautiful diversity.
president-in-office of the council. – mr president, since january this year, this is the second time that the council has been asked to intervene on this issue of the situation in poland. let me start by saying that the presidency, and indeed all of us, agree that the protection of the rule of law, democracy and fundamental rights in our union are of crucial importance. today’s debate relates to the follow-up to the dialogue established between the polish authorities and the commission concerning, in particular, the position of the constitutional tribunal and the governance of public media. as the presidency said here in january, both the independence of tribunals and freedom and pluralism of media are indispensable elements in ensuring the rule of law in a democratic society. the commitment to protecting and promoting human rights is a constant challenge, requiring unwavering attention and effort across the full range of policy areas. this is not the time to be complacent about the protection of fundamental rights. as we all know, the european union is currently facing multiple interrelated crises. those challenges test our core values in different ways, including in respect of fundamental rights, be it in the area of migration or internal security. it should be our joint commitment – member states and the eu institutions together – to ensure that these principles consistently remain a central part of our action. fundamental rights need to be upheld and defended as our best guarantee for sustainable, open and free societies. in june, the council stressed the importance of applying the charter of fundamental rights as a part of the wider set of applicable fundamental rights sources in the national context. also, this year’s rule of law dialogue in the council focuses on fundamental values in the context of the integration of third-country nationals. the rule of law and the separation of powers are at the heart of the european union and also of the wider european continent. our strongest partner, equally engaged in the promotion, protection and development of human rights and the rule of law, is the council of europe. in this context, i would like to mention three elements. firstly, the annual report of the secretary-general of the council of europe on the state of democracy, human rights and the rule of law has just been published, and i am of the view that being committed to the rule of law and fundamental rights also means being open to discussing problems and accepting constructive criticism. it is in that light that the report of the council of europe’s secretary-general is an important contribution. secondly, the same applies to the report by the council of europe commissioner for human rights, published in june 2016 following his visit to poland and taking into account the comments of the polish authorities. last, but not least, the council of europe’s guidance, in the form of the opinions of the venice commission in this area, is also of great value, and its views should be taken seriously by all member states. the council is aware of the situation and of the fact that the polish authorities are in constant contact with both the venice commission and the european commission. together they are working on finding a solution to the issues raised. vice-president timmermans will update us on the ongoing process and on his contacts with the polish authorities following the recommendation issued by the commission on 27 july 2016, and i look forward to hearing from him. the issues at stake go to the heart of our commitment to this union. we therefore trust that all sides act responsibly and constructively to reach a swift solution that leaves no doubt about our core values.
first vice-president of the commission. – mr president, i would like to thank honourable members for putting the recent developments in poland on the agenda of the plenary today. the last time we discussed the issue of the rule of law in plenary was in january. today i would like to talk about what has happened since and what action the commission has taken. as you know, the dispute concerning the composition and functioning of the constitutional tribunal led the commission in january to open a dialogue with the polish government under the rule of law framework. we decided to do so because the rule of law is one of the fundamental values on which our union is founded, as enshrined in article 2 of the treaty. respect for the rule of law is also a prerequisite for upholding the full spectrum of eu law, including the proper functioning of the internal market, and for mutual trust throughout the union. i would like to thank parliament for the strong support for this position which is expressed in the resolution adopted in april. very similar concerns were expressed in an opinion of the council of europe venice commission last march, an opinion, i might add, that it issued at the explicit request of the polish government. since then extensive exchanges at various levels have taken place between the commission and the polish government. in order to set out the commission’s concerns in writing and to focus the ongoing dialogue with the polish authorities towards finding a solution in june, the commission adopted an opinion. following the opinion in july the polish parliament adopted a new law on the constitutional tribunal. despite certain improvements, major concerns remained as regards the composition of the constitutional tribunal, the publication of judgments and the effectiveness of constitutional review by the tribunal. for this reason, on 27 july, the commission adopted a rule of law recommendation setting out its remaining concerns and recommending how these could be addressed. the recommendation identifies three main issues: firstly, the composition of the constitutional tribunal, as the three judges lawfully elected in october by the previous legislator have still not been able to take up their function; secondly, the publication of all judgments of the tribunal, which should be automatic and should not depend on any decision of the executive or legislature; and, thirdly, the effectiveness of the functioning of the tribunal, which should not be undermined by the new law on the constitutional tribunal or by any other legislative reform. a functioning constitutional review procedure is also essential for ensuring full respect for the constitution by other important laws in a wide range of areas which have been adopted by the polish parliament. the commission asked the polish authorities to address the remaining concerns within three months from the adoption of the resolution. since our recommendation there have been a number of further developments, which i would like to mention. in particular, on 11 august, the constitutional tribunal rendered a judgment holding that a number of provisions of the new law on the constitutional tribunal are unconstitutional. however, the polish government refuses to recognise the validity of the judgment and to publish it in the official journal. moreover, while the polish government has published a number of other judgments rendered by the tribunal, it still refuses to publish the judgment of 9 march annulling the constitutional tribunal act adopted last december. therefore i must conclude that, at this stage, the dispute concerning the composition of the constitutional tribunal, and respect for its judgments, remains unresolved. that said, the commission stands ready to continue the constructive dialogue with the polish authorities in order to find solutions to the issues raised. to conclude, i would like to thank parliament for its continuous efforts to uphold the rule of law in the eu and for supporting the commission’s actions concerning the situation in poland. i would like to echo what was said by the representative of the council. upholding the rule of law is our joint responsibility, one that we all share – the commission, member states in the council, and this house. the rapporteur. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, 2011 just five years ago, many greeted with naïve enthusiasm the so-called "arab spring" that had turned prematurely into "islamic winters". despair has replaced dreams, fear has replaced optimism, violence has taken over the squares where previously peaceful demonstrations took place. what was then the leading country of democratic aspirations in the arab world, today, in a north africa and a middle east torn apart by civil wars and terrorism, pressured by the return of strongmen and by a lasting economic, political and social instability, assumes the role of last hope, the only torch in the darkness: that hope is called tunisia. unfortunately, its recent achievements represent an extremely fragile architecture which needs protection primarily from us europeans, its immediate neighbours. to this end, together with my fellow rapporteurs - whom i warmly thank for the important contributions proposed and for the extremely constructive spirit which has animated every phase of our work - i have addressed the pillars of the definitive consolidation of a partnership and cooperation which we want to be solid, lasting and fruitful for both sides, on a basis of equality and parity. economic development and security are inseparable. the terrorist threat is fuelled by many young people who, disappointed by the lack of immediate responses to the high expectations raised by the jasmine revolution, end up being easy prey for the recruiters of terrorist organizations, fueling the sad tunisian primacy of the number of foreign fighters. libya is there, a step away, as is the entire sahel region and its perennial pre-insurgency state, where armed jihadist gangs easily violate borders. on the other hand, the difficult economic and financial situation of the country, with a public debt now at 62% of gdp, with a further decline in tourism of 15%, makes it necessary to take action in good time. without real social inclusion, without a vigorous fight against unemployment, we may win some battles but we will lose the revolution. that is why we are calling in the report for a decisive increase in the european neighbourhood instrument and for coordination of aid from other donors. i welcome the recent statements by the high representative, who has repeatedly expressed his willingness to do so as early as next year. but we must have the courage to face up to the problem of the sustainability of tunisia's debt, which is the odious fruit of the years of dictatorship. the aim is to convert this into investment projects, in particular by exploiting the country's enormous renewable energy potential and by bridging the regional disparities, which are particularly evident in the south and west of the country. the sense of responsibility and commitment are certainly not lacking among the tunisians, who continue to act, despite some physiological turbulence, with a rare commonality of intentions. reforms into reality, on the one hand, by the socioeconomic recovery of the country, in particular by starting with the public administration and an effective anti-corruption plan, and on the other
