in writing. ‒ eu-switzerland relations are very important for both sides, especially from an economic and political point of view. following the accession of croatia to the eu, as a result of the enlargement of the internal market, the importance of the eu-switzerland partnership has increased even more. i also consider that about 1 million eu citizens live in switzerland and that a very large number of them cross the border daily for work, so i have decided to vote in favour of guaranteeing the free movement of people between the eu and switzerland.
in writing. ‒ the eu is switzerland's main trading partner and the union's fourth largest economic partner. the close relations have developed systematically since the refusal of the confederation to join the european economic area in 1992, a factor which has led the two sides to conclude a series of bilateral agreements on specific issues. the agreement on the free movement of persons, signed as part of the first set of bilateral agreements, gave citizens of the two parties the right to enter, live and work in their respective territories, removing most restrictions. however, in order to be entitled to these rights, you must have a contract of employment or service or sufficient financial means and adequate insurance. the jazłowiecka report, which i supported with my vote today, approves the conclusion of a protocol amending the original agreement and allowing croatia to accede to it. this is a technical measure that will allow the balkan country, which joined the eu in july 2013, to take full advantage of the opportunities offered by its entry into the community.
in writing. ‒ on 9 february 2014, switzerland approved by referendum the popular initiative "against mass immigration", which states that switzerland can manage immigration autonomously. the eu reacted to the swiss referendum by suspending negotiations with switzerland on many agreements and threatening to cut switzerland's substantial funding as a participant in european research programmes. the eu is once again proving to be a profoundly undemocratic construct, which in no way respects the will of the people, even if it is officially expressed through a regular popular referendum. for these reasons i do not intend to support this text with my vote.
in writing. ‒ it is right that the republic of croatia, now fully part of the european union, should also participate in the trade agreements that the eu concludes with foreign states. we consider it a due process.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation today because i believe that switzerland is a partner of fundamental economic and political importance to the eu, not only because of its geographical and cultural proximity. the eu has closer ties with switzerland than with any other country outside the european economic area (eea), thanks to the large number of agreements it has concluded with switzerland. switzerland is europe's fourth largest economic partner, after the united states, china and russia. over 1 million european citizens live in switzerland and more than 230 000 europeans cross the border for work every day. the number of swiss nationals residing in europe is about 430,000. with the accession of romania, bulgaria and croatia, the internal market has expanded considerably. switzerland, like the eu member states, benefits considerably from the enlargement of the european internal market. both croatia and switzerland will therefore, with the signing of the current protocol iii, benefit from a wider internal market where freedom of movement plays a very important role.
in writing. ‒ with this vote, parliament gives the green light to the integration of croatia into the protocol on the eu-switzerland agreement on the free movement of persons. this is a practical act which is necessary because of accession. i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the european union, with its member states, is switzerland's most important partner because of its geographical and cultural proximity; the union has closer ties with switzerland than with any other country outside the european economic area (eea). with the accession of romania, bulgaria and croatia, the internal market has further expanded to almost 505 million people and has become even more important for our swiss partner. protocol iii, which was initiated on croatia's accession to the union, opens the door to croatian citizens, as well as swiss citizens, by extending the agreement on the free movement of persons to croatia. i am convinced that both croatia and switzerland can only benefit politically and economically from this opening up. freedom of movement is the cornerstone of citizenship of the union, and that is why i have decided to vote in favour of the agreement.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of extending the eu-switzerland agreement on the free movement of persons to croatia. in view of recent developments, and given the uncertainty caused by the swiss confederation's february 2014 'against mass migration' referendum, i hope that the successful outcome of protocol iii will help to create a renewed spirit of cooperation between the european union and switzerland.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the above-mentioned protocol because it guarantees both the swiss confederation and croatia a gradual adaptation to the agreement on the free movement of persons, through the introduction of limits on access to the labour market. switzerland will be able to maintain the limits which are still in force for employees and selfemployed persons with residence permits of four months to one year and of a duration equal to or greater than one year, restrictions which may also be applied by croatia. the restrictions on access are determined for each of the seven years of application of the protocol, will be progressive so as to gradually open up the labour market and both countries will have the right to maintain controls on working and pay conditions for nationals of the other contracting party.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of the agreement because i believe that the eu and switzerland have stable political and economic relations and are linked by geographical and cultural proximity. over one million eu citizens live in switzerland and over 230 000 cross the border every day to go to work. an important point of the agreement is the establishment between the union and switzerland of rules equivalent to those between the member states on access to employment and social security.
in writing. ‒ i am voting against because the eu is once again proving to be undemocratic and not respecting the will of the people.
in writing. the protocol to the eu-switzerland agreement on the free movement of persons, which officially entered into force in 2002, has been extended to new member states. with the accession of bulgaria and romania in january 2007, the agreement was amended once again and therefore entered into force as protocol ii. the eu and switzerland have ratified protocol iii, which follows protocol ii and provides for an extension of the agreement on the free movement of persons to croatia. under this procedure, the right to enter, live and work in the territory of the contracting parties is granted to their nationals, with most restrictions being lifted. the aim of the agreement is to make community rules equivalent within the countries, but also to facilitate the provision of services in them. therefore, i approve the conclusion of the protocol.
in writing. – as the eu’s newest member, i see no reason for the republic of croatia not being able to enjoy the same benefits as those of its european counterparts, especially the free movement of persons. therefore, i voted in favour on the protocol between the european community and its member states and the swiss confederation regarding the participation of croatia as a contracting party, as both the eu and switzerland will continue benefiting from free movement. certainly, switzerland has the right to prioritise employment opportunities for its citizens but it is also in the country’s benefit to open gradually its labour market to croatian workers and likewise with swiss workers in croatia.
in writing. ‒ ladies and gentlemen, i can only thank the rapporteur for her work and agree on the final text. the free movement of persons remains a fundamental pillar of the union and we must all fight to protect this right.
in writing. ‒ switzerland is the eu's fourth largest economic partner, just behind the us, china and russia, while the eu is switzerland's largest trading partner. over 1 million eu citizens live in switzerland and over 230 000 cross the border to work every day. there are about 430 000 swiss nationals living in the eu. in 2000, the agreement on the free movement of persons between switzerland and the eu-15 was signed. as a result, the agreement was extended to the 10 new member states (protocol i to the agreement entered into force in april 2006). with croatia, the european union in 2013, protocol iii was initiated and after a series of actions between the eu and switzerland, on 4 march 2016, the two parties signed protocol iii extending the agreement on the free movement of persons to croatia. this protocol iii shall be subject to the assent of the european parliament. i voted in favour of this protocol because i believe that the free movement of persons, although adequately supported by measures relating to security and public order, is one of the most important achievements of the first 60 years of european integration.
in writing. ‒ the report aims to endorse the trilateral social summit for growth and jobs and at the same time repeals ec decision 2003/174. as the council and the european commission have formally committed themselves to always inviting a representative of the committee on employment and social affairs to participate in trilateral summits, i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the entry into force of the lisbon treaty has necessitated an update in the organisation of the trilateral social summit for growth and employment. the council submitted its proposal in february 2014 and forwarded it to parliament before the adoption of a separate resolution by parliament in april 2014. after having asked the commission and the council to include a provision, which was accepted, allowing the chairman of the ep's committee on employment and social affairs to participate in the trilateral summit, i decided to vote in favour of the sógor report. the new measures will ensure that parliament will be able to attend the summit on a regular basis, thanks to the participation of the chairman of the empl committee.
in writing. ‒ the trilateral social summit for growth and jobs is part of the european semester process, which is a symbol of the total lack of democracy and transparency in eu governance. the amendments proposed by the council will not make this instrument any more democratic, since it serves only to validate the commission's unilateral decisions in a self-referential manner. i therefore voted against the measure.
in writing. ‒ the tripartite social summit for growth and employment (tse) was established by council decision 2003/174/ec of 6 march 2003, which formalised the practice, established since 1997, of holding informal high-level meetings in the framework of the european employment strategy and, subsequently, the lisbon strategy. the institutions participating in the social summit need to do more and act in a more integrated way to ensure growth and jobs in the european union. growth and employment must be of quality, because there is no way of maintaining european welfare and democracy by competing downwards, with the devaluation of wages and in a deflationary context. we need to support sustainable growth, based on innovation, solidarity and inclusiveness: innovation, high quality, efficient services and high-quality products are what make the european market strong. this is a fact which we must not forget, especially in times of economic difficulty.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the eu council decision rewriting the functioning of the trilateral social summit for growth and jobs to allow for better consultation between the european council, the eu council, the commission and the social partners and to enable the latter to contribute, in the social dialogue, to the various aspects of the union's strategy for growth and jobs. since its establishment (in accordance with decision 2003/174/ec repealed by that decision), the summit has played a key role in high-level consultation, contributing positively to the development of the social dialogue at union level under the lisbon strategy for the period 2000-2010 and under the europe 2020 strategy. the tasks and composition of the summit have been adapted to take account of the institutional changes introduced by the treaty of lisbon, in particular the creation of the function of president of the european council under article 15 teu.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's report gives its approval to the draft council decision on the trilateral social summit for growth and jobs. the position in favour of approval was supported by the council's commitment to invite a representative of the ep (and in particular of the committee on employment and social affairs) to each meeting of the summit. i voted in favour without delay.
in writing. ‒ the tripartite social summit for growth and jobs (tsg) was established in 2003 to institutionalise the practice of holding informal high-level meetings between the heads of the european institutions and representatives of business and labour in the context of the european employment strategy. i think, however, that an agreement between the european institutions is appropriate to allow the chairman of the committee on employment and social affairs (empl) to participate in these summits. i thought i should vote in favour of the council's decision because i believe that the way in which the summit is to be held needs to be updated to take account of the institutional changes brought about by the lisbon treaty. i hope that the new format of the summit will make a positive contribution to the development of social dialogue at european union level for the benefit of european citizens and workers.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of the trilateral social summit for growth and jobs as it allows for a simultaneous and continuous dialogue between the european council, the commission, parliament and the social partners. the current socioeconomic situation in the union as a whole is as fraught as it has been for years and it is therefore essential to provide for methods of concertation between those parties who must ensure an optimal solution for the citizens. it is in this perspective of social dialogue that new tactics and strategies can be found to ensure steady growth and full employment. all too often, the european decision-making bodies have been so far removed from the social partners that they have been in conflict or have reached a deadlock, thus contributing to the growth of anti-european sentiment. the legitimate euroscepticism that has emerged, however, has only complicated the work tables by preventing quick and effective deliberations.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the trilateral social summit is a key opportunity to involve the social partners in the european semester process. i am convinced that the widest possible representativeness and the legitimacy and effectiveness of consultation of the social partners are of the utmost importance and that only in this way can the social dialogue in the european union gain new impetus. i believe it is important to strengthen and exploit the synergies and complementarities between the various bodies in order to coordinate the economic and social strategies of the european union in a more coherent way.
in writing. ‒ i am against the council's proposed changes as they will not increase democracy.
in writing. the legal framework for the triennial social summit for growth and jobs (ssg) ensures joint action between the european council, parliament, the commission and the social partners. the participants exchanged views on three issues in particular: experiences in implementing the country-specific recommendations; the impact of the migration and refugee crisis on the labour market; and the challenges of digitalisation. these are issues of even greater central importance today than they were in the past, given the urgent need to promote and sustain growth and employment throughout the eu.
in writing. – the european union has reached impressive economic, political, and social levels but different reports suggest that there is still much more we need to accomplish in order to be an even stronger union. for the european union’s progress, we need to figure out the uncertainties and fill the gaps so we can move on. i voted in favour of the tripartite social summit for growth and employment. i agree with president juncker’s views that highlight the importance of advancing towards a fair and truly european labour market through social dialogue and the deepening of economic and monetary union.
in writing. ‒ i agree with my group in supporting and voting in favour of the text presented.
in writing. ‒ the trilateral social summit for growth and jobs ensures continuous consultation between the european council, the council, the commission and the social partners. the summit enables the european social partners to contribute, through social dialogue, to the various aspects of the union's strategy for growth and jobs. the social dialogue is a pillar of the social market economy which the epp wants to help bring about in europe. i voted in favour of the adoption of the draft council decision.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the trilateral social summit for growth and jobs. in particular, the report establishes the trilateral social summit, a forum for discussion between the european union (eu) institutions and representatives of employers and workers. the summit is part of the inter-professional dialogue and is intended to provide a continuous exchange between the social partners and the eu institutions and to ensure that the social partners contribute to the economic and social strategy of the european union.
in writing. ‒ the overall objective of the directive is to provide a coherent and uniform framework to ensure the same level of safety for inland waterway vessels, with emphasis on rationalising the use of resources for the development of technical standards and their adaptation to scientific and technical progress through the use of standards drawn up by international organisations. for these reasons i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the belet report approving the council's position at first reading on the requirements for inland waterway vessels. this is a technical measure which aims at the uniform application of technical requirements in order to ensure a high level of safety and efficiency in inland navigation, taking into account the standards established by international organisations such as the european committee for the elaboration of standards for inland navigation (cesni). the text also calls for a periodic review of the directive every three years, with the aim of assessing the mechanisms for cooperation with the international organisations involved.
in writing. ‒ although the text is partially shared, there are still some unclear passages which could open the door to criticism. i therefore decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ at first reading, parliament supported the need for uniform application of the common technical requirements for inland waterway vessels in the european union in order to ensure a high level of safety and efficiency in inland waterway transport. we in this house have also expressed our support for the rapid adaptation of the rules to scientific and technical progress, taking into account the rules drawn up by international organizations, in particular by the european committee for the elaboration of rules for inland navigation (cesni), to be set up under the aegis of the central commission for navigation on the rhine. parliament also called for a periodic review of the directive every three years to assess the cooperation mechanisms with the international organisations involved. today, confirming these demands, we ask that the proposal be approved in a manner consistent with the negotiated agreement reached between parliament and council on 17 march 2016 as approved by the tran committee on 7 april last.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation today because i consider it of great importance that the common technical requirements for inland waterway vessels in the european union should be applied uniformly. my choice was therefore based on the desire to ensure a high level of safety and efficiency in inland navigation. the aim of the directive is to provide a coherent and uniform framework to ensure a common safety standard for inland waterway vessels. of particular importance is the rationalization of the use of resources for the development of technical standards and the adaptation to the considerable scientific and technical progress made, also in relation to standards prepared by the various international organizations. in this respect, the european committee for the elaboration of standards for inland navigation (cesni) plays an important role. cesni is an international body, but it comprises only the member states and switzerland. it is therefore essential to achieve the adaptation of technical standards by means of delegated acts.
in writing. ‒ the cooperation mechanism with the european committee for the elaboration of standards for inland navigation (cesni) will be reviewed within five years. that is why i voted in favour of mr belet's report.
in writing. ‒ with regard to the directive laying down technical requirements for inland waterway vessels in the european union, we supported, at first reading, the uniform application of the common technical requirements with a view to harmonising and ensuring a high level of safety and efficiency in inland waterway transport. we also called for a rationalisation of the use of resources for the development of technical standards and their adaptation to scientific and technical progress by using standards already established by international organisations such as cesni. we have also called for a periodic review of the directive every three years, with a view to assessing the mechanisms for cooperation with the international organisations involved. the european parliament, by voting today, reaffirms its institutional prerogatives in the field of the adaptation of technical standards in the inland waterway sector. i therefore voted in favour of this because i believe it is in the interests of the citizens of the european union that no new technical standards are introduced without the scrutiny of the european parliament.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for the second reading on technical requirements for inland waterway vessels presented by mr belet. i believe that the adoption of the directive is a positive development in the shipping sector and represents a step forward in the integration of the technical standards required by the european union. the issuing of certificates for navigation on the basis of compliance with technical requirements as provided for in article 22 of the directive will ensure a new level of safety and efficiency, as well as the achievement of a uniform set of technical requirements within the eu states, thanks to the work carried out by cesni.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on technical requirements for inland waterway vessels, as i am in favour of a uniform application of maritime technical requirements throughout the european union, aimed at ensuring an increasingly high level of safety and efficiency.
in writing. ‒ i support this recommendation because it offers a coherent and uniform framework to rationalise the use of resources and ensure a high level of safety for inland waterway vessels. structured investment in such shipping also allows for better collaboration between member countries and trade that promotes economic growth. these reasons have led me to vote in favour of the recommendation.
in writing. i support the european parliament's decision to provide a coherent and uniform framework for a level of safety for inland waterway vessels. as regards the technical requirements for inland waterway vessels, they are laid down in directive 2006/87/ec, which lays down the conditions for the issue of certificates permitting navigation in the internal waters of the union, including the rhine. it shall also ensure that such certificates are issued on the basis of technical requirements which ensure a level of safety that is at all times adequate. parliament also called for a periodic review of the directive every three years to assess the cooperation mechanisms with the international organisations involved.
in writing. ‒ i can only express my appreciation and thanks to mr ivo belet for the work he has done and for the excellent contribution he has made to the preparation of this final document.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted against this agreement, i voted against the agreement between the european union and certain countries in southern africa, including south africa, because it would be yet another blow to our agriculture, to the agriculture of europe, and especially of southern europe, to our citrus fruits, to the oranges - i must mention it - of my region, which have the healthiest organoleptic qualities. i'm against it because i want to say enough: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i say enough of agriculture as a commodity in the european trade policy and enough of the monopoly and the hand-wringing of the commission, which makes agreements without any assessment of the impact of these agreements on local markets, which is quite different from considering the general market of the european union. if the european commission does not do this, our farmers will soon be the ones to mourn the damage caused by the wrong choices.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, my colleagues from the five star movement and i voted against this agreement, an agreement which the commission claims is an agreement to help africa, but which is in fact a full-fledged trade agreement, which will open up 86% of the african market, an opening which is unsustainable for africa, which will result in the loss of eur 3.5 billion in unpaid customs duties and at the same time the first consequence for us will be an invasion of south african oranges at the very time of our harvest. furthermore, there is no chapter on sustainable development in the treaty and civil society has not been included in the wording. this agreement could easily increase regional disintegration by pitting south africa against smaller states. finally, we are forcing our partners to march in force towards ratification in october, without their parliamentarians having had time to read the text they are signing. if they do not sign, we will also punish them with prohibitive customs duties - a very good example of democracy, but that is what we have always done with africa.
in writing. ‒ on 12 june 2002, the council authorised the opening of epa negotiations with the group of botswana, lesotho, mozambique, namibia, swaziland (blmns) and south africa (sadc). the agreement provides asymmetric market access for the eu and sadc countries from a trade point of view, allowing them to protect sensitive sectors from liberalisation; the commission has also adopted a number of safeguard measures and a clause to protect the new industry. while i recognize the need to promote the economic and industrial development of these countries, i do not approve of such an asymmetry between the two markets, especially in a context of severe crisis for the european economy, which would harm eu operators. for these reasons, i voted against.
in writing. ‒ my commitment to the european parliament has always been in favour of my country's farmers. the economic partnership agreement between the eu and the sadc countries, which includes 15 african countries including south africa, will severely penalise our producers, especially in the citrus sector. as has already happened, this european union is proving incapable of protecting the economies of the member states by opening the door to products of dubious quality, often harmful to the health of our citizens, and by abolishing the duties that protect the agriculture of our territories. for these reasons i did not intend to support the text with my vote.
in writing. ‒ today i voted against the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the economic partnership agreement between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and the sadc epa states, of the other part. in 2000, the cotonou agreement called for fundamental changes in the continuing non-reciprocal trade preferences that had governed, for many years, the economic and political relations between the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group of states and the european union. the impact of these trade preferences has been unsatisfactory and in some cases even incompatible with wto rules. the european union and the acp countries had agreed to negotiate reciprocal trade agreements known as economic partnership agreements (epas). these agreements can be a tool for development and sustainable economic growth, but supporting the economies of the sadc states which are members of the epa (botswana, lesotho, mozambique, namibia, south africa and swaziland) would be to the disadvantage of the mediterranean countries of europe, especially the agriculture of southern italy which would suffer a further blow.
in writing. ‒ on 12 june 2002, the council authorised the opening of epa (partnership agreement) negotiations with the countries of the sadc region (southern african countries). from a trade point of view, the agreement provides asymmetrical market access to the eu and sadc countries, allowing the latter to protect their sensitive sectors from liberalisation. but this puts at risk some european productions - particularly those in the mediterranean - and, moreover, the method used by the commission to conclude this type of agreement does not guarantee a democratic process for our african partners and imposes an unequal distribution of wealth and economic development among the different states of the region, which have different characteristics and growth rates. i therefore decided to vote against.
in writing. ‒ i strongly reject the economic partnership agreement between the commission and the countries of the southern african development community. while i cannot deny that a first fundamental step has been taken towards the advancement of trade relations with sub-saharan africa, i believe that the promotion of local products in order to strengthen their competitiveness is the essence of my work. i cannot deny that the question that perplexes me most is the opening up of our market to their oranges: i would not be doing my duty if i did not protect our excellences. and it is not always right to sacrifice agri-food products on the altar of free trade and the export of technology. i hope that in the future it will be possible to reach agreements which will be beneficial to both sides and thus seize the opportunity to promote the progressive integration of african states into the world economy, also contributing to the eradication of poverty.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the trade agreement signed between the european union and the southern african development community. the objectives of the agreement are to contribute to poverty reduction, to promote regional integration and to the gradual integration of african countries into the global economy. the adoption of this economic agreement is a major step forward in trade relations with africa, because for the first time it is not based on a relationship of unilateral concessions, but on a genuine agreement on a regional basis, which is intended to involve other countries in the future. moreover, although this regional agreement is mainly geared towards developing trade relations in terms of trade in goods and sustainable development cooperation, it also leaves room for negotiation of further provisions on services, investment and intellectual property. the trade agreement is therefore part of a broader strategy which the sadc states are called upon to implement through national policies that facilitate trade, development and structural reforms.
in writing. ‒ the conclusion of the economic partnership agreement between the european union, its member states and the southern african development community (sadc) states acceding to the epa marks an important step forward in trade relations and development cooperation with africa. in fact, despite the relatively positive data on african growth, poverty, inequality and instability still plague the african continent and are affected by international trade relations to the detriment of local economies. the economic partnership agreement introduces a chapter dedicated to regional integration and safeguarding sustainable trade and development in the sadc states. for example, the eu has shown flexibility, allowing sadc epa states to maintain existing export duties, to apply new export taxes in the event of specific revenue needs, and to exclude sensitive products from liberalisation, to promote nascent industries and to protect the environment. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution. in addition, my vote in favour is intended to maintain a high level of attention to the monitoring of the plant health risk from the cbs plant disease in agriculture in the sadc countries, which has so far been controlled by increased surveillance of orange consignments from the african region.
in writing. ‒ the european union-southern african development community (sadc) partnership agreement, together with the agreements with the west and southern africa region on which the european parliament will shortly be taking a decision, are an important signal of the european union's renewed interest in the african continent. trade relations with these macro-regions are all the more significant at a time when one of the major challenges for the european member states is the considerable increase in migration flows from this continent. in this context, although the agreement provides for an asymmetrical opening of the two markets to the benefit of the sadc countries, its structure raises some concerns in the field of human rights and sustainable development. in particular, i am against the fact that a monitoring mechanism has not been introduced to ensure and verify the effective respect of the human rights clauses contained in the agreement; the commission has also proposed a new instrument which would ensure greater coherence between trade policy and european development cooperation policy. i have therefore abstained on the decision of parliament to give its assent to the conclusion of the economic partnership agreement between the european union and the sadc states.
in writing. - i vote against: once again our producers are being penalized.
in writing. ‒ i voted to support this recommendation report by mr lambsdorff. this agreement, which is a trade and development partnership between the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) states and the european union, aims to support trade, regional integration and to foster sustainable development. these are very important issues and it is something that we should support, but it is also important that the report underlines that domestic development policies and structural reforms are needed in these countries and that this agreement will not do anything in a vacuum. for this reason, i also supported the call from my colleagues that it is important that we strengthen the monitoring process to this agreement.
in writing. ‒ the vote on the economic partnership agreement between the eu and the southern african development community (sadc) countries required very careful reflection on the assessment of the real benefits and mutual benefits between the parties. the agreement will allow botswana, lesotho, mozambique, namibia and swaziland free access to the european market through the elimination of quotas and customs duties, while south africa, already a bilateral partner of the eu, will see the freedom of access of its goods and agricultural products facilitated. after the tunisian oil disaster, we are seeing yet another blow to our farms and in particular to the small producers of citrus fruit in mediterranean europe, who are already subject to unfair competition from countries such as morocco and who will now have to endure the invasion of the european market by tons of cheap oranges without adequate plant health controls. my vote against the text is therefore also a firm no to the policy of selling off our agriculture without any proper impact assessment. as regards goods from the eu destined for south africa, i think that a good agreement could have taken into account, in addition to wine and foodstuffs, our olive oil with a protected designation of origin, which is not mentioned in the text.
in writing. the economic partnership agreement between the eu and the 15 sadc epa states is a regional economic development agreement that includes not only trade in goods, development cooperation and trade and sustainable development provisions, but also provisions on services, investment, intellectual property, public procurement and better conditions for sustainable development. however, i believe that this scenario could have serious consequences for certain strategic production sectors in our country. the agreement provides for the extension of the period of preferential tariff treatment for citrus fruit from 1 june to 16 october, when customs duties are reintroduced at the rate of 16%, and now extends it until 30 november, with a planned reduction of 1.8% per year, until total exemption by 2025. a further month and a half during which the production of orange blondes is likely to suffer from aggressive and harmful competition. for these reasons, and because i consider that agreement to be disadvantageous for southern europe and for mediterranean agriculture, i voted against mr lambsdorff's report.
in writing. – the european union holds many functions but economics is the main one. i voted in favour of the conclusion of the eu and the sadc epa states to set an economic partnership, for such activity shows signs of the following: bringing fundamental positive change, contributing to sustainable economic growth, and strengthening intra-regional trade and integration. trade has proven to be an effective tool in enhancing employment opportunities, and, therefore, the african countries that form part of the sadc epa could really benefit their economies and gdps by deepening economic ties with europe. however, there is a need to emphasise the importance of trade by the african states in a sustainable manner that can comply with eu regulations.
in writing. ‒ the reason why i decided to speak out against this agreement is that i wish to express my opposition to a method which is increasingly being used as a background for the negotiation of trade agreements with third countries. while recognising the need to establish trade links with developing countries, i believe it is unacceptable that the agri-food sector, the backbone of the mediterranean economy, should be sacrificed in the definition of such partnerships.
in writing. ‒ let me state my firm conviction (at this very particular historical moment) that the only way forward for the eu is through openness and partnership towards and with third countries, not through closure by the construction of physical or regulatory barriers. i therefore welcome the report and i shall vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament was asked to give its assent to the economic partnership agreement with the southern african development community, which comprises six countries: the commission has also proposed that the council adopt a decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european community and the republic of south africa on the conclusion of the agreement between the european community and the republic of south africa on the conclusion of the agreement between the european community and the republic of south africa. i voted against the approval of this agreement because i believe that, for the umpteenth time, the italian citrus fruit sector is being heavily penalized. it is enough to think that, although south african oranges are already allowed free access throughout the country from 1 june to 15 october, the entry of oranges into south africa would be delayed until 30 november if this agreement were to be introduced. moreover, with a gradual reduction in taxation, until complete abolition in 2025. the rejection of this partnership agreement does not mean that europe should be forced to adopt an autarchic trade model, but rather that it should be emphasized that measures must be taken to promote local products in order to strengthen their competitiveness. the protection of european products has been sacrificed to a view of international trade which does not include the principle of protecting southern european products, as has already happened with tunisian oil and moroccan tomatoes.
in writing. ‒ the aim of the report is to increase women's participation in the labour market by making the current eu legal and policy framework more modern and adapted to today's labour market, to enable people with children or other dependent family members to better balance family and working life, to allow for greater sharing of caring responsibilities between women and men and to strengthen gender equality in the labour market. for these reasons i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on the implementation of the labour convention in the fisheries sector. the convention, adopted in 2007 by the international labour organisation (ilo), has set out a set of rules covering issues essential to ensuring decent working and living conditions on board fishing vessels: minimum age for work, rest periods, rules on accommodation, food and wages; the commission has also proposed that the convention be amended to include the following matters: to date, only two countries have ratified the convention: france and estonia. the resolution adopted welcomes the agreement between the social partners and the commission implementing the ilo convention on labour in the fisheries sector and calls for the rapid adoption and implementation of the corresponding council directive. the approach of the text, which provides for the definition of minimum community standards, is the best because it guarantees the freedom of the member states and the social partners to adopt measures which are more favourable to workers in the sector concerned in the individual countries.
in writing. ‒ although the text is largely balanced and acceptable, there are still some passages which could open up the door to future criticism, and i therefore abstained.
in writing. ‒ the fisheries sector is a sector that has grown considerably, and this growth has also had a significant impact on working conditions and safety at work. workers in the fisheries sector often face difficult working conditions. it is therefore necessary to ensure adequate protection of fishermen at global level, taking into account the particular characteristics of work on board fishing vessels, the high rate of accidents and the risk of illness, and the lack of a clear distinction between working hours, rest and leisure time. the adoption of these international labour standards for what is one of the most dangerous professions in the world is extremely important to protect workers and provide them with decent working conditions. the objectives of this agreement are therefore to protect the living and working conditions, health and safety of workers in the maritime fisheries sector.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a council directive implementing the agreement concluded by the general confederation of agricultural cooperatives in the european union (cogeca), the european transport workers' federation (etf) and the association of national fisheries organisation organisations of the european union (europêche) on 21 may 2012, as amended on 8 may 2013, on the implementation of the international labour organisation's 2007 fisheries labour convention. the european union and its member states should play a leading role in promoting adequate wages and working conditions in the fisheries sector, bearing in mind that the agreement applies to all fishermen employed on board a fishing vessel registered in an eu member state. the european union, by incorporating the social partners' agreement on the ilo labour convention in its legislation, will be in a position to promote its implementation in partner countries around the world, thus contributing to greater equity in the sector.
in writing. ‒ the report recommends the adoption of the proposal for a council directive implementing the agreement concluded between cogeca, etf, europeche in 2013 on the implementation of the ilo labour convention in the fisheries sector. it is particularly worth noting that the convention and its accompanying recommendation 199 call for decent working and living conditions on board vessels, strict health and safety standards, the establishment of a minimum working age and the protection of young workers. i voted for it, for sure.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep resolution on the implementation of the agreement between the social partners of 21 may 2012, subsequently amended by the council, concerning the implementation of the ilo convention on work in the fisheries sector because i believe that this sector is very important for the economy of many member states and of certain areas of our country in particular. as shadow rapporteur for the s&d group, i have supported this resolution from the outset, the priority being to encourage the council to adopt the directive at the next epsco council on 13 october. four years after the signing of the agreement, the time has come to adopt the proposal for a council directive implementing the agreement, because it is urgent to ensure decent working conditions and safety at work for workers in the fisheries sector. the commission's proposal for a council directive incorporates the agreement reached between the social partners to improve the working conditions of the more than 100 000 workers in the european fishing industry, who are often forced to work in very difficult conditions and for long periods at sea.
in writing. this agreement builds on the implementation of the labour convention in the fisheries sector and provides for greater protection for workers working on board fishing vessels, given the high rate of fatal and non-fatal accidents, as well as the risk of occupational diseases and their frequency compared to other sectors in a hazardous work environment. it also aims to ensure decent working and living conditions on board, the responsibility of vessel owners and masters for the health and safety of workers; the establishment of a minimum age for work and the protection of young workers; compulsory medical examinations and certificates; the rest periods; employment agreements, which set out tasks and working conditions. the agreement applies to all fishermen employed on board a fishing vessel which is registered in or flies the flag of an eu member state and which is engaged in commercial fishing operations. for these reasons, the immediate adoption of the council directive is recommended, as requested by the social partners, and i therefore fully support it.
in writing. ‒ the issue of fisheries and fishermen is a very difficult one and the eu must show its capacity to be a solution, not a problem. i regard the text as a step forward for the workers and therefore i feel obliged to approve it.
in writing. ‒ according to commission figures, more than 100,000 people work in the eu fisheries sector, often in difficult conditions. the accident and injury rate can be up to 15 times higher than in other sectors. on 29 april 2016, the european commission, at the request of the social partners, therefore presented a proposal for a council directive implementing the ilo convention on labour in the fisheries sector. the fishing industry has grown considerably. however, this growth has not been without social costs - in terms of working conditions and safety - for both full-time and part-time workers. they often have to spend long periods at sea and are often exposed to unpredictable and dangerous conditions. i therefore voted in favour of this because the adoption of these international standards is essential to protect workers and to ensure more dignified working conditions for them.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to explain the reasons for my vote in favour of this report, which is a first step in the union's fight against social dumping. i believe that this is only the first step and that there is still a long way to go in the fight against social dumping, which, as we know, is the result of a wild globalization that allows capital to move freely and is linked to an increasingly radical process of deregulation, which is systematically eroding the rights of workers. i think that this race to the bottom in the field of labour rights must be stopped and i think that this must be done either by establishing european labour standards, and thus, say, supplementing national legislation upwards, or by establishing a minimum income for citizens at european level, as we shall be discussing tomorrow in the house.
in writing. ‒ unfair competition between companies is a huge problem, as european workers do not have the same social rights and obligations. the report proposes some solutions to this problem, focusing in particular on improving control and inspection tools, modernising the recording of work performance by also producing a single digital social rights transfer document for each european worker and finally producing a 'black list' containing all companies which have committed infringements in the field of workers' protection. to ensure that all european workers have a high level of social protection within the eu i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the current context presents a number of conditions which seriously undermine the level of social protection which underpins the whole project of european integration. the balas report, which i strongly supported, tackles the issue of social dumping in the union, strongly highlighting the damage caused by increased competition between economic operators. excessive competition leads not only to a reduction in labour costs but also to a weakening of social standards and the same rights that should be guaranteed to employees on the continent. reversing this downward trend must be a priority, and this requires first of all improving controls and inspections at all levels, increasing the human and financial resources available to the authorities. reforms are needed to modernise labour registration, urgent action in the transport sector, a single digital social rights transfer document for every european worker and measures such as the creation of a european list of companies guilty of serious infringements. only by resolving the asymmetry between the reality of the internal market and social rights will it be possible to create a real upward social convergence.
in writing. ‒ the single market is an unfair and sick project supported by the european institutions. the free movement of workers and the enormous differences in labour costs between member states have turned relocation and dumping into social scourges that are wiping out entire economic sectors in italy, such as construction and road transport. our territories and our workers are victims of the unfair maneuvers of foreign interim agencies and multinational companies, which are slaughtering our productive fabric, leaving italian workers in a desert of unemployment and social problems. the rules of the single market must be rewritten, this time in the interests of our people. for all these reasons i did not intend to support the text with my vote.
in writing. ‒ labour and social policy legislation is still a matter for the member states. in the absence of harmonisation mechanisms and with very different social systems, the single market and the free movement of workers can give rise to practices such as social dumping. these are forms of unfair competition between firms and indirectly between workers, which seek to use the most advantageous of the existing rules in the various member states. we are faced with a problem which is not only social but also political and which requires a european solution aimed at protecting its citizens. i therefore welcome this report which tackles the various aspects of the phenomenon and highlights the need for an initiative to tackle the issue of unfair competition between european companies and the resulting abusive practices which jeopardise the rights of citizens as workers.
in writing. ‒ in the eu, the economic side often prevails over the social side: this leads to imbalances, especially territorial ones, where a different level of protection of rights from one state to another leads to the exploitation of low-skilled labour, to internal migration of the same labour and to a risk of a double system of internal social and security standards, with the consequence of increasing internal differences and mistrust between citizens of the union and generating social envy. the specific weakness of the social protection of certain employees such as 'sea workers', who are victims of the use, by many shipowners, of flags of convenience, which allow employers to evade social obligations, should be emphasized. such practices have a negative impact on safety standards and contribute to the decline in the number of qualified european seafarers and the loss of their know-how. this is not acceptable for the world's leading political reality in promoting living standards and individual rights: the commission's proposal is a good one, but it is not enough. the introduction of a duty of care for the most important european companies in relation to the activities of their subsidiaries and subcontractors is necessary.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the problem of social dumping is of great urgency and requires urgent and targeted action. one of the fundamental principles of eu policies is social cohesion. this means that there is an urgent need to bring wages closer together in order to ensure better and more effective social protection for all workers. in the present union, considerable differences persist in terms of both working conditions and pay. unfair competition reduces operating and labour costs, and it leads to serious violations of workers' rights, even to the point of exploitation. the social rights, for which the member states still have competence in many cases, must be harmonized. i agree with the rapporteur that we should strengthen controls and inspections in accordance with the legislation in force.
in writing. ‒ the report highlights the distortions linked to the internal market as currently conceived. there are no social rights and treatment for workers valid throughout the union, which leads to dumping to their detriment. competition between economic operators is in fact being dumped on the cost of labour, leading to a deleterious race to the bottom of standards. the report recommends measures to address the shortcomings in the fight against unfair competition and to promote the portability of workers' social rights. i certainly voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ social and economic inequalities in europe are jeopardising the achievement of the europe 2020 poverty and employment goals. the increasing trend towards underground work, outsourcing and subcontracting, and the consequent increase in precariousness and deterioration in the level of protection of workers, are among the primary causes of this disparity. social dumping and other forms of unfair competition are preventing the achievement of working conditions and social standards guaranteed at european level. i therefore appreciated the emphasis in the report on the primacy of fundamental rights and the desire to intensify the social dialogue against dumping. i believe that the creation of a european body of labour inspectors to investigate unfair competition and cases of social dumping can be an effective measure. in addition, it should be noted that women are often the most affected by social dumping and undeclared work, especially in domestic and care work. i very much hope that the commission, in cooperation with its member states, will undertake a detailed and timely analysis of the situation of women who are victims of such practices. on the basis of these observations, i have decided to support the report.
in writing. ‒ i have spoken in favour of this important and controversial subject, in order to send a positive signal to the struggle for workers' social rights. i congratulate my colleague danuta jazlowiecka on the excellent work she has done on this report. i am glad that a final compromise with the s&d group has made it possible to propose, for the first time at european level, a definition of 'social dumping', understood as intentional abusive practices and circumvention of european and national legislation to the detriment of workers.
in writing. ‒ 'social dumping', a term which at present has no legally recognised and universally agreed definition, yet it is common knowledge that illegal practices are proliferating which allow unfair competition to develop, thus creating an asymmetry between the reality of a constantly evolving internal market and highly heterogeneous social rights, which weakens adherence to the principle of the internal market and weakens confidence in the european construction. rather than hiding behind protectionist policies, adopting unilateral decisions on social matters, states would do better to cooperate with each other, strengthening controls to prevent, above all, the use by certain economic actors of illegal practices such as underground work or abusive practices such as false selfemployment, which can lead to serious market distortions, to the detriment of honest companies, in particular smes, and all those sectors most affected, such as agriculture, construction and the food sector. i believe in the need to achieve social convergence in the eu, for a fairer labour market in order to achieve strong and sustainable competitiveness in all member states.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's resolution is a step forward for the europe of social convergence, which wants to affirm its will for social progress, and which reduces the differences and therefore the contrasts and discriminations between workers who practice the profession in different european nations. i voted in favour of the resolution because i think it is appropriate that the measures proposed by the european parliament include increased control and coordination between and by the member states against companies which are responsible for serious breaches of social labour legislation and of the fundamental rights of workers, in combating social dumping in the transport sector which is particularly fragmented at european level also through the creation of a european agency for wheeled transport and in protecting women who are particularly affected by social dumping.
in writing. ‒ the structural reforms in the field of labour demanded by europe have resulted in precarious contracts and reduced social security in some member states. in addition, the 'selling off' of social protection in favour of more favourable economic treatment, exploitation through breaches of working and rest times, reduced competitiveness with china and other third countries, but also the growing tendency in italy to use vouchers instead of regular employment contracts, or even to resort to the corporate sector, lead to an increase in precariousness, forms of enslavement, lack of security at the workplace and reduced tax revenues for the member states. the proposal to penalize those who use social dumping to make more profit is welcome, but more widespread and more stringent controls are needed. finally, i welcome the proposal to counter the decline in the employment rate caused by the economic and financial crisis with a paradigm shift that puts income ahead of work and pursues the objective of ensuring a 'citizenship minimum income' throughout the european union to ensure a free and dignified existence. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ the heterogeneity of national and european social and labour law means that social dumping is still a reality in the european union today. as in the case of trade relations with our partners, we must combat this phenomenon to prevent the serious market distortions we are facing and to ensure equal treatment and non-discrimination for all european workers. as the report argues, the european commission and the member states will need to ensure that checks are strengthened to ensure better implementation of existing legislation, and to encourage greater coordination between and by member states to combat the deterioration in the levels of protection of workers and the quality of work in general, which is very often caused by the abuse and circumvention of existing legislation by certain economic actors. the illegal reduction of operating and labour costs leads to unfair competition and the violation of workers' rights, which is harmful to honestly working enterprises, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, which are very important players in the european production system. that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ social dumping occurs when an employer hires labour at a lower cost than the resources available on the national market. this practice must be limited as it has a negative impact on the social fabric, affecting above all the weaker sections of employees. i supported the report because it is committed to improving controls and legislation at both european and national level for the development of a sustainable and competitive economy while respecting workers' rights and social progress.

in writing. ‒ i welcomed the proposal for a european policy to combat social dumping. when the european union was created, it was intended to be a democratic area with an efficient economy and a high level of social protection. the task of protecting the social rights of the peoples of europe had been delegated to the member states, which were to harmonise their welfare systems with the aim of avoiding unfair forms of competition. nevertheless, the problem of social dumping today affects european individuals and communities in violation of the principles of the internal market and the union's spirit of solidarity. the interconnection of markets raises the issue of reconciling different social protection systems, leading to widespread distrust in the union's ability to guarantee the rights of its citizens. this is why we need european policies to protect workers and regulate the activities of companies. we need measures to ensure that companies pay taxes in the countries where they make their profits, we need a tightening up of tax havens and a new directive on precarious work. in short, a european pillar of social rights must be activated.

in writing. ‒ i believe it is misleading for investors to exclude credit risk from the calculation of the risk categorisation of insurance products, as consumer information on investment products should be fully comparable in order to promote a level playing field in the market. therefore, since the delegated act adopted by the commission contains gaps in the methodology for calculating future performance scenarios and therefore does not fulfil the requirement under regulation (eu) no 1286/2014 to provide information that is 'accurate, correct, clear and not misleading', there is a risk of a conflict with the spirit and purpose of the legislation, which is to provide clear, comparable, understandable and non-misleading information on priips to retail investors. this report therefore calls for the dele­gated regulation not to enter into force, while at the same time calling on the commission to present a new delegated act to take account of the risks mentioned above. for these reasons i voted in favour.

in writing. this is a parliamentary objection to reject the delegated act proposed by the commission to implement the priips regulation on retail investment and insurance products. the technical implementing rules developed by the commission in the delegated act, under the strong pressure of the financial lobbies, have in fact been found to be in direct conflict with the objectives of the regulation to enable investors to invest in an informed manner on the basis of accurate, clear, understandable and non-misleading information, ensuring maximum transparency and comparability between financial products. since these technical standards are intended to regulate key elements of the kid, including the probabilistic performance scenarios, risk indicators, cost calculation methodology - this motion rightly asks the commission to postpone the date of application of the regulation and to rewrite the delegated act from scratch, taking full account of the objectives of the regulation and the concerns expressed by this parliament. in the absence of these fundamental technical rules, a provisional application of the priips would risk seriously harming investors by providing them with incomplete and misleading information, thus playing into the hands of lobbies, and would also allow unelected technocrats to override the democratic will of legislators. for these reasons i have voted in favour of this motion.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, yesterday morning president juncker said that despite the encouraging improvements, the question of employment remains a priority throughout europe. but there can be no sustainable employment growth if discrimination in access to employment and in the workplace is not also combated. fifteen years after the entry into force of the equal treatment in employment and working conditions directive, the unemployment rate for people with disabilities is still almost twice that of the general population. the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities provides, after its adoption by the union, a good basis for the definition of the concept of disability itself as well as for the concepts of universal design of physical spaces and reasonable accommodation. in addition, a significant economic return is possible from investments in accessibility as well as a gain in terms of social inclusion. the member states must therefore do much more to make these reasonable solutions which already exist attractive.
the commission has already submitted a proposal for a regulation to the council. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the lack of complete data makes it difficult for us to know whether the globalisation adjustment fund has been an effective instrument so far. for this reason, it is necessary that in future the commission should ensure public access to all documents relating to cases of assistance from the fund and provide complete information to enable it to be understood whether the training provided has been adapted to the economic prospects and labour market needs in the regions affected by the redundancies and what the expected and achieved results have been. in particular, it is necessary to be able to understand whether closures and redundancies are the result of relocating production to third countries or other member states which apply aggressive fiscal policies to attract investment. it is important that citizens do not pay for corporate profit-making, which is why we are asking the commission to consider a tool which would oblige companies moving production outside the eu to contribute to the reintegration measures for redundant workers.

author. – mr president, the situation in the philippines is extremely worrying, especially after the election of president duterte. he started with all kinds of provocations and insults, and this year became the protagonist of verbal attacks against the un, china, the president of the united states and the pope, with hate speeches instigating violence against suspected drug sellers and drug users. as a consequence of these promises and behaviour, according to the official information at our disposal, starting from the day of his election on 30 june 2016 until this month of september, 44 people have been killed every day – 2 927 in total – as a result of extrajudicial execution and lynching, following these hateful speeches. duterte is an elected president and in the near future he will play a fundamental role in the complex and delicate geopolitical balance of the south china sea between china, the united states and russia. with this resolution we ask the authorities to investigate and condemn the action of vigilance groups, and we urge the commission to use all available instruments to help the government in respecting its international human rights obligations. we have the duty to use all our means in order to block the rise of a new dictator and the consequences on human rights violations in the philippines.
author. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this person who is now governing the philippines has promised to clean up the illegal drug trade in order to be elected, and i must say that a battle which is in itself just is in fact being fought by a hateful repression. the figures for killings and extrajudicial executions have already been mentioned by my colleagues; i would add to these the fact that the massive campaign against drug dealers and consumers has led to more than 15 000 arrests and has prompted more than half a million people to turn themselves in in the hope of receiving adequate medical treatment and immunity. i think it is right that this resolution should ask, by joining the voice and appeals of the activists, to signal the concern that this zero tolerance policy has been accompanied by gross violations of human rights. i am convinced, as are others, that the european union must review its position towards the philippines.

in writing. strong condemnation of drug trafficking and abuse in the philippines is needed, stressing that illicit drugs are a threat to filipino youth and one of the most serious social problems. while welcoming the government's intention to reduce the high levels of crime and corruption in the country, it is necessary to adopt specific policies and programmes, including prevention and recovery measures, without focusing exclusively on violent repression, while also ensuring respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. in addition, the authorities should launch an immediate, thorough, effective and impartial investigation into the extraordinarily high number of people killed during police operations, in order to identify all those responsible, bring them to a competent and impartial civil court and apply the criminal sanctions provided for by law, while ensuring adequate protection for human rights defenders, trade unionists and journalists. the eu must use all available tools to help the philippine government to comply with its international human rights obligations.
the agenda includes seven motions for resolutions on somalia.
author. – mr president, somalia’s long-running conflict situation continues to leave civilians dead, wounded and displaced in large numbers. in july the unhcr reported that forced evictions due to an ongoing military offensive resulted in almost 28 000 new displacements. international human rights and humanitarian organisations continue to report serious abuses against people living in informal displacement camps and in government-controlled areas, including rape and forced evictions. according to international human rights organisations and the un mission in somalia, journalists continue to be killed, threatened, arbitrarily detained and denied due process or fair trial guarantees. this is an issue of major concern, particularly given the fact that elections should take place very soon. we think that the european union should support any effort to protect the population. we should also assist the government of somalia in its work to build peace and stability. on the other hand, the eu should better monitor the situation in order ensure accountability for abuses committed, fair and timely elections and legal reforms in order to secure respect for human rights. we hope that this joint resolution can help in this.
author. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the armed conflict that has been raging in somalia for some time is still causing enormous problems. despite the commitments made by the somali government, the continuing political instability prevents the country from initiating the necessary reform processes, especially in the area of justice and security. many journalists have been threatened and arrested in trials conducted in ways that are not in line with international law standards. in january 2016, the somali president signed a new media and information law that still contains several restrictions on freedom of expression. the need of the somali people for a free media is particularly important in view of the upcoming electoral process and it is therefore right to call for attention, including at international level, to the government of somalia to protect and protect journalists and to revise legislation so as to allow for effective freedom of the press and information, while respecting the right to freedom of expression and more generally the protection of human rights which have been largely neglected and long violated.

author. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, for many years the people of zimbabwe have suffered under an authoritarian regime led by president mugabe, who has maintained his power through corruption, violence, rigged elections and the use of brutal apparatuses. the situation in zimbabwe is worsening today, with impunity for human rights violations. since june, dozens of public protests have been launched by civil society leaders across the country. the police responded with violent methods, indiscriminately using batons and tear gas. hundreds of people have been injured, arrested and charged with public violence. we cannot forget in this context that the government of zimbabwe and the european union jointly signed the national indicative programme and, as part of this joint cooperation strategy, the european union has allocated eur 234 million to zimbabwe as development assistance. i believe that the european union should monitor effectively the implementation of these funds to ensure that zimbabwe uses this sum in the areas envisaged, such as support for civil society, human rights and agriculture. we call for the early holding of regular elections in order to establish a pluralistic, prosperous and human rights-respecting democracy.
author. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, following a series of anti-government demonstrations in zimbabwe, president mugabe, who has been in power for 36 years, has adopted a severe repressive policy. fearing to lose power, he has already announced his intention to run in the 2018 presidential elections but it is difficult to imagine how he can complete a new term, which would end at the venerable age of 99. the president has also been accused of voluntarily cutting off food aid to rural areas most hostile to his policies and hit by the worst drought in a century. with this urgent resolution we call on zimbabwe to respect its international obligations and to guarantee the independence of the judiciary and freedom of demonstration. the european union can play a key role in this delicate phase by maintaining and, if necessary, strengthening the restrictive measures against persons and entities linked to the mugabe regime, at least until there is a political reversal aimed at protecting the population and respecting democratic principles and the rule of law.
i would like to remind the zimbabwean authorities, if necessary, of the content of article 96 of the cotonou agreement and the obligations it imposes on respect for human rights, democratic principles and the rule of law. i also recall the restrictive measures imposed on certain authorities, first and foremost president mugabe, who has been in office since 1980. we can no longer tolerate the violence with which the security forces systematically suppress any voice of dissent in the country. we are protesting against violence against women, arbitrary arrests, interference by the authorities, disappearances and arbitrary killings. the people of zimbabwe are demanding a peaceful and democratic transition based on free elections, the rotation of power and respect for human rights. we will be at your side to support you in the political dialogue with the authorities and to denounce any violation of democratic principles.
mr president, colleagues have already described the difficult situation in zimbabwe, and i would just like to add that for me there is a key point 7 in the resolution which clearly states that the lifting of sanctions against zimbabwe was premature and that the commission should reconsider how to impose sanctions on a regime whose horrors have been described in detail here. in short, and well, some of my colleagues have said it, helping the regime of the current president mugabe by sending some 200 million euros is wrong. the money doesn't go to the people who need the money anyway, it ends up in the hands of the regime's supporters and the mugabe family itself. so the important thing is point 7. i am therefore prepared to support this resolution.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the republic of zimbabwe, now collapsing, is facing a very serious economic crisis: the situation is particularly serious in rural areas, particularly those most hostile to president mugabe, who, according to the zimbabwe human rights commission, has decided to cut off food aid to some 4 million citizens who are suffering from drought and are unable to feed themselves. the country has been plagued by violent demonstrations over the economic and political situation for several months. the european union must condemn the government's blockade of aid to the people affected by the drought and check that the funds granted to zimbabwe are actually used for the sectors concerned. we must work for a peaceful transition of power in a democratic manner and with respect for human rights.
