in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of appointing sir julian king as commissioner for security of the union because i believe that the commissioner-designate has all the necessary qualifications to be able to fulfil his duties in an optimal way. sir julian king was appointed by the british government after jonathan hill resigned last june following the brexit vote. as commissioner for security, julian king will take forward the implementation of the european agenda on security and contribute to the creation of an effective and effective security union. he will work under the leadership of the commission's first vice-president, frans timmermans, and will support commissioner dimitris avramopoulos' work on migration, home affairs and citizenship. for the first time parliament is deciding on the suitability of a commissioner to work in brussels during the process of his country's exit from the eu. sir julian king, currently ambassador to france, is an expert on international and european relations. from 2009 to 2011, sir king served as ambassador to ireland.

in writing. ‒ the regulation aims to create a single model within the member states that ensures high technological and security standards for the production of return documents for irregular residents. as i believe that the introduction of a single model can increase the rate of return of irregular migrants in order to maintain the integrity of the common european asylum system and improve cooperation with third countries, i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the halla-aho report on travel documents for the return of illegally staying third-country nationals. a substantial review of the format and implementation of the eu standard travel document should be carried out rapidly in order to increase its recognition by third countries and ensure its greater effectiveness. harmonisation can not only lead to a reduction in red tape and costs but also allow for safe return, respecting the fundamental rights guaranteed by international treaties and the charter of nice, and safeguarding the health conditions of migrants. multilingual translation and new technological standards can be key tools to increase the use of the document and protect it from counterfeiting.
in writing. ‒ a serious and concrete action plan must be found as soon as possible to repatriate the thousands of illegal immigrants in europe. although i share the report's objective, in that it calls for better cooperation with third countries to facilitate the return of illegal immigrants to their country, i do not agree with the eu being entrusted with the negotiation of return agreements with these countries, as i believe that this prerogative should be retained by the individual member states. for these reasons i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the european union must enforce its agreements with third countries on the return of irregular migrants: it is a question of justice for those who meet the conditions for being able to stay, of security for the overall maintenance of the reception system and of stability so as not to further damage the relationship of trust with the institutions. the european union cannot continue to be satisfied with the current rate of return of rejected asylum seekers. a substantial revision of the format and implementation of the eu standard travel document is necessary in order to increase its recognition by third countries and to ensure its effectiveness. by harmonizing the format of the travel document, member states will reduce red tape, discrepancies, costs and waiting times, in the hope that the document will be more widely recognised by third countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on 'travel documents for the return of illegally staying third-country nationals' today because i believe that the exceptional wave of migration that has swept europe is bringing us face to face with age-old problems which, however, given the emergency situation, require urgent, concrete responses, but above all in line with eu legislation. one of these is undoubtedly the mechanisms for returning thirdcountry nationals. this is a delicate matter which must be dealt with with a certain amount of rationality, without ever losing sight of the strict respect for the rights of these people. an effective and credible return policy goes hand in hand with a more open migration policy. the commission should also be able to provide information on the number of returnees to the member states, the number of persons who are to be returned to the member states and the number of persons who are to be returned to the member states. increasing the rate of return of irregular migrants certainly allows for the release of reception capacity for those who really need protection. this must be the main objective of the european union, in the respect of the law, but above all in the reception and assistance of all those who are fleeing from war, famine and persecution.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation concerns the introduction of a single eu-wide model for the return of those who do not qualify for international protection. this would facilitate uniformity of treatment and bureaucracy, and thus also facilitate relations with third countries which would be faced with the same type of travel documents. in fact, many third countries now often refuse to accept return documents issued by member states because of their poor quality. finally, this would help to protect against the risk of false or counterfeit documents. i voted for it with conviction.
in writing. ‒ my vote in favour is justified not only by the devastating migration crisis faced by our country mainly with its own resources, but also by the hope that full harmonisation of the union's migration policies can constitute an effective and resilient system to increase recognition rates by third countries. the council recommendation of 30 november 1994, now repealed, provided for the introduction of a standard travel document. however, it has never been uniformly established in the union, and has led to different ways of working which are likely to exacerbate the phenomenon. we must indeed be able to tackle common problems together, but to do so we need eu instruments with the same format and the same technical specificities, so that each member state can reduce red tape, waiting times for returnees and the associated costs. at the same time, this would simplify relations with non-eu countries by means of effective recognition and faster readmission of the citizen. in view of the increased efforts made by the countries concerned to ensure that the new european travel document can operate, the union is committed to establishing a harmonised, clear format that makes the exchange of information easy and secure.
in writing. - they already call it the "great wall of calais". after austria, london has also thought it wise to have a concrete barrier of two kilometres in length in the hope of limiting the flow of migrants. but is it really worthwhile to take such action which is totally contrary to the principle of solidarity? would it not be better to speed up the process of creating a genuine european strategy on immigration, with the structuring of a more coherent return policy as a priority? without a serious policy of development cooperation, in which europe must play a leading role, we shall condemn a part of the world to a certain and inevitable destiny of poverty and despair. the european travel document will increase the rate of return of irregular migrants, harmonise technical specifications to prevent counterfeiting and forgery, and resolve differences between states in the acceptance of the travel document, while ensuring the exchange of information between states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which aims to improve the european travel document for the return of illegally staying third-country nationals, as part of better cooperation on return and readmission with the main countries of origin and transit. the current travel document for the return of third-country nationals, established by the council recommendation of 30 november 1994, is not accepted by all third countries because of the inadequacy of its security standards, which hinders the execution of returns under the readmission agreements of the eu or its member states with third countries and thus the proper functioning of european migration policy. this report addresses the current situation by proposing a uniform system at european level for the travel document allowing for return to third countries, in accordance with the technical specifications already established by regulation (ec) no 333/2002.
in writing. the harmonisation of the format and technical specifications of the european travel document for the return of illegally staying third-country nationals is intended to facilitate the recognition of this document by third countries for the purposes of return and readmission. the aim of facilitating the successful completion of administrative procedures and reducing red tape, discrepancies, costs and waiting times is fully acceptable.
in writing. ‒ one of the european union's biggest challenges today is the effectiveness of the common european asylum system, which is still too weak and slow to deal with the deep refugee crisis. i voted in favour of issuing a travel document for the return of those who do not meet the requirements for international protection within the european union. it is a very important instrument which will speed up the procedures for reception and expulsion, but above all it will make it possible to avoid uncontrolled and unmanageable immigration with disastrous consequences for our countries, starting with italy. the european union must respond with all the instruments at its disposal and prevent the collapse of our reception system.

in writing. ‒ this is a very relevant and important proposal that tackles one of the most pressing issues that the eu is currently facing, namely the readmission of illegal immigrants. the document proposed by the commission would establish a common format with high security and safeguards against falsification. this is something very necessary, which will make the associated administrative work more efficient. the report highlights the fact that, in eu negotiations with third countries, readmission agreements should take precedence over bilateral agreements – something that would guarantee more effective implementation of readmission agreements. this is a very important report and a necessary step to protect the integrity of our union and the safety of our societies.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on a european travel document for the return of illegally staying third-country nationals because i believe that a single format and system for all member states will ensure that return operations are carried out safely, protecting the health and fundamental rights of migrants. in 2014, more than 60% of the measures to return migrants to their country of origin were not implemented, even in cases of voluntary decisions. the european agenda on migration lacks a system that would allow for genuine and loyal cooperation between eu countries and the countries of origin of migrants, who often refuse to take in their own citizens without recognising their documents. the obligation to recognise and accept a european document with a single format, written in the language of the state of return and translated into french, english and the language of the country of origin, with a photo identification system and anti-counterfeiting technology is therefore the appropriate instrument to solve this problem and allows the protection of the migrant himself to be improved.
in writing. ‒ the adoption of this regulation does not deal with the substance of return decisions taken by individual member states. we are simply establishing a more secure and uniform european travel document for the return of illegally staying third country nationals, the purpose of which is to help facilitate the return and readmission of these nationals to their country of origin. we have provided for harmonised reporting templates which will use security standards to prevent counterfeiting and forgery and which will ultimately also help to reduce the administrative and bureaucratic burden for member states and for the authorities of third countries. it is not a question, as some members have already said in this house, of endorsing common return policies, but simply of moving towards the recognition of harmonised documents which are valid and recognised by all member states. the return decision is not a legal document, but a legal document which is valid for the purpose of returning a third-country national to the territory of the member state of which he is a national.
in writing. this report addresses the issue of the return of migrants whose stay is found to be irregular, which is a practical one and one of our priorities. providing for the reinforcement of the rate of return of irregular migrants is essential for the integrity of the eu asylum system, for cooperation between eu member states and third countries to maintain the trust of european citizens. at present, many third countries are not willing to accept return documents issued by eu member states because of their poor quality, and the need to ensure adequate technological and security standards to mitigate or eradicate counterfeiting and forgery. a long-term solution is therefore needed to stabilise the current migrant crisis, to ease pressure on member states and union agencies and to increase eu capacity and resources. i think it is my duty to express my approval of the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on a european travel document for the return of illegally staying third-country nationals. the report aims to provide this document to non-eu nationals who are subject to a return decision, thereby ensuring a uniform model for all member states and preventing countries of origin from refusing to take back such nationals by not recognising their documentation. in addition, this document will be issued only to persons whose nationality has been identified, and in no case to persons whose nationality is unknown. the text also stresses the importance of respect for the fundamental rights of the eu charter, in particular dignity and protection in the event of removal, expulsion or extradition, in return procedures.

in writing. ‒ the ježek report, which i supported today, approves the revision of the european regulation on the prospectus to be published for the offer of securities to the public or admission to trading. this regulation constitutes an essential step towards the completion of the capital markets union, as already indicated by the commission, the european parliament and the council. the proposed amendments aim to fully harmonise the rules on prospectuses and define more precise european rules for the protection of investors. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 264 concerning the conditions for the granting of such authorisation. these measures will help smes to access the capital market more easily and increase their chances of obtaining financing. the reduction of the fragmentation of existing practices in the eu has many positive aspects and is a key step towards a genuine integration of the capital market. this is a necessary measure at a time when institutional investors are faced with the low interest rates that characterise the european economy.
in writing. ‒ investor protection through market transparency seems to be the focus of this report. however, given that nothing has been done to date to reimburse the savings of citizens who have been defrauded by the banks since the bail-in mechanism came into force, i cannot fully agree with this text. i therefore preferred to abstain.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the prospectus to be published for the offer to the public or admission to trading of securities. this regulation is a necessary step towards the completion of the union of markets. the objective of the capital markets union is to help companies raise capital from multiple sources of funding. this requires making markets more efficient and providing investors and savers with more opportunities to help boost growth and create jobs. disclosure of information about the offer of securities to the public or their trading on a regulated market is essential to protect investors. disclosure of information is necessary to enable investors to make informed investment decisions and thus to ensure their protection. in addition, information is an effective tool for building confidence in securities. the publication of a prospectus may be the right solution to make the information in question available to the public.
in writing. - i voted against this text: while the revision of the regulation aims to harmonise disclosure requirements at european level in relation to the offer of securities to the public or their admission to trading, as a means of increasing the transparency, adequacy and comparability of information on securities and ensuring greater investor protection, such a revision should have in my view strengthened the current disclosure rules and broadened their scope with respect to the markets, products and investors involved. on the contrary, this commission proposal weakens the rules and introduces a great many unjustified exemptions. the disclosure requirements for some entities have been relaxed and, moreover, entire market segments and entities have been excluded from the scope of the regulation, thus undermining the completeness and accuracy of information on the risks associated with investments. for these reasons, my vote was against.
in writing. ‒ i welcome this report because i strongly believe that investors should be able to know better the conditions offered by financial intermediaries. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are not undermined. the protection of savings is a constitutional right and everyone must have free access to what concerns him. the subject matter of the public savings call has elements of internationality, and thus becomes potentially susceptible to evaluation by a plurality of authorities. this raises inevitable doubts as to the interpretation of the law, since the national laws on this subject are often different. the aim of this perspective is therefore to make arrangements for the full implementation of the capital markets union, allowing effective and secure access for firms to these forms of financing. this is the only way to boost growth (especially that of our smes) and create jobs.
in writing. ‒ the revision of the regulation on the prospectus to be published for the offer of securities to the public or admission to trading constitutes one of the cornerstones of the completion of the capital markets union. with the report adopted today, the european parliament is relaunching this vital and ambitious project and clarifying its position on what is an essential tool to inform european citizens when they decide to invest in financial markets: the prospectus. i voted in favour of the report because it promotes full harmonization of the rules on prospectuses and sets out more precise european rules for the protection of investors. it also undertakes to reduce the administrative burden and legal costs of drawing up the prospectus for issuers, in particular smes, so as to enable them to access the capital market more easily and to increase their chances of obtaining financing. the european union has a duty to provide all the tools and information to help citizen-investors make informed and fully informed choices, based on the information in the prospectus, without imposing an undue burden on companies that decide to place financial instruments on the markets.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep's position on the proposal for a regulation on the prospectus to be published for the offer to the public or admission to trading of securities, as i believe that it constitutes a further step towards an integrated single market for financial services. i think the amendments made by the ep improve the commission's proposal. i agree that the prospectus drawn up under this regulation should contain the relevant and necessary information in relation to an investment in securities that an investor would reasonably need to make an informed assessment of the financial and asset position, profits and losses and prospects of the issuer and any guarantors, as well as the rights attaching to the securities. such information should be compiled and presented in an easily analysable form. similarly, the summary should contain a clear warning highlighting the risks, in particular for retail investors, in the case of securities issued by banks subject to bail-in under directive 2014/59/eu. finally, i welcome the incorporation of proportionality principles and criteria, taking into account the different sizes of the eu's financial markets, and the possibility for member states to provide for lower thresholds.
in writing. the current prospectus contains the information necessary for investors to make informed investment decisions. in the area of capital markets, the commission envisaged revising the prospectus directive to make it easier and cheaper for companies to raise capital and to provide clear information for potential investors. the current directive 2003/71/ec harmonises the rules for making prospectuses public when companies wish to raise capital by listing on a stock exchange or by offering investment opportunities to the general public. in order to be able to make an informed decision, it is essential for investors to have access to adequate information. for these reasons i am happy to approve and support the decision taken by parliament.
in writing. ‒ member states must commit to sharing responsibility for relocating the 160 000 asylum seekers from greece and italy. they must step up their efforts to make the european relocation scheme work better. the transformation of resettlement places into resettlement places for refugees from turkey, a key point of the eu agreement, does not appear to be the best way for the proper implementation of the resettlement scheme. i am convinced that, in the interests of european solidarity, each member state must respect the agreements by taking in the number of refugees it is responsible for, and i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the prolonged migration crisis is making more and more evident the efforts that countries such as greece and italy put in place on a daily basis to manage the influx of thousands of migrants who land on europe's shores fleeing poverty and conflict. the keller report, which i strongly supported, tackles the problem of asylum and temporary measures for the benefit of italy and greece by amending the proposal originally put forward by the commission. the european parliament has rejected a provision to use the 54 000 places originally allocated for the relocation of asylum seekers from greece and italy to other eu member states for the resettlement of syrian refugees from turkey to the eu. the proposed intra-union relocation scheme should not be confused with the commission's proposed relocation scheme for non-eu countries. the two mediterranean countries are facing a complex situation which is likely to deteriorate. it is urgent that all member states act to fulfil the promise to relocate 160 000 asylum seekers within two years. the european union must demonstrate that there is a real bond of solidarity between the states, and its future depends on this.
in writing. ‒ one year after the eu's relocation and resettlement mechanism came into force, the numbers have shown that we in the league were right. even the eu leaders had to admit that it was a complete failure: of the 160 000 relocations planned by 2017 to alleviate the immigration emergency in italy and greece, only just over 3 000 have been carried out to date. however, this report insists that the failure of this mechanism is the fault of the member states and not the eu, which with its insane policies does nothing to stop the invasion of illegal immigrants in italy. for all these reasons i did not support the text with my vote.
in writing. ‒ with today's vote, and on the eve of the bratislava summit, parliament reiterates once again that member states must respect the commitments they have made on the relocation of refugees to frontline countries such as italy and greece. the rapporteur rightly pointed out that the relocation scheme is a genuine instrument of solidarity, which should be strengthened and not weakened if possible. we are far from the figure of 160 000 refugees to be resettled some member states have not taken in a single refugee and while disembarkations continue in italy, it would be misleading, as the report points out, to include in this figure 54 000 refugees who would be resettled from turkey to the eu.
in writing. ‒ the human tragedy unfolding in the mediterranean cannot leave us indifferent. more than three thousand people have lost their lives since the beginning of this year trying to reach european shores. european costs, that is what this is about, because the phenomenon of migration does not only affect italy and greece but all of us. it is a common theme, which requires common responses. we need to increase the number of people to be relocated and support the italian and greek authorities who are struggling to manage this great challenge of the 21st century: it is not just a question of solidarity, it is also a question of foresight. no wall has ever stopped the great migrations of history, and our indifference will in no way stop the wars and poverty that cause these people to flee. the european union must practice its fundamental principles of solidarity and protection for those in need, and of unity and common action among its member states. and you have to do it now.
in writing. ‒ after careful reflection and extensive debate in the house, i have voted in favour of the proposal for a council decision establishing temporary measures in the field of international protection for the benefit of italy and greece. the plight of migrants is clear to all: we're not doing enough to relocate them. the numbers are all against us. i am very concerned that attempts to manage the refugee crisis are highlighting a utopian goal that is hard to achieve, with an obligation to do more and faster, responding to the humanitarian emergency in greece and preventing a deterioration of the situation in italy. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy.
in writing. ‒ last year, at the height of the so-called refugee crisis, the council decided, despite the opposition of some states, to relocate 160 000 refugees from greece and italy to other member states. the proposal calls for one third of the total number of refugees to be resettled (54 000) to be used for the implementation of the eu-turkey agreement; the member states had failed to agree on the increase in relocations following the agreement. however, most member states are not meeting their commitments and reception centres continue to be overcrowded, especially in greece. the report by my colleague rightly distinguishes between the posts devoted to resettlement and those required for the implementation of the agreement with turkey, and i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i can only welcome the keller report, hoping that it can help our country in the face of the devastating and exhausting migration crisis. i very much appreciate that the agreements between the union and turkey clearly specify the essential differences between resettlement and relocation and the conditions for resettlement. although these are two forms of transfer of asylum seekers, they are quite distinct in that the former is carried out with a country outside the community, whereas the latter occurs between two member states. i support the clarification of the conditions for relocation: the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the establishment of a european asylum support office (easo) for asylum seekers from greece and italy. suffice it to say that as of 5/6/2016 only 793 people present in italy have been relocated compared to the expected 12764 people. i very much hope that by the end of the year we will be able to see a more substantial cooperation.
in writing. ‒ it is urgent that member states honour their commitments to prevent the deterioration of the conditions of refugees in the countries of arrival, by working together efficiently to reduce the pressure on states such as italy and greece and thus to move quickly and create more safe and legal pathways. we cannot remain shortsighted in the face of this humanitarian emergency, and we cannot act with the slowness we have shown so far. progress, as the commission said last may, is unsatisfactory. to date, member states have made available only 7% of the number of places for relocation and according to the '5th ec report on resettlement and settlement', from 14 june to 11 july, at least in italy, only 66 people were relocated compared to 186 in the previous period and only 6 minors. in italy we are also working hard to create additional hotspots, because 1,600 is not enough. but it requires the cooperation of all the member states.
in writing. ‒ by voting in favour of this resolution, i intend to support the amendments proposed by the european parliament to the commission text amending council decision (eu) 2015/1601 of 22 september 2015 establishing temporary measures in the area of international protection for the benefit of italy and greece. in particular, i support the deletion of amendment 20 allowing for the reduction of the obligations on the relocation of asylum seekers for member states which take in syrian nationals in turkey on the basis of resettlement schemes other than temporary and exceptional relocation from italy and greece, as decided by the council on 20 july 2015. i believe that this amendment goes against the ratio of asylum measures to the benefit of the countries most affected by the arrival of asylum seekers, creating a risky legal precedent that justifies the reduction of the relocation obligations for member states established by the council in july 2015. moreover, i believe that reception on the basis of resettlement cannot replace the relocation mechanism which expresses the internal solidarity between member states and the need for a comprehensive eu approach to managing flows of people seeking international protection.

in writing. ‒ solidarity is the key principle that should govern the development of immigration and asylum policies. solidarity both internally, between the member states of the union, and externally, towards the third countries hosting the majority of refugees. the european parliament voted to extend the mandate of the european ombudsman to include the european ombudsman in the new european ombudsman's role. we therefore urge the member states to honour the commitments made in previous decisions and to ensure the rapid relocation of 54,000 applicants for international protection. we also call for the speedy treatment of the cases of vulnerable people, especially children, so that they can be reunited with their families. we are not only guaranteeing the right to relocate syrians, eritreans and iraqis, but we are also including afghans among those entitled to relocate. the efforts made so far are ridiculous: we cannot accept that only 7% of the number of relocation places have actually been allocated to date. the situation is becoming more critical for italy and greece every day and, given the high number of asylum seekers arriving mainly in italy, the need for emergency relocation places is expected to remain high.
in writing. – it should be the european union’s moral duty to assist asylum seekers reaching italy and greece, as these countries have declared a state of emergency. no member state should take a hands-off approach because failing to assist is against what the eu believes in. eu countries are encouraged to be as cooperative as possible, especially in relation to border control. i want to highlight the importance of travel documents to identify those reaching greek and italian coasts, because only by identifying them will we be able to assist more effectively in the relocation of migrants. italy and greece, as core members of the eu, should not have to battle alone to cope with the hundreds of asylum seekers arriving every day.
in writing. ‒ it has been a year since pope francis, on 6 september 2015, invited parishes, religious communities, monasteries and shrines across europe to welcome a refugee family in preparation for the holy year of mercy. the european union has tried to respond, through the commission and parliament, and at the instigation of some member states, by proposing solutions in support of a solidarity approach to the humanitarian emergency. however, a genuine rethinking of the dublin regulation and a sharing of responsibility have not yet been achieved. the partial relocation mechanisms proposed by the council, which provide for aid to the two most exposed countries, italy and greece, have been only partially complied with. meanwhile, the number of landings, although slightly decreased, continues to record very high figures: in 2016 alone, 281,055 people have already landed in italy and greece. i therefore support the report by the libe committee, which stresses the need for a mandatory allocation of migrants between member states, based on a quota system. only in this way will it be possible to develop a system of genuine solidarity between member states and to create a genuine european asylum system.
in writing. ‒ given the need to increase solidarity between member states, strengthen integration for border management and help prevent crisis situations at the external borders of the union, i welcome the report on temporary measures in the area of international protection for the benefit of italy and greece. our group has worked hard to produce a report which can stimulate the debate further and which calls primarily for more action by european leaders. the proposal responds to the need to ensure an adequate redistribution of migrants arriving on european shores among all member states. the commission notes that the european council has adopted a number of decisions on the basis of the 'european year of citizens' and 'european year of citizens' in order to promote the integration of citizens of third countries into the union. as of 5 july 2015, only 793 persons from italy and 33 from greece have been transferred; the council has not yet decided on the matter. it is therefore necessary to work to ensure that the redistribution mechanisms start to work and that, as agreed, there are 5,680 asylum seekers transferred every month.
in writing. ‒ the proposal to allocate 54,000 quotas initially allocated for resettlement from italy and greece to the resettlement programme for syrian refugees from turkey, as provided for in the eu-turkey declaration, cannot be shared by those who, like me, believe that a valid response to the refugee crisis can only be based on a solidarity approach between all member states. although i believe that the european union should comply with the clause in the agreement with turkey that for every person relocated from greece there should be a corresponding person resettled from turkey to european territory, i do not support the idea that italy and greece, already subject to unprecedented migratory pressure, should be penalized further. for the reasons i have just given, i have decided to vote in favour of the keller report, which, thanks to the will of several political groups, rejects the proposal to exchange 54,000 quotas for resettlement from italy and greece for quotas for resettlement from turkey. the text also conveys the urgency of making the relocation programme a truly effective instrument, capable of bringing about a real reduction in the burden borne by the border states.

in writing. ‒ last year, at the height of the refugee crisis, the council decided to relocate 160 000 refugees from greece and italy to other member states. although the decision was contested by the eastern european member states, a clear majority were in favour of such relocation. through this commission proposal, the council is planning to set aside one third of the total number of refugees to be resettled (54,000) for the implementation of the eu-turkey agreement: for every syrian refugee that turkey readmits from the greek islands, another syrian will be resettled by turkey in other eu member states. in negotiating the agreement, member states failed to agree on making additional places available for refugees from turkey and for this reason they now intend to use the 54,000 places originally allocated for the resettlement of refugees from greece and italy to resettle syrian refugees directly from turkey. however, member states are not meeting their commitments on relocation: some have not yet taken in any refugees, others have only taken in a handful of people. the commission has already made a number of proposals.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the agea report on guidelines for member states' employment policies. the outbreak of the economic crisis and its continued negative effects on growth and employment, as amply demonstrated by all indicators of strategy 2020, strongly require the development of a genuinely inclusive and integrated labour market that is supported by a coordinated and effective social and employment policy. member states, in cooperation with local and regional authorities, need to tackle the very serious problem of unemployment in a timely manner by facilitating investment in the creation of sustainable and quality jobs with a particular focus on the green, white and blue sector and the social economy. social innovation, reduction of bureaucratic burdens, a new balance between work and private life for workers are all fundamental aspects which must be linked to the introduction of common instruments for the participation, information and consultation of workers. the crisis can be overcome, but only if the union responds jointly to all the problems it has created.

in writing. ‒ policies to ensure that wages represent an adequate subsistence income remain important for creating employment and reducing poverty in the union. member states, in conjunction with the social partners, should therefore respect and encourage wage-setting mechanisms which allow real wages to be adjusted to productivity trends and help to correct past divergences without fuelling deflationary pressures: these mechanisms should ensure sufficient resources to meet basic needs, taking into account poverty indicators specific to each member state. in this respect, differences in skills and conditions in local labour markets should be duly assessed with a view to ensuring a living wage throughout the union. in setting minimum wages in accordance with national law and practice, member states and social partners should ensure that they are adequate and take into account the impact on workers' poverty, household income, aggregate demand, job creation and competitiveness. a europe which is more attentive to the wage situation of its workers is a europe which is more just, more humane, more solidary and more secure.

in writing. ‒ the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) is an international instrument aimed at protecting endangered species of wild fauna and flora by controlling international trade in specimens of these species. the resolution calls on the european commission to explain the union's main strategic objectives to the next conference of the parties to cites, highlighting the following aspects: the transparency of decision-making, the need to improve the reporting of wildlife smuggling, corruption and the implementation of cites. for these reasons i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora is the most important agreement on wildlife conservation, with 181 parties including the european union and its 28 member states. whereas the eu is one of the main markets for the transit and destination of illegal trade in wildlife, in particular birds, turtles, reptiles and plant species listed in cites; the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for adoption. the resolution adopted by parliament today supports the eu action plan against wildlife trafficking, encouraging all parties to strengthen cooperation, coordination and synergies between the biodiversity conventions. new legislation is needed to make it illegal to import, export, sell and buy wild plants and animals that are caught and possessed in violation of the law of the country of origin or transit. tackling illegal trade means fighting corruption, organised crime and terrorist organisations that profit from the trafficking of endangered species.

in writing. ‒ this is a sensitive issue that concerns us very closely as consumers. the trafficking of wildlife is a serious threat to biodiversity and sustainable development. species such as elephants, rhinos, great apes, tigers, and sharks are particularly affected and threatened with extinction. elephant and rhino poaching has reached an all-time high that is jeopardizing repopulation. wildlife trafficking is the fourth largest illegal activity in the world after drug, arms and human trafficking, with a turnover of about 17 billion euros per year. the resolution on the main objectives of cop 17 in johannesburg proposes tough action against corruption and organised crime involved in wildlife trafficking, which is often a means of financing many criminal organisations (think of the boko haram terrorist group in nigeria).
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today, which focuses on some key points that eu negotiators should focus their attention on at the next cites conference. first, the traceability of wildlife: all parties should introduce an electronic authorisation system, which is also useful for the purpose of combating corruption, which is a key factor in the illegal trade in endangered species of flora and fauna. corruption can be detected at every point in the wildlife trade chain and affects countries of origin, transit and destination, damaging the effectiveness, proper implementation and ultimate success of the cites convention. this is why it is necessary to insist on the introduction of robust and effective anti-corruption measures and on greater judicial cooperation between member states. finally, cites should provide for the full and prompt application of sanctions against parties that do not comply with the key elements of the convention. the union and the member states should use all available tools to encourage parties to respect the cites convention and other international agreements called for by the convention aimed at protecting wild flora and fauna and biodiversity.

in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report analyses the different possibilities for increasing funding for european small and medium-sized enterprises (smes), both through the traditional banking channel and through new alternative methods. given the crucial importance of smes in the european economy, ensuring easy access to finance is a necessary condition for the recovery of the european economy. while the banking channel needs to be strengthened, made more reliable and adapted to the specific needs of smes, alternative methods must be offered to end excessive reliance on banks. the report analyses several possibilities for increasing sme funding, some of which are not sustainable. firstly, the capital markets union, which, through increased financialization of the economy, represents a major risk for smes and small operators who will have to deal with financial instruments that are not very transparent and complex. it is also recommended that the return to securitisation, another risk factor par excellence, be considered. the efsi plan is used, despite its complete inefficiency. finally, the report supports the unconventional monetary policies initiated by the ecb which have proved to be totally inefficient, if not even harmful, due to excessive reduction of rates and price levels.

in writing. ‒ smes make an important contribution to the union's growth and socioeconomic development, and supporting them means fighting unemployment in a concrete way, particularly youth unemployment, which is now at historic levels. however, job creation in smes is influenced by a number of factors, both internal and external, ranging from access to finance to administrative burdens to skilled labour. the krasnodębski report, which i supported with my vote, calls on the commission and the member states to work to tackle crucial problems such as skills shortages, regulatory uncertainty, low innovation capacity and access to credit. only a holistic approach, which develops good social dialogue and takes into account the skills needed by 21st century workers, will be able to create new jobs in smes.
in writing. ‒ the reports voted on are balanced and widely shared. i believe that the role played by small and mediumsized enterprises in the economic growth of the member states is fundamental. i strongly reiterate my conviction that the system of programming and management of the european structural funds must be radically renewed, making it less complex and eliminating all the current administrative burdens on businesses before, during and after the granting of aid. for all these reasons i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ at the end of 2014, the eu had an average youth unemployment rate of 21.4%, or more than 7 million unemployed young people. however, at the same time, 2 million jobs were unfilled in the eu. this indicates the need to improve the link between the world of training and the world of work, to develop more flexible and interdisciplinary skills. cooperation, participation and partnerships are the means to establish a constructive relationship with smes and the diverse european business community and to ease the current administrative and financial constraints on starting up new business activities, through simplified procedures, easy access to credit, venture capital and microfinance, guaranteed high-speed internet connections, tailor-made multidisciplinary advice and the introduction, where possible, of incentive measures for entrepreneurs who hire young unemployed people. the importance of microfinance and the european programme for employment and social innovation (easi) in achieving full youth employment is clear. only by increasing the efficiency of the training pathway and creating a network of one-stop shops where all the administrative procedures necessary for setting up and running a business can be carried out will we be able to raise the rate of youth entrepreneurship in the short term.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today because smes, which account for almost 99% of european enterprises, are the undisputed backbone of the eu economy. in the last decade, smes have created as much as 85% of european jobs. moreover, as the report aptly points out, last year small enterprises contributed up to 71% to the growth of employment in the non-financial trading economy. i therefore believe that smes should be at the heart of the business policy making process in the eu. effective measures must therefore be put in place to strengthen the job creation potential of this key sector. however, the organisations and networks representing smes are still too weak. smes are in some cases faced with the additional problem of low capitalisation, which results in a worse market position and hinders fair competition. one of the main challenges is to reduce the burden on smes, especially labour costs. this challenge can only be met if there is a stable and high-quality regulatory framework, where the rules are applied in a uniform and equal way.
in writing. ‒ smes are very heterogeneous and despite the rules of the internal market, there are still significant differences across the european union in terms of the regulatory framework, particularly as regards their stability and their level of certainty. the report by mr krasnodębski stresses that in order to achieve a healthy environment for the development of enterprises and to boost their job creation potential, national and european policies must first of all be concerned with tackling the problems related to skills (shortage, inadequacy, brain drain), regulatory uncertainty and administrative burdens, as well as to undeclared work and the de facto privileged position of multinationals. unfortunately, some very important concepts proposed by the m5s in the empl committee were left out of the report: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. for these reasons i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) are the engine of the european economy and make a key contribution to employment. in 2014, smes employed almost 90 million people, or 67% of total employment in europe. i believe it is essential to create an economic environment which facilitates the development of smes and stimulates their ability to recruit. in this respect, policy action should improve smes' access to skills by encouraging vocational training and education activities. in addition, i think it is important to reduce the burden on smes, including labour costs, in order to encourage the creation of quality and lasting jobs. i also hope that the administrative burden on smes will be reduced. it has been shown that over-regulated administrative economic systems result in higher fixed costs by indirectly providing a competitive advantage to larger enterprises. i also thought i should vote in favour of the report because it calls on the commission and the member states to take measures to promote the internationalisation of smes, which can expand their market and consequently their employment potential. finally, it should be stressed that the underground and criminal economy is a form of unfair competition which particularly harms smes.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund is an instrument designed to provide additional support to workers who are affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. created by regulation (ec) no 1927/2006, it has quickly become a major social reintegration measure, with success rates ranging from 4% to 98% depending on the sector. the egf has included in its scope workers made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis, self-employed workers and neet shares in certain pre-determined regions. it is a tool with great added value for strengthening the social dimension of the union: i have therefore decided to support the harkin report. europe must increasingly ensure that its citizens have better living and working conditions. the european social model must be promoted to an ever-increasing extent, with the quality of public services, protection and social dialogue at its core.

in writing. ‒ the egf was established by regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 to provide solidarity for workers who have lost their jobs as a result of massive redundancies, as a result of major structural changes in the structure of world trade due to globalisation, where such redundancies have a significant negative impact on the regional or local economy. over time it has become an important tool for social reintegration, with success rates ranging from 4% to 98% depending on the sector, and a number of stakeholders exceeding 20,000 units with positive repercussions on the territories and on the training-reorganisation chains related to the interventions. for all these reasons, the european globalisation adjustment fund is a useful instrument, to be preserved and strengthened, which represents a concrete response of solidarity and social cohesion to the great changes that the globalised world brings to the market and european society of the 21st century.

in writing. ‒ to make the most of the great opportunities offered by globalisation, we must first of all be able to mitigate its effects. this is why we welcome the report on the activities, impact and added value of the european globalisation adjustment fund between 2007 and 2014. the fund has proved to be an important instrument of solidarity for workers who have suffered massive redundancies as a result of structural changes in world trade, through assistance, retraining and reintegration, and the promotion of entrepreneurial activity. the report also stresses the need to pay attention to the impact of trade policies and agreements on the european labour market, stresses the importance of social dialogue and urges the commission to ensure that job losses are only a last resort. the response to globalisation cannot and must not be one of suspicion and closure, but must be seen as a great opportunity which requires active adaptation to reap its benefits, keeping the achievements of the european social model and the protection of workers as firm reference points.
in writing. ‒ i thank the rapporteur and confirm that i would express my favourable opinion of the report.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund is an instrument that provides direct support to workers who have lost their jobs as a result of changes in international trade relations and the process of globalisation. over time, the criteria for accessing this support have broadened to include workers excluded from the world of production as a result of the global economic and financial crisis. this report analyses the activity, impact and added value of the fund between 2007 and 2014. the s&d group succeeded in including a number of priorities and recommendations which have greatly improved the text. these include the need to pay greater attention to the impact of trade policies and agreements on the european labour market; calls on the commission to ensure that adequate staff is available for the management of the fund, in order to avoid delays in the implementation of the operations; the committee also welcomed the commission's proposal to give greater weight to the social dialogue in the case of company restructuring. that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the activity, impact and added value of the european globalisation adjustment fund between 2007 and 2014. the european globalisation adjustment fund provides support for people who lose their jobs as a result of structural changes in world trade due to globalisation. in addition, the scope of the fund has been extended to include workers made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis of 2009-2011 and, to this end, has been further extended to include self-employed workers affected by the crisis between 2014 and 2020. it is important that the european union should do more and more to help workers in difficulty.

the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules are respected, and that the commission is able to take action in this area. match-fixing is often the preserve of organized crime operating on a global scale. this is a problem that has become a priority for the sports movement and law enforcement authorities worldwide. i very much appreciate the fact that european funds have been allocated to public-private partnerships for the implementation of projects aimed at identifying risk factors for match-fixing and developing tools for their management. i also very much appreciate the european regulations on online gambling and the creation of a european discussion platform for national gambling regulators, but that is not enough. the european union must play a greater role in the fight against match-fixing. we have two organizations in europe that deal with crossborder cooperation in the investigation and prosecution of serious crime: europol and eurojust. the commission can invite these agencies to cooperate more closely with the sports movement and to pay more attention to match-fixing. member states should implement measures to prevent conflicts of interest between betting operators and sports organisations and to encourage sports betting regulators to step up the fight against fraud and illegal betting. the european parliament has on several occasions emphasized its commitment to combating match-fixing, reiterating its full support for the council of europe convention on the manipulation of sports competitions, which in my view represents the best instrument and legal framework for fighting illegal sports betting at international level. i think it is essential that the european union and its member states are involved in force. i would remind you that article 165 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union calls on the union and the member states to promote cooperation with international organisations in match-fixing, which require joint efforts and a coordinated approach. one of the main objectives of the council of europe convention on the manipulation of sports competitions is to promote national and international cooperation. chapter 3 of the convention contains a number of provisions to facilitate the exchange of information between all the parties concerned. the fight against match-fixing requires close cooperation between sports movements, governments, betting operators, law enforcement authorities and international organisations, and such a wide range of stakeholders is a challenge in itself. the european union can help to create unity and ensure a more coordinated approach. the member states are at different stages of developing measures to combat match-fixing. the transnational nature of match-fixing is likely to involve cooperation between member states with different levels of experience, creating the need for sharing of good practices and developing skills. in this respect, the european union plays an important role in developing capacity as a catalyst for cooperation and ultimately as a support for the implementation of the council of europe convention on the manipulation of sports competitions. there is broad support from member states to facilitate the early entry into force of the convention, and some are ready to ratify it but have simply been unable to do so because of procedural issues all internal to the european union. i would therefore ask the commission what further steps it intends to take to break this deadlock and to enable the member states which played a key role in the preparation of the council of europe convention on the manipulation of sports competitions to sign and ratify it as soon as possible.

member of the commission. – mr president, let me remind you about the history of the ratification of the convention, which was declared open for signature in september 2014. the proposal for the signature by the eu of the convention has been one of the priorities of the new commission, and a matter of particular importance to me. on 2 march 2015 the commission submitted a proposal for the signing of the convention on behalf of the eu. this proposal took the form of two council decisions, one with regard to matters related to substantive criminal law and judicial cooperation in criminal matters, and one on other matters, such as cooperation between sports organisations, betting operators and state administrations. under the latvian and luxembourg presidencies in 2015, discussions took place within the council on these proposals for signature. while the contents of the proposals were agreed at coreper in november 2015, the proposals were blocked as the council requested confirmation of a common accord by all member states before proceeding to a vote. this allows one member state to continue blocking the process. the commission disagrees with this approach. the applicable procedure and voting is clear: the treaty clearly stipulates qualified majority voting for this kind of council decision. the court of justice has also confirmed in a recent judgment that the rules regarding the manner in which the eu institutions arrive at their decisions are laid down by the treaties and are not at the disposal of the member states or of the institutions themselves. however, this viewpoint was not shared during the discussions in coreper in november 2014 when the presidency refused to proceed to a vote. this is a question which the council and the presidency must find a solution to. despite the efforts of the dutch presidency, they were unable to find a compromise which would enable a breakthrough. the commission regrets the current stalemate. the commission is fully aware of the benefits of the convention, and we would like it to enter into force as soon as possible. for the convention to come into force, five signatories must ratify it and three of those five have to be council of europe members. to date, there are two such ratifications. if there is no agreement in the council, the convention will enter into force without the eu and most eu member states being on board. that would be a regrettable situation. given the nature of the convention, which links matters of national competence with eu competence, including exclusive eu competence, the commission considers that a coordinated approach to the signature and ratification of the convention by member states remains necessary in accordance with the principle of sincere cooperation. the commission adds its voice to the call by the honourable member for all parties to continue to seek a solution. the commission, for its part, will continue its efforts to convince all member states to support the signature and ratification process. we will use all opportunities to underline the importance of eu participation in this convention. we fully support the convention as a valuable tool in the fight against match-fixing. for the states that choose to ratify it, it will be the first legally binding international tool to fight match-fixing – representing a solid basis for ensuring pan-european coordination and cooperation in the fight against match-fixing. the commission needs your support in trying to find a breakthrough. i would like to thank you for the positive contributions you made during the debate. it is not an easy task to fight complex issues like match-fixing. the convention is, indeed, an important tool but we must continue to look at match-fixing from all angles. in the commission, colleagues dealing with sport, betting, organised crime and corruption will continue to work closely in this field. we will continue to finance projects to fight against match-fixing and to raise awareness about the problem. there is also an eu-funded pilot project which supports four major activities, including one preparing member states for the entry into force of the convention. we count on your support to help the council find a way to overcome the current stalemate and enable the member states and the eu to sign and ratify the convention as soon as possible.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the sustainable development goal of the un agenda aims to end world hunger by 2030 through increased productivity of smallholder farmers and the promotion of sustainable agriculture. however, it must be acknowledged that simply ensuring greater production and availability of food is not enough to solve the problem. the latest data available tells us that over 159 million children worldwide suffer from stunted growth. in this context, the implementation of the european policies developed by the commission's action plan on nutrition should be implemented. food and nutrition security requires constant strategic attention and support for investment, especially in rural areas. policy development and programming must take account of the links between nutrition, health and job creation, growth and sustainable production. the european union must work strategically to create the conditions for combating food waste and for the development of sustainable and quality agriculture, with particular reference to support for small and micro-farms.
i would like to thank commissioner vella for his commitment and for his replies. there are countries where the rate of illegal logging reaches 90%, involving corruption throughout the logging, transport and sale chain. the objectives set out in the action plan are still hampered by a multitude of factors, including the resistance to change in the forestry sector, the delay in the application of the european regulation, the importance of other markets such as china and india, and the boom in agricultural raw materials whose production occupies forest land. extensive agriculture plays a key role in the deforestation process, considering that since 2000, about half of the tropical forest has been converted to agricultural land or monoculture plantations, often against the will of the indigenous populations, as is the case with palm oil in indonesia, liberia and ecuador. it is estimated that 80% of global deforestation is now caused by agriculture and by importing products such as palm oil, beef, leather, soybeans, rubber, cocoa and timber, the european union is also contributing to this problem. the environmental damage caused by deforestation cannot be underestimated. in addition to the very serious loss of biodiversity, deforestation is one of the main causes of hydrogeological disruption and causes floods and landslides. the eu therefore needs to demonstrate and continue to demonstrate a strong political commitment to the effective implementation of the voluntary partnership agreements, to enhance their impact, to ensure the effective implementation of the timber regulation and to take further measures to support the protection and recovery of forest ecosystems.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in times of climate change, forests are becoming the only ally for the protection of the lives and well-being of millions of human beings. they are also the most important reservoir of biodiversity and a building block for indigenous communities and farmers worldwide. europe remains the number one destination for illegal timber trade and it is therefore crucial that there is a real commitment across the union in the coming years to ensure that flegt does not remain a voluntary commitment in trade agreements. we need binding commitments to regulate the activities of governments and multinationals and at the same time to stop the system of corruption. it is essential that the flegt reform explicitly prohibits trade in timber from conflict zones, providing for a system of sanctions up to the withdrawal of import licences and the suspension of free trade agreements or preferential tariffs for multinationals and states that violate the embargo. finally, we consider the system of voluntary monitoring of forestry investment by multinational companies in agriculture and the financial sector to be inadequate. instead, effective regulation and due diligence mechanisms are needed to curb illegal activities and provide hope for the planet's green lungs.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, because of the important but not dominant position of the european union on the world market for wood products, any measure will be ineffective unless it is shared with the major players in the sector, such as the united states, japan and china. i think the commission should give political impetus to the european union's action plan on forest law enforcement, governance and trade by completing the creation of a voluntary licensing system to ensure that only legally harvested timber is imported. in order for such a system to function properly, flegt partner countries should ensure that reliable systems and structures are in place for the correct identification and certification of the cut timber link. on the financial side, the commission should integrate the initiatives under the flegt programme into the main european development cooperation programmes in order to be able to implement technical assistance and capacity development programmes in the timber producing partner countries.

member of the commission. – mr president, following the path set out by the council in its roadmap from 2009, the commission presented two packages of legislative proposals strengthening procedural safeguards for eu citizens in criminal proceedings. the first was in 2010, on the right to translation and interpretation, the right to information, and the right to access a lawyer. later, in 2013, we proposed the directive to strengthen the presumption of innocence and the right to be present at trial, the directive on special safeguards for children suspected or accused of a crime, and the directive on the right to provisional legal aid. and this is the proposal you are going to vote on tomorrow, as the last piece missing from the system of procedural rights. i think we can all agree that there is no point in rights if you cannot really take advantage of them. what is the right of access to a lawyer worth, if you cannot afford a lawyer? in other words, access to justice and a fair trial must not be something which is only for rich people. i would like to thank your rapporteur, mr de jong, and the shadow rapporteurs for their dedicated work on this issue, which made an agreement on this directive possible after long and very difficult negotiations. the directive is an important step forward in the construction of an area of justice in the european union. today there are large disparities in the way legal aid is provided in the european union. the directive, once adopted, will significantly strengthen the procedural safeguards for all citizens in criminal proceedings. the scope of the directive covers those situations where legal aid is needed most: when persons are deprived of liberty, during a number of crucial evidence-gathering acts, and in cases of mandatory defence by a lawyer. as proposed by the commission, legal aid will also be granted at the very early stages of proceedings when persons are most vulnerable, especially during police questioning.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the implementation of the principle of mutual recognition of judicial decisions requires that the member states cooperate more closely and that they strengthen trust in each other's criminal justice systems, starting with the way in which the rights of suspects and accused persons are protected. the commission's approach has the advantage of providing a guarantee of a minimum level of legal aid at the expense of the state in all member states, but its fragmented nature requires appropriate arrangements to give effect to the rights of the defence. first, guarantees should be provided as to the quality of the legal assistance provided. secondly, the preferences of the suspects, the accused and the requested person must be taken into account as regards the choice of the ombudsman. the same principle applies to the need to ensure continuity in legal representation. it is also important to provide for the possibility of replacing the lawyer of the defence if the accused or the defendant has lost all confidence in his lawyer and is able to justify this with verifiable reasons.

in writing. ‒ on 17 november 2015, the ionian islands of greece were struck by a violent earthquake with a magnitude of 6.1 on the richter scale. the extensive damage caused by the earthquake, particularly in the islands of leucade, ithaca and kefalonia, damaged more than 120 houses, destroyed beaches and bathing establishments, compromised infrastructure networks and cultural sites. the hellenic republic therefore asked the eu to activate the european union solidarity fund, an instrument which aims to respond quickly, efficiently and flexibly to emergency situations, supporting the population of regions affected by natural disasters. i voted in favour of the kyrtsos report because i believe that european intervention in such situations is essential. the aid and resources provided, amounting to eur 1,65 billion, will enable infrastructure to be restored, the costs of emergency measures to be reimbursed and some of the costs of clean-up operations to be covered.

in writing. ‒ the directive on temporary access to legal aid is the last of six directives implementing the roadmap for strengthening the procedural rights of suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings adopted by the council in november 2009. the proposal for a directive lays down minimum rules on the right to legal aid for suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings in which they are deprived of liberty, and in certain other situations. it shall also ensure that legal assistance is made available in the context of a procedure for the execution of a european arrest warrant, at the time of the arrest of the requested person in the executing state. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the de jong report on the protection of suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings and of persons wanted in proceedings for the execution of a european arrest warrant. this is a particularly important issue and one of the cornerstones of the rule of law. the right to a lawyer must be guaranteed to those who lack the necessary financial means, through legal aid at the expense of the state. the text adopted is a concrete step forward in overcoming the differences in interpretation of the right to a fair trial by ensuring a minimum level of legal aid at the expense of the state in all member states. despite some provisions which may be too timid to overcome the differences in the quality of legal aid, the text proposes a fair line for judicial cooperation in criminal matters which is really fair and effective.

in writing. ‒ i supported this proposal for a directive aimed at ensuring the right of access to a lawyer for suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings and for requested persons who are the subject of european arrest warrant proceedings. i voted in favour of this proposal, because i think it is needed to strengthen the trust of member states in each other’s criminal justice systems.
in writing. ‒ in today's vote i voted in favour of the directive in question, which harmonises at eu level the institution of free legal aid for suspects and accused persons deprived of their liberty or involved in proceedings for the execution of a european arrest warrant. the scope of the directive covers admission to legal aid, both provisional and definitive, and provides legal certainty to the suspect, accused or requested person as regards the eligibility criteria. the differences in income and cost levels between member states preclude the possibility of providing detailed rules on the level of fees. however, the directive includes minimum guarantees concerning the quality of legal aid provided. specific provisions are also provided to take account, as far as possible, of the preferences of the suspects, accused and requested persons as regards the choice of the ombudsman. the same applies to the need for continuity in legal representation and the replacement of the lawyer of the defence if the accused has lost all confidence in his lawyer and can justify this with verifiable reasons.
in writing. ‒ the proposed directive on provisional access to legal aid is the last of a package of six directives aimed at implementing the roadmap for strengthening the procedural rights of suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings. since it has direct implications for the state budget, the question of free legal aid is not a simple one. the commission has not yet adopted a proposal to this effect. however, it is worth noting the contribution of parliament, which has succeeded in extending the scope beyond the provisional period, thus guaranteeing ordinary legal assistance. this is an important measure aimed at guaranteeing a minimum standard of procedural rights, which is also useful for the mutual recognition of criminal decisions. i voted for it without question.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure as on 27 november 2013 the european commission adopted a proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on provisional admission to legal aid for suspects or accused persons deprived of liberty and on admission to legal aid in european arrest warrant proceedings. the commission proposal is a positive step towards guaranteeing a minimum level of state sponsorship in all member states. however, it is limited to the right to provisional admission to legal aid for suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings involving deprivation of liberty and to the right to provisional and definitive admission to legal aid for wanted persons in proceedings for the execution of the european arrest warrant. the rapporteur is also aware of the differences between member states in the quality of legal aid provided. this depends, among other things, on the fees paid to lawyers for legal aid at the expense of the state. however, it is therefore all the more important to include at least some guarantees concerning the quality of legal aid offered in the directive.

in writing. ‒ the global abolition of the death penalty is one of the main objectives of the european union's human rights policies. it is precisely through the revision of this directive that community action aimed at protecting human dignity, the right to life, and the prohibition of torture and other inhuman and degrading punishments could be brought to fruition. with this new procedure, the european union is not only putting a stop to the marketing of all those instruments which, in some states, could be used to carry out torture or capital punishment, but is also prohibiting the advertising and transport of these throughout the european territory. the flexibility and precision of the 2005 regulation are also to be noted: an updated version of the 'black list' has been drawn up, listing all objects whose sole function is to torture or cause death, in order to respond to the development of new technologies in the field. i therefore welcome this review as a concrete example of a trade policy which can promote community values.
