in writing. ‒ the 'regulation against torture' is a unique instrument that serves to ensure the protection of human rights by controlling goods and activities that could be used to practice the death penalty or to inflict torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. the 'anti-torture regulation' is part of the eu's policy to abolish the death penalty worldwide and to prevent torture. it is important to ensure the right combination of eu legislative, administrative, judicial and external measures to prevent and prohibit the production, trade and use of goods for the purpose of torture and to effectively control items with potentially lethal and inhumane uses. export control regimes need to be long-term and flexible to adapt quickly to technological change and developments in the world. the effective implementation by national authorities of controls, checks, sanctions, guidelines and awareness raising actions is also of paramount importance.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report today because i believe that europe needs to reiterate its leading role in the international arena in the fight to abolish the death penalty, torture and inhuman and degrading practices that violate human rights. the 'regulation against torture' (regulation (ec) no 1236/2005) is a unique instrument that contributes to the protection of human rights through the control of goods and activities that are or could be improperly used for the purpose of capital punishment or torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. it is therefore essential to ensure uniformity in eu export controls, including on military dual-use firearms and items classified as instruments of torture. the strengthening of controls on instruments of torture involves the introduction of a specific annex iiia. the purpose of that annex is to prevent controlled medicinal products from being used for capital punishment by lethal injection. the eu should also establish a general export authorisation for countries which have made strict international commitments, in particular ratification of protocol 13 to the european convention on human rights.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 on trade in certain goods which could be used for capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. the 2005 revision of the regulation allowed the necessary updating of products whose marketing is prohibited within the european union, as well as the inclusion of a ban on advertising and promotion of these products, including online, and on their transit through the eu. it also provides for an 'urgent procedure' to include new products that could be considered risky in a timely manner and a review clause to verify the effectiveness of the legislation and review it, if necessary, by 2020. the provisions introduced by the revision are intended to increase the effectiveness of a regulation whose wider objective is to reaffirm the direct commitment of the european union to the defence of the right to life and the dignity of the person: the european union is also a very positive example of how european trade policy can increasingly be a means of strengthening the protection of human rights within and beyond the union's borders.
in writing. ‒ as a member of the european parliament and as a european, i am against the death penalty and all forms of torture. i would like to see closer cooperation between the national authorities of the eu member states to improve controls and raise awareness. i therefore support the revision of the legislation to stop the export and promotion of goods which can be used for capital punishment or torture, such as medicines for lethal injection or instruments of torture. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i can only support any measure aimed at preventing and prohibiting the production, trade and use of goods for torture and at effectively controlling articles with potentially lethal and inhumane uses. the regulation will eliminate some of the shortcomings in the legislation and ensure greater uniformity in eu export controls. the fight to abolish the death penalty and to oppose all forms of torture and other inhuman treatment or cruel punishment is a battle of civilisation to be fought in accordance with an all-encompassing approach which does not exclude the prohibition of harmful commercial practices. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report as it prohibits the export and import of equipment or goods intended solely for the purpose of torture and the death penalty and introduces a further restrictive regime, based on specific authorisations, for exports of equipment/goods potentially used for such purposes. the same report also allows member states to adopt or maintain additional national measures restricting the exercise of certain ancillary services linked to such exports.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on the report because i agree with the need to restrict trade in certain goods used for capital punishment, torture or other ill-treatment, but i would not like to risk imposing excessive bureaucratic costs on the manufacturing companies.
in writing. ‒ i find it essential to express my full support for the identified agreement on trade in goods that could be used for the death penalty, torture or other punishments. i believe that the european union should intensify its monitoring of the legal and illegal channels of trade in instruments which could be used against people and cause death or the destruction of life. the protection of the health and safety of citizens must be the highest priority in our political and human endeavours, and we must implement, with the utmost severity and tenacity, the most decisive measures for scrupulous checks on the transit and sale, including online, of goods that could be used against persons, and we must firmly pursue europe's concrete and solid commitment to combating capital punishment, where it is still recognised.
in writing. ‒ by adopting this measure, the eu is further demonstrating its role as a responsible global leader and actor in the fight against the death penalty and for the elimination of torture. the regulation we have amended has too many shadow areas and leaves some loopholes which have allowed, in the past, the trade, the intermediation and the advertising of these instruments of death. thanks to today's vote and the agreement reached with the council, it will not only be illegal to buy and sell these instruments online, but also to export, advertise and display them. none of these goods will be allowed to circulate in europe, and we have also foreseen the ban on intermediary services and technical assistance. the list of prohibited products is not closed. today's vote will enable the commission to add new products to the list of prohibited or controlled products quickly. it is essential, however, that member states do their part through a secure and encrypted communication and information exchange system.
in writing. the schaake report is a tool that contributes to the protection of human rights through the control of goods and assets used (or that could be improperly used) for the death penalty or torture, combining prohibitions with authorisation requirements for the trade in goods covered by the regulation in question. this action should include not only confidential and bilateral approaches, but also explicit statements and initiatives, to ensure concrete, preventive and meaningful responses to persons at risk of or suffering from torture. i have therefore decided to support this report.
in writing. ‒ the eu is currently working on its policy of eliminating the death penalty worldwide and preventing torture. to accomplish this goal, the rapporteur highlights the need for effective enforcement of controls, verifications, penalties, guidance and outreach carried out by national authorities to prevent the misuse of trading goods for crimes against humanity (i.e. capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment). therefore, i voted in favour in order to take action on the matter.
in writing. ‒ the 'regulation against torture' (regulation (ec) no 1236/2005) is a unique instrument that contributes to the protection of human rights through the control of goods and activities that are or could be improperly used for the purpose of capital punishment or torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. in this connection, i thought i would vote in favour of the amendment to the regulation, which aims to further strengthen the european union's role as a responsible leader in the fight against the death penalty and for the elimination of torture by strengthening the provisions on ancillary services related to the transfer of goods, as well as on transit, technical assistance and trade promotion. it is important to ensure the right combination of eu legislative, administrative, judicial and external measures to prevent and prohibit the production, trade and use of goods for the purpose of torture and to effectively control items with potentially lethal and inhumane uses.
in writing. ‒ whereas there is a need for new european rules to prevent trade in goods and services which can be used for torture or the death penalty; that the prohibition of these goods and services is aimed at protecting public morals and respecting the principles of human dignity which underlie european values, as enshrined in the treaty on european union and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union; the european union has always been at the forefront of the fight against torture and the death penalty, and it is essential that the export and import of goods used for such purposes be regulated in a precise and careful manner. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposal for a regulation aims to amend the previous regulation of 2005 on goods which can be used for capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment. the commission proposes to include in the new regulation an annex to prevent the goods in question from being used for capital punishment by lethal injection, to extend the restrictions to technical assistance services and to include the possibility of an emergency procedure to amend annexes ii, iii and iiia. the european parliament voted in october 2015 a series of amendments which amended the proposal, subsequently opening the informal trilogue with the council, which was successfully concluded on 24 may 2016. i am firmly against the death penalty and i consider this proposal for a regulation to be very important in order to protect the right to life of every human being. that is why i voted in favour of its approval.
in writing. ‒ strengthening the 2005 regulation will allow for better control of trade in goods that are or could be improperly used for capital punishment or torture. i voted in favour of this legislative update as it aims to close the loopholes in the basic text, ensuring the right combination of eu legislative, administrative, judicial and external measures to prevent and prohibit the production, trade and use of tools with potentially lethal and inhumane uses. more restrictions on marketing, promotion and transit within the union have also been introduced, as well as a system of prior authorisation for intermediation and technical assistance in respect of controlled goods. i hope that this approach will ensure effective controls and checks without any unnecessary burden that hampers legitimate business activities.
in writing. ‒ the following strategic agreement covers the exchange of information in the following areas: expertise, general situation reports, results of strategic analyses, information on criminal investigation procedures, information on crime prevention methods, training activities, as well as the provision of advice and support in the context of individual criminal investigations. the new europol regulation will enter into force in the european union in 2017, providing for a new procedure in which the role of the european parliament is strengthened. the procedure is that parliament gives an opinion and not just its approval, as is the case at present. for the reasons described above and in line with my views on international agreements with third countries, i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the people's republic of china is playing an increasingly important role as a country of origin, transit and destination in the fight against organised crime. i therefore decided to vote in favour of the moraes report approving the strategic cooperation agreement between europol and china. it will enable a wide exchange of information on expertise, reports, results of strategic analysis, information on criminal investigation procedures and training activities. given the presence of several high-impact organised criminal groups in the asian country, cooperation on issues such as illegal immigration, trafficking in human beings, drug-related crime, cybercrime and money laundering could prove particularly fruitful, strengthening the action of both sides in the area of justice and security. it should be noted that the agreement does not provide for the exchange of personal data, thus ensuring the protection of the rights of european citizens.
in writing. ‒ i support the proposal for an agreement on strategic cooperation between the people's republic of china and europol. i believe that greater cooperation between this country and europol will ensure more effective policies and action in the fight against crime, and i have therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the conclusion of the agreement on strategic cooperation between europol and the chinese ministry of public security because i share the strategic goal of increasing our effectiveness in preventing serious forms of crime. only the cooperation between global actors in security matters can improve the prevention efforts we carry out.
in writing. ‒ the eu and the member states share responsibilities for maintaining the security, justice, freedom and fundamental rights of the citizens of the union: this requires the creation of an effective level of data protection in the judicial and police activities of the eu and its member states. pushing for the creation of common institutions harmonising activities, by implementing genuine cooperation between supervisory authorities at national and union level, on the one hand, and increasing cooperation with police forces in third countries, on the other hand, is essential to improve strategic and operational cooperation between the member states of the european union and their trading partners, with a view to enhancing the effectiveness of the fight against terrorism, mafias, smuggling and international crime, thus increasing the security of both eu citizens and those of partner countries.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the europol-china strategic cooperation agreement because it is clear that europol has an operational need to work with china. china is playing an increasingly important role as a country of origin, transit and destination in the fight against organised crime, facilitation of illegal immigration, trafficking in human beings, drug-related crime, counterfeiting of the euro, infringements of intellectual property rights, corruption in sport, cybercrime and money laundering-related activities. it also appears that china is home to several organized crime groups. i am therefore in favour of concluding this strategic cooperation agreement with china, because i believe that it can be a valuable aid and support in the fight against organised crime and help to strengthen international cooperation in the field of law enforcement.
in writing. ‒ the cooperation agreement between europol and china covers the exchange of information, but excludes personal data. the information may include expertise, general situation reports, results of strategic analyses, information on criminal investigation procedures, information on crime prevention methods, training activities, as well as the provision of advice and support in the context of individual criminal investigations. however, it cannot be said that these are not sensitive data and, moreover, the new procedure which sees a strengthened role for parliament in the conclusion of agreements with third countries is not yet used. i therefore preferred to abstain.
in writing. ‒ organised crime and terrorism do not stop at the eu's borders to counter its activities. given their transactional nature, coordinated action and exchanges of information are also necessary with non-community countries. europol has an important role to play in making europe safer, including through strategic cooperation agreements with third countries such as china. the people's republic of china is playing an increasingly important role as a country of origin, transit and destination in the fight against international crime. i voted in favour of this because good international cooperation is an indispensable condition for combating organised crime effectively.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal under consideration which concerns the idea of approving a strategic cooperation agreement between europol and china. this strategic agreement excludes the exchange of personal data and therefore the issue of data protection is not relevant in this case. the information exchanged could include expertise, general situation reports, results of strategic analyses, information on criminal investigation procedures, information on crime prevention methods, training activities. there appears to be a clear operational need for europol to cooperate with china. according to europol, china plays an important role as a country of origin, transit and destination in the fight against organised crime, such as facilitation of illegal immigration, trafficking in human beings, drug-related crime, counterfeiting of the euro, infringements of intellectual property rights, cybercrime and money laundering-related activities. china is home to several major organized crime groups. the rapporteur is in favour of concluding this strategic cooperation agreement with china, as it would help and support the fight against organised crime and help to strengthen international cooperation in law enforcement.
in writing. ‒ endorses the resolution on europol's strategic agreements with china. it is recalled that europol is the european police office and that its purpose is to improve cooperation between the police forces of the member states in order to combat terrorism, illicit drug trafficking and other serious forms of international organised crime. these are therefore strategic agreements relating solely to the exchange of operational, strategic and technical information and not to operational cooperation agreements. this agreement therefore excludes the exchange of personal data with china.
in writing. ‒ in the name of the fight against international crime, i can only express my full support for the close strategic cooperation agreement between europol and the people's republic of china. the agreement includes the exchange of operational, strategic and technical information and, while excluding the exchange of personal data, provides for synchronisation of the specific knowledge required, the results of strategic analyses, investigative procedures and prevention methods, as well as training and support in specific cases. the newly approved strategic alignment will make it possible to combat organised crime in a more modern and aware manner, and to achieve much closer international cooperation, given that china is now the source, destination and transit point for illegal immigration, human trafficking, counterfeiting and corruption. as a 2011 cnel report showed, chinese organized crime has long been present in our territory and is mainly engaged in human trafficking, prostitution, gambling, extortion and, above all, counterfeiting of our brands and textile products. i therefore hope that these phenomena will be gradually reduced by the cohesion of as many states as have access to strategic agreements of the same size.

in writing. ‒ in today's vote, the european parliament approved the conclusion of the strategic cooperation agreement between the ministry of public security of the people's republic of china and the european police office (europol). recent studies have found that over the past decade, chinese organised crime has entered the crime landscape of a number of eu countries. criminal activities include extortion, trafficking in human beings, the production and trafficking of illegal drugs, counterfeiting of the euro, infringements of intellectual property rights, illegal gambling, counterfeiting of consumer goods, as well as cybercrime and money laundering-related activities. there is therefore a clear operational need for europol to cooperate with china. the key to success in the fight against organised crime lies in the exchange of information and expertise on criminal groups at eu level and with the countries concerned, such as china. europol can play a key role in this context in order to support and strengthen the action of the competent authorities of the member states and their mutual cooperation. i therefore voted in favour of concluding this strategic cooperation agreement.

in writing. ‒ the eu-acp relations date back to the postcolonial period, and were institutionalised through the first lomé convention. today, the eu-acp partnership is governed by the cotonou agreement, which is based on three fundamental pillars: aid, trade and economic cooperation. despite the positive results achieved so far, there is still much work to be done and the focus of the partnership in the future should be on the growth of the acp countries, the new geopolitical realities, globalisation and regionalisation.
in writing. ‒ 80% of the world's least developed countries are in the african, caribbean and pacific regions; the acp countries have been able to take advantage of the new opportunities offered by the lomé convention and, since 2000, the cotonou convention. the objective of the latter agreement was to reduce and eliminate poverty, pursuing the objectives of sustainable development and the progressive integration of these countries into the world economy. the expiry of the agreement in 2020 requires fresh thinking within the eu, which is why i have decided to vote in favour of the neuser report which outlines some prospects for the future of relations between the two regions. a new structure should be created that preserves the parts of the acp-eu acquis that are universal in nature, such as the commitment to human rights, good governance and democracy, but at the same time allows the main activities to be carried out in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity. political dialogue, the sustainable development goals and the 2030 agenda must be at the heart of new agreements, including the establishment of monitoring, accountability and peer review mechanisms to monitor the implementation of the targets on a regular basis.
in writing. ‒ the text acknowledges that the acp-eu partnership agreement has so far been ineffective in combating poverty in africa, the caribbean and the pacific, which represent 80% of the world's least developed areas. however, instead of thinking about a better use of the resources already available, the text insists on the creation of new funds for migration. i therefore believe that the resolution is unbalanced in favour of the usual good-natured rhetoric which does not lead to any concrete results for the acp countries. for these reasons i did not intend to support the text with my vote.
in writing. ‒ i endorsed the resolution on the future of acp-eu relations beyond 2020 because a new structure of cooperation must be adopted and a new commitment to human rights and democracy needs to be approved. moreover, i believe the 2030 agenda and the sustainable development goals have to be the focus of the new agreement and its implementation has to be monitored. last but not least, i share the call on all the parties to the agreement to give to local and regional governments a greater autonomy in order to enable them to play a significant role in the development of acp countries.
in writing. ‒ it is important to rebuild the acp-eu relationship on a new basis, creating a partnership that promotes strategic interests and shared values. it will have to pursue the objectives of sustainable development and ensure respect for human rights. it is essential that the acp countries participate fully in the review process, which should also take into account the growing importance of regionalisation. it would also be appropriate to carry out a thorough analysis of the past achievements and failures of the existing framework before taking decisions on the future of acp-eu relations. cooperation will need to be stepped up, particularly in areas of common interest, in order to address today's global challenges more effectively. this new partnership will have to be based on the principles of mutual growth and development between the eu and africa; facilitating the industrialisation of the african continent and the development of agriculture and encouraging investment in innovation and sustainable development policies. the future partnership should also provide for more effective joint action on conflict prevention, as a stable security environment is an essential condition for achieving the sustainable development goals.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today because the cotonou agreement has been a valuable platform for cooperation between the eu and the acp countries for many years now, given the large number of countries that are parties to the agreement and the links established between their peoples and parliaments. however, it is noted that half of the acp countries are still among the least developed countries in the world, and that together these countries account for less than 5% of world trade and about 2% of global gdp. the mobilisation of national resources in the acp countries and the funds of the diaspora can be an important source of development finance. the new cooperation agreement will have to provide for a stronger parliamentary dimension, through the much-desired joint parliamentary assembly (jpa). the main objective of this will be to facilitate an open and democratic parliamentary dialogue. further efforts will also be needed in the field of development cooperation, the promotion of democracy and human rights. the new agreement will therefore have to reflect an ambitious political project and make good governance a cornerstone, leaving behind, as the report rightly points out, the harmful donor-recipient mentality.
in writing. ‒ convinced of the importance of relations between the acp countries (africa, caribbean, pacific) and the european union, i voted in favour of this report on the future relations between the eu and the 79 acp countries, whose partnership is currently governed by the cotonou agreement, which will expire in 2020.
in writing. ‒ over the past 40 years, the partnership between the european union and the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) countries has been a valuable tool for strengthening development cooperation and trade. i believe that the new agreement must be primarily a political project based on sustainability and reducing disparities. only sustainable and lasting development can ensure an effective fight against poverty, which is the primary objective of eu-acp cooperation. we need to move beyond the donor-recipient mentality to build a strong partnership with reliable monitoring mechanisms and a peer review system that periodically monitors the implementation of common objectives. finally, it is important to involve civil society, in particular the local groups directly concerned, in the negotiations for the new agreement, and to give a voice to the most vulnerable groups such as minorities, young people and women, who are too often not given the opportunity to make their demands known. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i am voting against this report which examines a number of proposals for the renewal of the acp-eu agreement (partnership agreement between the members of the african, caribbean and pacific group of states, of the one part, and the european community and its member states, of the other part). the agreement has so far not brought any benefit in reducing poverty in the acp areas. the proposal also includes the establishment of a joint parliamentary assembly (jpa) which would become yet another useless political instrument.
in writing. ‒ i support the report on the future of relations between the african, pacific and caribbean countries and the union as it strengthens the spirit of cooperation between our nations, giving new life to common areas and interests. in particular, i am pleased that the new objectives proposed correspond to the needs that have been identified in the wake of demographic and structural change and the most significant institutional changes. while the report remains in line with the principles set out in the cotonou agreement concerning the eradication of poverty, democratic principles, the assertion of the rule of law and support for more sustainable development, it does add a number of points on the principle of subsidiarity and respect for cooperation, including at regional level. the monitoring, reliability and review mechanism between countries aimed at periodic monitoring of the implementation of the sustainable development goals is one of the aspects to be highlighted. the establishment of a joint parliamentary assembly will also create a new forum for dialogue and debate that is as open, democratic and fruitful as possible. this is accompanied by economic partnership agreements, which are milestones for integration and growth.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i believe it is useful to improve the effectiveness of acp-eu cooperation and to adapt it to the new challenges resulting from the political, structural and demographic changes of recent years. the new structure should also maintain the commitment to human rights, good governance and democracy, while the main activities should be carried out in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, i.e. they should be based on general agreements adapted to specific regional needs and mutual interests between the union and the respective region. it is also important that the private sector can be heard during the policy-making process of programming so that it can play a key role in the development process and can then help to finance it, provided that investments are made with respect for people, property, the environment and in line with the un guiding principles on business and human rights. i also hope that the new partnership will give greater attention to local small-scale producers and farmers and create a favourable environment for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (smes).
in writing. ‒ more than 80% of the world's leastdeveloped countries are in acp regions. the acp-eu partnership remains an important scenario in the light of the sustainable development goals, the main objective of the cotonou agreement identified as poverty reduction and eradication and the values on which eu external action is based, such as respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, democracy based on the rule of law and transparent and accountable governance. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that economic partnership agreements remain a fundamental instrument for promoting the integration of the acp states into the global economy, making full use of the potential of regional integration and promoting peace and security at local and cross-border level. the new cooperation agreement introduces interesting new features, such as the joint parliamentary assembly, which will be involved in all relevant discussions concerning the post-2020 acp-eu partnership, thus ensuring inclusive and multilateral participation of stakeholders. the report also stresses the need for a dedicated instrument for security expenditure linked to development cooperation, overtaking the approach of the european development fund (edf) as the main source of funding for the african peace fund.
in writing. ‒ i strongly supported this measure by which the european parliament calls on the commission to review and strengthen relations between the eu and the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) countries. the report is parliament's contribution to the follow-up of the cotonou agreement, launched in 2000 and due to expire in 2020, which regulated the eu's political and trade relations with the acp countries, including financial aid. high-profile international issues such as the fight against poverty, climate change, the management of migration flows and the fight against terrorism need a common platform for the eu and the countries concerned to cooperate in solving problems that can only be solved jointly. the cotonou agreement has helped to strengthen relations with the acp countries and to develop a framework for doing so. however, much has changed since the agreement came into force, and its updating is a good opportunity to review and improve the arrangements for political and economic cooperation with our acp partners.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote in favour of this report because i believe it is important to outline the future of acp-eu relations after 2020, the date on which the cotonou agreements expire. the report identifies as its cornerstones the promotion of human rights and the rule of law, as well as economic and trade development between the areas concerned, encouraging the private sector to invest in such cooperation in accordance with un principles.
in writing. ‒ i am voting against the report, which in my view is insufficient and risks being another highly political and ineffective instrument.
in writing. ‒ the report by the committee on development gives a very comprehensive overview of the cooperation agreements with african, caribbean and pacific countries which have been the most important form of eu-developing country relations for over 40 years. i think it is very important to remember the political success of this report. the cotonou agreements now include more than 100 countries, with a framework of cooperation in various political, economic and trade fields that is highly advanced and with a large budget financed by the european development fund. i particularly support the report by the committee on development on the need for an even more ambitious review of these agreements, in view of the changes in the global political and economic landscape, and to provide for more effective forms of achieving the objectives of the agreement, particularly in terms of poverty reduction and the strengthening of democratic standards. as an elected representative of europe, i too would like to stress the importance of interparliamentary cooperation between these macro-regional areas, which operates through the acp parliament, the largest interparliamentary assembly in the world.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep report on the future of acp-eu relations after 2020 because i believe that the time has come to update relations with these countries, based on the cotonou convention and its predecessors. the strength and the acquis of the cotonou agreement are based on its unique characteristics: the european union is a legally binding document, with an unprecedented number of countries joining (79+28 member countries), based on three pillars of development cooperation, political and economic and trade cooperation, and above all with a common institutional framework and a substantial budget (european development fund). i hope that the 2030 agenda and the sustainable development goals (sdgs) will become the focus of a new agreement and that robust monitoring mechanisms will be established to ensure that the implementation of the agreement contributes to the achievement and promotion of the sdgs. the post-cotonou agreement should be a framework political agreement, setting binding minimum requirements for epas (economic partnership agreements), in order to ensure continuity of constraints on provisions on good governance, respect for human rights, including of the most vulnerable persons, and respect for social and environmental standards.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because, more than ever, relations between the european union and the acp countries need to be reviewed in the light of all the elements of cooperation based on the donor-recipient logic, which has not produced much in the last few years. the new cooperation no longer speaks the language of assistance: with the new investment plan for africa, we really have an opportunity to create economic development and just societies. and this development path can only be linked to the pacification of an area that has already been the scene of too many tragedies. investment must be accompanied by controls and constraints. it is a path of institutional cooperation that focuses primarily on building more just societies, with great attention to respect for human rights. the joint parliamentary assembly must strengthen its role. the work must focus on regional focuses, analyze specific contexts, solve problems, develop strategies that serve in the context also as best practice for other similar situations. europe must help africa to become an equal partner and the commitment must be maximum.
in writing. the report under review aims to highlight the need to create a new structure, which retains its commitment to human rights, good governance and democracy. the main activities should be carried out in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, i.e. the principle of determining regional agreements adapted to the specific regional needs and mutual interests between the european union and the region. acp-eu cooperation is therefore a valuable achievement which, over the last 40 years, has strengthened the links between the peoples and countries of the acp and the eu and between their respective parliaments. at the same time, a monitoring, accountability and audit mechanism is required to ensure the implementation of the sustainable development goals in the member countries on a cyclical basis, with the relevant participation of acp and eu representatives from central government institutions, parliaments and regional and local authorities. i therefore support the report in the light of the foregoing.
in writing. ‒ in regard to the report on the future of acp-eu relations beyond 2020, i expressed a favourable vote given the fact that the partnership has been crucial in making progress towards achieving the millennium development goals (mdgs). the report also encourages engagement with other partners around the globe such as the united nations or the african union to tackle the challenges of wars, internal conflicts, insecurity, fragility and transition. finally yet importantly, the report calls for all international actors to come together to fight and eradicate poverty and inequalities while promoting sustainable development.
in writing. ‒ given the renewed centrality of relations between the european union and acp countries and the expiry in 2020 of the legal framework established by the cotonou convention, we strongly support the neuser report. since its foundation, the european union, recognising its historic responsibility and the need to promote a model of sustainable development in areas with high levels of poverty, has pursued policies of assistance and cooperation. the cooperation, which is characterized by a holistic approach, has been based on three pillars since 1975, the year of the lomé convention: the european union is committed to the development of a common foreign and security policy. the opening of negotiations to civil society and national parliaments, together with asymmetric trade facilitations, has led to a fruitful dialogue on human rights. however, looking ahead to 2020, we believe that the effectiveness of measures to support economic development and the rule of law must be reinforced, including through stricter legal clauses that make trade facilitation conditional on respect for fundamental rights. finally, we cannot fail to stress the importance of africa and the need for a broad european policy which considers migration as part of a complex phenomenon and which is able to recognize its remote causes.
in writing. ‒ i thought it appropriate to express my support for the proposal under consideration. i believe that the acp-eu partnership is of great importance, given that over 80% of the world's least developed countries are in acp regions. the european union, as a major player on the international scene, cannot fail to establish agreements aimed at promoting economic growth and welfare in these areas. the aim is to reduce and ultimately eliminate poverty in such a way as to achieve the development of a lasting and progressive integration of the acp countries, while safeguarding a set of values and principles which include respect for fundamental freedoms and human rights. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ over the past 40 years, acp-eu cooperation has strengthened the links between the peoples and countries of the acp and the eu. however, progress in the objectives of poverty eradication and the integration of the acp countries into the world economy has so far been insufficient. half of the acp countries are among the least developed countries and together these countries account for less than 5% of world trade and about 2% of global gdp. to improve the effectiveness of cooperation and make it fit for the challenges of today, it is necessary to rethink its structure, while maintaining the general principles of a universal nature (human rights, gender equality, human development, democracy, the rule of law, etc.) and organising the main activities on the basis of the principle of subsidiarity (favouring regional agreements and the participation of local actors and civil society). at the same time, a formal right of control over the programming of the european development fund (edf) by the european parliament should be guaranteed. budgeting the edf would allow for democratic control, enhance visibility and increase transparency and effectiveness in the use of eu development funds. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament, through this report, underlines the importance of cooperation between the acp countries and the eu. the text stresses that, in order to enhance their effectiveness and avoid overlaps, regional agreements with african, caribbean and pacific countries should be designed to take account of existing regional organisations, such as the african union, and existing regional agreements, such as economic partnership agreements (epas). given the changed political and economic landscape in which the acp states operate following the signing of the cotonou agreement, i believe that the key to improving cooperation with the eu must be sought in the private sector, through the promotion of public-private partnerships. i am convinced that the fight against poverty and, in the long term, its eradication must remain the main objective of the new acp-eu agreements. for all these reasons i voted in favour of adopting this report.
in writing. ‒ since 2000, the cotonou agreement has provided the framework for development finance cooperation, economic and trade cooperation and political dialogue between the 28 member states of the european union (eu) and 78 african, caribbean and pacific (acp) countries. since that agreement will expire in february 2020, it is necessary to define a new partnership taking into account the achievements and shortcomings of the agreement. over the past two decades, acp-eu relations have developed substantially. however, the effectiveness of cooperation needs to be improved and adapted to new international challenges that have an impact at all levels in the eu member states and the acp states, such as climate change, water, energy and food security, migration, health, security and financial issues. i voted in favour of the report, which is a good starting point for the forthcoming discussions on the future post-cotonou agreement. in particular, i welcome the fact that the report stresses the key role that the private sector can play in the development process and the importance of creating a favourable environment for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises in the context of the new partnership.

member of the commission. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, in april we had an exchange of views in this house on the impact of the migration crisis in the european union, particularly on the transport sector. we are all fully aware of the many challenges posed by migratory flows, including in calais. together with commissioner bulc, we take this issue very seriously and we want to find sustainable and viable solutions to, firstly, ensure the normal crossing of borders for people and goods in calais and, secondly, to improve the management of migration flows in this area and the living conditions of the migrants present. we must bear in mind that the franco-british border is an external border of the schengen area. for this reason, specific bilateral agreements have been concluded between france and the united kingdom, such as the touquet agreement in 2003. we recognize the desperation of migrants trying to board trains or lorries to get to the uk, but their attempts are clearly having a negative effect on the transport sector. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any information on the number of passengers and the number of freight trains. we goods across the border should function normally. the commission has taken exceptional measures to reduce the impact on the transport sector over the past summer. we have allowed the united kingdom to derogate temporarily from the rules on the working hours of road drivers. this allowed drivers to wait in a safe parking place to rest. in the summer of 2015, the commission wrote to the french and uk transport terminals in calais. the smugglers are present in the truck parking areas, sometimes several hundred kilometres from calais. in this regard, the commission services are preparing those without a legal right of residence. at the same time, the situation in calais demonstrates that the sources of migration must be better managed in the context of common action and a common policy on emigration. in this context, as you know, the commission has proposed a large number of measures to improve the management of migration flows and to combat the smuggling of migrants. these measures have already significantly reduced the flow of migrants across europe.

in writing. ‒ the following is a non-legislative act ratifying the accession of peru to the hague convention on international child abduction. as this is a formally necessary act, as the convention does not provide for the possibility of direct approval by the eu, i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction, ratified by all eu countries, has introduced a system that allows contracting states to cooperate in finding a solution to this type of case. the text of the treaty contains two main points: the jurisdiction and enforceability of the laws of the state of residence of the child and the establishment of a mechanism for the immediate return of the child. the european union currently has exclusive external competence in this area, but the convention does not provide for autonomous action by international organisations. for this reason, member states should act on behalf of the union by prior authorisation from the council. the dzhambazki report, which i have supported today, therefore authorises austria and romania to accept peru's accession to the convention, allowing it to exert its effects in relations between the south american country and the european union.
in writing. ‒ the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction provides for cooperation between signatory states to return a child or young person under 16 who has been arbitrarily 'abducted' from a parent to the family residence pending a court ruling, unless such return poses a serious threat to the child's safety. i believe it is of fundamental importance for the protection of our children that this convention be ratified and respected by more and more states. i therefore intend to support by my vote the authorization for austria and romania to accept the accession of peru to the convention.
in writing. ‒ i endorsed the authorisation given by the parliament to austria and romania to accept the accession of peru to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. indeed, i believe the 1980 hague convention is an important and successful instrument aimed at settling cases of international child abduction through cooperation between states. the accession of peru needs the authorisation of the council due to the fact that austria and romania had not accepted peru yet. this resolution is important because many eu citizens are of peruvian origin and as a consequence the convention will help more european families deal with separations or divorces.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a key instrument that has been ratified by all the member states of the european union. the convention introduces a system that allows contracting states to cooperate in finding a solution to cases of international child abduction. the convention is intended to resolve such situations at the international level by providing that the courts and laws of the state of residence of the child are the competent courts and laws of the state of residence of the child. the convention also introduces a system to guarantee the immediate return of the abducted child, protecting his or her health and fundamental rights. the accession of peru to the convention is a positive step in promoting the protection of children's rights at the global level and not just at the european level.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today because i consider the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction to be a vital instrument for the member states of the european union and beyond. the convention introduces a system which enables signatory states to cooperate effectively in order to find a concrete solution to cases of international child abduction. the problem arises mainly as a result of separation or divorce. in the case of mother and father coming from different states, the lack of cooperation between the states concerned could be exploited to date to address the issue of custody. the legal systems of the individual states tend to favour certain categories of persons on the basis of nationality. the convention aims to resolve such situations at international level by providing that the courts and applicable laws are those of the state of residence of the child. a system is also provided to ensure the immediate return of the child. many european citizens have peruvian origins and therefore, thanks to the accession of the country in question, minors with links to the peruvian community will be adequately protected against abduction.

in writing. ‒ the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction established a system of cooperation between the authorities of each contracting state, which provides for the immediate return of children who have been unlawfully transferred or detained. as this is an international agreement which aims to protect and safeguard children in situations of legal uncertainty, it must be ratified by as many states as possible. since the european union has exclusive external competence in the matter of child abduction, i believe that the european institutions should authorize the member states to accept the participation of peru. i therefore thought i should vote in favour of the decision, in the hope that the 1980 hague convention between peru and all the eu member states to prevent the abduction of children will enter into force as soon as possible.

in writing. ‒ the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction, ratified by all eu countries, has introduced a system that allows contracting states to cooperate in finding a solution to this type of case. the text of the treaty contains two main points: the jurisdiction and enforceability of the laws of the state of residence of the child and the establishment of a mechanism for the immediate return of the child. the european union currently has exclusive external competence in this area but the convention does not provide for autonomous action by international organisations. for this reason, member states should act on behalf of the union by prior authorisation from the council. the dzhambazki report, which i supported today, authorizes some member states to accept kazakhstan's accession to the convention, allowing it to have its effects on relations between the asian country and the european union.

in writing. ‒ the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a key instrument that has been ratified by all the member states of the european union. the convention introduces a system that allows contracting states to cooperate in finding a solution to cases of international child abduction. the convention is intended to resolve such situations at the international level by providing that the courts and laws of the state of residence of the child are the competent courts and laws of the state of residence of the child. the convention also introduces a system to guarantee the immediate return of the abducted child, protecting his or her health and fundamental rights. the accession of kazakhstan to the convention is a positive step in promoting the protection of children's rights at the global level and not only at the european level.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on the european public prosecutor's office. pursuant to article 86 tfeu, the council, by means of regulations adopted in accordance with a special legislative procedure, may establish a european public prosecutor's office, based on eurojust, to combat criminal offences, such as fraud, which affect the financial interests of the union. the text adopted today reaffirms parliament's support for the establishment of this instrument and calls on the council to establish clear and unambiguous powers and procedures for it, reopening the debate on the consolidated text. in particular, it is necessary to clarify the powers of the european public prosecutor's office and national public prosecutors' offices in criminal matters in cases of multiple and mixed offences and to ensure that the european public prosecutor's office itself has adequate investigative measures to conduct its own investigations. the regulation should also provide for additional rights of defence for suspects, such as the right to legal aid at the expense of the state, the right of access to investigation documents, the right to information and the right to present evidence and to request the eppo to collect evidence on behalf of the suspect.

on behalf of the efdd group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, materials and articles in contact with food are widely used in everyday life, from packaging to kitchen utensils. we know that there is a chemical-physical interaction between materials and food and that the release of substances which are dangerous to human health can occur during contact. we are talking about extremely harmful substances, such as the so-called endocrine disruptors, about which there has been a heated debate with the commission for months on their very definition. bisphenols, which are found in the plastic bottles of baby girls, just to give an example, and which have been cited as a cause of endometriosis and serious reproductive problems, are also disruptive. the sector has been well regulated in terms of general rules, but there is a lack of harmonisation of the specific legislation of the member states. many countries, including italy, have their own specific legislation, which has been notified to the european union, but there are often problems of mutual recognition. a further aggravation comes from the risk assessment. it happens that the european food safety authority, the efsa, which is supposed to be the guarantor of our health, is doing a partial job and does not take into account the so-called cocktail effect, nor does it take into account multiple exposures to different chemicals. we therefore call on the commission to harmonize specific sectors and to prevent the proliferation of regulations which may cause market distortions, while ensuring a uniform level of food safety, that efsa performs its role as the guarantor of food safety for european citizens and carries out risk assessments worthy of the name, and finally that the commission 100% avoid the presence of endocrine disruptors among these substances and finally protect the health of european citizens more than the interests of lobbies.

on behalf of the efdd group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the report on the monitoring of the application of european union law, which seems to us to be generally acceptable, shows that the reduction in infringement procedures is not so much linked to the monitoring and prevention activities carried out by the commission, but above all to the fact that in recent years there has been a drastic reduction in the number of legislative proposals by the commission. all this gives us the opportunity to reflect, and of course all the institutions of the european union should reflect, on the reasons for this behaviour. perhaps the commission has regulated most aspects of the lives of european citizens. or, on the contrary, it prefers not to intervene on issues which risk bringing up and in some cases aggravating further the differences between member states. i think there are still many questions for which the european citizens want answers. i am thinking in particular of legislation on the fight against corruption and organised crime, but also on the protection of whistleblowers or legislation on transparency. finally, i am somewhat perplexed about the fact that financial penalties can be a real deterrent to tackling infringements, since they would ultimately fall on the shoulders of the taxpayers. it would probably be wiser and more effective to introduce deterrent mechanisms such as the suspension of the voting rights of states which commit infringements.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, madam commissioner, the report highlights two serious problems which, in my view, should be solved quickly. the first concerns indicators. the report is based on purely quantitative indicators, but we also need qualitative assessments to understand the reasons and characteristics of non-application of european standards in certain countries. we need to express a political judgment which can only be made if we have all the elements of evaluation which are unfortunately lacking today. european integration cannot be measured by the same aspersive parameters as quantitative ones. the second issue is transparency. parliament, as you know, has difficult access to both the pilot system and the information on pending cases. we are not in a position to assess whether the reduction in the number of formal procedures really reflects the increased implementation of european union law, or whether it is not the compromise between the commission and the member states. so, having elements of transparency here too would make his work, but above all our intervention, much more effective and precise.
author. – madam president, victoire ingabire, the leader of the opposition unified democratic forces party, was arrested in 2010 and is being held in prison for allegedly posing a terrorist threat to the country. however, the sentence was based on unreliable evidence, while of course we would want her to be judged on the basis of a fair trial. like victoire ingabire, other political activists and government opponents have gone missing or are currently in prison. effectively, the rwandan government, despite calling itself democratic, is severely limiting political pluralism and obstructing freedom of expression and association throughout the country. therefore, it is fundamental to establish a true democratic process, even in the light of the economic agreement signed at the beginning of september. the protection and freedom of its citizens must be ensured by the rwandese government. it is necessary to allow a european delegation to attend and give evidence when this process will be seriously started.
author of the book. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, it was 2013 when this parliament passed a resolution on the eight-year prison sentence imposed on victoire ingabire, who was found guilty of attempting to run for the leadership of rwanda by challenging president kagame, in a process that was purely political in nature. three years later, we have to face the hardening of the sentence, extended to fifteen years, and the deterioration of the health of the rwandan leader, while the political climate in preparation for the 2017 elections is likely to be damaged by the pressure on journalists and the media, and in the country there are even talks of changes to the constitution to allow the president to run for a third term. with this resolution we want to keep the matter alive and we call on the rwandan government to guarantee the right to a fair trial and to ensure that the opposition forces have sufficient space, so that freedom of expression is guaranteed and there is a greater pluralistic climate in the next elections.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, victoire ingabire is an icon of the struggle for freedom and democracy in rwanda. she returned to the country in january 2010 after 16 years of exile to participate in the presidential elections, was arrested in october 2011 and is now in prison on charges of terrorism and threatening national security. the european parliament had called for a fair trial in accordance with international legal standards. unfortunately, a delegation of the european parliament and the european union, which recently came to rwanda to learn about the situation of ingabire in prison, was refused to see her. the country has changed a lot since the 1994 massacre. nevertheless, human rights watch has documented numerous disappearances and numerous politically motivated arrests and unlawful detentions, particularly of government opponents. it is now clear that the detention of victoire ingabire is only a logical policy of the incumbent government. the european union and the international community must call for the immediate release of ingabire and all political prisoners.
author. – madam president, the current issue of sudan is taking on increasingly alarming dimensions, especially with regard to the darfur region, where government forces have launched about thirty chemical attacks against the civilian population since the beginning of this year. the last two of these took place on 9 september, with dramatic and devastating effects; they have spared no-one. we must immediately take measures to stop any type of attack. the sudanese government must ensure strict respect for human rights and freedoms of its citizens. to make this possible, it is necessary to reinforce the united nations arms embargo and extend it to include all sudan – not just the region of darfur. for this purpose, we urge the sudanese government, this parliament and all stakeholders to act urgently to put an end to these atrocities, allowing the necessary provision of humanitarian assistance.
author of the book. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, sudan is still facing a dramatic situation, dominated by conflict, violence and a lack of protection of human rights. the case involving operative members of a trafficking ring from the tracks centre, one of the few remaining independent organisations working in the field of sudanese civil society, is an example of this. these activists, accused of inciting war against the state, a crime punishable by death, were put on trial last september. the trial and sentencing of human rights activists is a worrying sign to all those who work in sudanese civil society to defend human rights and civil liberties. with this resolution we want to draw attention once again to the worrying conflict situation in sudan and call on the government authorities to ensure that activists and civil society workers can play their full role as human rights defenders without being prosecuted or condemned in a manner contrary to international law.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the situation in sudan is very difficult. the country is shocked by the recent violence between supporters of president salva kiir and those of former vice president riek machar. amnesty international has reported that the sudanese government has even carried out chemical weapons attacks against the civilian population this year. added to the violence is a dramatic famine. that's at least five million people who are hungry. the political crisis has left the whole country in a state of great instability and violence. a very painful and very complex situation that has distant roots: war, the interweaving of international interests and tribal struggles for local power and so on. all at the expense of the civilian population. it is time for the european union and the international community to exert all their pressure to initiate a political transition or to open the country to democratic norms, the only way to help the people of sudan and also of darfur to emerge from the current state of underdevelopment and suffering.
member of the commission. – mr president, this is not the first time we are discussing sudan in this plenary, and of course we see with very much concern that the human rights situation in sudan has shown no sign of improvement and is, in fact, deteriorating. serious human rights violations have been perpetrated by state actors, government—supported militia and rebel forces in impunity. these happened with serious disregard for sudan’s interim constitutions of 2005, international commitments or recommendations presented by the human rights council. international and local civil society organisations in sudan face severe obstructions in their work, in particular those working on human rights issues and in conflict-affected areas. one of these organisations is the one you referred to, tracks, a human rights organisation which provides and facilitates training on a variety of topics, ranging from human rights to information technology. currently ten members or affiliates of the tracks staff, including its director, khalafalla alafif mukhtar, who has been in detention since may, are facing trial in two separate cases under sudan’s criminal court and these carry – as you also mentioned – the death penalty. the eu considers that the repeated official raids and summoning of staff on judicial charges are in violation of freedom of expression and association and appear to be a clear attempt to intimidate the members of the organisations due to their work on human rights or democratisation. accordingly, we have closely followed developments on the tracks case and we have observed several court sessions. it is coordinating with the different eu member states and other western embassies on the ground to ensure a continuous international presence throughout the trials on a rotation basis. this case is, of course, also continuously raised in meetings with sudanese officials. overall, promoting a conducive environment for civil society and the protection of human right defenders are key issues in eu relations with sudan. we have the eu country map for engagement of civil society and the human rights and democracy strategy for sudan. however, un agencies and humanitarian partners keep being denied access to so many areas in darfur, in south kordofan and blue nile by government authorities, preventing the delivery of assistance which is so needed to the vulnerable population. we have, in the eu, been at the forefront of calling for a speedy agreement on cessation of hostilities, humanitarian taxes and an inclusive, comprehensive and transparent national dialogue process in a conducive environment. efforts towards peace and human rights remain a priority for the eu. the eu, in particular through our special representative for the horn of africa, mr alexander rondos, supports efforts towards a holistic and inclusive political solution. political and financial support was provided to the mediation efforts led by president mbeki, in the framework of the african union high-level implementation panel for sudan and south sudan. we consider that the gravity of the human rights situation requires continued attention from the unhcr and therefore we have supported the extension of the mandate of the independent experts on sudan, while pushing strongly for his full access to all areas of the country. our commitments to enhance cooperation with african countries on migration is firmly anchored within international humanitarian law and international human rights law, and eu assistance to sudan is delivered at bilateral and regional levels through international organisations and ngos, not through that sudanese government. no support has ever been given to the rapid support forces, and we are aware of the specific situation of the christian minorities and are looking into that. there have recently been some arrests of pastors and we are following those cases on the ground as well. the eu will continue to call for the government to respect freedom of expression, peaceful assembly and the media, to release the detainees and to give them an opportunity for fair trial and to conduct credible investigations into human rights violations that led to killing, injuries and material damage. i am sure this is not going to be the last time we discuss the terrible situation in sudan.

in writing. we condemn today the use of chemical weapons against civilians in the jebel marra region of darfur by the sudanese government and stress that this is a serious violation of international norms and a war crime; we also condemn all other forms of violation of fundamental human rights perpetrated by the sudanese government and opposition forces against activists, journalists and civil society spokesmen. the eu and its member states must continue their commitment to support the efforts of the african union to bring peace to sudan and to the sudanese people in their transition to a reformed democracy from within.
the agenda includes seven motions for resolutions on thailand, notably the andy hall case.
author. – mr president, in october 2015 we highlighted the difficult political situation in thailand, where a military junta took power after the coup of may 2014. at present there is no way to foresee a full transition back to a civilian government. on the contrary, the thai military junta has adopted arbitrary and even more restrictive measures to disrupt the lives of everyone opposing the regime. arrests and intimidation are frequent in order to control the population and reduce or eliminate citizens’ freedom of expression. among them, andy hall, who has always been a defender of workers’ rights and a committed activist, has been falsely accused of defamation and now faces a three-year prison sentence. we ask for immediate withdrawal of this allegation, and stress the regime should change its attitude to its citizens and to fundamental freedoms. for these reasons, we think it is essential for the commission and the european external action service to take action on the issue.
author of the book. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, andy hall is one of many activists who have exposed the human rights and labour rights violations that migrant workers in thailand are facing on a daily basis. the reporting activity of andy hall and other rights defenders has been prosecuted as a crime of defamation and this represents a restriction of the space of freedom and freedom of expression available to civil society. we believe that the bangkok government must realize that exposing abuses and bad practices by companies will not damage the country's reputation or access to the global product market, but will help to improve the quality of the world of work for the benefit of workers of all nationalities. i hope that thailand will continue to make progress in the protection of labour rights and in particular that it will continue to implement the memorandum of cooperation with neighbouring countries on the employment of foreign workers, a regulatory system which is still too little used. we hope that there will be a positive response to our resolution from the thai authorities.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we must express our concern at the four-year prison sentence for defamation and computer crimes handed down on 20 september in bangkok to andy hall, a british citizen and migrant rights activist who three years ago denounced the exploitation of labour in the fruit processing industry, much of which was destined for export to europe. hall had denounced, on behalf of an ngo, the use of forced child labour, lower than legal wages and irregular working hours in a factory of the thai giant national fruit. the european union must condemn this measure, which once again affects those who denounce the use of child labour by these large multinationals. we must demand a review of the andy hall trial and at the same time ask ourselves about the ethical quality of the products entering our market. consumers must be informed about the quality of products, but also about the basic guarantees offered to every worker employed in production. in short, we must prevent products manufactured by minors from entering our market.
member of the commission. – mr president, a thai court has sentenced the british social rights campaigner, andy hall, to a three—year suspended prison sentence. mr hall is present with us today and i welcome his presence. the case was brought against him by a thai food processing company for his contribution to a report by the european ngo, finnwatch, which alleged serious labour rights abuses by the company concerned. this verdict sends shivers through thailand’s already nervous human rights and social rights community. criminal defamation laws are often used improperly by various actors to silence analysis and debate. mr hall’s reaction, that he was grateful for the international attention the case has brought to migrant rights in thailand, testifies to his character in a way that the verdict does not because this is, of course, a much bigger question than one person. it is not my role to criticise a court, but let me mention what the ilo country director said, and i quote, ‘labour rights abuses suffered by migrants in thailand have been well documented in various ilo reports. the treatment alleged in the finnwatch report is not unique to any one employer or industry’. this verdict casts a deep shadow over the real progress in thailand in recent months regarding labour conditions. let me mention, for instance, the prohibition of child labour in the seafood sector, the reinforcement of the labour inspection, the new legislation for labour agencies, measures to prevent debt bondage and trafficking in human beings, more deterrent sanctions schemes on labour abuses and the decision to ratify several ilo conventions. this would, of course, not have been possible without political will and dedicated thai officials, without our dialogue with them, and without the cooperation of the ilo. the eu has several projects in thailand, together with the ilo, on the issue of migrant workers and labour conditions. the progress made is good and we expect it to continue. we hope that the abuses and the type of abuses which mr hall has documented will soon no longer be found in thai factories. respecting human rights is important, but it is also good business. companies in thailand and everywhere in the world who want to send to the eu need to understand that european consumers demand products free of labour abuse. i say to them that they should not underestimate the fundamental decency of the european consumer during her or his daily shopping. do not underestimate the eu’s – and the increasingly global –determination in ensuring decent work in global supply chains and more transparency. this is indeed an issue we are working on with companies to see if we can formulate a more coherent corporate social responsibility strategy that we are working on within the commission. mr hall, finnwatch, thai workers, migrant workers in thailand and thai officials working on labour rights all deserve our continued support and the closest possible cooperation to accelerate the process which is still so necessary.
