mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this report because the customs union is a great asset for the european union and a necessary instrument for the single market. it is a further step forward, but much remains to be done. customs are the gateways to our union. unfortunately, the impression is that they are not sufficiently controlled. european trade policy is very controversial. the reduced or even zero duty arrangements granted to certain goods from third countries risk causing serious damage to the european market if customs are not rigorously controlled and enforced within the already very permissive limits. it is a battle i fought a few months ago to get the precise figures of the quantities of, for example, moroccan tomatoes which entered europe from spain. it was a war of numbers between the commission, the trade unions, the governments, the producers, and yet customs should record everything. it is right to seek to unify the penalties for infringements, but before that we must intensify checks and produce reliable data.
in writing. ‒ although the customs union is considered one of the foundations of the european union and the backbone of the single market, there is no integrated approach to sanctions. in the single market we often face the same rules, but when these rules are broken, the penalties applied in the 28 member states differ significantly. the court of justice has recently held that differences in the level of penalties have an effect equivalent to quantitative restrictions. this report therefore aims to standardize the system of penalties in this field. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ the customs union and trade policy are two fundamental elements of the european union, which has exclusive competence in these matters for this very reason. although these are the building blocks of the single market, an integrated approach is still lacking, both in the area of customs enforcement and in the area of customs penalties. this not only creates disparities in the way duties are set, but also represents a risk for companies operating on the european market. the kallas report, which i supported today, deals with the legal framework to be adopted with a view to creating an integrated approach to the application of customs legislation, including the sanctioning dimension. the establishment of common, clear and transparent rules will be a crucial step forward in strengthening the customs union while ensuring compliance with international rules. the eu customs code will facilitate trade and improve the consistency of customs administrative practices in the member states.
in writing. ‒ under the treaties, the customs union and trade policy are the exclusive competence of the european union. however, without an integrated approach to the enforcement of the rules, including sanctions, it is not possible for the customs administrations of the member states to act as a single administration, especially in view of their considerable differences between sanctioning systems. this is an important limitation that needs to be overcome by providing the eu with a customs code that facilitates trade and improves the compliance of customs administrative practices of the member countries. sustainability and proportionality must be the founding criteria of the customs code. the penalties must be proportionate and therefore cannot be based on the value of the goods because this could lead to a disproportionate system where a minor infringement committed in relation to a high value commodity could have disastrous consequences for the undertaking. we must link the amount of the penalty to the financial consequences of the infringement. customs authorities should also take into account the costs of litigation, in particular for small and medium-sized enterprises, and consequently provide for the possibility of a settlement procedure, which should be designed to ensure consistency across the european union.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the directive in question, which provides for an integrated approach to the application of customs legislation, including penalties. without a common approach, it is not possible for the customs administrations of the member states to act as a single administration, especially in view of the considerable differences between the sanctioning systems of the member states. these differences create a lack of mutual trust between administrations, while trust and cooperation between customs authorities are essential for the good functioning of the customs union and the protection of the eu's financial interests. the directive aims to harmonise the application of customs legislation, to ensure uniform implementation of the penalties system and to allow economic operators to compete on equal terms in the european union. the final vote on the dossier was not taken because the european parliament's negotiating team was given a mandate to try to reach an agreement at first reading in the trilogue.
in writing. ‒ although the customs union is considered one of the foundations of the european union, there is no integrated approach to sanctions. the european court of justice has recently ruled that differences in the level of penalties have an effect equivalent to quantitative restrictions and a proposal has therefore been prepared by the commission. parliament (including myself) voted in favour by a large majority, but it is known that the file is facing strong resistance in the council from some member states.
in writing. ‒ the customs union and trade policy are the pillars of our european single market. an efficient customs regime requires clear rules, transparency and an integrated approach. i believe that the proposal for a directive on the legal framework of the union for customs infringements and penalties is moving in this direction, precisely with the aim of creating an integrated approach to the application of customs legislation, including penalties. i voted in favour of the report because i believe that the differences between the customs sanctions at national level are substantially considerable restrictions on the integration of the customs system: in a system based on common rules, it is not permissible for member states to apply different penalties. finally, convergence between sanctions systems is necessary not only to enable the eu to comply with external obligations, especially under the general agreement on tariffs and trade (gatt), but also to effectively tackle breaches of european rules.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the proposal for harmonisation on customs infringements and penalties, since it was unacceptable to have a common customs policy without the application of the same penalties. the community approach thus achieved will make it possible to eliminate disparities which could jeopardize the proper functioning of the internal market. in addition, this will also provide greater certainty for our enterprises: in today's world, where foreign trade is a key to success, a thorough knowledge of the penalties for trafficking is essential. in this connection, i would like to recall that the epp has been waging a real battle to ensure that sanctions are not linked to the value of goods but are proportionate to the value of the duties evaded. in addition, non-criminal sanctions are provided for in relation to customs infringements, while criminal sanctions are provided for where the nature and gravity of the circumstance so require. in addition to what has been said so far, a scale of penalties is also introduced which is commensurate with the seriousness of the infringement itself, but it requires a commitment on the part of the member states to ensure that the authorities in charge are as competent as possible to decide at the appropriate time.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the amendments to improve the proposal for a directive because i consider it important that action has been taken, the main objective of which is to harmonise the approach to customs infringements and penalties in order to give greater regulatory certainty to companies by focusing on penalties proportionate to the duties evaded, thus also better protecting smes.
in writing. ‒ the current disparity between the member states' legal systems on customs infringements and penalties not only affects the optimal management of the customs union, but also prevents the creation of fair conditions of competition for economic operators as it affects their access to customs simplifications and facilitations. i therefore believe that the establishment of a common legal framework for the treatment of customs infringements and related sanctions would bridge the gap between different legal regimes through a common regulatory platform and would thus contribute to achieving equal treatment of economic operators in the eu, as well as the effective protection of the financial interests of the union and the application of customs legislation.
in writing. the measures contained in the proposal aim to harmonise the rules on infringements and penalties. the rules are currently applied in the same way across the eu, but there are no rules to regulate infringements and penalties, creating a state of uncertainty for businesses. it is therefore considered that convergence of sanctioning regimes is necessary to enable the eu to comply with its external obligations under the general agreement on tariffs and trade (gatt). the commission's proposal to create a common approach in this direction is part of this approach. we have had several debates on the wording of this proposal during the internal negotiations in parliament, but i support the final text put to the vote. i believe that in order to ensure that penalties are effective, proportionate and dissuasive, it is important to leave the customs authorities sufficient scope to assess the circumstances of the case.
in writing. ‒ the growth of trade has made it increasingly necessary to crack down on customs infringements. the european union has complete harmonization of customs legislation, but its application, including the imposition of customs penalties, remains the responsibility of the member states. we support this report because it aims, among other things, to reconcile the different legal regimes through a common rules platform and to improve the level playing field between the different economic players involved. we believe that this text is a good compromise, since it explicitly lists common infringements and establishes a common scale of administrative sanctions. the existence of divergent penalties is deeply problematic both for the operators themselves and for trade relations in general, as it creates, within the customs union, arbitrage possibilities in terms of unequal administrative costs between member states, making some more attractive than others. the report proposed is designed to avoid these imbalances.
in writing. ‒ i thought it appropriate to vote in favour of the proposal under consideration as i fully agree that the disparity in the legal systems of the member states is a problem. this disparity in the level of infringements and penalties not only affects the optimal management of the customs union but also prevents the creation of fair conditions of competition for operators. it should not be underestimated that this disparity in treatment leads to a lack of transparency as to the type and manner in which sanctions are applied in the various member states. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the customs legislation of the european union has been fully harmonised for almost 45 years now, but its implementation and the application of the relevant sanctions remain the responsibility of the member states. the differences in the legal traditions of the member states have thus led to a wide variation in the way infringements are punished in the various countries and, consequently, to a distortion of competition which is more damaging to some undertakings than others, in particular small and medium-sized enterprises. the customs union is one of the eu's most important successes, even from a symbolic point of view. it would be a mistake to consider it done, however, when it is necessary to proceed in the direction of harmonizing the definitions of infringements, the penalties for infringements and cooperation between the customs agencies of the member states. the aim must be to improve the transparency and clarity of the system, ensuring that all economic operators are treated on the same terms as they should be in a genuine single market. i therefore support this resolution and i hope that the council will also follow its political direction and constructive approach.
in writing. ‒ although the customs union is considered one of the foundations of the european union and a pillar of the single market, there is still no integrated approach to the application of customs legislation as regards penalties. this means that the rules are the same but that, in the event of infringement, the penalties applied differ significantly. the customs union and trade policy are the exclusive competence of the european union, which is why only the eu can develop a common approach to ensure that customs legislation is applied. this report clarifies the scope of the directive to ensure that only offences committed by negligence or intention are considered criminal offences, thus eliminating the twisted mechanism of objective liability, which does not provide for any element of fault. therefore, intentional infringements may be subject to criminal sanctions above a specific threshold in order to allow member states to take measures which are sufficiently dissuasive to punish fraudulent behaviour. i agree with the rapporteur that the proposal for a directive must be seen in the context of the trade facilitation agreement. i voted in favour of this proposal for a directive.
in writing. ‒ the fight against breaches of union customs legislation has become central with the increase in trade at a significant level with the growth of international trade. in the eu, although customs legislation is fully harmonised, its application and the imposition of legal penalties are a matter for national competence. i therefore welcome this proposal which aims to bridge the gap between the different legal regimes by creating a common platform of rules and improving the level playing field between economic operators in the customs union.

in writing. ‒ following the attacks in paris and brussels, all the european institutions have reviewed their security needs in the short and medium term. draft amending budget no 3 for the financial year 2016 proposes to strengthen the security budget by a total of eur 15,8 million. in particular, cybersecurity and the overall security of buildings are being enhanced to better protect staff working within the eu institutions. the european parliament is to be given 35 new posts for the recruitment of additional security officers to provide armed protection at strategic points inside the buildings in the three service locations. the impact on the general budget is neutral, as the additional resources come from a transfer of an under-utilized budget line. while i am aware that the security of the institutions needs special attention, i do not agree that parliament, after the drivers, now wants to internalise these 35 new units, which will be officially classified as officials of the european institutions. i believe that the security of the institutions should be guaranteed by the host countries or, where appropriate, by certified security agencies providing trained personnel.

in writing. ‒ the report makes proposals and recommendations to the european institutions and member states to strengthen the fight against corruption and organised crime, including: the call for a european definition of a mafia-type criminal organisation, following the example of article 416a of the italian criminal code; the recognition of the key role of whistleblowers in the fight against corruption and malpractices; the call on the member states and the commission to improve and ensure transparency in public procurement through the establishment of an e-procurement system, by creating blacklists to include companies with proven links to organised crime, by facilitating the rotation of public officials and by preventing those convicted of crimes related to organised crime or corruption from participating in elections or working in the public administration; measures to combat tax havens; the commission has also proposed to increase the penalties and introduce new categories of crime within the so-called environmental crimes. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ organized crime, owing to its adaptability and tendency to diversify its activities, is increasingly a global threat that requires strong action by the european union and its member states. beyond the greater dangers to public order linked to the manifestations of violence typical of criminal organisations, criminal penetration into the legal economy is particularly damaging, which is also achieved through the development of corrupt conduct towards officials and the consequent infiltration into institutions and public administration. the ferrara report, which i supported today, stresses the need to adopt a european action plan to eliminate organised crime, corruption and money laundering. this requires not only adequate financial resources and qualified staff but also a comprehensive and integrated approach to the problem. the transposition and correct implementation of existing rules, monitoring of their application and evaluation of their effectiveness are to be ensured. the existing legislation needs to be revised to introduce effective, proportionate and dissuasive sanctions and it is necessary to clarify common definitions of offences and common methods for the seizure of property.

in writing. ‒ organised crime, corruption and money laundering have a transnational dimension and encompass a wide range of criminal activities. the eradication of this dimension requires the introduction of national databases, the support of eu instruments and a european action plan, and the active participation of international and regional organisations, in the public and private sectors, based on transparency and mutual accountability. corruption is one of the main obstacles to development today, especially in developing countries, where it hijacks much of the funding that they receive. the european union should take a more active role in providing financial and technical assistance to these countries, developing a strong and comprehensive strategy for managing the risk of corruption in them. member states must make full use of the measures already in place against such crimes and it is essential to promote common investigative techniques. progress must be made on international cooperation to combat the trafficking of human beings from which crime derives great profits. transparency is the most effective tool to combat abuse and fraud; the commission has also proposed that the data be published on the basis of the data collected by the member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today because i believe that criminal organisations have changed their way of working and now have the support of professionals, banks, officials and politicians who, although not affiliated with the criminal organisation, support its activities at various levels. the danger of intimidating force arising from mere membership of an association is not a priority in the fight against the 'end-crimes' for which the association was created. this has left a regulatory and operational vacuum at european level, facilitating the transnational activities of organised criminal groups. the current eu policy cycle for the fight against organised crime must therefore place an emphasis on countering organised crime and provide for the punishability of membership of an association to commit crime irrespective of the commission of the offence. the fight against money laundering, corruption and human trafficking must also be included among the priorities in order to put in place a genuine european anti-corruption strategy. cross-border police cooperation should be strengthened and information sharing at member state level facilitated through europol and eurojust, thus ensuring greater use of joint investigation teams.

in writing. ‒ organised crime is a global threat which as such requires a joint and coordinated response by the eu and its member states. unfortunately, there is still a lack of full awareness today of the complexity of the mafia-type associative phenomenon and of the danger arising from the infiltration of criminal associations into the social, economic-business, political and institutional fabric of the member states. this resolution calls on the commission to propose, on the basis of an assessment of the transposition and application of existing rules, regulatory measures to address any shortcomings in the fight against organised crime and to improve crossborder judicial cooperation. i believe that it is a matter of priority to take concrete action to improve european coordination in the fight against organised crime, corruption and money laundering and to raise awareness of the social and economic damage caused by these phenomena. the fight against organised crime must be pursued with determination by the common european institutions. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament has approved a five-star report by our colleague laura ferrara. the report focuses on some of the priority issues for the current historical moment and makes proposals and recommendations to the european institutions and the member states to strengthen the fight against corruption and organised crime. the report calls for the first time in history to introduce the crime of association with mafia-type criminals at european level, following the example of article 416a of the italian penal code, in order to combat mafia-related crimes. our proposal on the release of prisoners was approved by the european parliament: calls for those who have been convicted of crimes related to organised crime, money laundering, corruption or other serious crimes against the public administration not to be allowed to stand for election or to work in public administration (including eu institutions, bodies and agencies). i believe that the adoption of this report is a great success for the movement which is proving to bring honesty and the fight against the mafia and corruption into the european institutions as well. my vote was therefore in favour.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's activities in the fight against crime are a key element in responding effectively to the phenomenon of organised crime. it is a global threat and as such requires a joint and adequate response by the european union and the member states. the crim committee has helped broaden the debate on the fight against corruption at international level by providing clear guidance on legislative action to be taken. it is essential to establish a common definition of organised crime in the eu in order to give effect to existing and future legislative instruments. it is not a matter of prosecuting the offence in a given state, it is a matter of combating complex phenomena which are not confined to the national borders of this or that member state. there is still no uniform definition of the types of crime, there are no provisions in many countries to combat organised crime and it is clear that any action to combat it at european and international level seems impossible. the european union must insist on combating organized crime and, in the context of a genuine and comprehensive european strategy, efforts and resources must be shared in the fight against money laundering, corruption and human trafficking.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, thank you for giving me the floor again. i voted in favour of this report because the european parliament must continue to speak out on a situation which only creates victims. the flow of migrants to europe in recent years has put our reception system in a very difficult position, has overburdened some countries, such as mine, and has forced them to make considerable economic efforts. in other countries, however, it has led to the birth and, unfortunately, the gradual growth of populist and nationalist movements. this is the most dangerous aspect: to give in to fear and irrationality, to see the weakest as the enemy. the response to the migrant emergency which is no longer an emergency, since it is everyday life exists and this parliament has repeatedly reiterated it: the european union is also working on a number of cooperation and partnership agreements with african countries to deal with the causes and redistribution of migrants arriving on our shores in the 28 member states. the answer is not forced evictions like in calais, not walls and barbed wire like in hungary. this is not europe. europe is that of my region, sicily: the european union is the europe of welcome, and we expect that there will also be a europe of solidarity, of sharing.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted strongly in favour of mrs vergiat's report because i believe that this report finally puts the question of how to deal with the migration challenge by placing the issue of respect for human rights as a priority and not repression, rejection, evictions such as those which are unfortunately happening in calais these very days. i believe that the agreement with turkey is the emblem, the expression of the european union's wrong approach to the question of migrants. we are now witnessing a growing number of complaints from humanitarian organizations against the treatment of refugees by the turkish authorities. for us, the road is the opening of safe passageways, the opening of humanitarian corridors, starting with those that are already being built from below, as the mediterranean hope project has shown us.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report addresses the phenomenon of migration flows in third countries in a coherent and balanced way, in a holistic perspective that takes account of the human dimension, including the positive aspect of demographic change and economic development. the human rights approach is also emphasised by requiring member states to ratify all the main international human rights instruments and to apply the rules on migrants' rights contained therein. the report stresses that the opening of safe and legal channels of migration is the best way to prevent trafficking in human beings. for these reasons i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ migration is a complex and multidimensional phenomenon, a global reality that today affects some 244 million people. different factors generate and influence migration flows, but a careful analysis of these factors makes it possible to anticipate their consequences and to devise appropriate policies. the vergiat report, which i supported today, tackles the issue of migration in a very effective way, linking it to the issue of human rights. the eu must ensure the protection of migrants' rights in order to be truly credible in the discussion on migration and human rights in third countries. responding to the migrant crisis today means first and foremost fighting for the respect of their rights, while at the same time establishing appropriate measures and policies for managing flows. integration must be promoted by focusing on education and work, and by recognising and preventing those forms of discrimination and violence to which women and lgbti people are subjected. the european union has a duty to act positively to eliminate the root causes of the migration crises and to do so it must necessarily resist the populist impulses that are manifesting themselves today in many of its member states. the only way to strengthen its foreign policy action is through solidarity.
in writing. ‒ the report on human rights in third countries is the usual publicity for the indiscriminate reception of various types of migrants, most of whom are not fleeing any war or persecution. this is the usual show of goodwill by those political forces who claim to be helping the rest of the world but who have no interest whatsoever in the problems of the european citizens, who are increasingly suffering from unemployment and poverty as a result of the economic crisis. i have always fought to help our citizens, to make this union change its course and take care first of our people and then of the rest of the world. for these reasons i voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on human rights and migration in third countries because i wanted to express my solidarity with persons who are forced to leave their countries. moreover, i share with my colleagues the concern regarding human rights violations which are occurring especially in countries of transit. thus, the parliament stressed with this resolution the need to lead by example in the promotion of the human rights of migration in order to be credible in discussing with third countries.
in writing. ‒ people forced to flee their country because of conflict, persecution, human rights violations, famine or dire economic conditions must be treated with respect and dignity in both transit and destination countries. we are well aware that only by stabilising the areas of origin of migration flows can the phenomenon be stopped or at least mitigated and that this will take a long time: however, this cannot be an excuse for lowering our standards and failing to protect the personal dignity of those who come to us in objective need. the european union must strengthen its foreign policy in order to be more present in crisis areas and take direct action to prevent the outbreaks of regional instability from flaring up, and at the same time it must translate into concrete deeds its hopes for a common management of the phenomenon, the distribution of migrant quotas and the coordinated action of men and means to manage at european level and, hopefully in the near future also at federal level, this great challenge of the third millennium.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on human rights and migration to third countries because decisive responses are needed to deal with the exceptional wave of migration. europe needs to develop an integrated policy on migration. the majority of these people are forced to suffer serious human rights violations on their migration routes through transit countries. it is essential to improve the exchange of good practices with third countries by providing training to humanitarian workers so that they can more effectively identify the different characteristics, backgrounds and experiences of migrants, in particular the most vulnerable. in short, the european union must be able to build a genuine common partnership with third countries if it is to tackle the problem in an appropriate and coherent way.

in writing. ‒ the report, for which i thought i would vote in favour, analyses the main causes of the mass migration phenomena we are witnessing today and makes some acceptable recommendations to improve the reception conditions for these populations. to date, some 65 million people have been forced to leave their home countries for humanitarian reasons linked to armed conflict or simply because of dire poverty. i believe that the european union, which is founded on respect for human rights enshrined in the charter of rights, must work to ensure that migrants are given a dignified welcome, with particular attention to the most vulnerable, such as minors, especially unaccompanied minors, who are entitled to specific protection because they are often the most defenseless victims of traffickers and criminal organisations. to this end, i believe it is essential that all the member states of the union ratify the conventions and treaties, giving effect to the rules on the rights of migrants. i welcome the fact that the report introduces specific provisions to improve the quality of life of migrants by giving them access to the health system, training courses and the labour market in order to facilitate their integration and inclusion in civil society.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the motion for a resolution because i think that the report is not clear and does not take into account many aspects of the situation of migrants. i agree that particular attention should be paid to guaranteeing the rights of vulnerable groups such as women, children, disabled people and the elderly, who are most vulnerable to all kinds of danger, namely violence, trafficking or abuse, without neglecting all other categories of people. i do not think it is necessary to give greater importance to migrant associations, since integration should take place at the social level, without necessarily going through development programmes within communities, and i do not agree with the creation and application of mechanisms for the protection of migrants in transit and in emergency situations at the eu's borders. i think that debt relief for countries in poverty is of little use, because it would not necessarily be aimed at developing public policies that ensure respect for human rights. migration should not be seen as a means of solving specific problems linked to labour market failures, as this would lead to unemployment among young europeans.
in writing. ‒ we are well aware that the european union is facing serious difficulties lately with regard to the so-called 'migrant issue'. we need to remind everyone of the precise role that europe should play and is still struggling to play. our credibility is undermined if there are borderline situations or serious human rights violations within our borders. that is why i support the vergiat report. the situation that has arisen in calais, to set an example to all, cannot be accepted. we cannot talk about the protection and promotion of human rights when we cannot guarantee them within our own borders. to achieve this, to give a concrete response, we must ensure that the states ratify all the international conventions and treaties on human rights. we need to open up safe and legal migration routes. we must work to prevent human trafficking and stop the illegal routes that have been flouted so far. we must change our attitude towards the phenomenon of migration in and of itself, recognizing it as a motor for development and not as a hindrance to it. development not only for the host country but also for the country of origin.
in writing. ‒ the rights enshrined in the universal declaration of human rights are universal and indivisible and go hand in hand with the right of all people to mobility. therefore, every individual has the right to decide to leave the country in which he or she is and to exercise his or her migration choices in a dignified manner, without suffering treatment that undermines human rights, such as arbitrary detention, return to third countries where there is a real risk of ill-treatment and torture, forms of forced labour and/or degrading working conditions in the countries of origin and destination, ghettoisation of migrants in urban areas and lack of access to education. in voting in favour of this resolution, i wanted to recognise the need for the eu and its member states to protect the human rights of migrants, asylum seekers, stateless persons, displaced persons and refugees - especially within their own borders and particularly with regard to vulnerable groups (women, minors and lgbt people) - in order to be credible in the discussion on migration and human rights in third countries. in addition, the eu can make a positive contribution to addressing the root causes of the crises that cause mass migration flows and to amplifying the potential of legal migration as a development factor.
in writing. ‒ with this resolution, the european parliament reaffirmed its commitment to the protection of human rights and, in particular, the conditions of workers in third countries. the globalisation of trade and the opening of branches on all continents have made it increasingly clear that companies have become the main actors in ensuring respect for human rights by promoting and protecting them in their production. in this context, therefore, international rules and cooperation are essential to prevent human rights violations in third countries. for this reason, parliament urged the european institutions to take further steps in this direction and reminded corporate actors of their responsibility to respect human rights in their operations worldwide, regardless of the location of users and whether the host state respects its human rights obligations.

in writing. ‒ this report addresses aspects related to human rights, labour and environmental protection. rules have been introduced which reiterate the duty of businesses to respect human rights and the consequent sanctionality of their violation, even when it occurs outside the eu. member states are called upon to establish clear requirements as to the need for companies domiciled in their territory and/or jurisdiction to respect human rights in all their operations and in every country and context in which they operate. another important point in the report concerns the proposal to create an abuse-free label at union level, which could be applied on a voluntary basis, monitored by an independent body governed by strict rules and with inspection powers, competent to verify and certify that no infringements have been committed at any stage of the production chain of the product in question. that is why i voted in favour.
