in writing. ‒ the protection of human rights must be a priority for the european union and its member states. and its international role, including trade policy, must be inspired by the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality and the rule of law. in this context, the adoption of the un guiding principles on economic activities and human rights is therefore to be welcomed as a very positive step forward and i welcome the call to european and non-european businesses to adapt to these principles and ensure their implementation. businesses are among the main actors in economic, financial and trade globalisation and can therefore play an important role in promoting human rights, democracy and environmental standards. trade and human rights can and must be mutually reinforcing. i hope that europe and its businesses will really set a good example and show others the best way forward, by ensuring transparency and accountability, in the interests of workers, consumers and the businesses themselves. for all these reasons i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ in order to preserve the european union's leading role in respecting human rights, including those of persons belonging to minorities, i believe it is necessary to stress the importance of corporate social responsibility. the report emphasizes that respect for human rights is a moral and legal duty for businesses and their managers and that it should be integrated into a long-term economic perspective wherever european businesses operate and regardless of their size or industry. in this context, i welcome the proposal to include human rights responsibilities in contractual obligations between companies and their suppliers. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by mr corrao, which deals with human rights, labour and environmental protection. the main objectives of the report are to ensure that europe and the member states act urgently, continuously and effectively at all levels in addressing the legal problems arising from the extraterritorial dimensions of companies and their behaviour, as well as the related uncertainty regarding the attribution of responsibility for human rights violations. the report calls on member states to set clear requirements on the need for companies domiciled in their territory and/or jurisdiction to respect human rights in all their activities and in every country and context in which they operate, and to ensure that victims have access to effective redress. another important point in the report concerns the proposal to create a 'abuse free' label at union level, which could be joined on a voluntary basis and monitored by an independent body. with this report, the five star movement lays the foundation for removing the causes that cause uncontrolled migration flows.
in writing. ‒ business has benefited greatly from the globalisation of the economy, creating jobs and profits and gaining power and influence in many developing countries. these positive aspects are unfortunately accompanied by clear violations of human rights which have exacerbated the conditions of poverty and oppression to which many people are subjected. it is also the european union's responsibility to promote policies which enable effective instruments to be created to hold companies to account for their actions or to ensure the protection and safety of workers. we must work on legislation that ensures that they are held accountable for the impact of their activities.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on corporate liability for serious human rights violations in third countries. considering that the eu is founded on the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy and equality, and considering that the un guiding principles on economic activities and human rights apply to all states and all national and transnational companies, i believe it is the task of the european institutions to regulate the liability of economic actors who do not respect human rights. the resolution calls on the commission to carry out a thorough examination, in consultation with all stakeholders, including civil society and business, of the legal obstacles to cases brought before member state courts for alleged human rights violations committed abroad by eu-based businesses, and calls on the council and the commission to act in accordance with article 83 tfeu in order to establish minimum rules on the definition of criminal offences and sanctions in the area of particularly serious crime with a transnational dimension.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, today we voted on a report on the european strategy for liquefied natural gas and storage. but, in practical terms, what did we talk about? the fact that we will be importing liquefied natural gas from the united states of america, on the pretext that by doing so we will be sure not to be left out in the cold. unfortunately, the hard data tells us that: 1) gas demand in europe is declining and infrastructure is underutilized, 2) the mediterranean basin can and must become a global leader in the development of carbon free energy resources, 3) we cannot ignore the environmental hazards to human health caused by regasifiers and storage activities, 4) there are specific cop21 targets that require the abandonment of fossil fuels. nevertheless, the commission uses the efsi, the european fund for strategic investments, for large projects, to the advantage of the gas multinationals. we believe, on the contrary, that it is urgent and a priority to concentrate all political and economic efforts in support of renewable energy, energy efficiency and sustainability. that is why we voted against.
in writing. ‒ the report is pro-fossil energy and completely ignores the issues of strategic dependence and infrastructure lock-in, made even more perverse by the considerable under-utilisation of existing european facilities (on average 25%). it is also based on eu gas consumption projections provided mainly by entsog, which are clearly exaggerated and have been criticised by the court of auditors. gas is presented as a relatively clean fuel, thus ignoring the problems of leakage and its contribution to the greenhouse effect, and the major problems posed by unconventional extraction methods. for these reasons i voted against.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the gyürk report on the eu strategy on liquefied natural gas and gas storage. this is an important text which touches on the crucial subject of energy supply and the development of the european energy strategy. already today, several eu member states are completely dependent on gas imports, a condition generated both by the limited number of suppliers and the lack of alternative supply routes. in the near future, this dependence is expected to increase, and european action should therefore be directed both at actively pursuing the development of its domestic conventional gas resources, such as those discovered in cyprus, and at facilitating the rapid transition to a secure and sustainable energy system. only through the creation of a real energy union, with a single energy market and a common energy policy, will it be possible to guarantee real energy security for the continent.
in writing. ‒ i do not agree with the report on the eu strategy on liquefied natural gas and gas storage and i believe that it moves even further towards the objective of promoting a european energy union, another attempt to control the institutions from above on our territories. for these reasons, i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ the ratification of the paris agreement has created the conditions for the global energy transition, making the shift towards a low-carbon economy irreversible. in this transition period, the adoption of a common energy strategy would help to support a rapid transition to a sustainable, secure and competitive energy system, while limiting dependence on external gas suppliers. with a view to exploiting the union's internal resources for greater energy self-sufficiency, the report presented by the european parliament today stresses that liquefied natural gas represents an opportunity for europe in terms of increased competitiveness in the short term. harnessing the potential of lng and its storage would make the european system more diversified and flexible and contribute to a reliable gas supply, including to the most energy-vulnerable regions. to achieve this, greater cooperation and solidarity between member states and a more efficient and safer use of existing infrastructure and terminals are needed.
in writing. ‒ i endorsed this resolution on an eu strategy for liquefied natural gas and gas storage with the aim of developing a resilient energy union. indeed, the energy union has the objective to make the eu more independent from the dependence on external gas suppliers. as a matter of fact, this resolution supports the integration of lng and gas storage within the framework of the internal energy market and i strongly believe better coordination of national energy policies is needed in order to achieve it.
in writing. ‒ gas can play a significant role in the union's energy system, in industrial production and as a source of heating in buildings and in support of renewable energy over the coming decades, pending the eu's achievement of its greenhouse gas emissions, energy efficiency and renewable energy targets and the transition to a low-carbon economy, in which the role of gas will gradually decline in favour of clean energy. however, several member states are now dependent on gas from abroad for more than 90% of their average annual needs: this poses serious limitations in terms of geopolitical security, strategic security, economic security and environmental security. any action to reduce external dependence and to improve the efficiency of supply methods and means is therefore welcome. closing the infrastructure gaps for gas storage and transport of liquefied natural gas is a key step towards strengthening the union and increasing solidarity and energy efficiency. the member states must support this process by promoting the commission's action, the completion of cross-border gas networks and the implementation of the latest package of agreements for the completion of the single energy market.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report in question, which sets out parliament's position on the eu strategy on liquefied natural gas (lng) and gas storage presented by the commission last february. the report highlights the benefits of using lng for a rapid transition to a sustainable, secure and competitive energy system and to end dependence on external gas suppliers. however, it notes some critical aspects, including the infrastructure aspect, highlighting the need to carefully analyse the alternatives and options for lng supply from a regional and environmental sustainability perspective before deciding to build new infrastructure, in order to improve energy security and ensure the most efficient use of existing infrastructure. furthermore, it notes that the existing lng infrastructure in the eu is significantly under-utilized and that the demand for gas in the eu continues to be overestimated. it therefore calls for planning of gas infrastructure based on a reduction in demand.
in writing. ‒ the report is pro-fossil energy and completely ignores the issues of strategic dependency. it is also based on projections of eu gas consumption, mainly supplied by entso gas, which have been strongly criticised by the court of auditors as being grossly exaggerated. gas is presented as a relatively clean fuel, ignoring the problems of leakage and the consequent very strong greenhouse effect; in addition, the aspects related to non-conventional extraction methods are not taken into account. i could only vote against the report.
in writing. ‒ the report contains parliament's contribution to the definition of a european strategy for liquefied natural gas (lng) and its storage. the increase in lng production expected in the coming years and the consequent fall in the price may indeed represent an opportunity for the union in the field of energy security which we must seize. this could benefit those member states which have only one source of energy supply. i thought i voted for the report because, if we are to make europe an attractive market for suppliers, we must make sure that the union is equipped with the right infrastructure. if we can achieve this, we can also gain an environmental advantage, as lng can go alongside renewable sources to effectively replace more polluting conventional fuels for both road and maritime transport.
in writing. ‒ i vote against this report on the energy package proposed by the european commission. in the dossier under consideration the usual european agencies will have exclusive power on gas, and the text is characterized by a strong russophobic approach.
in writing. ‒ given the rationale for having a forward-looking energy and climate policy, i am voting in favour of the report. the eu committed itself at the paris climate conference to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 40% by 2030, and in line with these targets, a strategy on liquefied natural gas (lng) and gas storage represents a real opportunity for europe. indeed, it was estimated that the dependence on natural gas imports will increase and in this respect lng would allow for increased competitiveness as it would drive down natural gas prices and enhance security of supply. however, it must be recognised that the european internal energy market is currently far from integrated due to insufficient interconnections. therefore, existing infrastructure for lng conversion and gas storage at regional level must be renewed or implemented, and alternatives to lng must be provided where new facilities are to be built.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure because i share the eu's strategy on liquefied natural gas and gas storage and because an internal energy market that addresses and integrates these issues more effectively will help achieve the goal of an energy resilient, secure, competitive and integrated eu, also through more effective use of existing regional structures.
in writing. ‒ the eu strategy on liquefied natural gas and gas storage is one element of the energy union, which aims to give concrete expression to the eu's ambition to achieve a rapid transition to a sustainable, secure and competitive energy system and to end dependence on external gas suppliers. i believe that liquefied natural gas, gas interconnections and gas storage are important elements and can help to eliminate any kind of energy isolation of member states and regions. in this context, it is all the more important to support the most vulnerable countries in their efforts to diversify their sources and supply routes through the establishment of new lng terminals, distribution and interconnection systems that can ensure the safety of maritime supply routes and strengthen member states' energy security by reducing demand through efficiency measures.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote against this resolution because i believe that the text, as presented, could weaken the future role of liquefied natural gas and gas deposits. the report contains several references to binding climate and energy parameters, set as minimum targets for 2030, which do not fall within the scope and objectives set out in the report itself and therefore undermine its intent and scope.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report because improvements were needed on certain topics dealt with.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament's resolution on an eu strategy on liquefied natural gas and gas storage because i believe this is a key issue for the eu's energy future, given the increasing international rigidities and difficulties and the need to honour the paris agreement and put in place coherent policies to combat global warming. liquefied natural gas can replace fossil fuels and it is therefore important that the eu, as called for by the commission, develops its own strategy to diversify suppliers and sources of supply, which is a serious problem in some countries. i think, however, that this choice cannot be in conflict with the need to avoid settlements in areas of the highest environmental and landscape value already classified as sites of community interest, nor must it be detrimental to investment in renewable energy. finally, i share the s&d group's position on the infrastructure issue. there is no doubt that liquefied natural gas requires adequate infrastructure and technology, but member states have various facilities which must be fully exploited, including jointly and across borders, before new infrastructure can be built which can be harmful to the environment and displease citizens.
in writing. the report on the eu strategy on liquefied natural gas and gas storage is part of the package outlining the future of eu energy policy, presented in february by the european commission. the report argues that the promotion of an internal energy market integrating liquefied natural gas and gas storage will help achieve the objectives of a resilient energy union. it also stresses the need to take market-based and use-based measures on existing regional lng infrastructure and explains that in order to ensure more efficient use of infrastructure, alternative lng supply options should be carefully analysed. the issue of energy and diversification of sources of supply is a central issue at this time, as we shape policies for the next decades, when we will be committed to implementing regulations to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and to combat climate change. our energy policy needs to focus on an integrated, secure, competitive and sustainable system. and this strategy has to be part of it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on an eu strategy for liquefied natural gas and gas storage. gas plays a strategic role in the eu energy system that aims to reach energy security.
in writing. ‒ we welcome the parliament's report on the european commission's energy security package, which contains the necessary proposals to prepare europe for the global energy transition and presents new tools to deal with possible disruptions to energy supply. the question of energy security is the basis on which an energy strategy for the union can be built and is one of the priorities of this parliament and the juncker commission. the set of rules presented by the commission contains a wide range of measures to strengthen the eu's resilience in the event of a gas supply disruption. the most important measures include a reduction in energy demand, an increase in european energy production, further investment in a fully integrated and functioning energy market, and diversification of sources, routes and suppliers. the package of measures is important because it follows the adoption of the paris convention of 12 december 2015, a global agreement to combat climate change. by approving this measure, parliament reaffirms its commitment to respect for the environment and the protection of the terrestrial ecosystem.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of your proposal because i believe that gas can play a significant role in the union's energy system in the coming decades, in industrial production and as a source of heating in buildings and in support of renewable energy. whereas the eu is not yet able to reap the benefits of an integrated internal energy market due to the lack of sufficient interconnections and coherence and the incomplete implementation of the third energy package; i have decided to vote in favour of this proposal, since liquefied gas represents a great opportunity for the eu in terms of increased competitiveness.
in writing. ‒ the report welcomes the commission communication entitled 'an eu strategy on liquefied natural gas and gas storage'; it considers that an internal energy market fully integrating liquefied natural gas and gas storage will play a significant role in achieving the ultimate goal of a resilient energy union. i believe that the issue of energy security should be at the heart of national energy policies and the eu's common strategy and that cooperation between member states in this area should be implemented in accordance with the principles of solidarity and trust. i think it is necessary for parliament to approve the following report, as i am convinced that an internal energy market which fully integrates liquefied natural gas and gas storage will certainly have a positive impact on the eu's economy and industrial policies. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the report is pro-fossil energy and completely ignores the issues of strategic dependence and infrastructure lock-in, made even more perverse by the significant under-utilisation of existing european facilities, which are on average 25% used. it is also based on clearly exaggerated projections of eu gas consumption, mainly supplied by entso gas, which have been criticised by the european court of auditors. it is hopeful that the us shale gas market will re-emerge and flood the european market. it presents gas as a relatively clean fuel, ignoring the problems of leakage with the corresponding (very enhanced) greenhouse effect, and the major problems of unconventional extraction methods. in short, the report is simply unattainable, which is why we are voting against it.
in writing. ‒ discussing energy and promoting european development and coordination policies are central actions for security of supply and the fight against climate change. when we invest in energy, we are investing in our future. liquefied natural gas, given its peculiar characteristics, has been the subject of increasing interest from a commercial and geopolitical point of view. i therefore believe it is essential that the eu develops a strategy in this area. i also believe that a long-term sustainable energy mix, in addition to renewables, will also include natural gas, which, due to its characteristics and its wide availability, is crucial for the full achievement of the post-cop21 climate objectives.
in writing. ‒ i strongly supported the report on the european strategy for liquefied natural gas and gas storage. with this strategy we intend to ensure access to the liquefied gas markets for all member states, thus considerably broadening the range of gas suppliers. the aim is therefore to improve europe's energy security, firstly by further diversifying our sources of supply and secondly by ensuring adequate flexibility in the system through the use of storage mechanisms. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european parliament, including the provision of information on the activities of the european parliament and the commission. i would like to conclude by reiterating my concern, which is also reflected in the report that has been approved, about the doubling of the nord stream gas pipeline. i am not sure that the commissioner has been able to give us a clear answer to this question.
in writing. in this report, parliament calls on the european commission to reduce the eu's dependence on gas supplies in the long term. the report is, however, in favour of the use of fossil fuels and completely fails to consider all the issues of strategic geopolitical dependence and infrastructure lock-in. the report itself was drawn up on the basis of projections of eu gas consumption, mainly supplied by entso gas, which were strongly criticised by the court of auditors for exaggerating the figures. gas is presented as a relatively clean fuel without taking into account the problem of leakage, which significantly increases the greenhouse effect, and unconventional extraction methods such as fracking, which certainly cannot be called sustainable. i would have voted against such an approach.
in writing. ‒ a few months after the revision of the fisheries control regulation, the aim of the own-initiative report is to formulate the european parliament's position on the subject. there are profound differences in controls between member states, but also between different fishing areas, which contribute to creating a sense of injustice among operators in the sector. the rapporteur proposes a number of measures, including more training for fishermen on control and sanctions, the need to make controls against illegal fishing more uniform and effective, including through the use of new technologies, the importance of collecting quality data and a general simplification of the rules. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the fisheries sector is one of the first to be concerned with the sustainable management of seas and oceans, and its full and active participation in the definition of control rules is therefore crucial. all too often there are cases of fishermen believing that there is discrimination in the regularity, frequency, duration, rigor, accuracy, effectiveness and methods of fisheries controls in europe, and in particular in the various member states. the thomas report, which i supported with my vote today, addresses this issue by calling on the commission to ensure uniform and correct transposition of existing legislation. closer cooperation between member states is needed to achieve effective harmonisation of controls, the mandate of the european fisheries control agency must be strengthened and better training and information for fishermen must be ensured. it is only by acting on the different levels that the system can be made more functional and fair.
in writing. ‒ the thomas report on how to make fisheries controls in europe more uniform is well structured and shareable. i think it is important to try to make the bureaucracy clearer and less burdensome for fishermen, who have been experiencing a period of severe economic crisis in recent years. i therefore wanted to support the text with my vote.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on how to make fisheries controls in europe uniform because i think the current available data do not allow the eu institutions to review the control regulation. indeed, some member states have still to properly implement it and we still face different approaches in control activities. moreover, the lack of transparency between member states does not help to improve the control mechanisms. in this regard, i believe that control requirements should be complied with in an equivalent manner in the member states in order to make these controls uniform as much as possible.
in writing. ‒ fisheries controls are crucial to achieving the objectives of the cfp reform. however, there are huge differences in the scope of control and procedures between member states. the mandate of the european fisheries control agency to implement joint projects is limited, its budget is insufficient. the instruments and financial resources used to carry out the checks vary from one member state to another; the regulations are transposed differently in national legislation; penalties and judicial proceedings are very different; data are not always shared and accessible; the training for fishermen and inspectors varies and needs to be strengthened. these are the highlights of this important initiative report which was approved by a large majority.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today to ensure that the requirements for controls of fishing activities are met, which must be equivalent in the various member states. fishermen often complain that fisheries control is much stricter in their own country than in their neighbours, whether in another member state or in another fishing zone. this sense of injustice raises a real problem: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules are applied uniformly and are therefore effective. the suspicion that the rules are not applied everywhere with the same rigor is accompanied by the risk that a situation will arise where the rules are no longer respected because they are not the same for everyone. the report adopted today identifies the shortcomings in the application of the rules that lead to this sense of injustice, and proposes in particular to simplify and then rapidly revise european regulation no 1224/2009 establishing a community control system to ensure compliance with the common fisheries policy, focusing first on better implementation of the rules in the various member states, in particular by seeking greater harmonisation.
in writing. ‒ in order to address the deep differences between member states in the field of fisheries controls, this report proposes a number of measures, such as more training for fishermen on control and sanctions, the need to make fisheries controls and sanctions more uniform, the importance of quality data collection and the use of new technologies to increase the effectiveness of controls. many of the amendments tabled by the five star movement have been accepted in the text, the most important of which are the need to simplify the technical measures which often make it difficult not only to understand them but also to control and apply them; rules on simpler, more comprehensive and more consistent controls; the importance of strengthening and enhancing controls in order to combat illegal fishing and to improve the quality of the data collected. i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the control of fishing activities must aim at the creation of a uniform and effective system. it is therefore imperative that the application of the common rules and their monitoring be uniform throughout the union in order to ensure uniformity in the levels of controls and penalties. i am pleased that the report has highlighted the importance of simplification and transparency in the monitoring of fisheries activities. only simplified and clear legislation on control procedures can ensure an effective fight against illegal fishing, which is so damaging to our precious marine ecosystem. i hope that the revision of the control regulation will be the result of constructive cooperation between the european commission and the european fisheries control agency (efca), whose role i believe needs to be strengthened. finally, it is important to promote a modern monitoring system where the use of new technologies for the transmission of information and communication in real time can improve maritime surveillance. on the basis of these observations, i have decided to support the report.
in writing. ‒ the report, which aims to lighten and harmonise the bureaucratic aspects of fisheries operators, was approved. the text also contains important measures to harmonise controls on illegal fishing.
in writing. ‒ the sharing of the measure is based on the hope of a breakthrough in the fisheries sector: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fishermen are not penalized by the lack of regulation in neighbouring countries. our made in italy products represent not only a very large market, but also a genuine excellence, thanks to the legislation, sometimes too strict, which we have to abide by. however, in order to avoid any penalty or distortion of competition, it is essential to harmonise controls in order to ensure sustainable development in line with a high level of protection and improvement of the quality of the environment. the achievement of regular, frequent, rigorous and accurate control methods is a priority, especially in the light of the identified risks associated with the often denied inspection access to foreign ships. the latter has often made it difficult to control illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing and has hampered inspections of previously detected infringements (infringement rates have been estimated to be significantly higher at sea than on land). the harmonization of controls is therefore aimed at ensuring greater safety for european producers and products, while at the same time ensuring the sustainable exploitation of marine biological resources and maintaining a level playing field between european fleets.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure because it highlights the importance of ensuring effective control of fishing activities to ensure the sustainable exploitation of living marine resources. the importance of strengthening the mandate of efca in order to create fisheries control operations that allow coordinated and effective action by local, regional, national authorities and community agencies performing coast guard functions at european level is also emphasised, while also seeking to achieve real-time sharing of the data collected between the various competent authorities.
in writing. ‒ the fisheries sector is affected by the lack of homogeneity in the application of control legislation in the individual member states, which, fuelled by a sense of injustice, undermines compliance with the rule itself. i believe that it is essential for the conservation of common resources to ensure that eu fisheries rules are properly respected, that national catch quotas are not exceeded and that member states adopt a common approach to fisheries control. i therefore believe that, in view of the revision of the control regulation, it is necessary to establish effective rules to prevent, detect and sanction infringements of the control regulation, with a focus on greater harmonisation and increased cooperation establishing standardised control procedures.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution as it aims to harmonise controls on fisheries in europe while respecting national competences. the report has the dual objective of identifying the limits to the coherence and effectiveness of the fisheries control system in the eu and proposing solutions to improve its consistency.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the report which aims to harmonise and reduce red tape for operators.
in writing. ‒ the plan to harmonise the control systems of the common european fisheries policy introduced general measures of regulatory uniformity, which are very important for this sector, but left a large number of provisions optional or subject to reinterpretation from country to country, giving rise to numerous and significant differences in training, control procedures and even sanctions between the different member countries. in particular, it generated a general distrust of regulation (ec) no 1224/2009 because of the diversity of application and interpretation it provided. i therefore fully support a revision of the current legislation, based on clearer, more accessible and more equitable principles, providing for greater certainty in the provisions, concrete harmonisation in terms of common tools and technologies to be used and, above all, uniformity in terms of training and principles of sanctions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on how to make fisheries controls in europe more uniform because i think it is right to listen to the voices and concerns of fishermen about the differences in controls and i believe that the next revision of the control regulation is the right place to achieve greater uniformity in this area in the eu. in the face of a regulation governing the matter at european level, there are still too many differences between the member states in the methods and implementation of controls, in the degree of depth of controls in relation to the fisheries chain and in the type of penalties provided for in the various regulations. i therefore share the call to use the forthcoming revision of the control regulation to simplify legislation and reduce red tape, to strengthen the fight against illegal fishing, to improve and standardise the training of fishermen and inspectors, including by involving the gacs and local and regional authorities, to extend controls to the whole chain and to promote conscious consumption in restaurants. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the common fisheries policy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it responds to the need to give concrete answers to fishermen, who are one of the groups most affected by the constraints imposed by european policies. but fishermen complain most of all that these restrictions are not applied in the same way in all countries. there are considerable differences in the systems of control or sanctions, for example, and this increases the sense of frustration and injustice. if the rules are european, then they must be the same for everyone and have the same effect on all fishermen. europe must therefore make an extra effort to standardize not only the obligations but also their application.
in writing. fishing is an important source of income for many european countries. but sometimes the same european legislation seems to be applied differently in different member states. for example, in the area of controls, some states provide for controls along the whole chain, while in other states controls are only carried out at certain stages of the production chain. these differences can cast doubt on both the eu's credibility and the effectiveness of the legislation itself. today's vote calls for the harmonization of european fisheries rules, such as the mesh size of nets, control procedures, catches and the penalties for infringements. in view of the forthcoming revision of the control regulation, we have asked for more attention to be paid to this issue in order to eliminate the differences between eu member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on how to make fisheries controls in europe uniform. equal treatment is something fishermen have been complaining about in terms of application of regulations, and the eu should work on this issue to work on the feeling of injustice, giving also as always a relevant importance to transparency.
in writing. ‒ whereas the effectiveness of community legislation is directly proportional to the homogeneity of its implementation by the member states; assess the concerns and complaints expressed by fishermen in this regard and, in particular, with regard to distortions of competition caused by different applications of the same standard; the seriousness of a potential internal fracture in the common market; we share the hope that the european commission, which is about to propose a reform of the fisheries control regulation, will identify any shortcomings in the application of the existing legislation and promote effective harmonisation in the common fisheries policy, one of the areas which has benefited most from european integration. we also share the view that the objective of integration cannot be achieved without joint training of the representatives of the agencies responsible for controls, greater transparency and accessibility of data, for example by putting information sites and databases online, and more effective consultation with trade associations. we also support the strengthening of the european fisheries agency, which is currently too underfunded. we stress that greater coordination can only be achieved by giving the joint agency a new role.
in writing. ‒ i thought it appropriate to vote in favour of the proposal under consideration, as i fully agree with the view that it is necessary to make fisheries controls in europe more uniform. whereas, beyond possible regional variations, there are substantial differences between member states in the application of european rules and whereas the scope of council regulation (ec) no 1224/2009 establishing a community control system is the european union; action is therefore essential to ensure that controls are applied uniformly throughout the union. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the own-initiative report was drawn up in preparation for the next so-called 'control regulation' (regulation (ec) no 1224/2009 establishing a community control system for ensuring compliance with the rules of the common fisheries policy) which is expected to be presented by the commission in the second half of 2017. the text of the proposal stresses the importance of ensuring effective control of fishing activities in order to ensure the sustainable exploitation of living marine resources and maintain equal working conditions among european fleets. the member states of the european union are also called upon to ensure the effective implementation of the control regulation currently in force. fishing is an activity of great importance, particularly for the mediterranean islands. fishermen are bearers of knowledge and traditions which deserve great attention from the european legislator. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the need to ensure the uniform application of fisheries rules at european level. unfortunately, the procedures for inspections and controls, the level of infringement and the penalties vary from one member state to another. this discrepancy is bound to jeopardise not only the effectiveness of european legislation but also the level playing field between eu fleets. i would like to stress that the differentiation of controls does not only concern fisheries, but the whole fisheries chain. i hope that the next revision of the regulations will also aim to provide consumers with appropriate information on the fish products served in restaurants. at present, only some member states organise checks from vessel to board, while others only check certain links in the chain, excluding, for example, the transport or catering part. it is also important to understand whether the rules are not being complied with because they are not being complied with or because the current complexity and the high number of sometimes contradictory provisions undermine their actual applicability.
in writing. ‒ fisheries controls are crucial to achieving the objectives of the cfp reform. however, there are huge differences in the scope of controls, and the procedures and strategies of all member states and regions are often different. the mandate of the european fisheries control agency for the implementation of joint projects is limited and its budget is insufficient. the instruments and financial resources used to carry out controls vary from one member state to another, regulations are transposed differently in national legislation, penalties and judicial procedures differ substantially, data are not always shared or accessible, and training for fishermen and inspectors is different and needs to be strengthened. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be given the opportunity to present their opinions on the draft directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster. finally, it is also a shared and highly important call for improving the european training programme for inspectors and providing adequate training for fishermen.

in writing. ‒ the european union has enshrined democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights (drf) in its treaties and eu accession criteria. the commission has the power to enforce eu law in the member states under the eu treaties. several instruments are available for this purpose, although these are often lacking, inadequate or ineffective. the establishment of an eu mechanism on democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights that is impartial and reliable and applied fairly by all member states is therefore necessary. a european pact for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights may be adopted in the form of an interinstitutional agreement. this agreement should aim to establish the modalities for optimal cooperation between the eu institutions and the member states, integrating and aligning existing mechanisms and providing an integrated review mechanism to prevent violations and non-compliance with the drf. respect for the rule of law is a prerequisite for the protection of fundamental rights and is of particular importance within the union as it is also a prerequisite for upholding all rights and obligations deriving from the treaties and from international law.
in writing. ‒ after careful reflection and debate in the house, i have given my positive vote to the report with recommendations to the commission on the establishment of an eu mechanism on democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. i believe that the rule of law and respect for fundamental rights are values which must be protected more than they are today, in the face of possible violations of the same principles that occur precisely in our western democracies. it should be stressed that the corollaries of legal certainty, 'substantive' protection of fundamental rights and the effectiveness of protection are a joint and innate expression of the fundamental rights themselves. the aim of ensuring effective protection is therefore not only the task of the judiciary but first and foremost that of the national and eu legislature, which must lay down correct and coherent legal bases to "replace fundamental rights at the centre" of the union's legal construction. i therefore voted in favour of the proposal for a union pact to raise awareness of these issues and promote good governance, transparency and accountability in the field of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights.

in writing. ‒ the european union has a wide range of instruments to ensure that its laws and treaties are respected in economic and market matters. this is not the case when it comes to enforcing obligations relating to democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. the commission can, for example, ask the member states to adjust their budgets when they are not in line with european legislation, and no one disputes that the member states are obliged to follow the commission's instructions. but when it comes to respect for the fundamental principles on which the union is founded, too often the member states are reluctant to follow the commission's invitations, in its role as guardian of the treaties, or openly refuse. this leads to an erosion of mutual trust and of the citizens' trust in the institutions. it is therefore time to develop a systematic, impartial and comprehensive procedure to monitor and ensure that the values on which the union is founded are respected, both by the member states and by the european institutions themselves. democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights are at the top of the priorities set out in the treaties, and it is time that these priorities were also defended in practice.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report with recommendations to the commission on the establishment of an eu mechanism on democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. the report stresses that the eu has a multitude of instruments at its disposal for the application of its laws and treaties when it comes to material issues (such as adjusting member states' budgets or implementing specific public health programmes), but has no influence on ensuring respect for democratic values and the rule of law which should be common to all member states. although the eu has several instruments to do this and to try to monitor compliance with the common principles, these are deficient, limited in scope and inadequate. the report considers it essential for the eu to have a regulatory framework enabling it to address and condemn, including through the application of sanctions, violations of fundamental rights and european principles (former articles 2, 3 and 7 teu) and therefore asks the commission to submit a proposal for the establishment of such a monitoring mechanism by september 2017.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the new regulation is an important step forward in the fight against organisms harmful to plants and thus in the protection of biodiversity. the definition of the most dangerous harmful organisms, known as quarantine, the better division between priority harmful organisms, i.e. subject to stricter rules on eradication and information to the public, and the obligation for professional operators to register will ensure more effective controls and better traceability. this regulation therefore adjusts the activities related to trade both within the union and with third countries by means of a risk-based assessment. these are rules designed to curb the increasing influx of organisms harmful to plants, such as xylella fastidiosa or cinipidae for chestnuts, into the european union. finally, it is essential to ensure that there is a sufficient interconnection, which is not at present foreseen, between the regulation in question and the international standards deriving from the agreements of the international plant protection convention.
author of the book. madam president, commissioner andriukaitis, ladies and gentlemen, mr minister, i rise to speak on behalf of the seven co-signatories of the resolution tabled following two questions for written answer. trans fatty acids are unsaturated fats found in many industrially produced partially hydrogenated vegetable oils. the legislation on tfa is one of the priorities of the european parliament, which here reiterates its concern about the risks posed by tfa to human health. consumption of these oils is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease. in fact, a study was recently published showing a significant correlation between the consumption of trans fats and brain ischaemic events. there is also strong suspicion that these acids may contribute to a large extent to arteriosclerosis processes and thus increase the risks of myocardial infarction. the who and fao recommend reducing intake to below 1% of daily caloric intake through diet, while efsa, the european food safety authority, recommends that as little as possible be taken. parliament therefore considers that action at national level alone is not appropriate and that action by the european union is necessary in order to reduce the average intake of trans acids significantly. trans-fatty acids are used by the food industry for their characteristics, giving products the desired consistency and ensuring a long shelf life, but above all they are an inexpensive production factor. the foods currently produced with these acids are mainly foods consumed widely among young people. it is precisely the lack of awareness on the part of consumers of the adverse health effects of tfas that makes mandatory labelling for these acids an important, if incomplete, tool. we call on the european commission to introduce as soon as possible a legal limit in the european union on the content of industrial tfas, both as ingredients and as final products in all food products, in order to reduce the intake by the entire population. we also ask that this proposal be accompanied by an impact assessment which examines the industrial reformulation costs to be incurred in the event of the introduction of a mandatory limit and the potential spillover of these costs to consumers. finally, we call on the commission to work with the member states to improve nutritional literacy by encouraging and enabling consumers to make healthier food choices and by engaging industry to promote the healthful reformulation of products. as representatives of the public, we have an obligation to call for the adoption of useful tools to enable consumers to make healthier choices about the food they eat and about diet in general, and which could promote the provision of healthier food options to consumers, including, in this case, the provision of information on trans fats or restrictions on their use.
on behalf of the efdd group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, you have spoken about impact assessment. we urge you to act quickly because it's scientifically proven that the intake of trans fats increases the risk of cardiovascular disease, obesity and even diabetes. it is almost superfluous to mention that these types of noncommunicable diseases are the leading cause of death in the world. yet, trans fats are found in industrially produced partially hydrogenated oils used in biscuits, cakes, popcorn, crackers, and many other supermarket products. all the foods that are mostly eaten by children. at the time, the world health organization reported that in the european union, 1 in 3 children between the ages of 6 and 9 are obese, and about 7 percent of european health spending is spent on treating obesity-related diseases, such as diabetes and cardiovascular disease. we therefore ask the commission to introduce this legal limit on tfa to reduce the use by citizens of the european union. we are calling for action to ensure that the food industry is obliged to obtain health-compliant treatments for trans fats. we also call for the substitution of palm oil for tfa. we also call for consumers to be given the opportunity to make more informed food choices by informing them of the health risks of their products.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, finally, i say finally, in this house today, i heard about the central mediterranean, the africa-italy route, where the situation has not improved, but has actually worsened, because we have a record year for landings this year, not only having surpassed last year, but also the record of 2014, and landings have only increased in italy. so, if the council finally recognises that we need a concrete commitment, with concrete measures to come quickly to combat illegal immigration and to stabilise that area of the mediterranean, we will avoid many unnecessary deaths, many unnecessary deaths, that is an impressive number, and we will restore security to our citizens. but you see that we will also have a benefit on the economic framework, because if there is no situation of stability, investors will not come, they will not come to invest in europe, they will choose other areas of the world. and more and more they will choose other areas of the world, while we need to grow again, we need to create new jobs, to give a future to our young people. and that is why we, as the italian delegation, have always said, for example, that we are against giving china the status of a market economy, because it is not a market economy. that's why i say with strength and passion: we must not abandon the objective of 20% of gross domestic product coming from manufacturing by 2020, we must defend the real economy, because without industry, without small and medium-sized enterprises, we cannot get out of the crisis.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, president pittella, in describing the outcome of the european council, recently referred to the words of romano prodi, president of the european commission: "to move forward, you have to ride". i would like to conclude by recalling the words of another great italian, the father of european socialism, pietro nenni, who said in one of his last speeches: 'we must either renew or perish.' i believe that this is the crossroads facing our europe today. and enough of the timid and routine european councils! our continent faces epochal emergencies from refugees begging for our welcome. it is therefore right to acknowledge the efforts, including financial ones, made by states such as italy at the forefront of immigration, but we also expect concrete commitments on the distribution between member states and on africa, with partnership agreements for migrants from countries of transit and origin. but we must also respond to the problems of employment, social security and the possibility for our citizens to lead a decent life, and this calls for the extension of the european investment plan, but also for economic policies that are more attentive to the fight against unemployment.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, another european council meeting on immigration. the commitments made cannot remain on paper, there is no more time, words must be followed by deeds. the way forward is clear to all but the populists: the european union must have a new european immigration policy, a comprehensive policy based on the principle of solidarity and fair sharing of responsibility between all the member states. we must turn words into deeds now. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the relocation of asylum seekers from italy and greece to all member states, in accordance with the commitments it has made. concrete actions, implementing the european migration compact without criminalizing immigration for security reasons, but aiming to address the root causes of immigration. the commission has also adopted a communication on the implementation of the european investment plan for the countries of origin and third countries of origin of migration flows in order to promote development. no more postponements!
first vice-president of the commission. – mr president, just a few reflections after the debate in the plenary. first of all, the migration issue: i share the concerns of all those who have raised their worries about what is happening in the southern mediterranean. it is a tragedy that so many people are still drowning in spite of the tremendous efforts of the italian authorities to save as many people as possible. we need to have a comprehensive approach about this. let me be very clear: better border protection is part of the answer, but it is not a panacea for the migration crisis. if we believe we can hide behind border and fences and rid ourselves of collective solidarity in this issue, we are being delusional. delusional! just imagine that in the next generation or two, the population of africa will be anywhere between three and six billion people. how do you think the mediterranean will ever be wide enough, or fences ever high enough to stop these people from coming to europe if we do not have a policy that will offer them perspective in their own nations and their own continents, in their own cities and villages. so do not believe in the delusion of borders as the only solution to this problem and do not believe in the illusion that you can rid yourself of collective european solidarity in tackling this huge crisis. if you think you can rid yourself of the solidarity, others will rid themselves also of solidarity and that will be the end of the european union. so i believe strongly in a collective approach and a comprehensive approach that addresses all the issues linked to the migration crisis. on ceta let me just say one thing: if you believe, at the beginning of what i would call the 4th industrial revolution, that you can protect yourselves from not entering into agreements with parts of the world where they share our values, you are delusional. look at what is happening in the world’s economy, look how fast the world’s economy is changing. we need to have comprehensive agreements with those parts of the world which share our values, which want social protection like we do, which want environmental protection like we do. it is only together that we will face the forces of globalisation in a way that will guarantee the rights our citizens demand and i really call upon the walloon parliament to study carefully. mr lambert said that it is the only parliament that has actually read the treaty – well, i will leave that to his own judgment. i fear i do not agree with that assessment. but, if they read the explanations and the assurances that we have given, the clear indications on social protection, on environmental protection, on assurances that disputes will be dealt with by judges in a way that is in accordance with our legal criteria; if they have studied this perhaps they can come to a conclusion of this matter. it is clear to me – let me end on this point – that it is not an isolated matter that people worry about trade agreements. it is not an isolated matter that people sometimes think that building fences is an answer to our problem. it is an element in a world that is changing so fast that people fear that they have lost control of their destinies. only by offering answers at a european level, so citizens feel that we can help them in a system in regaining control of our collective destiny, will we find solutions for global problems.
president of the european council. – mr president, thank you for what has been a good and lively debate. i have just a few comments. first, on ceta: many in this house have suggested that we should simply ignore the views of national parliaments on trade agreements and that the debate in belgium and wallonia’s resistance do not result from the belief that the competences of eu institutions regarding trade policy are too limited. today people would prefer the state and national parliaments to have a bigger influence on the course of things – not smaller. is it any easier to govern europe thanks to this? no, of course it isn’t, but no one will change the fact that the eu is still the union of the states and not the institutions. when it comes to russia, i have just one remark. the fears and concerns, for example on private arbitration, must be addressed, and they are being addressed and explained only now. i trust that after today’s talks in belgium, the climate around ceta and maybe also around the next free trade agreements will change for the better. when it comes to russia, i would like to say two things. first, we must keep unity in our relations with russia. the building of eu unity is a difficult, not to say unaesthetic, process, but there is no alternative. if we want to be effective vis—à-vis russia, we must stay united as the eu. (applause) second, at the european council i backed those who were pushing for a stronger position on russia’s role in syria. the letter written by verhofstadt, harms and weber was a real support for me. thank you for your initiative. i want to say to those in this room who were the harshest critics of the european council for not taking a sufficiently univocal position that they can help by doing the work both in their political families and in member states. when it comes to migration, i have just one remark. i am absolutely aware that the situation in greece remains critical. it is clear that it is too early to talk about success, but please just imagine what the situation on the greek islands would look like if not for the decrease in the number of irregular migrants by 98% – not 9%, not 8%, but 98% – which we managed to achieve. this is the beginning of the process but this is the only way, also for the central mediterranean route. this is why i am also starting to discuss the positive aspects of our activity. in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the general budget of the union for the financial year 2017. this year the eu is faced with a number of serious emergencies, unforeseen at the time of the mff 2014-2020, which now require a broader effort to resolve. more financial resources should therefore be allocated to address those policy challenges and enable the union to act effectively in the new global context. a balance needs to be struck first between long-term priorities and new challenges involving issues such as the union's internal and external security, the management of migration and the need to strengthen investment to foster growth and jobs. these evaluations should be made in the light of the parallel mid-term review of the multiannual financial framework. the text adopted today respects this, adding €1.5 billion in appropriations for the youth employment initiative and providing for the cancellation of all cuts made by the council in the area of development policy and humanitarian aid.

in writing. ‒ the budget of the european union represents about 1% of the eu's gross national income and is therefore complementary to national budgets. the draft budget for 2017 must take into account the expressed wish of the people of great britain to leave the european union. the draft budget reflects and supports the political priorities set by commission president juncker and seeks to provide a european response to the challenges of managing migration, combating terrorism and organised crime, protecting the union's external borders and working with the eu's neighbouring regions. one of the budget's main priorities is employment, growth and investment, as the growth forecasts remain modest, even as the european economy continues to recover. the committee on fisheries calls on the committee on budgets to take account of the fact that the emff, compared with other funds, has limited resources and that the network of agreements with third countries must be extended. in addition, funding for the fisheries sector must not be reduced, as this sector has an important economic, social and environmental dimension in the blue economy.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the draft general budget of the european union for the financial year 2017. i believe that many of the policy priorities, such as effectively managing the migration and refugee crisis, promoting competitiveness through job creation and pursuing the sustainable development goals, are supported by adequate financial resources. in particular, in the 2017 budget, parliament catalysed its focus on new and serious challenges not foreseen at the time of the preparation of the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020. the 2017 budget is therefore to be seen in the wider context of the mid-term review of the mff and, as the report appropriately shows, is in line with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. the eu, having ratified the cop21 agreement, will devote a large part of its financial resources to the fulfilment of its international commitments. the budget for 2017 is expected to allocate 19,2% of the total expenditure to this purpose.

in writing. ‒ this report, which deals with the post-election review of the mff (multiannual financial framework) 2014-2020, calls first for more flexibility and also for substantial additional resources to meet the union's new challenges and issues. while i agree with the need for greater flexibility and the search for new funds, i do not think that raising the ceilings is the right way to achieve these objectives, but rather that it is better to try to find new resources from other existing budget lines, and to try to review future priorities. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ the many challenges facing the european union, migration and the economic crisis in particular, make the chronic insufficiency of resources available under the current multiannual financial framework increasingly evident. in this context, its revision can provide a unique opportunity to address the budgetary difficulties that are undermining the eu's overall credibility. the resolution adopted by parliament today, which i support, strongly calls on the council to ensure a credible, coherent and sustainable budget for the remaining years of the current programming period. the budget must be made more flexible and able to respond promptly to the challenges of our time: the european union is also committed to the development of a common foreign and security policy. the new resources must also be linked to an evaluation of the post-2020 mff because the way to regain citizens' trust in the european project also involves the establishment of a more transparent, effective and accessible budget.
in writing. ‒ on 6 july, the european parliament adopted a report on the preparation of the revision of the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020. the resolution we have voted on today, tabled by the committee on budgets, takes note of this proposal and reaffirms the priorities of the european parliament, in line with the resolution of july. the proposal does not differ much from the report adopted before the summer: the eu is facing a new challenge, and this requires more flexibility and additional resources. i have very strong reservations on this last point in particular, as i do not see how the member states, in the present crisis situation, can undertake new economic efforts, especially in the light of the budgetary constraints imposed by brussels and the disastrous results of its policies. i think it would make more sense to move towards a review of existing priorities, making real cuts in the eu's unnecessary expenditure and costs and start doing the best for our citizens.
in writing. ‒ i endorsed the resolution on the mid-term revision of the mutual financial framework (mff) 2014-2020 because it underlines our concern with regard to the insufficient resources that are available at the moment. we are facing new challenges today such as the refugee crisis and i believe the revision of the mff shall have the aim of ensuring a fair balance between the long-term priorities and the new emerging challenges. in this regard, i welcome the proposal of the establishment of an eu crisis reserve by the commission as instrument to tackle rapidly the crises.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution today because i share its recommendations to the european council with a view to the mid-term review of the multiannual financial framework. parliament called for budgetary appropriations to be increased so that the eu could have a budget commensurate with the political commitments and strategic objectives it intends to pursue. the problems of migration, internal security, the crisis in the agricultural sector and the persistently high unemployment rate, especially among young people, require the adoption of appropriate measures and additional funds which, unfortunately, were not provided for in the first years of the current multiannual financial framework (mff) due to the limited resources available. the mid-term review of the mff should also be the start of a consensus-building process for the post-2020 mff. in this context, the report recommends strong commitments, including the creation of new own resources capable of significantly reducing the share of gni-based contributions to the eu budget, the gradual elimination of all forms of correction, and aligning the duration of the mff with the political cycles of the institutions.
in writing. ‒ on 6 july, the european parliament adopted a report on the preparation of the post-election review of the mff (multiannual financial framework) 2014-2020. this resolution is on the commission proposal and was strongly sought by the rapporteurs to strengthen parliament's position in the negotiations with the council. the commission has therefore reiterated its previous position: the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the new rules and will continue to monitor the implementation of the new rules. while we agree with the first point, it is clear that the states are not willing or able to undertake new economic efforts. it would therefore be more sensible to review the priorities, including, where appropriate, identifying budget lines on which to act to raise the necessary resources. that is why i voted against.
in writing. ‒ i share the proposal for revision because of the continuing concern about the insufficiency of the resources available under the current multiannual financial framework (mff) in the face of the multiple crises and emergencies that have emerged in recent years. substantial amounts of additional funds are needed for the eu budget and a mid-term review is a crucial link for the optimal weighting on the post-2020 side. among the measures presented, the one that has generated the most confidence in me is the commission's proposal to create an eu crisis reserve as a means of rapid reaction to events with serious humanitarian or security implications. in fact, in the light of what has recently happened in central italy following the earthquakes of september and october, it is a duty to provide assistance and aid to those who suddenly find themselves having lost everything. therefore, i call on the commission to implement these measures as soon as possible, to integrate them into the 2017 eu budget without delay and to enter into substantive negotiations with the council on the mid-term review of the mff in the context of the 2017 budgetary conciliation procedure. in addition to the above, i would ask the commission to provide clarification on the financial implications of the uk's withdrawal from the eu, without prejudice to future negotiations.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure because the text presented on the one hand positively incorporates some of the amendments which parliament had previously proposed, in particular on the subject of flexibility. some corrective needs and specific needs remain, such as that relating to the mobility of young people, which is essential to strengthening european awareness and identity. the creation of an eu reserve as a rapid response instrument to crises and events with serious humanitarian or security implications is welcome.
in writing. ‒ i am voting against this resolution because it would make more sense to review existing priorities, identify costs to be cut and avoid raising overall spending ceilings.
in writing. ‒ it is urgent to equip europe with the adequate resources to respond to the many open political emergencies. i therefore share the report of the committee on budgets which strongly underlines the concern about the insufficiency of the resources available under the current multiannual financial framework, drawing attention to the number of new crises and priorities that have emerged in recent years, in particular the migration and refugee crisis, internal security issues, the persistence of a high unemployment rate, especially among young people.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the mid-term review of the multiannual financial framework (mff) 2014-2020 because i believe that, after having approved the resolution of 6 july on the review of the functioning of the mff, an adequate response to the challenges we face requires a volume of additional funds from the eu budget. this is a unique opportunity for the eu to address the challenges that are undermining the eu's credibility and the achievement of its objectives. the eu needs a realistic and credible budget and the review can be the way to strike a balance between achieving the eu's long-term political priorities and responding to current challenges, which require an immediate response, which, however, cannot be at the expense of existing policies and programmes. for these reasons i have strongly supported the creation of a permanent reserve within the european budget; the commission has also incorporated the need for a flexible revision to respond promptly to challenges such as the migration crisis, terrorism and internal security.
in writing. ‒ the reality is much, much faster than the imagination, let alone the european budgetary review procedures. we have been talking for years about immigration, the costs of reception, border control and we are now discussing a commission proposal on the revision of the multiannual financial framework which does not add one euro to what has already been agreed, but makes the kindly concession of reprogramming, that is to say, moving and earmarking resources for emergency migration. it almost sounds like a joke. efforts to "simplify" are even more surreal. the commission, for the sake of simplicity, merges the revision of the basic acts of the major european policies, cohesion and agriculture, into a single regulation, omnibus, dangerously limiting the scope for action of the european parliament. some might think that even in europe, as in the cat's meow, "everything has to change, so that everything stays the same". but i am sure that will not be the case, because europe cannot afford to remain the same, and this parliament will at least have to fight for something to change.
in writing. the proposal aims to ensure greater flexibility in the mff and annual budgets and to better reflect the new eu priorities that emerged as a result of crises and challenges that could not be foreseen when the 2014-2020 weekly budget was decided. the mid-term review of the mff was a clause strongly wanted by parliament at the time of the negotiations, precisely to allow the european budget to be aligned with future needs. we are therefore ready to enter into talks with the council in order to reach agreement on a budget which is really efficient, capable of responding promptly to the crises of migration and refugees, terrorism and internal security, the crisis in agriculture and capable of countering, with the help of the member states, the increase in the rate of unemployment, especially among young people.
in writing. ‒ by voting in favour of this resolution, as i did, parliament is taking a clear position on the future financing of the eu budget. in summary, this resolution highlights many of the key figures and themes which have characterised the implementation of the mff so far: critical situations and delays in the implementation of programmes; the need to revise upwards the ceilings for commitment and payment appropriations; the commission's proposal for a regulation on the european union's financial instruments for the period 2007-13 is based on the principle of the european union's own resources. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a european agency for the evaluation of medicinal products for human use (emah) is a step in the right direction. we use the mff to show that our strategic priority is a europe that is more cohesive at home, stronger and more globally active, and really closer to its citizens. but from a dry debate such as that on the financial perspective, it is possible, through the choices made, to recover a renewed europeanism which puts the 500 million citizens we represent here at the centre of the action.
in writing. ‒ i thought it appropriate to vote in favour of the mid-term review of the mff, as i regard the proposed amendments to the mff package as positive. these amendments are consistent with the objectives set by the institutions, and i therefore voted in favour of them.
in writing. ‒ the commission's proposal for a revision of the multiannual financial framework is a step in the right direction as regards flexibility, but it fails to address the real problem of the matter, namely the amount of appropriations for the headings most under pressure because of the huge political challenges facing europe. migration flows, youth employment and the development of the neighbouring countries are issues which must be tackled with the highest priority and the appropriations we have in the mff today are totally inadequate because they are calibrated to a situation which is totally different from that of five years ago. this review will be one of the few opportunities to give new life and credibility to this eu which should look more at the lives of its citizens and not just at the budgets of its member states. if we want a europe which is not only about markets and the economy, but above all about rights and solidarity, we must demonstrate this by a budget that is up to the task, but at the same time by respect for the treaties by all the member states: it is a question of two elements that either go hand in hand or both are missing.
