in writing. ‒ on 6 july, parliament approved a report on the preparation of the post-election review of the mff (multiannual financial framework) 2014-2020: this text was a prelude to the commission proposal, which is now finally on the table. the resolution we have voted on today, tabled by the committee on budgets, takes note of this proposal and seeks to reiterate parliament's priorities. the two co-rapporteurs have stressed the need to produce this new document which, in their view, should serve to strengthen parliament's position in the negotiations with the council. the proposal does not depart much from what was said in the summer, namely that greater flexibility is required (which i fully support) and that substantial additional resources are required to meet new challenges and problems: i have reservations about this, because it is clear that the states are not willing or able to undertake new economic efforts, even in the light of all the budgetary constraints imposed by brussels. i think it would be more sensible to review the priorities, and if necessary to identify budget lines where we can intervene to find the necessary resources, but certainly not to increase the overall ceilings.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund provides additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. the necessary amounts shall be entered in the general budget of the union as a provision. for the activation procedure, the commission, in the event of a positive assessment of an application, shall submit to the budgetary authority a proposal to mobilise the fund together with a corresponding transfer request. in the event of disagreement, a trilogue procedure is used. in september 2016, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf for estonia to facilitate the reintegration into employment of redundant workers in three companies, concluding that the application qualified for a financial contribution. the personalised services to be offered to workers range from support for formal studies, training and work experience to study and mobility allowances. estonia shall ensure that the measures provided for in this decision are implemented in accordance with the principles laid down in the relevant union legislation. the estonian authorities have provided all the necessary guarantees. therefore, parliament agrees with the commission that estonia is entitled to a financial contribution as the conditions of the egf regulation are met.

in writing. ‒ the great digital revolution that is taking place before our eyes brings with it numerous opportunities but also many unknowns, especially for those people who, being in a disability situation, risk being more vulnerable to exclusion phenomena due to a failure to adapt new technologies to their needs. already today 80 million european citizens have a disability and as the population ages this figure is set to increase to 120 million by 2020. the charanzová report, which i supported with my vote today, deals with the issue of the accessibility of mobile banks' websites and mobile applications on the basis of these considerations. the new rules will require websites and mobile applications of public bodies such as administrations, courts, public hospitals and universities to meet common accessibility standards. public bodies will also be required to provide and regularly update a detailed accessibility statement on the compliance of their websites and applications with the directive, including explanations in case of non-accessible content, which will have to be duly justified.

in writing. ‒ article 9 of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities requires member states and the eu to take appropriate measures to ensure equal access for persons with disabilities to information and communication technologies, including the internet. in 2012, the european commission presented a proposal for a directive aimed at ensuring equal access to information, web browsing and management of mobile applications of public bodies for both people with physical or mental disabilities and people with advanced age and poor digital skills. the internet has become an essential tool for obtaining and providing information and services. it is therefore more important than ever to ensure that all citizens can perceive, understand and interact with websites and mobile applications appropriately. in the eu, some 80 million people are affected by a disability. and as europe's population ages, this figure is expected to rise to 120 million by 2020. a common approach to ensuring network accessibility is a prerequisite for an inclusive digital society, which takes full advantage of the digital single market to promote dignity, participation and fair information.

on behalf of the efdd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this new regulation is the result of months of constant work with the rapporteur and my colleagues, but above all it is a great success for the defence of agriculture and the environment. by replacing a 15-year-old directive, we are finally getting past the contradictions of the commission, which is showing quite a few shortcomings in its emergency management in the xylella affair. yes, because, after imposing measures that were simply impracticable to combat the bacterium, the commission, through commissioner andriukaitis, has initiated an infringement procedure against italy, denying it the possibility of carrying out an environmental impact assessment. the reason is that this would delay the obligation to act immediately and therefore to eradicate hectares of olive groves, even centuries old. but environment commissioner vella does not see it that way. in reply to a question i put, you stress that plans for the eradication of organisms harmful to plants of agricultural interest must be subject to environmental assessment, not excluding emergency cases. but beyond this exquisitely political quarrel, we should move along parallel tracks and therefore on the technical and scientific level, but we have on the one hand italy, which for months has only provided information on the pathogen and potential vectors, and on the other france, which has not been able to give any evidence of any kind on its infected plants and which, after discovering that it used a wrong test, unable to identify the xylella pauca strain, accuses italy of contagion and discovers, moreover, that in its territory a sub-species has already generated different strains, raising well-founded suspicions of a long presence of xylella pauca on french soil. i repeat what i have been saying for months: we are not going to be able to do that. is the problem european? well, then, it should be treated as such. it's only a matter of time before more outbreaks are discovered. there is no need to punish the member states: it is not by environmentally unfriendly eradication or economic blackmail that we can combat plant health emergencies, but by far-sighted policy action and regulation such as the one we voted for today.
in writing. ‒ the issue of plant pests is becoming, over time, a very sensitive one. in fact, just look at what is happening in italy with the xylella parasite, which is killing thousands of olive trees in the puglia region. it is therefore clear that a regulation introducing stricter import arrangements and restrictive conditions for the protection of the environment is needed. that is why i have decided to vote against the rejection amendment.
in writing. ‒ the outbreak of xylella fastidiosa, which has damaged many olive groves in italy, has brought the fundamental issue of plant health to the public's attention. the mcintyre report, which i support, is aimed specifically at defining a series of protective measures against harmful organisms affecting the plant world. in a globalised world, with continuous trade and climate change, the scale of risks is constantly increasing and requires the use of innovative tools that are able to respond effectively to new challenges. the new regulation is a response to this need. it provides for rapid response mechanisms for suspected plant importation, the establishment of emergency plans for outbreaks in all member states and a general increase in pest surveillance efforts in the union. the phytosanitary certificate requirement will be extended to all plants and plant products from third countries, as will the use of the 'plant passport' within the eu. member states will be allowed to impose eradication measures even in private places, provided that those farmers who are affected by such measures are fairly compensated.
in writing. ‒ the adoption of a new regulation on protection measures against harmful organisms of plants can be a good starting point for more effective action to combat the growing phytosanitary problems, in particular those caused by the spread of harmful organisms from distant countries, which damage crops and the environment of our territories. however, we must be careful that the new regulation does not create new bureaucratic burdens for our companies.
in writing. ‒ as a result of the globalisation of markets, we are seeing an increase in trade flows, but at the same time we are also seeing an increase in the risk of contagion by diseases and other harmful organisms. that is why an agreement at european level is needed to protect agriculture, a key sector of the european economy. i therefore welcome an agreement to strengthen prevention in this area, to limit the entry of harmful organisms into european territory through trade in plants. the new regulation introduces a risk pre-assessment mechanism, which is to be applied to all the member states. the commission has also proposed that the eu should be able to provide the necessary financial support to the member states in order to ensure that plants and other plant protection products considered to be at risk can no longer be transported across eu borders. in addition to increased control, there is also considerable trade facilitation, which aims to improve cooperation between member states, and a considerable simplification of certification practices. the instruments contained in the agreement will therefore enable the european union to develop a more proactive policy to protect biodiversity and the competitiveness of our agricultural sector.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopted, at first reading, a legislative resolution on the proposal for a council regulation on protective measures against organisms harmful to plants. attention should be paid to the risk of introduction of plant pests into the union territory, which has increased due to the globalisation of trade and climate change. parliament therefore stressed the importance of taking preventive and protective measures and of identifying the presence of harmful organisms at an early stage in order to ensure their rapid and effective eradication. this regulation should lay down rules on plant health inspections and plant health measures to prevent the introduction of harmful organisms from other member states or third countries. in addition, all information on the possible economic, environmental and social impacts of plant pests should be made available to the public. awareness raising and training in pest management for professionals, local government officials, garden centres, importers, researchers, government department officials, politicians and individuals is also of key importance. the text also provides for the modernisation of plant protection products' commercial instruments, with a focus on a risk-based approach.
in writing. ‒ today we have adopted new eu rules to help prevent the spread of plant pests in europe, such as xylella fastidiosa in olive groves, and to contain potential outbreaks. the regulation introduces new preventive rapid response mechanisms for suspected plant imports, intensifies pest surveillance efforts in the eu and requires all member states to draw up emergency plans for outbreaks. pests and diseases do not respect national boundaries. that is why it is so important to have eu-wide rules for the protection of our agriculture, horticulture and forestry, through a proportionate and risk-based approach, which provides for better cooperation between member states.
in writing. ‒ the phytosanitary factor is crucial for sustainable and competitive agriculture, horticulture and forestry, but also important for the protection of biodiversity and economic services. pests from other continents have proved to be particularly dangerous and can cause serious economic losses and undermine the competitiveness of our farmers. this regulation, which will replace a 15-year-old directive, contains favourable elements and measures such as: containment and prevention measures in cases where eradication is no longer possible, increases compensation for affected areas, ensures greater transparency through the creation of an ad hoc emergency register, is mentioned for the first time among the conditions for identifying a priority test of social and environmental conditions and in particular refers to tree species of great importance in terms of landscape and cultural or historical heritage for the union (secular olive trees), removes the reference to efsa as the main scientific interlocutor . in the light of the above, i voted against the rejection amendment.
in writing. ‒ plant health is a key factor in the competitiveness of the agriculture, horticulture and forestry sectors. pesticides or harmful organisms such as insects, fungi, bacteria and viruses, especially from other continents, can cause serious damage to plants and spread rapidly in the absence of an adequate protection system. i would like to mention the case of xylella fastidiosa, a bacterium from america, which in 2104 devastated some 30 000 hectares of olive groves in the italian region of puglia, causing significant economic losses for the growers. in the light of this dramatic event, i also believe that it is necessary to amend the basic legislation to deal with the risks associated with the arrival of new pests on the territory of the union as a result of the processes of globalisation and climate change. i therefore believe that the new regulation, which aims at a higher degree of security of the import system, is moving in this direction. for these reasons i voted in favour of the recommendation.
in writing. ‒ i fully support the proposal as italy, thanks to its climate, enjoys a particularly flourishing territory, but it is also sadly exposed and vulnerable to the risk of introducing new pathogens, whose presence has increased due to trade and climate change. consider how viruses, fungi and insects are attacking our earth's finest, one of them: the production of chestnuts has been cut down by the cynipids, a chinese tree-dweller parasite, causing over 200 million dollars in damage. this measure requires an update of phytosanitary certificates for extra-eu trade and plant passports in intra-eu trade. in conjunction with this, an electronic system shall be set up for the notification of information and for determining the nature for which a harmful organism is classified for quarantine in order to facilitate rapid protection against pathogens. i therefore renew the mandate to the commission to identify the organisms for which priority intervention obligations must necessarily be laid down and, at the same time, to draw up a list of plants and products at high risk for which special measures must be laid down.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the introduction of the procedure for suspending the import of plants considered to be dangerous. the requirement of a phytosanitary certificate for the transport of plants in baggage for both importers and consumers, and the extension of the 'plant passport' system for movements of plants for planting within the eu, strengthen and modernise the control mechanisms for plant diseases, which are particularly important for european countries most at risk of introducing new pathogens.
in writing. ‒ with this legislative resolution, parliament endorses the council's position with a view to adopting the regulation on protective measures against organisms harmful to plants. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the safeguarding of the agricultural and forestry sectors is a top priority for the eu economy and for the health of its citizens. the environmental damage and economic loss to farmers caused by the xylella parasite to olive groves in the southern member states must not be repeated. the regulation takes account of the rapid spread of pests and diseases across national borders and makes important improvements to the existing legislative framework. the current european objectives are: prevent the entry of organisms harmful to plants into the eu, eliminate them where they are already present and prevent the spread of any outbreaks. among the measures planned to achieve the identified objectives, improved protection for products to be imported, clearer rules for protected areas and the harmonisation of plant passports at european level were identified.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the proposal for a new regulation on protective measures against plant pests and harmful organisms. the safety of the eu plant health regime is essential for the safeguarding of the agricultural economy, but also for the health of the population. this requires more organised and stringent controls, a framework of prevention and rules that are secure for our safety and traceability of plant movements in the eu that can also deal with the new frontiers of online business. i particularly welcome the idea of the plant passport, to ensure full monitoring, especially of potentially dangerous imports from third countries into the union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the council position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on protective measures against organisms harmful to plants, amending regulations (eu) no 228/2013, (eu) no 652/2014 and (eu) no 1143/2014 of the european parliament and of the council and repealing council directives 69/464/eec, 74/647/eec, 93/85/eec, 98/57/ec, 2000/29/ec, 2006/91/ec and 2007/33/ec, because i think it is important to give final approval to the reform of eu plant protection legislation. as the xylella case has shown, the current eu legislation is inadequate to ensure the protection of plant organisms from harmful organisms, due to several shortcomings such as import controls, standard emergency interventions not related to the specific characteristics of the territories and organisms concerned, lack of compensatory measures, delays in the implementation of good agricultural practices. interinstitutional negotiations have led to some good compromises, such as the removal of the 10% limit for the quarantine of pesticides and the introduction of a precautionary approach to imports, and the requirement for importers to show a phytosanitary certificate. i hope therefore that the new legislation will be adopted quickly.
in writing. ‒ if up to a few years ago the plant health aspects of agriculture were the business of the insiders, today things have changed a lot. cases such as that of xylella in puglia and that of tristeza in sicily today are shining a spotlight on a problem, that of plant infection, which is causing enormous damage to an agricultural sector already in serious crisis. this regulation certainly improves the alert system: improved surveillance and early eradication of new outbreaks, as well as modernisation of trade tools are important measures. but more must be done. both ex ante and ex post. ex ante controls on products coming from third countries must be much stricter and the commission must be prompt in the case of interceptions of infested products, the 'precautionary principle' must be strengthened. today, for example, trade associations are alerting us to the citrus black spot and we must act immediately. ex post, when it is unfortunately necessary to plant and replant, farmers must be given adequate support through direct aid without demanding everything from the rdps. the european union is perhaps excessively exposed to the entry of goods from third countries and this has very heavy repercussions, especially on our agriculture.
in writing. in recent years we have seen the entry from third countries of pathogens of various kinds that have attacked crops, plantations and ornamental plants, with a daily record of ordinary devastation in terms of crop loss and economic damage. this vote is a major achievement for europe as the risk of invasion by pathogens from third countries remains high. in recent years we have seen the destruction of part of our production and ornamental heritage, due to lax controls and the failure to block imports when necessary. it is time for a change of course and i am sure that only by more serious analysis of the plant material entering the eu can we prevent further cases of invasion. the 'plant passport', an important new feature of the regulation, will ensure that plant material entering the eu is free from pathogens and will therefore considerably reduce the risk of importing harmful organisms from third countries. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat the spread of the disease. today's vote is a victory for our agriculture.

in writing. ‒ trans fatty acids (tfa) are a type of unsaturated fat found in ruminant foods and industrially produced partially hydrogenated vegetable oils. according to various studies, their consumption can increase the risk of cardiovascular disease, infertility, alzheimer's disease, diabetes, and obesity. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution tabled today in parliament because i believe that, in the light of the data presented, it is a priority to limit the use of fatty acids, following the example of denmark, which has already acted in this direction since 2003 with positive results and a considerable reduction in deaths from cardiovascular diseases. tfa are used in cheaper food with the consequence that people with lower socioeconomic status are found to be more exposed to their consumption and therefore more exposed to a risk that widen health inequalities. the resolution calls on the commission to introduce new eu rules to limit the content of industrial tfas in products, preferably within two years.

in writing. ‒ trans fatty acids (tfa) are found in many industrially produced foods to ensure a longer shelf life. they represent a real risk to human health; it has long been scientifically proven that the consumption of these hydrogenated fats is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, one of the main causes of mortality in the european union. this is all the more alarming when you consider that the people most likely to consume foods high in tfa are mostly younger and lower-income citizens. i therefore support the call on the commission in the report voted today to introduce a legislative framework which substantially reduces the amount of tfa in foodstuffs from industrial production in order to protect consumers from the risks of excessive intake. the european union must therefore act on two fronts: firstly, to protect the health of its citizens by encouraging them to make healthier and more informed food choices, and secondly, to facilitate the transition of the food industry by encouraging the health-reformulation of products that now contain tfa.

in writing. ‒ trans fats (also called hydrogenated fats) are those fats that have undergone the hydrogenation process, so that our body perceives them as saturated. these fats, used in many confections such as sweets and ice cream, greatly increase the risk of cardiovascular disease and should be eliminated from the diet altogether. the aim is therefore to identify a harmonised approach at eu level to counterfeiting; i agree with the end and the means chosen and i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the measure as it concerns unsaturated fatty acids of industrial production, maintaining the axiom that healthy fats contribute to the proper functioning of our organism. frequent consumption of trans fats, on the other hand, is associated with increased cardiovascular disease, infertility, diabetes and obesity, and a harmonised approach at european level is urgently needed. in fact, a patchwork of national regulations would not only have different impacts on the health of citizens, but would also create distortions in the internal market and obstacles to innovation in the food industry. in the light of these realities, the commission must introduce a legal limit as soon as possible, also assessing the costs of industrial reformulations that companies in the sector would have to face. limiting tfa can bring rapid and significant health benefits as can be seen from the example of denmark, which introduced a national limit of 2% in oils and fats in 2003 and has seen a significant decrease in deaths from cardiovascular disease. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it recognises the risks posed by trans fats (tfa) to human health and highlights the need for a uniform legislative framework at european level to reduce the average intake of tfa. at present there are no european provisions on the content of tfa in food and the obligation to label foodstuffs accordingly. some member states, such as denmark, have adopted a restrictive regulatory regime (national limit of 2% on the trans fat content of oils and fats), while most other member states have opted for voluntary measures. not only do tfa cause cardiovascular disease, but they are also more prevalent in cheaper food products, exposing lower-income citizens to excessive consumption of harmful foods. in addition, consumers under current eu rules may have difficulty understanding the difference between hydrogenated oils (which do not contain tfa but only saturated fatty acids) and partially hydrogenated oils. i therefore support the call on the commission to work with the member states to improve nutritional literacy and to introduce an eu legal limit on the content of industrial tfas in all food products.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on eu-wide limits on trans fats in food because i believe that the european union should impose binding limits on the amounts of industrially produced trans fatty acids (tfa) in food as these can increase the risk of cardiovascular disease, infertility, alzheimer's disease, diabetes and consumer obesity. the resolution stresses the lack of information among consumers, with only one in three consumers being adequately informed about tfa, according to ec figures, reflecting the lack of clarity in labelling. the ep therefore calls on the commission to introduce binding european standards to limit the content of industrial tfas within the next two years. denmark already set a national limit of 2% in 2003, and other member states have followed suit. these are good practices which other member states should follow, but the matter can only be regulated efficiently by establishing common rules at european level. i therefore hope that the next ec legislative proposal will be clear and compelling.
in writing. trans fatty acids (tfa) are unsaturated fats that can be found in food from ruminants and in industrially produced partially hydrogenated vegetable oils. unfortunately, high consumption of these fats is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, diabetes, obesity, infertility and alzheimer's disease, and they are more frequently used in cheaper foods, putting consumers from lower socioeconomic status at greater risk of these diseases. denmark was the first member state to implement a national plan regulating the use of tfas, which has had positive results in reducing deaths from cardiovascular disease. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of genetically modified organisms (gmos) and the use of genetically modified organisms (gmos) in food. citizens are often exposed to unhealthy food and as chairman of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, i believe it is the duty of the institutions to ensure that this is regulated. for these reasons, i have decided to support the motion for a resolution on trans fats.
in writing. ‒ given that trans fats are a particular type of unsaturated fat and that a high intake of trans fats increases the risk of developing coronary heart disease, and taking into account the who recommendations on the consumption of trans fats, i believe that efforts at european level to limit the intake of industrial trans fats should be intensified. i am also convinced that it is up to the eu to take appropriate decisions to regulate this sector and therefore i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ it is scientifically proven that the intake of trans fats increases the risk of cardiovascular disease, obesity and diabetes. it is almost superfluous to mention that these types of noncommunicable diseases are the leading cause of death in the world. yet, trans fats are found in industrially produced partially hydrogenated oils used in biscuits, cakes, popcorn, crackers, margarine, and many other supermarket products. all foods, you know, that are eaten mostly by children. we should bear in mind that the who has reported that in the eu 1 in 3 children aged between 6 and 9 are obese and that about 7% of european health expenditure is spent on the treatment of obesity-related diseases such as diabetes, high blood pressure, cardiovascular diseases. in this resolution we call on the commission to introduce a legal limit on the trans fat content to reduce the intake of trans fats by eu citizens. i therefore voted in favour of both the final text and our amendment, which unfortunately did not pass, which called for ensuring that policies to limit the tfa content of processed food do not encourage food producers to increase the amount of palm oil in these products.
in writing. ‒ consumption of industrially produced trans fats (tfa) has been associated with an increased risk of several diseases, such as infertility, alzheimer's disease, diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular disease. unfortunately, the labelling measures currently planned have not led to a decrease in the consumption of foods containing these substances, since according to some studies, only one in three consumers in the eu are aware of them. it is therefore important that the commission submit a proposal on trans fat limits, accompanied by an impact assessment examining the costs and benefits of industrial production, especially for small and mediumsized enterprises. i therefore decided to vote in favour of the motion for a resolution.
in writing. trans fats (also called hydrogenated fats, abbreviated tfa) are fats that have undergone the process of hydrogenation, that is, the addition of hydrogen to the carbon double bonds of unsaturated acids. while saturated fats in moderate amounts are essential for our bodies, trans fats should be eliminated from the diet altogether. in fact, the intake of these fats is associated with a significantly increased risk of cardiovascular disease, infertility, alzheimer's disease, diabetes, and obesity. tfas are used in a wide range of industrial preparations such as confectionery and ice cream and are more commonly used in cheaper food, with the consequence that people with lower socioeconomic status are more exposed to the intake of tfas. in this resolution, which i voted in favour of, we call on the commission to impose binding limits on the amounts of industrially produced trans fats (tfa) in food. to date, strategies to reduce tfa have been affected by the lack of a harmonised approach at eu level and individual actions by member states could have different health effects from one member state to another. health must be a protected and equal right for all european citizens.

associations, but also as a concrete expression of those values which europe desperately needs, those of voluntary commitment to others, solidarity, friendship, intercultural and interreligious dialogue and active citizenship. we know that there are at least 100 million volunteers in europe today, of all ages and social and personal backgrounds, engaged in humanitarian, educational, educational, cultural, environmental and sporting activities. we know that in every disaster, humanitarian crisis, emergency, like the ones we are experiencing in europe and on our borders, the precious work of volunteers from non-profit associations and non-governmental organizations supports and often anticipates that of the institutions. we know that free community volunteering not only creates inclusion, social cohesion, but also innovation, citizenship skills, creates wealth. it is estimated to contribute to 5% of the union's gdp. the european voluntary service within erasmus+ sees no coordinated policy, there is still no point of contact, no information within the eu. we ask the commission to compare national legal frameworks, to draw up a european legal framework defining the status of volunteers, with rights and duties, which facilitates mobility, the recognition of skills acquired also in the framework of europass, also promoting volunteering in the member states and in academic education systems. we also ask the commission to address the recommendations of the political agenda for volunteering and the european volunteers' charter to those member states which have not yet legislated on the subject by establishing national volunteering plans. it is also urgent that in the new financial regulation the commission should recognise as part-financing in european projects the contribution of activities by volunteers, even if they are provided free of charge. but we must create the conditions necessary for the volunteering experience to become a shared and accessible experience for everyone, of all ages and personal circumstances, everywhere. the reconciliation of work and volunteering must therefore be possible and associations and centres of volunteering services must also be supported, with an appropriate legal and financial framework, for the essential actions: mentoring, training and organisation of volunteers. it is also essential that the experience gained abroad by volunteers can become an opportunity for growth for the local and national community. i was in rome for a meeting with volunteers who had this experience and one of the experiences that struck me most was that of disabled young people who had volunteered "themselves" and who asked to be understood more and more in the service. finally, commissioner navracsics, they return from international, european experiences, because this enriches local communities, creates bridges and not walls and constitutes a practical experience of european and world citizenship.
the economic crisis, the sovereign debt crisis and the prevalence of a single liberal, neoliberal mindset have in recent years pushed many european states towards gradual cuts in public services and large-scale privatisation. this solution is proving more and more unsuccessful from an ethical, economic, social and political point of view, creating a poorer, more unjust europe and fuelling a european legislation, and above all there are no adequate funds to develop this phenomenon. there are great difficulties in cross-border volunteering. you have to invest in this. we must remember that member of the commission. – madam president, let me first thank ms costa for raising this issue in this parliament. it gives us a very good opportunity to discuss all the important aspects of volunteering. there is a growing awareness now of the importance of volunteering. the long list of discontent demonstrates this fact and i think this discussion was a very fruitful and useful discussion for us. when developing the concept and the scheme of the european voluntary service we can put all your remarks into the further drafts of the european voluntary service schemes. let me emphasise one thing. volunteering is not an ideological issue for me and i think this has been well demonstrated by the fact that we have a lot of supportive remarks from all the political groups in parliament. this again demonstrates that this is a consensual issue and we have to do more in developing volunteering at local level, regional level, national level, and also at the european level. what is the fundamental mission of the european voluntary service? it is not building up a homogeneous european voluntary scheme. it is about help, it is about solidarity, and it is about charity. the fundamental mission of the european voluntary service is to help local initiatives and we do exactly that. we have a lot of projects which help local stakeholders, ngos, local activists in implementing their own initiatives and we help young people to be mobile. we support mobility schemes to acquire skills and to acquire knowledge in each other’s member states. the second, and probably the most important, aspect of volunteering is acquiring skills, and that could be very important in tackling youth unemployment. that is why, when we review the european qualifications framework, we will put volunteering skills into the european qualifications framework and acknowledge those skills which could be acquired during volunteering. i think this is quite important because it can help us to promote social cohesion, to give one more chance to those people who have a different social background and probably cannot simply enter the labour market, but by volunteering they can acquire those very important skills which can help them to get better job opportunities. last, but not least, we are aware of the fact that the european voluntary service concentrates mostly on young people but, as i just mentioned in my introductory remarks, we are working on broadening the scope and giving the opportunity for older people to be included in our schemes and giving them the opportunity to work as volunteers in the framework of the european voluntary service.
in writing. today we are celebrating 20 years of the european voluntary service. this ambitious programme, which started as a pilot project in 1996, has so far involved as many as 100,000 young people who have chosen to invest their energy and time in solidarity projects free of charge. the young people who choose them, with a time commitment of 2 weeks to 12 months, receive financial support to cover the costs of transport, food and accommodation, as well as medical insurance, motivated by the deep desire to devote themselves to the other, to those in need, to those who have less. supporting such mobility is not only important to enable those who wish to do so, regardless of economic conditions, to volunteer, but is also a way in which the european union can help rediscover its deepest civic and human vocation. at this time of crisis of values, it is of paramount importance to invest in youth integration and mobility projects and to promote the exchange of best practices between member states. in this way, as pope francis has said, europe can rediscover its unity, rediscover itself and overcome the barriers and walls that divide it.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament has proposed postponing the discharge for the council for the eighth consecutive year. the main reason for the referral is that the council's expenditure is not subject to the same control procedures as those applied to the other institutions. the council does not communicate the annual report on expenditure to parliament, which undermines transparency for the public. i think that is unfair and undemocratic and i have therefore decided to vote in favour of not granting discharge.
in writing. ‒ the budget discharge procedure is an important moment in the institutional life of the european union. the european parliament, the only institution elected by universal suffrage, decides on the recommendation of the council whether or not to grant final approval for the implementation of the budget for a given financial year. this is a crucial step which also provides an opportunity to address specific recommendations to the institutions and agencies which make up the structure of the union. following the instructions of the committee on budgetary control (cont), i have today decided to vote in favour of the czarnecki report on the postponement of the discharge for the 2014 budget for the council and the european council. for years parliament has been asking the council for full figures on the implementation of the budget, but has received little cooperation from this institution. in view of the lack of transparency regarding budgetary and accounting data, parliament decided to refuse to grant the secretary-general of the council discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european council and of the council for the financial year 2014.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament decided, by 633 votes to 10, with no abstentions, to postpone the granting of a discharge to the secretary-general of the council in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european council and of the council for the financial year 2014. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the european parliament's budget for the financial year 2007 is based on the principle of the budgetary principle of the budgetary principle. this is unacceptable and undermines the reputation of the eu institutions. they call on the council to provide the necessary information and to adopt a code of conduct as soon as possible in order to ensure the integrity of the institution. they also call on the commission to participate in the eu transparency register and to develop detailed guidelines for the fight against corruption. they stress that effective budgetary control requires cooperation between parliament and the council. parliament also recalled that transparency and control of public accounts are general democratic principles which the union cannot derogate from and that the discharge procedure is part of the concept of representative democracy. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european parliament and the council.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report today because i believe that effective budgetary control requires cooperation between parliament and the council, as stated in the resolution of 28 april 2016. however, parliament is not yet in a position to take an informed decision on granting discharge. article 335 tfeu states that 'the union shall be represented by each of the institutions, in accordance with their administrative autonomy, in matters relating to the functioning of the respective institution' and that, consequently, taking into account article 55 of regulation (eu, euratom) no 966/2012 (the 'financial regulation'), the institutions are individually responsible for the implementation of their budgets. the council continues to take no position on the observations made by parliament in its discharge resolution of 28 april 2016 on the trend of the previous years towards an increase in under-utilisation and carry-overs of commitments. both the european council and the council do not send their annual activity reports to parliament, and this is certainly damaging to the reputation of the eu institutions. moreover, contrary to what parliament has recommended in its recent discharge resolutions, the budgets of the european council and the council have not yet been separated.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament proposed, in the first instance, to postpone the discharge to the council. the question now is whether or not to vote for the final discharge. the report by mr czarnecki confirms that parliament is not in a position to take an informed decision on granting discharge and therefore calls for no discharge to be given to the council: it is important to remember that the european parliament's refusal to grant discharge is politically significant but unfortunately has no legal consequences. i voted yes.

in writing. ‒ parliament gives discharge to the executive director of the ecsel joint undertaking (formerly the eniac joint undertaking and the artemis joint undertaking) in respect of the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2014 and approves the closure of the accounts of the eniac joint undertaking for the financial year 2014. acknowledges that the joint undertaking's accounts for the period from 1 january to 26 june 2014 present fairly the financial position of the joint undertaking, as well as the results of its operations and cash flows; parliament is concerned, however, that the court of auditors has delivered a strong opinion on the legality and regularity of the transactions on which the accounts are based, as the administrative agreements concluded with the national funding authorities (nfas) do not contain practical arrangements for carrying out ex post audits. parliament noted that it was not possible to draw any conclusions on the effective functioning of the ex post audits and called on ecsel to provide reasonable assurances as to the legality and regularity of the operations, deplored the lack of information available on contributions in kind and cash contributions and called on the court to include in its future reports specific provisions on the evaluation procedure and the level of contributions in kind and cash.
in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the report on the discharge for the implementation of the budget of the eniac joint undertaking for the financial year 2014, as the accounts of the joint undertaking for the reference period faithfully present the financial position of the joint undertaking as at 26 june 2014. the accounts shall be audited by the court of auditors in accordance with the principles laid down in the financial regulation. however, the court's report shows that the joint undertaking did not assess the quality of the audit reports submitted by the national funding authorities concerning the costs of the completed projects. due to the different methodologies used by the nfa, it was not possible to draw conclusions on the effectiveness of the functioning of the ex post audits. these did not allow the joint undertaking to calculate a weighted error rate or a residual error rate. according to the court's report, the final budget of the eniac joint undertaking for the financial year 2014 comprises commitment appropriations of eur 2 356 000 and payment appropriations of eur 76 500 250.
in writing. ‒ the court of auditors, in its report on the annual accounts of the joint undertaking for the period 1 january to 26 june 2014, gave for the fourth consecutive year a noteworthy opinion on the legality and regularity of the transactions underlying the accounts. furthermore, following an evaluation of the audit strategies of three national funding authorities, it was not possible to draw conclusions on the effective functioning of the ex post audits due to the different methodologies used. these shortcomings led to the non-discharge in the first instance: as the eniac joint undertaking and the artemis joint undertaking were merged in 2014 to create the joint technology initiative 'electronic components and systems for european leadership' (itc ecsel), these shortcomings cannot be addressed in any way (in fact eniac no longer exists). for this reason, while supporting the content of the resolution under consideration, we voted together with the m5s delegation against the granting of discharge.
in writing. ‒ i give discharge to the executive director of the eniac joint undertaking in respect of the implementation of the budget, given the importance of the implementation of a joint technology initiative (jti) on nanoelectronics. it is a research programme aimed at enhancing the integration and miniaturization of devices and consequently increasing their functionality. eniac is therefore a public-private partnership, bringing together the european commission and the european states and the states associated with aeneas, the association representing research and development players in the field of nanoelectronics (corporations, smes, research institutes and universities) in europe. the eu must be a leader in cutting-edge manufacturing in a globalised world where the volumes produced by emerging countries seem to leave european firms no room for competition. the 2014 budget of eniac provided for commitment appropriations of eur 2 356 000 and payment appropriations of eur 76 500 250, in line with the forecasts, but i am concerned about the strong assessment of the court of auditors in its report on the legality and regularity of eniac's operations. i therefore hope that clarifications will be provided as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the discharge for the implementation of the budget of the eniac joint undertaking for the financial year 2014. in view of the positive opinion of the court of auditors and in the absence of serious irregularities and errors, i considered it appropriate to approve the document in question.
in writing. ‒ eniac is a very important player in promoting public-private investment in nano-electric technologies in europe. in particular, synergistic coordination between resources, eu framework programme and national r & d funds, and universities, private and local authorities, is needed in a key area of innovation in europe. this report supports the legitimacy of the statements concerning the results of operations and cash flows for the period considered. it is also emphasised that the national procedures concerning the legality and regularity of the transactions are defined as a reasonable assurance under the joint undertaking. i therefore vote in favour of this text, and i appreciate the legitimacy and regularity of the discharge operations carried out by eniac.

in writing. ‒ the budget discharge procedure is an important moment in the institutional life of the european union. the european parliament, the only institution elected by universal suffrage, decides on the recommendation of the council whether or not to grant final approval for the implementation of the budget for a given financial year. this is a crucial step which also provides an opportunity to address specific recommendations to the institutions and agencies which make up the structure of the union. following the instructions of the committee on budgetary control (cont), i have today decided to vote in favour of the marinescu report giving discharge to the executive director of the ecsel joint undertaking (formerly the eniac joint undertaking and the artemis joint undertaking) in respect of the implementation of the joint undertaking's budget for the financial year 2014.

in writing. ‒ parliament gives discharge to the executive director of the ecsel joint undertaking (formerly the artemis joint undertaking and the eniac joint undertaking) in respect of the implementation of the budget of the artemis joint undertaking for the financial year 2014 and approves the closure of its accounts for the financial year 2014. acknowledges from the joint undertaking that the accounts of the joint undertaking for the period 1 january to 26 june 2014 present fairly the financial position of the joint undertaking; is concerned, however, that the court of auditors has given a strong opinion on the legality and regularity of the transactions underlying the accounts, as the administrative agreements concluded with the national funding authorities (nfas) do not contain practical arrangements for the carrying out of ex post audits. parliament called on the joint undertaking to provide evidence that the implementation of the national procedures provides a reasonable assurance as to the legality and regularity of the transactions and noted that the joint undertaking had not taken any measures with regard to certain internal control rules relating to information and financial reporting, noting that this was however due to the merger between eniac and artemis and that in the meantime the ecsel itc had made considerable progress.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report today because the court of auditors' report on the annual accounts of the artemis joint undertaking for the period 1 january to 26 june 2014 shows that the accounts and the related transactions attributable to the joint undertaking are reliable. the artemis joint undertaking was established in december 2007 for a period of 10 years to define and implement a research agenda for the development of key technologies for embedded information systems in various fields of application. the maximum union contribution to the joint undertaking for the whole decade is eur 420 000 000, to be charged to the budget of the seventh framework programme for research. the financial contributions of the artemis member states should instead be at least 1,8 times the union's financial contribution, while the in-kind contributions of the research and development organisations participating in the projects for the duration of the joint undertaking should be equal to or higher than the contribution of the public entities.
in writing. ‒ the court of auditors, in its report on the joint undertaking's annual accounts, had expressed a strong opinion on the legality and regularity of the transactions on which the accounts are based, as the administrative agreements concluded with the national funding authorities regarding the audit of the declarations of expenditure for projects did not contain practical arrangements for carrying out ex post audits: it was therefore not possible to draw conclusions on the effective functioning of the ex post audits due to the different methodologies used, which did not allow the joint undertaking to calculate a weighted error rate or a residual error rate. the joint undertaking had also failed to take any action on certain internal control rules relating to financial information and disclosure. these shortcomings led to the non-discharge in the first instance: the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 290 concerning the establishment of the european data protection supervisor, the appointment of the european data protection supervisor and the appointment of the european data protection supervisor. for this reason, while supporting the content of the resolution, we voted together with the m5s delegation against the granting of discharge.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of granting discharge for the 2014 budget of the artemis joint undertaking, and with this vote i want to reiterate my full openness to joint technological initiatives, i.e. modern mechanisms for the execution of research programmes under the seventh framework programme of the european union. these are examples of long-term public-private partnerships implemented as joint ventures on the basis of article 171 of the ec treaty, which states that 'the community may set up joint ventures or any other structure necessary for the better execution of research and technological development programmes'. i therefore approve the closure of the artemis accounts despite the strong opinion expressed in the court of auditors' report on the legality and regularity of the operations, to which must be added the inadequate quality of the audit reports received from the national financing authorities (afn) concerning the costs of the completed projects. i am also sorry that there are no internal control rules for financial information and reporting on the valuation of assets, no sound internal control system and no clear structure for internal audit itself. in any case, it is an ambitious project that will define a common strategic research agenda capable of attracting investment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the artemis joint undertaking for the financial year 2014, following the opinions of the court of auditors on the reliability of the accounts for the year 2014 and on the legality and regularity of the transactions, which certified the correctness of the expenditure incurred and recorded by artemis.
in writing. ‒ the artemis landfill has lights and shadows which are important to highlight. on the one hand, parliament expressed concern that the joint undertaking had not adopted measures concerning certain rules on information and financial reporting, the evaluation of activities and internal control and audit systems. part of these problems have been addressed by ecsel, which was created by the merger of eniac and artemis, and which has made progress on internal control systems and the establishment of an internal audit structure. on the other hand, it is emphasised that the data on the effectiveness of the guarantee systems are good with regard to the ex post audit strategy. i therefore vote in favour of this text, welcoming the progress made in national procedures but expressing the same concerns as the discharge with regard to internal control.

in writing. ‒ parliament gives discharge to the director of the european joint undertaking for iter and the development of fusion energy in respect of the implementation of the joint undertaking's budget for the financial year 2014 and approves the closure of the accounts of the joint undertaking for the financial year 2014. the joint undertaking's annual accounts present fairly the financial position of the joint undertaking as at 31 december 2014, as well as the results of its operations and cash flows. parliament noted that the new director-general of the iter organisation had presented to the iter council an action plan containing specific measures to overcome the main obstacles to the development of the iter project and noted that the new acting director had drawn up an action plan for the joint undertaking which was broadly in line with that of the iter organisation. the joint undertaking's management board has given its full approval to this action plan and since march 2015 the iter organisation and the joint undertaking have been implementing and closely following the action plans and therefore invites the joint undertaking to report on the implementation of these action plans.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today because the report drawn up by the court of auditors shows that the joint undertaking's annual accounts for the financial year 2014 present the financial position of the joint undertaking correctly as at 31 december 2014. the final financial envelope available for 2014 comprises commitment appropriations of eur 1 168 800 000 and payment appropriations equivalent to eur 567 600 000. the utilization rates for commitment and payment appropriations are 100 and 88.5% respectively. it is also noted that the implementation rate for the payment appropriations entered in the initial budget for 2014 is 73%. the conclusions of the iter council of 15 and 16 june 2016 confirmed that the iter project is moving in the right direction, allowing for a valid and realistic proposal to be made regarding the timing and associated costs. the updated integrated calendar for the iter project, which sets the date for the first plasma in september 2025, was also approved. so far all the project stages have been completed on time, if not ahead of schedule.
in writing. ‒ in 2014, the joint undertaking's internal audit function had carried out a review of the monitoring of the execution of the contracts, highlighting the existence of important risk factors such as unrealistic timing of projects and delays in the implementation of activities. the company had difficulty effectively limiting some of these risks, as they were attributable to the now changed iter organisation. finally, the review identified the need for more robust controls and process changes, in particular with regard to management and change control, financial management of contracts and the management of non-compliance situations. i voted with the m5s delegation against the granting of the discharge.
