madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would just like to say that i voted in favour of this resolution to express my closeness, above all to the iraqi people, to stress the right of displaced people to return to their lands and to have their rights recognized, thus protecting the chaldeans, the syrians, the assyrians and all the indigenous christian communities. two figures tell us how many christians in iraq have suffered prolonged discrimination: in 2003 alone, there were over 1.5 million, today the christian community is down to 200,000. they are truly sacrificial victims of conflict. of course, and i also strongly emphasize what the resolution says, to fight firmly against the further advance of the jihadist ideology of isis is certainly a precondition for pacifying the region and guaranteeing it a stable and prosperous future.
in writing. ‒ the situation in some regions of iraq, particularly in mosul, has reached a critical point. i firmly believe that the people in those areas have a right to live in better conditions and above all i believe that it is very important to give the displaced people a home and that this should be a priority for the iraqi government. however, i believe that the continued use of arms is aggravating the tragic conditions in which the people of those places are already forced to live, and i have therefore decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ mosul, iraq's second largest city, has always been a multiethnic reality where the sunni arab majority has lived peacefully alongside chaldeans, kurds, yazidis and turkmen. for two years now, it has been in the hands of daesh, which has imposed a climate of terror, persecution and violence in a vast area including the nineveh plain, tal afar and sinjar. the iraqi army has launched an operation to take the city and surrounding areas from the control of the terrorists, an action carried out jointly by the global coalition against isis, the peshmerga forces and the popular mobilization forces. the resolution adopted by parliament today, which i share, strongly supports this operation as a decisive step towards ending the reign of terror imposed by daesh. the text calls on regional and international actors not to obstruct military action and to act in full respect of iraqi sovereignty. after the liberation of mosul, the commitment must be to continue to fight to prevent the spread of islamist ideologies that act as theological and political incitement for the crimes perpetrated by isis.
in writing. ‒ the resolution analysing the situation in northern iraq and mosul is well structured and balanced. i share the condemnation of the genocide against the christian population and other minorities living in iraqi territory by isis. islamic terrorists must be fought and stopped as soon as possible. for all these reasons, i intend to support this text with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament supports the operation launched by iraq to liberate mosul from isis, seeing it as a decisive element in the global effort to defeat isis permanently. it reiterates its full support for the independence, territorial integrity and sovereignty of iraq and calls for these to be fully respected; it also called on the iraqi authorities to take concrete measures to protect civilians and prevent human rights violations. it also called on the parties to the conflict to respect international humanitarian law and urged them to open humanitarian corridors to allow civilians to escape. it called on the eu, the un and the international community to work with iraq's national and regional governments to facilitate the reintegration of iraqis and all ethnic and religious minorities who have been displaced. it stresses the absolute importance of ensuring security in a timely and effective manner and restoring the rule of law and basic services, as failure to provide them could result in the re-emergence of extremist forces. it also stresses the need to continue to combat the spread of islamist-jihadi ideologies, including salafi jihadism which acts as theological and political incitement to the crimes perpetrated by isis.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the statement by the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy on the situation in northern iraq/mosul, because it is necessary for europe and the international community to work first and foremost for the protection of civilians, who are today 'trapped in mosul and in nearby villages and exposed to the combat zones. secondly, we must ensure that aid and humanitarian assistance reach the inhabitants of the nineveh plain. fortunately, the offensive against the daesh jihadists in mosul, northern iraq, seems to be making progress. it is a question of freeing a city of 1.3 million people, men, women and children, who are still living in terrible conditions under the yoke of the jihadists, from a ruthless occupation. every effort must be made to avert a humanitarian catastrophe.
in writing. ‒ our role as europe's humanitarian champions is not enough if it is not accompanied by a clear vision of the fate of the liberated territories. we support the creation through an inclusive process of new autonomous provinces for the nineveh plain, tal afar, sinjar and wherever else it is necessary to ensure security and democracy for minorities in their ancestral territories. we will not allow the ashes and oil of mosul to be the object of a shameful bargain at the expense of its citizens, because mosul will eventually fall, and i believe it will soon, but it could have fallen long ago if the discord and the conflicting selfishness had not entered the minds of the powers involved. recent history teaches us that in iraq the difficulty is not winning the war, the difficulty is certainly not losing the peace. i chose to abstain on the final vote.
in writing. ‒ i take this opportunity not only to express my support for the joint resolution, but also to express my closeness to the iraqi army which, with the support of the global coalition against daesh, the peshmerga forces of the kurdish regional government and the popular mobilization forces, has launched an operation to remove mosul, and numerous towns and villages along the "mosul corridor", from isis control. in recent weeks we have witnessed with horror the atrocious suffering and mass executions that the inhabitants of the region have been subjected to constantly for years by isis, not to mention the one and a half million people at imminent risk of displacement due to the ongoing operations. we can only hope that the civilians will be guaranteed continued protection through alternative routes or humanitarian cordon, and that the rule of law and basic services such as health care, electricity and education will be restored in the liberated areas. it is well known that failure to provide services, security, a long-term strategy to combat root causes and efforts to promote social cohesion lead to the rise of extremist forces.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure as it strongly supports the operation launched by iraq to liberate mosul from isis/daesh and identifies this operation as a decisive element of the global effort currently underway to defeat isis/daesh permanently. the resolution also calls on the iraqi authorities to take concrete measures to protect civilians during operations, by exercising effective command and control over the militias and by taking all possible precautions to avoid civilian casualties and human rights violations during the offensive. the european union also strongly condemns the violence and mass executions being carried out in iraq by daesh and expresses its deep concern at the continuing reports of daesh's use of children, the elderly, women and vulnerable people as shields against the military operations of liberation in northern iraq.
in writing. ‒ the iraqi army, with the support of the global anti-isis coalition, kurdish peshmerga forces and popular mobilization forces, has launched an operation to wrest mosul from isis control. i voted in favour of this resolution because it expresses support for the ongoing operations to wrest iraqi territory from daesh control and highlights the need to take concrete measures to protect civilians during the operations. indeed, at least 1.5 million civilians are at risk of a full-blown humanitarian catastrophe, and the concern that isis is using civilians as human shields is real, given what has already happened in manbji, falluja and sirte. the resolution also stresses that the indigenous communities of the nineveh plain, tal afar and sinjar, already suffering from significant internal displacement, have the right to protection, security and regional autonomy within the federal structure of the republic of iraq. i am convinced that respecting iraq's multiethnic reality during and after the anti-terrorist operations is the first step towards building the country's political, economic and social future.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the resolution which supports iraq's operation to liberate mosul from isis and condemns the real genocide against the christian minority and all other minorities in the territory that isis is committing.
in writing. ‒ i fully supported the joint resolution of the political groups on the situation in northern iraq, in particular the commitment of europe, the external action service and the entire international community to provide practical and diplomatic support for a sustainable and inclusive post-war settlement of the region. i think it is particularly important to work towards the indigenous peoples of the region being politically represented in an autonomous province, and this also to give a gesture of inclusion and attention to all the ethnic and religious minorities, who are still largely displaced in the country.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint resolution of the european parliament on the situation in northern iraq in the mosul area because i am appalled by the news coming from mosul, which shows us a terrible reality, where women and children are used as human shields and suffer all kinds of atrocities, including the use of chemical weapons. i hope that the iraqi forces, the kurdish army and the international coalition fighting daesh will succeed in liberating the city as soon as possible and in stopping these horrible war crimes, and that those responsible will be brought to justice and be held accountable in the international arena. these operations must be carried out as quickly as possible, avoiding civilian casualties and protecting the most vulnerable, women and children. i also share the report's call for a future of peace, freedom, religious and ethnic inclusion and mutual respect when the city is liberated from daesh. it is absolutely essential to avoid further religious tensions and vendettas and to establish a real civil coexistence between the various ethnic groups and religions inhabiting mosul. only then can we give the iraqi people, after so many years of war, the peace and freedom to which they are entitled.
in writing. ‒ the deterioration of the situation in iraq and the launch of military operations, which are complex but indispensable in our fight against the terrorist organisation daesh/isis, must be on the agenda of our european and national foreign policy agendas. and the focus on these issues is even more delicate when you consider the repercussions these operations could have on syria: if effective, within a matter of weeks, the military offensive in iraq will force the isis militias to abandon mosul and retreat into syria. i voted in favour of this resolution precisely to reiterate this concept and to express my full support for the report presented today and for the ultimate meaning of these events: the european union is committed to the peace process, to the restoration of international security and to the protection of civilians forced to flee their homes and their towns, to doing everything in our power to avert a humanitarian crisis and to be as prepared as possible to provide assistance to the iraqi people.
in writing. ‒ the iraqi army, with the support of the global coalition against isis/daesh, the peshmerga forces of the kurdish regional government and the popular mobilization forces, has started the operation to liberate mosul from isis control. i would like to say that i am in favour of the proposal, given that the necessary security conditions should be guaranteed for all those who have been forced to leave their homelands and that their safety should also be guaranteed.
in writing. ‒ the european union must offer its full support to the efforts of the iraqi-led coalition to liberate mosul and, at the same time, do everything possible to alleviate the humanitarian crisis affecting the local population, in particular ethnic and religious minorities. for centuries these communities have coexisted peacefully, in a general climate of pluralism and cooperation. the occupation by isis/daesh of the city of mosul and the provinces of nineveh, tal afar and sinjar has caused untold suffering to the inhabitants, victims of crimes against humanity and of genocide itself. the european union, which supports the anti-isis/daesh coalition and wants to see those responsible for these crimes brought to justice and punished, also calls on the iraqi authorities to take all necessary measures to protect civilians, especially women, the elderly and children, during the campaign. the eu's support will be crucial even after the recapture of mosul and the surrounding region. its expertise and financial resources will be indispensable in the reconstruction of an inclusive and sustainable iraq, guaranteeing participation and fundamental rights for every community and every citizen.
in writing. ‒ after the failed coup, the situation of journalists in turkey is critical. many of them have been arrested without any evidence of criminal activity. i believe that the detention of journalists for the content of their articles and the closure of a very large number of news outlets are dangerous threats to the democracy of a country. for these reasons i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ following the failed coup attempt on 15 july, the turkish government has arrested 99 journalists and writers, revoked the accreditation of 330 other journalists and closed the offices of more than 100 broadcasters, newspapers, periodicals, publishing houses and distribution companies. according to human rights watch, many of these lawsuits were pursued without any evidence of the accused's participation in the failed coup. the resolution adopted by parliament today, which i supported with my vote, strongly condemns the attempted coup and reiterates its full support for the legitimate turkish authorities. the text expresses deep concern, however, at the arbitrary detention of journalists, which cannot be interpreted as a legitimate response to military action and which constitutes a reality that undermines the principles of the rule of law. the free and pluralistic press is an essential component of democracy, as are due process, the presumption of innocence and the independence of the judiciary. turkey must commit to reducing the scope of the emergency measures, releasing journalists detained without conclusive evidence and facilitating impartial investigations into the events surrounding the failed coup.
in writing. ‒ the report rightly condemns the repression of journalists in turkey by the erdogan government, but it does not go further, it does not underline the fact that human rights violations in this country are on the agenda and are unacceptable. i believe that turkey is not in the least respectful of the eu's founding values and that the negotiations for accession to the union must be suspended immediately. i therefore could not support this text in its entirety and decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the situation regarding press freedom in turkey has deteriorated considerably over the last decade. the turkish government is abusing the state of emergency and the failed coup attempt of july 2016 to significantly curtail freedom of expression and media freedom. parliament noted that 89 journalists had been arrested without charge during the first months of the state of emergency. the turkish government had committed numerous and systematic violations of press freedom even before the failed coup attempt and the subsequent state of emergency. thousands of websites are currently blocked in turkey. however, violations of freedom of expression and media are not the only structural problem in turkey; the european union is also concerned about the treatment of minorities, the refusal to recognise the republic of cyprus and the ambiguity regarding terrorist groups in syria and iraq. parliament therefore calls on the turkish government to respect all the conditions of democracy and the rule of law and to put an end to any discrimination against citizens with regard to freedom of expression and other fundamental rights.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the statement by the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy on the situation of journalists in turkey because unfortunately the events of last july have worsened the situation with an even greater contraction of freedoms, in particular freedom of expression. reporters without borders reports that at least 110 journalists are in prison, 70 of them arrested after the coup. plus 150 whistleblowers on the loose. it must be clear that respect for rights and freedoms in practice remains vital for a country which aspires to join the european union. the european union must work to ensure that european standards of democracy are guaranteed in this country.
in writing. ‒ the real coup actually succeeded erdogan and journalists are paying a heavy price for it. the candidate of the five star movement for this year's sakharov prize, the journalist can dündar, editor of the cumhuriyet newspaper, and many others who have denounced over the years the murky involvement of the national intelligence services, for example in the arms trade in syria, are among those who are paying with prison for their freedom of thought. meanwhile, the statistics are growing, we get to 100,000 websites blocked, we get to a country that is now ranked 151 in freedom of the press, 183 newspapers closed, 127 journalists arrested. i would remind the european union and the commission that freedom of expression is a right and not a crime, but the very essence of democracy. and if we do not say this forcefully to the turkish government, we will lose all credibility. my vote was in favour.
in writing. ‒ the complex situation that turkey has been experiencing since this summer has shaken our parliamentary activity and by reading the newspapers every day, i am lucky to be able to witness one of the greatest freedoms for the human being: the expression. if we were to be deprived of it, my own role would probably be empty. many people may make statements that are far from our worldview, sometimes even indefensible, and yet the very right to make those statements is inalienable and must be preserved in its essence. i therefore express my support for the resolution and my total disgust at the repressive measures taken against turkish journalists. the commission has also been asked to provide information on the implementation of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. in parallel, it emerged that the turkish authorities had closed the offices of more than 100 broadcasters, newspapers, periodicals, publishing houses and distribution companies after the coup attempt. i believe the government should reduce the scope of the emergency measures to avoid undermining freedom of expression.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution because, following the attempted coup d'état in turkey last july, the european federation of journalists and the turkish journalists' association have denounced the numerous arrests of journalists, most of whom have not yet been charged, and the closure of many broadcasters, newspapers, periodicals and publishing houses. while condemning the attempted coup, the resolution calls on the government of turkey to reduce the scope of the emergency measures so that they can no longer be used to restrict freedom of expression, as a free and pluralistic press is an essential component of any democracy.
in writing. ‒ after the failed coup, president erdoğan has launched an operation to purge alleged infiltrators of the gülen movement from the turkish public administration and society. the mass arrest campaign has also involved media and journalists, who already enjoyed restricted freedom of expression before the coup. after the coup, the situation worsened with the closure of 102 news outlets, authorized by a decree of 27 july 2016, and the detention of 101 journalists as of 14 september 2016. i voted in favour of this resolution because it supports the efforts of the legitimate authorities of turkey in dealing with the coup attempt of 15 july 2016. at the same time, it reiterates that such efforts must not run counter to the rule of law, which implies the right to a fair trial for all journalists who have been prosecuted in the absence of any evidence of involvement in the failed coup attempt. while recognizing the enormous terrorist threat to turkey, i am convinced that neither the coup nor the legislation in force can be used to prevent journalists and the media from peacefully exercising their freedom of expression through disproportionate actions and emergency measures.

in writing. ‒ i strongly supported the european parliament's resolution on the situation of journalists in turkey because turkish journalists still work in difficult circumstances, subject to regular government censorship and intimidation. the eu strongly condemns the forced closure of many newspapers, radio and television stations in the aftermath of the failed coup and does not favour the ongoing accession negotiations. freedom of the press is a sign of democracy and justice, and the independence and respect for the rights of journalists are the guarantors of this freedom. the european parliament wishes to condemn in the strongest terms the intimidation of the media sector. i therefore share the deep concern about the deterioration of the situation regarding freedom of speech, expression and opinion in the country over the last two years. it is therefore crucial that the turkish government continue on the path of european integration and fully align itself with european values, principles and standards of freedom and democracy by immediately ending the mass arrests of journalists and releasing those in prison: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament.
in writing. ‒ today we are faced with a necessary and inevitable debate on the worrying state of one of the fundamental rights in a democracy, freedom of expression, in turkey, our indispensable partner for historical and strategic reasons. the immigration agreement is a reminder of the importance of turkey to europe and to the stabilisation action it plays at regional level. but that cannot prevent us from denouncing the attack on freedom of the press and information as a whole. since the failed coup last july, the crackdown on newspapers and news channels has been relentless and indiscriminate. the arrest of many, too many journalists has been in the international news for months now and will certainly not help the turkish regime to embark on the road to a transparent democracy. the current crackdown on the judiciary is a complacent way of closing ranks on journalists who still try to do their jobs independently. i am voting for this report with conviction because we europeans must have the courage to demand that this should end as soon as possible.
in writing. last july, turkey was the victim of a failed coup d'état which had serious repercussions on turkish society as a whole. as we know, hundreds of people have been killed and more than 2,100 injured. but some serious consequences have been suffered by journalists, of whom about 100 have been arrested and more than 300 have been deprived of accreditation. this is a violation of citizens' rights, which has also seen the closure of more than 100 broadcasters, newspapers, publishers and distribution companies. we condemn these acts and express our solidarity with the victims and their families, while making urgent recommendations to turkey. we therefore remind turkey, an important partner for the eu, of the importance of protecting human rights and the rule of law, and that freedom of expression and the media, and therefore a free press, are fundamental parts of a democratic society. we therefore call on turkey to reopen the media outlets that have been closed and to release the journalists and ensure that they are given a fair trial.

in writing. ‒ history teaches us that nuclear weapons have been the cause of tragic events that have destroyed the population of entire cities. today, in addition to the five powers which are members of the un security council, many states possess nuclear weapons, creating a situation of extreme danger for the member states of the european union. i believe that the world's great powers should commit themselves to seeking peace and security without nuclear weapons by promoting the elimination of nuclear weapons. for the reasons i have just described, i have decided to vote against.
in writing. ‒ the issue of nuclear security and non-proliferation has recently received renewed attention following the increase in international tensions and the tightening of relations between states possessing nuclear weapons. as of january 2016, nine states (the united states, russia, the united kingdom, france, china, india, pakistan, israel, and north korea) are found to possess about 15,395 nuclear weapons. the resolution adopted by parliament today, which i support, expresses deep concern at the deterioration of the security environment in the area surrounding the union, and beyond its neighbourhood, and at the role that nuclear weapons have again assumed in military doctrines. europe has a duty to strengthen disarmament and non-proliferation policies and international cooperation in the peaceful use of nuclear energy. the warhead states must reduce all types of nuclear weapons and become protagonists of a new un conference in 2017 that can negotiate a legally binding instrument to ban nuclear weapons.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament recognises the right of recognised nuclear weapon states to maintain their nuclear deterrent as an important element of national security. it supports the objectives of the npt in laying the foundations for global efforts to prevent the proliferation of nuclear weapons, to promote the safe and secure use of civil nuclear energy and to pursue the goal of a world without nuclear weapons. it also believes that the conditions for security and sustainable nuclear disarmament can only be achieved through a multilateral process. it therefore deplores the absence of russia from the 2016 nuclear security summit and encourages renewed efforts to promote cooperation with moscow. it supported the work of the international atomic energy agency in promoting cooperation in the nuclear field, in favour of the safe and peaceful use of nuclear technologies, and encouraged the continued promotion and strict implementation of the convention on the physical protection of nuclear material, urging those countries which had not yet ratified the convention to do so. it also called for increased cooperation efforts and effective action on the security of nuclear materials in order to minimise the risk of these products ending up in the hands of terrorist groups.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the statement on 'nuclear security and non-proliferation' by the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy, because nuclear disarmament is the most important objective of global arms control policies. the objective of a world without nuclear weapons should be the ultimate long-term ambition. unfortunately, there is concern about international stability following the deterioration of relations between nuclear-armed states such as the united states and russia. the european union is also concerned about the reappearance of the nuclear spectrum as a deterrent on europe's borders. the eu needs to work tirelessly to continue the disarmament agenda and to call for an ad hoc conference in 2017 to negotiate a 'legally binding' instrument to definitively ban the proliferation of nuclear weapons.
in writing. ‒ my strong support for this resolution is a convinced attempt to make the world a better place. on the other hand, if we believe that the spread of nuclear weapons is inevitable, then we are in some way admitting that the use of the same weapons will be inevitable. therefore, in the face of a global security that is faltering in every respect, given the emergence of risks of the most diverse and multifaceted nature, no further delay in the full implementation of non-proliferation is acceptable. the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and their means of delivery is a major concern for the international community, and it is particularly important to prevent terrorists from acquiring and using them. the early establishment of a nuclear-free zone in the middle east would therefore be essential to ensure a lasting and stable peace. i have high hopes for the full traceability and security of all nuclear material for military use and look forward to a large-scale participation in the 2017 united nations conference to negotiate legally binding instruments to prohibit nuclear weapons and enable their complete elimination.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure because, taking into account the deterioration of the overall security situation, particularly in the eu, the current scenario could lead to the re-emergence of nuclear weapons as an active deterrent and their possible proliferation between state and non-state actors. it is therefore necessary for all nuclear-weapon states to take concrete interim measures to reduce the risk of nuclear weapons exploding, moving towards a weakening of their operational status and moving from deployment to storage.
in writing. ‒ nuclear security and non-proliferation is an important issue on the european agenda, especially in the current context of european and global security, which has become more permeable to hybrid and unconventional threats. since its entry into force in 1970, the treaty on the non-proliferation of nuclear weapons (npt) has been the legal reference point for non-proliferation and disarmament at international level. through its three pillars - nuclear disarmament, non-proliferation and the peaceful uses of atomic energy - the treaty aims to prevent the proliferation of nuclear weapons and to promote cooperation between states on nuclear energy for civilian purposes. nuclear weapon states and signatories to the npt are modernizing and upgrading their nuclear weapons arsenals and delaying action to reduce or eliminate them and to disengage from a military doctrine of nuclear deterrence. in addition, russia's exercises in some eu states, such as poland, raise concerns about further nuclear rearmament. by voting in favour of this resolution, i intend to support the respect and full implementation of the npt and the inf treaty.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the european voluntary service. this is an important instrument which is celebrating its 20th anniversary and has supported over 100 000 volunteers during this period. a demonstration of solidarity and responsibility that has contributed to strengthening active citizenship, social inclusion, training and intercultural dialogue. the text adopted today calls for encouraging the participation of organisations in programmes involving volunteers by allowing volunteering to be counted as a co-financing contribution to member states' projects linked to the eu structural funds. the commission should improve the communication strategy by ensuring simplified access to information on european voluntary service opportunities; the new european solidarity corps initiative should be supported but its implementation should not jeopardise existing voluntary schemes and their funding. the creation of a genuine european voluntary service statute would be an important instrument for ensuring that voluntary organisations receive the right legal and institutional recognition.

in writing. ‒ the current refugee crisis is a clear symbol of the importance of volunteers and how they embody european values. the european parliament recognises that volunteering is an expression of solidarity, freedom and responsibility that contributes to the strengthening of active citizenship and personal human development and that it is an essential tool for social inclusion and cohesion, training, education and intercultural dialogue. it argues that a european framework for volunteering activities is necessary, as a legal framework defining the status of volunteers, indicating their rights and duties, and facilitating mobility and recognition of skills; the commission is also proposing that each member state should set up national voluntary service programmes with adequate resources. it supports the commission's idea of setting up the eu solidarity corps, a new european voluntary service initiative for young people. it also encourages member states to promote the european voluntary service in their education and academic systems. the committee also welcomed the commission's proposal to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european voluntary service.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the resolution in question, which calls for the coordination and harmonisation of european policies on volunteering. european voluntary service is one of the most visible expressions of solidarity and makes a significant contribution to the dissemination of european values. the report stresses in particular the importance of a european legal framework for volunteering activities which defines the status of volunteers, indicating their rights and duties, and which facilitates mobility and recognition of skills. in the meantime, it encourages member states that have not yet defined a legal framework for volunteers to make use of the recommendations contained in the political agenda for volunteering in europe and the european charter of the rights and responsibilities of volunteers. member states are invited to adopt the system developed by the ilo to measure the economic value of volunteering and to cooperate with eurostat in developing indicators and new measurement methods for the collection of comparative data.

in writing. ‒ the european voluntary service (evs), which is celebrating its 20th anniversary this year, enables young people aged 17-30 to go abroad and take part in volunteering projects. i consider volunteering to be a noble activity as an expression of solidarity which also contributes to strengthening active citizenship and promoting a culture of legality, and counters phenomena such as organised crime, social exclusion, poverty, intolerance, racism, xenophobia and injustice. in this respect, i thought i would vote in favour of the resolution because i believe that the commission should update the framework for volunteering programmes to take account of the development of new digital technologies and the humanitarian crises taking place inside and outside the union. in addition, the scope, fields of activity and objectives of the voluntary service should be extended, the programme should be extended to include third-country nationals and the age range for applying should be extended. finally, i think it would be appropriate for the commission to promote a european civil service initiative by highlighting the skills that can be acquired through experience.
in writing. ‒ europe is plagued by deep wounds: the economic crisis and high unemployment have led to a frightening increase in the number of people living in poverty and social exclusion, and uncontrolled migration flows are exposing them to all kinds of problems on a daily basis. where there is even the slightest trust in institutions, there is fortunately a resource to be counted on: the volunteer work. it draws its power from the essence of the human soul and has no remuneration because its value itself is priceless. i therefore vote in favour of the resolution, knowing that in these 20 years of european voluntary service it has been possible to promote active citizenship and profound personal development. in this context, it is essential to establish a european framework for voluntary activities, which defines their rights and obligations and facilitates their interaction between individual initiatives and programmes. the adoption of a european map would also make it possible to facilitate mobility between member states, depending on the emergency situations to be dealt with. together, we would achieve a recognition of skills, which is essential to be able to face adversity in the best way with a peaceful 'league' of ready intervention. i therefore believe that involvement from an early age to active ageing is essential: in fact, the best way to feel useful is to help others.

madam president, mr draghi, mr dombrovskis, ladies and gentlemen, with this report the european parliament expresses its support for the monetary policy action of the ecb, recognizing that the measures implemented are consistent with its mandate, with the objective of price stability and, therefore, with that of competing with the more general economic policy of the union. it is hardly disputed that, in the face of the unprecedented scenario of low growth, low inflation, low natural interest rate, the extraordinary monetary policy measures implemented by the ecb have been decisive in preserving the euro area from deflation and contributing to the ongoing economic recovery. for those who wonder about their risks and negative implications, it is worth recalling that the ecb's monetary policy is not the cause of low interest rates but is a symptom of them and the necessary - though not the only - therapy. in view of the moderate pace of the recovery and its exposure to downside risks stemming from the current phase of political and economic uncertainty, it is clear that a continuation of the current accommodative stance of monetary policy will be necessary to ensure a return of the inflation rate to below, but close to, 2%. at the same time, it is equally clear that this action, while necessary, is not sufficient. we must therefore make better and stronger use of the economic policy instruments at our disposal. we are facing the risk of a vicious circle between low growth expectations and low investment, which can also have a negative impact on potential growth, making the crisis structural, and not just cyclical, in its effect. this scenario is aggravated by the uncertain political environment and the possible pursuit of a line of economic unilateralism by the new us administration. this requires making our policy mix of structural reforms and fiscal policies more growth-oriented, in particular by supporting public and private investment and strengthening social and territorial cohesion. in this sense, the commission's recommendation of a moderately expansionary fiscal stance is an important step forward which must now be translated into concrete actions and instruments. the european parliament will not fail to have a say in this debate.

the agenda includes the debate on the question with request for an oral reply to the commission on the completion of basel iii, by roberto gualtieri, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs (o-000136/2016 - b8-1810/2016) (2016/2959 ((rsp))
author. – mr president, this debate takes place one week before the next meeting of the basel committee in chile, which will be an important step in the process towards the finalisation of the so-called basel iii agreements with a fundamental review of the banking book. as we know, this review is focused on three groups of measures: the review of the standardised approach for credit and operational risk, in order to enhance the risk sensitivity and robustness; the introduction of constraints to the use of internal models; the potential introduction of capital ouput floor based on the standardised approaches that defines the minimum amount of capital requirement for internally model exposures. the parliament will be called, as co-legislator, to introduce the outcomes of this review into eu law. taking into account the relevance and potential impact of the measures under discussion, we consider it necessary to intervene in the debate. we had an exchange of views with the single supervisory mechanism (ssm), the commission, the european banking authority (eba) and the secretary-general of the basel committee, and we drafted this oral question and the resolution, which has been approved by the committee on economic and monetary affairs (econ) with a very broad majority and will now be put to the vote before the plenary. as the resolution clearly states, we believe in the importance of sound global standards, and we reaffirm that banks need to be well capitalised in order to support the real economy and reduce risk. we also consider it important to increase simplicity, comparability and convergence of the risk-weighted capital framework in order to address excessive variability in risk-weighted assets and to apply the same rules to the same risks. however, we think that the current revision, in order to be effective and not to have unintended and counterproductive consequences, needs to fully respect two principles. firstly, it should not significantly increase overall capital requirements for european banks as the basel oversight board has clearly stated. secondly, the revision should not have a negative impact on the level playing field at global level. it should not exacerbate – rather it should mitigate – the differences between types of banks and between geographical areas, and it should not unduly penalise the eu banking model. as we know, although the draft standard has been built up by specific proposal subject to public consultations and specific quantitative impact studies, during the summary many concerns have been expressed and it clearly emerged that the various drafts did not respect the two above-mentioned principles. for this reason, we are calling on the basel committee to revise its proposals. we also call on the ecb, the ssm and the commission to ensure the respect of the two principles in the finalisation and monitoring of the new standard. as the resolution clearly states, we consider that this would be instrumental for ensuring a consistent incorporation of the new measures into eu legislation. we understand that some steps in the right direction have been taken, and we encourage all the remaining critical elements to be addressed. as regards the use of internal models, they need to address the variability of risk-weighted assets should not be a reason to drop the sensitiveness of prudential requirement. it should be rather an incentive to deal with lack of organisation in modelling approaches, as the eba and the ssm have already been doing since 2014, in order to ensure that risk-weighted assets are always consistent with the actual risk behaviour of banking assets. last, but not least, the resolution expresses concerns about the potential effect on the real economy of the possible introduction of output floors. the output floor is closely linked to the leverage ratio, and the new standard should ensure that the level of calibration of these two measures does not lead to an unintended duplication that could not only end up with an undoubtedly punitive outcome for the euro in terms of capital requirements, but also undermine the effectiveness of the overall reform package. in conclusion, with this resolution the parliament reaffirms its commitment to work on agreed international standards, but at the same time it warns that those standards should fully take into account the specificity of the eu banking model and strike the right balance between stability and growth. we hope that the adoption of this resolution with a broad majority will contribute to this balanced outcome.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the dodds report on the establishment of a long-term plan for cod stocks and the fisheries exploiting those stocks. this is an important text updating regulation (ec) no 1342/2008 with a view to improving and clarifying some of the provisions contained therein. the scientific evaluation of the current legislative text has shown that there are some problems, particularly with regard to the strategy for managing stocks in the north sea. the amendments adopted today will bring the regulation into line with the new common fisheries policy by introducing a landing obligation and prohibiting discards. the new measures will make it possible to obtain more accurate data on actual catches and thus ensure better planning. the long-term plan aims to maintain cod stocks above levels that can produce the maximum sustainable yield, thus promoting a fishery that is profitable for fishermen and sustainable for the ecosystem.
in writing. ‒ there are some important criticisms in the text which have convinced me not to support this new long-term plan for cod stocks. we need much more to revive fishing, to put our fishermen and the fishermen of the whole sector back to work, who expect less obstacles and more support from the union.
in writing. ‒ today we have approved the new cod stock regulation which is in line with the reform of the common fisheries policy, particularly in terms of definitions and objectives. the rules currently governing the setting of annual catch limits by the council would be replaced by this new regulation with the obligation to respect the precautionary principle, together with a system of fishing authorizations and fishing capacity ceilings. it seems to me a very good result and a step in the right direction. in 2012, the council adopted on its own initiative, bypassing the european parliament, several measures to amend the fisheries management plan for a number of cod stocks in european seas. this regulation, which was only enacted by the council, has been annulled by the european court of justice. today we finally have a new regulation, based on the appropriate legal basis of 'co-decision', which makes it possible to adapt the long-term plan for cod stocks and the fisheries exploiting those stocks.
in writing. ‒ in june 2016, agreement was reached between parliament, the commission and the council to amend the 2008 regulation establishing a long-term management plan for cod stocks and the new rules will enter into force on 10 january 2017. the plan identified is in line with the reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp) and includes the obligation to respect a precautionary approach, as well as a system of fishing authorisations and capacity limits. i therefore voted in favour of adopting it.
in writing. ‒ i support the long-term plan as i believe it is essential to implement the principles of the new common fisheries policy and to support its implementation, in order to avoid the mismatches that have been created in the market due to the application of unequal and tendentious national regulations, as well as the frequent damage to biodiversity and the ecosystem due to lack of controls. i hope that this orientation in the north sea will continue to be fully represented. however, i am concerned to recall how often the increasing and unfair competition that the mediterranean countries face from non-european countries, where fishing is poor, uncontrolled and certainly not in line with the health regulations, is overlooked in fisheries policies. more attention should be paid to this.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure approving the advance agreement at second reading reached between parliament and the council in june 2016. the draft regulation puts an end to the complicated fishing regime currently in force since 2008 which has failed to improve the state of cod stocks in the north sea. the amendments introduced, which take account, among other things, of the introduction of the landing obligation in the plan areas and which guarantee greater flexibility in the definition of tacs and total allowable quotas, are in my view improvements on the present situation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution to support the council's position on the amendment of the long-term plan for fisheries exploiting cod stocks. in fact, i believe that the amendment of regulation (ec) no 1342/2008 in order to improve and clarify its provisions is of fundamental importance to ensure the implementation of a sustainable plan for cod fisheries and related activities, in line with the principles of the new common fisheries policy. this is also an important achievement for the european parliament, which, as confirmed by the opinion of the court of justice, has legislative power on fisheries policies under the ordinary legislative procedure.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for the second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1342/2008 establishing a long-term plan for cod stocks and the fisheries exploiting those stocks, as this is a necessary and long overdue measure. the file on the amendment of regulation (ec) no 1342/2008 has been stalled for almost four years because of the institutional clash between the commission, parliament and council, which has seen them challenge the applicable legislative procedure before the court of justice. this conflict has effectively paralysed a process of adaptation of eu legislation that is badly needed in view of the reform of the common fisheries policy and the recent introduction of the landing obligation and rules on unwanted catches. i therefore think it is important that, while member states are still waiting to draw up their multiannual plans for multispecies fisheries, the existing regulation should be amended to ensure the survival of cod stocks and to provide legal certainty for european fishermen.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because there is no doubt that the need to protect fish stocks must be very carefully combined with the need for flexibility. it is difficult to explain why brussels is the one to decide the size of the nets, the size of the clams, the quantity of fish caught. there are sectors, i am thinking of fishing but also of agriculture, where the link between worker and resource goes far beyond the profession. the fisherman with the sea, the farmer with the land: the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. in the largest fishing district in my region, mazara del vallo, the number of deep-sea fishing vessels has fallen from 400 to 80. fishing in a border area makes it even clearer to fishermen that the european fisheries policy is strong with the member states and weak with the non-member countries. with these rules and these production costs, our fish will never be as competitive as the libyan, egyptian, tunisian, let alone the philippine. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for adoption.
in writing. the current fishing regime in force since 2008 should be discontinued as it has not been able to improve the stock of north sea cod. in april 2016, a mandate was adopted by the pech committee for negotiations with the council. the agreement, which implements the principles of the new common fisheries policy by supporting its implementation, was approved by the same pech committee in july 2016. it provided for the application of certain amendments aimed at introducing the landing obligation in the areas of the plan, ensuring greater flexibility in the fishing pattern and the total allowable quotas. the new proposal will enter into force in january 2017 and will be valid until the adoption of the new multiannual north sea management plan, which was recently submitted to the european commission. for these reasons, i vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. ‒ the draft regulation puts an end to the complicated fishing regime currently in place since 2008, which has failed to improve the state of cod stocks in the north sea. the amendments introduced take account of the introduction of the landing obligation in the plan areas and provide for greater flexibility in the definition of tacs and total allowable quotas. i therefore voted in favour of the measure.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of my colleagues' proposal because i believe it is right to safeguard the existence of marine fauna, in particular that of cod, by setting stock limits. one of the main concerns with regulation (ec) no 1342/2008, which is the subject of the second reading, is caused by the setting of the tac (total allowable catch), which has not led to a reduction in cod catches. in fact, in some member states the discard limits established for fishing activities are not respected. moreover, the regulation entered into force long before the treaty of lisbon and may have to be applied until a new mixed fisheries plan is identified. but at the same time i think that the needs of the citizens of the european union who live off fishing alone must be taken into account. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the new regulation aims to ensure the long-term sustainable exploitation of cod stocks in accordance with the principle of maximum sustainable yield. i have decided to vote in favour of the agreement reached between the council and parliament, which is a sure step forward towards the timely implementation of the new principles of the common fisheries policy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting the regulation establishing a long-term plan for cod stocks and the fisheries exploiting those stocks. the matter has been referred to the court of justice by the european parliament and the commission, because we considered that the council's decision to split the proposal for a long-term plan for cod stocks was unlawful. the judgment annulled the council regulation and the co-legislators are therefore required to adopt a new text by the end of the year in order to ensure legal certainty. after the court's ruling, the pech committee adopted a mandate for negotiations with the council and the file was closed. the agreement, which implements the principles of the new common fisheries policy and supports its implementation, was approved by the committee. the s&d group actively contributed to the swift adoption of the plan in order to ensure legal certainty for fishermen: we have ensured that the plan in question respects the principles of cfp reform.
i voted in favour of this report because the fight against fraud, tax evasion and money laundering must be a priority for the european union. it's about justice, about fairness: it's a matter of policy. in recent years, most citizens of the european union have faced an unprecedented economic crisis. in recent years, tax fraud has become increasingly common - the panama papers speak for themselves - and scandals have involved former european union commissioners. it is time to clarify matters, to strengthen cooperation and to allow the transfer of tax information which can lead quickly to investigations. european taxpayers are often forced to close down their businesses. they are not afraid of transparency, nor of controls: they fear being governed by crooks and evaders, they distrust the institutions that protect their interests and seem to side with the big corporations. europe must choose and it must choose with facts.
in writing. ‒ the following report deals with the revision of the directive on the automatic exchange of information in tax and taxation matters. i think it is of the utmost importance to put in place mechanisms that ensure transparency and make money laundering difficult. a step in this direction would certainly be to make the exchange of information mandatory and automatic, to avoid a repetition of events such as luxleaks and the panama papers. for the reasons stated above, i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ tax evasion is a very topical issue, one made even more central by the panama papers investigations which have rightly caused a stir in public opinion worldwide and within the union, also because of the important figures involved. the maurel report, which i supported with my vote today, is a joint response by the european institutions to the persisting phenomenon of tax evasion. the new measures are designed to reinforce the commission's proposal by allowing the tax authorities of each member state to access and share all information on bank current account holders, with particular attention to their income, interest and dividends. the new legislation is aimed at identifying the evaders, rendering ineffective those tools, legal devices and entities, which are used today to cover up these illegal operations. we must not forget that there are very strong links between evasion, money laundering, terrorist financing and organised crime. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the amendments proposed by my colleague and rapporteur mr maurel because i think that combating tax evasion and tax avoidance is a political priority for the european union. in this regard, a skilled staff is needed in order to facilitate a rapid and complete exchange of information.
in writing. ‒ the european commission is pursuing a programme against tax evasion and avoidance to ensure fairer and more effective taxation in the eu. significant progress has been made in strengthening tax transparency and cooperation between tax administrations across the union. member states have agreed on new rules for the automatic exchange of information on tax rulings and tax returns. the eu tax transparency programme is of key importance in identifying and tackling tax evasion effectively, as tax authorities need wider access to information on the beneficial ownership of intermediary entities and other relevant information on customer due diligence. this requires the effective and rapid implementation of the global standard for the automatic exchange of financial information for tax purposes, implemented by directive 2014/107/eu, which also ensures that information on the holders of financial accounts is transmitted to the member state in which the account holder is resident. in the absence of anti-money laundering information, tax authorities will not be able to monitor, verify and confirm whether financial institutions are properly applying the administrative cooperation directive.
in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the report in question, which allows automatic access to money laundering information by the tax authorities of the member states. systematic access by tax authorities to anti-money laundering information will allow for greater transparency and faster identification and processing of data, avoiding delays and dysfunctions in administrative cooperation by financial institutions. the directive will apply to taxes of all kinds levied by or on behalf of a member state or the territorial or administrative subdivisions of a member state, including local authorities, as well as to virtual currency exchange services and digital wallet service providers. member states will have to ensure that all information exchanged and obtained is subject to timely investigation, regardless of whether such information was obtained by the authorities upon request, through a spontaneous exchange of information or through public leaks.
in writing. ‒ the directive implementing global standards for the automatic exchange of tax information is under review and the proposal introduces the possibility for national tax authorities to access anti-money laundering information. this will help to combat terrorist financing, corruption and other criminal activities. the exchange of information should be automatic and compulsory, in order to ensure maximum transparency, as the honourable member's report intends. thanks to our contribution, the report also includes a sanctioning mechanism for banks that facilitate money laundering, such as the withdrawal of a banking licence. i therefore voted in favour.

in writing. the report adopted today aims to enable tax authorities to have systematic access to anti-money laundering information and to carry out their monitoring functions on the correct and proper application of the administrative cooperation directive. this is to strengthen eu and international transparency measures, so that tax authorities can have as much information as possible about customers, also preventing tax evasion. in order to provide for mechanisms of this magnitude, it is necessary that member states exchange information and documents relating to financial movements in a fully automated manner. directive 849/2015/eu will allow them to access such information in the course of monitoring the correct application of the rules on the automatic exchange of tax information. finally, access to such information will ensure that tax authorities are better prepared to fulfil their monitoring obligations and thus be able to prevent tax evasion and tax fraud.

in writing. ‒ every year parliament is called upon to vote on the report on the ecb and this year i am forced to disagree and express my negative opinion on the report presented as it only partially analyses the work of the central bank. the analysis is not very objective, praising the work of the ecb without any real criticism of it. i would also stress that the ecb should consider as soon as possible an opt-out mechanism allowing member states to opt out of the euro area should this be deemed necessary.
in writing. ‒ the report provides a generally positive assessment of the ecb 's monetary policies with clear references to: asset purchase programme, main refinancing operations and targeted longer-term refinancing operations. the report underlines that the euro area continues to suffer from high unemployment, excessively low inflation, large macroeconomic imbalances, including current account imbalances, and a very low level of productivity growth, which is the result of a lack of investment, the inability to implement structural reforms and weak domestic demand. this clear reference to the lack of investment is something that we, as a group of socialists and democrats, have insisted on very strongly, and i believe that it is a central point in our struggle. the report also calls for the step-by-step completion and full implementation of the banking union, the capital markets union and a solution to the problem of non-performing loans to improve the effectiveness of monetary policy and mitigate the risks of a financial sector shock. i therefore think that this text is acceptable, although further steps could have been taken to emphasize, in line with the commission's proposals, the need for a positive fiscal stance.
in writing. ‒ the ecb's activity has been detrimental since its inception, i.e. since the start of monetary union in a non-optimal currency area. austerity, unemployment, privatisation, the selling off of strategic assets of member states in difficulty, cuts in investment, wages, workers' rights, the closure of small and mediumsized enterprises: these are just some of the tangible effects that millions and millions of european citizens have paid for on their own skin. the ecb's replies were inadequate in terms of timing and manner. from quantitative easing to low interest rates, every measure imagined to be an immediate and temporary response to a lack of liquidity and access to credit has turned into a quicksand, with a real deterioration in macroeconomic conditions, which in turn has led to the need to call for structural reforms and the capital markets union. these are described as a lifeline for citizens, while they do nothing more than guarantee the profitability of banks and financial entities. the political, economic and social consequences of the euro and the dictates of the ecb are very serious and it is not possible to support those who actually induce poverty in order to save the euro and the profits of the banks. for these reasons, i am voting against.
in writing. ‒ i vote against the report on the ecb, which is too biased and unrealistic.
in writing. ‒ i share the tone of the report by the committee on economic and monetary affairs, which expresses a very positive assessment of the ecb's work, in particular in relation to monetary policies to support growth and the financing of long-term operations. i would also like to stress the serious economic difficulties of the euro area reflected in the report, in the first place employment, low inflation, macroeconomic imbalances, low productivity, a serious lack of investment, the delay in structural reforms in the countries and extreme weakness of demand. it is important to me that the s&d group's priorities in support of the expansionary monetary policy pursued by mario draghi are well represented, in particular because it has stressed that the ecb's choices alone cannot correct the euro area's shortcomings and must therefore be accompanied by socially balanced investment and structural reforms.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ecb's annual report 2015 because i believe that monetary policy and in particular the unconventional quantitative easing measures implemented by the ecb are in line with the price stability objectives and consistent with its mandate, but above all because they have been decisive in preserving the integrity of the euro area, protecting it from deflation and contributing to the economic recovery, which is still uncertain in many euro area states. this report provides the european parliament with an opportunity to take stock of the policy mix of structural reforms and fiscal policies in the euro area, but also to note the need for greater growth orientation of these policies through public and private investment that strengthens territorial cohesion, and the effects of monetary policies on the european financial system, which is now much stronger in terms of capital, leverage, financing and risk-taking. as stated by president draghi, the common equity tier 1 of the significant banking groups in the eurozone is now over 14%. finally, the issue of bank profitability and, above all, the completion of the banking union, through the creation of the third pillar (edis) and the creation of a final public backstop under the second pillar, remains open.
in writing. the report highlights that the euro area continues to suffer from the negative effects of high unemployment, inflation and macroeconomic imbalances, and a still very low level of growth. in the light of these issues, the measures taken by the ecb to bring inflation back to the mediumterm inflation target of 2% appear to be consistent with the terms of its mandate. the ecb has contributed to the climate of confidence by countering risks to the integrity of the euro area, mainly related to the events in greece over the past year. on the basis of the implementation of targeted programmes for the long-term refinancing of the real economy, financial conditions have improved, facilitating a recovery in lending to firms and households in the euro area.
in writing. ‒ i expressed a favourable vote for the report on the european central bank annual report for 2015. supporting the report represents our commitment to reducing unemployment, government deficit, macroeconomic imbalances, and the debt-to-gdp ratio in the euro area. 2015 represented a year of recovery for the euro area economy and, therefore, the report represents a means to encourage european institutions to further cooperate and strengthen consumer confidence to boost spending, which in turn represents resuming hiring and investing. the report by the ecb shows areas of weakness that need improvement.
