in writing. ‒ i abstain from the report because it would have been more appropriate to proceed with the second reading to assess in a more thorough and transparent way the impact of the different proposals on the table in order to achieve a wider consensus among member states.
in writing. ‒ this is an important report on ensuring our air quality and on action needed to be taken so that there are no significant negative impacts on and risks to human health and the environment. i support the report in establishing emission reduction commitments for the member states in atmospheric emissions of sulphur dioxide (so2), nitrogen oxides (nox), non-methane volatile organic compounds (nmvoc), ammonia (nh3) and fine particulate matter (pm 2.5 ). for this directive to be successful and to ensure air quality and emission levels in the eu, the member states should set up and implement national control programmes. to achieve this it is important that the member states can access eu funds for implementation of this directive and that there is an easy access for member states to exchange best practises and experiences in reducing emissions and ensuring air-quality. lastly i support the flexibility for member states that is included in this directive, it is important that member states are not forced to take a certain action to ensure air quality and emissions levels as the most efficient way for one member state to deal with these issue might not hold true for another.
in writing. ‒ i have expressed my support for the amendment of the emissions ceiling directive, and i think it is important to set new high standards to further limit certain harmful substances such as sulphur dioxide, nitrogen, particulate matter and ammonia. i want to highlight the important improvement for public health: it is estimated that by 2030 the number of deaths caused by toxic air could be halved. the commission will therefore be required to verify that governments are keeping their commitments to drastically reduce emissions to the required standards.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the reduction of national emissions of certain atmospheric pollutants and amending directive 2003/35/ec because it is an important vote that unlocks a file that has been closed for almost three years and gives important answers to european citizens. the quality of the air we breathe is not just an environmental issue, but a serious health emergency, with almost 90% of eu citizens living in polluted places and some 400 000 premature deaths a year linked to it. if we want to improve the quality of life of our citizens, especially in large urban areas, then ambitious reform with strong objectives is needed. i personally welcome the effort made by parliament, and by the s&d group in particular, to push for binding targets by 2025. the agreement with the council, however, meets the needs of the governments and gives us more flexible and open legislation, with non-binding objectives, the exclusion of certain sectors and a series of flexibility clauses. the agreement is still an important step forward, and its implementation and enforcement will now have to be carefully scrutinised by parliament.
in writing. ‒ i voted positively for the report on reduction of national emissions of certain atmospheric pollutants. it is clear that air quality needs support and requires of immediate action because, just like the report points out, air is ‘a significant trans-boundary human health and environmental issue that profoundly affects all eu citizens.’ air pollution has increased to worrying levels for the health and we can no longer let this keep on taking place. it is important to acknowledge the existing air-related health issues by introducing new legislation and policy that can lead to potential change even when the situation is challenging.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal because i believe it is important to commit ourselves, at national level, to further reducing air pollution emissions from 2020 to 2030. the aim of this directive is to improve human health on the one hand and to protect the environment on the other. these national programmes to control air pollution would be applicable from the agricultural sector to the industrial sector, so anyone could benefit. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ policy-making based on concrete elements must be the cornerstone of eu legislation. in the case of air quality, this is a matter of extreme importance for both human health and the environment, which affects all citizens of the union and requires immediate action at supranational level. air pollution, which has been neglected by policy for years, is now a priority. it is essential that the commission should play a supervisory and political role in this respect. i believe that it is of paramount importance to ensure an adequate level of air quality as a public good. i believe that this requires the identification of innovative ways of financing emission reductions. i think this directive is going in the right direction and that is why i have decided to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ air pollution causes over 400 000 premature deaths in the european union each year, making it the main environmental risk factor for human health. pollution from transport, heating, industry and agriculture, for example, also imposes high external costs due to lost working days, health costs, crop yield losses and damage to buildings, totalling between eur 330 and 940 billion per year. i therefore voted in favour of the proposal to update the directive setting national emission limits for air pollutants, hoping that the new legislation will help to reduce premature deaths and improve air quality.
in writing. ‒ the level of air pollutants in the air has not yet fallen below levels necessary to protect human health and the environment. i believe that further efforts are needed to reduce the more than 460,000 premature deaths caused each year by fine dust, as well as the 80,000 caused by nitrogen dioxide emissions. i believe that the reduction in pollutant emissions each year, while recognising the possible negative economic effects that would be experienced by certain sectors, is an important stimulus to research in green technologies. the creation of countless jobs in this sector would send a positive signal from brussels, demonstrating concretely the commitment that the european union has made to protecting its citizens, also in the face of new challenges in terms of economic growth. the public health costs, now substantial due to cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, will also be greatly reduced.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a parliament and council directive on the reduction of national emissions of certain atmospheric pollutants. the development of policies on the basis of concrete elements must be the cornerstone of european union legislation. in the case of air quality, the answer is clear: this is a major and cross-border issue for both human health and the environment that affects all citizens of the union and requires immediate action. the commission proposal sets new emission limits for sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and ammonia for 2020 and 2030: the new 2030 targets aim to achieve 70% of the maximum technically feasible reductions in health effects as set by the who. the commission has set the limits for individual member states on the basis of an assessment of the areas where the most cost-effective measures can be implemented. the commission text also requires member states to adopt national air pollution control programmes to be updated every two years.
in writing. ‒ the following motion for a resolution concerns the completion of basel iii, a set of reform proposals concerning banking regulation. european banks are experiencing a very critical period, caused mainly by inadequate and sometimes absent financial regulation that began in the last decades of the last century. i believe that basel iii is far from perfect or even adequate for the conditions in which the present banking system operates. however, to vote against would be to promote the deregulation mentioned earlier. these are the main reasons why i decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the global financial crisis has led g20 leaders to agree on a comprehensive reform agenda to strengthen the regulatory standards to which international banks are subject, a project in which the basel committee is playing a central role in developing minimum standards for prudential requirements applicable to large banks operating internationally. the motion for a resolution adopted today by parliament, which i support, reflects on the central role played by banks in the eu and sets out to define some of the key elements for a successful completion of the basel iii regulatory framework. the basel committee should commit itself to promoting quality standards, transparency and consistency in the area of capitalisation and risk coverage. the primary objective must be to ensure real support to the real economy by reducing systemic risk and by defining an approach that mitigates differences between banking models and jurisdictions by establishing risk-based regulatory mechanisms.
in writing. ‒ 'basel 3' is a comprehensive set of reform measures, prepared by the basel committee on banking supervision, to strengthen the regulation, supervision and risk management of the banking sector. although the objectives of this text are shared, i think it is unacceptable that it does not contain any critical passage on the behaviour of certain european banks which could have been avoided by an effective supervisory system. i am convinced that the right references to the role of the banking system in helping households and smes are only a rhetorical exercise given the state of crisis in the assets of many institutions, which are also crushed by the private debt generated by the eu monetary policy. for all these reasons i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ following the 2008 economic and financial crisis, the basel committee on banking supervision was established with the aim of strengthening the capacity of banks to absorb shocks arising from financial and economic stresses, so as to reduce the risk of contagion from the financial sector to the real economy. in the eu, banks play a major role in financing the economy. in this resolution, which i support, the european parliament stresses the need for internationally agreed minimum standards to avoid fragmentation of legislation on asset regulation. the need is to ensure that the basel iii agreement meets quality, transparency and consistency standards in terms of capitalisation and risk coverage, and to ensure that the new rules promote and not slow down the moderate growth that the eu is experiencing in the post-crisis period. parliament also stressed the importance of reforms based on a global level playing field, so that differences between countries and banking models were reduced rather than increased.
in writing. ‒ the basel accords are guidelines on bank capital requirements drawn up by the basel committee, which is made up of the regulators of the main so-called 'first world' countries, with the aim of pursuing international monetary and financial stability. the most recent of the three basel agreements, which entered into force six years ago, established a body, the cbvb (basel committee on banking supervision), which has presented to the international community a package of proposals aimed at improving the prudential framework for banks dealing with credit and operational risks. these proposals should be collected by the european union and reworked with the aim of improving the risk sensitivity and robustness of standardised approaches, better regulating financial flows and implementing where necessary appropriate restrictions, finalising the design and calibration of leverage with a long-term perspective and the political will to prioritise stability and the real economy over short-term financial speculation.
in writing. ‒ after careful reflection and debate in the house, i have voted in favour of the resolution on the conclusion of the basle iii agreement, on the basis of the following considerations: improved management of the bank/enterprise relationship is a priority for both the enterprise and the bank side, in order to avoid operational risks and to improve the prudential framework for banks; proper access to the capital market and practical assistance in identifying new forms of capitalisation are essential elements in ensuring the stability of the production system; the commission must be a leader in ensuring a level playing field and in calibrating the final standards.
in writing. ‒ the basel iii accord represents a robust network of reform measures for banking supervision in order to strengthen the sector's regulation, supervision and risk management, specifically, minimum capital thresholds are imposed on banks to prevent financial shocks from bringing them to their knees with disruptive consequences for the entire system. i believe that prudential regulation should be encouraged and implemented, and i therefore support this measure. the reason that drives me to act in this way more than any other is that it is in support of the real economy. basel rules are designed to stabilise the financial world and impose sound practices on its players in terms of capitalisation, risk management and liquidity, strongly conditioning their use towards the real economy and thus their conveyance to companies and citizens. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial system is not undermined by the crisis. balance is everything and basel 3 requires banks to provide capital and liquidity guarantees so that financing to households and businesses is traceable and secure.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure as i share the proposals put forward by the basel committee on banking supervision (cbvb) to improve the prudential framework for banks facing credit and operational risks (finalization of the basel iii agreement, the so-called 'basel iv'). the objective of the proposals is to improve the risk sensitivity and robustness of the standardised approaches, to analyse further constraints on the role of internally modelled approaches in the capital framework and to finalise the design and calibration of leverage and a possible minimum level of capital, based on standardised approaches. i believe that the activity of banks which today play a key role in financing the european economy and are likely to remain the main source of financing for households and businesses, particularly smes should continue to be monitored in order to reduce any systemic risk.
in writing. ‒ the specific features of the european banking system must be safeguarded: the european union is a global economy, where the big international banks are joined by small regional and cooperative banks, the wealth of europe. it is essential to protect the diversity and heterogeneity of the european financial landscape, which also allows for risk diversification. it is particularly important to protect those banks which are familiar with the needs and problems of local artisans and small and mediumsized enterprises. the rules must therefore be proportionate to the size and risk of the bank. regulation needs to be risk-based. in particular, the same risk must be treated in a common way at the level of the overall regulation. this will ensure a reduction in regulatory arbitrage. in this respect, it is important that parliament reaffirm its legislative power in relation to a matter such as the implementation of the basle standards, which is very often accused of being decided outside democratic frameworks. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of the future of the internal market. for these reasons, i think the final text is a good compromise in defence of the democratic role of parliament towards policies in defence of a commitment of the financial system to the real economy.
in writing. ‒ i voted to support this important report on the work of the bcbs to finalise the basel iii framework. this is a key part of legislation to develop internationally agreed minimum standards and requirements for large, international banks. this would serve to add simplicity and comparability of the existing framework on risk-weighted capital – this could serve to address excessive variability of these assets and it would importantly mean that the same rules are applied to the same risks. extensive monitoring of the effects will be necessary in order to ensure no negative effects on the banking sector. banks play a key role in financing the european economy and they are especially important for smes – who makes up the real backbone of the european economy. in regard to smes, flexibility plays a key role in their financing needs, and we as lawmakers must keep this a relevant theme in all financial regulation. it is of crucial importance that we promote the financing of, and investments in, european smes since they are already underfunded and financing possibilities are needed to reverse the sluggish growth of the eu economy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on completing basel iii on capital requirements for financial institutions, which the ep worked on for a long time in the last parliamentary term to transpose into european law. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the whole of the european union, including the countries of central and eastern europe, the former soviet union and the former soviet union. i strongly share the concerns about further tightening of capital requirements, because of the potential effects on the real economy at a very delicate stage for the whole european economy, whose growth signals are still weak, as stated by president draghi this week before the ep. as well as the need for european banks to be well capitalised in order to be able to support the real economy and smes while reducing risks. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of my colleagues' proposal because i believe that a well-established and well-capitalised system is the fundamental prerequisite for safeguarding financial security, ensuring the proper provision of credit to the real economy and supporting economic growth. the g20 also agreed to develop a reform agenda to protect regulatory standards, and the cbvb jointly developed international standards to establish prudential requirements for international banks. however, as these prudential requirements may vary in their application depending on the banking activity, the cbvb is considering further changes to the prudential regime for banks. the cbvb will, however, have to carefully assess the impact of the reforms on countries and banking models. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the basel committee on banking supervision (cvbv) has proposed stricter requirements on bank capital, as required by the revision of the rules contained in the basel iii agreement. it is important that such measures allow banks to continue to play their key role as financiers of the european economy, without, for example, compromising their ability to provide loans. in the hope that the relevant bodies, such as the commission and the european central bank, will provide parliament with accurate and transparent updates and assessments of the work being done by the cbvb, i have decided to vote in favour of the resolution.
in writing. a motion on the finalisation of basel iii and the future basel 4 on capital requirements for banks was voted during the last plenary session. there are points of agreement in the motion, but also some important criticisms. we do not think, for example, that the call for the use of the internal method, which allows banks to calculate their capital requirements through internal models, instead of the standardised method, is sustainable, since the use of this method has generated distortions and opened the way to real abuses by the big banks. we also do not support the introduction of a risk-based approach to government securities, which would have the effect of discouraging investment in the securities of countries judged by the markets to be more risky, thus harming countries such as italy. we do, however, share some of the principles that are very clearly outlined in the motion, including the need for regulation not to further restrict the lending capacity of banks to the real economy and the importance of ensuring a level playing field in the market between operators. for these reasons we have abstained from voting in the house.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the completion of basel iii. this resolution is to be considered as balanced, as it should respect the principle of not significantly increasing the overall capital requirements, while at the same time strengthening the overall financial position of european banks. banks are a key component of the effective functioning of our economy; the commission notes that the bank's capital needs are well capitalised in order to support the real economy, reduce systemic risk and avoid the bailouts that occurred during the crisis. the work being done by the basel committee should be able to mitigate differences between european banking jurisdictions and models.

in writing. ‒ the major changes in the global landscape in recent years make it increasingly necessary to reflect on europe's ability to meet the enormous challenges of our time, which are not only presented in conventional forms but increasingly in the form of hybrid threats involving state and non-state actors. the paşcu report, which i supported with my vote today, strongly underlines the need for a substantial revision of the csdp in order to enable the eu and its member states to make a decisive contribution to the management of international crises and to the affirmation of the union's strategic autonomy. a white paper on european defence and security is needed to chart the way for a strengthening of the continent's defence industry and at the same time to foreshadow the lines of action in the international arena. the core of the new csdp must, however, be the creation of a genuine autonomous defence capability for the eu to protect its citizens and promote its values and interests, in full respect of the treaties, international law and human rights.

in writing. ‒ the eu is facing a series of regional crises and increasingly interconnected and complex challenges, not least islamist terrorism. european security is in danger because of uncoordinated and fragmented action among the member states. i believe that the eu should be able to intervene in crisis management, from prevention to resolution, not only through dialogue and cooperation with third countries in the region, but above all through greater cooperation and interoperability between member states. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, which supports the full involvement of the member states in the process of reviewing the common security and defence policy. the eu should encourage member states to meet nato's targets requiring a minimum level of defence spending of 2% of gdp, in order to enhance the complementarity of eu-nato capabilities in terms of collective defence and efficient financing. the eu's commitment should follow a roadmap defined in the form of a security and defence implementation plan and white paper, in line with the priorities identified in the global strategy.

in writing. ‒ the european union is a great entity capable of promoting democracy and prosperity not only among its citizens but also in the regions around it. it is a space of freedom which is often seen as an example for peoples embarking on the path of integration and respect for the rule of law, but it is also seen as a threat by those who see respect for freedom of thought, speech and religion as a limitation of their power. authoritarian and violent realities still surround europe: the european union is not only a political force, but also a political force. these realities are implementing a tight propaganda to mystify the work of the eu and to strengthen those who work to disintegrate it. we must be aware that a weaker europe means a strengthening of authoritarian regimes at our borders, a weaker internal democracy and an impoverishment of the population. we must work to change europe, to improve it, not to destroy it.

in writing. the european union symbolises and pursues the ideals of democracy, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, including the right to freedom of expression. these principles may legitimately give rise to misunderstandings by those who have not understood them or fought for them, but often their content is deliberately misrepresented, giving rise to anti-eu (mis) information and propaganda. however, today, predominantly non-state actors are waging campaigns of discredit and hatred against us. in fact, today's wars are fought not with weapons but with instruments such as financial speculation and discredit, as has unfortunately also been shown to the detriment of italy. the role of the fourth power has an extraordinary responsibility and i therefore vote in favour of the report, as i believe that defensive measures must be taken against the hate campaigns against the union. i believe it is a priority to offer decisive cooperation with social media service providers in the it field to curb hate speech and disinformation. at the same time, the socio-demographic reasons for radicalisation need to be investigated and multidimensional institutional tools need to be developed to link academic research, prison administration, police, justice, social services and education.
in writing. ‒ european citizens are exposed to disinformation and propaganda campaigns by third countries and non-state actors that undermine the concept of objective reporting or ethical journalism, making information biased or a mere tool of political power. two clear examples are both the propaganda war and the russian media intrusion into the countries of the eastern neighbourhood, and the communication and direct propaganda strategies deployed by isis/daesh, al-qaeda through social media. i voted in favour of this resolution because it brings to the european attention, and not only, a sensitive but underestimated issue which has a major impact on eu citizens, particularly the younger generation. the resolution also suggests measures to counter propaganda. i believe that the strategic communication plan in the joint framework to counter hybrid threats is effective and i support further efforts towards greater coordination between member states, nato, the european endowment for democracy, the osce and the eu institutions. another useful tool is the two weekly newsletters of the eu strategic communication task force that each member state could make available to its citizens to raise public awareness of the propaganda methods used by third parties.

in writing. ‒ benzatone is a substance that acts as a post-emergency selective herbicide against broadleaf weeds in a wide variety of crops and is commonly used in agriculture. however, it has a high potential for direct leaching into groundwater (sloughs, streams, springs) and is present in very significant quantities in many surface water bodies throughout europe. analyses and studies of its actual or alleged danger are not yet complete and so far do not allow it to be completely ruled out. for this reason, and in accordance with the precautionary principle, we in the european parliament ask the commission to withdraw its draft regulation on benzatone, to wait for new data and to redefine a new draft that puts the protection of the health of citizens and the safety of water and agricultural land at the centre.

in writing. ‒ the draft commission implementing regulation renewing the approval of the active substance bentazone for the placing of plant protection products on the market provides, on the basis of a scientific evaluation by the european food safety authority (efsa), for the authorisation of bentazone until 31 january 2032, i.e. for the maximum period allowed. however, the consumer risk assessment has not yet been finalised as the proposed residue definitions for the risk assessment in plants and for the application to animals are considered provisional due to the identified data gaps. i therefore decided to vote in favour of this objection, because a commission decision to approve an active substance would allow the active substance to be placed on the market before all the data needed to support that decision have been obtained.

on behalf of the efdd group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to try to put a different question to you. it is now more than five years since the adoption of the istanbul convention and i think we must ask ourselves: why have not all eu countries ratified it yet and others not even signed it? the states that have not ratified it have certainly not done so, because they are not against violence against women. so let us pause to understand the real motives behind these non-ratifications. the reason why some states oppose ratification is to be found in certain contents of the convention itself, which are outside the scope of the fight against gender-based violence, such as the introduction, for the first time in an international treaty, of the social definition of "gender", which becomes binding on the states that ratified the convention. and it is therefore understandable that the states where the gender debate is more complicated are resistant to such ratification. if this pressure had not been applied at the time, which has nothing to do with the urgency of the issue of violence against women, we would probably not be facing such a paradoxical situation today. let us ask ourselves, rather, whether in the states where it has been ratified and for which legislation has been enacted, there have been clear positive statistical results in terms of reducing gender-based violence. should we not focus on the fact that member states are actually legislating and taking measures to prevent and combat violence against women? many states have concentrated on repressive measures and still too little on preventive ones. from the experience we have had in europe, unfortunately, the concept of prevention is still focused on locking up the potential victim in a protected structure, thus restricting his freedom and movement, and leaving the dangerous subject free to move. it seems absurd that an instrument such as the convention, which should unite us in this battle, should end up dividing us and, five years later, we have still not reached a result, a solution. in short, let us get past these formal questions and concentrate more on monitoring what is actually happening in individual countries.

member of the commission. – mr president, thank you for this discussion. i am really unhappy to have to repeat that the situation is not getting better; the situation is becoming worse in europe and that is why we decided to earmark quite a lot of money to the campaign. that is why we keep exerting pressure on the member states to ratify the istanbul convention. that is why we are in such intensive discussions with the council to have the accession of the european union to the istanbul convention adopted. these are the concrete measures and concrete steps. i just want to tell you and confirm that what was quoted here by ms arena – from simone de beauvoir – was right: we are now in a period of where the atmosphere in society as such is worsening. i am working also in the field of anti-extremism and anti-radicalisation of society. i am in contact with the main it providers. we are trying to combat hate speech online with all possible efficient tools, and this is the sphere where a lot of violence against women starts. and it is not only against women. it is against all the other vulnerable groups in our societies. we should bear in mind that this is a complex issue and the worsening of the atmosphere in our society is not any excuse for saying, ‘okay, so this is also the case with violence against women’. we must combat and mobilise forces against this on all fronts. i know that you expect answers from me and i am going to raise several questions here. i will not be long as i know that we are limited by time. you asked: is the political will missing? mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the reform of the european vat system is now indispensable. the current, outdated system has proved vulnerable to fraud and a source of distortion of competition to the detriment of small and medium-sized enterprises. for example, vat fraud, carried out by criminal groups alone, is estimated to cost the european union between 40 and 60 million euros a year. several investigations by europol have shown that criminal groups also finance themselves through large-scale cross-border vat fraud, so-called 'carousel' fraud, also taking advantage of the legislative gaps between member states. to eradicate this phenomenon, it is essential to strengthen administrative cooperation between states in order to remove legal obstacles to the exchange of information between administrative and judicial authorities. i therefore thank the rapporteur for his work on the text proposing a reform of vat, a text which i share.

member of the commission. – mr president, i would like to welcome the report by mr riquet which provides a really balanced view of current developments in the transport sector, while pointing out some of the major challenges. let me respond to the elements of his report. first, on the importance of smes in the transport sector. road transport is a sector which is characterised by hundreds of thousands of smes. as an example, 95% of road freight companies are micro-companies with less than 10 employees. as opposed to other modes of transport, companies in road transport are subject to stiff competition in an already open market. this is largely due to the creation of a single market. however, looking at the local level and at passenger transport in particular, the development has been quite different. local and regional markets are often closed and strictly regulated, or even operated directly by public authorities. this way of functioning has not been challenged until recently. in some cases it has not promoted the industry to develop innovative solutions for transport. on the role of the commission, our role is to propose, where appropriate, eu legislation that addresses issues identified in a proportionate manner, having regard to the different public interests possibly involved, such as road safety or social working conditions, and of course our role is also to ensure that member states comply with eu law, and the responsibility of member states highlighted by your report is therefore very welcome. on the 2017 road initiatives, as you know, the commission has announced legislative proposals in the field of road transport to be presented in the first semester of 2017. when reviewing existing eu legislation in road transport, we will be looking for a balance between social standards and enhancing the functioning of the internal market. in particular, we are looking at ways to improve rules on access to the profession of road transport operator that are supposed to ensure fair conditions for hauliers of different member states. we need to adjust and clarify rules in a way that does not increase administrative burdens. on digitalisation of the economy, digitalisation is an opportunity to increase mobility and reduce congestion in cities, but it may also be a challenge for transport. we must ensure access to relevant transport data by all potential service providers, which is essential to ensure fair competition and effective functioning of the single market, and for municipalities and regulators to improve mobility services. on the collaborative economy and regulation of shared passenger transport, the commission has made it clear, notably in the communication on the collaborative economy, that it supports initiatives that help make better use of resources and that make the lives of citizens easier. we have also made it clear that all undertakings must observe union law, as well as applicable national law, which itself must be in line with union law. within this framework, however, it is up to the undertakings concerned to choose their business model. at the same time, we have encouraged member states to take the emergence of new technological solutions and business models as an opportunity to modernise decades-old regulations, and only apply restrictions if fully justified, proportionate and non-discriminatory. when looking at the legislation and applying it to new business models, the commission encourages member states to take into account the particularities of the collaborative economy. in this context, thresholds may be a good means to distinguish between professional providers and peer providers. banning services should only be a last resort and should be objectively justified by reason of an overriding public interest. in the specific case of passenger transport by taxi, hire car and ride-sharing, the commission launched a fact-finding study which has identified a huge diversity of national and local rules, resulting in a very different development on the market in each member state. while one can see some restrictions which are difficult to justify, we also see some good examples. more and more member states realise the potential of technological development, as well as new ways of organising transport services. some member states have decided to modify and simplify their laws by removing unnecessary barriers while ensuring minimum standards. these signs are encouraging and the commission will continue to support this process.
the commission has already submitted a proposal for a regulation on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in the transport market, traditional business models are now being supplemented by new business models which are attractive because of the employment benefits they bring and because they make the services offered more competitive, to the benefit of the final consumers. but we cannot but express our concern about the possible repercussions on working conditions, on precariousness and safety, and the risk that the boundary between selfemployment and employment will become blurred. furthermore, digitised business models do not appear to be as transparent as the competition rules, with the risk of encouraging unfair market practices, tax avoidance and evasion. we therefore need a legal framework that establishes a grid within which the need to protect the traditional market, to ensure the safety of workers, to guarantee consumers, to prevent the collaborative economy from being placed within the spaces of the economy and underground work prevails.

member of the commission. – mr president, ensuring a safe, reliable and uninterrupted energy supply in the eu is a top objective of european energy policy. as stated in the energy union strategy, we need to adopt a broad approach on energy security, encompassing solid emergency plans, external supply diversification, enforcement of internal market rules, infrastructure development, indigenous renewable generation and energy savings. first, the commission has proposed a revision of the 2010 security of gas supply regulation in order to improve further the level of preparedness and resilience of our gas system. this proposal aims at a more robust and consistent security of support framework, in particular by strengthening regional cooperation to lay the foundation for true solidarity among member states. second, the eu needs to ensure that intergovernmental agreements signed by its member states with third countries in the area of energy are more transparent and fully compliant with eu law. to that end, the commission proposed to significantly improve the information exchange mechanism with regard to intergovernmental agreements and non-binding instruments. third, the commission adopted the lng and gas storage strategy, which analyses the related strategic infrastructure to complete the internal energy market and the necessary projects to end the single source dependency of some member states. lastly, the security of supply package included the heating and cooling strategy. the commission strategy focuses on removing barriers to decarbonisation in buildings and industry, highlighting the role of modern technologies, increased energy efficiency and the use of renewables. in july 2015 the commission proposed a revision of the energy labelling directive and it will soon present a comprehensive review of the renewable energy efficiency and energy performance of buildings directives. but energy security also refers to the electricity sector itself, where security of supply requires us to develop a more integrated approach, based on common methods and rules, as well as regional cooperation. to ensure this, the commission is currently considering a proposal for a new regulation on how to prevent and manage crisis situations in the european electricity sector, which would include the obligation to draw up risk preparedness plans for member states, as well as sharing information and cooperation in times of crisis. in 2014 more than 80% of our total gas imports came from just three countries. the diversification of both suppliers and supply routes is therefore a key area to ensure security of supply, but we also need more competition that keeps prices in check. as argued in the energy union strategy, the commission has identified four main areas that can play a crucial role in enhancing gas supply diversification in europe. first, the realisation of the southern gas corridor is a landmark project as it will link the eu market to the immense gas resources around the caspian basin. the implementation of the project is on track and, as of 2020, it will start supplying the european market with 10 billion cubic meters of azeri gas each year. the caspian region has an incredible potential in terms of expanding these gas volumes. following the signature of the ashgabat declaration, the commission is working with azerbaijan, georgia, turkey and turkmenistan to extend the southern gas corridor to central asia. second, we have to cooperate with the countries bordering the eastern mediterranean in order to develop their rich resources. with regard to eastern mediterranean gas, a solution to the transport mode is required. both the lng and pipeline options are on the table. third, although north africa already supplies 15% of our gas imports, the region still has untapped oil and gas reserves, both conventional and unconventional. the main challenge to realising this potential and linking it to the eu market is to overcome the current security issues and political instability. in order to realise the opportunities in our southern neighbourhood a euro-mediterranean platform on gas has been set up and is operational. fourth, with the emergence of new suppliers, lng will become an important flexibility element in the coming years. in this respect, we need to ensure an optimal use of our existing and future regasification capacities. when it comes to gas supply, it is important to stress that ukraine is – and should remain – an important transit country for russian gas to europe. the commission has led trilateral negotiations between russia, ukraine and the eu to ensure a continuous flow of russian gas into ukraine and to the rest of europe. we are also working with our ukrainian partners to revise and upgrade the existing memorandum of understanding on energy cooperation to be fit for the common challenges ahead. we hope to sign this at the eu—ukraine summit later this week. let me conclude this intervention with a few words on nord stream ii. irrespective of the organisational set—up of nord stream ii, the commission’s overall negative assessment of the project’s contribution to the eu’s energy policy goals remains valid. if built, nord stream ii would have to fully comply with applicable eu law, as the project cannot happen in a legal void or only according to russian law. nord stream ii, if built, has to be operated under a legal framework which also takes due account of the key principles of our energy market rules. transport capacity from russia is currently only used at a rate of about 50%. if constructed, nord stream ii would, according to our estimates, increase access transmission capacity from russia even further. in this context, let me also mention the decision on opal that the commission took a few weeks ago. this is the result of an exemption procedure under the eu’s third energy package legislation for the use of an internal pipeline in the eu, and was requested by a national regulator. this decision will allow a more efficient use of the existing infrastructure and, in particular, allow competitors better access to it, thereby enhancing competition. in our view, this makes the economic case for nord stream ii even less compelling. i am now ready to listen to your comments and then respond to them.

in writing. ‒ the objective of this revision of the pension fund directive (iorp ii) is to remove the current prudential barriers in order to foster the creation of a single european market for private pension funds. it is therefore proposed to remove the restrictions imposed by national social security and labour legislation in order to grant these funds greater freedom of investment throughout the union, with the resulting risks and complications in terms of the security of savings and the protection of the rights of beneficiaries. the aim is therefore to encourage the further expansion of private funds to replace the public pension system, which has become unsustainable as a result of austerity policies and the effects of the crisis on public finances. to avoid the risk that people's retirement savings will be jeopardized by speculative finance, i voted against.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the hayes report on the activity and supervision of occupational or business pension schemes. the text adopted defines new measures to optimise the mechanisms for saving for occupational pensions by encouraging cooperation between the member states and the social partners. the overall objective of the proposal is to facilitate retirement saving within the union by strengthening its contribution to retirement income. a key point is the establishment of clear and transparent procedures to enable pension institutions to carry out cross-border activities, while improving discipline and transparency and strengthening the internal market. the proposal increases the capacity of the european economy to channel long-term savings into growth-enhancing investments and enhances the role of epaps as institutional investors in the real economy. the text also sets out structural actions to ensure equal pension levels between women and men across the eu, and also promotes intergenerational balance in pension schemes.
in writing. ‒ the text of the hayes report analysing the proposed directive on the activities and supervision of occupational pension schemes is unbalanced and not acceptable. i believe that this will open the way for new private players from foreign countries to enter our internal market, adding another piece to the dismantling of national welfare planned and orchestrated by the eu. for all these reasons i voted against this measure.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on activities and supervision of institutions for occupational retirement provision because it represented a more straightforward codification of the existing legislative acts and did not add any changes in substance. this better codification is important because the issue of the national pension systems concerns many europeans due to the average age of our society.
in writing. ‒ pension systems need to be adapted across the eu to ensure adequate, secure and sustainable pensions. the proposal to revise directive 2003/41/ec on the activities of epaps will ensure better discipline and transparency for institutions and an increase in their cross-border activity, strengthening the internal market. some business or professional pension funds are large financial institutions and their failure could affect financial stability. at present, cross-border occupational or occupational pension schemes are rare; however, cross-border iorps may represent a growing share of occupational and occupational pension schemes. the revision of the directive is intended to enhance the ability of epaps to invest in long-term assets and to support the financing of sustainable growth in the real economy. without an updated regulatory framework at eu level, there is a risk that member states will continue to develop different solutions, exacerbating regulatory fragmentation. the general objective of the proposal is to facilitate retirement saving, thereby strengthening the contribution of supplementary pension saving to retirement income. the proposal will also enhance epaps as institutional investors in the real economy and strengthen the capacity of the european economy to channel long-term savings into growth-enhancing investments.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today because it encourages member states to introduce the necessary regulation at national and eu level for the secure provision of occupational or company pensions. it is important that member states pursue the objective of ensuring intergenerational balance in pension schemes and increase the protection of the rights of european citizens who are in another member state for work reasons. the report points to the need for appropriate measures to optimise savings for occupational pensions and proposes measures to support member states' cooperation with the social partners and structural actions to ensure equal pension levels between women and men across europe. the functioning of the internal market in this area needs to be improved by means of clear procedures that allow institutions to also carry out cross-border activities.
in writing. ‒ the implicit objective of the revision of the pension fund directive (iorp ii) is clearly to encourage the further expansion and profitability of private funds, so that they gradually take the place of the public pension system, which has become unsustainable due to austerity policies and the effects of the crisis on public finances. i am very concerned about the impact of the new rules on people's retirement savings, which would be highly exposed to the systemic risks of speculative finance, and i voted against.
in writing. ‒ as the demographic developments in the union and the situation of national budgets require it, i express my support for the report. in fact, occupational or business pensions are a valuable addition to the social security pension system, but they cannot replace them given their fundamental importance for the provision of adequate, secure and sustainable pension benefits. member states should ensure the social protection of workers with regard to pensions by providing public pensions enabling them to maintain a decent standard of living and to be protected from poverty in old age and by promoting supplementary pension schemes linked to employment contracts as supplementary cover. the directive is not subject to substantial amendments and aims not only to establish strict prudential rules to provide and safeguard adequate and complete information to be provided to members and beneficiaries of funds, but also to carry out cross-border activities. in future, therefore, pan-european pension funds will be possible thanks to a minimum of harmonization, which will not, however, prevent the member states from adopting additional prudential provisions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this measure as the text provides for minimum harmonisation in this area and should therefore not prevent member states from maintaining or adopting additional provisions to protect members and beneficiaries of occupational or business pension schemes, provided that such provisions are consistent with the obligations of member states under union law. the measure also addresses the issue of worker mobility between member states in a correct way, with a view to ensuring sound governance and correct information for pension scheme members.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal for a directive because i believe that facilitating retirement savings of a business or professional nature contributes to improving and ensuring the security of retirement benefits. the text also provides for appropriate provisions on governance, supervision and transparency and ensures that pensioners are regularly consulted on the state of their pension systems, which could help to encourage individual member states to establish occupational or enterprise pension schemes (epaps) that citizens can trust.

in writing. ‒ this is an important report as iorps (institutions for occupational retirement provision) play an important role in the long-term financing of the eu’s economies and in securing of retirement benefits. the financial importance of iorps cannot be overstated as they have holding assets worth around eur 2.5 trillion on behalf of around 75 million members and beneficiaries, a large percentage of the eu population. this directive aims to ensure that iorps need to have the possibility to operate in other member states while ensuring a high level of protection and security for their members and beneficiaries. it is important that this directive ensure that member states shall make sure that members and beneficiaries are correctly informed about their respective pension scheme operated by an iorp. this is essential so that members of pension schemes have information on, for example, their financial risks, their investment profile, guarantees for the scheme and the options available to them.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the parliament's resolution on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the activities and supervision of institutions for occupational retirement provision (epaps) recast because i believe that in the light of demographic trends in the eu and the situation of national budgets, epaps constitute an important complement to public pension systems. for that reason, those institutions should be allowed to operate in other member states, while ensuring a high level of protection and, in particular, safety for epap scheme members. the cross-border operation of these requires a minimum of harmonisation and above all european supervisory rules, while preserving the possibility for the member states to determine their organisation, according to their different traditions and within the framework of their activities, in compliance with national law and social and labour security. i share the need for appropriate regulation and supervision at union and national level, because these activities are of fundamental importance if the rights of beneficiaries are to be protected. i also share the need for occupational or occupational pension schemes to take account of the intergenerational balance in order to ensure a fair distribution of risks and benefits in pension benefits between generations.

in writing. i voted against this revision of the pension funds directive because, instead of focusing on strengthening the regulation of the investment activities of these funds, which perform a very delicate social function, its priority is to remove the prudential barriers to social and labour protection, which today rightly restrict their cross-border activity and certain types of investment. the aim of the new directive is to promote the creation of a genuine european single market and the further expansion of these private funds, as they gradually replace the increasingly difficult public pension system, without at the same time providing adequate safeguards. we had called for measures to be introduced to prevent the life savings of a person from ending up in the zero-sum game of casino finance. our proposals have been ignored, so today pension funds remain free to operate in unregulated markets and invest in hedge funds or in risky and complex instruments such as derivatives, securitizations or subordinated bonds. it even prevents member states from introducing stricter restrictions on investment than those permitted by europe. i think it is deeply immoral and irresponsible to encourage financial speculation on a fundamental right such as the right to a pension.
in writing. ‒ the revision of this directive aims to remove the persistent prudential barriers that currently limit its crossborder activity in order to foster the creation of a genuine single european market for private pension funds, at the heart of the capital markets union project. in particular, the directive considers the restrictions imposed by national social security and labour legislation to be obstacles to be removed in order to guarantee these funds the widest possible freedom of investment throughout the european territory, with worrying risks and complications in terms of the security of savings and the adequate and effective protection of the rights of beneficiaries. the implicit objective is clearly to encourage the further expansion and profitability of private funds so that they gradually take the place of the public pension system, which has become unsustainable due to austerity policies and the effects of the crisis on public finances. for these reasons, while i have worked constructively on some important aspects of transparency obligations and the requirement to take environmental, social and governance risks into account in its investment activities, i have found it appropriate to strongly oppose this directive, because of the strong concerns it raises about the impact of the new rules on people's retirement savings.

in writing. ‒ the european ombudsman deals with cases of maladministration in the action of the union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies to the detriment of european citizens. in 2015, the european ombudsman's office assisted 17,033 european citizens, offering advice on 13,966 of these cases (81,99%) through the interactive guide available on the european ombudsman's website; 2,077 cases (12.19%) were treated as complaints and 1,060 cases (6.22%) were requests for information to which the european ombudsman's services provided a response. the number of citizens assisted in 2015 was significantly lower than in the previous year (23,072 in 2014, a decrease of 26,17%); the number of complaints remained unchanged but the proportion of complaints to the total number of cases was higher in 2015 (12,19%) than in 2014 (9,01%). overall, it is an active institution, offering a useful service to the public, but it is still little known. it is important to support its work both in the area of transparency of the various eu institutions which take decisions which have an impact on european citizens and in the dissemination of correct knowledge and information on legislation and citizens' rights.

in writing. ‒ this report aims to reform the vat system by proposing the principle of taxation in the country of destination of goods and services, replacing the current country of origin principle, which has not proved sufficiently effective in adequately protecting competition and preventing fraud. this new system is also being extended to crossborder operations. while it contains some positive proposals, some critical points remain, such as the harmonization and total convergence of systems which are not compatible with the values of social justice and equity, sustainable growth and development. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. for these reasons i abstained.
in writing. ‒ the vat rules currently in force date back to 1993 and constitute a system originally conceived as a transitional system which should therefore be subject to amendments in order to complete the common vat system. in europe, the annual revenue from this tax is about eur 1 000 billion, equivalent to 7% of the continent's gdp. i voted in favour of the langen report because i believe that we need to update the rules quickly, not only to meet the needs of growing businesses and e-commerce, but above all to reduce the number of fraud and frauds that occur every year. the text provides for a reduction in the number of products exempt from vat, simplification of the rules, the application of the lowest possible rate and the introduction of a system of payment of vat based on payment in the country of final destination of the goods or services. the commission is also invited to study carefully the consequences of the reverse accounting mechanism, to verify that this procedure actually reduces tax fraud and really simplifies the situation for smes.

in writing. ‒ value added tax in the eu is a significant source of revenue; but your current system is vulnerable to fraud. the requirement of unanimity among member states is, however, an obstacle to reform of the vat system. in its action plan, the commission will present a legislative proposal for a definitive vat system based on the principle of taxation in the country of destination; the european union is not a country of origin. it will also put forward a proposal to modernise vat on cross-border trade and to give member states more freedom, freeing the eu from unnecessary litigation. in general, the commission is satisfied with proposals for enhanced cooperation and hopes for greater trust between tax administrations. a lasting vat system could be the extension of the reverse charge mechanism to the whole of the eu and to all transactions between businesses. it makes the collection and refund of the upstream tax superfluous, reduces distortions of competition and provides entrepreneurs with enormous relief from financing and administrative burdens. the commission's reservations about the use of this mechanism are therefore incomprehensible. it has already proved effective in certain sectors which are particularly vulnerable to fraud in certain member states.
in writing. ‒ after careful reflection and debate in the house, i voted in favour of the report on 'towards a definitive vat system and the fight against vat fraud', as i believe that it contains a number of proposals and points of order which can inspire and encourage improvements to the current vat system, as announced by the commission in its communication of 7 april. as is well known, the harmful effects of distortions in the field of vat are reflected negatively on the basic principles of the union, if one considers the effects on free competition, on the correct supply of eu financial resources, on small and medium-sized enterprises, creating a distorted tax environment. these distortions are combined, with a multiplier effect, with those of tax avoidance and evasion, tax ruling, vulnerability to vat fraud. the first thing to be tackled vigorously is the phenomenon of carousel fraud, the financial lifeblood of criminal activities, which exploit the differences in information between the various member states and generate up to eur 53 billion in vat revenue lost each year.

in writing. ‒ the amount of vat collected is almost eur 1 trillion in 2014 and is one of the main sources of revenue in the eu. it represents about 7% of the union's gdp and provides part of the european union's own resources. from the outset, the current vat system has been vulnerable to fraud and is now largely obsolete. despite numerous initiatives to remedy this, the problem remains, and the commission considers that fraud is responsible for a total 'vat gap' of around €170 billion per year, of which at least €50 billion is due to cross-border fraud. we have fought two important battles on this in the dossiers. the first concerns the further simplification of business operations for smes by harmonising tax policies at european level. the second concerns the promotion of alternative models to the reverse charge mechanism in order to ensure more serious and rigorous policies to combat evasion. since both these two objectives have been achieved in the final text, i am voting in favour of these texts, in order to make a major change in this direction towards a more united europe.

in writing. ‒ eur 170 billion: the eu's gdp is estimated at 7% of the eu's gdp, just below that of a member country such as romania or the czech republic. this is the enormous value of the 'vat gap', or the evasion of value added tax in europe. of these 170 billion, between 45 and 53 billion are attributable to intra-community fraud, the so-called 'carousel fraud', while another 40 to 60 billion are directly attributable to the action of organised criminal groups. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal. it is now some 23 years since the vat directive was introduced in europe - a directive which was supposed to be purely provisional. the commission's initiative brings a long wait to an end. in the words of the commission, the system should be 'simple, fair, robust, efficient and less vulnerable to fraud'. the proposal specifically abandons the country of origin principle, i.e. the rule whereby the supplier of goods collects vat from the customer only within the country of origin, leaving ample scope for cross-border fraud.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep resolution on the ec periodic report 'towards a vat system and the fight against vat fraud' because i believe that the time has come for the member states to give serious thought to the functioning of the current transitional vat system which came into force with the internal market in 1993, in order to develop a definitive system capable of overcoming the shortcomings of the current system, which has generated intra-community fraud and vat evasion for an estimated revenue of between 45 and 53 billion per year and puts an end to the system of derogations which have fuelled fraud and evasion. i therefore shared the ep's call on the member states to facilitate the exchange of information with judicial and law enforcement authorities such as europol and olaf, as recommended by the european court of auditors. finally, i agree with the commission that the vat system must be based on the principle of taxation in the country of destination of goods and services, just as i believe that the single european vat action plan is necessary, which can support a deeper and fairer single market, which helps to encourage tax fairness, sustainable consumption, growth, investment and fair competition.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on towards a definitive vat system and fighting vat fraud as its proposals show signs of strengthening cooperation, increasing mutual trust among tax administrations, and decreasing distortion of competition. supporting the report means that a wide economic burden would be lifted off companies and accounting would become an easier process. on the other hand, the report also emphasizes that companies will not have to be responsible for a ‘pre-finance prior to vat charges’ and finally, that cases of non-payment of vat because of insolvency can be greatly avoided.
in writing. ‒ i would vote in favour of the proposal because i believe that the value added tax system, which has been in force in the european union since 1993, has always been considered a transitional system. the council is required to adopt a directive designed to complete the common system of vat and to phase out the derogations from it. in addition, the current tax system is proving vulnerable to fraud, with the commission estimating that the 'vat gap' due to fraud is €170 billion to date. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ value added tax is a major and growing source of revenue in the european union, with revenues of almost €1 trillion in 2014. it is equivalent to about 7% of european gdp and generates part of the union's own resources. however, commission studies show that each year some €170 billion is lost to fraud, of which at least €50 billion is lost in crossborder trade. the eu's vat system, in force since 1993, was designed as a transitional system and has proved inadequate in combating fraud. it is now more than ever time to define a definitive regime that will eliminate the loopholes that make these frauds possible and, at the same time, eliminate red tape, simplify accounting operations for smes and contribute to the harmonization of tax policies at european level. i therefore voted in favour of the report, so that the commission can make a commitment to this.
in writing. ‒ the value added tax system, which has been in force in the european union since 1993, was conceived as a transitional system. in order to avoid european companies suffering a competitive disadvantage, the 'taxation of trade between member states' scheme must be replaced by a definitive scheme based on the principle of taxation of supplies of goods and services in the member state of origin. the current situation is that non-eu suppliers sell goods to union consumers vat-free thanks to the exemption for small consignments. the commission has therefore committed itself to presenting a proposal to modernise vat on crossborder e-commerce, in particular for smes. the report welcomes the commission's intention to propose a definitive vat system by 2017 that is simple, fair, robust, efficient and less prone to fraud.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the major criticism of the current taxation system is its extreme vulnerability to fraud: the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to take account of the fact that the number of fraud cases in the member states is increasing. this report aims to make proposals to improve the vat collection system and to combat vat fraud. it aims to simplify business operations for smes and, above all, it stresses the need to harmonise tax policies at european level. i share this report as a whole and in particular it is worth highlighting a few key points: the commission has also proposed that the member states should be required to provide for the introduction of a vat rate for financial services and that member states should agree on increasing convergence of vat rates.
in writing. ‒ according to this report, the new value added tax system will have to be based on the principle of taxation in the country of destination of goods and services, abandoning the current principle of the country of origin, which is not sufficiently effective in protecting competition and preventing fraud, in particular so-called carousel fraud. the new system also extends the tax provision whereby the supplier of goods collects vat from the customer to cross-border transactions, thus significantly reducing the possibility of vat fraud. i have tabled amendments calling for greater transparency, accountability of national tax administrations and greater cooperation. however, some critical issues remain, such as the creation of a single european list of goods and services at reduced rates of tax, as well as the harmonization and total convergence of the various systems, which goes in the opposite direction to the values of social justice and equity, sustainable growth and development. the creation of a single, transparent, public and digital european business register to better coordinate vat is also lacking, and there is no reference to greater accountability of the banking system, as i had requested in the amendments. for these reasons i have opted for an abstention.
in writing. ‒ the report assesses the eu action plan against illegal wildlife trafficking developed as part of the eu's response to the 2030 agenda (sustainable development goal 15). this action plan will strengthen the union's role in the global fight against illegal wildlife trafficking by setting a number of priorities: the prevention, application of the existing framework, cooperation and recognition of the european union as the destination market and as the point of origin and transit for wildlife products. in addition, it is called for a total and immediate ban at european level on the trade, export or re-export to non-eu destinations of ivory and rhino horn. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ wildlife trafficking generates an estimated €20 million in revenue each year. it is the fourth most lucrative criminal activity after drug trafficking, human trafficking and arms trafficking. rhinoceroses, elephants, great apes and tigers are just some of the animal species most affected by poaching, with irreparable damage to ecosystems and biodiversity. the bearder report, which parliament adopted today and which i support, calls for a total and immediate ban at european level on the trade, export or re-export of ivory and rhino horn. the union and its member states should strengthen cooperation with the financial sector, engage with social media platform operators, search engines and e-commerce platforms and step up controls to stop illegal wildlife trade on the internet. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment from harmful organisms.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on new opportunities for small businesses providing transport services for passengers and goods. this own-initiative report analyses the challenges and opportunities for small businesses in the transport sector, particularly in the context of the collaborative economy. the growth of the digital economy and the emergence of platforms must be seen as great opportunities to foster growth, fair competition within a clear legal framework. the two major challenges for smes are to adapt to the changes taking place and to respond to the needs of society through sustainable solutions that take account of the respect for the environment.
in writing. ‒ this resolution takes note of the shortcomings identified during the 2015 presidential and 2016 parliamentary elections and calls on the belarusian authorities to resume electoral reform activities in the framework of a broader democratisation process and in collaboration with international partners. it also urges belarus, as the only country in europe still applying the death penalty, to join the global moratorium on the execution of the death penalty as a first step towards its final abolition. finally, it expressed concern at the security problems raised by the construction of the belarusian nuclear power plant at ostrovets, less than 50 km from vilnius, the capital of lithuania, and close to the polish border. stresses the need for comprehensive international oversight of the project implementation to ensure compliance with international nuclear and environmental safety requirements and standards. however, there are many points which need to be clarified and that is why i have decided to abstain.

in writing. ‒ belarus is an undemocratic state where the death penalty, the systematic repression of dissent and the harassment of opposition are still in force. since its independence from the soviet union, there have been no free elections in the country, which has always been ruled by alexander grigoryevich lukashenko. in recent years, there has been a moderate improvement in living conditions and respect for human rights in the country, thanks to constant pressure from the european union and international bodies. however, this progress is not enough and belarus still remains subject to an authoritarian and nationalist government. the european union must continue its cultural, political and diplomatic efforts to help the belarusian people to progress along the path of democracy and to peacefully integrate into the international scene.

in writing. ‒ belarus is often referred to as 'the last dictatorship in europe'. its president, alexander lukashenko, has been elected with incredible majorities since 1991, while his party regularly wins 110 out of 110 seats in parliament. belarus is also the only country on the european continent that still applies the death penalty: at least four people have been sentenced to death since february and some 400 people have been executed since the country gained independence in 1991. i abstained on the final vote.
