madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the control of declarations of financial interests and, more generally, of potential conflicts of interest concerning the members of the commission cannot be confined to the appointment procedure alone. any substantial change in the financial interests of a commissioner in office or any allocation of responsibilities between the members of the commission must be subject to a procedure of examination by parliament. the declaration of financial interests must include any current or past interests or assets of a financial, professional or personal nature, including extended family, over the last two years. the commission must review and tighten the code of conduct to adhere to high ethical standards and ensure that the declaration of financial interests provides parliament and the public with accurate information. it is essential to extend the period of incompatibility from the current 18 months to at least five years for commissioners and the president of the commission. stricter standards are certainly not sufficient to ensure ethical behaviour, but they are undoubtedly an indispensable starting point towards a more transparent relationship.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the european centre for disease prevention and control reports that from 2012 to 2015, the phenomenon of antibiotic resistance has increased enormously. the united nations is calling antibiotic resistance a public health emergency on par with ebola and aids, which are being celebrated on world aids day tomorrow. the misuse of antibiotics is therefore another major european and italian challenge, exacerbated by the overuse of antibiotics in livestock farming. italy is the third largest european user of antibiotics in livestock, with critical cases in intensive care units. 71% of the milk sold in italy goes to farm animals and 94% of the treatments are mass-produced. this mode of use makes the emergence of superbugs increasingly likely, as does the risk of spread from livestock to humans, raising the number of deaths due to their resistance, some 7 000 in italy alone. so there is no other way to counter antibiotic resistance than to significantly reduce it. i call on the commission to adopt guidelines on the correct use of antibiotics in humans and animals and to do more in the implementation and enforcement of measures and in the coordination of health and agricultural policies, to increase the effectiveness of european action against antibiotic resistance.
president-in-office of the council. – mr president, commissioner, honourable members, you have invited the council to intervene on a topic of common concern: how to combat racism, xenophobia, homophobia and other forms of intolerance. we very much share your preoccupation. the evidence from different sources such as the eu agency for fundamental rights and the council of europe confirms an alarming increase of intolerance and hatred in europe. there might be several reasons explaining this worrying phenomenon, but let me be clear on this: there can be no justification for it. the eu has adopted specific legislation on combating intolerance and hatred, in particular the 2008 framework decision on combating racism and xenophobia. the presidency is aware that the commission is currently looking into the national laws of the member states to assess the framework and to ensure its correct implementation. only a few months ago, in june, the council reminded member states of the need to ensure the effective transposition and implementation of the framework decision and other relevant laws at national level to counter the plight of hate crimes. in addition, the council asked member states to develop effective methods to report and ensure proper recording of hate crimes. it is also worth mentioning that the council has adopted a directive that prohibits discrimination on grounds of racial or ethnic origin. it has been in place for more than 15 years and it is an important tool in the fight against racial discrimination. as for the future: we need to combine our actions and strengthen the existing cooperation between institutions. in this context, i would like to recall the important step made last june, when the council responded positively to the commission’s list of actions to advance lgbti equality. the council invited the commission to promote the measures outlined in that list and report regularly on the progress achieved. the council has likewise invited the member states to take action to combat discrimination on the grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity. the council has also consistently supported the efforts of the eu and its member states to improve the situation of the roma, which is europe’s largest ethnic minority. moreover, in the context of interinstitutional cooperation, the council has supported the ambitious plan of the new commission high-level group seeking to develop with member states concrete practices and tools to improve responses to racism, xenophobia and other forms of intolerance. we also welcome the ongoing eu-level dialogue with major it companies, in cooperation with member states, to address online hate speech. last but not least, we should remember and commend the remarkable work done by the fundamental rights agency in this field. let me stress once again that racism, xenophobia, homophobia and other forms of intolerance are incompatible with our common values and principles. according to the legal framework in place they can even constitute a crime that should be prosecuted. there is indeed no exception from this for politicians abusing the freedom of expression by inciting to violence or hatred. our role – and on this i count on your support – is to remind ourselves of our responsibility for what we say. words have power, including the power to harm. for this reason, freedom of expression has its limits. it is our common responsibility to find the right balance, and this is never an easy task. i look forward to your debates, honourable members, and i thank you for your attention.
member of the commission. – mr president, commissioner jourová sends her apologies for being unable to attend this morning. she asked me to replace her and i am glad to do so. increasing fear and high rates of verbal and physical violence against ethnic, religious or other minorities across europe are – and remain – a major concern. as we never get tired of reiterating, the commission condemns all manifestations of racism, xenophobia, homophobia and all other forms of intolerance as these are incompatible with the values and principles upon which the european union is founded. i personally believe that we all, collectively and individually, have the duty to fight against intolerance and hatred and reject all of its expressions. political and opinion leaders bear, in this regard, a particularly important responsibility since racist, xenophobic and other attitudes of intolerance expressed by leaders are, by their very nature, incompatible with the responsibilities they are called upon to fulfil. they also contribute to a climate in which hatred and intolerance become normalised. history should have taught us to be wary. but for those who live in the here-and-now, very recent events have shown that this is not simply a theoretical issue, but a very real danger. i commend the efforts that this place, the european parliament, makes in ensuring that incitement to hatred pronounced by its members is taken seriously and addressed. public condemnation of racism and xenophobia by the authorities, political parties and civil society contributes to acknowledging the seriousness of these phenomena and actively fighting against racist and xenophobic speech and behaviour. in the commission prevention and the fight against racism, xenophobia and all other forms of intolerance are shared priorities. the fact that we devoted the first annual colloquium on fundamental rights to combating racism and intolerance last year reflects that commitment. the commission appointed two commission coordinators to contribute to combating hate crime, hate speech and intolerance by engaging and listening to the community’s concerns with regard to two particular forms of racism and xenophobia which have reared their heads: anti-semitism and anti-muslim hatred. to give one illustration, in 2015 jews were the target of 40% of all racist crimes committed in france and, as the november fundamental rights agency report on hate crime and the current migration situation puts it, muslims experience increased hostility as they are often perceived as perpetrators or sympathisers of terrorist attacks or for being part of a refugee movement seen as threatening safety and security. the commission is acutely aware of this developing narrative and will continue to speak out forcefully against such stigmatisation and incitement to hatred against certain communities. we are also working with member states to ensure they effectively enforce the legislation criminalising illegal hate speech, with particular regard to the eu’s framework decision on combating racism and xenophobia by means of criminal law, which concerns, as you know, the public incitement to violence and hatred on grounds of race, colour, religion, descent, national or ethnic origin. this legislation applies to incitement to violence or hatred, online and offline, including statements by political and opinion leaders. in the bilateral dialogues we have with member states to ensure the correct transposition and implementation of this instrument, we have raised a series of issues and concerns. as a result, in the past two years, six member states have made amendments to their criminal law to bring their legislation in line with the framework decision. commissioner jourová strongly reiterated the importance of ensuring correct transposition and effective implementation of the instrument at the justice and home affairs council on 14 october and urged national governments to do everything possible to ensure that national provisions can be swiftly and fully aligned to the eu rules and, just as importantly, that they are applied in practice. member states’ law enforcement authorities and courts remain competent to investigate, prosecute and try individual cases of hate speech and hate crime. so it is only through working together with the member states and other key actors, including civil society, that we can make a real difference on the ground, supporting national efforts to ensure implementation of the rules and to set up effective policies to prevent and combat this phenomenon. it is a matter of building the necessary commitment, capacity and making available resources and tools. the eu high level group on combating racism, xenophobia and other forms of intolerance is a unique platform for the exchange of best practice, guidance, strengthening cooperation and synergies, bringing together the key actors: civil society, community representatives, eu agencies, in particular the fundamental rights agency, and relevant international organisations, including the un, osce and the council of europe. the engagement of the european parliament intergroup against racism with this high level group is very welcome. we need to join our efforts to achieve common objectives. the group is focusing on issues such as how to improve awareness, enhance the effectiveness of investigations and prosecutions, better address under-reporting and ensure adequate victims’ support. the group is discussing forms of intolerance in order to develop and improve targeted responses. one priority for the high level group is to help all member states develop sound methodologies for recording and collecting data on hate crimes, which can often go unreported or get mistaken for other offences. this work is carried out by a specific sub-group led by the eu agency for fundamental rights and that met for the first time in october. we have also taken important steps to counter illegal hate speech on the internet. a code of conduct on countering illegal hate speech online was agreed by the commission with facebook, twitter, microsoft and youtube in may this year. we will present a preliminary assessment of the work in this area on 7 december. we are also looking at how to support further the role of the media and ethical journalism in promoting fundamental rights and to ensure that a pluralistic media environment can foster political debate on crucial issues for democratic societies. these and other related issues were at the heart of the discussion at this year’s annual colloquium on fundamental rights, which first vice-president frans timmermans hosted together with commissioners oettinger and jourová earlier in november. furthermore, we have consistently supported concrete projects to prevent racism, xenophobia homophobia and other forms of intolerance under the rights, equality and citizenship programme. through the new call for proposals, which is now open, we are making available eur 6 million for projects in this area. in addition, the radicalisation awareness network (ran) continues to support frontline practitioners and civil society actors to effectively address the challenges of radicalisation and polarisation at a local level. practitioners are concerned about how violent, extremist, racist groups, on one hand, or daesh, on the other, exploit the refugee crisis to promote their own poisonous narratives. within the ran practitioners are developing practical approaches and ways to address and prevent polarisation in schools and local communities with the objective of supporting a cohesive and inclusive society and reaching out to all communities. they will look into more effective ways of countering different types of extremist propaganda, including xenophobic propaganda, also drawing on the expertise within the european strategic communications network. everybody should be able to enjoy their fundamental rights. we are all entitled to the respect of our right to non-discrimination, to human dignity, to life, to integrity of the person, and to protection from violence. that is why the high level group will also include exchanges on the intolerance and violence suffered by members of the lgbti community. all that said, notwithstanding our efforts and the results we have achieved so far, we know there is a lot more to be done. we are ready to report regularly on the progress made and evaluate the need for further actions, and we count on your continued support as well the european union is a party to the convention on the elimination of all forms of racial discrimination, and we are all in favour of it. it is urgent that the framework decision explicitly condemns the islamophobia, anti-semitism, anti-gypsyism and homophobia which are polluting our countries and even our common institutions. it is a serious matter that commissioner oettinger's attacks on women, gays, chinese, become a normal thing. it is also a matter of language, we are not united by abstract values but by precise norms. if there is a union demos, it is because of this regulatory pact: the commission has already made a number of proposals. i think that every free individual, especially in times of high immigration, has multiple belongings, multiple identities. assimilation has a unique identity, it breeds violence. i would prefer to see integration in accordance with the rules rather than the word assimilation.

in writing. ‒ this report aims to change the scope of article 136 of regulation (eu) no 952/2013 i.e. customs code by distinguishing between union and non-union goods. the first port of call for many goods from non-eu countries is not the place where the goods are destined, but other ports where fuel is often cheaper. this means that different rules and obligations apply to ships and the cargo they carry, depending on the first port of call (even if different from the actual port of destination). this is likely to result in import duties and other charges not being collected correctly and in veterinary and plant health checks not being carried out effectively. i voted in favour of this resolution to overcome these differences.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the grapini report on the union customs code as regards goods temporarily removed from the customs territory of the union by sea or air. this is an important text that aims to fill a gap in regulation (eu) no 952/2013. the current wording of article 136 of that regulation has in fact had negative consequences for the customs authorities, which have encountered several obstacles in the performance of their supervisory functions. today they are not in a position to collect import duties properly, to apply non-tax measures such as health checks properly and to identify risks associated with goods arriving at the various ports and airports in the eu. the amendments will ensure that the legislation is more effective, that equal treatment of goods is restored and that the overall action of the authorities is strengthened.
in writing. this measure will enable the customs authorities of the member states to carry out the necessary customs surveillance activities on goods which only temporarily leave the territory of the eu. the text is acceptable and i therefore intend to support it with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the provisions of regulation (eu) no 952/2013 of the european parliament and of the council establishing the union customs code have revealed certain shortcomings in its drafting. for article 136, the competent authorities of the member states do not have a legal basis for applying provisions concerning the lodging of the entry summary declaration, the notification of the arrival of a ship or aircraft, the transport and presentation of goods to customs, the waiting for an authorisation before unloading or transhipping the goods, temporary storage. in the absence of a clear legal basis for requiring the presentation of goods to customs authorities, the latter are effectively hampered in their customs supervision functions, insofar as they are unable to correctly collect import duties and other charges, correctly apply non-fiscal measures such as health checks, identify risks related to goods arriving at their ports or airports. the current proposal to amend article 136 aims to fill this gap and to ensure equal treatment of goods.
in writing. ‒ in today's vote i gave my consent to the amendment of the union customs code which gives the competent authorities of the member states a legal basis for the application of provisions concerning goods which have temporarily left the customs territory of the union by sea or air. in the absence of a clear legal basis, customs authorities are effectively hampered in their customs supervision functions, being unable to properly collect import duties and other charges, and to properly apply non-tax measures such as health checks, and to identify risks related to goods arriving at their ports or airports. the amendment aims to fill this gap, to ensure equal treatment of goods and to restore the legal basis established by the old customs code.
in writing. ‒ today, many goods from outside the eu arrive at their first port in the union not at the place where the goods are destined, but at ports such as malta, where fuel is cheaper. a ship delivering goods to the netherlands after a stopover in malta may therefore not be subject to the same arrival obligations in the eu. the current wording of article 136 means that there is no clear legal basis for requiring the presentation of such goods to the customs authorities in the netherlands after a ship has stopped in malta. the basis for this was the following prior to the application of the customs code: regulation (eu) no 952/2013 of the european parliament and of the council of 9 october 2013 on common rules for the internal market in electricity. if the goods are not presented at a dutch port, because there is no obligation, it may be difficult for the dutch authorities to ensure their supervision and there is a risk that import duties and other charges are not correctly collected and that veterinary and phytosanitary checks are not carried out. it is therefore essential to propose a change in the scope of article 136 of the code, distinguishing between union and non-union goods. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the report, for which i thought i would vote in favour, amends article 136 of the new union customs code which entered into force in 2013 in order to simplify and rationalise customs arrangements through standardisation of controls in individual member states. i think that the article in question should be amended, since it provides that certain provisions do not apply to goods temporarily removed from the customs territory of the union by a direct line between two points in that territory by sea or air without a stopover outside the union, thus jeopardising the effective customs supervision of those goods. it is therefore essential that the customs authorities have a clear legal basis for requiring the presentation of goods and for exercising their fiscal and health surveillance functions. i believe that the european union customs code should be designed to facilitate legitimate trade while ensuring adequate supervision to combat fraud.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it will allow the customs authorities of the member states to apply appropriate legal instruments to goods temporarily leaving the customs territory of the eu.
in writing. ‒ i fully support the proposal to amend regulation (eu) no 952/2013 as it has some deep flaws despite having entered into force last may. it is considered that action should be taken as soon as possible in the light of the practical implications of goods temporarily leaving the customs territory of the union by sea or air. the deficiencies referred to are caused by the lack of a sound legal basis allowing the competent authorities of the member states to apply provisions concerning the lodging of the entry summary declaration, the transport and the presentation of goods to customs at the time of unloading or transhipment or temporary storage. this means that the authorities are unable to correctly collect import duties and other charges, to apply non-tax measures such as health checks and to identify risks related to incoming goods. once these critical issues are understood, it is clear that the union customs code needs to be smoothed over as soon as possible in order to operate efficiently.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure to amend article 136 of the union customs code (ucc) in response to the concerns of the customs authorities of the member states. the measure clarifies the legal situation as regards the customs supervision of goods entering the union through a seaport or an airport but continuing their journey. the measure is intended to increase the list of customs control provisions necessary for goods in transit.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the following proposal because i consider it necessary to fill the gaps that have accompanied the entry into force of the provisions relating to the union customs code. in particular, i believe it is essential to ensure equal treatment of goods and to re-establish the legal basis provided for by the previous customs code.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the report to allow customs supervision, to collect duties properly, to provide for health checks and to carry out security checks.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal to amend the union customs code, which is being simplified and made more suitable for cases of temporary transfer of goods leaving the eu territory by air or sea. we have used an accelerated procedure for the adoption of this amendment, but i think it is important to stress the importance of a measure which makes the european economy more competitive.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it seeks to remedy certain obvious problems. assessing the implementation of the rules imposed by the european union is essential to correct their malfunctioning where necessary. the customs union, a great success of the united europe, is not working as we would like and the operators tell us so. the weakest aspect is precisely the controls and checks on goods, which are not effective and have major gaps. this is particularly serious when it comes to health checks: we must not forget how the xylella virus that has affected our olive groves entered europe. it is at customs that the mechanisms for alerting to infected or sick products can and must be triggered. and it is just as serious that we are not able to exercise the right controls over the quantities we import. the european union's trade policy allows imports from several third countries to enter europe, often at zero duty, which does not have to mean zero control.

in writing. ‒ the report analyses several aspects of the european commission's report on the reform of the european union solidarity fund (eusf) implemented in 2014 and highlights how, despite the improvements introduced (e.g. advance payments, eligibility of costs related to the preparation and implementation of emergency and recovery operations, the introduction of a six-week deadline for the commission's response to member state requests), beneficiaries still encounter several difficulties, mainly related to the length of the entire procedure. the member states are also invited to optimise the use of existing eu funds to support investments in the prevention and risk reduction of natural disasters. the report also mentions the 'budgeting' of the annual financial allocation provided for in the omnibus regulation proposed by the commission, which is intended to speed up the mobilisation procedure and provide a more timely and effective response to citizens affected by a disaster. the calls for greater transparency in the whole management and implementation of the eusf are also welcome. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund was set up in 2002 as a tool to respond to particularly severe natural disasters. it is a good example of solidarity between the regions and the member states of the union, which has managed to mobilise almost eur 4 billion in recent years for the more than 70 disasters that have affected 24 member states and the countries in the process of accession. the cicu report, which i supported with my vote today, stresses the importance of the fund as a support for local and regional authorities affected by natural disasters. the 2014 review enabled the eusf to improve its effectiveness through measures such as advance payments and new prevention provisions coupled with improvements in financial management procedures. the text adopted today suggests some improvements and calls on member states to strengthen the means of communication and cooperation with local authorities to support the process of assessing damage and preparing applications. the overall use of existing resources, in particular esi funds, should be encouraged, with a focus on investment policies dedicated to the prevention of natural disasters.
in writing. the report which proposes an evaluation of the european union solidarity fund is well structured and shareable, which is why i wanted to support it with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund (regulation (ec) no 2012/2002) was established to give a tangible sign of the union's solidarity towards countries affected by major natural disasters. the eusf may provide assistance to member states if the total direct damage caused by a natural disaster exceeds eur 3 billion (2011 prices) or 0,6% of the country's gross national income (gni). provisions are also in place to respond to minor regional disasters (1.5% of the region's gdp and 1% for an outermost region). the unpredictability of a natural disaster not only causes discomfort for the people affected, but also raises the question of the speed of action of the public authorities, who have to cope with unforeseen costs. we must therefore make it ever easier for those who are entitled to do so to mobilise the eusf: the availability of funds and immediate assistance after a disaster is crucial to allowing the recovery and continuation of productive activities in the affected areas.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report in question, which calls on the commission and the court of auditors to carry out an in-depth assessment of the functioning of the european union solidarity fund (eusf) by the end of the current multiannual financial programming period. the report underlines the importance of redefining the scope of the eusf in light of the 2014 reform, by setting clear requirements for the definition of regional disasters and by increasing prevention strategies. investment efforts need to be stepped up to mitigate climate change and to ensure maximum transparency in the award, management and implementation of the eusf. member states need to improve cooperation and communication with local and regional authorities in order to cooperate more effectively with the european union's assistance.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by mr cicu on the european union solidarity fund. the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was established in 2002 as a valuable tool to enable the eu to respond to major natural disasters and regional disasters of extraordinary magnitude within the eu and in countries engaged in accession negotiations, and to show solidarity with the regions and states concerned. the cicu report assesses several aspects of the european commission's report on the eusf reform implemented in 2014 and rightly points out that despite the significant improvements introduced, beneficiaries still face difficulties as a result of the length of the entire process, from the submission of the application to the payment of the final contribution. the report also calls on the member states to optimise the use of existing eu funds and stresses the need to start thinking about the search for new indicators beyond gdp, such as the human development index and the regional index of social progress.
in writing. ‒ the report, on which i thought i would vote in favour, examines the operation of the european union solidarity fund, set up in 2002 to support member states in the event of natural disasters. the fund, which has already been activated for 72 natural disasters, still presents, in my view, areas for improvement; in fact, the speed of reaction and coordination between european and national institutions should be improved so that financial support can be unblocked quickly. we cannot tolerate the victims of such serious disasters feeling abandoned in the period between the emergency response and the arrival of funds. i also believe that the union's funding should be used for risk prevention and management, in particular ensuring that the reconstruction of works destroyed as a result of a natural disaster is carried out by bringing them back to normal. finally, i believe that transparency in the use of funds must be improved by close monitoring of expenditure and by the publication of the reports submitted by the member states. it would also be important to improve communication with citizens throughout the aid process in order to allow beneficiaries to follow the procedure better for each individual application.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the european social fund to finance emergency situations in the member states. it is worth noting that this fund cannot adequately finance prevention and reconstruction plans because of budgetary constraints. however, the report is limited to a general call for greater synergy between the funds.
in writing. ‒ natural disasters happen when we least expect them; in today's world, we can predict many things, but claiming to be able to control the dynamics of our earth is not one of them. in the light of this certainty, i am voting in favour of the report which assesses the instrument which, since 2002, has made it possible to provide solidarity and adequate and timely assistance to citizens affected by major disasters. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 264 concerning the establishment of the european data protection supervisor. however, beneficiaries still face difficulties due to the length of the entire process from the submission of the application to the payment of the final grant. in any event, it is necessary to remind member states that it is clearly preferable to prevent disasters by means of adequate investments, such as those obtainable through the union's esi funds, rather than having to resort subsequently to the eusf with greater burdens and likely damage.

in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund is a very important instrument that has served the eu very well, in total the fund has mobilised eur 3.8 billion in connection with more than 70 disasters within 24 countries. the fund has been used to mount effective responses to several types of natural disasters, such as earthquakes, flooding, storms and forest fires. the effective use of this mechanism is still, however, hampered by the length of the overall process from application to payment of the final contribution. this can lead to unnecessary and potentially dangerous delays. there is also a need to increase and optimise the use of existing eu funding, for investing in the prevention of natural disasters. this will save money long-term as every euro invested in prevention saved between four to seven euros in disaster management later.

in writing. ‒ the agreement between the european union and the united states approved today marks the starting point of a process initiated by parliament in 2010 to call for stronger measures to protect personal data exchanged for the purpose of fighting crime. the albrecht report, which i support, concludes a six-year negotiation process by defining a number of key points which do not constitute the legal basis for the transfer of data, but which establish a supplement to the security measures aimed at protecting those which are already legally exchanged between the two sides of the atlantic. the text allows data protection authorities to check compliance with the new measures at any time and guarantees citizens the right to be informed in the event of security breaches, to claim damages and to be able to correct inaccurate information. these provisions are supplemented by those which set limits on subsequent transfers of data and on the period for which data are retained. i am convinced that the agreement represents a clear improvement on the regulatory framework.
in writing. this report is a first proposal for an agreement between the united states of america and the european union on the protection of personal information, which recent developments in technology have brought to the fore, especially through the internet and social media. i think it is important to promote this type of bilateral agreement in order to ensure a high level of data protection in the interests of citizens. i therefore voted in favour of the text.
in writing. ‒ the eu-us agreement on the protection of personal data in the course of their transfer and/or processing aims to ensure a high level of protection of fundamental rights and personal freedoms, in particular the right to privacy. this agreement will not constitute a legal basis for the transfer of data. it aims to improve, harmonise and provide safeguards for the rights of the persons concerned. the agreement applies to transfers of personal data between law enforcement authorities in the union or member states and the corresponding authorities in the united states for the purpose of detecting and preventing crime; and covers all transfers of data between those authorities, irrespective of the nationality or place of residence of the data subject. the agreement also provides that each party shall implement its provisions without arbitrary or unjustified discrimination between its own nationals and those of the other contracting party. it also contains provisions laying down the basic principles for data protection; the commission has also proposed to the member states that they should be able to apply the same rules to the use of the data, such as restrictions on use, preservation of integrity and rules for subsequent transfers. the agreement also defines the rights of individuals and the rights of administrative and judicial redress.

in writing. ‒ in terms of content, the agreement, while not perfect, is a step forward from the status quo, especially in light of the fact that personal data is still transferred between the eu and the us. however, some important questions remain open; in particular, judicial review is excluded for certain types of data such as pnr; as an international agreement it takes precedence over eu domestic law and the umbrella agreement rather than the relevant eu legislation on the subject will be the framework for the rights that european citizens can enjoy. the fact that it is an agreement with the usa could also be a political problem in view of the possible ideological hostility to conclude agreements with the usa.

in writing. ‒ the regulation establishing the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2021 (mff) allows the use of the contingency margin instrument, which can amount to up to 0,03% of eu-28 gross national income, as a last resort to respond to unforeseen circumstances, when all other options available within the mff have been exhausted. to meet the needs arising from the migration, refugee and security crisis, it was therefore decided to increase the commitment appropriations for 2016 for heading 3 by eur 240.1 million through the contingency margin, after having already used the flexibility instrument by eur 1 530 million for headings 3 and 4, thus exhausting all the room for manoeuvre within the mff. it is undeniable that heading 3 is under particular pressure, mainly because of the migration and refugee crisis. it is therefore difficult to oppose the request to mobilise these additional resources for the current year, even though the issue of migration has been a major issue for some years now, and should be properly assessed when drawing up the annual budgetary periods. i have voted in favour of this request, since it concerns the current budget.
in writing. ‒ the following draft proposes changes to expenditure in both revenue and expenditure in the 2017 budget. of particular interest are the cuts in cohesion policy funds. the reasons given by the european commission merely point to a delay in the implementation of these funds in the eastern countries. this is very puzzling to me because if it is true that the causes of the cuts in expenditure are delays in implementation, then in the years to come europe may find itself faced with expenditure arising from commitments already made, without having the necessary resources. that's why i decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the fernandes report on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the contingency margin in 2016. parliament considered it necessary to mobilise the contingency margin to meet the new requirements arising from the outbreak of the migration and refugee crisis and the new security framework. the increase in appropriations for the financial year 2016 will therefore exceed the ceiling of 0,03 % of the eu's gross national income, as set out in article 13 of regulation (eu, euratom) no 1311/2013. this exceptional measure will make available an additional eur 240.1 million to be used to meet the new challenges.

in writing. ‒ the commission proposes to mobilise the european union solidarity fund (eusf) to provide financial assistance following a disaster in germany floods that damaged the district of lower bavaria in may and june 2016. the german authorities estimated the total damage caused by the disaster at eur 1 259,005 million. the amount to be mobilised through the eusf is eur 31 475 125, by means of the adoption of an amending budget. in order to help the affected populations and to facilitate reconstruction operations, i voted in favour.
in writing. in may and june 2016, germany was hit by a series of flash floods and extremely intense flooding that caused the destruction of homes, agricultural facilities, businesses and caused considerable damage to various public infrastructure. the authorities estimated the damage at around eur 1,2 billion. 47 000 people in lower bavaria were affected by this tragic event, seven lost their lives and over 2000 were unable to return to their homes after more than two months of flooding. the town of simbach am inn was almost completely destroyed and was without access to water for three weeks. the hohlmeier report, which i supported with my vote today, allows the european union solidarity fund to be mobilised to provide assistance to the areas affected by this natural disaster. this measure will provide for the disbursement of some eur 31 million in commitment and payment appropriations. this is a necessary measure to support the german people in a time of difficulty.

in writing. ‒ larger countries can also be affected by natural disasters, which are by their nature unforeseen and unpredictable. this is the case in germany, which this spring was hit by exceptional rains which caused numerous floods and landslides. damage to public infrastructure (schools, dams, telecommunications networks and roads), private homes and businesses (hundreds of buildings were flooded) was extensive. there has also been damage to agriculture and forests from mudslides, landslides and landslides. the exceptional nature and gravity of the situation have necessitated the use of the european union solidarity fund. parliament must approve the mobilisation of the fund to allocate the amounts envisaged by the commission as emergency aid to the affected regions as soon as possible, since the rapidity of the institutional response to a flood intervention is essential for the resumption of economic activities and the normal conduct of the daily activities of the citizens.

in writing. ‒ the regulation establishing the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020 (mff) provides for a residual instrument - the contingency margin, which can amount to up to 0,03% of the eu-28's gross national income - as an extrema ratio to deal with unforeseen circumstances, should all other options available within the mff have been exhausted. in order to respond to the increased resource needs resulting from the migration, refugee and security crisis, it has been decided to increase the commitment appropriations of heading 3 and 4 of the mff in the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2017, beyond the ceilings set for those headings. while recognising the need for such increases in areas which are currently under particular pressure, it must be remembered that the use of the contingency margin is only a buffer solution, which does not solve the root problems, nor does it address the real need to rationalise the eu budget by focusing on real priorities such as these. for these reasons i have abstained.

in writing. technically, the contingency margin is a last resort tool to raise funds when europe faces serious and unexpected situations, if and only if all other sources of funding available under the mff have been exhausted. the solution of the migration crisis and the problem of the security of citizens are priorities which i share. my support for the call for increased funds for these headings would therefore be obvious if it were accompanied by a real and radical change in the policies in which these contributions are invested. as long as frontex, easo and fami are financed to encourage the invasion of migrants and not to block their flow, i am not going to vote in favour of measures like this.

in writing. ‒ the regulation establishing the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020 (mff) allows the use of the contingency margin instrument, which can amount to up to 0,03% of eu-28 gross national income, as a last resort to respond to unforeseen circumstances, when all other options available within the mff have been exhausted. in order to meet the needs arising from the migration, refugee and security crisis, it has been decided to increase the commitment appropriations of heading 3 and 4 of the mff in the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2017 beyond the ceilings set for those headings: the commission has therefore resorted to both the flexibility instrument and the contingency margin. it is undeniable that heading 3 (security and citizenship) and heading 4 (europe's role in the world) are currently under particular pressure, mainly because of the migration and refugee crisis. it is therefore difficult to oppose the call to mobilise these additional resources, but the use of the contingency margin is only a buffer solution, which does not solve the root problems, and which does not even address the real need to rationalise the eu budget by focusing it on real priorities such as these.
in writing. ‒ the regulation establishing the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020 (mff) authorises the use of the flexibility instrument to allow the financing of clearly identified expenditure which could not otherwise be financed within the available ceilings of one or more mff headings. the european commission, after considering all possibilities for reallocating appropriations, proposes to mobilise the flexibility instrument in 2017, for an amount of eur 530 million over the ceiling, to finance measures to manage the migration, refugee and security crisis. while i am in favour of maximum flexibility within the mff and aware of the importance of tackling the migration crisis, i remain opposed to the use of these 'special' instruments provided for by the mff, instead of seeking reallocation from less priority budget lines. i have to say that i am not in favour of the commission's proposal, but i would like to say that i am in favour of the commission's proposal.

in writing. ‒ this report intends to enter in the general budget of the union for 2017 an amount of eur 50 million in commitment and payment appropriations for the payment of advances under the european union solidarity fund (eusf), in order to ensure a faster response in the event of future natural disasters. this advance, which may not exceed 10% of the planned financial contribution and in any event eur 30 million, is granted at the request of a member state, following a preliminary assessment by the commission. the possibility of providing for advances is a positive change compared to the initial version of the eusf regulation. for these reasons i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ as you know, the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was set up to enable the union to respond to emergency situations caused by natural disasters of recognised severity, as well as to demonstrate in concrete terms the solidarity of the european institutions with the regions affected by these events. the fund may provide financial support to member states and countries involved in accession negotiations which have been affected by major natural disasters, i.e. where the total direct damage caused by the disaster exceeds eur 3 billion. the fund may also be mobilised in the event of a regional disaster. enabling the eusf to be mobilised quickly means reducing the time needed for economic intervention in the event of major natural disasters and providing concrete assistance to those affected. it is an act of responsibility that we must all agree to.

in writing. ‒ central italy has been hit, since august 2016, by a series of earthquakes of considerable intensity that have devastated cities, seriously damaged local and regional infrastructure, compromised economic activities and, above all, destroyed part of the great historical and cultural heritage that was preserved in the territory. the peak of seismic events occurred with the october 30 earthquake, with a magnitude of 6.5 on the richter scale. some 400 people were injured, 290 people lost their lives and over 100,000 residents were forced to flee their homes. the joint resolution adopted today by parliament, which i strongly support, is an important signal of the union's concern for our country and the areas tragically affected by the recent earthquakes. the text calls for the exclusion of investments in post-earthquake reconstruction from the calculation of the deficit provided for in the stability pact and for all available eu funds to be used to help earthquake-hit areas. the european commission has already announced an initial disbursement of aid worth eur 30 million from the solidarity fund which will be voted on shortly by parliament.
in writing. ‒ in recent months, central italy has been hit by several earthquakes, the most severe of which occurred on 30 october: it was the strongest earthquake to hit the european union since 1980. it is important that we continue to act with the speed and professionalism we have seen in these months into the future: the european union must continue to show the whole of its solidarity, both moral and material, to the affected territories. the budgeting of the annual financial allocation of the european union solidarity fund (eusf) is certainly going in the right direction, but the commission needs to speed up the procedures as much as possible and to advance the disbursement of the support funds. the european agricultural fund for rural development (eafrd) will certainly be useful in supporting agricultural activities that have been damaged by earthquakes but it is crucial to create synergies between all available instruments, including the european structural and investment funds (esi funds) and to ensure that resources are used effectively for reconstruction activities and all other necessary actions, in full cooperation with the italian national and regional authorities. a more humane, more united and closer europe also depends on how it responds to situations like this.

in writing. ‒ in the plenary session in brussels, we approved parliament's resolution on the situation in italy following the earthquakes. it is a very positive resolution, which recognizes - in view of the extraordinary exceptional nature of the italian case - both the efforts being made by the government and the need to be better prepared for the risks of extraordinary events. the proposal to amend the regulation on the solidarity fund is certainly a step forward, since it speeds up the procedures, simplifies them and makes the disbursement of funds more immediate than the decision taken. i voted in favour of this resolution because it not only meets the needs of the italian people, but also responds to the european need to allow a strategic plan for security, facilitating and derogating from the rules of the stability and growth pact. i therefore consider it essential that paragraphs 6 and 7 be adopted, which call for the greatest possible flexibility and stress the urgency of excluding from the stability and growth pact investments made through the structural funds to secure the most vulnerable territories and areas.

in writing. ‒ despite the heroic efforts made by civil protection forces the earthquakes in italy have led to the tragic loss of 290 lives and an urgent need to provide relief and reconstruction to the affected areas and to the 100 000 people displaced by the disaster. due to the costs of this disaster, it is very important that italy receive increased flexibility in its deficit calculations – this important issue is included in paragraph 6 of the resolution. this paragraph also rightly calls on the italian government to ensure that extra resources provided are used to the benefit of those affected and displaced by this tragic disaster. another key paragraph in the resolution is paragraph 7, as it calls on the commission to evaluate investing in sustainable reconstruction and other forms of important anti-seismic projects. these investments should be co-financed with esi funds and excluded from the deficit calculations in regard to the stability and growth pact. this is very important, as it would be wrong to restrict necessary short-term and emergency expenditure on behalf of the affected citizens and their communities.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it contains an important principle: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the budgetary constraints are not applied to reconstruction expenditure and to prevention expenditure. because while it is true that earthquakes, unfortunately, like other catastrophes, are not predictable, it is demonstrated the inadequacy of public structures and houses in the major italian seismic areas. we don't know where or when the next earthquake will strike, but sadly we know that it would be, for the umpteenth time, a terrible tragedy. we are not asking europe to replace our local administrations or to take responsibility for them, we are asking europe to enable our governments and our regions to invest, to rebuild, to modernise, to provide security, without this weighing on those budgetary constraints, which are no longer constraints but obstacles.
in writing. ‒ with today's vote we have shown our full solidarity with the thousands of people affected by the earthquakes in central italy. the solidarity machine worked perfectly thanks to the timely mobilisation of the voluntary civil protection units and the coordination of local, regional and national authorities. reconstruction will take time and will have a significant impact on national finances. italy, like no other country facing a similar catastrophe in the future, can be left alone in this reconstruction effort. we therefore ask the commission to consider excluding from the calculation of national public deficits under the stability and growth pact investments in sustainable reconstruction and earthquake prevention. the existing european funds which allow for investment in the prevention of natural disasters and for the consolidation of reconstruction projects will be used to the best of our ability to achieve the long-term sustainable development of earthquake-hit areas. we call on the commission, however, to take all necessary steps to examine requests for assistance from the union solidarity fund as soon as possible.

in writing. in the earthquakes that struck italy between august 24 and october 30, more than 400 people were injured, 290 lost their lives, and 100,000 were displaced from their homes as a result of these events. these seismic events have damaged local infrastructure, ruined historical and cultural heritage and damaged economic activities, in particular smes, agriculture and the potential of tourism and hospitality industries. the state of emergency must therefore be recognised and all necessary measures taken to provide rapid and effective funding through the european union solidarity fund. consideration should also be given to the possibility of using the european rural development fund to support rural areas and agricultural activities that have been affected by earthquakes. today's resolution confirms our call for immediate aid and for reconstruction costs to be outside the constraints of the stability pact. our appeal now goes to the italian state: we must work to give a future to the destroyed villages, with seriousness, security and maximum transparency!

in writing. ‒ the recent events involving former european commission president josé manuel barroso and energy commissioner miguel arias cañete have opened up new thinking at eu level about possible conflicts of interest involving eu top officials. the durand report, which i supported with my vote, addresses this issue by asking the commission to revise the code of conduct for commissioners. it is necessary to ensure that declarations of interests provide a complete picture of their financial situation, their activities and those of their family members. in the event of a conflict, the president should follow parliament's recommendations or allow parliament to recommend a vote of no confidence or to deprive the commissioner of his pension benefits and rights. the commission is also proposing to extend the period of reflection for former commissioners from 18 months to at least 36 months, the time that must elapse before they can take up private sector roles in their areas of competence. these are coherent measures which can extend the role of parliament, ensure greater transparency of the institutions and increase the confidence of the citizens.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament's rules of procedure, in annex xvi to the guidelines for the approval of the commission, provide that 'parliament may request any information relevant to the adoption of a decision on the qualifications of commissioners-designate and expects full information as regards their financial interests. the declarations of interests of the commissioners-designate shall be referred to the committee responsible for legal affairs for examination.' however, that annex does not specify the exact scope of the examination by the legal affairs committee: it is not clear whether the examination should be limited to a formal analysis of the information provided or whether it should be an in-depth analysis. this lack of clarity has led to major difficulties (also relevant to the appointment process of the current european commission). the committee on constitutional affairs of the european parliament, which is responsible, among other things, for the interpretation of parliament's rules of procedure, therefore needs to clarify this. the aim of this work must be to ensure a transparent procedure and the greatest possible information for the citizens, who have the right to know and evaluate who is called upon to lead them.

in writing. ‒ the revolving door principle also affects the european commission, as was demonstrated by the case of former president josé manuel barroso, who joined the giant goldman sachs shortly after the end of his mandate in the european institution. the problem of conflict of interest is very broad. without going back to the mass resignation of the santer commission over allegations of corruption involving some of its members, it is enough to recall neelie kroes, vice-president of the commission between 2004 and 2010, who during her tenure was a director of an offshore company in the bahamas. juncker's refusal to publish decisions on the post-term activities of former commissioners at the ombudsman's request is certainly not helpful. the european parliament calls on commissioners to declare any current or past financial interests of their own or their family members, their assets, liabilities and any affiliation to non-governmental organisations and secret societies which may interfere with the exercise of their public functions. this request is made to strengthen the ethics and transparency of the institutions and to ensure the impartiality, integrity, diligence, honesty, accountability and discretion of the governing body of the european union. for these reasons, my vote is in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of your proposal because i fully accept the principle of integrity and the principle of independence of the members of the commission as laid down in the treaties, in which the two principles mentioned play a central role. the investiture in eu institutional roles must always be consistent with the public interest, marginalizing, and even eliminating, the existence of interests which might be incompatible with the office held. to remove any doubt about a conflict of interest is to reaffirm the independence of the commission itself and to give it new strength and credibility in the eyes of european citizens as well as the other institutions of the union. it is therefore important that the verification of the absence of conflicts of interest within the commission be placed on a different level from the assessment of the competences of commissioners and that this assessment be carried out not only at the time of appointment but also in those cases where a substantial change in the financial interests of the commissioner occurs during his term of office. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. with this resolution, the european parliament strongly calls for stricter control rules on commissioners' declarations of interests. the proposed measures are designed to increase the level of transparency and accountability of the european institutions, which are essential requirements for maintaining and strengthening the bond of trust with citizens. commissioners-designate should also be required to declare any contractual relationship and financial interests of family members. in the event that there is no certainty that there is no conflict of interest, the appointment of the commissioner concerned should be suspended. if, on the other hand, a conflict of interest is found, the juri committee may indicate the measures necessary to resolve it, such as the waiver of the financial interests in question and, in the most serious cases, it may decide on the incapacity of the commissioner-designate to perform his duties. from the appearance of commissioner cañete in the panama papers to the discovery that former commissioner kroes ran an offshore company in the bahamas, there have been too many scandals involving high-level figures in the european commission. when we talk about fighting corruption and tax evasion, we must be sure that such cases cannot happen again and that these new rules will make it possible to prevent them.
in writing. ‒ the following report analyses the 2013 directive on safety of operations at sea. the content analysis is quite critical. i agree that the lack of clear references to the civil liability of natural and legal persons and to criminal liability for accidents at sea is a negative aspect. another rather controversial aspect of the directive is the lack of an adequate financial guarantee for environmental disasters. i voted in favour of the proposal because i am very concerned about the protection of the environment and especially our seas.
in writing. ‒ 90% of oil and 60% of gas produced in europe comes from offshore operations. these activities are now taking place in increasingly extreme environments, further from the coast and in deeper waters. the increased difficulties also entail a possible increase in risks, which must therefore be properly assessed and avoided in order to avoid devastating consequences for the environment, the marine economy and coastal areas. the chrysogonos report, which i supported today, deals with liability, compensation and financial guarantees in the event of damage arising from offshore oil operations. the text calls on the commission to work closely with the member states to ensure the general updating of compensation and financial guarantee schemes. in particular, it called for provision to be made for claims for traditional damage caused by accidents, for an effective system to be set up for the management of payments and for operators and other responsible parties to be given adequate financial resources to meet any claims they may have as a result of the damage.
in writing. the chrysogonos report on liability, compensation and financial guarantees for offshore oil operations is balanced, deals with the issue in a concrete way and proposes that the recognition of damage be extended to environmental impact as well as to the more strictly economic-equity areas. that is why i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ offshore hydrocarbon operations are carried out in deep water and some in harsh environments and in areas where the main source of income is tourism. the safety of operations at sea directive was adopted following the deepwater horizon explosion, with the aim of setting minimum requirements to prevent major accidents from occurring and limiting their consequences. however, the directive does not deal with liability for civil damage caused to natural or legal persons and does not address the issue of criminal liability. the definition of criminal offences and the type and minimum level of penalties are not harmonised within the eu. criminal liability should therefore be introduced at eu level, thus leading to improved environmental protection and compliance with safety measures. in the case of claims for damages following an accident at sea in the hydrocarbon sector, the damage is usually purely economic. a close correlation is needed between traditional liability regimes, claims management regimes and the availability of financial guarantee instruments; the commission and the member states must therefore work together to update these schemes.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today because i believe that the absence of an effective system of liability and financial guarantee to cover compensation for damage caused by offshore oil and gas operations represents a serious risk for the member states. i think that an update of the liability regimes in force in the member states could limit the outsourcing of operator liability for accidental pollution to the detriment of public finances. i therefore urge the commission to encourage member states to develop financial guarantee instruments for claims for damages arising from accidents in the field of offshore oil and gas activities or the transport of oil and gas, including in the event of insolvency.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this own-initiative report by parliament which proposes an analysis of the directive on safety of operations at sea 2013/30/eu adopted following the deepwater horizon explosion on 20 april 2010 and the subsequent oil spill, and which set out the objective of establishing minimum requirements to prevent major accidents in the framework of operations at sea in the hydrocarbon sector.
in writing. ‒ the report, for which i voted in favour, assesses the effects of the directive on safety of operations at sea, which lays down minimum requirements to prevent the occurrence of major accidents in the framework of operations at sea in the hydrocarbon sector in the european union and to limit the consequences of such accidents. i believe that the directive should be updated to take account of civil liability such as personal injury, property damage and economic loss. i appreciate that the report notes that the liability regimes available in the member states are having difficulty in meeting the majority of claims for compensation in relation to accidents resulting in widespread pollution damage. in this connection, i believe it is necessary for the european union to have a legal framework which enables claimants, such as ferry companies or fishery processing companies, to obtain compensation in the event of oil spills from offshore installations. i also believe that the european union should raise the current minimum guarantee amounts and go beyond the limitation of the compulsory guarantee to insurance products alone, including bank guarantees, good faith guarantees and, if necessary, guarantees from the insurer.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which aims to ensure that compensation schemes and financial guarantees for offshore oil and gas operations are updated.
in writing. ‒ as offshore oil and gas operations are forced to relocate to increasingly extreme and unfavourable areas, i believe it is a priority to provide precise rules on the liability of operators, compensation and related financial guarantees. i therefore agree with the report, which points out that hydrocarbon sources are increasingly farther from the coast and at greater depths, so that accidents in these environments would have devastating transboundary consequences. in view of the above, i welcome the adoption of directive 2013/30/eu on safety at sea, but i believe that it should be supplemented by precise rules on the subject of civil liability for damage to natural and legal persons. these rules need to be harmonised because national legislation is still applied to these events, which are usually transnational. i also urge the commission to encourage the member states to develop financial guarantee instruments for maritime activities and the transport of hydrocarbons, even in the event of insolvency.

in writing. ‒ considering the key role of energy in ensuring the fulfilment of certain human rights, such as access to drinking water; recognising energy as an indispensable tool for economic development; and weighed the importance of clean forms of energy in determining their sustainability; we support the mcavan report. these considerations are of particular relevance for africa, and in particular for sub-saharan africa. in this region, access to energy is particularly poor, the lowest in the world, but renewable energy sources are plentiful. we also agree with the emphasis on the importance of the sustainable and environmental dimension of energy. the increase in co2 emissions, of which 20% is emitted by deforestation, and more generally the effects of climate change increase the poverty of the most vulnerable regions, which are not responsible for causing the phenomenon. the increase in drought and energy poverty is also aggravating and, more and more often, directly causing wars and migration. in this context, it should be remembered that the groups most affected are the most socially vulnerable. to this end, we share the desire for the integration of a gender perspective in european energy policies. we therefore hope that the commission, adopting an increasingly holistic approach, will pursue greater cooperation with regional partners in this area.
in writing. ‒ sustainable access to affordable energy is the prerequisite for meeting basic human needs and rights and for the development of any economic activity. in africa, 600 million people still lack access to electricity, and that number is rising, as the rate of population growth is faster than the rate at which access to energy is expanding. the vast majority of the continent's energy consumption also comes from the use of biomass, which has a very negative impact on the environment in terms of deforestation, soil erosion and desertification, and on the lives of women, who are forced to make enormous sacrifices to collect wood and prepare meals using outdated and inefficient methods. yet africa is the continent with the greatest potential in the world for renewable energy production, wind and hydro. europe, through its development cooperation instruments and programmes and in accordance with the principles of climate justice, i.e. sharing the burden of environmental policies in a fair and equitable way, must support the efforts of local governments, promote investment and provide technical assistance to ensure access to energy for all.

in writing. ‒ the report proposes to amend and improve the european order for payment system. these amendments are necessary mainly because some member states have not yet applied the regulation, causing very negative consequences for those who want to recover a transactional claim. it is essential to standardise certain aspects of credit recovery, such as the timing of the granting of credit in the various member states, in order to streamline and speed up the processes. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the chrysogonos report on the application of the european order for payment procedure. this is an important text which aims to provide feedback, after ten years, on the application of regulation (ec) no 1896/2006 which established a european procedure in this field. the report presents an overall positive picture of the application of the regulation in the various member states, but also stresses the need to make the regulation more widely used and known by union citizens. the text calls on the commission to present an impact assessment and, above all, to prepare for a future revision of the text aimed at ensuring greater harmonisation in the application of the procedure and removing some of the exceptions currently considered.
in writing. the report on the application of the european order for payment procedure is well structured and does not contain any criticisms. that is why i voted in favour of the text.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of the european order for payment procedure is to facilitate the recovery of sums in crossborder proceedings. it is an optional procedure, i.e. available as an alternative to equivalent national procedures. it may be applied for by correspondence or by electronic means and is enforceable in the other member states. the procedure is automatically issued on application, but the debtor may lodge an objection within 30 days. in the event of opposition, the injunction is terminated and the adversarial proceedings may be commenced. the essential elements for the use of this procedure are the speed with which the injunction must be granted, since the regulation provides that injunctions are issued within 30 days; and secondly, it must be possible to submit the relevant forms online. the european order for payment procedure may be used for interest due in the future, up to the date of actual payment. if the defendant opposes the application, the proceedings may not continue and may be abandoned, continued in ordinary court proceedings or continued in the european small claims procedure. there is no need for imminent changes, but more effort is needed on the review requests.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the application of the european order for payment procedure. as the statistics show, the functioning of the european order for payment procedure is satisfactory, but it appears to be limited in member states which already have such a tool at national level. the report indicates the need for concrete measures and awareness-raising campaigns to involve citizens, businesses and stakeholders in the benefits of a clear functioning of the procedure. the report stresses the need to issue payment orders more quickly, given that the procedure is not currently being applied in accordance with the existing regulation in many member states. the regulation provides that injunctions are issued within 30 days, but in many states the time limit is often longer than 6 months. the report proposes to revise the provisions on the application of the procedure and the exceptional review of injunctions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this implementation report on the state of play of regulation 1896/2006 establishing a european order for payment procedure. the rapporteur rightly pointed out that in many member states the regulation is still being applied very poorly, with negative consequences for those who want to recover a crossborder debt (especially small and medium-sized enterprises). the problems identified include the lack of the possibility to file the request for an injunction in different languages (the number of requests is increasing significantly in the states where it is allowed) and the lack of implementation of the e-codex system which allows for online submission of requests for injunctions.
in writing. ‒ as late payment is one of the main causes of insolvency, putting the survival of small and medium-sized enterprises at risk, the european order for payment procedure is an important instrument of judicial cooperation in civil matters, which is necessary for the functioning of the internal market. however, in some member states the rate of use was extremely low. i therefore believe that more can be done by focusing on more information through awareness campaigns that highlight the advantages of the procedure, such as speed, simplification and cost reduction, compared to similar national instruments. i also think that we should encourage the development of the e-codex system to allow applications to be submitted online, as well as to allow applications to be submitted in other languages. i therefore voted in favour of the report because i recognise the positive results of the use of this procedure in all member states, but i am convinced at the same time that much more can be done by promoting greater harmonisation and removing some exceptions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which aims to facilitate the procedure for the recovery of uncontested pecuniary claims in crossborder civil and commercial disputes.
in writing. i can only say that i am in favour of the application of a mechanism which would enable the recovery of sums arising from debts which are certain, are defined in the amount beyond that due and are not disputed by the defendant, to be carried out quickly, easily and economically. i believe, however, that the european order for payment procedure needs more information for citizens and professionals in the member states, since it is a system designed to simplify, speed up and reduce the costs of proceedings for crossborder claims. it is optional, which makes it a useful alternative to national orders for payment. it should be noted, however, that this report does not take into account the many and very different national provisions and their interoperability, and i therefore encourage the commission to act accordingly. i also encourage member states to issue injunctions within 30 days and to accept applications in foreign languages.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure because the existing regulation on this subject is working satisfactorily and has succeeded in simplifying, speeding up and improving the recovery of crossborder disputed claims. i also agree with the recommendations in the text which aim to reduce the length of the procedure for issuing european orders for payment, particularly for small and mediumsized enterprises.
