in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the report because i believe that the procedure is a useful tool for the business world.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it favours, without however abolishing the procedures existing in the member states and therefore without creating legislative conflicts since the procedure is optional, the easier recovery of sums in crossborder proceedings. the latter are increasingly important in promoting economic recovery policies in order to exploit the full economic potential of the union's internal market. there are many requests for payment orders of this type, some 12 000 and more widespread where such requests are already made in accordance with national procedures. this confirms the soundness of the underlying principles of the report, but also a direction to follow in informing businesses and legal professionals about the existence and benefits of the new procedure.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal because i believe that the application of the european order for payment procedure should be fully implemented. the purpose of that procedure is to enable the best possible recovery of debts which are certain and defined in amount, due and uncontested by the defendant. this type of debt, if not recovered, endangers the survival of small and medium-sized enterprises and causes serious damage to the economic fabric. it is therefore necessary that the injunction procedure be applied in accordance with the current regulation, avoiding any misuse of it and aiming at maximising its functioning as in france, the czech republic, estonia, cyprus and sweden, which endeavour to issue injunctions within 30 days and accept applications in foreign languages. i believe that the aim should be to simplify and speed up the procedure for the recognition and enforcement of crossborder creditor rights in the eu. i therefore voted in favour.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank the council and commissioner bulc, in particular, for their active cooperation, and also the shadows of all the political groups who have contributed during the long months of negotiations, because after three years and two months of work, this negotiation on the fourth railway package, probably the most important railway reform in the european union, has been completed. there was close cooperation between parliament, the commission and the presidency, in particular the dutch and luxembourg presidencies, which opened the trilogue, and all of them made it possible to complete a complex process, but one which went in the direction desired by parliament. we know very well that rail systems are very complex and this is shown, you know, by the number of employees in european companies: in italy there are about 70 000 employees, in france there are about 150 000, in germany 170 000, in belgium there are about 30 000. we are therefore talking about large national companies which, of course, offer the possibility of european know-how of particular value. the figures show that the reform, as it was conceived, would have been the subject of a great deal of debate, but this is natural, especially in those countries which preferred to consolidate their position by avoiding the opening up of the market and the consequences of competition. as i said, the scope of the reform is truly historic, since it touches on all the aspects that remained to be discovered in order to achieve a genuine liberalization of the market. one of the most controversial points in parliament was the separation between the infrastructure manager and the railway undertaking. finally, after many interventions on the text, parliament and council agreed that there should be no complete separation and that existing models can continue to coexist, but that it is important to put safeguards in place to ensure that infrastructure managers are impartial and can operate independently. i would also remind you that, in order to clarify the philosophy of the reform on a point which is also the subject of incomprehensible controversy, the network remains public. the network and maintenance remain public and not just because of the costs that are impossible for any private individual to bear, but as a recognition of a public good that we are committed to protecting. it's the service that's going to the race. and in connection with the structure of the railway undertaking there is a sensitive issue of financial transparency, which is a matter for the european parliament. we have always been thinking at european level about the whole text and we have decided that the distribution of dividends made with public money should not go to the holding companies to avoid private use of public funds, but should go directly to the state. the social repercussions of liberalization, as you will understand, are considerable. the commission has also adopted a proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. i would like to emphasize, and i apologize if i take a few more seconds, that the european parliament's text has for the first time proposed a wording designed to protect railway workers. i would like to thank the house for its support of the railway package and i would like to thank all those who have worked on this reform over the past few months.
i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in the negotiations, but that it should be involved in the negotiations. unfortunately, the data says the exact opposite happened. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the fourth railway package is a continuation of this path, which is wrong and which is why we shall vote against it. it is true, as mr van de camp says, that there was a good debate in the committees, but in the end downward compromises were accepted and social clauses disappeared everywhere, for example the clause on the transfer of workers, the maintenance of employment levels. we will vote against this fourth railway package which, under the rhetoric of modernisation and liberalisation, actually conceals a decades-long backward step in the field of workers' rights, the quality of services, the safety of citizens, which is very important, and also the protection of the disabled. that's why we're saying no. (the president agreed to reply to a question with a blue card (rule 162 (8) of the rules of procedure))
answer to a blue-card question. this is exactly what we intend to do, also in contact with the trade unions in the sector. the rights acquired have been abolished and parliament at first reading, this parliament, had more to do with protecting the rights of workers. all this has been lost in the search for a compromise, provided that it is a compromise, and in our opinion it is a wrong compromise.
on behalf of the efdd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i speak today on behalf of mrs daniela aiuto, who was unable to be here but who wanted to take part in the debate, and i therefore read her message to you. we have supported the three reports on the technical pillar, but we could not do the same for the governance part of the package, because we are disappointed with the result achieved which exposes european services to risks that we have already seen in other sectors, and i am thinking of the airline sector and the alitalia case. while we are in favour of the creation of a single market and the harmonization of rules, we cannot forget that excessive liberalization without proper safeguards can have a negative impact on the european market. we have tried to include internal and external reciprocity clauses, but it has been decided not to do so. we are thus running the risk that, in order to dismantle established state monopolies, we will open up new public and private funds over which, however, we have far less control. the same applies to the protection of workers, who are increasingly exposed to occupational risks linked to new changes of operator and for whom no additional protection has been envisaged. for these and other reasons we cannot support the reports on which we are voting this week.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr sassoli, and all the other rapporteurs for the excellent work they have done. the adoption of the fourth railway package will complete the single european railway area, bringing to a conclusion a process begun ten years ago but which is twenty years behind the liberalisation of the european aviation market. the railway sector has never been able to respond to consumer demands, and has consequently lost more and more market share. the gradual opening of the market, through the introduction of european transparency rules and the limitation of the use of public funding for commercial activities, will improve the performance of rail services and open up new investment opportunities, fostering job creation. the opening up of the high-speed rail market was a necessary step towards making a sector which is struggling to compete with other modes of transport competitive. the increased use of rail transport by european citizens will ultimately contribute to the achievement of the european decarbonisation targets.
member of the commission. – mr president, honourable members, thank you very much for a very frank and dynamic debate. it clearly shows the importance you attach to the railway sector. allow me now to reply to some of your comments and hopefully provide some clarification on what this package delivers. first, let me clarify some of the comments that were made by mr liberadzki and some other members of parliament. on pso, the text clarifies that all existing binding provisions at eu and member state level remain applicable after market opening, as does their scope of application. the provisions on staff transfer of the directive on transfer of enterprises apply to the situation of a change of freight public service contracts if the conditions of the directive are complied with. this would essentially have to be a transfer of assets and rolling stock to the new public service operator. it is also stated that member states can go beyond the level of staff protection, defined at eu level by directive 2001/23/ec, for instance by requiring a transfer of staff and social rights even if directive 2001/23/ec would not apply. moreover, member states are encouraged to assess the need for additional social safeguards in the case of market opening – of course in a reasonable manner. experience shows that they do take action with mandatory measures. the new pso regulation also spells out more clearly the transparency requirements on social rights and obligations, where a change of public service operator contributed to better staff protection. in no way does the fourth railway package lead to less social rights and protection for workers. on the contrary. the original commission proposals were even more ambitious, that is for sure, than what you have on your table today. i know that some of you, including all my liberal colleagues, would have liked to go further in reforming the regulatory framework for rail, but there were also many who were not ready to take bolder steps immediately. in the negotiations, we took into account the diversity of railway systems and structures across the eu, as well as the calls for flexibility and gradual change for the benefit of a single market. the text ready for the vote is what i believe eu stakeholders can absorb and implement at this stage. however, i am also confident that we very largely shared the same ambition for the future of rail and i am convinced that when the package is implemented, it will bring the railway sector into a brighter 21st century. let me now make a few other comments. rail will only be able to contribute decisively to the decarbonisation of transport – and i wish ms deli were still here – if it becomes more attractive, also from a service—offering point of view. this requires new investments, more efficiency and more innovation, and this is what the fourth railway package is about. other transport modes don’t sleep. they are picking up on decarbonisation and i believe in the long run, the differences will be in the amount of investments and in the amount of attractive services offered, so i hope railway will pick up on that and use this advantage, which it still has. let me also be very clear. the package does not address the issue of railway ownership. this is a very important message. there is absolutely no obligation to privatise railway operators. what we are establishing is an equal level playing field and competitive market conditions for the benefit of our citizens and businesses. this is what the fourth railway package is about. in the same manner, national and local authorities will still have the possibility to determine what are the needs for public service. with this package we ensure that the public services are improved and that value for taxpayers’ money is increased. this is why i would really like to encourage you to adopt the three texts by a very large majority being approved in the committee on transport and tourism, and i am really looking forward to your support and positive vote and to really together make this important step forward to finally give the railways a push to be back as a full player in the single transport area arena.
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, thank you to all the speakers, including those who criticised certain aspects of the reform. but i must say that it is a little bit incredible, and i say this with sympathy, that after three years and two months of work and seven months of trilogue, you come to this house to argue that the fourth package calls for privatization: i have to say, this is a little unbearable. i am sorry that there are no colleagues who have spoken on this point, because, as i say to the public, no national or european trade union has ever argued that the fourth package leads to privatisation. there are some comments, for example on transfer, as the rapporteur, mr van de camp, knows very well, but we are not talking about processes leading to the privatisation of anything. we talk about opening up the market, liberalizing services, and, tell that to your people, here the network and maintenance will remain public. that's the philosophy and the outline of this fourth package. we will open the market from 2019, which is why some remarks, such as that made by mr d'amato, are, let us say, out of place, because reciprocity would have been in place during a transitional period, but since we have decided to open from 2019, until 2019 everyone behaves as he has decided to behave. then as regards mr bilbao, who has kindly and diligently followed the whole debate, we have discussed the question of unbundling - because your criticism, the criticism of the liberal democrats is on this aspect - but the economic incompatibility was really very great. and so what we have done is we have given powers to the national regulators and the novelty of the fourth package compared to the previous ones is precisely the power of the national regulators, their centrality in the system and this should make you say that it is a step forward, it is certainly not a step back or to stand still, as mr riquet knows very well who has followed all our work also with great competence, availability and with great experience. i would like to say, mr president, and i would like to thank everyone who has spoken, really, because we have a great opportunity, and i apologize for the time taken. we have the possibility for our companies in a european market to give jobs, to give jobs, not to take jobs away, because we need to make sure that our companies participate in a larger market, because our companies, even the strongest, in their domestic and national markets can no longer do it. that is why this reform is important and why it opens up great possibilities for the european railway sector.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the adoption of this regulation by the plenary is a milestone that is not to be taken for granted. as we know, previous attempts to approve the proposal have failed, which is a sign that this is a very complex and delicate matter which requires great care and caution. the 1 200 european seaports handle more than 70% of imported and exported goods and account for almost 40% of intra-eu trade. that is why the vote in favour of the agreement reached, the result of our parliamentary work with the contribution of all the stakeholders, is all the more important. i thank the rapporteur for his determination and for his acceptance of my request for greater transparency in the customs services. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the port infrastructure is properly managed. i also believe that the choice of legislation for the regulation was decisive, because to have a real impact it is necessary to have the same rules for all member states, which are immediately applicable, and it is necessary to have a certain flexibility in order to achieve the goal commensurate with the needs of the individual port. these factors of financial transparency, liberalisation of services and incentives to competitiveness will enable maritime transport to grow, to the benefit not only of trade but also of its sustainability.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, with more than 1 200 ports in europe, port activities represent 3 million jobs. 96% of goods and 93% of passengers transit through 319 ports on the ten-t network. the proposal for a regulation by mr fleckenstein is in this context, albeit somewhat lighter than the commission's initial objectives. we do not support the full liberalisation of port services, given the inevitable negative consequences on such a heterogeneous sector in europe, but the regulation is nevertheless a step forward. collective actions shall not be considered as interruptions of services justifying emergency measures; the right to strike and minimum services are both protected. the reference to the 2001 directive reiterates the rights of workers in the event of a transfer of an undertaking, as well as the obligations of the transferor and the transferee. the right to training and the provision of minimum professional requirements guarantee the safety and proper performance of services. finally, transparency on the use of public funds, achieved by a clear separation in budgets between public and private funds, will make it possible to trace the use of taxpayers' money and understand the activities for which it is used.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the adoption of the new regulation on access to the market for port services will make european ports more efficient and provide fair competition in a sector which employs three million people in europe. the strengthening of the competitiveness of ports will create the conditions for promoting short sea shipping as an alternative to road transport, with a consequent reduction in user costs. the introduction of general rules for greater financial transparency of ports, legislation which has so far been required of individual member states, is important. the reform will make the costs of port services and infrastructure more transparent, especially in the financial relations between the state, ports and operators. it should be noted that there are some important derogations, such as for drainage services, and some flexibility, such as for piloting services, but the introduction of greater transparency, regulatory simplification, market opening and internationalisation in an intermodal european framework within the ten-t can really be a driver for the recovery and economic growth of the european union.
on behalf of the efdd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we have finally reached a final vote on this matter after years of negotiations. the troubled path of this proposal arises from the conflict between two very broad interests: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fisheries sector is not left behind. the strenuous negotiating effort was, as far as i am concerned, aimed at this. we therefore welcome the limit of 800 metres below which no trawling can take place, and the limit of 400 metres in the case of areas with particularly sensitive ecosystems. these are largely unexplored and poorly understood environments, ecosystems yet to be understood that we know to be very fragile and fragile: and that's why we have to be very careful about treating them as a resource to be exploited. we should never use the precautionary principle more than in this case, and i am not just talking about fishing. we think that in this case, thanks to the work of the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs, a good compromise has been reached and we will therefore support this report.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by congratulating my colleague, mrs isabelle thomas, on her successful handling of a very difficult matter. the main objective was to protect, through sustainable fishing, a particularly fragile habitat where fish stocks are depleted and where species are present that reproduce very slowly. the new rules include a ban on trawling below 800 metres and a limit of 400 metres in the most vulnerable marine environments. fishermen will also have to report the number of sponges and corals caught, as they will be required to move to other fishing areas when a certain quantity is reached. finally, new transparency rules have been introduced, including the obligation to make public the information collected and not only: 20% of vessels will be required to have an observer on board to enable scientific data to be collected. the new rules will apply mainly to vessels operating in the north-east atlantic. it is true that we can always do better, but after more than four years of work we have finally struck the right balance between the needs of fishermen and the need to safeguard marine habitats.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i think it is essential to ensure, as far as possible, the sustainable exploitation of deep-sea stocks, reducing the environmental impact and implementing the information base necessary for scientific evaluation. it is essential to set a bathymetric limit in order to better protect the vulnerable marine ecosystems of the seabed, just as i think it is necessary to introduce strict transparency rules, rules, for example, which may include the obligation to take on board scientific observers and to record catches. another key measure concerns the collection of data and, in particular, the obligation for member states to provide information on the location of vulnerable ecosystems and on european vessels fishing in deep waters, information which should enable the european commission to assess and, accordingly, adjust the fishing zones authorised: it is better to have this evaluation annually. the agreement reached can therefore ensure conditions to avoid negative impacts on vulnerable marine ecosystems and to establish better conditions for more effective data collection. i congratulate mrs thomas on her excellent work.

answer to a blue-card question. first of all, i would like to point out that if we are having a debate here in the plenary, it is thanks to a minority group which has asked for a debate in the plenary, it is thanks to my group in this parliament, the gue/ngl group, which has asked for a debate in the plenary because, let us say, the majority of the european parliament did not foresee that there would be a parliamentary debate on such an important element, namely, what common rules we give ourselves to decide. i remember that we had difficulty in having parliamentary debates here: the european parliament has been denied the right to appeal to the european court of justice over ceta until a few weeks ago. what's the point? that the rules of the european parliament cannot be decided by a majority, the rules of the european parliament are democratic if they protect first of all the individual rights of members and the rights of minorities, which is something this report does not do at all.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i should like to congratulate mr corbett on his excellent work. the general revision of the rules of procedure of the european parliament is based on the need to ensure a better functioning of parliament and to clarify the interpretation of certain rules, with particular attention to not restricting the scope of action of members. i fully agree with the rigorousness and transparency introduced, for example by requiring former members to inform parliament if they undertake new lobbying activities and by providing for the withdrawal of the access cards of registered lobbyists who do not comply with the rules of procedure. i believe that the introduction of the right of a committee to speed up a legislative procedure and the obligation for the committee to reply within three months to requests for initiatives from parliament and, if no reply is given, the obligation for the committee to appear before the committee responsible will make legislative work more efficient. finally, the provision that, in the event of the withdrawal of legislative proposals, the commission is obliged to discuss them first with the competent committee of the european parliament and then, in the absence of agreement, with the plenary.
in writing. during the work leading up to the text tabled in plenary, which introduces amendments to parliament's rules of procedure, the major groups did not adopt a collaborative attitude towards the smaller groups. the requests of the latter to have their rights in the various bodies and agencies safeguarded were not granted and, on the contrary, rules were inserted which restricted the autonomy of individual members and groups. in addition, the issue of transparency was completely ignored during the reform process, which should have been addressed in an ad hoc report that was blocked in committee, so that the amendments it introduced could not affect the revision of the current regulation. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect, and i am sure that the commission will do so.

i am grateful to mr andersson for answering his question immediately, and then we shall vote on mr ferreira's proposal. as regards the president's decision to declare the amendment to which you refer inadmissible, it is a final decision because, under article 232 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, parliament has the power to establish its own rules of procedure on the basis of case law; this means that it can decide on its internal organisation and take appropriate measures to ensure the proper functioning and conduct of its procedures. in this context, parliament may regulate, in its rules of procedure, certain matters concerning its members where this is necessary to ensure the proper functioning and conduct of its proceedings. however, the rules of procedure cannot be used to regulate the activities of former members. hence the president's decision. as regards mr ferreira's proposal, i would like to know whether there are any members who wish to speak in favour of it, or against it. in writing. ‒ despite the fact that the debate on deep sea has been going on for a long time, the vote has only just taken place. the dossier proposes lowering the limit within which trawling can be practised, intensifying controls on board vessels and increasing transparency regulations. it is very important that the institutions commit themselves to protecting and preserving our seas, and i therefore voted against the rejection amendment.
in writing. ‒ technological development has radically changed the methods and forms of fishing, an activity which today can involve areas that were unthinkable just a few years ago and have a strong impact on the environment and biodiversity. the thomas report, which i have supported today, sets out specific conditions for fishing for deep-sea stocks in the north-east atlantic to protect particularly vulnerable marine ecosystems, characterised by long-lived species, slow growth and very long reproductive periods. with this in mind, member states will be asked to provide data on the location of vulnerable ecosystems, which the commission will then have to assess in order to define the fishing zones authorised. the report focuses on transparency and data collection, the obligation to have scientific observers on board vessels and the recording of catches. several penalties are established and a new bathymetric limit of 800 metres is set. deep-sea fishing shall be authorised only in the area exploited by the vessels in the period 2009-2011.
in writing. ‒ the measure is very technical and although it may be generally acceptable, it contains some requirements that could open up future criticisms in the implementation phase. that is why i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ this report sets out specific conditions for fishing for deep-sea stocks in the north-east atlantic and provisions for fishing in international waters of the north-east atlantic. it is essential to ensure the sustainable exploitation of deep-sea stocks by reducing the environmental impact of deep-sea fishing and to improve the information base necessary for scientific evaluation. the regulation we have adopted is going in that direction. the european union will freeze the fishing footprint by defining the area in which deep-sea fishing activities will be allowed. that area includes that in which directed fisheries were carried out between 2009 and 2011 in european waters of the north-west atlantic. in addition, specific sanctions have been introduced for vessels that violate the deep-sea fisheries regulation and no derogations have been made for the control rules.
in writing. ‒ the text, which is being adopted at second reading after three years of negotiations, contains important and positive elements. these include a ban on trawling below 800 metres (up to 400 metres in areas with particularly sensitive ecosystems), increased controls and environmental protection, and stricter transparency rules. i voted for it without question.
in writing. ‒ deep-sea ecosystems and species are highly vulnerable to fishing and increasingly at risk: deep-sea species are characterised by low biological productivity, which means that they can only support low levels of exploitation. there are clear european obligations for the protection of these species and for the protection of the seabed, obligations which the member states are called upon to respect strictly. the report, for which i think i am voting in favour, has the merit of introducing specific sanctions for vessels which violate the regulation on deep-sea fishing and of having laid down new provisions with a view to better protecting the seabed. i believe that the new rules for the recording of all deep-sea catches can be a guarantee of transparency in fishing vessel operations and that the involvement of scientific observers on board can not only ensure a profitable collection of scientific data but also strengthen the link between research and fishing enterprises.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the adoption of a new regulation as it is all the more necessary to put in place effective measures to address the vulnerability of stocks and to establish a sustainable level of fishing that protects habitats and reduces unwanted by-catches throughout the north-east atlantic. in particular, i fully support the introduction of an absolute ban on fishing beyond the 800 metre limit because deep-sea fishing involves the scraping of the seabed. it is also aimed primarily at slow-growing and highly vulnerable fish species, and i hope that this provision will prove decisive. i also welcome the introduction of the obligation to publish information for deep-sea fishing vessels, i.e. those vessels whose deep-sea fishing activity represents more than 8% of their total catches on at least one trip during the year. it is therefore essential not only to establish a catch register but also to commit member states to geographically delimiting the areas where deep-sea fishing is permitted and to provide data and impact studies on the vulnerability of the ecosystem.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure, as the main purpose of the proposal is to establish specific conditions for fishing for stocks in the deep waters of the north-east atlantic and to regulate fishing in the international waters of the north-east atlantic through specific provisions. this new provision will help protect vulnerable deep-sea marine ecosystems, ensure more sustainable fisheries and reduce unwanted catches.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which sets clear and stringent limits to limit the damage of trawling by prohibiting it below 800 metres deep, a limit which rises to 400 metres in the case of areas with particularly sensitive ecosystems. the protection of marine environments, because of their fragility and sensitivity, is of particular importance, especially for environments that are still poorly understood, such as the seabed and deep water.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this compromise solution because i am concerned that the european parliament's intervention should not be to the detriment of those who work in this sector and those who benefit from and live from the fisheries industry, especially small-scale fishing. as i have said many times, together with the trade associations, we must try to find solutions that are less burdensome for the operators, such as the remodulation of fishing gear, spatial-temporal closures and traceability systems. applying the principles of the blue economy to our actions goes hand in hand with countering the illegal practices of those who take vital resources from our seas. the depletion of the wealth of our seas and the limitation of marine resources must not always and necessarily result in limitations without taking account of the economic nature of the sector, on which many families depend. the protection of marine resources is not incompatible with these priorities.
in writing. with this agreement, the eu defines the area where deep-sea fishing activities will be allowed. the demarcated area provides for the application of a bathymetric limit, such as 800 metres, to vessels fishing directly for deep-sea species, or at least one fishing trip during the year, with the aim of better protecting vulnerable marine ecosystems of the seabed. the ep also called for the introduction of specific sanctions for vessels that violate the rules on deep-sea fishing. it has been provided that above 400 metres and in case of catches in vulnerable ecosystems, fishing vessels engaged in deep-sea fishing activities will have to cease their activities and move at least 5 miles away from the catch zone of the ecosystem. the ep therefore called for the introduction of strict transparency rules, including the obligation to provide data on deep-sea fishing vessels and the obligation for member states to provide all data relevant to the location of these vulnerable ecosystems.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the recommendation of my colleague concerning the adoption of the regulation establishing specific conditions for fishing and deep-sea stocks and fishing in international waters in the north-east atlantic area, because, while i share the principle of safeguarding the marine ecosystem, with particular reference to the most vulnerable species, i believe that the introduction of stricter rules in the regulation itself could have a negative socioeconomic impact. i am thinking of the ban on all deep-sea dredging, including exploratory dredging, over 800 metres, which has no scientific basis, and the difficulty of explaining to a bona fide operator in the sector that this formerly legal activity is now unworkable; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment. i appreciate the progress made in the drafting of the new regulation, but i think that more flexibility is needed. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ deep-sea stocks and marine ecosystems have unique characteristics that make them particularly vulnerable to human activities. many species are slow-growing, long-lived, and late reproducers. the new regulation will introduce a number of specific measures to ensure sustainable deep-sea fishing and to prevent damage to the seabed and its life forms, such as cold-water coral reefs, sponge gardens and seamount ecosystems. a ban on trawling at depths of more than 800 metres or more than 400 metres in the presence of a vulnerable marine ecosystem will be introduced, and a 'geographical footprint' will be defined so that fishing vessels can only fish in areas already affected by fishing activities. finally, some control measures such as the presence of observers on board will help to ensure compliance with the rules. i have decided to vote in favour of this regulation because the new proposal strikes the right balance between protecting the environment and responsible management of this fishery.

in writing. ‒ throughout its history, the european parliament has carried out several periodic revisions of its rules of procedure in order to adapt its internal working arrangements to changes in the institutional and political system. the corbett report, which i supported with my vote today, is the result of 18 months of collective work, the aim of which was to draw up a general revision of the regulation to meet the new needs of the institution and to optimise the use of internal resources. the text, which is highly articulated and technical in nature, introduces important innovations aimed at making parliament even more transparent and efficient, strengthening its institutional image and its capacity to listen to the citizens. the following measures are to be taken: increased penalties for members who use defamatory, xenophobic and racist language; the drawing up of more detailed and regular declarations of members' financial interests; the commission has also proposed a strengthening of the code of conduct and an explicit ban on members working as paid lobbyists. written questions, motions for resolutions and calls for a rollcall vote are also more limited. the regulation will enter into force on 16 january 2017.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european union, which for thousands of people fleeing war and hunger represents a promised land of prosperity and civilization, is unfortunately still hiding many skeletons in the closet. we cannot deny that some member states are not exactly the champions of respect for human rights. this house has often been confronted with situations of violence within the union itself, and it is here that we have heard the cry of alarm from citizens who have been abused by their governments. as long as we have to convince some states that closing down television and newspapers, that erecting walls and shooting at borders has nothing to do with the principles on which the european union is founded, as long as all this is still on the agenda of the plenary, it will be necessary to monitor the human rights situation and make amends. it is not violence, repression and the denial of rights that are the support, the pillar of a project which has given us and still guarantees us, fortunately, more than sixty years of peace. and we should remind this to the many, many political movements that incite hatred and violence. that is why i voted in favour of this report.

member of the commission. – madam president, i wish first of all to thank ms delahaye and the shadow rapporteurs for all the work that they have done in producing this report, as well as mr ali for the opinion provided on behalf of the committee on budgets. i would like to congratulate you, ms delahaye, on achieving your first parliamentary report. this report comes at a very good time, when the commission is preparing a communication for adoption next year on the modernisation and simplification of the cap, as announced by president juncker at the agricultural outlook conference last week. i have identified three principles which i believe should guide the new cap: market resilience, more sustainable agricultural production and progress on generational renewal. the issues that are raised in this report go to the heart of the debate about the future of the cap by asking how best to deal with risks and crises in agriculture and reflecting on the whole range of public policy instruments that are currently available. i want to assure ms delahaye that we will fight together for farmers’ livelihoods and that we are on the same political page in this regard. i fully agree with the central thesis of this report that we need to maintain sustainable agricultural production in europe, and for this we need to seek efficient ways to ensure farmers can cope with risks and crises. we all know that risks and crises are inherent in agricultural production, and farmers have consistently demonstrated resilience in the face of adversity. despite this resilience in the market orientation of the cap, there continues to be clear justification for a formal public intervention, either at the level of the member states or of the european union, in order to support our farmers. several interventions by farmers and stakeholders at last week’s european union agricultural outlook conference demonstrated the importance of this message. the report quite rightly acknowledges that the cap has evolved over time and in line with the needs of european farmers and society, and in response to the challenges of the day. however, during the past two years we have experienced particular difficulties in the dairy, pig—meat and fruit and vegetable sectors in particular. thankfully, we are now seeing a recovery in those markets, not least as a consequence of the robust actions that have been taken by the european commission. in response to the crisis in various sectors, we have deployed virtually the full toolkit that is available under the common market organisation and mobilised in excess of eur 1.5 billion extra resources. if we take the example of the mill sector, as many as 24 regulations have been adopted between september 2014 and september 2016. these measures adopted included the opening, extension and enhancement of private storage aid schemes, the extension of public intervention periods and fixed price ceilings, the granting of targeted aid for our livestock farmers, the authorisation of collective agreements on the planning of milk production, and even the introduction of a milk production reduction scheme. we will also remember that we managed to find synergies between the migration and agricultural policies to make sure that milk is distributed to school children in syria. there are also other instruments available to help market actors to become more resilient and sustainable by their own means. i am referring here to the significant progress in market transparency that has been made over the past two years, with dashboards being developed for the main agricultural products, and observatories being established for milk, pigmeat, beef and veal to give market signals to our farmers and our agribusinesses. building on the work of the milk market observatory, these have been a good success in terms of providing accurate and timely information to all of our operators so that they can make market-led and good decisions. the experience has also raised some questions, of course, about the effectiveness of the toolkit available. our responsibility as policymakers is to create an adequate framework to help the farming sector to successfully deal with risks and crises by enhancing its resilience. in my view, there are a number of questions we need to ask ourselves: do the existing tools allow us to act where needed, and to do so quickly enough? should farmers have greater built-in measures to help them in times of crisis on the basis of a risk management approach? and do producers and processors have the ability to diversify their markets, or to find new markets in times of market loss? these are questions, perhaps, that indicate to us the existing tools are not perfect. so we have to continually look at the variety of instruments at our disposal in order to try and improve them. one of those ways is through the provision of a basic income support in order to help farmers within an effective safety net. this will continue as an essential element of any new cap through a system of direct payments, something which ms delahaye’s report calls for. you will by now be familiar with report of the agri-market taskforce whose recommendations have been well received. several of these recommendations, for instance those on market transparency, the improved functioning of producer organisations, as well as risk management, go hand in hand with the concerns that have been expressed in this report. i welcome and look forward to the hearing which the committee on agriculture and rural development will hold next month on the agri-market taskforce report. the recommendations contained in ms delahaye’s report will form part of the debate on the future of the cap, particularly in relation to the adequacy of the existing risk and crisis management tools. in addressing the adequacy and use of these tools, we should consider any obstacles which prevent or discourage their use. this report, then, is a valuable contribution to the debate and i acknowledge the emphasis which the report places on the importance of a common policy. in this context of preparing a new cap which aims to modernise and simplify the policy, i can assure the house that my services will examine this report very carefully and ensure that appropriate account is taken of it and its recommendations.

prices is one of the main causes of the dire situation facing european agriculture and the forecasts are not reassuring. globalisation, the instability and sophistication of agricultural markets, the increasing variability of supply due to climate instability, the increase of health risks and the fragile balance of the food chain will continue to have a negative impact on farmers' exposure to price volatility. a more effective policy is needed, with targeted instruments to ensure sustainable agricultural production, accompanied by fair and remunerative prices that mitigate the negative effects on farmers of exposure to price volatility. it is worth noting that while the european union is reducing strategic support to agriculture, its global market competitors, the united states, brazil and china, are introducing significant and growing public financial support to develop new risk policy models and to provide tools to protect their farmers from the negative effects of price volatility. if we want to protect our agriculture, we have to change the traditional approach. the negotiating power of producers in the food chain should be strengthened through standardised, transparent, balanced and collectively negotiated written contracts, with the aim of combating unfair trading practices, promoting competitiveness and ensuring income stability. to protect agricultural enterprises in a market-oriented cap, it is necessary to further develop climate, health and economic risk management tools, income stabilisation tools, individual provisioning mechanisms, mutual funds and income stabilisation tools. more needs to be done in terms of awareness and training, as well, in relation to existing risk management tools. i call on the commission to adopt, in close cooperation with the national authorities and farmers' associations, a plan to raise awareness of the risk management tools available under the second pillar of the cap. the countercyclical aid is a real novelty of the motion for a resolution we are discussing, it is intended to support farmers' incomes when unfavourable years are depressing their incomes and it is a key and innovative instrument for european policy which i hope the european commission will be able to evaluate properly, providing for greater flexibility in annual budgets or financial mechanisms which will enable the european farmer to receive the difference between a target price and the price actually received from the market. the access of farmers to credit must also be facilitated, and greater use must be made of financial instruments, possibly with the involvement of the eib, which could help to develop a credit guarantee mechanism for european farmers. european farmers can no longer wait, nor can they continue to pay the price of prolonged periods of low prices. it is time to protect european farmers from price volatility by strengthening their role in the food chain to ensure that they receive fair compensation for their products.

madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the fall in the prices of many agricultural products, together with the extreme volatility which has in recent years led to ever wider, unpredictable and unfortunately often downward price fluctuations, is putting the sustainability of a sector as vital to the european economy as the agri-food sector at serious risk. if price volatility has always been a feature of agricultural markets, the present size, and even more so the size that may be reached in the future, require a common effort to ensure agricultural production capable of meeting the global challenge of food security, while ensuring stable and adequate incomes for our farmers. the measures provided for in the last reform of the common agricultural policy to counter market volatility have proved to be insufficient, as the crisis in the dairy sector has shown. the introduction of a complex system of red tape has, in fact, killed the potential that these instruments could have had in protecting european agricultural enterprises from market risks. the fact that the income stabilisation tool, considered one of the most innovative instruments introduced by the last reform, has been applied in only three countries of the union confirms the need to act as soon as possible in order to make the current measures simpler, more effective, more efficient and more usable by all member states. i would therefore like to thank the rapporteur, angélique delahaye, for the text we are about to vote on, a text which represents an excellent starting point, offering important insights not only in the short term, with measures which can be included in the omnibus package, but also in the long term, opening up a more articulated reflection on the use of countercyclical aid to protect farmers' incomes, with a view to complementarity between initiatives aimed at managing risks on the one hand and market crises on the other.

in writing. ‒ regulation (eu) 2015/848 on insolvency proceedings includes annexes containing lists of insolvency proceedings and insolvency practitioners. in december 2015, poland notified the commission of a substantial reform of its national restructuring law and requested to amend the lists in annexes a and b to the regulation. national procedures fall within the definition of 'insolvency proceedings' only if they are listed in annex a. the annexes may be amended only by a regulation adopted in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure. the commission has examined whether the application submitted by poland complies with the requirements of the regulation and has submitted a proposal to the european parliament and to the council to ensure that the scope of the recast regulation is adapted to the current legal framework of the polish insolvency law. the commission proposal is purely technical and does not involve any substantial amendment of the regulation. however, it is felt that it needs three amendments of a technical nature. the first two amendments reflect the position of the united kingdom and ireland with regard to the area of freedom, security and justice. the third amendment aligns the date of entry into force of regulation (eu) 2015/848.

in writing. ‒ the european trade policy has a twofold value: the first is purely economic, i.e. aimed at increasing opportunities for european enterprises. the second is purely social, that is to say, it is concerned with the promotion and protection of human rights in third countries. the agreement with uzbekistan is a clear example of this. in the light of the dramatic phenomenon of child labour in uzbekistan, in 2011 the european parliament at the instigation of our group refused to give its consent to the cotton protocol in the cooperation agreement with the country. this denial was a strong political signal for uzbekistan, with significant economic consequences since cotton is one of the country's major export products. uzbekistan has started to cooperate with the eu and the international labour organisation (ilo) as a result of this decision. although respect for human rights in uzbekistan still needs to be strengthened, the ilo has noted considerable progress in recent years, with the first being the definitive abolition of child labour. the priorities set by our group have therefore led the european union to achieve two extraordinary results: the opening of a new trade channel and, above all, respect for human rights.

in writing. ‒ the agreement which is the subject of the following report allows access to the fishing zones in the skagerrak for both swedish and danish vessels, as well as norwegian vessels. as it is a very important agreement, almost a historic event, i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ many european maritime zones retain a tradition dating back to before the creation of states and the recognition of territorial waters and eezs, whereby fishermen operate in the waters where certain fish stocks and species are found, and follow them during migrations. the kattegat and skagerrak are typical examples of this condition; the european union is not a mere fishing community, but a community of fishermen who have been fishing together for centuries in the same waters. on 15 january 2015, a new agreement between the eu and norway was signed, replacing an earlier international treaty of 1966 between denmark, sweden and norway on access to the skagerrak fishing zones. it is of the utmost importance that these historical fishing rights are respected; i therefore decided to vote in favour of the recommendation presented to parliament today. the agreement guarantees the support of historical fishing rights in this area, is in line with the united nations convention on the law of the sea and related provisions, and is above all a useful instrument for the implementation of the reformed cfp in the kattegat and skagerrak.
in writing. ‒ the skagerrak and kattegat are two natural channels linking the north sea with the baltic sea. in these two arms of the sea, swedish, danish and norwegian fishermen have been fishing together since the middle ages. i think it is important that these historical fishing rights are respected, even though norway is not a member state of the eu. that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i fully support this agreement, which is in line with the 1980 bilateral fisheries agreement, the un convention on the law of the sea and the objectives of the cfp. the agreement ensures that fishing vessels from denmark, norway and sweden comply with the laws, regulations and control and enforcement measures for the conservation and sustainable use of biological resources in the skagerrak.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the recommendation approving the renewal of the agreement between the european union and the kingdom of norway on reciprocal access to fishing zones in the skagerrak for vessels flying the flags of denmark, norway and sweden. in fact, an agreement between denmark, norway and sweden on reciprocal access to fishing zones in the skagerrak and kattegat has been in force since 1967. however, in the light of the most recent developments in international fisheries law and, in particular, following the adoption of the 1982 united nations convention on the law of the sea and the 1995 united nations fish stocks agreement, that agreement no longer complies with the current provisions of the law of the sea and therefore a new agreement has become necessary. the new agreement will continue to grant vessels from denmark, norway and sweden exclusive access to their respective waters beyond 4 nautical miles from the baselines.
in writing. ‒ with the accession of denmark (1973) and sweden (1995) to the eu, the european commission became responsible for managing the agreement on behalf of these two member states. this is a truly historic fisheries agreement: swedish, danish and norwegian fishermen have been fishing together in these waters for the same fish stocks since at least the middle ages. norway has held formal negotiations with the european commission. i therefore voted in favour of the agreement.
in writing. ‒ the agreement, which guarantees sweden, denmark and norway continued reciprocal access to their respective waters in the skagerrak and kattegat, has the merit of regulating fisheries in the area through certain conservation measures and effective instruments for joint management. the agreement will also make it possible to have control measures in accordance with the principles of the normal jurisdiction of coastal states, as is already the case for fisheries in the north sea. swedish, danish and norwegian fishermen have been fishing together in these waters since at least the middle ages. the fact that two of the countries have become member states of the european union has not changed the principle that their fishermen should enjoy historical fishing rights in the skagerrak and kattegat. i think it is important that these historical fishing rights be respected: the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. i therefore believe that the agreement under consideration is in line with these principles and useful for the implementation of the eu's common fisheries policy. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i support the agreement between the european union and norway to define as clearly as possible the mutual access to fishing zones in the skagerrak and kattegat. these are areas where the north sea waters mix with the less saline waters of the baltic sea, thus producing a favourable habitat for many marine species and making it a very fishery area. it is therefore essential to ensure exclusive access for danish, swedish and norwegian vessels to their respective waters beyond 4 nautical miles from the baselines. in addition, the continuity of mutual access to the other parties' respective waters in the skagerrak and kattegat must be affirmed and respected, while fully respecting the historical fishing rights in the above-mentioned areas (the first agreement between the three states sharing this area dates back to 1966 and comprised only three articles, the first of which defined the area in question, while the second defined the access rights and the desire to harmonise technical regulations).
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the agreement defining mutual access to fishing zones in the skagerrak and kattegat as it contributes to the shared regulation of this important sector in the territorial waters of denmark, sweden and norway.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation because i believe that the new agreement grants the vessels of denmark, norway and sweden exclusive access to their respective waters beyond 4 nautical miles from the baselines. it also guarantees the two member states and norway continued reciprocal access to each other's waters in the skagerrak and kattegat, while allowing the fisheries in the area to be regulated by certain conservation and management measures.

in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote in favour of the eu-norway agreement on mutual access to fishing zones in the skagerrak. the new agreement not only continues to guarantee sweden, denmark and norway the reciprocal exercise of fishing activities up to a distance of 4 nautical miles from their respective baselines, but also promotes fisheries conservation and management measures in the area and allows for control measures in accordance with the principles of the normal jurisdiction of coastal states. this agreement is necessary following the accession of denmark and sweden to the european union in order to reflect new developments in international fisheries law.

in writing. ‒ with the accession of denmark (1973) and sweden (1995) to the eu, the european commission became responsible for managing the agreement on behalf of these two member states. this is a truly historic fisheries agreement: swedish, danish and norwegian fishermen have been fishing together in these waters for the same fish stocks since at least the middle ages. norway has held formal negotiations with the european commission. i therefore voted in favour of the resolution.

in writing. ‒ studies show that interoperability and rail safety are central elements of the sustainable development model for the europe of the future. to improve them, the european railway agency (era) was established by regulation (ec) no 881/2004 of 29 april 2004, with offices in lille and valenciennes (france). the agency shall promote the progressive harmonisation, registration and monitoring of technical specifications for interoperability (tsis) across the european rail system and the development of common safety objectives for european railways. although the era does not have autonomous decision-making powers, it contributes to drafting proposals for decisions for the european commission. regulation (ec) no 1335/2008 of 16 december 2008 has conferred new tasks on the era, which are related to the amendments to the railway safety directives (2004/r) and (2008/57/ec). now, with the adoption of the fourth railway package, the era's powers of investigation and audit in its fields of competence will finally be strengthened. this will help to avoid having 28 different systems for the type approval of trains: the agency will act as a single point of contact for issuing authorisations for vehicles intended for cross-border operations and safety certificates to railway undertakings operating in different eu states.
in writing. ‒ the agreement reached at the second reading of the trilogue repeals regulation (eec) no 1192/69 on common rules for the normalisation of the accounts of railway undertakings. this repeal is part of the measures to liberalise the rail transport market adopted under the fourth railway package. the regulation in question authorised member states to compensate railway undertakings for the costs of obligations which undertakings in other transport sectors do not have to bear, but it was adopted before the liberalisation of the railway market and when rail transport in europe was mainly developing within national borders, with integrated companies managing both rail services and rail infrastructure. at that time the aim of the regulation was to equalise railway undertakings with undertakings operating in other modes of transport as regards the costs incurred for social costs or externalities. the repeal was necessary because the regulation no longer complies with the current legal framework.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal, which forms part of the governance pillar of the fourth railway package, which provides for the standardisation of the accounts of railway companies in europe. the text provides for the repeal of regulation no 1192/69 on common rules for the standardisation of the accounts of railway undertakings, which authorises member states to compensate railway undertakings for expenses arising from obligations which undertakings in other transport sectors are not required to bear.
in writing. ‒ the repeal of regulation (eec) no 1192/69 opens up additional railways to the single railway market and allows the end of discrimination suffered by european companies operating in the railway segment by those operating in other transport sectors. in view of the obsolescence of the above-mentioned regulation, i shall vote in favour of a measure representing the third pillar of the fourth railway package. the commission has therefore decided to normalize the accounts of railway undertakings in order to compensate for the payment of obligations which others, also in the field of transport, do not have to bear. these fall into 15 categories (classes) which define their specific scope and the criteria for calculating costs. overall, the charges are mainly special accident payments, pensions for railway workers who perform a very strenuous job, or costs related to level crossing facilities. in any case, it is necessary to take account of the historical moment in which regulation 1192/69 was developed, that is to say before the liberalisation of the market and, therefore, when rail transport operated mainly within national borders, so demonizing it would be a rather ignorant mistake, but today it has been markedly inadequate by progress.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure proposing to repeal council regulation 1192/69 laying down common rules for the normalisation of the accounts of railway undertakings, as i share the need to adapt the legislation by updating it and eliminating possible discrimination between undertakings in the sector in this area.
in writing. ‒ regulation no 1192/69 on common rules for the normalisation of the accounts of railway undertakings, which authorises member states to compensate railway undertakings for costs arising from obligations which undertakings in other transport sectors are not required to bear, no longer complies with the current legal framework. i therefore welcomed the proposal to repeal the regulation, which is also discriminatory. i agree, however, that a transitional period should be allowed for compensation for level crossing facilities (category iv) because some member states continue to use this regulation as the basis for such compensation.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the proposal to reject the council's position because i consider that regulation no 1192/69 is obsolete and incompatible with the current body of eu legislation and should therefore be repealed.
in writing. ‒ this regulation importantly allows member states to compensate railway undertakings for any obligation that other transport modes do not have to support, this is very important as it allows for a much fairer market in the transportation sector. our ultimate goal must be to create and ensure the best and most competitive transport market, where each method of travel or transportation is on a level playing field – this legislative proposal, alongside the other proposals of the market pillar in the fourth railway package goes a long way to make this a reality. given the substantial change in regulation, there is a clear need for a transitional period so that the member states have time to adapt to the new rules regarding compensation. this transitional period is set until 31 december 2017 and i hope that this will give the member states enough time to adapt their national legislation.
in writing. in conjunction with the fourth railway package, it is proposed to implement several legislative procedures, including the repeal of regulation no 69/1192 on common rules for the standardisation of the accounts of railway undertakings, which provides member states with the possibility of being able to offset the payment of obligations incurred by undertakings operating in other sectors; proposes to amend directive (eu) no 34/2012 establishing a single european railway area with regard to the opening of the market for national rail passenger services and the governance of railway infrastructure; and finally, it analyses the amendment of regulation no 1370/2007 with regard to the opening of the market for national rail passenger services. the report recommends that the commission's proposal for the repeal of the regulation, with the exception of the rules applying to the normalisation of accounts for category iv cases, be followed, that the council's position which appears to be in line with the agreement reached during the negotiations be followed and that the approval be without amendments.
in writing. ‒ today's vote repeals an earlier regulation on state aid to railway undertakings. this regulation, which was adopted before the liberalisation of the railway market, no longer complies with the current legal framework and discriminates between the railway undertakings listed in it and those excluded. i have therefore decided to vote in favour of its repeal.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that it is essential to ensure better access to the railway market in all member states in order to increase competition, choice and quality of services for the benefit of passengers. rail transport should also be revitalised in view of its contribution to sustainable mobility in our societies. the review of the rules will make it easier for new operators to enter the market and offer their services efficiently to travellers. the results should be in greater choice, cheaper fares and improved quality for the benefit of passengers. calls for tender will become the rule for public service contracts, while direct award will continue to be allowed where it improves the quality of service or cost efficiency. the inclusion in the contracts of efficiency and quality objectives, which include punctuality and frequency of trains, is also positive. the reform will help to strengthen railway undertakings so that they have equal access to tracks and stations.
in writing. ‒ the following report is part of the governance project of the fourth railway package and is mainly concerned with fostering market opening in rail transport. although i understand the strong need to introduce rules to encourage greater openness in the railway market, i have decided to vote in favour of the proposal to reject the council's position because i think that certain aspects which are very important to me are being neglected. one of them is the introduction of too many exceptions and exemptions in public service contracts, which are detrimental to increased competition. i also think that very sensitive social issues such as the transfer of staff are not being dealt with adequately.
in writing. ‒ i intend to support the motion for a resolution tabled.
in writing. ‒ the adoption of the fourth railway package and the strengthening of the era's powers of investigation and audit in its fields of competence will help to harmonise the trans-european transport and rail networks. we will no longer have 28 different systems for the approval of trains: the agency will act as a single point of contact for issuing authorisations for vehicles intended for cross-border operations and safety certificates to railway undertakings operating in different eu states. the adoption of the regulation will also increase the competitive pressure on national transport agencies, with the hope that this will lead to an increase in service quality and cost optimisation.
in writing. ‒ the agreement reached in the trilogue at second reading amends regulation no 1370/2007 on public passenger transport services by road and rail. this amendment concerns the opening of the market for national rail passenger services and aims to improve the quality of the services offered and to increase operational efficiency. this should increase the competitiveness and attractiveness of rail in comparison with other modes of transport and further develop the single european railway area. the amendment introduces mandatory competitive tendering procedures for public service contracts in order to intensify the competitive pressure on national railway markets. these measures are accompanied by provisions to ensure favourable framework conditions for competitive tendering procedures, including rules on access to rolling stock.
in writing. ‒ the report is part of the liberalization of services in europe, which unfortunately has not always had the positive effects expected. all too often, in order to eliminate historical monopolies, savage liberalizations have been carried out which have had the sole purpose of favouring industry at the expense of the quality of services, social protection and public service obligations. that is why i voted against.
in writing. ‒ in approving the measure under consideration, i believe that competition is poised to increase the quality, volume and efficiency of transport systems by preserving and giving new impetus to already excellent structures. the main aim is to introduce three substantial innovations: first, the competent authorities will have to clearly define the specifics of the public service obligations in the provision of services and in a manner consistent with the stated political obligations. in addition, public service operators will be required to comply with applicable obligations in the field of social and labour law. finally, public service contracts will be awarded through competitive tendering procedures, although exceptions may be made for direct or simplified procedures. this will increase the efficiency and attractiveness of the sector, leading to improved quality and thus to greater railway development.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it aims to increase competition in the rail transport sector by introducing specific improvement measures. it is important, however, that competition should not be an end in itself but rather a means of gradually increasing the quality, volume and efficiency of passenger transport services. the existing efficient structures should therefore be maintained and should not lose their efficiency as a result of the new regulation. it is important that the european union should make greater efforts to improve the quality and efficiency of rail passenger services.
in writing. ‒ i believe it is important to improve the quality of rail passenger services and to promote their operational efficiency. this should increase the competitiveness and attractiveness of rail in comparison with other modes of transport and further develop the single european railway area. i therefore welcomed the commission's proposal to introduce compulsory competitive tendering procedures for public service contracts in order to intensify the competitive pressure on national railway markets. i would, however, like to stress that public service operators will have to comply with the applicable obligations in the field of social and labour law laid down by union law, national law or collective agreements.
in writing. ‒ this important proposal introduces mandatory competitive tendering for public service contracts in order to intensify the competitiveness of member states’ railway markets. the aim is to increase efficiency and to improve the quality of rail passenger services. in more detail this proposal introduces extra obligations on psos in public passenger transport, that authorities ensure related compensation of net financial effects of public service, that all operators fulfil obligations in social and labour law. it is also important that the proposal includes that public service operators and infrastructure managers will be under obligation to provide information that is essential for the tendering process, including information on passenger demand, fares, costs and revenues. this proposal should provide for a more open, entry-free and competitive market, while ensuring the legitimate protection of confidential business information.
in writing. the parliament's report is in line with the commission's proposal on improving competition in rail transport, competition aimed at increasing the quality and efficiency of passenger transport services. the new rules are intended to optimise the quality of rail passenger services and operational efficiency, and to increase competitiveness in relation to other transport services, thus strengthening the single european railway area. it is therefore proposed to introduce compulsory competitive tendering procedures for public service contracts in order to ensure favourable framework conditions. in addition, this proposal is closely linked to the subsequent report on the establishment of a single european railway area, which discusses free access rights for companies and improves the provisions on infrastructure management. in view of both recommendations, which are aimed at the same result, i vote in favour of this proposal.

in writing. ‒ the agreement reached in the trilogue at second reading amends directive 2012/34/eu on the single european railway area. the amendment aims, firstly, to open up the market for national rail passenger services with the aim of increasing competitive pressure on national rail markets with a view to increasing the quantity and improving the quality of passenger services. secondly, to improve the governance of the infrastructure manager, with the aim of ensuring equal access to infrastructure. in this respect, it provides for the elimination of conflicts of interest affecting the decisions of the infrastructure manager regarding market access and the elimination of cross-subsidisation possibilities between infrastructure managers and railway undertakings, which exist in integrated structures. the amendments also aim to strengthen coordination between infrastructure managers and railway operators in order to better respond to market needs and to enhance cross-border cooperation between infrastructure managers.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the regulation establishing a regulatory framework for market access to port services and financial transparency for ports. the objective of the regulation is to contribute to a more efficient, interconnected and sustainable operation of the ten-t by establishing a framework to improve the efficiency of all ports and help them to cope with changing logistics and transport requirements. for this reason, it also includes the modernisation of port services and operations and the creation of framework conditions to attract investment in ports. since it covers only port services offered directly to users, dredging is excluded from the list of services, as it is not a service offered to individual users but maintenance work to ensure the accessibility of the port. the regulation will apply to all maritime ports identified in the ten-t guidelines and will avoid imposing additional burdens on ports that are already functioning well, while creating the conditions to enable other ports to address their structural problems.
